readme: A formally verified library for computable polynomial operations over finite fields and general rings, supporting univariate, multivariate, multilinear, and bivariate polynomials.

folders.CompPoly/Bivariate: Formally verified computable bivariate polynomials for [CompPoly](../../README.md), represented as `CPolynomial (CPolynomial R)` — polynomials in Y whose coefficients are univariate polynomials in X. Matches Mathlib's `R[X][Y]` and is compatible with [ArkLib](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/ArkLib)'s `Polynomial.Bivariate` interface.
folders.CompPoly/Fields: This directory contains formally verified field infrastructure used in zero-knowledge proof systems and elliptic-curve cryptography, including scalar prime fields and binary-field constructions.
folders.CompPoly/LinearAlgebra:
Executable matrices for [CompPoly](../../README.md), in two independent flavours:
dense matrices over a field, and row-oriented matrices whose entries are
univariate polynomials. Both exist to serve the Guruswami-Sudan interpolation
backends (see [`../../docs/wiki/coding-theory.md`](../../docs/wiki/coding-theory.md)),
but neither depends on the decoder and both are usable on their own.
folders.CompPoly/Univariate: Formally verified computable univariate polynomials for [CompPoly](../../README.md), built on array-backed coefficient representation.

modules.title: Computable Bivariate Polynomials
modules.doc:
This file defines `CBivariate R`, the computable representation of bivariate polynomials with
coefficients in `R`. The type is `CPolynomial (CPolynomial R)`, i.e. polynomials in `Y` with
coefficients that are polynomials in `X`, matching Mathlib's `R[X][Y]`
(i.e. `Polynomial (Polynomial R)`).

The design is intended to be compatible with:
- Mathlib's `Polynomial.Bivariate` (see `CompPoly/Bivariate/ToPoly.lean`)
- ArkLib's `Polynomial.Bivariate` interface (see ArkLib/Data/Polynomial/Bivariate.lean and
  ArkLib/Data/CodingTheory/PolishchukSpielman/Degrees.lean, BCIKS20.lean, etc.)

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate
items.doc:
Computable bivariate polynomials: `F[X][Y]` as `CPolynomial (CPolynomial R)`.

Each `p : CBivariate R` is a polynomial in `Y` whose coefficients are univariate polynomials
in `X`. The outer structure is indexed by powers of `Y`, the inner by powers of `X`.
items.statement: def CBivariate (R : Type*) [Zero R]

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.ext
items.doc: Extensionality: two bivariate polynomials are equal if their underlying values are.
items.statement: theorem ext {p q : CBivariate R} (h : p.val = q.val) : p = q

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.CC
items.doc: Constant as a bivariate polynomial. Mathlib: `Polynomial.Bivariate.CC`.
items.statement: def CC {R : Type*} [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (r : R) : CBivariate R

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.X
items.doc: The variable X (inner variable). As bivariate: polynomial in Y with single coeff `X` at Y^0.
items.statement: def X {R : Type*} [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] : CBivariate R

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.Y
items.doc: The variable Y (outer variable). Monomial `Y^1` with coefficient 1.
items.statement:
def Y {R : Type*} [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R] :
    CBivariate R

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.monomialXY
items.doc: Monomial `c * X^n * Y^m`. ArkLib: `Polynomial.Bivariate.monomialXY`.
items.statement:
def monomialXY {R : Type*} [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (n m : ℕ) (c : R) : CBivariate R

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.coeff
items.doc:
Coefficient of `X^i Y^j` in the bivariate polynomial. Here `i` is the X-exponent (inner)
and `j` is the Y-exponent (outer). ArkLib: `Polynomial.Bivariate.coeff f i j`.
items.statement: def coeff {R : Type*} [Zero R] (f : CBivariate R) (i j : ℕ) : R

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.supportY
items.doc: The Y-support: indices j such that the coefficient of Y^j is nonzero.
items.statement: def supportY {R : Type*} [Zero R] [BEq R] (f : CBivariate R) : Finset ℕ

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.supportX
items.doc:
The X-support: indices i such that the coefficient of X^i is nonzero
(i.e. some monomial X^i Y^j has nonzero coefficient).
items.statement: def supportX {R : Type*} [Zero R] [BEq R] (f : CBivariate R) : Finset ℕ

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.natDegreeY
items.doc:
The `Y`-degree (degree when viewed as a polynomial in `Y`).
ArkLib: `Polynomial.Bivariate.natDegreeY`.
items.statement: def natDegreeY {R : Type*} [Zero R] (f : CBivariate R) : ℕ

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.natDegreeX
items.doc:
The `X`-degree: maximum over all Y-coefficients of their degree in X.
ArkLib: `Polynomial.Bivariate.natDegreeX`.
items.statement: def natDegreeX {R : Type*} [Zero R] [BEq R] (f : CBivariate R) : ℕ

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.totalDegree
items.doc:
Total degree: max over monomials of (deg_X + deg_Y).
ArkLib: `Polynomial.Bivariate.totalDegree`.
items.statement: def totalDegree {R : Type*} [Zero R] [BEq R] (f : CBivariate R) : ℕ

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.natWeightedDegree
items.doc: The `(u, v)`-weighted degree: max over monomials of `u * deg_X + v * deg_Y`.
items.statement: def natWeightedDegree {R : Type*} [Zero R] [BEq R] (f : CBivariate R) (u v : ℕ) : ℕ

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.evalX
items.doc:
Evaluate in the first variable (X) at `a`, yielding a univariate polynomial in Y.
ArkLib: `Polynomial.Bivariate.evalX`.
items.statement:
def evalX {R : Type*} [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [DecidableEq R]
    (a : R) (f : CBivariate R) : CPolynomial R

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.evalY
items.doc:
Evaluate in the second variable (Y) at `a`, yielding a univariate polynomial in X.
ArkLib: `Polynomial.Bivariate.evalY`.

Folds the Y-coefficients of `f` with a raw Horner pattern (`smulRight a` then
`addRaw`), trimming once at the end. This avoids paying one `CPolynomial.mul`
and one `CPolynomial.add` trim per Y-coefficient.
items.statement:
def evalY {R : Type*} [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R]
    (a : R) (f : CBivariate R) : CPolynomial R

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.evalYHorner
items.doc:
Evaluate in the second variable (Y) at `a` using Horner's method,
yielding a univariate polynomial in X.
items.statement:
def evalYHorner {R : Type*} [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R]
    (a : R) (p : CBivariate R) : CPolynomial R

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.evalEval
items.doc:
Full evaluation at `(x, y)`: `p(x, y)`. Inner variable X at `x`, outer variable Y at `y`.
Equivalently `(evalY y f).eval x`. Mathlib: `Polynomial.evalEval`.

See `CBivariate.eval_y_horner_eq_eval_y` in `CompPoly/Bivariate/ToPoly.lean` for
agreement between `evalY` and `evalYHorner`.
items.statement:
def evalEval {R : Type*} [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R]
    (x y : R) (f : CBivariate R) : R

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.evalEvalHornerYThenX
items.doc:
Full evaluation at `(x, y)` using Horner in Y, then Horner in X on the
intermediate univariate polynomial.
items.statement:
def evalEvalHornerYThenX {R : Type*} [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R]
    (x y : R) (p : CBivariate R) : R

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.evalEvalHornerXThenY
items.doc:
Full evaluation at `(x, y)` by evaluating each X-coefficient polynomial at
`x`, then Horner-evaluating the resulting scalar polynomial in Y.
items.statement: def evalEvalHornerXThenY {R : Type*} [Semiring R] (x y : R) (p : CBivariate R) : R

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.swap
items.doc:
Swap the roles of X and Y.
ArkLib/Mathlib: `Polynomial.Bivariate.swap`.
TODO a more efficient implementation
items.statement:
def swap {R : Type*} [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (f : CBivariate R) : CBivariate R

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.leadingCoeffY
items.doc:
Leading coefficient when viewed as a polynomial in Y.
ArkLib: `Polynomial.Bivariate.leadingCoeffY`.
items.statement: def leadingCoeffY {R : Type*} [Zero R] (f : CBivariate R) : CPolynomial R

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.leadingCoeffX
items.doc:
Leading coefficient when viewed as a polynomial in X.
The coefficient of X^(degreeX f): a polynomial in Y.
items.statement:
def leadingCoeffX {R : Type*} [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (f : CBivariate R) : CPolynomial R

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.coeff_eq_coeff_coeff
items.doc: `CBivariate.coeff` as two composed `CPolynomial.coeff`.
items.statement:
theorem coeff_eq_coeff_coeff [Zero R] (f : CBivariate R) (i j : ℕ) :
    coeff f i j = CPolynomial.coeff (CPolynomial.coeff f j) i

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.coeff_add
items.doc: Bivariate coefficients are additive.
items.statement:
theorem coeff_add [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R]
    (p q : CBivariate R) (i j : ℕ) :
    coeff (p + q) i j = coeff p i j + coeff q i j

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.coeff_finset_sum
items.doc: Bivariate coefficients distribute over finite sums.
items.statement:
theorem coeff_finset_sum [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R]
    {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] (s : Finset ι) (f : ι → CBivariate R) (i j : ℕ) :
    coeff (s.sum f) i j = s.sum (fun t => coeff (f t) i j)

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.coeff_monomialXY
items.doc: Coefficient of a bivariate monomial `c * X^a * Y^b`.
items.statement:
theorem coeff_monomialXY [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (a b : ℕ) (c : R) (i j : ℕ) :
    coeff (monomialXY a b c) i j = if i = a ∧ j = b then c else 0

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.coeff_monomialY
items.doc: Coefficient of `Y^m * c(X)` as a bivariate polynomial.
items.statement:
theorem coeff_monomialY [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (m : ℕ) (c : CPolynomial R) (i j : ℕ) :
    coeff (CPolynomial.monomial m c) i j = if j = m then CPolynomial.coeff c i else 0

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.eq_iff_coeff
items.doc: Two bivariate polynomials are equal iff all their coefficients agree.
items.statement:
theorem eq_iff_coeff [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] {p q : CBivariate R} :
    p = q ↔ ∀ i j, coeff p i j = coeff q i j

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.totalDegree_eq_natWeightedDegree
items.doc: The total degree is the `(1, 1)`-weighted degree.
items.statement:
theorem totalDegree_eq_natWeightedDegree (f : CBivariate R) :
    CBivariate.totalDegree (R := R) f = CBivariate.natWeightedDegree (R := R) f 1 1

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.natDegreeX_eq_natWeightedDegree
items.doc: The X-degree is the `(1, 0)`-weighted degree.
items.statement:
theorem natDegreeX_eq_natWeightedDegree (f : CBivariate R) :
    CBivariate.natDegreeX (R := R) f = CBivariate.natWeightedDegree (R := R) f 1 0

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.natDegreeY_eq_natWeightedDegree
items.doc: The Y-degree is the `(0, 1)`-weighted degree.
items.statement:
theorem natDegreeY_eq_natWeightedDegree (f : CBivariate R) :
    CBivariate.natDegreeY (R := R) f = CBivariate.natWeightedDegree (R := R) f 0 1

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.natWeightedDegree_monomialXY
items.doc:
The weighted degree of a nonzero monomial `c * X^n * Y^m`
is `u * n + v * m` where `u` is the weight of `X` and `v` the weight of `Y`.
items.statement:
theorem natWeightedDegree_monomialXY [DecidableEq R]
    {n m : ℕ} {c : R} (hc : c ≠ 0) (u v : ℕ) :
    CBivariate.natWeightedDegree
      (CBivariate.monomialXY n m c) u v
      = u * n + v * m

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.natWeightedDegree_zero
items.doc: The weighted degree of the zero polynomial is zero.
items.statement:
theorem natWeightedDegree_zero (u v : ℕ) :
    CBivariate.natWeightedDegree (0 : CBivariate R) u v = 0

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.natWeightedDegree_le_iff
items.doc:
The weighted degree is at most `d` iff every Y-support index
satisfies the weighted bound.
items.statement:
theorem natWeightedDegree_le_iff (f : CBivariate R) (u v d : ℕ) :
    natWeightedDegree f u v ≤ d ↔
    ∀ j ∈ f.supportY , u * (f.val.coeff j).natDegree + v * j ≤ d

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.natWeightedDegree_le_iff_coeff
items.doc:
The weighted degree is at most `d` iff every monomial index
satisfies the weighted bound.
items.statement:
theorem natWeightedDegree_le_iff_coeff (f : CBivariate R) (u v d : ℕ) :
    f.natWeightedDegree u v ≤ d ↔
    ∀ i j, CBivariate.coeff f i j ≠ 0 → u * i + v * j ≤ d

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.natWeightedDegree_CC
items.doc: The natWeightedDegree of a constant bivariate polynomial `CBivariate.CC` is zero.
items.statement:
theorem natWeightedDegree_CC {r : R} (u v : ℕ) :
    CBivariate.natWeightedDegree (CBivariate.CC r) u v = 0

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.natWeightedDegree_add_le
items.doc: The weighted degree of a sum is at most the max of the weighted degrees.
items.statement:
theorem natWeightedDegree_add_le [DecidableEq R] (p q : CBivariate R) (u v : ℕ) :
    CBivariate.natWeightedDegree (p + q) u v ≤
      max (CBivariate.natWeightedDegree p u v) (CBivariate.natWeightedDegree q u v)

modules.title: Serialization of bivariate polynomials
modules.doc:
`CBivariate R` is `CPolynomial (CPolynomial R)`, so its self-delimiting encoding is the
univariate one nested: a `u64` count of `Y`-coefficients, each a `u64` count of
`X`-coefficients followed by those coefficients. Nothing new is defined; the instance is the
univariate codec at coefficient type `CPolynomial R`, which is what the delimited-codec design
exists for.

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.encode_eq
items.statement:
theorem encode_eq [DelimitedCodec R] (p : CBivariate R) :
    DelimitedCodec.encode p = DelimitedCodec.encode (p : CPolynomial (CPolynomial R))

modules.title: Equivalence between `CBivariate` and `CMvPolynomial 2`
modules.doc:
This file establishes the ring equivalence
`bivariateEquiv : CBivariate R ≃+* CMvPolynomial 2 R`
by composing `CBivariate.ringEquiv` with `CMvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv`
and `CMvPolynomial.isEmptyRingEquiv`.

The equivalence chain is:
  `CBivariate R ≃ R[X][Y] ≃ (CMvPolynomial 0 R)[X][Y]
    ≃ (CMvPolynomial 1 R)[Y] ≃ CMvPolynomial 2 R`

## Main definitions

* `bivariateEquiv` — ring equivalence `CBivariate R ≃+* CMvPolynomial 2 R`

## Bridge lemmas

* `bivariateEquiv_CC` — `bivariateEquiv (CC r) = C r`
* `bivariateEquiv_X` — `bivariateEquiv X = CMvPolynomial.X 1`
* `bivariateEquiv_Y` — `bivariateEquiv Y = CMvPolynomial.X 0`
* `bivariateEquiv_symm_C` — `bivariateEquiv.symm (C r) = CC r`
* `bivariateEquiv_symm_X0` — `bivariateEquiv.symm (X 0) = Y`
* `bivariateEquiv_symm_X1` — `bivariateEquiv.symm (X 1) = X`

## Helper lemmas (for `CMvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv`)

* `CMvPolynomial.isEmptyRingEquiv_symm_apply` —
  `isEmptyRingEquiv.symm r = C r`
* `CMvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv_symm_C` —
  `finSuccEquiv.symm (Polynomial.C x) = rename Fin.succ x`
* `CMvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv_symm_X` —
  `finSuccEquiv.symm Polynomial.X = CMvPolynomial.X 0`

items.name: CMvPolynomial.isEmptyRingEquiv_symm_apply
items.doc: `isEmptyRingEquiv.symm` maps scalars to constants.
items.statement:
lemma isEmptyRingEquiv_symm_apply
    {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (r : R) :
    CMvPolynomial.isEmptyRingEquiv.symm r = CMvPolynomial.C r

items.name: CMvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv_symm_C
items.doc: `finSuccEquiv.symm` maps `Polynomial.C` to `rename Fin.succ`.
items.statement:
lemma finSuccEquiv_symm_C
    {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    {n : ℕ} (x : CMvPolynomial n R) :
    CMvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv.symm (Polynomial.C x) =
      CMvPolynomial.rename Fin.succ x

items.name: CMvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv_symm_X
items.doc: `finSuccEquiv.symm` maps `Polynomial.X` to the zeroth variable.
items.statement:
lemma finSuccEquiv_symm_X
    {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    {n : ℕ} :
    CMvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv.symm
      (Polynomial.X : Polynomial (CMvPolynomial n R)) =
      CMvPolynomial.X 0

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.bivariateEquiv
items.doc: Ring equivalence between `CBivariate R` and `CMvPolynomial 2 R`.
items.statement:
noncomputable def bivariateEquiv :
    CBivariate R ≃+* CMvPolynomial 2 R

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.bivariateEquiv_add
items.doc: `bivariateEquiv` preserves addition.
items.statement:
lemma bivariateEquiv_add (p q : CBivariate R) :
    bivariateEquiv (p + q) =
      bivariateEquiv p + bivariateEquiv q

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.bivariateEquiv_mul
items.doc: `bivariateEquiv` preserves multiplication.
items.statement:
lemma bivariateEquiv_mul (p q : CBivariate R) :
    bivariateEquiv (p * q) =
      bivariateEquiv p * bivariateEquiv q

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.bivariateEquiv_zero
items.doc: `bivariateEquiv` maps zero to zero.
items.statement:
lemma bivariateEquiv_zero :
    bivariateEquiv (0 : CBivariate R) = 0

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.bivariateEquiv_CC
items.doc: `bivariateEquiv` maps bivariate constants to multivariate constants.
items.statement:
lemma bivariateEquiv_CC (r : R) :
    bivariateEquiv (CBivariate.CC r) = CMvPolynomial.C r

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.bivariateEquiv_X
items.doc: `bivariateEquiv` maps `CBivariate.X` to the second variable.
items.statement:
lemma bivariateEquiv_X :
    bivariateEquiv (CBivariate.X : CBivariate R) =
      CMvPolynomial.X 1

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.bivariateEquiv_Y
items.doc: `bivariateEquiv` maps `CBivariate.Y` to the first variable.
items.statement:
lemma bivariateEquiv_Y :
    bivariateEquiv (CBivariate.Y : CBivariate R) =
      CMvPolynomial.X 0

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.bivariateEquiv_symm_C
items.doc: `bivariateEquiv.symm` maps multivariate constants to bivariate constants.
items.statement:
lemma bivariateEquiv_symm_C (r : R) :
    bivariateEquiv.symm (CMvPolynomial.C r) =
      CBivariate.CC r

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.bivariateEquiv_symm_X0
items.doc: `bivariateEquiv.symm` maps the first variable to `CBivariate.Y`.
items.statement:
lemma bivariateEquiv_symm_X0 :
    bivariateEquiv.symm (CMvPolynomial.X 0 : CMvPolynomial 2 R) =
      CBivariate.Y

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.bivariateEquiv_symm_X1
items.doc: `bivariateEquiv.symm` maps the second variable to `CBivariate.X`.
items.statement:
lemma bivariateEquiv_symm_X1 :
    bivariateEquiv.symm (CMvPolynomial.X 1 : CMvPolynomial 2 R) =
      CBivariate.X

modules.title: Coefficient Rows for Bivariate Polynomials
modules.doc: Conversions between finite `Y`-coefficient rows and `CBivariate`.

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.ofCoeffRow
items.doc: Interpret a polynomial row `[q_0, ..., q_l]` as `∑ q_j(X) Y^j`.
items.statement:
def ofCoeffRow [Zero F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (row : PolynomialRow F) : CBivariate F

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.toCoeffRow
items.doc: Truncate a bivariate polynomial to its first `width` `Y`-coefficient rows.
items.statement:
def toCoeffRow [Zero F] (width : Nat) (Q : CBivariate F) :
    PolynomialRow F

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.toCoeffRow_size
items.doc: Truncated coefficient rows have the requested width.
items.statement:
theorem toCoeffRow_size [Zero F] (width : Nat) (Q : CBivariate F) :
    (toCoeffRow width Q).size = width

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.weightedDegreeShift
items.doc: Lee-style shift array for `(1, w)` weighted degree.
items.statement: def weightedDegreeShift (w width : Nat) : Array Nat

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.coeff_ofCoeffRow_of_lt
items.doc: Coefficient-row conversion preserves finite `Y` coefficients below row width.
items.statement:
theorem coeff_ofCoeffRow_of_lt [Zero F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (row : PolynomialRow F) {i j : Nat} (hj : j < row.size) :
    CBivariate.coeff (ofCoeffRow row) i j = CPolynomial.coeff (row.getD j 0) i

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.coeff_ofCoeffRow_of_size_le
items.doc: Coefficients past the row width vanish after row-to-bivariate conversion.
items.statement:
theorem coeff_ofCoeffRow_of_size_le [Zero F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (row : PolynomialRow F) {i j : Nat} (hj : row.size ≤ j) :
    CBivariate.coeff (ofCoeffRow row) i j = 0

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.rowShiftedDegree?_eq_natWeightedDegree_ofCoeffRow
items.doc: Row shifted degree for the Lee shift matches weighted degree of the bivariate view.
items.statement:
theorem rowShiftedDegree?_eq_natWeightedDegree_ofCoeffRow
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (row : PolynomialRow F) (w d : Nat)
    (hdeg :
      PolynomialMatrix.rowShiftedDegree? row (weightedDegreeShift w row.size) = some d) :
    CBivariate.natWeightedDegree (ofCoeffRow row) 1 w = d

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.natWeightedDegree_ofCoeffRow_le_of_rowShiftedDegree?_le
items.doc: Weighted-degree bounded rows convert to weighted-degree bounded bivariate polynomials.
items.statement:
theorem natWeightedDegree_ofCoeffRow_le_of_rowShiftedDegree?_le
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (row : PolynomialRow F) (w bound d : Nat)
    (hdeg :
      PolynomialMatrix.rowShiftedDegree? row (weightedDegreeShift w row.size) = some d)
    (hle : d ≤ bound) :
    CBivariate.natWeightedDegree (ofCoeffRow row) 1 w ≤ bound

modules.title: Partial Derivatives and Multiplicity of Computable Bivariate Polynomials
modules.doc:
This file defines partial derivatives (`partialDerivX`, `partialDerivY`, iterated
and mixed partials) and the multiplicity condition `hasMultiplicity` used in the
Guruswami–Sudan interpolation step.

Multiplicity of a root at `(a, b)` is defined through the Taylor shift
`shiftC a b Q = Q(X + a, Y + b)`. `Q` has multiplicity at least `r` at `(a, b)`
when every coefficient of the shifted polynomial of total degree less than `r`
is zero. This is the Hasse-derivative criterion for root multiplicity over a field
of any characteristic: the coefficient of `Xⁱ Yʲ` in `shiftC a b Q` is the
order-`(i, j)` Hasse derivative of `Q` evaluated at `(a, b)`. The zero polynomial
has infinite multiplicity. As an aside, ordinary partial derivatives fail to capture
this in positive characteristic. The integer factor introduced by differentiation can
vanish, so its product with a nonzero coefficient may become zero.

`shiftC_toPoly` identifies the computable shift with Mathlib's
`Polynomial.Bivariate.shift`, and `hasMultiplicity_iff_rootMultiplicity` proves
that `hasMultiplicity` agrees with the reference `Polynomial.Bivariate.rootMultiplicity`.

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.partialDerivX
items.doc: Partial derivative with respect to X: differentiate each Y-coefficient in X.
items.statement:
def partialDerivX [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (f : CBivariate R) : CBivariate R

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.partialDerivY
items.doc: Partial derivative with respect to Y: differentiate in the outer variable.
items.statement:
def partialDerivY [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R]
    (f : CBivariate R) : CBivariate R

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.outerCoeff_support_monomial
items.doc:
Outer coefficient of a `support`-sum of monomials whose `Y`-coefficients are mapped by a
zero-preserving `g`: the `j`-th coefficient is `g` applied to the `j`-th `Y`-coefficient.
items.statement:
theorem outerCoeff_support_monomial [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R]
    [DecidableEq R] (f : CBivariate R) (g : CPolynomial R → CPolynomial R) (hg : g 0 = 0) (j : ℕ) :
    CPolynomial.coeff ((CPolynomial.support f).sum fun k =>
      CPolynomial.monomial k (g (f.val.coeff k))) j = g (CPolynomial.coeff f j)

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.outerCoeff_partialDerivX
items.doc: Outer coefficient of the X-partial derivative: differentiate the j-th Y-coefficient.
items.statement:
theorem outerCoeff_partialDerivX [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (f : CBivariate R) (j : ℕ) :
    CPolynomial.coeff (partialDerivX f) j =
      CPolynomial.derivative (CPolynomial.coeff f j)

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.coeff_partialDerivX
items.doc: Coefficient formula for the X-partial derivative.
items.statement:
theorem coeff_partialDerivX [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (f : CBivariate R) (i j : ℕ) :
    CBivariate.coeff (partialDerivX f) i j =
      CBivariate.coeff f (i + 1) j * (↑(i + 1) : R)

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.coeff_partialDerivY
items.doc: Coefficient formula for the Y-partial derivative.
items.statement:
theorem coeff_partialDerivY [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R]
    (f : CBivariate R) (i j : ℕ) :
    CBivariate.coeff (partialDerivY f) i j =
      CBivariate.coeff f i (j + 1) * (↑(j + 1) : R)

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.partialDerivX_zero
items.doc: The X-partial derivative of zero is zero.
items.statement:
theorem partialDerivX_zero [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R] :
    partialDerivX (0 : CBivariate R) = 0

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.partialDerivY_zero
items.doc: The Y-partial derivative of zero is zero.
items.statement:
theorem partialDerivY_zero [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] :
    partialDerivY (0 : CBivariate R) = 0

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.partialDerivX_add
items.doc: The X-partial derivative distributes over addition.
items.statement:
theorem partialDerivX_add [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (f g : CBivariate R) :
    partialDerivX (f + g) = partialDerivX f + partialDerivX g

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.partialDerivY_add
items.doc: The Y-partial derivative distributes over addition.
items.statement:
theorem partialDerivY_add [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (f g : CBivariate R) :
    partialDerivY (f + g) = partialDerivY f + partialDerivY g

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.partialDerivX_toPoly
items.doc: The X-partial derivative differentiates each Y-coefficient under `toPoly`.
items.statement:
theorem partialDerivX_toPoly [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (f : CBivariate R) (j : ℕ) :
    (toPoly (partialDerivX f)).coeff j =
      Polynomial.derivative ((toPoly f).coeff j)

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.partialDerivY_toPoly
items.doc: The Y-partial derivative corresponds to `Polynomial.derivative` under `toPoly`.
items.statement:
theorem partialDerivY_toPoly [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (f : CBivariate R) :
    toPoly (partialDerivY f) = Polynomial.derivative (toPoly f)

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.partialDerivY_mul
items.doc: The Y-partial derivative satisfies the Leibniz product rule.
items.statement:
theorem partialDerivY_mul [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (f g : CBivariate R) :
    partialDerivY (f * g) = partialDerivY f * g + f * partialDerivY g

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.partialDerivX_mul
items.doc: The X-partial derivative satisfies the Leibniz product rule.
items.statement:
theorem partialDerivX_mul [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (f g : CBivariate R) :
    partialDerivX (f * g) = partialDerivX f * g + f * partialDerivX g

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.iterPartialDerivX
items.doc: Iterated partial derivative with respect to X.
items.statement:
def iterPartialDerivX [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (n : ℕ) (f : CBivariate R) : CBivariate R

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.iterPartialDerivY
items.doc: Iterated partial derivative with respect to Y.
items.statement:
def iterPartialDerivY [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R]
    (n : ℕ) (f : CBivariate R) : CBivariate R

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.iterPartialDerivX_toPoly
items.doc: Iterated X-partial derivative differentiates each Y-coefficient under `toPoly`.
items.statement:
theorem iterPartialDerivX_toPoly [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (n : ℕ) (f : CBivariate R) (j : ℕ) :
    (toPoly (iterPartialDerivX n f)).coeff j =
      Polynomial.derivative^[n] ((toPoly f).coeff j)

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.iterPartialDerivY_toPoly
items.doc: Iterated Y-partial derivative corresponds to `Polynomial.derivative^[n]` under `toPoly`.
items.statement:
theorem iterPartialDerivY_toPoly [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (n : ℕ) (f : CBivariate R) :
    toPoly (iterPartialDerivY n f) = Polynomial.derivative^[n] (toPoly f)

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.mixedPartialDeriv
items.doc: Mixed partial derivative: i-fold in X, then j-fold in Y.
items.statement:
def mixedPartialDeriv [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (i j : ℕ) (f : CBivariate R) : CBivariate R

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.partialDerivX_partialDerivY_comm
items.doc: X and Y partial derivatives commute.
items.statement:
theorem partialDerivX_partialDerivY_comm [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R]
    [DecidableEq R] (f : CBivariate R) :
    partialDerivX (partialDerivY f) = partialDerivY (partialDerivX f)

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.mixedPartials_comm
items.doc: Mixed partial derivatives commute.
items.statement:
theorem mixedPartials_comm [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (i j : ℕ) (f : CBivariate R) :
    iterPartialDerivX i (iterPartialDerivY j f) =
      iterPartialDerivY j (iterPartialDerivX i f)

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.shiftY
items.doc: Shift the outer `Y` variable: `Q(X, Y + b)`.
items.statement:
def shiftY [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (b : R) (Q : CBivariate R) : CBivariate R

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.shiftX
items.doc: Shift the inner `X` variable: `Q(X + a, Y)`, Taylor-shifting each `Y`-coefficient.
items.statement:
def shiftX [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (a : R) (Q : CBivariate R) : CBivariate R

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.shiftC
items.doc: The full shift `Q(X + a, Y + b)`.
items.statement:
def shiftC [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (a b : R) (Q : CBivariate R) : CBivariate R

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.hasMultiplicity
items.doc:
`Q` has multiplicity at least `r` at `(a, b)`: every coefficient of the shifted
polynomial `Q(X + a, Y + b)` of total degree `< r` vanishes.
items.statement:
def hasMultiplicity [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (Q : CBivariate R) (r : ℕ) (a b : R) : Prop

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.checkMultiplicity
items.doc: Decidable check for multiplicity.
items.statement:
def checkMultiplicity [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (Q : CBivariate R) (r : ℕ) (a b : R) : Bool

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.shiftY_toPoly
items.doc: The outer (Y) shift corresponds to `Y ↦ Y + b` under `toPoly`.
items.statement:
theorem shiftY_toPoly [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (b : R) (Q : CBivariate R) :
    (shiftY b Q).toPoly = (Q.toPoly).comp (Polynomial.X + Polynomial.C (Polynomial.C b))

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.outerCoeff_shiftX
items.doc: Outer coefficient of the X-shift: Taylor-shift the j-th Y-coefficient.
items.statement:
theorem outerCoeff_shiftX [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (a : R) (P : CBivariate R) (j : ℕ) :
    CPolynomial.coeff (shiftX a P) j = CPolynomial.taylor a (CPolynomial.coeff P j)

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.shiftX_toPoly
items.doc: The inner (X) shift corresponds to `X ↦ X + a` under `toPoly`.
items.statement:
theorem shiftX_toPoly [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (a : R) (P : CBivariate R) :
    (shiftX a P).toPoly
      = (P.toPoly).map (Polynomial.compRingHom (Polynomial.X + Polynomial.C a))

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.shiftC_toPoly
items.doc: The computable shift agrees with `Polynomial.Bivariate.shift` under `toPoly`.
items.statement:
theorem shiftC_toPoly [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (a b : R) (Q : CBivariate R) :
    (shiftC a b Q).toPoly = Polynomial.Bivariate.shift Q.toPoly a b

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.eval_C_eq_evalY
items.doc: Evaluating the outer variable at the constant `C b` agrees with the Horner evaluator `evalY`.
items.statement:
theorem eval_C_eq_evalY [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R]
    (b : R) (Q : CBivariate R) :
    CPolynomial.eval (CPolynomial.C b) Q = evalY b Q

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.coeff_shiftC_zero_zero
items.doc: The (0,0) coefficient of the shift is evaluation at the point.
items.statement:
theorem coeff_shiftC_zero_zero [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (a b : R) (Q : CBivariate R) :
    CBivariate.coeff (shiftC a b Q) 0 0 = evalEval a b Q

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.hasMultiplicity_one_iff
items.doc: Multiplicity at least 1 is equivalent to vanishing at the point.
items.statement:
theorem hasMultiplicity_one_iff [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R]
    [DecidableEq R] (Q : CBivariate R) (a b : R) :
    hasMultiplicity Q 1 a b ↔ evalEval a b Q = 0

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.hasMultiplicity_iff_rootMultiplicity
items.doc:
`hasMultiplicity` agrees with the reference `Polynomial.Bivariate.rootMultiplicity`,
where `none` denotes infinite multiplicity (the zero polynomial).
items.statement:
theorem hasMultiplicity_iff_rootMultiplicity [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R]
    [DecidableEq R] (Q : CBivariate R) (r : ℕ) (a b : R) :
    hasMultiplicity Q r a b ↔
      ∀ m ∈ Polynomial.Bivariate.rootMultiplicity Q.toPoly a b, r ≤ m

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.hasMultiplicity_zero
items.doc: Every polynomial has multiplicity at least 0 at any point.
items.statement:
theorem hasMultiplicity_zero [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R]
    [DecidableEq R] (Q : CBivariate R) (a b : R) :
    hasMultiplicity Q 0 a b

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.hasMultiplicity_succ
items.doc: Multiplicity is monotone: higher multiplicity implies lower.
items.statement:
theorem hasMultiplicity_succ [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R]
    [DecidableEq R] (Q : CBivariate R) (r : ℕ) (a b : R) :
    hasMultiplicity Q (r + 1) a b → hasMultiplicity Q r a b

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.toPoly_injective
items.doc: `toPoly` is injective on canonical bivariate polynomials.
items.statement:
theorem toPoly_injective [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R]
    [DecidableEq R] {P Q : CBivariate R} (h : toPoly P = toPoly Q) : P = Q

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.shiftC_add
items.doc: The generic Taylor shift is additive.
items.statement:
theorem shiftC_add [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (a b : R) (P Q : CBivariate R) :
    shiftC a b (P + Q) = shiftC a b P + shiftC a b Q

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.shiftC_mul
items.doc: The generic Taylor shift is multiplicative.
items.statement:
theorem shiftC_mul [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R]
    [DecidableEq R] (a b : R) (P Q : CBivariate R) :
    shiftC a b (P * Q) = shiftC a b P * shiftC a b Q

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.hasMultiplicity_iff_check
items.doc: The decidable check agrees with the propositional multiplicity.
items.statement:
theorem hasMultiplicity_iff_check [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R]
    [DecidableEq R] (Q : CBivariate R) (r : ℕ) (a b : R) :
    hasMultiplicity Q r a b ↔ checkMultiplicity Q r a b = true

modules.title: Factorisation of Computable Bivariate Polynomials
modules.doc:
Defines `evalYPoly` (substitute `Y ↦ f(X)`), `isLinearYFactor` (test
divisibility by `Y - f(X)`), and `divByLinearY` (synthetic division of a
bivariate polynomial by the monic linear factor `Y - f(X)`).

`divByLinearY` is the computable factor theorem for the nested representation
`CBivariate R = CPolynomial (CPolynomial R)`: given a root `f(X)`, it deflates
`Q` by `Y - f(X)` over an arbitrary commutative ring. It is
the degree-one special case of monic Euclidean division; division by an
arbitrary monic divisor in `Y` is available generically through
`CPolynomial.divByMonic` / `CPolynomial.modByMonic` over the coefficient ring
`CPolynomial R` (see `CPolynomial.modByMonic_add_mul_divByMonic`).

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.evalYPoly
items.doc:
Substitute `Y ↦ f(X)` into a bivariate polynomial `Q`, i.e. evaluate `Q` at
`f` in the `Y` variable. The result is the univariate polynomial `Q(X, f(X))`.
items.statement:
def evalYPoly [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R]
    (f : CPolynomial R) (Q : CBivariate R) : CPolynomial R

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.isLinearYFactor
items.doc:
Decide whether `Y - f(X)` divides `Q`, i.e. whether `Q(X, f(X)) = 0`. By the
factor theorem this is exactly the test for `f(X)` being a `Y`-root of `Q`.
items.statement:
def isLinearYFactor [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (Q : CBivariate R) (f : CPolynomial R) : Bool

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.evalYPoly_zero
items.doc: `evalYPoly` sends the zero polynomial to `0`.
items.statement:
theorem evalYPoly_zero [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R]
    (f : CPolynomial R) :
    evalYPoly f (0 : CBivariate R) = 0

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.evalYPoly_add
items.doc: `evalYPoly` is additive in the polynomial being evaluated.
items.statement:
theorem evalYPoly_add [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R]
    (f : CPolynomial R) (P Q : CBivariate R) :
    evalYPoly f (P + Q) = evalYPoly f P + evalYPoly f Q

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.isLinearYFactor_iff
items.doc: The `isLinearYFactor` boolean test agrees with the proposition `Q(X, f(X)) = 0`.
items.statement:
theorem isLinearYFactor_iff [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (Q : CBivariate R) (f : CPolynomial R) :
    isLinearYFactor Q f = true ↔ evalYPoly f Q = 0

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.evalYPoly_toPoly
items.doc:
Bridge to Mathlib: evaluating `Q` at `f` and mapping to `Polynomial R` agrees
with evaluating the mapped `toPoly Q : R[X][Y]` at `f.toPoly`.
items.statement:
theorem evalYPoly_toPoly [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (f : CPolynomial R) (Q : CBivariate R) :
    (evalYPoly f Q).toPoly = (toPoly Q).eval (f.toPoly)

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.divByLinearY
items.doc:
Synthetic (Horner) division of a bivariate polynomial `Q` by the linear factor
`Y - f(X)`, performed in the `Y` variable. Returns the pair `(quotient, remainder)`
where the quotient is a `CBivariate R` and the remainder is a `CPolynomial R`.

Writing `Q = Σ_{j=0}^n aⱼ Yʲ` with `aⱼ = coeff Q j`, the quotient coefficients
`bⱼ` and the remainder `r` satisfy the synthetic-division recurrence
`b_{n-1} = aₙ`, `b_{j-1} = aⱼ + f · bⱼ`, `r = a₀ + f · b₀`, so that
`Q = quotient · (Y - f) + r`. See `divByLinearY_spec`.
items.statement:
def divByLinearY [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R]
    (Q : CBivariate R) (f : CPolynomial R) : CBivariate R × CPolynomial R

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.divByLinearY_const
items.statement:
theorem divByLinearY_const [CommRing R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R] (a f : CPolynomial R) :
  divByLinearY (CPolynomial.C a : CBivariate R) f = (0, a)

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.divByLinearY_zero
items.statement:
theorem divByLinearY_zero [CommRing R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R] (f : CPolynomial R) :
  divByLinearY (0 : CBivariate R) f = (0, 0)

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.divByLinearY_spec
items.doc:
Correctness of `divByLinearY`: in `R[X][Y]` the computed quotient and
remainder satisfy the Euclidean division identity
`Q = quotient · (Y - f) + remainder`, over any commutative ring.
items.statement:
theorem divByLinearY_spec [CommRing R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (Q : CBivariate R) (f : CPolynomial R) :
    let quot := (divByLinearY Q f).1
    let rem := (divByLinearY Q f).2
    toPoly Q = toPoly quot * (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C (f.toPoly)) +
        Polynomial.C (rem.toPoly)

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.divByLinearY_rem_eq_eval
items.doc:
The remainder of dividing `Q` by `Y - f` is the substitution `Q(X, f(X))`
(`evalYPoly f Q`), by the factor/remainder theorem.
items.statement:
theorem divByLinearY_rem_eq_eval [CommRing R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (Q : CBivariate R) (f : CPolynomial R) :
    (divByLinearY Q f).2 = evalYPoly f Q

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.divByLinearY_exact
items.doc:
If `Y - f` divides `Q` (`isLinearYFactor Q f`), the division is exact:
the remainder is `0`.
items.statement:
theorem divByLinearY_exact [CommRing R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (Q : CBivariate R) (f : CPolynomial R) (h : isLinearYFactor Q f = true) :
    (divByLinearY Q f).2 = 0

modules.title: Bridge: synthetic linear division equals general monic division
modules.doc:
Proves that the bespoke synthetic division `divByLinearY Q f` (Horner) coincides
with general monic Euclidean division of `Q` by the linear factor `Y - f`, using
the `CommRing`-general `CPolynomial.divByMonic` / `CPolynomial.modByMonic` at the
coefficient ring `CPolynomial R` (recall `CBivariate R = CPolynomial (CPolynomial R)`).

`divByLinearY_eq_divByMonic` shows the quotient equals `(divByLinearY Q f).1` and
the remainder equals `CPolynomial.C (divByLinearY Q f).2`, so `divByLinearY` is a
verified fast path for division by `Y - f`.

The proof works in the outer polynomial ring `(CPolynomial R)[Y]` (the image of
`CPolynomial.toPoly`): it rewrites the divisor as `X - C f`
(`linearYDivisor_toPoly`), establishes the Euclidean identity by transporting
`divByLinearY_spec` across the coefficient ring-equiv
(`divByLinearY_euclid_toPoly`), and concludes via
`Polynomial.div_modByMonic_unique`.

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.linearYDivisor
items.doc:
The linear monic divisor `Y - f`, as a bivariate polynomial
(`CBivariate R = CPolynomial (CPolynomial R)`).
items.statement:
def linearYDivisor [CommRing R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R]
    (f : CPolynomial R) : CBivariate R

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.linearYDivisor_toPoly
items.doc: `toPoly` sends the linear divisor `Y - f` to `X - C f` in `(CPolynomial R)[Y]`.
items.statement:
theorem linearYDivisor_toPoly [CommRing R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (f : CPolynomial R) :
    CPolynomial.toPoly (linearYDivisor f) = Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C f

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.linearYDivisor_monic
items.doc: The linear divisor `Y - f` is monic.
items.statement:
theorem linearYDivisor_monic [CommRing R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (f : CPolynomial R) :
    CPolynomial.monic (linearYDivisor f) = true

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.divByLinearY_euclid_toPoly
items.doc:
Euclidean identity for `divByLinearY` in the outer ring `(CPolynomial R)[Y]`:
`C rem + (Y - f) * quot = Q` after `toPoly`. Transports `divByLinearY_spec`
across the coefficient ring-equiv.
items.statement:
theorem divByLinearY_euclid_toPoly
    [CommRing R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (Q : CBivariate R) (f : CPolynomial R) :
    (CPolynomial.C (divByLinearY Q f).2).toPoly
        + CPolynomial.toPoly (linearYDivisor f) * CPolynomial.toPoly ((divByLinearY Q f).1)
      = CPolynomial.toPoly Q

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.divByLinearY_eq_divByMonic
items.doc:
The bespoke synthetic division `divByLinearY` agrees with general monic
division by `Y - f`: the quotient matches `divByMonic`, and the constant-in-`Y`
remainder `C (divByLinearY Q f).2` matches `modByMonic`.
items.statement:
theorem divByLinearY_eq_divByMonic [CommRing R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (Q : CBivariate R) (f : CPolynomial R) :
    CPolynomial.divByMonic Q (linearYDivisor f) = (divByLinearY Q f).1
      ∧ CPolynomial.modByMonic Q (linearYDivisor f)
          = CPolynomial.C (divByLinearY Q f).2

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.LinearKernelContext
items.doc:
A dense homogeneous linear-kernel backend.

The operation returns a nonzero kernel witness in the backend's chosen
normalization when it can find one. Completeness is stated in the negative form
needed by dense interpolation systems: if no witness is returned, no nonzero
homogeneous solution exists.
items.statement:
structure LinearKernelContext (F : Type*) [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F] where
  homogeneousWitness : DenseMatrix F → Option (Array F)
  witness_width :
    ∀ {M : DenseMatrix F} {v : Array F},
      homogeneousWitness M = some v →
        DenseMatrix.VectorWidth M v
  witness_sound :
    ∀ {M : DenseMatrix F} {v : Array F},
      DenseMatrix.WellFormed M →
        homogeneousWitness M = some v →
          DenseMatrix.IsHomogeneousSolution M v
  witness_nonzero :
    ∀ {M : DenseMatrix F} {v : Array F},
      homogeneousWitness M = some v →
        DenseMatrix.NonzeroVector v
  witness_complete :
    ∀ {M : DenseMatrix F},
      DenseMatrix.WellFormed M →
        homogeneousWitness M = none →
          ∀ v,
            DenseMatrix.VectorWidth M v →
              DenseMatrix.IsHomogeneousSolution M v →
                ¬ (DenseMatrix.NonzeroVector v)

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.denseLinearKernelContext
items.doc:
The dense Gaussian-elimination homogeneous-kernel backend.

The executable witness is computed by the in-place reduction
`DenseMatrix.homogeneousWitnessInPlace`, which mutates the matrix array instead of
copying it on every row operation. It returns the same witness as the copying
`DenseMatrix.homogeneousWitness` (`DenseMatrix.homogeneousWitnessInPlace_eq`), so the
backend contract is discharged by the copying-kernel correctness lemmas.
items.statement:
def denseLinearKernelContext (F : Type*) [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F] :
    LinearKernelContext F

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.GSInterpContext
items.doc:
Guruswami-Sudan-facing interpolation backend.

The backend packages the executable interpolation operation together with the
contract fields used by callers, using the explicit context style used by
univariate multiplication and remainder backends.
items.statement:
structure GSInterpContext (F : Type*) [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    [DecidableEq F] where
  interpolate : Array (Prod F F) → GSInterpParams → Option (CBivariate F)
  sound :
    ∀ points params Q,
      interpolate points params = some Q →
        ValidInterpolationWitness points params Q
  complete :
    ∀ points params,
      DistinctXCoordinates points →
      (exists Q, ValidInterpolationWitness points params Q) →
        exists Q, interpolate points params = some Q

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.FieldRootContext
items.doc:
Executable root finder for univariate field polynomials.

Completeness is only required for nonzero polynomials. A zero univariate
polynomial vanishes on every field element, so an unconditional array-valued
complete root finder would have to enumerate the whole field.
items.statement:
structure FieldRootContext (F : Type*) [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F] where
  rootsInField : CPolynomial F → Array F
  sound :
    ∀ p a,
      a ∈ (rootsInField p).toList →
        CPolynomial.eval a p = 0
  complete :
    ∀ p a,
      p ≠ 0 →
      CPolynomial.eval a p = 0 →
        a ∈ (rootsInField p).toList

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.GSRootContext
items.doc:
Guruswami-Sudan-facing bounded-degree root backend.

Completeness is only required for nonzero bivariate input. The zero bivariate
polynomial has every degree-bounded univariate polynomial as a root, which is not
a finite output contract for large fields.
items.statement:
structure GSRootContext (F : Type*) [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    [DecidableEq F] where
  rootsYDegreeLt : CBivariate F → Nat → Array (CPolynomial F)
  sound :
    ∀ Q k p,
      p ∈ (rootsYDegreeLt Q k).toList →
        degreeLt p k ∧ CBivariate.composeY Q p = 0
  complete :
    ∀ Q k p,
      Q ≠ 0 →
      degreeLt p k →
      CBivariate.composeY Q p = 0 →
        p ∈ (rootsYDegreeLt Q k).toList

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.composeY_eq_zero_of_enough_matching_multiplicity_points
items.doc:
If a bounded-degree candidate agrees with enough distinct packed
multiplicity-constrained points, it roots any valid interpolation witness.
items.statement:
theorem composeY_eq_zero_of_enough_matching_multiplicity_points {F : Type*}
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F] [DecidableEq F]
    {points : Array (Prod F F)} {params : GSInterpParams}
    {Q : CBivariate F} {p : CPolynomial F}
    (hQ : ValidInterpolationWitness points params Q)
    (hpdeg : degreeLt p params.messageDegree)
    (hdistinct : DistinctXCoordinates points)
    (hmatches :
      params.weightedDegreeBound <
        params.multiplicity * matchingPointCount points p) :
    CBivariate.composeY Q p = 0

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.GSFilteredCoreContext
items.doc:
Backend-parametric filtered core exposed as a reusable executable context.

The context packages an executable filtered decoder together with its CompPoly
soundness and completeness contracts.
items.statement:
structure GSFilteredCoreContext
    (F : Type*) [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F] [DecidableEq F] where
  run :
    Array (F × F) →
    GSInterpParams →
    Nat →
    Array (CPolynomial F)
  sound :
    ∀ {points params radius p},
      p ∈ (run points params radius).toList →
        ∃ Q,
          ValidInterpolationWitness points params Q ∧
            degreeLt p params.messageDegree ∧
              CBivariate.composeY Q p = 0 ∧
                candidateMismatchCount points p ≤ radius
  complete :
    ∀ {points params radius p},
      (∃ Q, ValidInterpolationWitness points params Q) →
      DistinctXCoordinates points →
      degreeLt p params.messageDegree →
      params.weightedDegreeBound <
        params.multiplicity * matchingPointCount points p →
      passesCandidateDistance points radius p = true →
        p ∈ (run points params radius).toList

ski-rental rent/buy break-even, set near the cost ratio between one
approximant-fallback solve and one reduction step. Both scale with the input
mass, so the ratio is proportional to `ℓ^(ω−1)` (with `ℓ + 1` the module
width) and independent of `n` and `m` under softly-linear multiplication;
the constant is calibrated from the `n = 5040` long-code benchmark shape.

modules.title: Executable Approximant-Basis Interpolation
modules.doc:
This backend constructs the GS diagonal modular equations, calls an explicit
solution-basis context, selects a least shifted-degree solution row, and
normalizes the resulting bivariate polynomial.

## References

* [Chowdhury, M. F. I., Jeannerod, C.-P., Neiger, V., Schost, E., and
    Villard, G., *Faster algorithms for multivariate interpolation with
    multiplicities and simultaneous polynomial approximations*][CJNSV15]

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.ApproximantBasis.gsModuli
items.doc:
GS column moduli `M_b = G^(s-b)`, for `b = 0, ..., s-1`, built by iterated
context multiplication so each power costs one fast product.
items.statement:

    Array (CPolynomial F)

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.ApproximantBasis.gsRelationEntry
items.doc:
Specification for one relation-matrix entry
`choose(j,b) * R^(j-b) mod M_b`, with zero below the triangular support.
This is the reference definition; the production path builds whole columns
incrementally with `gsRelationColumn`.
items.statement:
def gsRelationEntry (modCtx : CPolynomial.ModContext F)
    (R modulus : CPolynomial F) (j b : Nat) : CPolynomial F

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.ApproximantBasis.gsRelationColumn
items.doc:
One relation-matrix column, built by iterated multiply-and-reduce.  Entry
`j` of column `b` is `choose(j,b) * R^(j-b) mod M_b`; the reduced power of `R`
is carried across entries so each step costs one context multiplication of
operands already reduced below `deg M_b` plus one context remainder.
items.statement:
def gsRelationColumn (mulCtx : CPolynomial.MulContext F)
    (modCtx : CPolynomial.ModContext F)
    (R modulus : CPolynomial F) (width b : Nat) :
    Array (CPolynomial F)

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.ApproximantBasis.gsModularEquation_row_iff_multiplicity
items.doc:
The executable GS modular row predicate is equivalent to packed
multiplicity constraints for the bivariate coefficient-row view, for distinct
interpolation nodes and rows inside the interpolation width.
items.statement:
theorem gsModularEquation_row_iff_multiplicity
    (V : CPolynomial.VanishingPolynomialContext F)
    (E : CPolynomial.BatchEvalContext F)
    (modCtx : CPolynomial.ModContext F)
    (mulCtx : CPolynomial.MulContext F)
    (points : Array (F × F)) (params : GSInterpParams)
    (row : PolynomialRow F)
    (hdistinct : DistinctXCoordinates points)
    (hwidth : row.size ≤ interpolationWidth params) :
    let data := buildGSModularData V E mulCtx modCtx points params
    rowSatisfiesModularBool mulCtx modCtx row data.matrix data.moduli = true ↔
      CBivariate.satisfiesMultiplicityConstraintsBool
        (CBivariate.ofCoeffRow row) points params.multiplicity = true

modules.title: Executable GS Modular-Data Bridges
modules.doc:
Semantic characterizations of the executable approximant-basis modular data:
the modulus array `gsModuli`, the incrementally built binomial relation matrix
`gsRelationColumn` / `gsRelationMatrixWithModuli`, and the executable row
predicate `rowSatisfiesModularBool`.  The main result identifies the modular
row predicate over the GS data with divisibility of every sheared coefficient
`(hasseDeriv b Q.toPoly).eval R` by `G^(s-b)`.

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.ApproximantBasis.ofFn_rowGet
items.doc: Entry access for `PolynomialMatrix.ofFn`.
items.statement:
theorem ofFn_rowGet (rows width : Nat) (entry : Nat → Nat → CPolynomial F)
    {i j : Nat} (hi : i < rows) (hj : j < width) :
    rowGet ((PolynomialMatrix.ofFn rows width entry).getD i #[]) j = entry i j

items.doc: Row count of `PolynomialMatrix.ofFn`.
items.statement:
theorem ofFn_size (rows width : Nat) (entry : Nat → Nat → CPolynomial F) :
    (PolynomialMatrix.ofFn rows width entry).size = rows

items.doc: Width of `PolynomialMatrix.ofFn` with at least one row.
items.statement:
theorem ofFn_matrixWidth (rows width : Nat) (entry : Nat → Nat → CPolynomial F)
    (hrows : 0 < rows) :
    MatrixWidth (PolynomialMatrix.ofFn rows width entry) = width

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.ApproximantBasis.modByMonicWith_toPoly
items.doc: `modByMonicWith` computes the Mathlib monic remainder under `toPoly`.
items.statement:
theorem modByMonicWith_toPoly (modCtx : CPolynomial.ModContext F)
    {p M : CPolynomial F} (hM : Polynomial.Monic M.toPoly) :
    (PolynomialMatrix.modByMonicWith modCtx p M).toPoly = p.toPoly %ₘ M.toPoly

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.ApproximantBasis.dvd_modByMonicWith_sub
items.doc: `modByMonicWith` is congruent to the identity modulo the modulus.
items.statement:
theorem dvd_modByMonicWith_sub (modCtx : CPolynomial.ModContext F)
    {p M : CPolynomial F} (hM : Polynomial.Monic M.toPoly) :
    M.toPoly ∣ (PolynomialMatrix.modByMonicWith modCtx p M).toPoly - p.toPoly

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.ApproximantBasis.modByMonicWith_eq_zero_iff_dvd
items.doc: The executable remainder vanishes exactly on multiples of the modulus.
items.statement:
theorem modByMonicWith_eq_zero_iff_dvd (modCtx : CPolynomial.ModContext F)
    {p M : CPolynomial F} (hM : Polynomial.Monic M.toPoly) :
    PolynomialMatrix.modByMonicWith modCtx p M = 0 ↔ M.toPoly ∣ p.toPoly

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.ApproximantBasis.gsModuli_eq
items.doc: Closed form for the GS modulus array before reversal.
items.statement:
theorem gsModuli_eq (mulCtx : CPolynomial.MulContext F) (G : CPolynomial F) (s : Nat) :
    gsModuli mulCtx G s = (((List.range s).map fun i ↦ G ^ (i + 1)).toArray).reverse

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.ApproximantBasis.gsRelationColumn_getD_congr
items.doc: Entries of the GS relation column are congruent to the binomial powers.
items.statement:
theorem gsRelationColumn_getD_congr (mulCtx : CPolynomial.MulContext F)
    (modCtx : CPolynomial.ModContext F) {R modulus : CPolynomial F}
    (hM : Polynomial.Monic modulus.toPoly)
    {width b j : Nat} (hbj : b ≤ j) (hj : j < width) :
    modulus.toPoly ∣
      ((gsRelationColumn mulCtx modCtx R modulus width b).getD j 0).toPoly -
        Polynomial.C ((j.choose b : F)) * R.toPoly ^ (j - b)

theorem gsRelationMatrixWithModuli_entry (mulCtx : CPolynomial.MulContext F)

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.ApproximantBasis.hasseDeriv_toPoly_ofCoeffRow_eval
items.doc:
Sheared coefficients of a coefficient row: the outer Hasse derivative of
`ofCoeffRow row` evaluated at `R` is the binomial-weighted power sum.
items.statement:
theorem hasseDeriv_toPoly_ofCoeffRow_eval (row : PolynomialRow F)
    (R : Polynomial F) (b : Nat) :
    (Polynomial.hasseDeriv b (CBivariate.ofCoeffRow row).toPoly).eval R =
      ∑ k ∈ Finset.range row.size,
        Polynomial.C ((k.choose b : F)) * (row.getD k 0).toPoly * R ^ (k - b)

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.ApproximantBasis.rowMulMatrixWith_congr_of_agree
items.doc: The row-by-matrix product only sees the first `M.size` row entries.
items.statement:
theorem rowMulMatrixWith_congr_of_agree (mulCtx : CPolynomial.MulContext F)
    {row row' : PolynomialRow F} (M : PolynomialMatrix F)
    (hagree : ∀ k, k < M.size → rowGet row k = rowGet row' k) :
    rowMulMatrixWith mulCtx row M = rowMulMatrixWith mulCtx row' M

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.ApproximantBasis.rowSatisfiesModularBool_congr_of_agree
items.doc: The modular row predicate only sees the first `M.size` row entries.
items.statement:
theorem rowSatisfiesModularBool_congr_of_agree (mulCtx : CPolynomial.MulContext F)
    (modCtx : CPolynomial.ModContext F) {row row' : PolynomialRow F}
    (M : PolynomialMatrix F) (moduli : Array (CPolynomial F))
    (hagree : ∀ k, k < M.size → rowGet row k = rowGet row' k) :
    rowSatisfiesModularBool mulCtx modCtx row M moduli =
      rowSatisfiesModularBool mulCtx modCtx row' M moduli

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.ApproximantBasis.rowSatisfiesModularBool_gsRelationMatrix_iff
items.doc:
The executable GS modular row predicate over the relation matrix and
modulus array is exactly divisibility of every sheared coefficient
`(hasseDeriv b (ofCoeffRow row).toPoly).eval R` by `G^(s-b)`.
items.statement:
theorem rowSatisfiesModularBool_gsRelationMatrix_iff
    (mulCtx : CPolynomial.MulContext F) (modCtx : CPolynomial.ModContext F)
    {G : CPolynomial F} (hG : Polynomial.Monic G.toPoly)
    (R : CPolynomial F) (params : GSInterpParams) {row : PolynomialRow F}
    (hwidth : row.size ≤ interpolationWidth params) :
    rowSatisfiesModularBool mulCtx modCtx row
        (gsRelationMatrixWithRG mulCtx modCtx R G params)
        (gsModuli mulCtx G params.multiplicity) = true ↔
      ∀ b, b < params.multiplicity →
        G.toPoly ^ (params.multiplicity - b) ∣
          (Polynomial.hasseDeriv b (CBivariate.ofCoeffRow row).toPoly).eval R.toPoly

modules.title: Shear Equivalence for Guruswami-Sudan Multiplicity Constraints
modules.doc:
The approximant-basis backend reduces GS interpolation to diagonal modular
congruences on the `Z^b`-coefficients of the sheared polynomial `Q(X, R + Z)`.
This file proves the underlying semantic equivalence: for distinct
interpolation nodes, the packed multiplicity constraints on `Q` hold iff every
sheared coefficient `C_b = (hasseDeriv b Q.toPoly).eval R` is divisible by
`G^(s-b)`, where `G` is the vanishing polynomial of the nodes and `R`
interpolates the values.

The proof works one node at a time.  Writing `M_b = (hasseDeriv b Q.toPoly)`
for the outer `Y`-Hasse derivatives, multiplicity at `(x, y)` says that the
family `M_b.eval (C y)` is `(X - x)^(s-b)`-divisible, while the modular
congruence constrains the family `M_b.eval R`.  Because `R` and `C y` agree at
`x`, an outer Taylor expansion transfers each divisibility family to the
other; distinctness of the nodes then glues the per-node factors into powers
of `G`.

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.ApproximantBasis.X_sub_C_pow_dvd_iff_hasseDeriv_eval_eq_zero
items.doc:
`(X - x)^k` divides `A` iff the first `k` Hasse derivatives of `A` vanish
at `x`.
items.statement:
theorem X_sub_C_pow_dvd_iff_hasseDeriv_eval_eq_zero
    (A : Polynomial F) (x : F) (k : Nat) :
    (X - C x) ^ k ∣ A ↔
      ∀ a, a < k → (Polynomial.hasseDeriv a A).eval x = 0

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.ApproximantBasis.X_sub_C_pow_dvd_hasseDeriv_eval_of_dvd_sub
items.doc:
Shear-transfer core: the `(X - x)`-adic divisibility family of the outer
Hasse-derivative evaluations of `P` moves between outer evaluation points `u`
and `v` that agree modulo `X - x`.
items.statement:
theorem X_sub_C_pow_dvd_hasseDeriv_eval_of_dvd_sub
    {P : Polynomial (Polynomial F)} {u v : Polynomial F} {x : F} {s : Nat}
    (huv : (X - C x) ∣ (v - u))
    (h : ∀ b, b < s →
      (X - C x) ^ (s - b) ∣ (Polynomial.hasseDeriv b P).eval u)
    {b : Nat} (hb : b < s) :
    (X - C x) ^ (s - b) ∣ (Polynomial.hasseDeriv b P).eval v

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.ApproximantBasis.X_sub_C_pow_dvd_hasseDeriv_eval_iff_hasMultiplicity
items.doc:
At a single node `(x, y)` with `R(x) = y`, the `(X - x)`-adic divisibility
family of the sheared coefficients `(hasseDeriv b Q.toPoly).eval R` is
equivalent to GS multiplicity of `Q` at the node.
items.statement:
theorem X_sub_C_pow_dvd_hasseDeriv_eval_iff_hasMultiplicity
    {Q : CBivariate F} {R : Polynomial F} {x y : F} {s : Nat}
    (hRx : R.eval x = y) :
    (∀ b, b < s →
      (X - C x) ^ (s - b) ∣ (Polynomial.hasseDeriv b Q.toPoly).eval R) ↔
      CBivariate.hasMultiplicity Q s x y

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.ApproximantBasis.linearFactor_toPoly_eq
items.doc: The linear factor of one node under `toPoly`.
items.statement:

    (CPolynomial.linearFactor x).toPoly = (X - C x : Polynomial F)

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.ApproximantBasis.vanishingPolynomialArray_toPoly
items.doc:
The array vanishing polynomial is the product of the node linear factors
under `toPoly`.
items.statement:
theorem vanishingPolynomialArray_toPoly (xs : Array F) :
    (CPolynomial.vanishingPolynomialArray xs).toPoly =
      (((xs.toList : Multiset F).map fun x ↦
        (X - C x : Polynomial F))).prod

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.ApproximantBasis.vanishingPolynomialArray_toPoly_monic
items.doc:
The array vanishing polynomial is monic over the underlying `toPoly`
image.

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.ApproximantBasis.prod_X_sub_C_pow_dvd_of_nodup
items.doc:
Per-node `(X - x)^k` divisibility glues to divisibility by the `k`-th
power of the product of distinct linear factors.
items.statement:
theorem prod_X_sub_C_pow_dvd_of_nodup
    {A : Polynomial F} {xs : List F} {k : Nat}
    (hA : A ≠ 0) (hnodup : xs.Nodup)
    (hroot : ∀ x, x ∈ xs → (X - C x) ^ k ∣ A) :
    (((xs : Multiset F).map fun x ↦ (X - C x : Polynomial F)).prod) ^ k ∣ A

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.ApproximantBasis.vanishing_pow_dvd_hasseDeriv_eval_iff_satisfiesMultiplicityConstraints
items.doc:
Batch shear equivalence: over distinct nodes, divisibility of every
sheared coefficient `C_b` by `G^(s-b)` is equivalent to the packed GS
multiplicity constraints.
items.statement:
theorem vanishing_pow_dvd_hasseDeriv_eval_iff_satisfiesMultiplicityConstraints
    {points : Array (F × F)} {Q : CBivariate F} {R : CPolynomial F} {s : Nat}
    (hdistinct : DistinctXCoordinates points)
    (hR : ∀ point, point ∈ points.toList → CPolynomial.eval point.1 R = point.2) :
    (∀ b, b < s →
      (CPolynomial.vanishingPolynomialArray (points.map fun p ↦ p.1)).toPoly ^ (s - b) ∣
        (Polynomial.hasseDeriv b Q.toPoly).eval R.toPoly) ↔
      CBivariate.SatisfiesMultiplicityConstraints Q points s

modules.title: Dense Guruswami-Sudan Interpolation
modules.doc:
Executable interpolation backend for the Guruswami-Sudan decoder [GS99]. For
positive `Y` weight, it builds a Hasse-constraint matrix, computes one
homogeneous-kernel witness, and normalizes it. For low message degree, it returns
an explicit product witness.

## References

* [Guruswami, V., and Sudan, M., *Improved decoding of Reed-Solomon and
    algebraic-geometry codes*][GS99]

modules.title: Hybrid Guruswami-Sudan Interpolation
modules.doc:
Output-sensitive interpolation backend combining the adaptive Lee-O'Sullivan
route with the order-driven approximant-basis route through a ski-rental
budget policy.

The Mulders-Storjohann reduction of the Lee-O'Sullivan basis terminates after
a number of steps that vanishes on codewords and scales with the distance of
the received word from the code, while the approximant-basis backend costs
the same on every input. The hybrid runs the reduction with a calibrated step
budget `B` as fuel; if the budget is exhausted before the basis is
conflict-free, it falls back to the approximant solver, so the total cost is
within a constant factor of the cheaper route on every input.

The budget is the entire fuel policy: the reduction loop stops by itself as
soon as the basis is conflict-free, so unused fuel is free and any cap below
`B` could only trigger premature fallback. (In particular the excess of the
initial shifted-degree sum over the weak-Popov floor is *not* a usable cap:
the step count includes leading-position moves that leave the shifted-degree
sum unchanged, so reductions routinely need more steps than that excess.)

The dispatch affects performance only: both branches are complete verified
interpolators, and `Interpolation/Hybrid/Correctness.lean` shows the hybrid
result always coincides with one of them.

## References

* [Karlin, A. R., Manasse, M. S., Rudolph, L., and Sleator, D. D.,
    *Competitive snoopy caching*][KMRS88]

modules.title: Correctness of Hybrid Guruswami-Sudan Interpolation
modules.doc:
The hybrid's fuel/fallback dispatch affects performance only: its result
always coincides with the result of one of the two verified backends
(`hybridPositiveInterpolate_eq_lee_or_approximant`). Soundness and
completeness of `hybridInterpContext` follow by case analysis from the
corresponding backend theorems.

The only reduction-level fact needed is determinism of the fueled
Mulders-Storjohann loop (`muldersStorjohannReduceWithFuel_eq_of_no_conflict`):
when the budgeted probe ends without a shifted leading conflict, it stopped at
the same matrix as the full reduction, so the kept Lee branch is literally the
Lee-O'Sullivan backend run with the fast reducer context.

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.Hybrid.hybridPositiveInterpolate_eq_lee_or_approximant
items.doc:
The hybrid branch result always coincides with one of the two verified
backends.
items.statement:
theorem hybridPositiveInterpolate_eq_lee_or_approximant
    (V : CPolynomial.VanishingPolynomialContext F)
    (E : CPolynomial.BatchEvalContext F)
    (solver : ModularSolutionBasisContext F)
    (budget : GSInterpParams → Nat)
    (points : Array (F × F)) (params : GSInterpParams) :
    hybridPositiveInterpolate V E solver budget points params =
        LeeOSullivan.leeOSullivanPositiveInterpolate V E
          (muldersStorjohannFastReducerContext F) points params ∨
      hybridPositiveInterpolate V E solver budget points params =
        ApproximantBasis.approximantBasisPositiveInterpolate V E solver
          points params

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.Hybrid.hybridInterpolate_eq_lee_or_approximant
items.doc:
The hybrid result always coincides with one of the two verified
backends.
items.statement:
theorem hybridInterpolate_eq_lee_or_approximant
    (V : CPolynomial.VanishingPolynomialContext F)
    (E : CPolynomial.BatchEvalContext F)
    (solver : ModularSolutionBasisContext F)
    (budget : GSInterpParams → Nat)
    (points : Array (F × F)) (params : GSInterpParams) :
    hybridInterpolate V E solver budget points params =
        LeeOSullivan.leeOSullivanInterpolate V E
          (muldersStorjohannFastReducerContext F) points params ∨
      hybridInterpolate V E solver budget points params =
        ApproximantBasis.approximantBasisInterpolate V E solver points params

theorem coeff_neg {R : Type*}

    [Ring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R]
    (P Q : CBivariate R) (i j : Nat) :
    coeff (P - Q) i j = coeff P i j - coeff Q i j

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.hasseDerivative_sub

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.hasseDerivative_CC_mul

theorem hasseDerivativeEval_CC_mul {F : Type*}

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.hasseDerivativeEval_sub

theorem hasseDerivativeEval_sub {F : Type*}

    (a b : Nat) (x y : F) (P Q : CBivariate F) :
    hasseDerivativeEval a b x y (P - Q) =
      hasseDerivativeEval a b x y P - hasseDerivativeEval a b x y Q

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.hasseDerivativeEval_X_mul_zero_xOrder
items.statement:
theorem hasseDerivativeEval_X_mul_zero_xOrder {F : Type*}
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F] [DecidableEq F]
    (b : Nat) (x y : F) (Q : CBivariate F) :
    hasseDerivativeEval 0 b x y (X * Q) =

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.hasseDerivativeEval_X_mul_succ_xOrder
items.statement:
theorem hasseDerivativeEval_X_mul_succ_xOrder {F : Type*}
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F] [DecidableEq F]
    (a b : Nat) (x y : F) (Q : CBivariate F) :
    hasseDerivativeEval (a + 1) b x y (X * Q) =

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.hasseDerivativeEval_ofYConstant_mul_eq_eval_mul_of_lower
items.statement:
theorem hasseDerivativeEval_ofYConstant_mul_eq_eval_mul_of_lower {F : Type*}
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F] [DecidableEq F]
    (x y : F) (b : Nat) :
    ∀ (A : CPolynomial F) (P : CBivariate F) (order : Nat),
      (∀ a, a < order → CBivariate.hasseDerivativeEval a b x y P = 0) →
        CBivariate.hasseDerivativeEval order b x y
            (CBivariate.ofYConstant A * P) =
          CPolynomial.eval x A * CBivariate.hasseDerivativeEval order b x y P

    (hLower : ∀ a, a ≤ order →
      CBivariate.hasseDerivativeEval a b x y P = 0) :
    CBivariate.hasseDerivativeEval order b x y (CBivariate.ofYConstant A * P) = 0

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.foldl_add_congr_terms
items.statement:
theorem foldl_add_congr_terms {α : Type*} [Add α]
    (xs : List Nat) (f g : Nat → α) (z : α)
    (h : ∀ x, x ∈ xs → f x = g x) :
    xs.foldl (fun out x ↦ out + f x) z =
      xs.foldl (fun out x ↦ out + g x) z

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.foldl_add_distrib_terms_aux
items.statement:
theorem foldl_add_distrib_terms_aux {α : Type*} [AddCommMonoid α]
    (xs : List Nat) (f g : Nat → α) (a b : α) :
    xs.foldl (fun out x ↦ out + (f x + g x)) (a + b) =
      xs.foldl (fun out x ↦ out + f x) a +
        xs.foldl (fun out x ↦ out + g x) b

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.foldl_add_distrib_terms
items.statement:
theorem foldl_add_distrib_terms {α : Type*} [AddCommMonoid α]
    (xs : List Nat) (f g : Nat → α) :
    xs.foldl (fun out x ↦ out + (f x + g x)) 0 =
      xs.foldl (fun out x ↦ out + f x) 0 +
        xs.foldl (fun out x ↦ out + g x) 0

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.foldl_add_single_beq_of_not_mem
items.statement:
theorem foldl_add_single_beq_of_not_mem {α : Type*} [AddCommMonoid α]
    (xs : List Nat) (target : Nat) (term acc : α)
    (hnot : target ∉ xs) :
    xs.foldl (fun out idx ↦ out + if idx == target then term else 0) acc =
      acc

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.foldl_add_single_beq_of_nodup_mem
items.statement:
theorem foldl_add_single_beq_of_nodup_mem {α : Type*} [AddCommMonoid α]
    (xs : List Nat) (target : Nat) (term : α)
    (hnodup : xs.Nodup) (hmem : target ∈ xs) :
    xs.foldl (fun out idx ↦ out + if idx == target then term else 0) 0 =
      term

CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.koetterBasisCombination_eq_zero_of_weights_zero
items.statement:
theorem koetterBasisCombination_eq_zero_of_weights_zero {F : Type*}
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F] [DecidableEq F]
    (weights : Nat → CPolynomial F) (basis : Array (CBivariate F))
    (hzero : ∀ idx, idx < basis.size → weights idx = 0) :
    koetterBasisCombination weights basis = 0

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.coeff_koetterBasisCombination
items.statement:
theorem coeff_koetterBasisCombination {F : Type*}
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F] [DecidableEq F]
    (weights : Nat → CPolynomial F) (basis : Array (CBivariate F))
    (i j : Nat) :
    CBivariate.coeff (koetterBasisCombination weights basis) i j =
      (List.range basis.size).foldl
        (fun out idx ↦
          out + CBivariate.coeff
            (CBivariate.ofYConstant (weights idx) * basis.getD idx 0) i j)
        0

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.LeeOSullivan.leeCoefficientForm_eval_point
items.doc: The coefficient-form `R` used by Lee evaluates to the packed values at distinct nodes.

theorem leeCoefficientForm_eval_point
    (V : CPolynomial.VanishingPolynomialContext F)

    {point : F × F} (hpoint : point ∈ points.toList) :
    CPolynomial.eval point.1
      (CPolynomial.interpolateCoefficientForm V E points) =
      point.2

modules.title: Lee-O'Sullivan Interpolation Completeness

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.LeeOSullivan.leeOSullivanPositiveInterpolate_complete_of_row
items.statement:
theorem leeOSullivanPositiveInterpolate_complete_of_row
    (V : CPolynomial.VanishingPolynomialContext F)
    (E : CPolynomial.BatchEvalContext F)
    (reducer : ShiftedRowReducerContext F)
    {points : Array (F × F)} {params : GSInterpParams}
    (hdistinct : DistinctXCoordinates points)
    (hHigh : ¬ params.messageDegree ≤ 1)
    {row : PolynomialRow F} {rowDegree : Nat}
    (hrowSpan :
      row ∈ RowSpan
        (leeOSullivanBasisRowsWithRG
          (CPolynomial.interpolateCoefficientFormWithVanishing E
            (V.vanishingPolynomial (points.map fun point ↦ point.1)) points)
          (V.vanishingPolynomial (points.map fun point ↦ point.1)) params))
    (hrowDegree :
      rowShiftedDegree? row (leeOSullivanShifts params) = some rowDegree)
    (hrowBound : rowDegree ≤ params.weightedDegreeBound) :
    ∃ Q, leeOSullivanPositiveInterpolate V E reducer points params = some Q

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.LeeOSullivan.leeOSullivanPositiveInterpolate_complete_of_span

    (reducer : ShiftedRowReducerContext F)
    {points : Array (F × F)} {params : GSInterpParams} {Q : CBivariate F}
    (hdistinct : DistinctXCoordinates points)
    (hHigh : ¬ params.messageDegree ≤ 1)
    (hQ : ValidInterpolationWitness points params Q)
    (hspan :
      koetterBasisSpanContains
        (leeOSullivanBasisPolynomials (F := F)
          (CPolynomial.interpolateCoefficientFormWithVanishing E
            (V.vanishingPolynomial (points.map fun point ↦ point.1)) points)
          (V.vanishingPolynomial (points.map fun point ↦ point.1)) params) Q) :
    ∃ Q, leeOSullivanPositiveInterpolate V E reducer points params = some Q

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.LeeOSullivan.coeffY_dvd_vanishingPolynomial_pow_of_multiplicity
items.statement:
theorem coeffY_dvd_vanishingPolynomial_pow_of_multiplicity
    (V : CPolynomial.VanishingPolynomialContext F)
    {points : Array (F × F)} {P : CBivariate F} {m n : Nat}
    (hdistinct : DistinctXCoordinates points)
    (hn : n < m)
    (hY : ∀ j, n < j → P.val.coeff j = 0)
    (hmult : CBivariate.SatisfiesMultiplicityConstraints P points m) :
    ∃ W : CPolynomial F,
      P.val.coeff n =
        W * (V.vanishingPolynomial (points.map fun point ↦ point.1)) ^ (m - n)

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.LeeOSullivan.normalizeLeeCandidate?_sound_of_raw
items.doc:
Normalizing a bounded raw Lee candidate preserves the interpolation witness
contract when the raw candidate already satisfies the multiplicity constraints.
items.statement:
theorem normalizeLeeCandidate?_sound_of_raw
    {points : Array (F × F)} {params : GSInterpParams}
    {rawQ Q : CBivariate F}

      CBivariate.natWeightedDegree rawQ 1 (yWeight params) ≤
        params.weightedDegreeBound)
    (hmult :
      CBivariate.SatisfiesMultiplicityConstraints rawQ points params.multiplicity)

    ValidInterpolationWitness points params Q

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.LeeOSullivan.coeff_ofCoeffRow_rowLinearCombination_lee_of_lt
items.doc:
Within the Lee row width, a row-linear combination of executable Lee rows
has the same coefficients as the corresponding bivariate basis combination.
items.statement:
theorem coeff_ofCoeffRow_rowLinearCombination_lee_of_lt
    (R G : CPolynomial F) (params : GSInterpParams)
    (coeffs : Array (CPolynomial F)) {k j : Nat}
    (hj : j < leeOSullivanWidth params) :
    CBivariate.coeff
        (CBivariate.ofCoeffRow
          (rowLinearCombination coeffs
            (leeOSullivanBasisRowsWithRG R G params))) k j =
      CBivariate.coeff

          (leeOSullivanBasisPolynomials (F := F) R G params)) k j
