modules.title: Divisibility-Based Interpolation Witness Checking
modules.doc:
A fast full recognizer for the Guruswami-Sudan multiplicity constraints.

The pointwise check (`CBivariate.satisfiesMultiplicityConstraintsBool`)
evaluates every Hasse derivative of order below `m` at every interpolation
point, costing `O(n * m^2 * terms(Q))` field operations. For point sets with
distinct `x`-coordinates the same property has a module-theoretic
characterization: writing `Q = Σ_t c_t * (Y - R)^t` for the base-`(Y - R)`
expansion of `Q`, where `R` interpolates the points, `Q` has a zero of
multiplicity at least `m` at every point if and only if
`G^(m - t) ∣ c_t` for all `t < m`, with `G = Π_i (X - x_i)` the vanishing
polynomial of the `x`-coordinates.

`satisfiesMultiplicityConstraintsViaDivisibilityBool` checks the right-hand
side directly: it peels `m` digits off `Q` by synthetic division by `Y - R`
and tests each digit for divisibility by the corresponding power of `G` with
a monic remainder. With NTT-backed multiplication and remainder contexts the
whole check is quasi-linear in the input size, with no per-point loop.

`interpolationWitnessIsValidViaDivisibilityBool` combines the divisibility
check with the nonzero and weighted-degree witness conditions, mirroring
`interpolationWitnessIsValidBool`.

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.divByLinearYWith
items.doc:
`divByLinearY` with the inner univariate products supplied by an explicit
multiplication context, for callers that want NTT-backed Horner steps.
items.statement:
def divByLinearYWith {R : Type*} [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R]
    (M : CPolynomial.MulContext R) (Q : CBivariate R) (f : CPolynomial R) :
    CBivariate R × CPolynomial R

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.divByLinearYWith_eq_divByLinearY
items.doc: The context-parametric synthetic division agrees with `divByLinearY`.
items.statement:
theorem divByLinearYWith_eq_divByLinearY {R : Type*}
    [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R]
    (M : CPolynomial.MulContext R) (Q : CBivariate R) (f : CPolynomial R) :
    divByLinearYWith M Q f = divByLinearY Q f

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.satisfiesMultiplicityConstraintsViaDivisibilityBool
items.doc:
Divisibility form of the multiplicity constraints: the digit `c_t` of the
base-`(Y - R)` expansion of `Q` must be divisible by `G^(m - t)` for every
`t < m`. The recursion peels one digit per step by synthetic division, so the
step at recursion depth `t` checks `G^(m - t) ∣ c_t` on the running quotient.

For `G` the vanishing polynomial of the (distinct) `x`-coordinates of a point
set and `R` its interpolant, this is equivalent to
`CBivariate.satisfiesMultiplicityConstraintsBool` on the same point set; see
`satisfiesMultiplicityConstraintsViaDivisibilityBool_eq`.
items.statement:
def satisfiesMultiplicityConstraintsViaDivisibilityBool {F : Type*}
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (Mul : CPolynomial.MulContext F) (Mod : CPolynomial.ModContext F)
    (G R : CPolynomial F) : Nat → CBivariate F → Bool

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.interpolationWitnessIsValidViaDivisibilityBool
items.doc:
Divisibility-based recognizer for the semantic interpolation witness
contract, agreeing with `interpolationWitnessIsValidBool` on point sets with
distinct `x`-coordinates but avoiding its per-point Hasse derivative loop.
items.statement:
def interpolationWitnessIsValidViaDivisibilityBool {F : Type*}
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F] [DecidableEq F]
    (V : CPolynomial.VanishingPolynomialContext F)
    (E : CPolynomial.BatchEvalContext F)
    (Mul : CPolynomial.MulContext F) (Mod : CPolynomial.ModContext F)
    (points : Array (F × F)) (params : GSInterpParams) (Q : CBivariate F) : Bool

modules.title: Correctness of Divisibility-Based Witness Checking
modules.doc:
`satisfiesMultiplicityConstraintsViaDivisibilityBool` agrees with the
pointwise Hasse checker `CBivariate.satisfiesMultiplicityConstraintsBool`
on point sets with distinct `x`-coordinates, and consequently
`interpolationWitnessIsValidViaDivisibilityBool` agrees with
`interpolationWitnessIsValidBool`.

The proof peels one base-`(Y - R)` digit per multiplicity level.

* Soundness: from `Q = C c + (Y - R) * Q'` with `c = W * G^(m+1)`, the digit
  term gains multiplicity `m + 1` from the `G`-power
  (`hasMultiplicityAtLeast_ofYConstant_pow_mul_eval_zero`), the quotient term
  gains one from `Y - R` (`hasMultiplicityAtLeast_linearYDivisor_mul`) on top
  of the inductive hypothesis, and multiplicity is closed under addition.

* Completeness: the quotient `Q'` keeps multiplicity `m` at every point
  (`witness_hasMultiplicity_quot`, by a strong induction on the
  `X`-coefficients of the Taylor-shifted division identity), so the digit
  `C c = Q - (Y - R) * Q'` has multiplicity `m + 1` with `Y`-degree zero, and
  `coeffY_dvd_vanishingPolynomial_pow_of_multiplicity` forces
  `G^(m+1) ∣ c`.

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.satisfiesMultiplicityConstraintsViaDivisibilityBool_eq
items.doc:
The divisibility-based multiplicity checker agrees with the pointwise
Hasse checker on point sets with distinct `x`-coordinates.
items.statement:
theorem satisfiesMultiplicityConstraintsViaDivisibilityBool_eq
    (Mul : CPolynomial.MulContext F) (Mod : CPolynomial.ModContext F)
    {points : Array (F × F)} (R : CPolynomial F)
    (hdistinct : DistinctXCoordinates points)
    (hR : ∀ point, point ∈ points.toList → CPolynomial.eval point.1 R = point.2)
    (m : Nat) (Q : CBivariate F) :
    satisfiesMultiplicityConstraintsViaDivisibilityBool Mul Mod
        (CPolynomial.vanishingPolynomialArray (points.map fun p ↦ p.1)) R m Q =
      CBivariate.satisfiesMultiplicityConstraintsBool Q points m

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.interpolationWitnessIsValidViaDivisibilityBool_eq
items.doc:
The divisibility-based witness recognizer agrees with
`interpolationWitnessIsValidBool` on point sets with distinct
`x`-coordinates.
items.statement:
theorem interpolationWitnessIsValidViaDivisibilityBool_eq
    (V : CPolynomial.VanishingPolynomialContext F)
    (E : CPolynomial.BatchEvalContext F)
    (Mul : CPolynomial.MulContext F) (Mod : CPolynomial.ModContext F)
    {points : Array (F × F)} (params : GSInterpParams)
    (hdistinct : DistinctXCoordinates points) (Q : CBivariate F) :
    interpolationWitnessIsValidViaDivisibilityBool V E Mul Mod points params Q =
      interpolationWitnessIsValidBool points params Q

items.doc: Reading an in-bounds entry from a matrix constructed by `ofFn` returns that entry.

    {row col : Nat} (hrow : row < rows) (hcol : col < cols) :
    (ofFn rows cols f).get row col = f row col

items.name: CompPoly.DenseMatrix.foldl_range_one_special
items.doc: Fold over a range with one distinguished nonzero entry.
items.statement:
theorem foldl_range_one_special {F : Type*} [AddCommMonoid F] {pivot : Nat} (x : F) :
    ∀ start len (init : F),
    (List.range' start len).foldl (fun acc j ↦ acc + if j = pivot then x else 0) init =
      init + if start ≤ pivot ∧ pivot < start + len then x else 0

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.ofMonomialCoeffs_coeff
items.doc:
Coefficients of a polynomial assembled from a monomial array are the folded
sum of matching monomial coefficients.
items.statement:
theorem ofMonomialCoeffs_coeff {R : Type*}
    [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (monomials : Array Monomial) (coeffs : Array R) (i j : Nat) :
    coeff (ofMonomialCoeffs monomials coeffs) i j =
      (List.range' 0 monomials.size).foldl
        (fun acc col ↦
          let monomial := monomials.getD col ⟨0, 0⟩
          acc + if i = monomial.xDegree ∧ j = monomial.yDegree then coeffs.getD col 0
            else 0)
        0

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.monomialsWeightedDegreeLE_sound
items.doc: All returned weighted-degree monomials satisfy the requested bound.
items.statement:
theorem monomialsWeightedDegreeLE_sound
    {xWeight yWeight bound : Nat} {m : Monomial}
    (hm : m ∈ (monomialsWeightedDegreeLE xWeight yWeight bound).toList) :
    xWeight * m.xDegree + yWeight * m.yDegree ≤ bound

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.ofMonomialCoeffs_coeff_getD
items.doc:
For a nodup monomial array, the assembled polynomial recovers the matching
coefficient at each listed monomial.
items.statement:
theorem ofMonomialCoeffs_coeff_getD {R : Type*}
    [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    {monomials : Array Monomial} {coeffs : Array R}
    (hnodup : monomials.toList.Nodup) {k : Nat} (hk : k < monomials.size) :
    coeff (ofMonomialCoeffs monomials coeffs)
        (monomials.getD k ⟨0, 0⟩).xDegree (monomials.getD k ⟨0, 0⟩).yDegree =
      coeffs.getD k 0

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.ofMonomialCoeffs_ne_zero_of_coeff_getD_ne_zero
items.doc:

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.natWeightedDegree_le_of_coeff_zero
items.doc:
If all coefficients above a weighted-degree bound are zero, the executable
weighted degree is below that bound.
items.statement:
theorem natWeightedDegree_le_of_coeff_zero {R : Type*} [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (f : CBivariate R) (u v bound : Nat)
    (hzero : ∀ i j, bound < u * i + v * j → coeff f i j = 0) :
    natWeightedDegree f u v ≤ bound

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.ofMonomialCoeffs_coeff_eq_zero_of_weight_gt
items.doc:
Coefficients above a bound are zero for a polynomial assembled from monomials
all below that bound.
items.statement:
theorem ofMonomialCoeffs_coeff_eq_zero_of_weight_gt {R : Type*}
    [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    {monomials : Array Monomial} {coeffs : Array R} {u v bound i j : Nat}
    (hall : ∀ monomial, monomial ∈ monomials.toList →
      u * monomial.xDegree + v * monomial.yDegree ≤ bound)
    (hgt : bound < u * i + v * j) :
    coeff (ofMonomialCoeffs monomials coeffs) i j = 0

A polynomial assembled from bounded monomials has weighted degree below the

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.hasseDerivativeFromTerms_coeff
items.doc:
Coefficients of a polynomial materialized from Hasse terms are the folded
sum of matching term coefficients.
items.statement:
theorem hasseDerivativeFromTerms_coeff {R : Type*}
    [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (terms : List (HasseTerm R)) (i j : Nat) :
    coeff (hasseDerivativeFromTerms terms) i j =
      terms.foldl
        (fun acc term ↦ acc + if i = term.xDegree ∧ j = term.yDegree then term.coeff else 0)
        0

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.hasseDerivativeEvalFromTerms_append_single
items.doc: Evaluating after appending one Hasse term adds that term's contribution.
items.statement:
theorem hasseDerivativeEvalFromTerms_append_single {R : Type*} [Semiring R]
    (terms : List (HasseTerm R)) (term : HasseTerm R) (x y : R) :
    hasseDerivativeEvalFromTerms (terms ++ [term]) x y =
      hasseDerivativeEvalFromTerms terms x y +
        term.coeff * x ^ term.xDegree * y ^ term.yDegree

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.hasseDerivativeTermList_coeff_fold
items.doc:
The fixed coefficient of the executable Hasse term list is the matching
coefficient fold over the same degree ranges.
items.statement:
theorem hasseDerivativeTermList_coeff_fold {R : Type*} [Semiring R]
    (a b i j : Nat) (Q : CBivariate R) :
    (hasseDerivativeTermList a b Q).foldl
        (fun acc term ↦ acc + if i = term.xDegree ∧ j = term.yDegree then term.coeff else 0)
        0 =
      (List.range' 0 Q.val.size).foldl
        (fun acc yDeg ↦
          let coeffY := Q.val.coeff yDeg
          if b ≤ yDeg then
            (List.range' 0 coeffY.val.size).foldl
              (fun acc xDeg ↦
                if a ≤ xDeg then
                  acc +
                    if i = xDeg - a ∧ j = yDeg - b then
                      (Nat.choose xDeg a : R) * (Nat.choose yDeg b : R) * coeffY.coeff xDeg
                    else 0
                else acc)
              acc
          else acc)
        0

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.hasseDerivativeTermList_coeff_inner_fold
items.doc: Collapse the inner `x`-fold in a fixed Hasse coefficient calculation.
items.statement:
theorem hasseDerivativeTermList_coeff_inner_fold {R : Type*} [Semiring R]
    (a b i j yDeg : Nat) (coeffY : CPolynomial R) (acc : R) (hy : b ≤ yDeg) :
    (List.range' 0 coeffY.val.size).foldl
        (fun acc xDeg ↦
          if a ≤ xDeg then
            acc +
              if i = xDeg - a ∧ j = yDeg - b then
                (Nat.choose xDeg a : R) * (Nat.choose yDeg b : R) * coeffY.coeff xDeg
              else 0
          else acc)
        acc =
      acc +
        if yDeg = j + b ∧ i + a < coeffY.val.size then
          (Nat.choose (i + a) a : R) * (Nat.choose yDeg b : R) * coeffY.coeff (i + a)
        else 0

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.hasseDerivativeTermList_coeff_value
items.doc:
The fixed coefficient of the executable Hasse term list has the closed
coefficient-shift formula.
items.statement:
theorem hasseDerivativeTermList_coeff_value {R : Type*} [Semiring R]
    (a b i j : Nat) (Q : CBivariate R) :
    (hasseDerivativeTermList a b Q).foldl
        (fun acc term ↦ acc + if i = term.xDegree ∧ j = term.yDegree then term.coeff else 0)
        0 =
      (Nat.choose (i + a) a : R) * (Nat.choose (j + b) b : R) *
        coeff Q (i + a) (j + b)

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.hasseDerivative_coeff
items.doc:
Coefficients of the executable Hasse derivative are shifted source
coefficients scaled by the corresponding binomial factors.
items.statement:
theorem hasseDerivative_coeff {R : Type*}
    [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (a b i j : Nat) (Q : CBivariate R) :
    coeff (hasseDerivative a b Q) i j =
      (Nat.choose (i + a) a : R) * (Nat.choose (j + b) b : R) *
        coeff Q (i + a) (j + b)

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.hasseDerivative_add
items.doc: Hasse derivatives are additive.
items.statement:
theorem hasseDerivative_add {R : Type*}
    [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (a b : Nat) (P Q : CBivariate R) :
    hasseDerivative a b (P + Q) = hasseDerivative a b P + hasseDerivative a b Q

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.hasseDerivative_zero
items.doc: The Hasse derivative of zero is zero.
items.statement:
theorem hasseDerivative_zero {R : Type*}
    [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (a b : Nat) :
    hasseDerivative a b (0 : CBivariate R) = 0

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.hasseDerivative_monomialXY
items.doc: Hasse derivative of a single bivariate monomial.
items.statement:
theorem hasseDerivative_monomialXY {R : Type*}
    [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (a b n m : Nat) (c : R) :
    hasseDerivative a b (monomialXY n m c) =
      if a ≤ n ∧ b ≤ m then
        monomialXY (n - a) (m - b)
          ((Nat.choose n a : R) * (Nat.choose m b : R) * c)
      else 0

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.evalEval_add
items.doc: Full evaluation is additive.
items.statement:
theorem evalEval_add {R : Type*}
    [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R]
    (x y : R) (P Q : CBivariate R) :
    evalEval x y (P + Q) = evalEval x y P + evalEval x y Q

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.evalEval_zero
items.doc: Full evaluation of zero is zero.

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.evalEval_monomialXY
items.doc: Full evaluation of a bivariate monomial has the expected closed form.
items.statement:
theorem evalEval_monomialXY {R : Type*}
    [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (x y c : R) (n m : Nat) :
    evalEval x y (monomialXY n m c) = c * x ^ n * y ^ m

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.hasseDerivativeTerms_eval_aux
items.doc: Evaluating the materialized derivative-term fold matches the direct scalar fold.
items.statement:
theorem hasseDerivativeTerms_eval_aux {R : Type*}
    [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (x y : R) (terms : List (HasseTerm R)) (acc : CBivariate R) :
    evalEval x y (terms.foldl
      (fun out term ↦ out + monomialXY term.xDegree term.yDegree term.coeff) acc) =
    terms.foldl
      (fun z term ↦ z + term.coeff * x ^ term.xDegree * y ^ term.yDegree)
      (evalEval x y acc)

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.hasseDerivativeFromTerms_eval
items.doc: Evaluating a materialized derivative-term polynomial matches direct term evaluation.
items.statement:
theorem hasseDerivativeFromTerms_eval {R : Type*}
    [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (x y : R) (terms : List (HasseTerm R)) :
    evalEval x y (hasseDerivativeFromTerms terms) =
      hasseDerivativeEvalFromTerms terms x y

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.hasseDerivative_eval_eq_eval
items.doc: Correctness of executable Hasse derivative evaluation.
items.statement:
theorem hasseDerivative_eval_eq_eval {R : Type*}
    [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (a b : Nat) (x y : R) (Q : CBivariate R) :
    evalEval x y (hasseDerivative a b Q) = hasseDerivativeEval a b x y Q

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.eval_hasseDeriv_eval_hasseDeriv_toPoly
items.doc:
Evaluating the univariate `X`-Hasse derivative of the evaluated `Y`-Hasse
derivative matches the executable bivariate Hasse derivative.
items.statement:
theorem eval_hasseDeriv_eval_hasseDeriv_toPoly {F : Type*}
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F] [DecidableEq F]
    (Q : CBivariate F) (x y : F) (a b : Nat) :
    Polynomial.eval x (Polynomial.hasseDeriv a
        (Polynomial.eval (Polynomial.C y) (Polynomial.hasseDeriv b Q.toPoly))) =
      CBivariate.hasseDerivativeEval a b x y Q

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.coeff_shiftC_eq_hasseDerivativeEval
items.doc:
The coefficient of the generic Taylor shift is the direct Hasse derivative
evaluation at the shift point.
items.statement:
theorem coeff_shiftC_eq_hasseDerivativeEval {F : Type*}
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F] [DecidableEq F]
    (Q : CBivariate F) (x y : F) (a b : Nat) :
    CBivariate.coeff (CBivariate.shiftC x y Q) a b =
      CBivariate.hasseDerivativeEval a b x y Q

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.hasMultiplicity_iff_hasMultiplicityAtLeast
items.doc:
The generic multiplicity predicate agrees with the direct GS Hasse
multiplicity predicate.
items.statement:
theorem hasMultiplicity_iff_hasMultiplicityAtLeast {F : Type*}
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F] [DecidableEq F]
    (Q : CBivariate F) (r : Nat) (x y : F) :
    CBivariate.hasMultiplicity Q r x y ↔
      CBivariate.HasMultiplicityAtLeast Q x y r

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.satisfiesMultiplicityConstraints_iff_hasMultiplicity
items.doc:
The GS batch Hasse predicate agrees with the generic multiplicity
predicate over every packed point.
items.statement:
theorem satisfiesMultiplicityConstraints_iff_hasMultiplicity {F : Type*}
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F] [DecidableEq F]
    (Q : CBivariate F) (points : Array (F × F)) (r : Nat) :
    CBivariate.SatisfiesMultiplicityConstraints Q points r ↔
      ∀ point, point ∈ points.toList →
        CBivariate.hasMultiplicity Q r point.1 point.2

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.multiplicityAtLeastBool_iff_hasMultiplicity
items.doc:
The executable GS point checker agrees with the generic multiplicity
predicate.
items.statement:
theorem multiplicityAtLeastBool_iff_hasMultiplicity {F : Type*}
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F] [DecidableEq F]
    (Q : CBivariate F) (x y : F) (r : Nat) :
    CBivariate.multiplicityAtLeastBool Q x y r = true ↔
      CBivariate.hasMultiplicity Q r x y

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.satisfiesMultiplicityConstraintsBool_iff_hasMultiplicity
items.doc:
The executable GS batch checker agrees with the generic multiplicity
predicate over every packed point.
items.statement:
theorem satisfiesMultiplicityConstraintsBool_iff_hasMultiplicity {F : Type*}
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F] [DecidableEq F]
    (Q : CBivariate F) (points : Array (F × F)) (r : Nat) :
    CBivariate.satisfiesMultiplicityConstraintsBool Q points r = true ↔
      ∀ point, point ∈ points.toList →
        CBivariate.hasMultiplicity Q r point.1 point.2

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.multiplicityAtLeastBool_iff_checkMultiplicity
items.doc:
The executable GS point checker agrees with the generic boolean
checker.
items.statement:
theorem multiplicityAtLeastBool_iff_checkMultiplicity {F : Type*}
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F] [DecidableEq F]
    (Q : CBivariate F) (x y : F) (r : Nat) :
    CBivariate.multiplicityAtLeastBool Q x y r = true ↔
      CBivariate.checkMultiplicity Q r x y = true

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.satisfiesMultiplicityConstraintsBool_iff_checkMultiplicity
items.doc:
The executable GS batch checker agrees pointwise with the generic
boolean checker over the packed point array.
items.statement:
theorem satisfiesMultiplicityConstraintsBool_iff_checkMultiplicity {F : Type*}
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F] [DecidableEq F]
    (Q : CBivariate F) (points : Array (F × F)) (r : Nat) :
    CBivariate.satisfiesMultiplicityConstraintsBool Q points r = true ↔
      ∀ point, point ∈ points.toList →
        CBivariate.checkMultiplicity Q r point.1 point.2 = true

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.hasseDerivativeEval_add
items.doc: Direct Hasse evaluation is additive in the input polynomial.
items.statement:
theorem hasseDerivativeEval_add {R : Type*}
    [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (a b : Nat) (x y : R) (P Q : CBivariate R) :
    hasseDerivativeEval a b x y (P + Q) =
      hasseDerivativeEval a b x y P + hasseDerivativeEval a b x y Q

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.hasseDerivativeEval_zero
items.doc: Direct Hasse evaluation of zero is zero.
items.statement:
theorem hasseDerivativeEval_zero {R : Type*}

modules.title: Alekhnovich Bivariate Bounded Root Search
modules.doc:
Executable batched `X`-adic root lifting for the Guruswami-Sudan bivariate root
phase. The public output is exactly filtered against `Q(X, p(X)) = 0` and
`degree p < k`, following Alekhnovich's lattice-based root-search approach
[Ale05].

## References

* [M. Alekhnovich, *Linear Diophantine Equations Over Polynomials and Soft
    Decoding of Reed-Solomon Codes*, IEEE Transactions on Information Theory
    51(7), 2257-2265, 2005][Ale05]

  precision : Nat
deriving BEq, DecidableEq

    (CPolynomial.truncate p n).coeff i = if i < n then p.coeff i else 0

theorem composeY_add {R : Type*}

    (P Q : CBivariate R) (p : CPolynomial R) :
    CBivariate.composeY (P + Q) p = CBivariate.composeY P p + CBivariate.composeY Q p

theorem composeY_outer_monomial {R : Type*}

    CBivariate.composeY (CPolynomial.monomial y c : CBivariate R) p = c * p ^ y

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.composeY_coeff_zero_zipIdx_eq_range_aux
items.statement:
theorem composeY_coeff_zero_zipIdx_eq_range_aux {F : Type*}
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (xs : List (CPolynomial F)) (p accPoly : CPolynomial F) (accCoeff : F)
    (offset : Nat) (hacc : accPoly.coeff 0 = accCoeff) :
    List.foldl
        (fun acc y ↦ acc + (xs.getD (y - offset) 0).coeff 0 * p.coeff 0 ^ y)
        accCoeff (List.range' offset xs.length) =
      (List.foldl (fun acc x ↦ acc + x.1 * p ^ x.2) accPoly
        (xs.zipIdx offset)).coeff 0

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.composeY_coeff_zero_fold_eq
items.statement:
theorem composeY_coeff_zero_fold_eq {F : Type*}
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (coeffs : Array (CPolynomial F)) (p : CPolynomial F) :
    List.foldl (fun acc y ↦ acc + (coeffs.getD y 0).coeff 0 * p.coeff 0 ^ y) 0
        (List.range' 0 coeffs.size) =
      (Array.foldl (fun acc x ↦ acc + x.1 * p ^ x.2) 0 coeffs.zipIdx).coeff 0

    (offset n : Nat) (hacc : accPoly.coeff n = accCoeff) :
    List.foldl
        (fun acc y ↦ acc + ((xs.getD (y - offset) 0) * p ^ y).coeff n)
        accCoeff (List.range' offset xs.length) =
      (List.foldl (fun acc x ↦ acc + x.1 * p ^ x.2) accPoly
        (xs.zipIdx offset)).coeff n

theorem fold_range_coeff_add_mul_pow {R : Type*}
    [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R]
    (coeffs : Array (CPolynomial R)) (p : CPolynomial R) :
    ∀ (ys : List Nat) (acc : CPolynomial R) (accCoeff : R) (n : Nat),
      acc.coeff n = accCoeff →
        (List.foldl (fun acc y ↦ acc + coeffs.getD y 0 * p ^ y) acc ys).coeff n =
          List.foldl
            (fun acc y ↦ acc + ((coeffs.getD y 0) * p ^ y).coeff n)
            accCoeff ys

        (fun acc y ↦ acc + Q.val.coeff y * p ^ y) 0

modules.title: Roth-Ruckenstein-Style Root Finding
modules.doc:
Executable bounded-degree roots for `CBivariate F` using recursive coefficient
reconstruction and an explicit univariate field-root backend, following the
Roth-Ruckenstein root-search step [RR00].

## References

* [Roth, R. M., and Ruckenstein, G., *Efficient decoding of Reed-Solomon codes
    beyond half the minimum distance*][RR00]

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.initialCoefficientPolynomial_coeff_fold
items.statement:
theorem initialCoefficientPolynomial_coeff_fold {F : Type*}
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F] [DecidableEq F]
    (Q : CBivariate F) (j : Nat) :
    ∀ (ys : List Nat) (out : CPolynomial F),
      ys.Nodup →
        (List.foldl
          (fun out y ↦ out + CPolynomial.monomial y (CBivariate.coeff Q 0 y))
          out ys).coeff j =
          out.coeff j + if j ∈ ys then CBivariate.coeff Q 0 j else 0

items.statement:
theorem cpoly_dropXPower_add {R : Type*} [Zero R]
    (p : CPolynomial R) (m n : Nat) :
    CPolynomial.dropXPower (CPolynomial.dropXPower p m) n =
      CPolynomial.dropXPower p (m + n)

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.dropXPower_eq_C_add_X_mul_dropXPower_succ
items.statement:
theorem dropXPower_eq_C_add_X_mul_dropXPower_succ {F : Type*}
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (p : CPolynomial F) (depth : Nat) :
    CPolynomial.dropXPower p depth =
      CPolynomial.C (p.coeff depth) +
        CPolynomial.X * CPolynomial.dropXPower p (depth + 1)

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.polynomial_monomial_substitution_term
items.statement:
theorem polynomial_monomial_substitution_term {F : Type*} [Field F]
    (a coeff : F) (p : Polynomial F) (x y t : Nat) :
    Polynomial.monomial x coeff *
        ((Polynomial.X * p) ^ t * Polynomial.C a ^ (y - t) *
          Polynomial.C (Nat.choose y t : F)) =
      Polynomial.monomial (x + t) (coeff * (Nat.choose y t : F) * a ^ (y - t)) *
        p ^ t

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.polynomial_monomial_substitution_sum
items.statement:
theorem polynomial_monomial_substitution_sum {F : Type*} [Field F]
    (a coeff : F) (p : Polynomial F) (x y : Nat) :
    (∑ t ∈ Finset.range (y + 1),
        Polynomial.monomial (x + t) (coeff * (Nat.choose y t : F) * a ^ (y - t)) *
          p ^ t) =
      Polynomial.monomial x coeff * (Polynomial.C a + Polynomial.X * p) ^ y

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.foldl_cpoly_toPoly_add
items.statement:
theorem foldl_cpoly_toPoly_add {F : Type*}
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (f : Nat → CPolynomial F) :
    ∀ (xs : List Nat) (acc : CPolynomial F) (accPoly : Polynomial F),
      acc.toPoly = accPoly →
        (xs.foldl (fun acc x ↦ acc + f x) acc).toPoly =
          xs.foldl (fun acc x ↦ acc + (f x).toPoly) accPoly

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.cpoly_monomial_substitution_sum
items.statement:
theorem cpoly_monomial_substitution_sum {F : Type*}
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F] [DecidableEq F]
    (a coeff : F) (p : CPolynomial F) (x y : Nat) :
    (List.range' 0 (y + 1)).foldl
        (fun acc t ↦
          acc + CPolynomial.monomial (x + t)
            (coeff * (Nat.choose y t : F) * a ^ (y - t)) * p ^ t)
        0 =
      CPolynomial.monomial x coeff * (CPolynomial.C a + CPolynomial.X * p) ^ y

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.shiftedSubstitutionCoeffTerm_sum
items.doc:
The univariate coefficient sum produced by one `Y`-coefficient in shifted
substitution composes to the corresponding binomial expansion.
items.statement:
theorem shiftedSubstitutionCoeffTerm_sum {F : Type*}
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F] [DecidableEq F]
    (coeffY f g : CPolynomial F) (t y : Nat) :
    (List.range (y + 1)).foldl
        (fun acc r ↦ acc + shiftedSubstitutionCoeffTerm coeffY f t y r * g ^ r)
        0 =
      coeffY * (f + CPolynomial.X ^ t * g) ^ y

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.composeY_shiftedSubstitutionCoeffFold
items.doc:
Composing the bivariate contribution from one `Y`-coefficient gives the
corresponding univariate shifted-substitution term.
items.statement:
theorem composeY_shiftedSubstitutionCoeffFold {F : Type*}
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F] [DecidableEq F]
    (coeffY f g : CPolynomial F) (t y : Nat) :
    CBivariate.composeY
        ((List.range (y + 1)).foldl
          (fun (out : CBivariate F) r ↦
            let contribution : CBivariate F := CPolynomial.monomial r
              (shiftedSubstitutionCoeffTerm coeffY f t y r)
            out + contribution)
          0)
        g =
      (List.range (y + 1)).foldl
        (fun acc r ↦ acc + shiftedSubstitutionCoeffTerm coeffY f t y r * g ^ r)
        0

items.name: CompPoly.GuruswamiSudan.composeY_substituteYPolynomialPlusXPowerY
items.doc: Semantic correctness of the shifted substitution `Y = f(X) + X^t Y`.
items.statement:
theorem composeY_substituteYPolynomialPlusXPowerY {F : Type*}
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F] [DecidableEq F]
    (Q : CBivariate F) (f g : CPolynomial F) (t : Nat) :
    CBivariate.composeY (substituteYPolynomialPlusXPowerY Q f t) g =
      CBivariate.composeY Q (f + CPolynomial.X ^ t * g)

modules.title: Kronecker substitution for bivariate polynomials
modules.doc:
Kronecker substitution turns a bivariate multiplication into a univariate multiplication by
fixing a gap `D` and substituting `X ↦ t`, `Y ↦ t ^ D`. This sends a bivariate
polynomial `p : CBivariate R` to a univariate polynomial `kroneckerPack D p : CPolynomial R`
in which the coefficient of `X ^ i Y ^ j` is placed at position `D * j + i`.

Packing is a ring homomorphism, so for any `p` and `q` the packed product equals the
product of the packed operands, with no condition on degrees. A condition is needed only to
unpack the result. The position `D * j + i` determines `i` and `j` only when `i < D`, so
packing can be reversed exactly on polynomials with `natDegreeX < D`. Recovering a product
`p * q` therefore needs
`natDegreeX (p * q) < D`, and since `natDegreeX (p * q) ≤ natDegreeX p + natDegreeX q`, it is
enough to choose `D` greater than `natDegreeX p + natDegreeX q`.

Kronecker substitution is not itself an optimisation; it lets a fast univariate
multiplication carry out the bivariate one. The NTT versions multiply through `withFallback`,
which uses an NTT domain when one fits and otherwise multiplies the ordinary way, so it is
always equal to `*` and adds no assumption about the domain beyond the gap condition above.

## Main results

* `kroneckerPack` / `kroneckerUnpack` — the substitution and its inverse.
* `kroneckerPack_mul` — packing is multiplicative.
* `kroneckerUnpack_mul` — bivariate multiplication as pack, multiply, unpack.
* `kroneckerPackFast` / `kroneckerUnpackFast` — linear-time versions, proved equal to the above.
* `kroneckerUnpack_withFallback` / `kroneckerUnpack_withFallbackFast` — multiplication backed by
  the classic and recursive NTT.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.coeff_mul_X_pow
items.doc: Coefficient of `c * X ^ m`.
items.statement:
theorem coeff_mul_X_pow [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R]
    (c : CPolynomial R) (m n : ℕ) :
    coeff (c * X ^ m) n = if m ≤ n then coeff c (n - m) else 0

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.shiftPow
items.doc: Multiplication by `X ^ m`, implemented as a coefficient shift.
items.statement: def shiftPow [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (m : ℕ) (p : CPolynomial R) : CPolynomial R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.coeff_shiftPow
items.doc: Coefficient of `shiftPow m p`.
items.statement:
theorem coeff_shiftPow [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (m : ℕ) (p : CPolynomial R) (n : ℕ) :
    coeff (shiftPow m p) n = if m ≤ n then coeff p (n - m) else 0

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.shiftPow_eq_mul_X_pow
items.doc: `shiftPow m p = p * X ^ m`.
items.statement:
theorem shiftPow_eq_mul_X_pow [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R]
    (m : ℕ) (p : CPolynomial R) : shiftPow m p = p * X ^ m

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.kroneckerPack
items.doc: Pack a bivariate polynomial into a univariate one with gap `D`.
items.statement:
def kroneckerPack [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R]
    (D : ℕ) (p : CBivariate R) : CPolynomial R

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.kroneckerUnpack
items.doc: Unpack a univariate polynomial into a bivariate one with gap `D`.
items.statement:
def kroneckerUnpack [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (D : ℕ) (P : CPolynomial R) : CBivariate R

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.kroneckerPack_mul
items.doc: Packing is multiplicative.
items.statement:
theorem kroneckerPack_mul [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R]
    (D : ℕ) (p q : CBivariate R) :
    kroneckerPack D (p * q) = kroneckerPack D p * kroneckerPack D q

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.kroneckerPack_eq_sum
items.doc: Packing written as a sum of shifted `Y`-coefficients.
items.statement:
theorem kroneckerPack_eq_sum [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R]
    (D : ℕ) (p : CBivariate R) :
    kroneckerPack D p
      = (CPolynomial.support p).sum
          (fun i => CPolynomial.coeff p i * CPolynomial.X ^ (D * i))

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.coeff_kroneckerPack
items.doc: Coefficient of the packed polynomial, when the `X`-degree is below the gap.
items.statement:
theorem coeff_kroneckerPack [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R]
    {D : ℕ} (hD : 0 < D) (p : CBivariate R) (hp : natDegreeX p < D) (n : ℕ) :
    CPolynomial.coeff (kroneckerPack D p) n = coeff p (n % D) (n / D)

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.kroneckerPackFast
items.doc: Efficient packing, linear in the output.
items.statement:
def kroneckerPackFast [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (D : ℕ) (p : CBivariate R) : CPolynomial R

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.kroneckerPackFast_eq
items.doc: `kroneckerPackFast` equals `kroneckerPack`.
items.statement:
theorem kroneckerPackFast_eq [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R]
    (D : ℕ) (p : CBivariate R) : kroneckerPackFast D p = kroneckerPack D p

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.coeff_kroneckerUnpack_of_le
items.doc: Unpacked coefficients with `X`-exponent at least `D` are zero.
items.statement:
theorem coeff_kroneckerUnpack_of_le [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R]
    [DecidableEq R] {D : ℕ} (hD : 0 < D) (P : CPolynomial R) (i j : ℕ) (hi : D ≤ i) :
    coeff (kroneckerUnpack D P) i j = 0

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.coeff_kroneckerUnpack
items.doc: Unpacked coefficient at `(i, j)` with `i < D`.
items.statement:
theorem coeff_kroneckerUnpack [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R]
    [DecidableEq R] {D : ℕ} (hD : 0 < D) (P : CPolynomial R) (i j : ℕ) (hi : i < D) :
    coeff (kroneckerUnpack D P) i j = CPolynomial.coeff P (D * j + i)

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.window
items.doc: The length-`D` slice of `P` holding column `j`.
items.statement: def window [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (D j : ℕ) (P : CPolynomial R) : CPolynomial R

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.coeff_window
items.doc: Coefficient of a column slice.
items.statement:
theorem coeff_window [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (D j : ℕ) (P : CPolynomial R) (i : ℕ) :
    CPolynomial.coeff (window D j P) i =
      if i < D then CPolynomial.coeff P (D * j + i) else 0

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.kroneckerUnpackFast
items.doc: Efficient unpacking, assembling columns directly.
items.statement:
def kroneckerUnpackFast [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (D : ℕ) (P : CPolynomial R) : CBivariate R

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.kroneckerUnpackFast_eq
items.doc: `kroneckerUnpackFast` equals `kroneckerUnpack`.
items.statement:
theorem kroneckerUnpackFast_eq [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    {D : ℕ} (hD : 0 < D) (P : CPolynomial R) :
    kroneckerUnpackFast D P = kroneckerUnpack D P

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.kroneckerUnpack_kroneckerPack
items.doc: Unpacking recovers a packed polynomial when its `X`-degree is below the gap.
items.statement:
theorem kroneckerUnpack_kroneckerPack [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R]
    [DecidableEq R] {D : ℕ} (hD : 0 < D) (p : CBivariate R) (hp : natDegreeX p < D) :
    kroneckerUnpack D (kroneckerPack D p) = p

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.kroneckerUnpack_mul
items.doc:
Bivariate multiplication as pack, univariate multiply, unpack, when the product fits
the gap.
items.statement:
theorem kroneckerUnpack_mul [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R]
    [DecidableEq R] {D : ℕ} (hD : 0 < D) (p q : CBivariate R)
    (hpq : natDegreeX (p * q) < D) :
    kroneckerUnpack D (kroneckerPack D p * kroneckerPack D q) = p * q

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.kroneckerUnpackFast_mul
items.doc: `kroneckerUnpack_mul` for the efficient `kroneckerPackFast` / `kroneckerUnpackFast`.
items.statement:
theorem kroneckerUnpackFast_mul [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R]
    [DecidableEq R] {D : ℕ} (hD : 0 < D) (p q : CBivariate R)
    (hpq : natDegreeX (p * q) < D) :
    kroneckerUnpackFast D (kroneckerPackFast D p * kroneckerPackFast D q) = p * q

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.kroneckerUnpack_withFallback
items.doc: Bivariate multiplication using the NTT (`withFallback`) as the univariate backend.
items.statement:
theorem kroneckerUnpack_withFallback [Field R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [DecidableEq R]
    (bestDomainForLength? : (requiredLen : Nat) →
      Option (CPolynomial.NTT.FittingDomain R requiredLen))
    {D : ℕ} (hD : 0 < D) (p q : CBivariate R) (hpq : natDegreeX (p * q) < D) :
    kroneckerUnpack D
        (CPolynomial.NTT.FastMul.withFallback bestDomainForLength?
          (kroneckerPack D p) (kroneckerPack D q))
      = p * q

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.kroneckerUnpack_withFallbackFast
items.doc:
Bivariate multiplication using the recursive NTT (`NTTFast.withFallback`) as the
univariate backend.
items.statement:
theorem kroneckerUnpack_withFallbackFast [Field R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [DecidableEq R]
    (bestDomainForLength? : (requiredLen : Nat) →
      Option (CPolynomial.NTT.FittingDomain R requiredLen))
    {D : ℕ} (hD : 0 < D) (p q : CBivariate R) (hpq : natDegreeX (p * q) < D) :
    kroneckerUnpack D
        (CPolynomial.NTTFast.withFallback bestDomainForLength?
          (kroneckerPack D p) (kroneckerPack D q))
      = p * q

modules.title: Equivalence with Mathlib Bivariate Polynomials
modules.doc:
This file establishes the conversion from `CBivariate R` to Mathlib's `R[X][Y]`
(`Polynomial (Polynomial R)`).

Main definitions:
- `toPoly`: converts `CBivariate R` to `R[X][Y]`
- `ofPoly`: converts `R[X][Y]` back to `CBivariate R`

Main results:
- round-trip identities: `ofPoly_toPoly`, `toPoly_ofPoly`
- ring equivalence: `ringEquiv`
- API correctness lemmas for evaluation, coefficients, support, and degrees

items.note: Core conversion lemmas between `CBivariate R` and `R[X][Y]`.

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.toPoly
items.doc:
Convert `CBivariate R` to Mathlib's bivariate polynomial `R[X][Y]`.

Maps each Y-coefficient through `CPolynomial.toPoly`, then builds
`Polynomial (Polynomial R)` as the sum of monomials.
items.statement:
noncomputable def toPoly {R : Type*} [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Semiring R]
    (p : CBivariate R) : R[X][Y]

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.ofPoly
items.doc:
Convert Mathlib's `R[X][Y]` to `CBivariate R` (inverse of `toPoly`).

Extracts each Y-coefficient via `p.coeff`, converts to `CPolynomial R` via
`toImpl` and trimming, then builds the canonical bivariate sum.
items.statement:
def ofPoly {R : Type*} [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [Semiring R]
    [DecidableEq R] [Semiring (Polynomial R)] (p : R[X][Y]) : CBivariate R

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.toPoly_add
items.doc: `toPoly` preserves addition.
items.statement:
lemma toPoly_add {R : Type*} [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [Semiring R]
    (p q : CBivariate R) : toPoly (p + q) = toPoly p + toPoly q

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.toPoly_monomial
items.doc: `toPoly` sends a Y-monomial to the corresponding monomial in `R[X][Y]`.
items.statement:
lemma toPoly_monomial {R : Type*} [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [Semiring R]
    [DecidableEq R]
    (n : ℕ) (c : CPolynomial R) :
    toPoly (CPolynomial.monomial n c) = monomial n (c.toPoly)

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.ofPoly_monomial
items.doc: `ofPoly` sends a Y-monomial in `R[X][Y]` to a bivariate monomial.
items.statement:
lemma ofPoly_monomial {R : Type*} [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [Semiring R]
    [DecidableEq R]
    (n : ℕ) (c : R[X]) :
    ofPoly (monomial n c) =
    CPolynomial.monomial n ⟨c.toImpl, CPolynomial.Raw.isCanonical_toImpl c⟩

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.toImpl_add
items.doc: `Polynomial.toImpl` preserves addition, accounting for trimming in the raw representation.
items.statement:
lemma toImpl_add {R : Type*} [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Semiring R] (p q : R[X]) :
    p.toImpl + q.toImpl = (p + q).toImpl

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.ofPoly_add
items.doc: `ofPoly` preserves addition in `R[X][Y]`.
items.statement:
lemma ofPoly_add {R : Type*} [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [Semiring R]
    [DecidableEq R]
    (p q : R[X][Y]) : ofPoly (p + q) = ofPoly p + ofPoly q

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.ofPoly_coeff
items.doc: The outer coefficient of `ofPoly p` converts back to the corresponding `R[X]` coefficient.
items.statement:
theorem ofPoly_coeff {R : Type*} [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [Semiring R]
    [DecidableEq R]
    (p : R[X][Y]) (n : ℕ) : (CPolynomial.coeff (ofPoly p) n).toPoly = p.coeff n

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.toPoly_coeff
items.doc: The outer coefficient of `toPoly p` is `CPolynomial.coeff p n` converted to `R[X]`.
items.statement:
theorem toPoly_coeff {R : Type*} [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Semiring R]
    (p : CBivariate R) (n : ℕ) : (toPoly p).coeff n = (CPolynomial.coeff p n).toPoly

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.toPoly_eq_map
items.doc: `toPoly` is the map of the outer polynomial via `CPolynomial.ringEquiv`.
items.statement:
theorem toPoly_eq_map {R : Type*} [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [Semiring R]
    (p : CBivariate R) :
    toPoly p = (CPolynomial.toPoly p).map (CPolynomial.ringEquiv (R := R))

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.toPoly_mul
items.doc: `toPoly` preserves multiplication.
items.statement:
theorem toPoly_mul {R : Type*} [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [Semiring R]
    (p q : CBivariate R) :
    toPoly (p * q) = toPoly p * toPoly q

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.ofPoly_toPoly
items.doc: Round-trip from Mathlib: converting a polynomial to `CBivariate` and back is the identity.
items.statement:
theorem ofPoly_toPoly {R : Type*} [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [Semiring R]
    [DecidableEq R]
    (p : R[X][Y]) : toPoly (ofPoly p) = p

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.toPoly_ofPoly
items.doc: Round-trip from `CBivariate`: converting to Mathlib and back is the identity.
items.statement:
theorem toPoly_ofPoly {R : Type*} [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [Semiring R]
    [DecidableEq R]
    (p : CBivariate R) : ofPoly (toPoly p) = p

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.ringEquiv
items.doc: Ring equivalence between `CBivariate R` and Mathlib's `R[X][Y]`.
items.statement:
noncomputable def ringEquiv

    CBivariate R ≃+* R[X][Y]

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.toPoly_one
items.doc: `toPoly` preserves `1`.
items.statement:
theorem toPoly_one
    {R : Type*} [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [Semiring R] [DecidableEq R] :
    toPoly (1 : CBivariate R) = 1

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.ofPoly_one
items.doc: `ofPoly` preserves `1`.
items.statement:
theorem ofPoly_one
    {R : Type*} [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [Semiring R] [DecidableEq R] :

items.doc: `toPoly` maps the zero bivariate polynomial to `0`.
items.statement:
lemma toPoly_zero {R : Type*} [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [Semiring R] :

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.ofPoly_zero
items.doc: `ofPoly` maps `0` in `R[X][Y]` to the zero bivariate polynomial.
items.statement:
lemma ofPoly_zero {R : Type*} [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [Semiring R] [DecidableEq R] :

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.toPolyRingHom
items.doc: Ring hom from computable bivariates to Mathlib bivariates.
items.statement:
noncomputable def toPolyRingHom
    {R : Type*} [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [Semiring R] [DecidableEq R] :

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.ofPolyRingHom
items.doc: Ring hom from Mathlib bivariates to computable bivariates.
items.statement:

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.ofPoly_mul
items.doc: `ofPoly` preserves multiplication.
items.statement:
theorem ofPoly_mul

    ofPoly (p * q) = ofPoly p * ofPoly q

items.note:
### Shared helper: deferred-trim Horner foldr commutes with `toPoly`

`evalY` and (transitively) `evalEval` fold the Y-coefficients of `f : CBivariate R`
with a raw Horner pattern (`smulRight a` then `addRaw`) and trim once at the end.
The helper below bridges that raw fold's `toPoly` image with the `Finset.sum` form
of the polynomial evaluation.
Correctness lemmas for evaluation, coefficients, support, and degrees.

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.evalY_toPoly
items.doc: `evalY a` corresponds to outer evaluation at `Polynomial.C a`.
items.statement:
theorem evalY_toPoly {R : Type*} [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [Semiring R]
    (a : R) (f : CBivariate R) :
    (evalY (R := R) a f).toPoly = (toPoly f).eval (Polynomial.C a)

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.eval_y_horner_eq_eval_y
items.doc:
Horner evaluation in Y agrees with the deferred-trim sum-of-powers evaluator.

Both `evalYHorner` and the new `evalY` reduce to the same `Polynomial` under
`toPoly`, and `toPoly` is injective on canonical polynomials, so the two
canonical results coincide.

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.eval_eval_horner_y_then_x_eq_eval_eval
items.doc: `Y`-then-`X` Horner full evaluation agrees with the existing evaluator.
items.statement:
theorem eval_eval_horner_y_then_x_eq_eval_eval {R : Type*}
    [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R]
    (x y : R) (p : CBivariate R) :
    evalEvalHornerYThenX x y p = evalEval x y p

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.evalEval_toPoly
items.doc: `toPoly` preserves full evaluation: `evalEval x y f = (toPoly f).evalEval x y`.

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.coeff_toPoly
items.doc: `toPoly` preserves coefficients: coefficient of `X^i Y^j` matches.
items.statement:
theorem coeff_toPoly {R : Type*} [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [Semiring R]
    (f : CBivariate R) (i j : ℕ) :
    ((toPoly f).coeff j).coeff i = CBivariate.coeff (R := R) f i j

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.support_toPoly_outer
items.doc: The outer support of `toPoly f` equals the Y-support of `f`.
items.statement:
theorem support_toPoly_outer {R : Type*} [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [Semiring R]
    (f : CBivariate R) : (toPoly f).support = f.supportY

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.natDegreeY_toPoly
items.doc: `toPoly` preserves Y-degree.
items.statement:
theorem natDegreeY_toPoly {R : Type*} [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [Semiring R]
    (f : CBivariate R) : (toPoly f).natDegree = f.natDegreeY

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.coeff_toPoly_Y
items.doc: The outer `Y`-coefficient formula used for X-degree transport.
items.statement:
theorem coeff_toPoly_Y {R : Type*} [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [Semiring R]
    (f : CBivariate R) (j : ℕ) :
    (toPoly f).coeff j = CPolynomial.toPoly (f.val.coeff j)

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.natDegreeX_toPoly
items.doc: `toPoly` preserves X-degree (max over Y-coefficients of their degree in X).
items.statement:
theorem natDegreeX_toPoly {R : Type*} [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [Semiring R]
    (f : CBivariate R) :
    (toPoly f).support.sup (fun j ↦ ((toPoly f).coeff j).natDegree) = f.natDegreeX

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.CC_toPoly
items.doc: `CC` corresponds to the nested constant polynomial in `R[X][Y]`.
items.statement:
theorem CC_toPoly {R : Type*} [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [Semiring R] (r : R) :
    toPoly (CC (R := R) r) = Polynomial.C (Polynomial.C r)

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.X_toPoly
items.doc: `X` (inner variable) corresponds to `Polynomial.C Polynomial.X` in `R[X][Y]`.
items.statement:
theorem X_toPoly {R : Type*} [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [Semiring R] :
    toPoly (X (R := R)) = Polynomial.C Polynomial.X

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.Y_toPoly
items.doc: `Y` (outer variable) corresponds to `Polynomial.X` in `R[X][Y]`.
items.statement:
theorem Y_toPoly {R : Type*} [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [Semiring R] [DecidableEq R] :
    toPoly (CBivariate.Y (R := R)) = (Polynomial.X : Polynomial (Polynomial R))

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.monomialXY_toPoly
items.doc: `monomialXY n m c` corresponds to `Y^m` with inner coefficient `X^n * c`.
items.statement:
theorem monomialXY_toPoly {R : Type*} [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [Semiring R]
    [DecidableEq R] (n m : ℕ) (c : R) :
    toPoly (monomialXY (R := R) n m c) = Polynomial.monomial m (Polynomial.monomial n c)

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.supportX_toPoly
items.doc: `supportX` corresponds to the union of inner supports of outer coefficients.
items.statement:
theorem supportX_toPoly {R : Type*} [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [Semiring R]
    (f : CBivariate R) :
    CBivariate.supportX (R := R) f =
      (toPoly f).support.biUnion (fun j ↦ ((toPoly f).coeff j).support)

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.totalDegree_toPoly
items.doc: `totalDegree` corresponds to the supremum over `j` of `natDegree ((toPoly f).coeff j) + j`.
items.statement:
theorem totalDegree_toPoly {R : Type*} [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [Semiring R]
    (f : CBivariate R) :
    CBivariate.totalDegree (R := R) f =
      (toPoly f).support.sup (fun j ↦ ((toPoly f).coeff j).natDegree + j)

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.evalX_toPoly_coeff
items.doc: `evalX a` evaluates each inner coefficient at `a`.
items.statement:
theorem evalX_toPoly_coeff {R : Type*} [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [Semiring R]
    [DecidableEq R] (a : R) (f : CBivariate R) (j : ℕ) :
    ((evalX (R := R) a f).toPoly).coeff j = ((toPoly f).coeff j).eval a

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.evalX_toPoly_eval_commute
items.doc: `evalX` is compatible with full bivariate evaluation when `a` and `y` commute.
items.statement:
theorem evalX_toPoly_eval_commute {R : Type*} [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [Semiring R]
    [DecidableEq R] (a y : R) (hc : Commute a y) (f : CBivariate R) :
    (evalX (R := R) a f).eval y = (toPoly f).evalEval a y

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.evalX_toPoly_eval
items.doc: `evalX_toPoly_eval_commute` specialized to commutative rings.
items.statement:
theorem evalX_toPoly_eval {R : Type*} [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [CommSemiring R]
    [DecidableEq R] (a y : R) (f : CBivariate R) :
    (evalX (R := R) a f).eval y = (toPoly f).evalEval a y

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.eval_eval_horner_x_then_y_eq_eval_eval
items.doc:
`X`-then-`Y` Horner full evaluation agrees with the existing evaluator over
commutative coefficient semirings.
items.statement:
theorem eval_eval_horner_x_then_y_eq_eval_eval {R : Type*}
    [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [CommSemiring R] [DecidableEq R]
    (x y : R) (p : CBivariate R) :
    evalEvalHornerXThenY x y p = evalEval x y p

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.evalX_toPoly_eval_commute_converse
items.doc:
The `Commute` hypothesis in `evalX_toPoly_eval_commute` is necessary:
if the identity holds for every bivariate polynomial then `a` and `y` commute.
items.statement:
theorem evalX_toPoly_eval_commute_converse
    {R : Type*} [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [Semiring R] [DecidableEq R]
    (a y : R)
    (h : ∀ f : CBivariate R,
      (evalX (R := R) a f).eval y = (toPoly f).evalEval a y) :
    Commute a y

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.eval_comm
items.doc:
Computable analogue of `Polynomial.map_evalRingHom_eval`:
evaluating `Y` at `a` and then `X` at `x` agrees with first applying the
`X = x` evaluation through the inner coefficients and then evaluating `Y`
at `a`.
items.statement:
theorem eval_comm {R : Type*} [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [CommSemiring R]
    [DecidableEq R] (a x : R) (f : CBivariate R) :
    (evalY (R := R) a f).eval x = (evalX (R := R) x f).eval a

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.leadingCoeffY_toPoly
items.doc: `leadingCoeffY` corresponds to the leading coefficient in the outer variable.
items.statement:
theorem leadingCoeffY_toPoly {R : Type*} [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [Semiring R]
    (f : CBivariate R) :
    (leadingCoeffY (R := R) f).toPoly = (toPoly f).leadingCoeff

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.swap_toPoly_coeff
items.doc: `swap` exchanges X- and Y-exponents.
items.statement:
theorem swap_toPoly_coeff {R : Type*} [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [Semiring R]
    [DecidableEq R] (f : CBivariate R) (i j : ℕ) :
    ((toPoly (swap (R := R) f)).coeff j).coeff i = ((toPoly f).coeff i).coeff j

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.leadingCoeffX_toPoly
items.doc: `leadingCoeffX` is the Y-leading coefficient of the swapped polynomial.
items.statement:
theorem leadingCoeffX_toPoly {R : Type*} [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [Semiring R]
    [DecidableEq R] (f : CBivariate R) :
    (leadingCoeffX (R := R) f).toPoly = (toPoly (swap (R := R) f)).leadingCoeff

items.name: Array.matchSize_toList

items.doc: `Array.map` and `getD` agree with indexed access on in-bounds indices.

Array.foldl_zipIdx_eq_foldl_toList_zipIdx_size
Array.mem_foldl_append_of_mem

Array.findIdxRev?
items.doc: find index from the end of an array
items.statement: def findIdxRev? (cond : α → Bool) (as : Array α) : Option (Fin as.size)

items.name: Array.findIdxRev?_def
items.doc: if findIdxRev? finds an index, the condition is satisfied on that element
items.statement:
lemma findIdxRev?_def {cond} {as : Array α} {k : Fin as.size} :
    findIdxRev? cond as = some k → cond as[k]

items.name: Array.findIdxRev?_maximal
items.doc: if findIdxRev? finds an index, then for every greater index the condition doesn't hold

lemma findIdxRev?_maximal {cond} {as : Array α} {k : Fin as.size} :
    findIdxRev? cond as = some k → ∀ j : Fin as.size, j > k → ¬ cond as[j]

items.doc: if the condition is false on all elements, then findIdxRev? finds nothing

items.name: Nat.fold_push_eq_append_ofFn
items.doc:
A `Nat.fold` that pushes `e k h` at step `k` appends `e 0 _, …, e (n - 1) _` to its initial
array. The pushed element can depend on the proof `h : k < n`.
items.statement:
theorem fold_push_eq_append_ofFn {α : Type*} {n : ℕ} (e : (k : ℕ) → k < n → α)
    (init : Array α) :
    n.fold (fun k h acc ↦ acc.push (e k h)) init = init ++ Array.ofFn fun k : Fin n ↦ e k k.2

modules.title: Bias of the reduce-modulo-order decoder
modules.doc:
A challenge squeezed from a byte sponge is `CanonicalNat.ofBytesModOrder`: `n` bytes read as a
little-endian integer and reduced modulo `bound`. Reducing the `256 ^ n` strings modulo `bound`
hits every residue `256 ^ n / bound` or `256 ^ n / bound + 1` times, so the induced distribution
on `F` is within `bound / 256 ^ n` of uniform in total variation. Sixteen bytes beyond the
field's width make that below `2 ^ -128`, which is the margin spongefish uses.

* `Bytes.equivFin`: `n`-byte strings are the naturals below `256 ^ n`.
* `CanonicalNat.card_fiber_ofBytesModOrder`: the exact fiber count, from Mathlib's
  `Nat.count_modEq_card`.
* `CanonicalNat.tv_ofBytesModOrder_le`: the total-variation bound, over `ℚ`.

Everything here is counting; no probability theory is imported. ArkLib's
`Deserialize.CloseToUniform` instance for `ZMod p` is derived from the last theorem by casting
into its `PMF` distance.

items.name: CompPoly.Bytes.equivFin
items.doc: Little-endian byte strings of length `n` are the naturals below `256 ^ n`.
items.statement: def equivFin (n : ℕ) : Vector UInt8 n ≃ Fin (256 ^ n)

items.name: CompPoly.Bytes.instFintypeVectorUInt8
items.doc: `n`-byte strings are finite, through `equivFin`.
items.statement: instance instFintypeVectorUInt8 (n : ℕ) : Fintype (Vector UInt8 n)

items.name: CompPoly.Bytes.card_vector_uint8
items.statement: theorem card_vector_uint8 (n : ℕ) : Fintype.card (Vector UInt8 n) = 256 ^ n

items.name: CompPoly.CanonicalNat.ofNat_eq_iff
items.statement: theorem ofNat_eq_iff {m : ℕ} {x : F} : ofNat m = x ↔ m % bound F = toNat x

items.name: CompPoly.CanonicalNat.fiberEquiv
items.doc:
The `n`-byte strings decoding to `x` modulo the order, as the naturals below `256 ^ n`
congruent to `toNat x`.

items.name: CompPoly.CanonicalNat.instFintypeFiber
items.statement:
instance instFintypeFiber [DecidableEq F] (n : ℕ) (x : F) :
    Fintype {v : Vector UInt8 n // ofBytesModOrder v = x}

items.name: CompPoly.CanonicalNat.card_fiber_ofBytesModOrder
items.doc:
Exactly how many `n`-byte strings decode to `x` modulo the order: the quotient
`256 ^ n / bound`, plus one for the residues below the remainder.

items.name: CompPoly.CanonicalNat.abs_card_fiber_div_sub_le
items.doc:
Every fiber is within one of the ideal `256 ^ n / bound`, so each residue's probability is
within `1 / 256 ^ n` of uniform.
items.statement:
theorem abs_card_fiber_div_sub_le (n : ℕ) (x : F) :
    |((Fintype.card {v : Vector UInt8 n // ofBytesModOrder v = x} : ℚ) / 256 ^ n)
      - 1 / bound F| ≤ 1 / 256 ^ n

items.name: CompPoly.CanonicalNat.tv_ofBytesModOrder_le
items.doc:
The total-variation distance of `ofBytesModOrder` on `n` bytes from the uniform
distribution on `F` is at most `bound / 256 ^ n`: sixteen bytes beyond the width give
`2 ^ -128`. Stated over `ℚ`; ArkLib derives its `PMF` form from it.
items.statement:
theorem tv_ofBytesModOrder_le [Fintype F] (n : ℕ) :
    ∑ x : F, |((Fintype.card {v : Vector UInt8 n // ofBytesModOrder v = x} : ℚ) / 256 ^ n)
      - 1 / bound F| ≤ bound F / 256 ^ n

modules.title: Byte codecs from canonical naturals
modules.doc:
A type with a `CanonicalNat` structure has a fixed-width byte codec: the little-endian bytes
of `toNat`, `bytesFor bound` of them, decoded by `ofNat?`. This is `ByteCodec.ofCanonicalNat`,
a definition rather than an instance so that a composite type may choose a different codec
(an extension field concatenates its coefficients) while still having a canonical natural.

The same structure gives the total decoder used for challenges: `ofBytesModOrder` reads any
number of bytes as an integer and reduces it modulo `bound`. Reading back an exact-width
encoding this way recovers the element (`ofBytesModOrder_toBytes`); reading more bytes than
the width is what makes the result close to uniform.

`ZMod p` receives both: `instCanonicalNatZMod` from `CompPoly.Data.Classes.CanonicalNat` and the
derived `ByteCodec (ZMod p)` here, so every spec prime field in `CompPoly.Fields` serializes.

items.name: CompPoly.ByteCodec.ofCanonicalNat
items.doc:
The fixed-width byte codec of a type with canonical naturals: `bytesFor bound` little-endian
bytes of `toNat`, decoded by `ofNat?`.
items.statement: def ByteCodec.ofCanonicalNat (F : Type u) [CanonicalNat F] : ByteCodec F

items.name: CompPoly.CanonicalNat.ofBytesModOrder
items.doc:
Read any byte string as a little-endian integer and reduce it modulo `bound`. Total, and
close to uniform when the string is longer than `bytesFor bound`.
items.statement: def ofBytesModOrder {n : ℕ} (v : Vector UInt8 n) : F

items.name: CompPoly.CanonicalNat.ofByteArrayModOrder
items.doc: `ofBytesModOrder` on a `ByteArray` of any size.
items.statement: def ofByteArrayModOrder (b : ByteArray) : F

theorem deserialize_vector_eq {n : ℕ} (v : Vector UInt8 n) :

items.name: CompPoly.CanonicalNat.deserialize_byteArray_eq
items.statement:

items.doc: Reading back an exact-width little-endian encoding modulo the order recovers the element.
items.statement:
theorem ofBytesModOrder_toVecLE_toNat (x : F) :
    ofBytesModOrder (toVecLE (bytesFor (bound F)) (toNat x)) = x

items.doc: Reading back the `ofCanonicalNat` encoding modulo the order recovers the element.

    CanonicalNat.ofBytesModOrder ((ByteCodec.ofCanonicalNat F).toBytes x) = x

items.doc: The little-endian residue codec of `ZMod p`, `bytesFor p` bytes wide.
items.statement: instance instByteCodecZMod (p : ℕ) [NeZero p] : ByteCodec (ZMod p)

items.name: CompPoly.ByteCodec.width_zmod
items.statement: theorem ByteCodec.width_zmod (p : ℕ) [NeZero p] : ByteCodec.width (ZMod p) = bytesFor p

items.statement:
theorem ByteCodec.toBytes_zmod {p : ℕ} [NeZero p] (x : ZMod p) :

items.statement:
theorem ByteCodec.ofBytes?_zmod {p : ℕ} [NeZero p] (v : Vector UInt8 (bytesFor p)) :
