items.note:
## Round trips through the class interfaces

For a type whose codec is `ByteCodec.ofCanonicalNat`, the total decoder inverts the serializer
at the codec's width. Together with `ByteCodec.deserialize_serialize` (the partial decoder) and
the `Serialize.IsInjective` instances, this is the full round-trip story a protocol relies on.

items.name: CompPoly.CanonicalNat.deserialize_serialize
items.doc:
The total decoder inverts the serializer at the codec's own width, whenever the codec is
the one derived from canonical naturals.
items.statement:
theorem CanonicalNat.deserialize_serialize {F : Type u} [CanonicalNat F] [inst : ByteCodec F]
    (h : inst = ByteCodec.ofCanonicalNat F) (x : F) :
    (Deserialize.deserialize (serialize x : Vector UInt8 (ByteCodec.width F)) : F) = x

items.name: CompPoly.CanonicalNat.deserialize_serialize_byteArray
items.statement:
theorem CanonicalNat.deserialize_serialize_byteArray {F : Type u} [CanonicalNat F]
    [inst : ByteCodec F] (h : inst = ByteCodec.ofCanonicalNat F) (x : F) :
    (Deserialize.deserialize (serialize x : ByteArray) : F) = x

items.name: CompPoly.deserialize_serialize_zmod
items.doc: `ZMod p`: the total decoder inverts the serializer.
items.statement:
theorem deserialize_serialize_zmod {p : ℕ} [NeZero p] (x : ZMod p) :
    (Deserialize.deserialize (serialize x : ByteArray) : ZMod p) = x

modules.title: Fixed-width byte codecs
modules.doc:
`ByteCodec F` is a fixed-width byte encoding of `F` with a decoder that succeeds on every
encoding. Its single law, `ofBytes?_toBytes`, makes `toBytes` injective, and from it the
protocol-facing classes follow for free: `HasSize F UInt8`, `Serialize F ByteArray` with
`Serialize.IsInjective`, `DeserializeOption`, and `Serde`, together with the same for
`Vector UInt8 (width F)`.

The encoding is a property of the *value*, not of the carrier: two carriers of the same field
must give the same bytes for the same element. Scalar fields derive their codec from
`CanonicalNat` (`ByteCodec.ofCanonicalNat`, in `CompPoly.Data.Bytes.CanonicalNat`); composite
types such as extensions and degree-bounded polynomials concatenate the codecs of their parts.

items.name: CompPoly.ByteCodec
items.doc: A fixed-width byte encoding of `F` whose decoder recovers every encoded element.
items.statement:
class ByteCodec (F : Type u) where
  /-- The number of bytes of every encoding. -/
  width : ℕ
  /-- Encode an element. -/
  toBytes : F → Vector UInt8 width
  /-- Decode `width` bytes, failing on strings that encode no element. -/
  ofBytes? : Vector UInt8 width → Option F
  ofBytes?_toBytes (x : F) : ofBytes? (toBytes x) = some x

items.name: CompPoly.ByteCodec.toBytes_injective
items.statement: theorem toBytes_injective : Function.Injective (toBytes : F → Vector UInt8 (width F))

items.name: CompPoly.ByteCodec.toBytes_inj
items.statement: theorem toBytes_inj {x y : F} : toBytes x = toBytes y ↔ x = y

items.name: CompPoly.ByteCodec.toByteArray
items.doc: The encoding as a `ByteArray` of size `width F`.
items.statement: def toByteArray (x : F) : ByteArray

items.name: CompPoly.ByteCodec.data_toByteArray
items.statement: theorem data_toByteArray (x : F) : (toByteArray x).data = (toBytes x).toArray

items.name: CompPoly.ByteCodec.size_toByteArray
items.statement: theorem size_toByteArray (x : F) : (toByteArray x).size = width F

items.name: CompPoly.ByteCodec.toByteArray_injective
items.statement: theorem toByteArray_injective : Function.Injective (toByteArray : F → ByteArray)

items.name: CompPoly.ByteCodec.ofByteArray?
items.doc: Decode a `ByteArray`, failing unless it has size `width F` and encodes an element.
items.statement: def ofByteArray? (b : ByteArray) : Option F

items.name: CompPoly.ByteCodec.ofByteArray?_toByteArray
items.statement: theorem ofByteArray?_toByteArray (x : F) : ofByteArray? (toByteArray x) = some x

items.name: CompPoly.ByteCodec.serialize_eq_toByteArray
items.statement: theorem serialize_eq_toByteArray (x : F) : (serialize x : ByteArray) = toByteArray x

items.name: CompPoly.ByteCodec.serialize_eq_toBytes
items.statement:
theorem serialize_eq_toBytes (x : F) :
    (serialize x : Vector UInt8 (width F)) = toBytes x

items.name: CompPoly.ByteCodec.deserialize_byteArray_eq
items.statement:
theorem deserialize_byteArray_eq (b : ByteArray) :
    (DeserializeOption.deserialize b : Option F) = ofByteArray? b

items.name: CompPoly.ByteCodec.deserialize_vector_eq
items.statement:
theorem deserialize_vector_eq (v : Vector UInt8 (width F)) :
    (DeserializeOption.deserialize v : Option F) = ofBytes? v

items.name: CompPoly.ByteCodec.deserialize_serialize
items.statement:
theorem deserialize_serialize (x : F) :
    (DeserializeOption.deserialize (serialize x : ByteArray) : Option F) = some x

modules.title: Self-delimiting byte codecs
modules.doc:
A variable-length type such as a polynomial cannot have a `ByteCodec`, whose width is fixed.
What it can have is a *self-delimiting* encoding: a decoder that reads exactly the bytes of one
encoding from the front of a stream and returns the rest. `DelimitedCodec α` is that pair,
with the one law `decode? (encode x ++ rest) = some (x, rest)`, stated for the `Valid x` the
format can represent. Every fixed-width codec is a delimited codec with `Valid = True`
(`DelimitedCodec.ofByteCodec`).

Lengths, counts, and exponents are framed as `u64` little-endian words, the arkworks layout,
so a natural is `Valid` when it is below `2 ^ 64` and a list when its length is and its
entries are. `Serialize.IsInjective` is derived only for `Total` codecs, where everything is
valid; for the others the injectivity theorem `encode_inj` carries the validity hypotheses.
Composite codecs for lists, pairs, and fixed-length vectors are built here, and the polynomial
codecs in `CompPoly.Univariate.Bytes`, `CompPoly.Multivariate.Bytes`, and
`CompPoly.Bivariate.Bytes` are assembled from them.

items.name: CompPoly.DelimitedCodec
items.doc:
A self-delimiting byte encoding of `α`: `decode?` reads one encoding off the front of a
stream and returns the remainder. `Valid` marks the elements the format represents.
items.statement:
class DelimitedCodec (α : Type u) where
  /-- Encode an element. -/
  encode : α → List UInt8
  /-- Read one encoding from the front of a stream, returning the element and the rest. -/
  decode? : List UInt8 → Option (α × List UInt8)
  /-- The elements the format can represent. -/
  Valid : α → Prop
  decode?_encode_append (x : α) (rest : List UInt8) (h : Valid x) :
    decode? (encode x ++ rest) = some (x, rest)

items.name: CompPoly.DelimitedCodec.Total
items.doc: A codec every element of whose type is valid.
items.statement:
class Total (α : Type u) [DelimitedCodec α] : Prop where
  valid (x : α) : Valid x

items.name: CompPoly.DelimitedCodec.decode?_encode
items.statement: theorem decode?_encode {x : α} (h : Valid x) : decode? (encode x) = some (x, [])

items.name: CompPoly.DelimitedCodec.encode_inj
items.statement: theorem encode_inj {x y : α} (hx : Valid x) (hy : Valid y) (h : encode x = encode y) : x = y

items.name: CompPoly.DelimitedCodec.encode_injective
items.statement: theorem encode_injective [Total α] : Function.Injective (encode : α → List UInt8)

items.name: CompPoly.DelimitedCodec.toByteArray
items.doc: The encoding as a `ByteArray`.
items.statement: def toByteArray (x : α) : ByteArray

items.name: CompPoly.DelimitedCodec.ofByteArray?
items.doc: Decode a `ByteArray` holding exactly one encoding.
items.statement: def ofByteArray? (b : ByteArray) : Option α

items.name: CompPoly.DelimitedCodec.ofByteArray?_toByteArray
items.statement: theorem ofByteArray?_toByteArray {x : α} (h : Valid x) : ofByteArray? (toByteArray x) = some x

items.name: CompPoly.DelimitedCodec.toByteArray_inj
items.statement:
theorem toByteArray_inj {x y : α} (hx : Valid x) (hy : Valid y)
    (h : toByteArray x = toByteArray y) : x = y

items.note:
The protocol-facing instances are low priority so that a type with a `ByteCodec` keeps the
fixed-width instances of `CompPoly.Data.Bytes.Codec`; the two agree byte for byte
(`toByteArray_ofByteCodec`), but only one should be the canonical instance.

items.name: CompPoly.DelimitedCodec.serialize_eq
items.statement: theorem serialize_eq (x : α) : (serialize x : ByteArray) = toByteArray x

items.name: CompPoly.DelimitedCodec.deserialize_eq
items.statement:
theorem deserialize_eq (b : ByteArray) :
    (DeserializeOption.deserialize b : Option α) = ofByteArray? b

items.name: CompPoly.DelimitedCodec.deserialize_serialize
items.statement:
theorem deserialize_serialize {x : α} (h : Valid x) :
    (DeserializeOption.deserialize (serialize x : ByteArray) : Option α) = some x

items.name: CompPoly.DelimitedCodec.ofByteCodec
items.doc: A fixed-width codec read as a delimited one: `width` bytes, every element valid.
items.statement: instance (priority := low) ofByteCodec {β : Type v} [ByteCodec β] : DelimitedCodec β

items.name: CompPoly.DelimitedCodec.valid_ofByteCodec
items.statement: theorem valid_ofByteCodec {β : Type v} [ByteCodec β] (x : β) : Valid x ↔ True

items.name: CompPoly.DelimitedCodec.encode_ofByteCodec
items.statement:
theorem encode_ofByteCodec {β : Type v} [ByteCodec β] (x : β) :
    encode x = (ByteCodec.toBytes x).toList

items.name: CompPoly.DelimitedCodec.toByteArray_ofByteCodec
items.doc: Read as a delimited codec, a fixed-width codec produces the same bytes.
items.statement:
theorem toByteArray_ofByteCodec {β : Type v} [ByteCodec β] (x : β) :
    DelimitedCodec.toByteArray x = ByteCodec.toByteArray x

items.name: CompPoly.DelimitedCodec.encodeU64
items.doc: The `u64` little-endian framing of a natural: lengths, counts, exponents.
items.statement: def encodeU64 (n : ℕ) : List UInt8

items.name: CompPoly.DelimitedCodec.decodeU64?
items.doc: Read a `u64` little-endian word from the front of a stream.
items.statement: def decodeU64? (l : List UInt8) : Option (ℕ × List UInt8)

items.name: CompPoly.DelimitedCodec.length_encodeU64
items.statement: theorem length_encodeU64 (n : ℕ) : (encodeU64 n).length = 8

items.name: CompPoly.DelimitedCodec.decodeU64?_encodeU64_append
items.statement:
theorem decodeU64?_encodeU64_append {n : ℕ} (h : n < 2 ^ 64) (rest : List UInt8) :
    decodeU64? (encodeU64 n ++ rest) = some (n, rest)

items.name: CompPoly.DelimitedCodec.instNat
items.doc: Naturals framed as `u64` words; valid below `2 ^ 64`.
items.statement: instance instNat : DelimitedCodec ℕ

items.name: CompPoly.DelimitedCodec.valid_nat
items.statement: theorem valid_nat (n : ℕ) : Valid n ↔ n < 2 ^ 64

items.name: CompPoly.DelimitedCodec.encode_nat
items.statement: theorem encode_nat (n : ℕ) : encode n = encodeU64 n

items.name: CompPoly.DelimitedCodec.encodeList
items.doc: The concatenated encodings of a list, with no framing.
items.statement: def encodeList (l : List α) : List UInt8

items.name: CompPoly.DelimitedCodec.encodeList_nil
items.statement: theorem encodeList_nil : encodeList ([] : List α) = []

items.name: CompPoly.DelimitedCodec.encodeList_cons
items.statement:
theorem encodeList_cons (x : α) (l : List α) :
    encodeList (x :: l) = encode x ++ encodeList l

items.name: CompPoly.DelimitedCodec.decodeN?
items.doc: Read `m` consecutive encodings from the front of a stream.
items.statement: def decodeN? : ℕ → List UInt8 → Option (List α × List UInt8)

items.name: CompPoly.DelimitedCodec.decodeN?_encodeList_append
items.statement:
theorem decodeN?_encodeList_append {l : List α} (hv : ∀ x ∈ l, Valid x) (rest : List UInt8) :
    decodeN? l.length (encodeList l ++ rest) = some (l, rest)

items.name: CompPoly.DelimitedCodec.instList
items.doc:
Lists: a `u64` count, then the encodings. Valid when the count fits and the entries are
valid.
items.statement: instance instList : DelimitedCodec (List α)

items.name: CompPoly.DelimitedCodec.valid_list
items.statement: theorem valid_list (l : List α) : Valid l ↔ l.length < 2 ^ 64 ∧ ∀ x ∈ l, Valid x

items.name: CompPoly.DelimitedCodec.encode_list
items.statement: theorem encode_list (l : List α) : encode l = encodeU64 l.length ++ encodeList l

items.name: CompPoly.DelimitedCodec.instProd
items.doc: Pairs: the first encoding, then the second.
items.statement: instance instProd {β : Type v} [DelimitedCodec β] : DelimitedCodec (α × β)

items.name: CompPoly.DelimitedCodec.valid_prod
items.statement: theorem valid_prod {β : Type v} [DelimitedCodec β] (p : α × β) : Valid p ↔ Valid p.1 ∧ Valid p.2

items.name: CompPoly.DelimitedCodec.vectorOfList?
items.doc: A list of exactly `n` entries as a vector.
items.statement: def vectorOfList? {γ : Type v} (n : ℕ) (xs : List γ) : Option (Vector γ n)

items.name: CompPoly.DelimitedCodec.vectorOfList?_toList
items.statement:
theorem vectorOfList?_toList {γ : Type v} {n : ℕ} (v : Vector γ n) :
    vectorOfList? n v.toList = some v

items.name: CompPoly.DelimitedCodec.vector
items.doc:
Fixed-length vectors of delimited elements: the `n` encodings with no count. Not an
instance, since a vector of fixed-width elements already has a codec through
`ByteCodec.instVector`; use it for element types without a `ByteCodec`.
items.statement: def vector (n : ℕ) : DelimitedCodec (Vector α n)

modules.title: Little-endian byte encodings of naturals
modules.doc:
The one encoder every fixed-width serialization in CompPoly is built from: a natural number
becomes exactly `w` bytes, least significant first, and `w` bytes become a natural.

* `toListLE w n` / `ofListLE` on `List UInt8`, with the round-trip laws
  `ofListLE_toListLE` (as `n % 256 ^ w`, hence exact below `256 ^ w`) and
  `toListLE_ofListLE`, and the concatenation law `ofListLE_append`.
* `toVecLE` / `ofVecLE` and `toByteArrayLE` / `ofByteArrayLE`, the same maps on `Vector UInt8 w`
  and `ByteArray`.
* `bytesFor bound`, the number of bytes needed to hold every natural below `bound`, with
  `le_pow_bytesFor : bound ≤ 256 ^ bytesFor bound`. It is `Nat.log2`-based so that the kernel
  evaluates it on numerals by `decide`.

The layout is the one arkworks and plonky3 use for field elements: the canonical integer,
little-endian, padded to a fixed width.

items.name: CompPoly.Bytes.toListLE
items.doc: The `w` little-endian bytes of `n`; bits above `8 * w` are dropped.
items.statement: def toListLE : ℕ → ℕ → List UInt8

items.name: CompPoly.Bytes.ofListLE
items.doc: The natural with the given little-endian bytes.
items.statement: def ofListLE : List UInt8 → ℕ

items.name: CompPoly.Bytes.toListLE_zero
items.statement: theorem toListLE_zero (n : ℕ) : toListLE 0 n = []

items.name: CompPoly.Bytes.toListLE_succ
items.statement:
theorem toListLE_succ (w n : ℕ) :
    toListLE (w + 1) n = UInt8.ofNat (n % 256) :: toListLE w (n / 256)

items.name: CompPoly.Bytes.ofListLE_nil
items.statement: theorem ofListLE_nil : ofListLE [] = 0

items.name: CompPoly.Bytes.ofListLE_cons
items.statement:
theorem ofListLE_cons (b : UInt8) (bs : List UInt8) :
    ofListLE (b :: bs) = b.toNat + 256 * ofListLE bs

items.name: CompPoly.Bytes.length_toListLE
items.statement: theorem length_toListLE (w n : ℕ) : (toListLE w n).length = w

items.name: CompPoly.Bytes.ofListLE_toListLE
items.statement: theorem ofListLE_toListLE (w n : ℕ) : ofListLE (toListLE w n) = n % 256 ^ w

items.name: CompPoly.Bytes.ofListLE_toListLE_of_lt
items.statement: theorem ofListLE_toListLE_of_lt {w n : ℕ} (h : n < 256 ^ w) : ofListLE (toListLE w n) = n

items.name: CompPoly.Bytes.ofListLE_lt
items.statement: theorem ofListLE_lt (l : List UInt8) : ofListLE l < 256 ^ l.length

items.name: CompPoly.Bytes.toListLE_ofListLE
items.statement: theorem toListLE_ofListLE (l : List UInt8) : toListLE l.length (ofListLE l) = l

items.name: CompPoly.Bytes.toListLE_inj_of_lt
items.statement:
theorem toListLE_inj_of_lt {w n m : ℕ} (hn : n < 256 ^ w) (hm : m < 256 ^ w)
    (h : toListLE w n = toListLE w m) : n = m

items.name: CompPoly.Bytes.ofListLE_append
items.statement:
theorem ofListLE_append (l₁ l₂ : List UInt8) :
    ofListLE (l₁ ++ l₂) = ofListLE l₁ + 256 ^ l₁.length * ofListLE l₂

items.name: CompPoly.Bytes.bytesFor
items.doc:
The number of bytes needed to hold every natural below `bound`: one byte for `bound ≤ 256`,
and in general the least `w` with `bound ≤ 256 ^ w`, except that `bound ≤ 1` still takes one
byte. Defined through `Nat.log2` so that the kernel evaluates it on numerals.
items.statement: def bytesFor (bound : ℕ) : ℕ

items.name: CompPoly.Bytes.bytesFor_pos
items.statement: theorem bytesFor_pos (bound : ℕ) : 0 < bytesFor bound

items.name: CompPoly.Bytes.le_pow_bytesFor
items.statement: theorem le_pow_bytesFor (bound : ℕ) : bound ≤ 256 ^ bytesFor bound

items.name: CompPoly.Bytes.bytesFor_two_pow
items.doc:
The width of a power of two: `k` bits need `⌈k / 8⌉` bytes. Stated so that a bit-pattern
type's width is a small numeral computation rather than a kernel evaluation of `2 ^ k`.
items.statement: theorem bytesFor_two_pow {k : ℕ} (hk : 0 < k) : bytesFor (2 ^ k) = (k + 7) / 8

items.name: CompPoly.Bytes.toVecLE
items.doc: The `w` little-endian bytes of `n` as a vector.
items.statement: def toVecLE (w n : ℕ) : Vector UInt8 w

items.name: CompPoly.Bytes.ofVecLE
items.doc: The natural with the given little-endian bytes.
items.statement: def ofVecLE {w : ℕ} (v : Vector UInt8 w) : ℕ

items.name: CompPoly.Bytes.toList_toVecLE
items.statement: theorem toList_toVecLE (w n : ℕ) : (toVecLE w n).toList = toListLE w n

items.name: CompPoly.Bytes.ofVecLE_toVecLE
items.statement: theorem ofVecLE_toVecLE (w n : ℕ) : ofVecLE (toVecLE w n) = n % 256 ^ w

items.name: CompPoly.Bytes.ofVecLE_toVecLE_of_lt
items.statement: theorem ofVecLE_toVecLE_of_lt {w n : ℕ} (h : n < 256 ^ w) : ofVecLE (toVecLE w n) = n

items.name: CompPoly.Bytes.ofVecLE_lt
items.statement: theorem ofVecLE_lt {w : ℕ} (v : Vector UInt8 w) : ofVecLE v < 256 ^ w

items.name: CompPoly.Bytes.toVecLE_ofVecLE
items.statement: theorem toVecLE_ofVecLE {w : ℕ} (v : Vector UInt8 w) : toVecLE w (ofVecLE v) = v

items.name: CompPoly.Bytes.toVecLE_inj_of_lt
items.statement:
theorem toVecLE_inj_of_lt {w n m : ℕ} (hn : n < 256 ^ w) (hm : m < 256 ^ w)
    (h : toVecLE w n = toVecLE w m) : n = m

items.name: CompPoly.Bytes.toByteArrayLE
items.doc: The `w` little-endian bytes of `n` as a `ByteArray`.
items.statement: def toByteArrayLE (w n : ℕ) : ByteArray

items.name: CompPoly.Bytes.ofByteArrayLE
items.doc: The natural with the given little-endian bytes.
items.statement: def ofByteArrayLE (b : ByteArray) : ℕ

items.name: CompPoly.Bytes.size_toByteArrayLE
items.statement: theorem size_toByteArrayLE (w n : ℕ) : (toByteArrayLE w n).size = w

items.name: CompPoly.Bytes.data_toByteArrayLE
items.statement:
theorem data_toByteArrayLE (w n : ℕ) :
    (toByteArrayLE w n).data = (toListLE w n).toArray

items.name: CompPoly.Bytes.ofByteArrayLE_toByteArrayLE
items.statement: theorem ofByteArrayLE_toByteArrayLE (w n : ℕ) : ofByteArrayLE (toByteArrayLE w n) = n % 256 ^ w

items.name: CompPoly.Bytes.ofByteArrayLE_toByteArrayLE_of_lt
items.statement:
theorem ofByteArrayLE_toByteArrayLE_of_lt {w n : ℕ} (h : n < 256 ^ w) :
    ofByteArrayLE (toByteArrayLE w n) = n

items.name: CompPoly.Bytes.toByteArrayLE_inj_of_lt
items.statement:
theorem toByteArrayLE_inj_of_lt {w n m : ℕ} (hn : n < 256 ^ w) (hm : m < 256 ^ w)
    (h : toByteArrayLE w n = toByteArrayLE w m) : n = m

modules.title: Byte codecs of vectors
modules.doc:
A `Vector F n` encodes as the concatenation of the encodings of its entries, `n * width F`
bytes, and decodes entry by entry. This is the codec of every fixed-length composite: an
extension field element is its coefficient vector, a multilinear polynomial its evaluation
vector, a degree-bounded univariate polynomial its padded coefficient vector. It matches how
arkworks and plonky3 serialize extension fields and coefficient lists.

`Deserialize (Vector F n) (Vector UInt8 (n * k))` likewise decodes total, entry by entry, from
any per-entry total decoder, which is how a vector of challenges is read from a byte sponge.

items.name: CompPoly.ByteCodec.ofBytesList?
items.doc: Decode a list of exactly `width F` bytes.
items.statement: def ofBytesList? (l : List UInt8) : Option F

items.name: CompPoly.ByteCodec.ofBytesList?_toList
items.statement: theorem ofBytesList?_toList (x : F) : ofBytesList? (toBytes x).toList = some x

items.name: CompPoly.ByteCodec.encodeList
items.doc: The concatenated encodings of a list.
items.statement: def encodeList (l : List F) : List UInt8

items.name: CompPoly.ByteCodec.encodeList_nil
items.statement: theorem encodeList_nil : encodeList ([] : List F) = []

items.name: CompPoly.ByteCodec.encodeList_cons
items.statement:
theorem encodeList_cons (x : F) (l : List F) :
    encodeList (x :: l) = (toBytes x).toList ++ encodeList l

items.name: CompPoly.ByteCodec.length_encodeList
items.statement: theorem length_encodeList (l : List F) : (encodeList l).length = l.length * width F

items.name: CompPoly.ByteCodec.decodeList
items.doc: Decode `m` consecutive encodings, failing on leftover bytes.
items.statement: def decodeList : ℕ → List UInt8 → Option (List F)

items.name: CompPoly.ByteCodec.decodeList_encodeList_of_length
items.statement:
theorem decodeList_encodeList_of_length {m : ℕ} {l : List F} (h : l.length = m) :
    decodeList m (encodeList l) = some l

items.name: CompPoly.ByteCodec.decodeList_encodeList
items.statement: theorem decodeList_encodeList (l : List F) : decodeList l.length (encodeList l) = some l

items.name: CompPoly.ByteCodec.instVector
items.doc: The concatenation codec of `Vector F n`: `n * width F` bytes.
items.statement: instance instVector (n : ℕ) : ByteCodec (Vector F n)

items.name: CompPoly.ByteCodec.width_vector
items.statement: theorem width_vector (n : ℕ) : width (Vector F n) = n * width F

items.name: CompPoly.ByteCodec.toList_toBytes_vector
items.statement:
theorem toList_toBytes_vector {n : ℕ} (v : Vector F n) :
    (toBytes v).toList = encodeList v.toList

items.name: CompPoly.Vector.ofBytesEach
items.doc: Total entry-by-entry decoding of a vector from `n * k` bytes.
items.statement:
def Vector.ofBytesEach {F : Type u} {k : ℕ} [Deserialize F (Vector UInt8 k)] (n : ℕ)
    (b : Vector UInt8 (n * k)) : Vector F n

modules.title: Canonical naturals
modules.doc:
`CanonicalNat F` says that every element of `F` has a canonical natural number below a fixed
`bound`, and that every natural reduces to an element by `ofNat`, with `ofNat` acting as
reduction modulo `bound`. The laws make `toNat` a bijection onto `Fin bound`, so `bound` is the
cardinality of `F` and `ofNat` is exactly "the element whose canonical natural is `n % bound`".

For a prime field the canonical natural is the residue in `[0, p)`; for a binary field it is
the bit pattern of the declared basis; for an extension of degree `d` over a base of size `q`
it is the base-`q` expansion of the coefficients.

Serialization is *derived* from this class rather than stated with it. The fixed-width byte
codec of a scalar field is the little-endian bytes of `toNat` (`ByteCodec.ofCanonicalNat` in
`CompPoly.Data.Bytes.CanonicalNat`), and sampling a field element from a longer byte string
is `ofNat` of the string's integer, which is uniform up to a bound proved in `Nat` terms.
Two carriers of the same field agree on `toNat`, so they agree on every derived encoding.

items.name: CompPoly.CanonicalNat
items.doc:
`F` has a canonical natural below `bound` for every element, and every natural reduces to
an element of `F` modulo `bound`. The laws make `toNat` a bijection `F ≃ Fin bound`.
items.statement:
class CanonicalNat (F : Type u) where
  /-- The exclusive upper bound on canonical naturals; equal to the cardinality of `F`. -/
  bound : ℕ
  /-- The canonical natural of an element. -/
  toNat : F → ℕ
  /-- The element with canonical natural `n % bound`. -/
  ofNat : ℕ → F
  toNat_lt (x : F) : toNat x < bound
  ofNat_toNat (x : F) : ofNat (toNat x) = x
  toNat_ofNat_of_lt {n : ℕ} (h : n < bound) : toNat (ofNat n) = n
  ofNat_mod (n : ℕ) : ofNat (n % bound) = ofNat n

items.name: CompPoly.CanonicalNat.bound_pos
items.statement: theorem bound_pos : 0 < bound F

items.name: CompPoly.CanonicalNat.toNat_injective
items.statement: theorem toNat_injective : Function.Injective (toNat : F → ℕ)

items.name: CompPoly.CanonicalNat.toNat_inj
items.statement: theorem toNat_inj {x y : F} : toNat x = toNat y ↔ x = y

items.name: CompPoly.CanonicalNat.toNat_ofNat
items.statement: theorem toNat_ofNat (n : ℕ) : toNat (ofNat (F := F) n) = n % bound F

items.name: CompPoly.CanonicalNat.ofNat?
items.doc: Decode a natural as an element, failing when it is not a canonical natural.
items.statement: def ofNat? (n : ℕ) : Option F

items.name: CompPoly.CanonicalNat.ofNat?_toNat
items.statement: theorem ofNat?_toNat (x : F) : ofNat? (toNat x) = some x

items.name: CompPoly.CanonicalNat.ofNat?_eq_some_iff
items.statement: theorem ofNat?_eq_some_iff {n : ℕ} {x : F} : ofNat? n = some x ↔ n < bound F ∧ toNat x = n

items.name: CompPoly.CanonicalNat.ofNat?_eq_none_iff
items.statement: theorem ofNat?_eq_none_iff {n : ℕ} : ofNat? (F := F) n = none ↔ bound F ≤ n

items.name: CompPoly.CanonicalNat.equivFin
items.doc: The canonical natural as an equivalence with `Fin (bound F)`.
items.statement: def equivFin : F ≃ Fin (bound F)

items.name: CompPoly.CanonicalNat.card_eq
items.doc: The bound is the cardinality of `F`.
items.statement: theorem card_eq [Fintype F] : Fintype.card F = bound F

items.note:
## Constructors

Two ways a concrete type acquires the structure. A fast carrier of a prime field supplies its
own `toNat` together with the conversion from `ZMod p`; a binary field supplies its bit
pattern. Both are `@[instance_reducible]` definitions so an instance can be
`CanonicalNat.ofToField …` or `CanonicalNat.ofBitVec …` directly.

items.name: CompPoly.CanonicalNat.ofToField
items.doc:
The canonical-natural structure of a carrier of `ZMod p`: the carrier's own `toNat`, with
`ofField` as the way back. The hypothesis `toNat_ofField` is the carrier-agreement law, so
every encoding derived from this structure agrees with the one on `ZMod p`.

items.name: CompPoly.CanonicalNat.ofBitVec
items.doc:
The canonical-natural structure of a type presented as `k`-bit patterns: the bit pattern
read as an integer, with `bound = 2 ^ k`.

items.name: CompPoly.instCanonicalNatZMod
items.doc: `ZMod p` with the residue in `[0, p)` as canonical natural.
items.statement: instance instCanonicalNatZMod (p : ℕ) [NeZero p] : CanonicalNat (ZMod p)

items.name: CompPoly.CanonicalNat.bound_zmod
items.statement: theorem CanonicalNat.bound_zmod (p : ℕ) [NeZero p] : CanonicalNat.bound (ZMod p) = p

items.name: CompPoly.CanonicalNat.toNat_zmod
items.statement:
theorem CanonicalNat.toNat_zmod {p : ℕ} [NeZero p] (x : ZMod p) :
    CanonicalNat.toNat x = x.val

items.name: CompPoly.CanonicalNat.ofNat_zmod
items.statement:
theorem CanonicalNat.ofNat_zmod {p : ℕ} [NeZero p] (n : ℕ) :
    CanonicalNat.ofNat (F := ZMod p) n = (n : ZMod p)

modules.title: Dependent casts
modules.doc:
This file contains type classes for dependent or custom cast operations

This allows us to state theorems with more refined casts, without which we cannot make progress in
proving them

items.name: cast_eq_cast_iff
items.statement:
theorem cast_eq_cast_iff {α β γ : Sort u} {h : α = γ} {h' : β = γ} {a : α} {b : β} :
    cast h a = cast h' b ↔ a = cast (h'.trans h.symm) b

items.name: cast_symm
items.statement:
theorem cast_symm {α β : Sort u} {h : α = β} {a : α} {b : β} :
    cast h a = b ↔ a = cast h.symm b

items.name: congrArg₃
items.statement:
theorem congrArg₃ {α β γ δ : Sort*} {f : α → β → γ → δ} {a a' : α} {b b' : β} {c c' : γ}
    (h : a = a') (h' : b = b') (h'' : c = c') : f a b c = f a' b' c'

DCast
items.doc:
`DCast` is a type class for custom cast operations on an indexed type family `β a`

We require the cast operation `dcast`, along with the property that `dcast` reduces to `id` under
reflexivity.
items.statement:
class DCast (α : Sort*) (β : α → Sort*) where
  dcast : ∀ {a a' : α}, a = a' → β a → β a'
  dcast_id : ∀ {a : α}, dcast (Eq.refl a) = id

items.name: dcast_eq
items.statement: theorem dcast_eq : dcast (Eq.refl a) b = b

items.name: dcast_symm
items.statement: theorem dcast_symm (ha : a = a') (hb : dcast ha b = b') : dcast (ha.symm) b' = b

items.name: dcast_trans
items.statement:
theorem dcast_trans (h : a = a') (h' : a' = a'') :
    dcast h' (dcast h b) = dcast (h.trans h') b

items.name: dcast_eq_dcast_iff
items.statement:
theorem dcast_eq_dcast_iff (h : a = a'') (h' : a' = a'') :
    dcast h b = dcast h' b' ↔ b = dcast (h'.trans h.symm) b'

items.name: heq_of_dcast
items.statement: theorem heq_of_dcast (ha : a = a') (hb : dcast ha b = b') : HEq b b'

items.name: dcast_fun
items.statement:
theorem dcast_fun {γ : (a : α) → β a → Sort*} {f : (b : β a) → γ a b} :
    f (dcast rfl b) = dcast (α := β a) (β := γ a) dcast_eq.symm (f b)

items.name: dcast_fun₂
dcast_eq_root_cast
items.statement: theorem dcast_eq_root_cast (h : a = a') : dcast h b = _root_.cast (congrArg β h) b

items.name: DCast₂
items.doc:
`DCast₂` is a type class for custom cast operations on a doubly-indexed type family `γ a b`,
  given an underlying dependent cast `DCast α β`

We require the cast operation `dcast₂`, along with the property that `dcast₂` reduces to `id` under
reflexivity.
items.statement:
class DCast₂ (α : Sort*) (β : α → Sort*) (γ : (a : α) → β a → Sort*) [DCast α β] where
  dcast₂ : ∀ {a a' : α} {b : β a} {b' : β a'},
    (ha : a = a') → (dcast ha b = b') → γ a b → γ a' b'
  dcast₂_id : ∀ {a : α} {b : β a}, dcast₂ (Eq.refl a) dcast_eq = (id : γ a b → γ a b)

items.name: dcast₂_eq
items.statement: theorem dcast₂_eq : dcast₂ (Eq.refl a) dcast_eq c = c

items.name: dcast₂_eq'
items.statement: theorem dcast₂_eq' (h : a = a) (h' : dcast h b = b) : dcast₂ h h' c = c

items.name: dcast₂_symm
items.statement:
theorem dcast₂_symm (ha : a = a') (hb : dcast ha b = b') (hc : dcast₂ ha hb c = c') :
    dcast₂ ha.symm (dcast_symm ha hb) c' = c

items.name: dcast₂_trans
items.statement:
theorem dcast₂_trans (ha : a = a') (ha' : a' = a'')
    (hb : dcast ha b = b') (hb' : dcast ha' b' = b'') :
      dcast₂ ha' hb' (dcast₂ ha hb c) = dcast₂ (ha.trans ha') (by simp [← hb', ← hb]) c

items.name: dcast₂_eq_dcast₂_iff
items.statement:
theorem dcast₂_eq_dcast₂_iff (ha : a = a'') (ha' : a' = a'')
    (hb : dcast ha b = b'') (hb' : dcast ha' b' = b'') :
    dcast₂ ha hb c = dcast₂ ha' hb' c' ↔
      c = dcast₂ (ha'.trans ha.symm)
        ((dcast_eq_dcast_iff ha ha').mp (hb.trans hb'.symm)).symm c'

items.name: dcast₂_dcast
items.statement: theorem dcast₂_dcast : dcast₂ rfl rfl c = dcast dcast_eq.symm c

items.name: instDCast₁₂
items.statement: instance instDCast₁₂ : DCast (β a) (γ a)

items.name: instDCastPSigma
items.statement: instance instDCastPSigma : DCast ((a : α) ×' β a) (fun a => γ a.1 a.2)

items.name: instDCastSigma
items.statement:
instance instDCastSigma {α : Type*} {β : α → Type*} {γ : (a : α) → β a → Type*}

items.name: instDCastForall
items.statement: instance instDCastForall : DCast α (fun a => ∀ b : β a, γ a b)

items.name: DCast₃
items.doc:
`DCast₃` is a type class for custom cast operations on a triply-indexed type family `δ a b c`,
  given underlying dependent casts `DCast α β` and `DCast₂ α β γ`

We require the cast operation `dcast₃`, along with the property that `dcast₃` reduces to `id` under
reflexivity.
items.statement:
class DCast₃ (α : Sort*) (β : α → Sort*) (γ : (a : α) → β a → Sort*)
    (δ : (a : α) → (b : β a) → γ a b → Sort*) [DCast α β] [DCast₂ α β γ] where
  dcast₃ : ∀ {a a' : α} {b : β a} {b' : β a'} {c : γ a b} {c' : γ a' b'},
    (ha : a = a') → (hb : dcast ha b = b') → (hc : dcast₂ ha hb c = c') → δ a b c → δ a' b' c'
  dcast₃_id : ∀ {a : α} {b : β a} {c : γ a b},
    dcast₃ (Eq.refl a) dcast_eq dcast₂_eq = (id : δ a b c → δ a b c)

items.name: dcast₃_eq
items.statement: theorem dcast₃_eq : dcast₃ (Eq.refl a) dcast_eq dcast₂_eq d = d

items.name: dcast₃_symm
items.statement:
theorem dcast₃_symm (ha : a = a') (hb : dcast ha b = b') (hc : dcast₂ ha hb c = c')
    (hd : dcast₃ ha hb hc d = d') :
    dcast₃ ha.symm (dcast_symm ha hb) (dcast₂_symm ha hb hc) d' = d

items.name: dcast₃_trans
items.statement:
theorem dcast₃_trans (ha : a = a') (ha' : a' = a'')
    (hb : dcast ha b = b') (hb' : dcast ha' b' = b'')
    (hc : dcast₂ ha hb c = c') (hc' : dcast₂ ha' hb' c' = c'') :
    dcast₃ ha' hb' hc' (dcast₃ ha hb hc d) =
    dcast₃ (ha.trans ha') (by simp [← hb', ← hb]) (by simp [← hc', ← hc]) d

items.name: dcast₃_eq_dcast₃_iff
items.statement:
theorem dcast₃_eq_dcast₃_iff (ha : a = a') (hb : dcast ha b = b') (hc : dcast₂ ha hb c = c') :
    dcast₃ ha hb hc d = d' ↔ d = dcast₃ ha.symm (dcast_symm ha hb) (dcast₂_symm ha hb hc) d'

items.name: dcast₃_dcast₂
items.statement: theorem dcast₃_dcast₂ : dcast₃ rfl rfl rfl d = dcast₂ dcast_eq.symm dcast₂_dcast.symm d

modules.doc:
A type has a size in units of `β` when it embeds into `Vector β size`. A duplex sponge over
units `β` absorbs and squeezes elements of such a type `size` units at a time.

Ported verbatim from ArkLib (`ArkLib/Data/Classes/HasSize.lean`).

items.name: HasSize
items.doc:
Type class for types that has an injective mapping to a vector of a given length `size` of
another type (often `UInt8`).
items.statement:
class HasSize (α : Type*) (β : Type*) where
  size : Nat
  toFun : α ↪ Vector β size

modules.title: `LawfulBEq` from `DecidableEq`
modules.doc:
A canonical `LawfulBEq` derived from `DecidableEq`, suitable for `letI` use at
call sites that need to satisfy `BEq`/`LawfulBEq` constraints (for example on
`CMvPolynomial` API surfaces) from a `DecidableEq`-only context.

This is intentionally *not* registered as an instance: doing so would conflict
with other `BEq` paths chosen by typeclass synthesis.

items.name: CPoly.lawfulBEqOfDecidableEq
items.doc:
A canonical `LawfulBEq` instance derived from `DecidableEq`. Intended for
`letI` use at call sites that need to satisfy `BEq`/`LawfulBEq` constraints
from a `DecidableEq`-only context.
items.statement:
def lawfulBEqOfDecidableEq {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] :
    @LawfulBEq α (instBEqOfDecidableEq)

modules.title: Serialization and deserialization classes
modules.doc:
Simple type classes for serializing a type into another type, most often `ByteArray` or a
fixed-length `Vector` of units, and for deserializing back, with or without failure.

These declarations are ported verbatim from ArkLib (`ArkLib/Data/Classes/Serde.lean`) so that
CompPoly can supply instances for its field and polynomial types directly. The
statistical-closeness class `Deserialize.CloseToUniform` stays in ArkLib, where the probability
theory it needs already lives; CompPoly proves the counting facts behind it in `Nat` terms.

items.name: Serialize
items.doc:
Type class for types that can be serialized to another type (most often `ByteArray` or
`String`).
items.statement:
class Serialize (α : Type u) (β : Type v) where
  serialize : α → β

items.name: Serialize.IsInjective
items.doc: Type class for injective serialization.
items.statement:
class Serialize.IsInjective (α : Type u) (β : Type v) [inst : Serialize α β] : Prop where
  serialize_inj : Function.Injective inst.serialize

items.name: Deserialize
items.doc:
Type class for types that can be deserialized from another type (most often `ByteArray` or
`String`), which _never_ fails.
items.statement:
class Deserialize (α : Type u) (β : Type v) where
  deserialize : β → α

items.name: DeserializeOption
items.doc:
Type class for types that can be deserialized from another type (most often `ByteArray` or
`String`), returning an `Option` if the deserialization fails.
items.statement:
class DeserializeOption (α : Type u) (β : Type v) where
  deserialize : β → Option α

items.name: Serde
items.doc:
Type class for types that can be serialized and deserialized (with potential failure) to/from
another type (most often `ByteArray` or `String`).
items.statement: class Serde (α : Type u) (β : Type v) extends Serialize α β, DeserializeOption α β

modules.title: Auxiliary lemmas for `Std.DTreeMap`
modules.doc:
Lemmas about `mergeWith` and `filter` on `Std.DTreeMap` (and its internal
implementation) that are used downstream by the multivariate polynomial
representation in `CompPoly.Multivariate.Unlawful`.

Vendored from
[`Verified-zkEVM/ExtTreeMapLemmas`](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/ExtTreeMapLemmas)
(tag `v4.29.1`, commit `3fee686227f18dca03bb7fc42ca5a9275d6cfda6`).

items.name: Std.DTreeMap.Const.get?_foldl_no_touch
items.statement:
theorem Const.get?_foldl_no_touch
    [TransCmp cmp] [LawfulEqCmp cmp]
    (k : α) (f : α → β → β → β)
    (l : List (α × β)) (t : DTreeMap α (fun _ => β) cmp)
    (hno : ∀ p ∈ l, cmp p.1 k ≠ .eq) :
    Const.get? (l.foldl (fun acc p =>
      Const.alter acc p.1 (fun
        | none => some p.2
        | some b₁ => some (f p.1 b₁ p.2))
    ) t) k = Const.get? t k

items.name: Std.DTreeMap.Const.get?_mergeWith
items.statement:
theorem Const.get?_mergeWith [TransCmp cmp] [LawfulEqCmp cmp]
    (f : α → β → β → β) (t₁ t₂ : DTreeMap α (fun _ => β) cmp) (k : α) :
    get? (mergeWith f t₁ t₂) k =
      match get? t₁ k, get? t₂ k with
      | some v₁, some v₂ => some (f k v₁ v₂)
      | some v₁, none => some v₁
      | none, some v₂ => some v₂
      | none, none => none

items.name: Std.DTreeMap.Internal.Impl.Const.get?_filter_with_getKey_pfilter
items.statement:
theorem Internal.Impl.Const.get?_filter_with_getKey_pfilter [Ord α] [TransOrd α]
    (m : DTreeMap.Internal.Impl α (fun _ => β)) (h : m.WF) (f : α → β → Bool) (k : α) :
    Const.get? (m.filter f h.balanced).1 k =
      (Const.get? m k).pfilter (fun v h' =>
        f (m.getKey k ((contains_eq_isSome_get? h).trans
          (Option.isSome_of_eq_some h'))) v)

items.name: Std.DTreeMap.get?_filter_with_getKey_pfilter
items.statement:
theorem get?_filter_with_getKey_pfilter {cmp : α → α → Ordering} [TransCmp cmp]
    (m : DTreeMap α (fun _ => β) cmp) (f : α → β → Bool) (k : α) :
    Const.get? (m.filter f) k =
      (Const.get? m k).pfilter (fun v h' =>
        f (m.getKey k (Const.contains_eq_isSome_get?.trans
          (Option.isSome_of_eq_some h'))) v)

modules.title: Auxiliary lemmas for `Std.ExtDTreeMap`
modules.doc:
Bridge lemma lifting `DTreeMap.get?_filter_with_getKey_pfilter` to
`Std.ExtDTreeMap`, used in turn by the `Std.ExtTreeMap` layer.

Vendored from
[`Verified-zkEVM/ExtTreeMapLemmas`](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/ExtTreeMapLemmas)
(tag `v4.29.1`, commit `3fee686227f18dca03bb7fc42ca5a9275d6cfda6`).

items.name: Std.ExtDTreeMap.get?_filter_with_getKey_pfilter
items.statement:
theorem ExtDTreeMap.get?_filter_with_getKey_pfilter {cmp : α → α → Ordering} [TransCmp cmp]
    (m : ExtDTreeMap α (fun _ => β) cmp) (f : α → β → Bool) (k : α) :
    Const.get? (m.filter f) k =
    (Const.get? m k).pfilter (fun v h' =>
      f (m.getKey k
          (Const.contains_eq_isSome_get?.trans (Option.isSome_of_eq_some h'))) v)

modules.title: Auxiliary lemmas for `Std.ExtTreeMap`
modules.doc:
`mergeWith` and `filter` lemmas for `Std.ExtTreeMap`, used by the multivariate
polynomial representation in `CompPoly.Multivariate.Unlawful`.

Vendored from
[`Verified-zkEVM/ExtTreeMapLemmas`](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/ExtTreeMapLemmas)
(tag `v4.29.1`, commit `3fee686227f18dca03bb7fc42ca5a9275d6cfda6`). The original
imported `Mathlib.Tactic` wholesale; here we narrow to the specific tactic
modules actually needed by the proofs below.

items.name: Std.ExtTreeMap.getElem?_pfilter
items.statement:
theorem getElem?_pfilter
    {cmp : α → α → Ordering} [TransCmp cmp]
    {m : ExtTreeMap α β cmp} {f : α → β → Bool} {k : α} :
    (m.filter f)[k]? =
    m[k]?.pfilter (fun v h' =>
      f (m.getKey k
          (contains_eq_isSome_getElem?.trans (Option.isSome_of_eq_some h'))) v)

items.name: Std.ExtTreeMap.filter_empty
items.statement:
lemma filter_empty {f : α → β → Bool} :
    filter f (∅ : Std.ExtTreeMap α β cmp) = ∅

items.name: Std.ExtTreeMap.getElem?_mergeWith_at
items.statement:
theorem getElem?_mergeWith_at
    {m₁ m₂ : ExtTreeMap α β cmp} {f : α → β → β → β} {k : α} :
  (m₁.mergeWith f m₂)[k]? =
  match m₁[k]?, m₂[k]? with
  | .some v₁, .some v₂ => .some (f k v₁ v₂)
  | .some v₁, .none    => .some v₁
  | .none,    .some v₂ => .some v₂
  | .none,    .none    => .none

items.name: Std.ExtTreeMap.mergeWith_of_mem_mem
items.statement:
lemma mergeWith_of_mem_mem (h₁ : k ∈ m₁) (h₂ : k ∈ m₂) :
    (m₁.mergeWith f m₂)[k]? = .some (f k m₁[k] m₂[k])

items.name: Std.ExtTreeMap.mergeWith_of_mem_left
items.statement:
lemma mergeWith_of_mem_left (h₁ : k ∈ m₁) (h₂ : k ∉ m₂) :
    (m₁.mergeWith f m₂)[k]? = m₁[k]?

items.name: Std.ExtTreeMap.mergeWith_of_mem_right
items.statement:
lemma mergeWith_of_mem_right (h₁ : k ∉ m₁) (h₂ : k ∈ m₂) :
    (m₁.mergeWith f m₂)[k]? = m₂[k]?

items.name: Std.ExtTreeMap.mergeWith_of_not_mem
items.statement:
lemma mergeWith_of_not_mem (h₁ : k ∉ m₁) (h₂ : k ∉ m₂) :
    (m₁.mergeWith f m₂)[k]? = .none

items.name: Std.ExtTreeMap.mergeWith_empty
items.statement:
lemma mergeWith_empty {f : α → β → β → β}
    {cmp : α → α → Ordering} [Std.TransCmp cmp] [Std.LawfulEqCmp cmp]
    {t : ExtTreeMap α β cmp} :
    mergeWith f t ∅ = t

items.name: Std.ExtTreeMap.mergeWith_of_comm
items.statement:
lemma mergeWith_of_comm (h : ∀ {x}, Std.Commutative (f x)) :
    m₁.mergeWith f m₂ = m₂.mergeWith f m₁

items.name: Std.ExtTreeMap.toList_ofList
items.statement: lemma toList_ofList [BEq α] [LawfulBEq α] : ofList (toList m) cmp = m

items.name: Std.ExtTreeMap.getElem?_filter_with_getKey
items.statement:
lemma getElem?_filter_with_getKey {f : α → β → Bool} {k : α} {m : ExtTreeMap α β cmp} :
    (m.filter f)[k]? = m[k]?.filter (f k)

items.name: Std.ExtTreeMap.filter_mem
items.statement: lemma filter_mem (h : k ∈ m) : f k m[k] → (filter f m)[k]? = .some m[k]

items.name: Std.ExtTreeMap.filter_not_mem
items.statement: lemma filter_not_mem (h : k ∉ m) : (filter f m)[k]? = .none

items.name: Std.ExtTreeMap.filter_not_pred

items.name: Fin.succRecOnSameFinType
items.doc:
Recursion principle for `Fin r` that iterates upwards from `0`.
This is useful when the type `Fin r` is fixed and we want to induct on the element.
It's similar to `Fin.inductionOn`, but formulated with an explicit upper bound check.
items.statement:
def Fin.succRecOnSameFinType {motive : Fin r → Sort _}
    (zero : motive (⟨0, Nat.pos_of_neZero r⟩ : Fin r))
    (succ : ∀ i : Fin r, i + 1 < r → motive i → motive (i + 1)) : ∀ (i : Fin r), motive i
  | ⟨0, _⟩ => by exact zero
  | ⟨Nat.succ i_val, h⟩ => by -- ⊢ motive ⟨i_val.succ, h⟩
    simp only [Nat.succ_eq_add_one] at h
    set i : Fin r

items.name: Fin.predRecOnSameFinType
items.doc:
Recursion principle for `Fin r` that iterates downwards from `r - 1`.
This is useful for definitions that process elements in reverse order, like `foldr`.
items.statement:
def Fin.predRecOnSameFinType {motive : Fin r → Sort _}
    (last : motive (⟨r - 1, by
      have h_r_ne_0: r ≠ 0 := by exact NeZero.ne r
      omega
    ⟩ : Fin r))
    (succ : ∀ i : Fin r, i.val > 0 → motive i → motive (⟨i.val - 1, by omega⟩ : Fin r))
    (i : Fin r): motive i

items.name: Fin.sum_univ_split_even_add_odd
items.doc:
Splits a sum over `Fin (2 * r)` into a sum over even indices and a sum over odd indices.
Useful for Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) type recursions.
items.statement:
theorem Fin.sum_univ_split_even_add_odd {r : ℕ} {M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M]
    (f : Fin (2 * r) → M) :
    ∑ i : Fin (2 * r), f i
    = (∑ i : Fin r, f ⟨2 * i.val, by have := i.isLt; omega⟩)
    + (∑ i : Fin r, f ⟨2 * i.val + 1, by have := i.isLt; omega⟩)

items.name: Fin.sum_univ_pow_two_even_add_odd
items.doc: Specialized form of `Fin.sum_univ_split_even_add_odd` for `r = 2 ^ n`.
items.statement:
theorem Fin.sum_univ_pow_two_even_add_odd {n : ℕ} {M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M] (f : ℕ → M) :
    (∑ i : Fin (2 ^ n), f (2 * i)) + (∑ i : Fin (2 ^ n), f (2 * i + 1))
    = ∑ i : Fin (2 ^ (n + 1)), f i

items.name: sum_Icc_split
items.doc:
Splits a sum over an interval `[a, c]` into two sums over `[a, b]` and `[b+1, c]`.
Requires `a ≤ b ≤ c`.
items.statement:
theorem sum_Icc_split {α : Type*} [AddCommMonoid α] (f : ℕ → α) (a b c : ℕ)
    (h₁ : a ≤ b) (h₂ : b ≤ c):
    ∑ i ∈ Finset.Icc a c, f i = ∑ i ∈ Finset.Icc a b, f i + ∑ i ∈ Finset.Icc (b+1) c, f i

modules.title: Useful Notation
modules.doc:
We define notation `R[X σ]` to be `MvPolynomial σ R`.

  For a Finset `s` and a natural number `n`, we also define `s ^ᶠ n` to be
  `Fintype.piFinset (fun (_ : Fin n) => s)`. This matches the intuition that `s ^ᶠ n`
  is the set of all tuples of length `n` with elements in `s`.

theorem getBit_repr {ℓ : Nat} :
    ∀ j, j < 2^ℓ → j = ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 0 (ℓ-1), (getBit k j) * 2^k

items.name: Nat.getBit_repr_univ
items.statement:
theorem getBit_repr_univ {ℓ : Nat} :
    ∀ j, j < 2^ℓ → j = ∑ k ∈ Finset.univ (α:=Fin ℓ), (getBit k j) * 2^k.val

items.name: Nat.getBit_injective
items.doc: Two natural numbers with identical bits at every position are equal.
items.statement: theorem getBit_injective (a b : ℕ) (h : ∀ k, getBit k a = getBit k b) : a = b

items.name: Nat.getBit_repr_unique
items.doc:
The binary representation of a number via `getBit` is unique: any sequence of
0/1 coefficients that sums to `j` must agree with `getBit` at each position.
items.statement:
theorem getBit_repr_unique {ℓ : ℕ} {j : ℕ} (h_j : j < 2 ^ ℓ)
    (c : ℕ → ℕ) (h_bin : ∀ k, k < ℓ → c k = 0 ∨ c k = 1)
    (h_sum : j = ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 0 (ℓ - 1), c k * 2 ^ k) :
    ∀ k, k < ℓ → c k = getBit k j

items.name: Nat.getLowBits_succ
items.statement:
lemma getLowBits_succ {n: ℕ} (numLowBits: ℕ) :
    getLowBits (numLowBits + 1) n = getLowBits numLowBits n
    + (getBit numLowBits n) <<< numLowBits

items.name: Nat.getHighBits_no_shl
items.doc: This takes a argument for the number of lowBitss to remove from the number
items.statement: def getHighBits_no_shl (numLowBits : ℕ) (n : ℕ) : ℕ

items.name: Nat.getHighBits
items.statement: def getHighBits (numLowBits : ℕ) (n : ℕ) : ℕ

items.name: Nat.and_highBits_lowBits_eq_zero
items.statement:
theorem and_highBits_lowBits_eq_zero {n : ℕ} (numLowBits : ℕ) :
    getHighBits numLowBits n &&& getLowBits numLowBits n = 0

items.name: Nat.num_eq_highBits_add_lowBits
items.statement:
lemma num_eq_highBits_add_lowBits {n: ℕ} (numLowBits: ℕ) :
    n = getHighBits numLowBits n + getLowBits numLowBits n

items.name: Nat.num_eq_highBits_xor_lowBits
items.statement:
lemma num_eq_highBits_xor_lowBits {n: ℕ} (numLowBits: ℕ) :
    n = getHighBits numLowBits n ^^^ getLowBits numLowBits n

items.name: Nat.getBit_of_highBits
items.statement:
lemma getBit_of_highBits {n: ℕ} (numLowBits : ℕ) :
    ∀ k, getBit k (getHighBits numLowBits n) = if k < numLowBits then 0 else getBit (k) (n)

items.name: Nat.getBit_of_highBits_no_shl
items.statement:
lemma getBit_of_highBits_no_shl {n: ℕ} (numLowBits : ℕ) :
    ∀ k, getBit k (getHighBits_no_shl numLowBits n) = getBit (k + numLowBits) (n)

items.name: Nat.getBit_of_lt_two_pow
items.statement:
lemma getBit_of_lt_two_pow {n: ℕ} (a: Fin (2^n)) (k: ℕ) :
    getBit k a = if k < n then getBit k a else 0

items.name: Nat.exist_bit_diff_if_diff
items.statement:
lemma exist_bit_diff_if_diff {n: ℕ} (a: Fin (2^n)) (b: Fin (2^n)) (h_a_ne_b: a ≠ b) :
    ∃ k: Fin n, getBit k a ≠ getBit k b

items.name: Nat.binaryFinMapToNat
items.statement: def binaryFinMapToNat {n : ℕ} (m : Fin n → ℕ) (h_binary : ∀ j: Fin n, m j ≤ 1) : Fin (2^n)

items.name: Nat.getBit_of_binaryFinMapToNat
items.statement:
lemma getBit_of_binaryFinMapToNat {n : ℕ} (m : Fin n → ℕ) (h_binary: ∀ j: Fin n, m j ≤ 1) :
    ∀ k: ℕ, Nat.getBit k (binaryFinMapToNat m h_binary).val
      = if h_k: k < n then m ⟨k, by omega⟩ else 0

items.name: Nat.getMiddleBits
items.doc: Middle bits: take `len` bits starting at `offset` from `n`.
items.statement: def getMiddleBits (offset len n : ℕ) : ℕ

items.name: Nat.getBit_of_middleBits
items.doc: Bit-level characterization of middle bits.
items.statement:
lemma getBit_of_middleBits {n offset len k : ℕ} :
    getBit k (getMiddleBits offset len n) = if k < len then getBit (k + offset) n else 0

items.name: Nat.getMiddleBits_lt_two_pow
items.doc: Middle bits are strictly less than `2^len`.
items.statement:
lemma getMiddleBits_lt_two_pow {n offset len : ℕ} :
    getMiddleBits offset len n < 2 ^ len

items.name: Nat.getMiddleBits_eq_mod
items.doc: Middle bits as a modulus form.
items.statement:
lemma getMiddleBits_eq_mod {n offset len : ℕ} :
    getMiddleBits offset len n = (n >>> offset) % (2 ^ len)

items.name: Nat.and_shl_eq_zero_of_lt_two_pow
items.statement: lemma and_shl_eq_zero_of_lt_two_pow {a n b : ℕ} (hb : b < 2 ^ n) : (a <<< n) &&& b = 0

items.name: Nat.joinBits
items.doc: Concatenate high (length m) and low (length n) using shifts.
items.statement: def joinBits {n m : ℕ} (low : Fin (2 ^ n)) (high : Fin (2 ^ m)) : Fin (2 ^ (m+n))

items.name: Nat.getBit_joinBits
items.doc: Bit characterization: below cut use low, above cut use high.
items.statement:
lemma getBit_joinBits {n m k : ℕ} (low : Fin (2 ^ n)) (high : Fin (2 ^ m)) :
    getBit k (joinBits low high).val = if k < n then getBit k low.val
      else getBit (k - n) high.val

items.name: Nat.getLowBits_joinBits
items.doc: Low n bits of joinBits are exactly low.
items.statement:
lemma getLowBits_joinBits {n m : ℕ} (low : Fin (2 ^ n)) (high : Fin (2 ^ m)) :
    getLowBits n (joinBits low high).val = low.val

items.name: Nat.getHighBits_no_shl_joinBits
items.doc: Dropping low n bits by shifting right recovers high.
items.statement:
lemma getHighBits_no_shl_joinBits {n m : ℕ} (low : Fin (2 ^ n)) (high : Fin (2 ^ m)) :
    getHighBits_no_shl n (joinBits low high).val = high.val
