modules.title: Auxiliary lemmas for `Option`

items.name: Option.filter_eq_self
items.doc:
`Option.filter` leaves its argument alone exactly when the predicate holds of the contained
value. The `Option` analogue of `List.filter_eq_self` and `Array.filter_eq_self`.
items.statement:
theorem filter_eq_self {α : Type*} {o : Option α} {p : α → Bool} :
    o.filter p = o ↔ ∀ a ∈ o, p a

modules.title: Frobenius polynomial identities
modules.doc:
This file establishes fundamental identities involving the Frobenius endomorphism for polynomials
over finite fields. The main results include factorization identities, Frobenius polynomial
identities, and divisibility conditions for irreducible polynomials.

## Main Definitions and Theorems

1. **Field Vanishing Polynomial Equality:**
   - `prod_X_sub_C_eq_X_pow_card_sub_X`: The identity `∏_{c ∈ Fq} (X - c) = X^q - X` in `Fq[X]`
   - `prod_X_sub_C_eq_X_pow_card_sub_X_in_L`: Lifted version for field extensions `L[X]`
   - `prod_poly_sub_C_eq_poly_pow_card_sub_poly_in_L`: General version
     `∏_{c ∈ Fq} (p - c) = p^q - p` for any polynomial `p` in `L[X]`

2. **Frobenius Polynomial Identity:**
   - `frobenius_identity_in_ground_field`: `(f + g)^q = f^q + g^q` in `Fq[X]` (Freshman's Dream)
   - `frobenius_identity_in_algebra`: Lifted version for `Fq`-algebras `L[X]`
   - `aeval_pow_card_eq_aeval_pow_card`: `(aeval x f)^q = aeval (x^q) f` for polynomial evaluation
   - `aeval_pow_card_pow_eq_aeval_pow_card_pow`: Iterated version
     `(aeval x f)^(q^n) = aeval (x^(q^n)) f`

3. **Frobenius Polynomial Divisibility:**
   - `X_pow_sub_one_dvd_X_pow_sub_one_of_dvd`: If `k ∣ n`, then `X^k - 1 ∣ X^n - 1`
   - `X_pow_card_pow_dvd_X_pow_card_pow_of_dvd`: If `d ∣ n`, then `X^(q^d) - X ∣ X^(q^n) - X`
   - `irreducible_dvd_X_pow_card_pow_sub_X`: An irreducible polynomial `p` of degree `d` divides
     `X^(q^d) - X`
   - `degree_dvd_of_irreducible_dvd_X_pow_card_pow_sub_X`: If irreducible `p` divides `X^(q^n) - X`,
     then `deg(p) ∣ n`
   - `irreducible_dvd_X_pow_sub_X_iff_natDegree_dvd`: Fundamental theorem:
     `p ∣ X^(c^n) - X ↔ deg(p) ∣ n`, with the field size as a numeral `c` together with
     `Fintype.card R = c`
   - `irreducible_dvd_X_pow_add_X_iff_natDegree_dvd`: its characteristic-two form, stated with
     `+ X` as the binary fields write it

## TODOs
- potentially generalize the Frobenius theorems to generic algebras?

items.name: instExpCharOfAlgebra
items.doc:
An algebra over a field of positive characteristic inherits its exponential characteristic:
if `ringChar Fq ≠ 0`, then `ExpChar K (ringChar Fq)` for any `Fq`-algebra `K` that is a field.
Named as an instance but kept a theorem deliberately — it is introduced locally where a Frobenius
argument needs it, rather than added to the instance graph for every algebra.
items.statement:
theorem instExpCharOfAlgebra {K : Type*} [Field K] [Algebra Fq K]
    {h_ringChar_Fq_pos : (ringChar Fq) ≠ 0} : ExpChar K (ringChar Fq)

items.name: Polynomial.prod_X_sub_C_eq_X_pow_card_sub_X
items.doc:
The polynomial `X^q - X` factors into the product of `(X - c)` ∀ `c` ∈ `Fq`,
i.e. `∏_{c ∈ Fq} (X - c) = X^q - X`.
items.statement:
theorem prod_X_sub_C_eq_X_pow_card_sub_X :
    (∏ c ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset Fq), (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C c)) =
    Polynomial.X^(Fintype.card Fq) - Polynomial.X

items.name: Polynomial.prod_X_sub_C_eq_X_pow_card_sub_X_in_L
items.doc:
The identity `∏_{c ∈ Fq} (X - c) = X^q - X` also holds in the polynomial ring `L[X]`,
where `L` is any field extension of `Fq`.
items.statement:
theorem prod_X_sub_C_eq_X_pow_card_sub_X_in_L :
    (∏ c ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset Fq), (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C (algebraMap Fq L c))) =
    Polynomial.X^(Fintype.card Fq) - Polynomial.X

items.name: Polynomial.prod_poly_sub_C_eq_poly_pow_card_sub_poly_in_L
items.doc:
The identity `∏_{c ∈ Fq} (X - c) = X^q - X` also holds in the polynomial ring `L[X]`,
where `L` is any field extension of `Fq`.
items.statement:
theorem prod_poly_sub_C_eq_poly_pow_card_sub_poly_in_L
    (p : L[X]) :
    (∏ c ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset Fq), (p - Polynomial.C (algebraMap Fq L c))) =
    p^(Fintype.card Fq) - p

items.name: Polynomial.frobenius_identity_in_ground_field
items.doc:
The Frobenius identity for polynomials in `Fq[X]`.
The `q`-th power of a sum of polynomials is the sum of their `q`-th powers.
items.statement:
theorem frobenius_identity_in_ground_field
    [Fact (Nat.Prime (ringChar Fq))] (f g : Fq[X]) :
    (f + g)^(Fintype.card Fq) = f^(Fintype.card Fq) + g^(Fintype.card Fq)

items.name: Polynomial.frobenius_identity_in_algebra
items.doc:
The lifted Frobenius identity for polynomials in `L[X]`, where `L` is an `Fq`-algebra.
The exponent `q` is the cardinality of the base field `Fq`.
items.statement:
theorem frobenius_identity_in_algebra [Fact (Nat.Prime (ringChar Fq))]
    (f g : L[X]) : (f + g)^(Fintype.card Fq) = f^(Fintype.card Fq) + g^(Fintype.card Fq)

items.name: Polynomial.linear_map_of_comp_to_linear_map_of_eval
items.doc: Restricting a linear map on polynomial composition to a linear map on polynomial evaluation.
items.statement:
theorem linear_map_of_comp_to_linear_map_of_eval (f : L[X])
    (h_f_linear : IsLinearMap (R := Fq) (M := L[X]) (M₂ := L[X])
      (f := fun inner_p ↦ f.comp inner_p)) :
    IsLinearMap (R := Fq) (M := L) (M₂ := L) (f := fun x ↦ f.eval x)

items.name: Polynomial.aeval_pow_card_eq_aeval_pow_card
items.doc:
Frobenius endomorphism interaction with polynomial evaluation.
(aeval x f)^|Fq| = aeval (x^|Fq|) f
items.statement:
theorem aeval_pow_card_eq_aeval_pow_card {Fq K : Type*} [Field Fq] [Fintype Fq]
    [CommRing K] [Algebra Fq K] [Fact (Nat.Prime (ringChar Fq))] [ExpChar K (ringChar Fq)]
    (f : Fq[X]) (x : K) :
    (aeval x f) ^ (Fintype.card Fq) = aeval (x ^ (Fintype.card Fq)) f

items.name: Polynomial.aeval_pow_card_pow_eq_aeval_pow_card_pow
items.doc:
Iterated Frobenius endomorphism interaction with polynomial evaluation.
(aeval x f)^(|Fq|^n) = aeval (x^|Fq|^n) f
items.statement:
theorem aeval_pow_card_pow_eq_aeval_pow_card_pow {Fq K : Type*} [Field Fq] [Fintype Fq]
    [CommRing K] [Algebra Fq K] [Fact (Nat.Prime (ringChar Fq))] [ExpChar K (ringChar Fq)]
    (f : Fq[X]) (x : K) (n : ℕ) :
    (aeval x f) ^ ((Fintype.card Fq) ^ n) = aeval (x ^ ((Fintype.card Fq) ^ n)) f

items.name: Polynomial.X_pow_sub_one_dvd_X_pow_sub_one_of_dvd
items.doc:
**Lemma 1: Polynomial Divisibility of Powers**
If `k` divides `n`, then `X^k - 1` divides `X^n - 1`.
This is the polynomial version of `a | b => x^a - 1 | x^b - 1`.
items.statement:
theorem X_pow_sub_one_dvd_X_pow_sub_one_of_dvd (k n : ℕ) (h_dvd : k ∣ n) :
    (X ^ k - 1 : Fq[X]) ∣ (X ^ n - 1)

items.name: Polynomial.X_pow_card_pow_dvd_X_pow_card_pow_of_dvd
items.doc:
**Lemma 2: Frobenius Divisibility Transitivity**
If `d` divides `n`, then `X^(q^d) - X` divides `X^(q^n) - X`.
This allows us to say: "If a poly divides the small Frobenius, it divides the big one."
items.statement:
theorem X_pow_card_pow_dvd_X_pow_card_pow_of_dvd (d n : ℕ) (h_dvd : d ∣ n) :
    let q := Fintype.card Fq
    (X ^ (q ^ d) - X : Fq[X]) ∣ (X ^ (q ^ n) - X)

items.name: Polynomial.irreducible_dvd_X_pow_card_pow_sub_X
items.doc:
**Lemma 3: Irreducible Divides Own Frobenius (The Base Case)**
An irreducible polynomial `p` of degree `d` divides `X^(q^d) - X`.
Proof:
1. Consider the extension `K = Fq[x]/(p)`.
2. The group of units `K*` has order `q^d - 1`.
3. So every element `α` satisfies `α^(q^d - 1) = 1` (if `α ≠ 0`).
4. Thus `α^(q^d) = α` for all `α`.
5. `X^(q^d) - X` has `root p` as a root.
6. Since `p` is the minimal polynomial of its root, `p` divides the target.
items.statement:
theorem irreducible_dvd_X_pow_card_pow_sub_X (p : Fq[X]) (hp_irr : Irreducible p) :
    let q := Fintype.card Fq
    let d := p.natDegree
    p ∣ (X ^ (q ^ d) - X)

items.name: Polynomial.degree_dvd_of_irreducible_dvd_X_pow_card_pow_sub_X
items.doc:
**Theorem: The Rabin Condition (One Direction)**
If `p` is irreducible, and `p` divides `X^(q^n) - X`, then `deg(p)` divides `n`.
items.statement:
theorem degree_dvd_of_irreducible_dvd_X_pow_card_pow_sub_X
    [Fact (Nat.Prime (ringChar Fq))]
    (p : Fq[X]) (hp_irr : Irreducible p) (n : ℕ)
    (h_dvd : p ∣ (X ^ ((Fintype.card Fq) ^ n) - X)) :
    p.natDegree ∣ n

items.name: Polynomial.irreducible_dvd_X_pow_sub_X_iff_natDegree_dvd
items.doc:
**Fundamental Theorem of Irreducible Polynomials over Finite Fields:**
For an irreducible polynomial `q` over a finite field `R` with `c` elements:
`q ∣ X^(c^n) - X` ↔ `deg q ∣ n`.

The field size enters as a numeral `c` together with `hcard : Fintype.card R = c`, rather than
being read off as `Fintype.card R`. A concrete field then states the divisibility at its own
field-size literal and supplies `hcard` as `ZMod.card _`; a caller with no numeral in hand passes
`rfl` and recovers the `Fintype.card R` statement verbatim. See the section comment in
`CompPoly/Data/Polynomial/Rabin.lean` for why every criterion in the library is shaped this way.
items.statement:
lemma irreducible_dvd_X_pow_sub_X_iff_natDegree_dvd {R : Type*} [Field R]
    [Fact (Nat.Prime (ringChar R))]
    [Fintype R] {c : ℕ} (hcard : Fintype.card R = c) (n : ℕ) (q : Polynomial R)
    (hq_irr : Irreducible q) :
    q ∣ (X ^ (c ^ n) - X) ↔ q.natDegree ∣ n

items.name: Polynomial.irreducible_dvd_X_pow_add_X_iff_natDegree_dvd
items.doc:
The characteristic-two form of `irreducible_dvd_X_pow_sub_X_iff_natDegree_dvd`, stated with `+ X`
as a binary field writes it: `q ∣ X^(c^n) + X ↔ deg q ∣ n`.

Over `GF(2)` the two spellings are the same polynomial, but only one of them is *syntactically*
what a caller has. Absorbing `CharTwo.sub_eq_add` here — once, at a statement generic in `c` and
`n` — means the concrete caller applies this as a term instead of rewriting a hypothesis whose
type carries a large exponent such as `X ^ 2 ^ 128`.
items.statement:
lemma irreducible_dvd_X_pow_add_X_iff_natDegree_dvd {R : Type*} [Field R]
    [Fact (Nat.Prime (ringChar R))]
    [Fintype R] [CharP R 2] {c : ℕ} (hcard : Fintype.card R = c) (n : ℕ) (q : Polynomial R)
    (hq_irr : Irreducible q) :
    q ∣ (X ^ (c ^ n) + X) ↔ q.natDegree ∣ n

items.name: Polynomial.sum_degreeLT_monomial_eq_subtype
items.statement:
theorem sum_degreeLT_monomial_eq_subtype {n : ℕ} (p : L⦃< n⦄[X]) :
    (⟨p.val.sum (fun n a => Polynomial.monomial n a), by
    -- degree of sum is degree of p.val, which is < n
    rw [Polynomial.sum_monomial_eq p.val]
    exact p.property
  ⟩ : L⦃< n⦄[X]) = p

items.name: Polynomial.monomialBasisOfDegreeLT
items.statement: noncomputable def monomialBasisOfDegreeLT {n : ℕ} : Basis (Fin n) L (L⦃< n⦄[X])

items.name: Polynomial.finrank_degreeLT_n
items.statement: theorem finrank_degreeLT_n (n : ℕ) : Module.finrank L (L⦃< n⦄[X]) = n

items.name: Polynomial.finiteDimensional_degreeLT
items.statement:
theorem finiteDimensional_degreeLT {n : ℕ} (h_n_pos : 0 < n) :
    FiniteDimensional L L⦃< n⦄[X]

modules.title: Rabin's irreducibility test
modules.doc:
A polynomial `f` of degree `d` over a finite field `F` with `q = |F|` elements is irreducible
exactly when

* `f ∣ X^(q^d) - X`, and
* `f` is coprime to `X^(q^(d/ℓ)) - X` for every prime `ℓ ∣ d`.

The first condition says every irreducible factor of `f` has degree dividing `d`; the second
rules out all *proper* divisors of `d` as factor degrees, forcing `f` itself to be irreducible.
Both rest on the fundamental correspondence
`Polynomial.irreducible_dvd_X_pow_sub_X_iff_natDegree_dvd` from
`CompPoly/Data/Polynomial/Frobenius.lean`.

This generalizes `irreducible_of_rabin_128_passed_over_GF2`
(`CompPoly/Fields/Binary/BF128Ghash/Basic.lean`), which is the `d = 128`, `F = GF(2)`
specialization, to arbitrary degree over any finite field.

## Main statements

* `Polynomial.irreducible_of_rabin`: the two conditions imply irreducibility.
* `Polynomial.rabin_of_irreducible`: the converse, so the test is exact.
* `Polynomial.irreducible_iff_rabin`: the resulting characterization.

All three take the field size as a numeral `q` with `hcard : Fintype.card F = q`; see "The shape
of these statements" below for why, and pass `rfl` if you have no numeral.

## References

* [Rabin80] Michael O. Rabin, *Probabilistic Algorithms in Finite Fields*,
  SIAM Journal on Computing 9(2), 1980.

items.name: Nat.exists_primeFactor_dvd_div_of_dvd
items.doc:
If `m` is a proper divisor of a nonzero `d`, then `m` divides `d / ℓ` for some prime factor `ℓ`
of `d`.

This is the arithmetic core of Rabin's test: it is why checking the prime-index quotients
`d / ℓ` suffices to rule out *every* proper divisor of `d`.
items.statement:
theorem exists_primeFactor_dvd_div_of_dvd {m d : ℕ} (hd : d ≠ 0) (hmd : m ∣ d) (hne : m ≠ d) :
    ∃ ℓ ∈ d.primeFactors, m ∣ d / ℓ

items.note:
### The shape of these statements

Each test below takes the field size as a numeral `q` together with `hcard : Fintype.card F = q`,
rather than reading it off as `Fintype.card F`, and substitutes it away internally. Both kinds of
caller are served: a concrete field supplies `hcard` as `ZMod.card _` (or its own cardinality
lemma) and states its conditions at the numeral its certificates were generated for; a caller with
no numeral in hand passes `rfl` and gets the `Fintype.card F` statement back verbatim.

Stating the conditions at `Fintype.card F` would make a concrete caller cast each condition
with `rw [hcard]`. Such a cast leaves an `Eq.mpr` transport around a certificate argument whose
type carries a large exponent, such as `X ^ (q ^ d)`. In an earlier kernel replay, such a
transport caused `npowRec` to unfold one exponent step at a time until the kernel hit its
recursion limit. The numeral parameter lets concrete callers pass their certificates directly.
`docs/wiki/field-extensions.md` records the history, and
`CompPoly/Data/Polynomial/RabinCertificate.lean` packages these tests at concrete degrees.

items.name: Polynomial.irreducible_of_rabin
items.doc:
**Rabin's irreducibility test (soundness).**

If a degree-`d` polynomial `f` over a finite field with `q` elements divides `X^(q^d) - X` and is
coprime to `X^(q^(d/ℓ)) - X` for every prime `ℓ ∣ d`, then `f` is irreducible.
items.statement:
theorem irreducible_of_rabin {f : F[X]} {d q : ℕ} (hcard : Fintype.card F = q)
    (h_deg : f.natDegree = d) (h_pos : 0 < d)
    (h_trace : f ∣ X ^ (q ^ d) - X)
    (h_coprime : ∀ ℓ ∈ d.primeFactors, IsCoprime f (X ^ (q ^ (d / ℓ)) - X)) :
    Irreducible f

items.name: Polynomial.rabin_of_irreducible
items.doc:
**Rabin's irreducibility test (completeness).**

An irreducible polynomial of degree `d` satisfies both Rabin conditions.
items.statement:
theorem rabin_of_irreducible {f : F[X]} {d q : ℕ} (hcard : Fintype.card F = q)
    (h_deg : f.natDegree = d) (h_pos : 0 < d) (h_irr : Irreducible f) :
    f ∣ X ^ (q ^ d) - X ∧
      ∀ ℓ ∈ d.primeFactors, IsCoprime f (X ^ (q ^ (d / ℓ)) - X)

items.name: Polynomial.irreducible_iff_rabin
items.doc:
**Rabin's irreducibility test.** For a polynomial of positive degree `d` over a finite field
with `q` elements, irreducibility is equivalent to the two Rabin conditions.
items.statement:
theorem irreducible_iff_rabin {f : F[X]} {d q : ℕ} (hcard : Fintype.card F = q)
    (h_deg : f.natDegree = d) (h_pos : 0 < d) :
    Irreducible f ↔
      (f ∣ X ^ (q ^ d) - X ∧
        ∀ ℓ ∈ d.primeFactors, IsCoprime f (X ^ (q ^ (d / ℓ)) - X))

modules.title: Kernel-checkable Rabin irreducibility certificates over prime fields
modules.doc:
Rabin's test (`CompPoly/Data/Polynomial/Rabin.lean`) reduces irreducibility of a degree-`d`
polynomial `f` over `ZMod p` to divisibility and coprimality conditions against `X^(p^k) - X`.
Verifying those conditions requires computing `X^(p^k) mod f` — around `d · log₂ p` modular
squarings — which is far beyond what `decide` can do on `Polynomial` values and which this
repository's TCB policy forbids delegating to `native_decide`.

This file provides the reusable, degree-agnostic *certificate* infrastructure:

* Polynomials are represented as little-endian `ℕ`-coefficient lists (`toPoly` interprets them
  in `(ZMod p)[X]`), with schoolbook arithmetic (`addNat`, `mulNat`) by structural recursion,
  so every check reduces in the kernel via GMP-accelerated `Nat` operations.
* A certificate `Step` records a squaring (or multiply-by-`X`) together with the quotient and
  remainder of the division by `f`; `checkStep` verifies `cur² = q·f + r` (coefficientwise,
  mod `p`) and `runChain` folds a whole square-and-multiply chain, so an entire exponentiation
  certificate is one list literal checked by a single kernel reduction.
* `runChain_sound` lifts a checked chain to `X^N % f = r % f` in `(ZMod p)[X]`; the two Rabin
  conditions follow via `dvd_X_pow_sub_X_of_runChain` (trace) and
  `isCoprime_X_pow_sub_X_of_runChain` (coprimality, from a Bézout certificate on the reduced
  residue).
* `irreducible_of_rabin_prime_degree` packages Rabin's test for *prime* degree `d`, where the
  conditions collapse to a single trace and a single coprimality check;
  `irreducible_of_rabin_prime_power` does the same at `d = ℓ ^ k`, where the collapse is still
  sound; `irreducible_of_rabin_two_prime_factors` and `irreducible_of_rabin_degree_six` cover a
  degree with two distinct prime factors. All take the field size as a numeral `q` with
  `Fintype.card F = q`, the shape concrete extensions use.

Certificate data is produced by the untrusted generator `scripts/gen_rabin_certificate.py`;
the kernel re-checks every step. Contrast `CompPoly/Fields/Binary/BF128Ghash/`, the bespoke
GF(2¹²⁸) predecessor of this framework, which spells out each step as a separate lemma.

items.note:
### `ℕ`-level polynomial arithmetic

Little-endian coefficient lists. No coefficient is ever reduced during a product — entries
stay below `d² · p²`, comfortably inside GMP range — and comparisons reduce mod `p` at the
end (`eqModP`), so no subtraction (and hence no truncation) occurs anywhere.

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.addNat
items.doc: Coefficientwise addition of little-endian coefficient lists.
items.statement: def addNat : List ℕ → List ℕ → List ℕ

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.scaleNat
items.doc: Scale a coefficient list by a constant.
items.statement: def scaleNat (c : ℕ) (l : List ℕ) : List ℕ

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.mulNat
items.doc: Schoolbook product of little-endian coefficient lists.
items.statement: def mulNat : List ℕ → List ℕ → List ℕ

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.eqModP
items.doc: Coefficientwise equality modulo `p`, treating entries beyond a list's end as `0`.
items.statement: def eqModP (p : ℕ) : List ℕ → List ℕ → Bool

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.toPoly
items.doc:
Interpret a little-endian coefficient list in `(ZMod p)[X]`, Horner-style. Specification
only; certificate checking never evaluates it.
items.statement: noncomputable def toPoly (p : ℕ) : List ℕ → (ZMod p)[X]

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.toPoly_nil
items.statement: theorem toPoly_nil {p : ℕ} : toPoly p [] = 0

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.toPoly_cons
items.doc:
The defining Horner step of `toPoly`, as a rewrite rule: a head coefficient contributes a
constant and the tail is multiplied by `X`.
items.statement:
theorem toPoly_cons {p : ℕ} (c : ℕ) (cs : List ℕ) :
    toPoly p (c :: cs) = C (c : ZMod p) + X * toPoly p cs

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.toPoly_X
items.statement: theorem toPoly_X {p : ℕ} : toPoly p [0, 1] = X

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.toPoly_one
items.statement: theorem toPoly_one {p : ℕ} : toPoly p [1] = 1

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.toPoly_addNat
items.doc:
`addNat` denotes addition: the coefficientwise sum of two lists is the sum of the
polynomials they denote. One of the three specification bridges that make the `ℕ`-list
arithmetic usable as a certificate format.
items.statement:
theorem toPoly_addNat {p : ℕ} : ∀ a b : List ℕ,
    toPoly p (addNat a b) = toPoly p a + toPoly p b

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.toPoly_scaleNat
items.doc: `scaleNat` denotes multiplication by a constant.
items.statement:
theorem toPoly_scaleNat {p : ℕ} (c : ℕ) : ∀ l : List ℕ,
    toPoly p (scaleNat c l) = C (c : ZMod p) * toPoly p l

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.toPoly_mulNat
items.doc:
`mulNat` denotes multiplication: schoolbook convolution of the coefficient lists is the
product of the polynomials they denote. Proved from `toPoly_addNat` and `toPoly_scaleNat`,
following the same recursion `mulNat` uses.
items.statement:
theorem toPoly_mulNat {p : ℕ} : ∀ a b : List ℕ,
    toPoly p (mulNat a b) = toPoly p a * toPoly p b

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.cast_eq_cast_of_mod_eq
items.doc: Two naturals equal mod `p` cast to the same element of `ZMod p`.
items.statement:
theorem cast_eq_cast_of_mod_eq {p a b : ℕ} (h : a % p = b % p) :
    (a : ZMod p) = (b : ZMod p)

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.toPoly_eq_zero_of_all_mod_eq_zero
items.doc:
A list whose every coefficient is `0` mod `p` denotes the zero polynomial. This is the base
case behind `toPoly_eq_of_eqModP`, which is how a `eqModP` kernel check becomes an equation
between polynomials.
items.statement:
theorem toPoly_eq_zero_of_all_mod_eq_zero {p : ℕ} : ∀ {l : List ℕ},
    l.all (· % p == 0) = true → toPoly p l = 0

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.toPoly_eq_of_eqModP
items.doc: Soundness of the coefficientwise checker: `eqModP` lists denote the same polynomial.
items.statement:
theorem toPoly_eq_of_eqModP {p : ℕ} : ∀ {a b : List ℕ},
    eqModP p a b = true → toPoly p a = toPoly p b

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.verify_mulAdd
items.doc: Lift a checked `ℕ`-level identity `a·b ≡ q·f + r (mod p)` to `(ZMod p)[X]`.

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.Step
items.doc:
One step of a square-and-multiply chain modulo `f`: from the current residue `cur`, either
square it (`mulX = false`) or multiply it by `X` (`mulX = true`), and divide by `f` to get
quotient `q` and next residue `r`. The generator supplies `q` and `r`; the checker only has
to confirm one polynomial identity per step.
items.statement:
structure Step where
  /-- `true` for a multiply-by-`X` step, `false` for a squaring step. -/
  mulX : Bool
  /-- The quotient of the step's product by the modulus. -/
  q : List ℕ
  /-- The remainder — the next residue in the chain. -/
  r : List ℕ

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.checkStep
items.doc: Check one chain step: `cur² = q·f + r` (or `X·cur = q·f + r`), coefficientwise mod `p`.
items.statement: def checkStep (p : ℕ) (fL cur : List ℕ) (s : Step) : Bool

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.runChain
items.doc:
Fold a chain of steps from the residue `cur`, checking each; returns the final residue,
or `none` if any check fails. One kernel reduction of `runChain` verifies a whole chain.
items.statement: def runChain (p : ℕ) (fL : List ℕ) : List ℕ → List Step → Option (List ℕ)

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.chainExp
items.doc: The exponent a chain computes: squaring doubles it, multiply-by-`X` adds one.
items.statement: def chainExp : ℕ → List Step → ℕ

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.step_sound
items.doc: Soundness of one chain step.

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.runChain_sound
items.doc:
**Soundness of a whole chain**: a checked chain starting at the residue of `X^e` ends at
the residue of `X^(chainExp e steps)`.
items.statement:
theorem runChain_sound {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {fL : List ℕ} {f : (ZMod p)[X]}
    (hfL : toPoly p fL = f) (hf0 : f ≠ 0) :
    ∀ (steps : List Step) (cur out : List ℕ) (e : ℕ),
      runChain p fL cur steps = some out →
      (X : (ZMod p)[X]) ^ e % f = toPoly p cur % f →
      (X : (ZMod p)[X]) ^ chainExp e steps % f = toPoly p out % f

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.xpow_mod_of_runChain
items.doc: A chain started at `[0, 1]` (the residue of `X¹`) computes `X^N % f`.

items.note: ### The two Rabin conditions from certificates

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.dvd_sub_of_mod_eq
items.doc: Equal remainders mean the divisor divides the difference.
items.statement:
theorem dvd_sub_of_mod_eq {R : Type*} [EuclideanDomain R] {a b n : R} (h : a % n = b % n) :
    n ∣ a - b

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.dvd_X_pow_sub_X_of_runChain
items.doc:
**The trace condition from a chain.** A checked chain for `X^N` ending back at `[0, 1]`
(the residue `X`) proves `f ∣ X^N - X`.

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.isCoprime_X_pow_sub_X_of_runChain
items.doc:
**The coprimality condition from a chain plus a Bézout certificate.**

The chain reduces `X^N` to a residue `rp`; writing `rp = w + X` (checked by `eqModP`), we have
`X^N - X ≡ w (mod f)`, so a Bézout identity `u·f + v·w = 1` (again checked by `eqModP`)
witnesses `IsCoprime f (X^N - X)`.
items.statement:
theorem isCoprime_X_pow_sub_X_of_runChain {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {fL : List ℕ} {f : (ZMod p)[X]}
    (hfL : toPoly p fL = f) (hf0 : f ≠ 0) {steps : List Step} {rp w u v : List ℕ} {N : ℕ}
    (hrun : runChain p fL [0, 1] steps = some rp)
    (hexp : chainExp 1 steps = N)
    (hw : eqModP p rp (addNat w [0, 1]) = true)
    (hbez : eqModP p (addNat (mulNat u fL) (mulNat v w)) [1] = true) :
    IsCoprime f ((X : (ZMod p)[X]) ^ N - X)

items.note:
### Packaging Rabin's test at a concrete degree

`Polynomial.irreducible_of_rabin` already quantifies the coprimality condition over
`d.primeFactors`. The wrappers below discharge that quantifier for the shapes of `d` that
concrete extensions use, so a caller supplies one coprimality proof per prime factor and nothing
else. Each takes the field size as a numeral `q` with `hcard : Fintype.card F = q`, exactly as
`Polynomial.irreducible_of_rabin` does — supply `ZMod.card _` at a concrete field, or `rfl` to
read the conditions at `Fintype.card F`. The section comment in
`CompPoly/Data/Polynomial/Rabin.lean` records why that is the only shape these statements have.

Note that `irreducible_of_rabin_prime_degree` does **not** apply at composite `d`, and its
collapsed condition is not merely inconvenient but unsound there: a product of equal-degree
factors divides `X^(q^d) - X` and is coprime to `X^q - X`, so it would pass.
`irreducible_of_rabin_prime_power` is the collapse that *is* sound at `d = ℓ ^ k`.

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.irreducible_of_rabin_prime_degree
items.doc:
**Rabin's test for prime degree.** For `f` of *prime* degree `d` over a finite field with `q`
elements, the per-prime-factor conditions collapse to a single coprimality check at exponent `q`:
`f` is irreducible provided `f ∣ X^(q^d) - X` and `IsCoprime f (X^q - X)`.
items.statement:
theorem irreducible_of_rabin_prime_degree {F : Type*} [Field F] [Fintype F] {f : F[X]} {d q : ℕ}
    (hcard : Fintype.card F = q)
    (hd : d.Prime) (h_deg : f.natDegree = d)
    (h_trace : f ∣ X ^ (q ^ d) - X)
    (h_cop : IsCoprime f (X ^ q - X)) :
    Irreducible f

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.irreducible_of_rabin_prime_degree_of_card
items.statement: alias irreducible_of_rabin_prime_degree_of_card

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.irreducible_of_rabin_prime_power
items.doc:
**Rabin's test for a prime-power degree**, such as `d = 8`, `64` or `128`.

`d = ℓ ^ k` has the single prime factor `ℓ`, so — exactly as at prime degree — the caller supplies
the trace condition plus one coprimality certificate, here at exponent `q ^ (d / ℓ)`. Unlike
`irreducible_of_rabin_prime_degree` this is *sound* at composite `d`: the check at `d / ℓ` rules
out every proper divisor of `d`, because every proper divisor of `ℓ ^ k` divides `ℓ ^ (k - 1)`.

`d` is kept separate from `ℓ ^ k` and tied to it by `hd_eq` so that the conditions read at the
caller's numeral (`q ^ 64`, not `q ^ 2 ^ 6`); supply `hd_eq` as `by norm_num`. This is the shape
the characteristic-two moduli use — `Aes.modulus` at `d = 8` and `BF64.basePoly` at `d = 64`.
items.statement:
theorem irreducible_of_rabin_prime_power {F : Type*} [Field F] [Fintype F] {f : F[X]}
    {d ℓ k q : ℕ} (hcard : Fintype.card F = q)
    (hℓ : ℓ.Prime) (hk : k ≠ 0) (hd_eq : d = ℓ ^ k)
    (h_deg : f.natDegree = d)
    (h_trace : f ∣ X ^ (q ^ d) - X)
    (h_cop : IsCoprime f (X ^ (q ^ (d / ℓ)) - X)) :
    Irreducible f

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.irreducible_of_rabin_two_prime_factors
items.doc:
**Rabin's test for a degree with exactly two prime factors**, such as `d = 6`.

The caller supplies the trace condition plus one coprimality certificate per prime factor, at
exponents `q^(d/ℓ₁)` and `q^(d/ℓ₂)`. The hypothesis `h_factors` is `by decide` at a concrete
degree — for `d = 6` it is `(6 : ℕ).primeFactors = {2, 3}`, giving checks at `q^3` and `q^2`.

Both checks are needed. Dropping the `q^3` one admits a product of two irreducible cubics;
dropping the `q^2` one admits a product of three irreducible quadratics.
items.statement:
theorem irreducible_of_rabin_two_prime_factors {F : Type*} [Field F] [Fintype F] {f : F[X]}
    {d ℓ₁ ℓ₂ q : ℕ} (hcard : Fintype.card F = q)
    (h_deg : f.natDegree = d) (h_pos : 0 < d)
    (h_factors : d.primeFactors = {ℓ₁, ℓ₂})
    (h_trace : f ∣ X ^ (q ^ d) - X)
    (h_cop₁ : IsCoprime f (X ^ (q ^ (d / ℓ₁)) - X))
    (h_cop₂ : IsCoprime f (X ^ (q ^ (d / ℓ₂)) - X)) :
    Irreducible f

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.irreducible_of_rabin_degree_six
items.doc:
**Rabin's test at degree 6.** `f` of degree 6 over a finite field with `q` elements is irreducible
provided `f ∣ X^(q^6) - X`, `IsCoprime f (X^(q^3) - X)`, and `IsCoprime f (X^(q^2) - X)`.

This is the shape used by the KoalaBear degree-6 extension. It differs from
`irreducible_of_rabin_two_prime_factors` only in discharging `Nat.primeFactors 6 = {2, 3}`
internally, so callers never touch `Nat.primeFactors`.

The `q^3` check is what rules out a product of two irreducible cubics, and the `q^2` check a
product of three irreducible quadratics; the trace condition alone permits both.
items.statement:
theorem irreducible_of_rabin_degree_six {F : Type*} [Field F] [Fintype F] {f : F[X]} {q : ℕ}
    (hcard : Fintype.card F = q)
    (h_deg : f.natDegree = 6)
    (h_trace : f ∣ X ^ (q ^ 6) - X)
    (h_cop₃ : IsCoprime f (X ^ (q ^ 3) - X))
    (h_cop₂ : IsCoprime f (X ^ (q ^ 2) - X)) :
    Irreducible f

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.irreducible_of_rabin_degree_six_of_card
items.statement: alias irreducible_of_rabin_degree_six_of_card

modules.title: Rabin certificates over `GF(2)` on `ℕ` bitmasks
modules.doc:
`CompPoly/Data/Polynomial/RabinCertificate.lean` checks a square-and-multiply chain on
little-endian coefficient lists with schoolbook arithmetic, which works over any prime field.
Over `GF(2)` a polynomial is a bitmask: bit `i` of `n : ℕ` is the coefficient of `X^i`.
Addition is `xor` and multiplication is carry-less, so the kernel checks each step with a few
GMP-backed `Nat` operations (`xor`, `shiftLeft`, `%`, `/`) instead of walking lists of
numerals. For the degree-64 modulus of `BF64` this takes the certificate check from about 26 s
to about 2 s.

The chain format mirrors the list version: each `Step` carries the quotient and remainder of
one squaring (or multiply-by-`X`) step, the kernel checks `cur² = q·f + r` exactly, and
`runChain_sound` lifts a checked chain to `X^N % f = r % f` in `(ZMod 2)[X]`. Because the
bitmask of a `GF(2)` polynomial is unique, checks compare with `==` and need no reduction.

## Main definitions

* `clmul` — carry-less product of two bitmasks, by structural recursion on a bit count.
* `toPoly` — the polynomial a bitmask denotes. Specification only; checking never evaluates it.
* `Step`, `checkStep`, `runChain`, `chainExp` — the chain checker.

## Main statements

* `toPoly_clmul` — `clmul` is polynomial multiplication.
* `dvd_X_pow_sub_X_of_runChain`, `isCoprime_X_pow_sub_X_of_runChain` — the two Rabin
  conditions from certificates, with the same shape as the list versions, so they feed
  `irreducible_of_rabin_prime_degree` and its siblings unchanged.

Certificate data comes from `scripts/gen_rabin_certificate.py --binary`.

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.Binary.clmulBits
items.doc:
Carry-less product of the low `n` bits of `a` with `b`. Structural recursion on `n`, so the
kernel unfolds it once per bit of `a`.
items.statement: def clmulBits : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → ℕ

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.Binary.clmul
items.doc: Carry-less product of two bitmasks: polynomial multiplication over `GF(2)`.
items.statement: def clmul (a b : ℕ) : ℕ

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.Binary.toPoly
items.doc:
The polynomial over `GF(2)` whose coefficient of `X^i` is bit `i` of `n`. Every set bit of
`n` is below `n`, so the sum over `range n` covers them. Specification only.
items.statement: noncomputable def toPoly (n : ℕ) : (ZMod 2)[X]

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.Binary.coeff_toPoly
items.statement:
theorem coeff_toPoly (n i : ℕ) :
    (toPoly n).coeff i = if n.testBit i then 1 else 0

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.Binary.toPoly_congr
items.doc: Two bitmasks with the same bits denote the same polynomial.
items.statement: theorem toPoly_congr {a b : ℕ} (h : ∀ i, a.testBit i = b.testBit i) : toPoly a = toPoly b

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.Binary.toPoly_zero
items.statement: theorem toPoly_zero : toPoly 0 = 0

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.Binary.toPoly_xor
items.statement: theorem toPoly_xor (a b : ℕ) : toPoly (a ^^^ b) = toPoly a + toPoly b

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.Binary.toPoly_two_pow
items.statement: theorem toPoly_two_pow (k : ℕ) : toPoly (2 ^ k) = X ^ k

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.Binary.toPoly_one
items.statement: theorem toPoly_one : toPoly 1 = 1

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.Binary.toPoly_two
items.doc: The bitmask `2` is `X`.
items.statement: theorem toPoly_two : toPoly 2 = X

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.Binary.toPoly_shiftLeft_one
items.statement: theorem toPoly_shiftLeft_one (a : ℕ) : toPoly (a <<< 1) = X * toPoly a

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.Binary.toPoly_mod_two_pow_succ
items.doc:
Splitting off the lowest bit: the low `n + 1` bits of `a` are bit `0` plus `X` times the low
`n` bits of `a / 2`.
items.statement:
theorem toPoly_mod_two_pow_succ (a n : ℕ) :
    toPoly (a % 2 ^ (n + 1)) = (if a % 2 = 1 then 1 else 0) + X * toPoly (a / 2 % 2 ^ n)

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.Binary.toPoly_clmulBits
items.statement:
theorem toPoly_clmulBits (n a b : ℕ) :
    toPoly (clmulBits n a b) = toPoly (a % 2 ^ n) * toPoly b

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.Binary.toPoly_clmul
items.doc: **`clmul` is polynomial multiplication over `GF(2)`.**
items.statement: theorem toPoly_clmul (a b : ℕ) : toPoly (clmul a b) = toPoly a * toPoly b

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.Binary.Step
items.doc:
One step of a square-and-multiply chain modulo `f`, as for the list checker: square the
current residue (`mulX = false`) or multiply it by `X` (`mulX = true`), with quotient `q` and
next residue `r` supplied by the generator.
items.statement:
structure Step where
  /-- `true` for a multiply-by-`X` step, `false` for a squaring step. -/
  mulX : Bool
  /-- The quotient of the step's product by the modulus, as a bitmask. -/
  q : ℕ
  /-- The remainder — the next residue in the chain — as a bitmask. -/
  r : ℕ

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.Binary.checkStep
items.doc: Check one chain step: `cur² = q·f + r` (or `X·cur = q·f + r`) over `GF(2)`.
items.statement: def checkStep (f cur : ℕ) (s : Step) : Bool

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.Binary.runChain
items.doc:
Fold a chain of steps from the residue `cur`, checking each; returns the final residue, or
`none` if any check fails. One kernel reduction of `runChain` verifies a whole chain.
items.statement: def runChain (f : ℕ) : ℕ → List Step → Option ℕ

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.Binary.chainExp
items.doc: The exponent a chain computes: squaring doubles it, multiply-by-`X` adds one.
items.statement: def chainExp : ℕ → List Step → ℕ

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.Binary.checkStep_sound
items.doc: A checked step is a polynomial identity.
items.statement:
theorem checkStep_sound {f cur : ℕ} {s : Step} (h : checkStep f cur s = true) :
    toPoly (cond s.mulX (cur <<< 1) (clmul cur cur)) = toPoly s.q * toPoly f + toPoly s.r

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.Binary.step_sound
items.doc: Soundness of one chain step.
items.statement:
theorem step_sound {fN cur : ℕ} {f : (ZMod 2)[X]} (hfN : toPoly fN = f) (hf0 : f ≠ 0)
    {s : Step} {e : ℕ} (hcheck : checkStep fN cur s = true)
    (hprev : (X : (ZMod 2)[X]) ^ e % f = toPoly cur % f) :
    (X : (ZMod 2)[X]) ^ (cond s.mulX (e + 1) (2 * e)) % f = toPoly s.r % f

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.Binary.runChain_sound
items.doc:
**Soundness of a whole chain**: a checked chain starting at the residue of `X^e` ends at
the residue of `X^(chainExp e steps)`.
items.statement:
theorem runChain_sound {fN : ℕ} {f : (ZMod 2)[X]} (hfN : toPoly fN = f) (hf0 : f ≠ 0) :
    ∀ (steps : List Step) (cur out : ℕ) (e : ℕ),
      runChain fN cur steps = some out →
      (X : (ZMod 2)[X]) ^ e % f = toPoly cur % f →
      (X : (ZMod 2)[X]) ^ chainExp e steps % f = toPoly out % f

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.Binary.xpow_mod_of_runChain
items.doc: A chain started at `2` (the bitmask of `X`) computes `X^N % f`.
items.statement:
theorem xpow_mod_of_runChain {fN : ℕ} {f : (ZMod 2)[X]} (hfN : toPoly fN = f) (hf0 : f ≠ 0)
    {steps : List Step} {out N : ℕ} (hrun : runChain fN 2 steps = some out)
    (hexp : chainExp 1 steps = N) :
    (X : (ZMod 2)[X]) ^ N % f = toPoly out % f

items.note: ### The two Rabin conditions from certificates

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.Binary.dvd_X_pow_sub_X_of_runChain
items.doc:
**The trace condition from a chain.** A checked chain for `X^N` ending back at `2` (the
residue `X`) proves `f ∣ X^N - X`.
items.statement:
theorem dvd_X_pow_sub_X_of_runChain {fN : ℕ} {f : (ZMod 2)[X]} (hfN : toPoly fN = f)
    (hf0 : f ≠ 0) {steps : List Step} {N : ℕ} (hrun : runChain fN 2 steps = some 2)
    (hexp : chainExp 1 steps = N) :
    f ∣ (X : (ZMod 2)[X]) ^ N - X

items.name: CompPoly.RabinCert.Binary.isCoprime_X_pow_sub_X_of_runChain
items.doc:
**The coprimality condition from a chain plus a Bézout certificate.** The chain reduces `X^N`
to a residue `rp`; `rp = w ^^^ 2` says `rp = w + X`, so `X^N - X ≡ w (mod f)`, and the Bézout
identity `u·f + v·w = 1` witnesses `IsCoprime f (X^N - X)`.
items.statement:
theorem isCoprime_X_pow_sub_X_of_runChain {fN : ℕ} {f : (ZMod 2)[X]} (hfN : toPoly fN = f)
    (hf0 : f ≠ 0) {steps : List Step} {rp w u v N : ℕ}
    (hrun : runChain fN 2 steps = some rp)
    (hexp : chainExp 1 steps = N)
    (hw : (rp == w ^^^ 2) = true)
    (hbez : (clmul u fN ^^^ clmul v w == 1) = true) :
    IsCoprime f ((X : (ZMod 2)[X]) ^ N - X)

modules.title: Towers of algebras and their equivalences
modules.doc:
An `AlgebraTower` is a preorder-indexed family of commutative semirings with ring
homomorphisms between comparable levels. Self-maps are identities, and the maps compose
along chains of indices. Each map induces an algebra structure on its target, and
composition gives compatible scalar actions across three levels.

`AlgebraTower.ofNatStep` constructs a natural-number-indexed tower by composing chosen
homomorphisms between adjacent levels. These homomorphisms need not be injective.

An `AlgebraTowerEquiv` consists of ring equivalences at each level that commute with
the tower maps.

items.name: AlgebraTower
items.doc:
A preorder-indexed family of commutative semirings with compatible ring homomorphisms.

The map from a level to itself is the identity. For `i ≤ j ≤ k`, the map from `i` to `k`
is the composite of the maps from `i` to `j` and from `j` to `k`.
items.statement:
class AlgebraTower {ι : Type*} [Preorder ι] (AT : ι → Type*)
  [∀ i, CommSemiring (AT i)] where
  /-- Ring homomorphisms from `AT i` to `AT j` for all `i ≤ j`. -/
  protected algebraMap : ∀ i j, (h : i ≤ j) → (AT i →+* AT j)
  /-- The ring homomorphism from level `i` to itself is the identity. -/
  algebraMap_self' : ∀ i, algebraMap i i le_rfl = RingHom.id (AT i)
  /-- Every image element commutes with every element of the target semiring. -/
  commutes' : ∀ (i j : ι) (h : i ≤ j) (r : AT i) (x : AT j),
    (algebraMap i j h r) * x = x * (algebraMap i j h r)
  /-- The map from `i` to `k` is the composite of the maps from `i` to `j` and `j` to `k`. -/
  coherence' : ∀ (i j k : ι) (h1 : i ≤ j) (h2 : j ≤ k),
    algebraMap i k (h1.trans h2) =
      (algebraMap j k h2).comp (algebraMap i j h1)

items.name: AlgebraTower.ofNatStep
items.doc:
Construct a tower by composing chosen ring homomorphisms between adjacent levels.

The map from a level to itself is the identity. The map from `i` to `j + 1`, for `i ≤ j`,
is `step j` composed with the map from `i` to `j`. No injectivity assumption is required.
items.statement: def ofNatStep (step : ∀ k, A k →+* A (k + 1)) : AlgebraTower A

items.name: AlgebraTower.ofNatStep_algebraMap_succ_right
items.doc: Extending a constructed tower map by one level composes it with the chosen next map.
items.statement:
theorem ofNatStep_algebraMap_succ_right (step : ∀ k, A k →+* A (k + 1))
    {i j : ℕ} (h : i ≤ j) :
    (ofNatStep step).algebraMap i (j + 1) (h.trans (Nat.le_succ j)) =
      (step j).comp ((ofNatStep step).algebraMap i j h)

items.name: AlgebraTower.ofNatStep_algebraMap_succ
items.doc: The map between adjacent levels is the homomorphism supplied to the constructor.
items.statement:
theorem ofNatStep_algebraMap_succ (step : ∀ k, A k →+* A (k + 1))
    (i : ℕ) (h : i ≤ i + 1) :
    (ofNatStep step).algebraMap i (i + 1) h = step i

items.name: AlgebraTower.algebraMap_self
items.doc: The tower map from level `i` to itself is the identity for every proof of `i ≤ i`.
items.statement:
lemma AlgebraTower.algebraMap_self (i : ι) (h : i ≤ i) :
    AlgebraTower.algebraMap (AT := A) i i h = RingHom.id (A i)

items.name: AlgebraTower.algebraMap_self_apply
items.doc: The tower map from level `i` to itself fixes every element of that level.
items.statement:
lemma AlgebraTower.algebraMap_self_apply (i : ι) (h : i ≤ i) (x : A i) :
    AlgebraTower.algebraMap (AT := A) i i h x = x

items.name: AlgebraTower.toAlgebra
items.statement: abbrev AlgebraTower.toAlgebra {i j : ι} (h : i ≤ j) : Algebra (A i) (A j)

items.name: AlgebraTower.toIsScalarTower
items.statement:
instance AlgebraTower.toIsScalarTower (a : AlgebraTower C) {i j k : ι}
    (h1 : i ≤ j) (h2 : j ≤ k) :
    letI : Algebra (C i) (C j) := by exact a.toAlgebra h1
    letI : Algebra (C j) (C k) := by exact a.toAlgebra h2
    letI : Algebra (C i) (C k) := by exact a.toAlgebra (h1.trans h2)
    IsScalarTower (C i) (C j) (C k)

items.name: AlgebraTowerEquiv
items.statement:
structure AlgebraTowerEquiv (A : ι → Type*) [∀ i, CommSemiring (A i)] [a : AlgebraTower A]
  (B : ι → Type*) [∀ i, CommSemiring (B i)] [b : AlgebraTower B]
  where
    toRingEquiv : ∀ i, (A i ≃+* B i)
    commutesLeft' : ∀ (i j : ι) (h : i ≤ j) (r : A i),
      (b.algebraMap (i:=i) (j:=j) (h:=h)) ((toRingEquiv i) r) =
      (toRingEquiv j) (a.algebraMap (i:=i) (j:=j) (h:=h) r)

items.name: AlgebraTowerEquiv.commutesRight'
items.statement:
lemma AlgebraTowerEquiv.commutesRight' (e : AlgebraTowerEquiv A B)
    {i j : ι} (h : i ≤ j) (r : B i) :
  AlgebraTower.algebraMap (AT:=A) (i:=i) (j:=j) (h:=h) ((e.toRingEquiv i).symm r) =
  (e.toRingEquiv j).symm (AlgebraTower.algebraMap (AT:=B) (i:=i) (j:=j) (h:=h) r)

items.name: AlgebraTowerEquiv.symm
items.statement: def AlgebraTowerEquiv.symm (e : AlgebraTowerEquiv A B) : AlgebraTowerEquiv B A

items.name: AlgebraTowerEquiv.algebraMapRightUp
items.statement:
def AlgebraTowerEquiv.algebraMapRightUp (e : AlgebraTowerEquiv A B) (i j : ι)
    (h : i ≤ j) : (A i) →+* (B j)

items.name: AlgebraTowerEquiv.algebraMapLeftUp
items.statement:
def AlgebraTowerEquiv.algebraMapLeftUp (e : AlgebraTowerEquiv A B) (i j : ι)
    (h : i ≤ j) : (B i) →+* (A j)

items.name: AlgebraTowerEquiv.toAlgebraOverLeft
items.statement:
abbrev AlgebraTowerEquiv.toAlgebraOverLeft (e : AlgebraTowerEquiv A B) (i j : ι)
    (h : i ≤ j) : Algebra (A i) (B j)

items.name: AlgebraTowerEquiv.toAlgebraOverRight
items.statement:
abbrev AlgebraTowerEquiv.toAlgebraOverRight (e : AlgebraTowerEquiv A B) (i j : ι)
    (h : i ≤ j) : Algebra (B i) (A j)

items.name: AlgebraTowerEquiv.toAlgEquivOverLeft
items.statement:
def AlgebraTowerEquiv.toAlgEquivOverLeft (e : AlgebraTowerEquiv A B) (i j : ι) (h : i ≤ j) :
    letI : Algebra (A i) (A j) := by exact AlgebraTower.toAlgebra h
    letI : Algebra (A i) (B j) := by exact e.toAlgebraOverLeft i j h
    AlgEquiv (A i) (A j) (B j)

items.name: AlgebraTowerEquiv.toAlgEquivOverRight
items.statement:
def AlgebraTowerEquiv.toAlgEquivOverRight (e : AlgebraTowerEquiv A B) (i j : ι) (h : i ≤ j) :
    letI : Algebra (B i) (B j) := by exact AlgebraTower.toAlgebra h
    letI : Algebra (B i) (A j) := by exact e.toAlgebraOverRight i j h
    AlgEquiv (B i) (B j) (A j)

modules.title: Bases from adjacent tower coordinates
modules.doc:
`AlgebraTower.natBasis` is the basis determined by the executable equivalence
`AlgebraTower.natCoordinates`. Its `repr` is the coordinate map, and its vectors equal the
executable `AlgebraTower.natBasisVector` values.

`AlgebraTower.natBasisOfLE` provides the same basis at arbitrary endpoints `i ≤ j`,
with vectors in `A j` and coefficients in `A i`. Its representation agrees with
`AlgebraTower.natCoordinatesOfLE`, and `AlgebraTower.natBasisVectorOfLE` computes its vectors.

The successor basis agrees with `Module.Basis.smulTower'`, reindexed by `finProdFinEquiv`.
The old coordinate index varies fastest. Each vector is the embedded old basis vector
multiplied by the corresponding new successor basis vector. No normalization of that
successor vector is assumed.

The construction uses `Module.Basis.ofEquivFun` and the scalar-tower basis equations from
Mathlib's `Mathlib.RingTheory.AlgebraTower` module.

items.name: AlgebraTower.natBasis
items.doc: The basis whose coordinates are `natCoordinates`, over the action of the given tower map.
items.statement:
noncomputable def natBasis (i n : ℕ) :
    letI := t.toAlgebra (Nat.le_add_right i n)
    Module.Basis (Fin (coordinateSize d i n)) (A i) (A (i + n))

items.name: AlgebraTower.natBasis_repr
items.doc: The mathematical basis representation is the executable coordinate map.
items.statement:
theorem natBasis_repr (i n : ℕ) (x : A (i + n)) (j : Fin (coordinateSize d i n)) :
    letI := t.toAlgebra (Nat.le_add_right i n)
    (natBasis step i n).repr x j = natCoordinates step i n x j

items.name: AlgebraTower.natBasisVector_eq_natBasis
items.doc: Packing a unit coordinate vector gives the corresponding mathematical basis vector.
items.statement:
theorem natBasisVector_eq_natBasis (i n : ℕ) (j : Fin (coordinateSize d i n)) :
    natBasisVector step i n j = natBasis step i n j

items.name: AlgebraTower.natBasis_succ
items.doc:
The next relative basis is the scalar-tower composition of the previous basis and the
next successor basis, with the old index varying fastest.
items.statement:
theorem natBasis_succ (i n : ℕ) :
    letI := t.toAlgebra (Nat.le_add_right i n)
    letI := t.toAlgebra (Nat.le_succ (i + n))
    letI := t.toAlgebra (Nat.le_add_right i (n + 1))
    letI := toIsScalarTower t (Nat.le_add_right i n) (Nat.le_succ (i + n))
    natBasis step i (n + 1) =
      ((natBasis step i n).smulTower' (Module.Basis.ofEquivFun (step (i + n)))).reindex
        finProdFinEquiv

items.name: AlgebraTower.natBasisVector_succ
items.doc:
At flattened index `oldIndex + oldSize * newIndex`, the vector is the embedded old
vector multiplied by the new successor vector.
items.statement:
theorem natBasisVector_succ (i n : ℕ) (b : Fin (d (i + n)))
    (j : Fin (coordinateSize d i n)) :
    natBasisVector step i (n + 1) (finProdFinEquiv (b, j)) =
      t.algebraMap (i + n) (i + n + 1) (Nat.le_succ (i + n)) (natBasisVector step i n j) *
        (step (i + n)).symm (Pi.single b 1)

items.name: AlgebraTower.natBasisOfLE
items.doc: The basis at arbitrary comparable endpoints, over the action of the given tower map.
items.statement:
noncomputable def natBasisOfLE {i j : ℕ} (h : i ≤ j) :
    letI := t.toAlgebra h
    Module.Basis (Fin (coordinateSize d i (j - i))) (A i) (A j)

items.name: AlgebraTower.natBasisOfLE_repr
items.doc: The endpoint basis representation is the executable endpoint coordinate map.
items.statement:
theorem natBasisOfLE_repr {i j : ℕ} (h : i ≤ j) (x : A j)
    (idx : Fin (coordinateSize d i (j - i))) :
    letI := t.toAlgebra h
    (natBasisOfLE step h).repr x idx = natCoordinatesOfLE step h x idx

items.name: AlgebraTower.natBasisVectorOfLE_eq_natBasisOfLE
items.doc: Packing a unit coordinate vector computes the corresponding endpoint basis vector.
items.statement:
theorem natBasisVectorOfLE_eq_natBasisOfLE {i j : ℕ} (h : i ≤ j)
    (idx : Fin (coordinateSize d i (j - i))) :
    natBasisVectorOfLE step h idx = natBasisOfLE step h idx

items.name: AlgebraTower.natBasisOfLE_apply
items.doc: Endpoint basis vectors agree with the height-indexed basis after identifying the endpoints.
items.statement:
theorem natBasisOfLE_apply {i j : ℕ} (h : i ≤ j)
    (idx : Fin (coordinateSize d i (j - i))) :
    natBasisOfLE step h idx =
      cast (congrArg A (Nat.add_sub_of_le h)) (natBasis step i (j - i) idx)

items.name: AlgebraTower.natBasisOfLE_self
items.doc: At equal endpoints the unique basis vector is one.
items.statement:
theorem natBasisOfLE_self (i : ℕ) (idx : Fin (coordinateSize d i (i - i))) :
    natBasisOfLE step (Nat.le_refl i) idx = 1

modules.title: Coordinates along a natural-number-indexed algebra tower
modules.doc:
Given linear coordinate equivalences between adjacent levels of an `AlgebraTower`,
`AlgebraTower.natCoordinates` gives coordinates at level `i + n` over level `i`. Each scalar
action is induced by the corresponding map of the given tower. The number of successor
coordinates may vary with the level, and may be zero when such an equivalence exists.

The old coordinate index varies fastest: a pair `(newIndex, oldIndex)` has flattened index
`oldIndex + oldSize * newIndex`. Constant successor coordinate count two gives the usual
least-significant-bit-first order.

`AlgebraTower.natPack` is the inverse coordinate map. `AlgebraTower.natBasisVector` packs
a unit coordinate vector. Both are executable, with no enumeration of the tower carriers.
The corresponding mathematical basis is constructed in
`CompPoly.Data.RingTheory.AlgebraTower.Basis`.

For arbitrary endpoints `h : i ≤ j`, `AlgebraTower.natCoordinatesOfLE` and its packing
and vector companions accept elements of `A j` directly. `AlgebraTower.natCoordinatesConstOfLE`
also presents constant successor coordinate count `r` as `Fin (r ^ (j - i))`.

The construction uses `LinearEquiv.restrictScalars`, `LinearEquiv.piCongrRight`,
`LinearEquiv.curry`, and `finProdFinEquiv`. Endpoint and coordinate-count identifications use
`LinearEquiv.cast`, `LinearEquiv.funCongrLeft`, and `finCongr`.

items.name: AlgebraTower.coordinateSize
items.doc:
The number of coordinates from level `i` through `n` steps with chosen coordinate counts `d`.
The next step contributes a new outer block of coordinates.
items.statement: abbrev coordinateSize (d : ℕ → ℕ) (i n : ℕ) : ℕ

items.name: AlgebraTower.coordinateSize_zero
items.doc: An interval with no successor steps has one coordinate.
items.statement: theorem coordinateSize_zero (d : ℕ → ℕ) (i : ℕ) : coordinateSize d i 0 = 1

items.name: AlgebraTower.coordinateSize_succ
items.doc: The number of coordinates is multiplied by the next successor coordinate count.
items.statement:
theorem coordinateSize_succ (d : ℕ → ℕ) (i n : ℕ) :
    coordinateSize d i (n + 1) = d (i + n) * coordinateSize d i n

items.name: AlgebraTower.coordinateSize_const
items.doc: A constant successor coordinate count `r` gives `r ^ n` coordinates over `n` steps.
items.statement:
theorem coordinateSize_const (r i n : ℕ) :
    coordinateSize (fun _ => r) i n = r ^ n

items.name: AlgebraTower.natCoordinates
items.doc:
Coordinates of `A (i + n)` over `A i`, obtained by composing adjacent equivalences.

The scalar action is induced by the given tower map from `i` to `i + n`. At each step,
the old index varies fastest, so `(b, j)` is placed at `j + oldSize * b`.
items.statement:
def natCoordinates (i : ℕ) : (n : ℕ) →
    letI := t.toAlgebra (Nat.le_add_right i n)
    A (i + n) ≃ₗ[A i] (Fin (coordinateSize d i n) → A i)

items.name: AlgebraTower.natCoordinates_zero
items.doc: At height zero the single coordinate is the original element.
items.statement:
theorem natCoordinates_zero (i : ℕ) (x : A i) (j : Fin (coordinateSize d i 0)) :
    natCoordinates step i 0 x j = x

items.name: AlgebraTower.natCoordinates_succ
items.doc:
Read the new outer coordinate, then the old inner coordinate.
Division selects the outer block and remainder selects the position within that block.
items.statement:
theorem natCoordinates_succ (i n : ℕ) (x : A (i + (n + 1)))
    (j : Fin (coordinateSize d i (n + 1))) :
    natCoordinates step i (n + 1) x j =
      natCoordinates step i n (step (i + n) x j.divNat) j.modNat

items.name: AlgebraTower.natPack
items.doc: Pack coordinates in the order used by `natCoordinates`, using the inverse successor maps.
items.statement: def natPack (i n : ℕ) (c : Fin (coordinateSize d i n) → A i) : A (i + n)

items.name: AlgebraTower.natPack_zero
items.doc: At height zero packing returns the single input coefficient.
items.statement:
theorem natPack_zero (i : ℕ) (c : Fin (coordinateSize d i 0) → A i) :
    natPack step i 0 c = c ⟨0, by simp only [coordinateSize_zero]; decide⟩

items.name: AlgebraTower.natPack_succ
items.doc: Pack each old coordinate block, then apply the inverse of the next successor map.
items.statement:
theorem natPack_succ (i n : ℕ) (c : Fin (coordinateSize d i (n + 1)) → A i) :
    natPack step i (n + 1) c =
      (step (i + n)).symm
        (fun b => natPack step i n (fun j => c (finProdFinEquiv (b, j))))

items.name: AlgebraTower.natCoordinates_natPack
items.doc: Reading back packed coordinates recovers the input coefficients.
items.statement:
theorem natCoordinates_natPack (i n : ℕ) (c : Fin (coordinateSize d i n) → A i) :
    natCoordinates step i n (natPack step i n c) = c

items.name: AlgebraTower.natPack_natCoordinates
items.doc: Packing the coordinates of an element recovers that element.
items.statement:
theorem natPack_natCoordinates (i n : ℕ) (x : A (i + n)) :
    natPack step i n (natCoordinates step i n x) = x

items.name: AlgebraTower.natBasisVector
items.doc: The executable vector whose coordinate at `j` is one and whose other coordinates are zero.
items.statement: def natBasisVector (i n : ℕ) (j : Fin (coordinateSize d i n)) : A (i + n)

items.name: AlgebraTower.natCoordinates_natBasisVector
items.doc: A basis vector reads back as its unit coordinate vector.
items.statement:
theorem natCoordinates_natBasisVector (i n : ℕ) (j : Fin (coordinateSize d i n)) :
    natCoordinates step i n (natBasisVector step i n j) = Pi.single j 1

items.name: AlgebraTower.natCoordinatesOfLE
items.doc:
Coordinates of `A j` over `A i` for comparable endpoints, with the given tower action.
The coordinate count and order are those of the `j - i` successor steps starting at `i`.

items.name: AlgebraTower.natCoordinatesOfLE_apply
items.doc:
Endpoint coordinates are height coordinates after identifying `j` with `i + (j - i)`.
The coordinate index is unchanged.
items.statement:
theorem natCoordinatesOfLE_apply {i j : ℕ} (h : i ≤ j) (x : A j)
    (idx : Fin (coordinateSize d i (j - i))) :
    natCoordinatesOfLE step h x idx =
      natCoordinates step i (j - i) (cast (congrArg A (Nat.add_sub_of_le h).symm) x) idx

items.name: AlgebraTower.natCoordinatesOfLE_self
items.doc: With equal endpoints the single coordinate is the original element.
items.statement:
theorem natCoordinatesOfLE_self (i : ℕ) (x : A i)
    (idx : Fin (coordinateSize d i (i - i))) :
    natCoordinatesOfLE step (Nat.le_refl i) x idx = x

items.name: AlgebraTower.natPackOfLE
items.doc: Pack coordinates into `A j`, inverting the coordinate map over the given tower action.
items.statement: def natPackOfLE {i j : ℕ} (h : i ≤ j) (c : Fin (coordinateSize d i (j - i)) → A i) : A j

items.name: AlgebraTower.natPackOfLE_eq_natPack
items.doc: Endpoint packing is height packing followed by the identification `i + (j - i) = j`.
items.statement:
theorem natPackOfLE_eq_natPack {i j : ℕ} (h : i ≤ j)
    (c : Fin (coordinateSize d i (j - i)) → A i) :
    natPackOfLE step h c = cast (congrArg A (Nat.add_sub_of_le h)) (natPack step i (j - i) c)

items.name: AlgebraTower.natPackOfLE_self
items.doc: Packing at equal endpoints returns the single coefficient.
items.statement:
theorem natPackOfLE_self (i : ℕ) (c : Fin (coordinateSize d i (i - i)) → A i) :
    natPackOfLE step (Nat.le_refl i) c =
      c ⟨0, by simp only [Nat.sub_self, coordinateSize_zero]; decide⟩

items.name: AlgebraTower.natCoordinatesOfLE_natPackOfLE
items.doc: Reading packed endpoint coordinates recovers the input coefficients.
items.statement:
theorem natCoordinatesOfLE_natPackOfLE {i j : ℕ} (h : i ≤ j)
    (c : Fin (coordinateSize d i (j - i)) → A i) :
    natCoordinatesOfLE step h (natPackOfLE step h c) = c

items.name: AlgebraTower.natPackOfLE_natCoordinatesOfLE
items.doc: Packing the endpoint coordinates of an element recovers that element.
items.statement:
theorem natPackOfLE_natCoordinatesOfLE {i j : ℕ} (h : i ≤ j) (x : A j) :
    natPackOfLE step h (natCoordinatesOfLE step h x) = x

items.name: AlgebraTower.natBasisVectorOfLE
items.doc: The executable endpoint vector with coordinate one at `idx` and zero elsewhere.
items.statement: def natBasisVectorOfLE {i j : ℕ} (h : i ≤ j) (idx : Fin (coordinateSize d i (j - i))) : A j

items.name: AlgebraTower.natBasisVectorOfLE_eq_natBasisVector
items.doc: Endpoint vectors agree with height vectors under the canonical endpoint identification.
items.statement:
theorem natBasisVectorOfLE_eq_natBasisVector {i j : ℕ} (h : i ≤ j)
    (idx : Fin (coordinateSize d i (j - i))) :
    natBasisVectorOfLE step h idx =
      cast (congrArg A (Nat.add_sub_of_le h)) (natBasisVector step i (j - i) idx)

items.name: AlgebraTower.natCoordinatesOfLE_natBasisVectorOfLE
items.doc: An endpoint vector reads back as its unit coordinate vector.
items.statement:
theorem natCoordinatesOfLE_natBasisVectorOfLE {i j : ℕ} (h : i ≤ j)
    (idx : Fin (coordinateSize d i (j - i))) :
    natCoordinatesOfLE step h (natBasisVectorOfLE step h idx) = Pi.single idx 1

items.name: AlgebraTower.natBasisVectorOfLE_self
items.doc: At equal endpoints the unique executable basis vector is one.
items.statement:
theorem natBasisVectorOfLE_self (i : ℕ) (idx : Fin (coordinateSize d i (i - i))) :
    natBasisVectorOfLE step (Nat.le_refl i) idx = 1

items.name: AlgebraTower.natCoordinatesConstOfLE
items.doc:
Endpoint coordinates with constant successor coordinate count `r`, indexed by `Fin (r^(j-i))`.
Only the coordinate count is identified with a power; each index retains its numeric value.

items.name: AlgebraTower.natCoordinatesConstOfLE_apply
items.doc: Constant-count coordinates read the same numeric index in the endpoint coordinate map.
items.statement:
theorem natCoordinatesConstOfLE_apply {i j : ℕ} (h : i ≤ j) (x : A j)
    (idx : Fin (r ^ (j - i))) :
    natCoordinatesConstOfLE constantStep h x idx =
      natCoordinatesOfLE constantStep h x
        (Fin.cast (coordinateSize_const r i (j - i)).symm idx)

items.name: AlgebraTower.natCoordinatesConstOfLE_self
items.doc: Constant-count coordinates at equal endpoints consist of the original element.
items.statement:
theorem natCoordinatesConstOfLE_self (i : ℕ) (x : A i) (idx : Fin (r ^ (i - i))) :
    natCoordinatesConstOfLE constantStep (Nat.le_refl i) x idx = x

modules.title: Canonical Euclidean Domains
modules.doc:
This module defines `CanonicalEuclideanDomain` and provides instances for ℤ, `Polynomial F`,
and `Field`.

items.name: CanonicalEuclideanDomain
items.doc:
# Canonical Euclidean Domains

A `CanonicalEuclideanDomain` is a restriction of `EuclideanDomain`. It introduces a selection
rule for canonical remainders and guarantees there exists exactly one
`canonical` quotient (`q`) and remainder (`r`) for any pair of dividend (`a`) and divisor (`b`)
(assuming `b ≠ 0`), no matter how the division is implemented (i.e. the division result is
unique and consistent across different implementations).

## Motivation: The unpredictable behaviors of `/` and `%` in `EuclideanDomain`

In a standard `EuclideanDomain`, the operators `/` and `%` are viewed as black-boxes and are
only required to return *some* valid pair satisfying `a = b * q + r` and `r ≺ b`. This loose
specification allows implementations to be **unpredictable** and **inconsistent**:
1. **Unprovable Algebraic Identities:**
  An implementation is permitted to switch strategies arbitrarily (e.g., rounding up for input `x`
  but down for input `y`; or following truncation-towards-zero as in C/Rust/Java, ...).
  This makes natural identities like `(a + b * k) / b = a / b + k` **false** in the general
  case, as the term `b * k` might trigger a strategy switch.
2. **Non-Determinism Accumulation (Unit Drift):**
  Algorithms that chain multiple operations (like GCD) accumulate arbitrary unit factors
  at every step. For example, `gcd(a, b)` is only unique up to a unit.
    * `gcd(a, gcd(b, c))` might return `g`.
    * `gcd(gcd(a, b), c)` might return `-g` (or `u * g`).
    While mathematically equivalent (associates), they are **not equal** as data structures.
    This breaks any system relying on bit-exact equality (hashing, caching, serialization).

**The Solution:** `CanonicalEuclideanDomain` solves this by enforcing a strict
`is_canonical_remainder` predicate. This restricts the implementation space to **exactly one**
valid function, ensuring the `bit-exact` uniqueness of the outputs, no matter what
implementations are used.

## Advantages

* **Algebraic Stability:** Restores critical algebraic properties,
    enabling a suite of powerful rewrite rules (e.g., `add_mod_eq`, `add_mul_div_right`,
    `mul_mod_eq`, `mod_eq_of_eq_add_mul`) that are unprovable in the normal `EuclideanDomain`
    setting. This brings **canonical regularity** to domains with **non-unique remainders**
    (e.g., `ℤ`, `Polynomial F`).

* **Generic Algorithms over Rings:** Guarantees strictly normalized outputs (positive GCDs,
    monic generators) for high-level algorithms (Smith Normal Form, Hermite Normal Form).
    It prevents the `unit drift` described above, allowing generic algorithms to run
    deterministically on complex domains like `Polynomial F`.

* **Protocol Determinism:** Essential for cryptographic protocols (ZK transcripts, Fiat-Shamir)
    where objects must have bit-exact representations. It ensures that every implementation
    (Lean, Rust, ZK circuits) converges to the *same* remainder given the same canonical
    remainder rule, guaranteeing correctness and hash consistency.

## Supported Instances

This abstraction unifies commonly used mathematical objects under one interface:
1.  **Integers (`ℤ`):** The canonical rule enforces **non-negative remainders** (`0 ≤ r < |b|`).
    This matches the behavior of Python's `%` or Rust's `rem_euclid`.
2.  **Polynomials (`Polynomial F`):** Uniqueness is naturally enforced by the degree structure.
    Any remainder with `degree(r) < degree(b)` is automatically unique due to the ultrametric
    property of polynomial degrees (i.e., `degree(a - b) ≤ max(degree a, degree b)`).
3.  **Fields (`ℚ`, `ℝ`, `ZMod p` where p is prime, ...):** Division is exact; the canonical
  remainder is always `0`.
4.  **Other Euclidean Rings:** Gaussian Integers (`ℤ[i]`), Eisenstein Integers (`ℤ[ω]`), and
    Discrete Valuation Rings (DVRs) can potentially be adapted to this interface by defining
    strict geometric or valuation-based selection rules.

## Definition
It extends `EuclideanDomain` with:
1.  `is_canonical_remainder b r`: A predicate deciding if a remainder `r` is the "chosen one".
2.  `remainder_is_canonical`: A proof that the built-in `%` operator satisfies this predicate.
3.  `unique_division`: The `Uniqueness Axiom` stating that if `(q1, r1)` and `(q2, r2)`
    both satisfy the division equation and the canonical rule, they must be equal.
items.statement:
class CanonicalEuclideanDomain (R : Type u) extends EuclideanDomain R where
  is_canonical_remainder : (b : R) → (r : R) → Prop
  -- The built-in operator `remainder (%)` must obey the rule
  remainder_is_canonical : ∀ (a b : R), (hb : b ≠ 0) → is_canonical_remainder b (remainder a b)

  unique_division : ∀ {a b q₁ q₂ r₁ r₂: R}, (hb : b ≠ 0) → (h_eq_div_mul_add₁ : a = b * q₁ + r₁)
    → (h_eq_div_mul_add₂ : a = b * q₂ + r₂)
    → (is_canonical_remainder₁ : is_canonical_remainder b r₁)
    → (is_canonical_remainder₂ : is_canonical_remainder b r₂)
    → q₁ = q₂ ∧ r₁ = r₂

items.name: CanonicalEuclideanDomain.div_eq_of_canonical_eq_mul_add
items.doc:
The Fundamental Theorem of Canonical Euclidean Domains.
If you find ANY pair (q, r) that satisfies the division equation
AND the canonical condition, then q MUST be the result of the division operation.
items.statement:
theorem div_eq_of_canonical_eq_mul_add {a b q r : R} (hb : b ≠ 0)
    (h_eq : a = b * q + r)
    (h_can : is_canonical_remainder b r) :
    a / b = q

items.name: CanonicalEuclideanDomain.div_eq_and_mod_eq_iff
items.doc:
The Fundamental Theorem of CEDs:
Satisfying the division equation + size constraint is EQUIVALENT
to being the output of the division function.
items.statement:
theorem div_eq_and_mod_eq_iff {a b q r : R} (hn : b ≠ 0) :
    (a / b = q ∧ a % b = r) ↔ (a = b * q + r ∧ is_canonical_remainder b r)

items.name: CanonicalEuclideanDomain.add_mul_div_right
items.doc:
Generalized `add_mul_div_right`: `(a + b * r) / b = a / b + r`
In a standard ED, this isn't always true (the quotient is not unique).
In a CED, it is always true.
items.statement:
theorem add_mul_div_right (a b r : R) (hb : b ≠ 0) :
    (a + b * r) / b = a / b + r

items.name: CanonicalEuclideanDomain.add_mul_mod_right
items.doc:
Generalized `add_mul_mod_right`: (a + b * r) % b = a % b
The remainder ignores multiples of the divisor.
items.statement:
theorem add_mul_mod_right (a b r : R) (hb : b ≠ 0) :
    (a + b * r) % b = a % b

items.name: CanonicalEuclideanDomain.add_mul_mod_left
items.doc:
Generalized `add_mul_mod_left`: (a * r + b) % a = b % a`
The remainder ignores multiples of the divisor.
items.statement:
theorem add_mul_mod_left (a b r : R) (hb : a ≠ 0) :
    (a * r + b) % a = b % a

items.name: CanonicalEuclideanDomain.mod_eq_of_eq_add_mul
items.doc: `If a = b + n * r, then a % n = b % n.`
items.statement:
theorem mod_eq_of_eq_add_mul {a b n q : R} (h_eq_add_mul : a = b + n * q) (hn : n ≠ 0) :
    a % n = b % n

items.name: CanonicalEuclideanDomain.mul_mod_eq_mul_mod_left
items.statement:
theorem mul_mod_eq_mul_mod_left (a b n : R) (hn : n ≠ 0) :
    (a * b) % n = ((a % n) * b) % n

items.name: CanonicalEuclideanDomain.mul_mod_eq_zero_of_mod_dvd
items.statement:
theorem mul_mod_eq_zero_of_mod_dvd (a b n : R) (hn : n ≠ 0)
    (h_mod_eq_zero : a % n = 0) : (a * b) % n = 0

items.name: CanonicalEuclideanDomain.add_mod_eq_add_mod_left
items.statement:
theorem add_mod_eq_add_mod_left (a b n : R) (hn : n ≠ 0) :
    (a + b) % n = ((a % n) + b) % n

items.name: CanonicalEuclideanDomain.add_mod_eq
items.statement:
theorem add_mod_eq (a b n : R) (hn : n ≠ 0) :
    (a + b) % n = (a % n + b % n) % n

items.name: CanonicalEuclideanDomain.mul_mod_eq
items.statement:
theorem mul_mod_eq (a b n : R) (hn : n ≠ 0) :
    (a * b) % n = ((a % n) * (b % n)) % n

items.name: CanonicalEuclideanDomain.mod_mod_eq_mod
items.statement:
theorem mod_mod_eq_mod (a n : R) (hn : n ≠ 0) :
    (a % n) % n = a % n

items.name: CanonicalEuclideanDomain.dvd_sub_mod
items.statement:
theorem dvd_sub_mod (a b : R) :
    b ∣ a - (a % b)

modules.title: Definitions and lemmas for `Vector`
modules.doc:
`accumulateProducts` separates product accumulation from reduction. Its reduction theorem
recovers `dotProduct` whenever reduction preserves zero, addition, and the chosen products.

items.name: Vector.induction₂_temp
items.statement:
def induction₂_temp {α β} {motive : {n : ℕ} → Vector α n → Vector β n → Sort*}
    (v_empty : motive #v[] #v[])
  (v_insert : {n : ℕ} → (hd : α) → (tl : Vector α n) → (hd' : β) → (tl' : Vector β n) →
      motive tl tl' → motive (tl.insertIdx 0 hd) (tl'.insertIdx 0 hd')) {m : ℕ} :
    (v : Vector α m) → (v' : Vector β m) → motive v v'

items.name: Vector.nil
items.doc: The empty vector.
items.statement: def nil {α} : Vector α 0

items.name: Vector.cons
items.doc:
Construct a vector by prepending an element to the front of a vector,
using `insertIdx` at `0`.
items.statement: def cons {α} {n : ℕ} (hd : α) (tl : Vector α n) : Vector α (n + 1)

items.name: Vector.head_cons
items.statement: theorem head_cons {α} {n : ℕ} (hd : α) (tl : Vector α n) : (cons hd tl).head = hd

items.name: Vector.cons_get_eq
items.statement:
lemma cons_get_eq {α} {n : ℕ} (hd : α) (tl : Vector α n) (i : Fin (n + 1)) :
    (cons hd tl).get i =
      if hi: i.val == 0 then hd else tl.get (⟨i.val - 1, by
        simp only [beq_iff_eq, Fin.val_eq_zero_iff] at hi
        apply Nat.sub_lt_left_of_lt_add
        · by_contra hi_ne_gt_1
          simp only [not_le, Nat.lt_one_iff, Fin.val_eq_zero_iff] at hi_ne_gt_1
          contradiction
        · have hi_lt:= i.isLt; omega
      ⟩)

items.name: Vector.cons_empty_tail_eq_nil
items.statement:
lemma cons_empty_tail_eq_nil {α} (hd : α) (tl : Vector α 0) :
    cons hd tl = ⟨#[hd], rfl⟩

items.name: Vector.tail_cons
items.statement: theorem tail_cons {α} {n : ℕ} (hd : α) (tl : Vector α n) : (cons hd tl).tail = tl

items.name: Vector.cons_toList_eq_List_cons
items.statement:
theorem cons_toList_eq_List_cons {α} {n : ℕ} (hd : α) (tl : Vector α n) :
    (cons hd tl).toList = hd :: tl.toList

items.name: Vector.foldl_eq_toList_foldl
items.statement:
theorem foldl_eq_toList_foldl {α β} {n : ℕ} (f : β → α → β) (init : β) (v : Vector α n) :
    v.foldl (f:=f) (b:=init) = v.toList.foldl (f:=f) (init:=init)

items.name: Vector.foldl_succ
items.statement:
theorem foldl_succ
    {α β} {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] (f : β → α → β) (init : β) (v : Vector α n) :
    v.foldl (f:=f) (b:=init) = v.tail.foldl (f:=f) (b:=f init v.head)

items.name: Vector.zipWith_cons
items.statement:
theorem zipWith_cons {α β γ} {n : ℕ} (f : α → β → γ)
    (a : α) (b : Vector α n) (c : β) (d : Vector β n) :
  zipWith f (cons a b) (cons c d) = cons (f a c) (zipWith f b d)

items.name: Vector.dotProduct
items.doc:
Inner product between two vectors of the same size. Should be faster than `_root_.dotProduct`
due to efficient operations on `Vector`s.
items.statement: def dotProduct [Zero R] [Add R] [Mul R] (a b : Vector R n) : R

items.name: Vector.accumulateProducts
items.doc:
Accumulate paired products from equal-length vectors, from left to right, starting at `init`.
The products and accumulator lie in `W`; no reduction is performed.
items.statement:
def accumulateProducts {W : Type*} [Add W] (product : R → R → W) (init : W)
    (a b : Vector R n) : W

items.name: Vector.reduce_accumulateProducts
items.doc:
If reduction preserves addition and each paired product, reducing the accumulator gives
the reduced initial value plus the dot product of the input vectors.
items.statement:
theorem reduce_accumulateProducts {W : Type*} [AddZero W] [AddMonoid R] [Mul R]
    (reduce : W →+ R) (product : R → R → W)
    (hproduct : ∀ x y, reduce (product x y) = x * y) (init : W) (a b : Vector R n) :
    reduce (accumulateProducts product init a b) = reduce init + dotProduct a b

items.name: Vector.reduce_accumulateProducts_zero
items.doc: Reducing a product accumulator initialized at zero recovers the dot product.
items.statement:
theorem reduce_accumulateProducts_zero {W : Type*} [AddZero W] [AddMonoid R] [Mul R]
    (reduce : W →+ R) (product : R → R → W)
    (hproduct : ∀ x y, reduce (product x y) = x * y) (a b : Vector R n) :
    reduce (accumulateProducts product 0 a b) = dotProduct a b

items.name: Vector.accumulateProducts_mul
items.doc: Ordinary multiplication is an eager product accumulator, with identity reduction.
items.statement:
theorem accumulateProducts_mul [AddMonoid R] [Mul R] (init : R) (a b : Vector R n) :
    accumulateProducts (· * ·) init a b = init + dotProduct a b

items.name: Vector.dotProduct_cons
items.statement:
lemma dotProduct_cons [AddCommMonoid R] [Mul R] (a : R) (b : Vector R n) (c : R) (d : Vector R n) :
    dotProduct (cons a b) (cons c d) = a * c + dotProduct b d

items.name: Vector.Matrix.ofFinMatrix
items.doc: Convert from a `Fin`-indexed matrix (the definition in Mathlib): `Fin m → Fin n → α`
items.statement: def ofFinMatrix {m n : ℕ} (matrix : _root_.Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) α) : Matrix α m n

items.name: Vector.Matrix.transpose
items.doc: Transpose a matrix by swapping rows and columns.
items.statement: def transpose {m n : ℕ} (matrix : Matrix α m n) : Matrix α n m

items.name: dotProduct_cons
items.statement:
lemma dotProduct_cons (a : R) (b : Vector R n) (c : R) (d : Vector R n) :
    _root_.dotProduct (cons a b).get (cons c d).get = a * c + _root_.dotProduct b.get d.get

items.name: Vector.dotProduct_eq_root_dotProduct
items.statement:
theorem dotProduct_eq_root_dotProduct (a b : Vector R n) :
    dotProduct a b = _root_.dotProduct a.get b.get

items.name: Vector.map_dotProduct
items.doc: A ring homomorphism maps a dot product to the dot product of the mapped vectors.
items.statement:
theorem map_dotProduct {R S : Type*} [NonAssocSemiring R] [NonAssocSemiring S]
    (f : R →+* S) {n : ℕ} (a b : Vector R n) :
    f (dotProduct a b) = dotProduct (a.map f) (b.map f)

## Constants

These are convenience constants for the BabyBear field:
- `pBits = 31`
- `twoAdicity = 27` with `fieldSize - 1 = 2^27 * 15`

items.doc: Fermat-style inversion in `ZMod fieldSize`.

items.note:
## Two-adicity and roots of unity table

We record the factorization of `fieldSize - 1` and provide a precomputed table
of `2^n`-th roots of unity for `0 ≤ n ≤ twoAdicity`.

items.name: BabyBear.fieldSize_sub_one_factorization
items.doc: The factorization `fieldSize - 1 = 2^twoAdicity * 15`.
items.statement: lemma fieldSize_sub_one_factorization : fieldSize - 1 = 2 ^ twoAdicity * 15

items.note:
A table of `2^n`-th roots of unity. The element at index `n` generates the
multiplicative subgroup of order `2^n`.

The first entry n = 0 is 1.

items.name: BabyBear.twoAdicGenerators
items.doc: Precomputed generators for the BabyBear two-adic subgroups.
items.statement: def twoAdicGenerators : List Field

items.name: BabyBear.twoAdicGenerators_length
items.doc: The BabyBear two-adic generator table has one entry for each supported exponent.
items.statement: lemma twoAdicGenerators_length : twoAdicGenerators.length = twoAdicity + 1

items.name: BabyBear.twoAdicGenerators_succ_square_eq'
items.doc: Consecutive BabyBear two-adic generators square to the previous generator.
items.statement:
lemma twoAdicGenerators_succ_square_eq' (idx : Fin twoAdicity) :
    twoAdicGenerators[idx.val + 1] ^ 2 = twoAdicGenerators[idx]

items.name: BabyBear.twoAdicGenerators_succ_square_eq
items.doc: Consecutive BabyBear two-adic generators square to the previous generator.
items.statement:
lemma twoAdicGenerators_succ_square_eq (idx : Nat) (h : idx < twoAdicity) :
    haveI : idx + 1 < twoAdicGenerators.length := by simp [twoAdicGenerators_length, h]
    twoAdicGenerators[idx + 1] ^ 2 = twoAdicGenerators[idx]

items.name: BabyBear.twoAdicity_maximal
items.doc: `twoAdicity` is maximal: `2^(twoAdicity+1)` does not divide `fieldSize - 1`.
items.statement: lemma twoAdicity_maximal : ¬ (2 ^ (twoAdicity + 1)) ∣ (fieldSize - 1)

items.name: BabyBear.twoAdicGenerators_pow_twoPow_eq_one
items.doc: The power `(twoAdicGenerators[bits])^(2^bits) = 1`.
items.statement:
lemma twoAdicGenerators_pow_twoPow_eq_one (bits : Fin (twoAdicity + 1)) :
    twoAdicGenerators[bits] ^ (2 ^ (bits : Nat)) = 1

items.name: BabyBear.twoAdicGenerators_pow_twoPow_ne_one_of_lt
items.doc: If `m < bits`, then `(twoAdicGenerators[bits])^(2^m) ≠ 1`.
items.statement:
lemma twoAdicGenerators_pow_twoPow_ne_one_of_lt
    {bits : Fin (twoAdicity + 1)} {m : Nat} (hm : m < bits) :
    (twoAdicGenerators[bits]) ^ (2 ^ m) ≠ (1 : Field)

items.name: BabyBear.isPrimitiveRoot_twoAdicGenerator
items.doc: The precomputed element at index `bits` is a primitive `2^bits`-th root of unity.
items.statement:
lemma isPrimitiveRoot_twoAdicGenerator (n : Fin (twoAdicity + 1)) :
    IsPrimitiveRoot (twoAdicGenerators[n]) (2 ^ (n : Nat))

items.name: BabyBear.twoAdicGenerator_unit_mem_rootsOfUnity
items.doc: As a unit, the precomputed element is a member of `rootsOfUnity (2^bits)`.
items.statement:
lemma twoAdicGenerator_unit_mem_rootsOfUnity
    (bits : Fin (twoAdicity + 1)) (h : twoAdicGenerators[bits] ≠ 0) :
    Units.mk0 (twoAdicGenerators[bits]) h ∈ rootsOfUnity (2 ^ (bits : Nat)) Field

items.name: BabyBear.twoAdicGenerators_order
items.doc: The order of `twoAdicGenerators[bits]` equals `2^bits`.
items.statement:
lemma twoAdicGenerators_order (bits : Fin (twoAdicity + 1)) :
    orderOf (twoAdicGenerators[bits]) = 2 ^ (bits : Nat)

modules.title: The degree-4 extension of BabyBear
modules.doc:
`BabyBear[X] / (X^4 - 11)`, the challenge field used alongside the BabyBear base field in
RISC Zero and Plonky3.

Irreducibility of `X^4 - 11` is discharged by
`Polynomial.irreducible_X_pow_four_sub_C`, whose two hypotheses are single
exponentiations in the base field: `11^((p^4-1)/4) = 1` and `11^((p^2-1)/4) ≠ 1`.

## Main definitions

* `BabyBear.ext4Params`: the `BinomialParams` for `X^4 - 11`.
* `BabyBear.Ext4`: the extension field itself.

items.doc: The parameters of the quartic extension `BabyBear[X] / (X^4 - 11)`.

items.name: BabyBear.ext4Params_W
items.statement: theorem ext4Params_W : ext4Params.W = 11

items.name: BabyBear.ext4Params_q
items.statement: theorem ext4Params_q : ext4Params.q = fieldSize

items.name: BabyBear.ext4Gen_eq_gen
items.doc:
`ext4Gen` is the framework's `Ext.gen`.

Deliberately **not** `@[simp]`: as a rewrite it fires before `ext4Gen_pow_four` can match, which
would knock that lemma out of the simp set. Use `simp [ext4Gen_eq_gen]` to reach the general
`Ext.gen` lemmas (`Ext.coeff_gen`, `Ext.gen_pow_d`) when the specialized ones below are not
enough.
items.statement: theorem ext4Gen_eq_gen : ext4Gen = Ext.gen

items.name: BabyBear.toQuot_ext4Gen
items.doc: `ext4Gen` maps to the adjoined root of the specification.
items.statement: theorem toQuot_ext4Gen : Ext.toQuot ext4Gen = Ext.rt ext4Params.toExtensionParams

items.name: BabyBear.ext4Gen_pow_four

items.statement: theorem ext4Gen_pow_four : ext4Gen ^ 4 = Ext.ofBase (11 : Field)
