modules.title: Serialization of `BF64`
modules.doc:
A `BF64` element is a bit pattern in the polynomial basis of
`GF(2)[X] / (X^64 + X^4 + X^3 + X + 1)`, bit `i` the coefficient of `X^i`. Its canonical natural
is that pattern read as an integer, and its encoding is the eight little-endian bytes of the
word, the same bytes a `u64::to_le_bytes` of the word gives. No other presentation of
`GF(2^64)` is implied.

items.name: BF64.canonicalNat_bound
items.statement: theorem canonicalNat_bound : CanonicalNat.bound BF64 = 2 ^ 64

items.name: BF64.canonicalNat_toNat
items.statement: theorem canonicalNat_toNat (x : BF64) : CanonicalNat.toNat x = x.toBitVec.toNat

items.name: BF64.byteCodec_width
items.statement: theorem byteCodec_width : ByteCodec.width BF64 = 8

modules.title: The degree-3 extension of `GF(2^64)`
modules.doc:
```text
GF(2^64)[y] / (y^3 + y + 1),   giving GF(2^192)
```

An element is `c0 + c1 * y + c2 * y^2` with each coefficient in `BF64`. The carrier comes
from the computable extension framework in `CompPoly/Fields/Extension/`. Its coefficient
vector is `Vector BF64 3`, with the three limbs ordered as `c0`, `c1`, and `c2`.
`Ext.coeffs` and `Ext.ofVector` give inverse maps between elements and these coordinates.

Irreducibility needs no certificate here, unlike the degree-64 base modulus: a cubic is
irreducible exactly when it has no root, and a short characteristic-two argument rules one
out. See `CompPoly/Fields/KoalaBear/Ext5.lean` for the general monic-modulus pattern this
follows.

## Main definitions

* `ext3Poly` — the modulus `y^3 + y + 1` over `BF64`.
* `ext3Params` — its `CompPoly.Extension.ExtensionParams`.
* `Ext3` — the extension field itself.

## Main statements

* `ext3Poly_irreducible` — the cubic is irreducible over `BF64`.
* `ext3Params_poly` — the coefficient vector `#v[1, 1, 0]` denotes that cubic.
* `nat_card_ext3` — `Nat.card Ext3 = 2 ^ 192`.

## Implementation notes

`ext3Params_poly` is load-bearing: it ties the coefficient vector `#v[1, 1, 0]` to
`y ^ 3 + y + 1`. A wrong vector there would still compile and would silently give a
different field, so it is checked against reference vectors in
`tests/CompPolyTests/Fields/Binary/BF64.lean` rather than only re-derived.

items.name: BF64.ext3Poly
items.doc: The extension modulus `y^3 + y + 1` over `GF(2^64)`.
items.statement: noncomputable def ext3Poly : Polynomial BF64

items.name: BF64.ext3Poly_natDegree
items.doc: The cubic has degree `3`.
items.statement: theorem ext3Poly_natDegree : ext3Poly.natDegree = 3

items.name: BF64.ext3Poly_degree
items.doc: `ext3Poly_natDegree` in `degree` form.
items.statement: theorem ext3Poly_degree : ext3Poly.degree = (3 : ℕ)

items.name: BF64.ext3Poly_monic
items.doc: The cubic is monic, as the extension framework requires.
items.statement: theorem ext3Poly_monic : ext3Poly.Monic

items.note:
## Irreducibility

A cubic is irreducible exactly when it has no root. A root `a` of `y^3 + y + 1` satisfies
`a^3 = a + 1`, from which `a^7 = 1`. The multiplicative group of `GF(2^64)` has order
`2^64 - 1`, which is coprime to `7`, so `a = 1` — and `1` is not a root.

items.name: BF64.ext3Poly_no_root
items.doc:
The cubic has no root in `GF(2^64)`.

A root has `a ^ 7 = 1`, so its multiplicative order divides `7`. It also divides
`Fintype.card BF64 - 1 = 2 ^ 64 - 1`, which is coprime to `7`, so the order is `1` and
`a = 1`. But `1` is not a root.
items.statement: theorem ext3Poly_no_root (a : BF64) : ¬ext3Poly.IsRoot a

items.doc: The cubic `y^3 + y + 1` is irreducible over `GF(2^64)`.
items.statement: theorem ext3Poly_irreducible : Irreducible ext3Poly

modules.title: The computable `GF(2^64)` carrier
modules.doc:
An element stores a 64-bit word whose bit `i` is the coefficient of `x^i`. Addition is `xor`,
multiplication is a carry-less product followed by `reduce`, and inversion is the
Itoh-Tsujii addition chain. The carrier maps into `AdjoinRoot basePoly` through
`BF64.toQuot`, so Mathlib's field theory applies while the operations stay executable.
The nominal carrier separates this polynomial presentation from raw words and binary towers.
`ofBitVec` and `toBitVec` expose its coordinates; field numerals use characteristic-two casts.
Finiteness is supplied as a proposition, with cardinality stated using `Nat.card`. Enumeration
is an explicit proof-side choice and is never constructed during native module startup.

## Main definitions

* `BF64` — the nominal carrier with `Add`, `Mul`, `Inv`, `CommRing` and `Field`.
* `BF64.ofBitVec`, `BF64.toBitVec` — explicit maps to and from its 64-bit coordinates.
* `BF64.toQuot` — the bridge into `BF64Quot`.
* `BF64.powTwoPow` — repeated squaring, `a ^ (2 ^ k)`.
* `BF64.invItohTsujii` — inversion by the Itoh-Tsujii addition chain.

## Main statements

* `BF64.toQuot_add`, `BF64.toQuot_mul` — the bridge is a ring homomorphism.
* `BF64.toQuot_injective`, `BF64.toQuot_surjective` — it is a bijection.
* `BF64.mul_invItohTsujii` — the addition chain really inverts.
* `BF64.nat_card_bf64` — `Nat.card BF64 = 2 ^ 64`.

## Implementation notes

The algebraic instances are written out field-by-field rather than obtained from
`Function.Injective.commRing`. That transport takes the bridge map as *data*, which makes
the whole structure noncomputable and shadows the computable `Mul` and `Pow`; because
`CompPoly.Extension.Ext.mul` reaches through the base field's `Field` instance, a
noncomputable base field would take the extension in `BF64/Ext3.lean` down with it too.
The `#guard` checks in `tests/CompPolyTests/Fields/Binary/BF64.lean` run the compiled
arithmetic and so fail the build if this ever regresses.

`Pow` is `npowBinRec`, binary exponentiation, matching
`CompPoly.Extension.Ext.instPowNat`. The linear `npowRec` would need `2 ^ 64`
multiplications for a full-order exponent and is unusable in the kernel.

items.doc: An element of `GF(2)[X] / (X^64 + X^4 + X^3 + X + 1)`, stored in a polynomial basis.

structure BF64 where
  /-- Bit `i` is the coefficient of `X^i`. -/
  toBitVec : BitVec 64
  deriving DecidableEq, BEq

items.name: BF64.mul_def
items.doc: Multiplication uses the named executable product.
items.statement: theorem mul_def (a b : BF64) : a * b = mul a b

items.name: BF64.toBitVec_mul
items.doc: The product word is the reduced carry-less product of the input words.
items.statement:
theorem toBitVec_mul (a b : BF64) :
    (a * b).toBitVec = reduce (carryLessMul (w := 128) a.toBitVec b.toBitVec)

items.note: ## The bridge is a ring homomorphism

items.name: BF64.toPolyBF64_zero
items.statement: theorem toPolyBF64_zero : toPolyBF64 0 = 0

items.name: BF64.toQuot_zero
items.statement: theorem toQuot_zero : toQuot 0 = 0

items.name: BF64.toPolyBF64_add
items.statement:
theorem toPolyBF64_add (a b : BF64) :
    toPolyBF64 (a + b) = toPolyBF64 a + toPolyBF64 b

items.name: BF64.toQuot_add
items.statement: theorem toQuot_add (a b : BF64) : toQuot (a + b) = toQuot a + toQuot b

items.name: BF64.toQuot_mul
items.doc: Multiplication agrees with the quotient's, because `reduce` computes the remainder.
items.statement: theorem toQuot_mul (a b : BF64) : toQuot (a * b) = toQuot a * toQuot b

items.name: BF64.toQuot_injective
items.doc:
Distinct carrier values denote distinct quotient elements.

A difference of two carrier values has degree below 64, while the modulus has degree
exactly 64, so the modulus can divide it only when it is zero.
items.statement: theorem toQuot_injective : Function.Injective toQuot

items.note:
## Algebraic structure

Every law is discharged by pushing through the injective `toQuot` into the quotient,
where it holds because `BF64Quot` is a commutative ring. The instances are
built field-by-field rather than by `Function.Injective.commRing`, because that transport
takes `toQuot` as data and would make the operations noncomputable.

items.name: BF64.toPolyBF64_one
items.statement: theorem toPolyBF64_one : toPolyBF64 1 = 1

items.name: BF64.toQuot_one
items.statement: theorem toQuot_one : toQuot 1 = 1

items.name: BF64.toQuot_inj
items.statement: theorem toQuot_inj {a b : BF64} : toQuot a = toQuot b ↔ a = b

items.name: BF64.add_self
items.doc: Addition is self-cancelling: the field has characteristic two.
items.statement: theorem add_self (a : BF64) : a + a = 0

items.note:
### Scalar and power operations

Scalar multiples use the additive recursion. Natural casts use parity, and integer casts
use the corresponding natural cast and negation. Raw polynomial-basis words enter through
`ofBitVec`, independently of numeral casting.

items.name: BF64.natCast
items.doc: Cast a natural number by its parity in characteristic two.
items.statement: def natCast (n : ℕ) : BF64

items.name: BF64.natCast_succ
items.doc: Casting a successor adds the multiplicative unit.
items.statement: theorem natCast_succ (n : ℕ) : natCast (n + 1) = natCast n + 1

items.name: BF64.npow_def
items.statement: theorem npow_def (a : BF64) (n : ℕ) : a ^ n = npowBinRec n a

items.note:
### The commutative-ring structure

Every law is discharged by pushing through the injective `toQuot` into `BF64Quot`,
where it holds because the quotient is a commutative ring. The instances are written out
field-by-field rather than via `Function.Injective.commRing`: that transport takes `toQuot`
as *data*, which would make the whole structure noncomputable and shadow the computable
operations. This mirrors `CompPoly.Extension.Ext.instCommRing`.

items.name: BF64.toQuot_neg
items.statement: theorem toQuot_neg (a : BF64) : toQuot (-a) = -toQuot a

items.name: BF64.toQuot_sub
items.statement: theorem toQuot_sub (a b : BF64) : toQuot (a - b) = toQuot a - toQuot b

items.name: BF64.npow_eq_npowRec
items.doc:
`npowBinRec` agrees with the linear `npowRec`, so the power can be reasoned about by
ordinary recursion on the exponent while still *evaluating* by binary exponentiation.
Mathlib's `npowBinRec_succ` needs a `Semigroup`, which is not available until `mul_assoc`
below, so associativity is supplied here from the quotient.
items.statement: theorem npow_eq_npowRec (a : BF64) (n : ℕ) : a ^ n = npowRec n a

items.name: BF64.toQuot_npow
items.statement: theorem toQuot_npow (a : BF64) (n : ℕ) : toQuot (a ^ n) = toQuot a ^ n

items.name: BF64.toQuot_natCast
items.statement: theorem toQuot_natCast (n : ℕ) : toQuot (n : BF64) = (n : BF64Quot)

items.note:
### Inversion by Itoh-Tsujii

Inversion uses the Itoh-Tsujii addition chain: `a⁻¹ = a^(2^64 - 2) = (a^(2^63 - 1))^2`,
with `a^(2^k - 1)` built along `1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 14, 15, 30, 31, 62, 63`. This is an
explicit algorithm rather than an existence proof, so the resulting inverse evaluates.
`BF128Ghash.inv_itoh_tsujii` is the analogous chain at degree 128.

items.name: BF64.powTwoPow
items.doc: Repeated squaring: `a ^ (2 ^ k)`.
items.statement: def powTwoPow (a : BF64) (k : ℕ) : BF64

items.name: BF64.toQuot_powTwoPow
items.statement:
theorem toQuot_powTwoPow (a : BF64) (k : ℕ) :
    toQuot (powTwoPow a k) = toQuot a ^ (2 ^ k)

items.name: BF64.invItohTsujii
items.doc: The multiplicative inverse, by the Itoh-Tsujii addition chain, with `0⁻¹ = 0`.
items.statement: def invItohTsujii (a : BF64) : BF64

items.name: BF64.toQuot_invItohTsujii
items.doc: The Itoh-Tsujii chain computes `a ^ (2 ^ 64 - 2)`.
items.statement:
theorem toQuot_invItohTsujii (a : BF64) (h : a ≠ 0) :
    toQuot (invItohTsujii a) = toQuot a ^ (2 ^ 64 - 2)

items.note:
### The field structure

`BF64Quot` is a field because `basePoly` is irreducible, and `toQuot` is an
injective ring homomorphism onto it, so the carrier is a field too. Following
`CompPoly.Extension.Ext.instField`, the structure is assembled field-by-field so that every
operation stays computable.

items.name: BF64.toQuot_eq_zero_iff
items.statement: theorem toQuot_eq_zero_iff {a : BF64} : toQuot a = 0 ↔ a = 0

items.name: BF64.exists_pair_ne
items.statement: theorem exists_pair_ne : ∃ x y : BF64, x ≠ y

items.name: BF64.equivFin
items.doc: The carrier is in bijection with `Fin (2 ^ 64)`, by its underlying representation.
items.statement: def equivFin : BF64 ≃ Fin (2 ^ 64)

items.name: BF64.nat_card_bf64
items.doc: `BF64` has `2 ^ 64` elements, independently of an enumeration.
items.statement: theorem nat_card_bf64 : Nat.card BF64 = 2 ^ 64

items.name: BF64.card_bf64
items.doc: Any enumeration of `BF64` has `2 ^ 64` elements.
items.statement: theorem card_bf64 [Fintype BF64] : Fintype.card BF64 = 2 ^ 64

items.name: BF64.toQuot_surjective
items.doc: The bridge is surjective: it is injective between finite types of equal cardinality.
items.statement: theorem toQuot_surjective : Function.Surjective toQuot

items.name: BF64.mul_invItohTsujii
items.doc: The Itoh-Tsujii inverse really is a multiplicative inverse.
items.statement: theorem mul_invItohTsujii {a : BF64} (h : a ≠ 0) : a * invItohTsujii a = 1

items.name: BF64.exists_mul_inv
items.doc: Every nonzero carrier value has a multiplicative inverse.
items.statement: theorem exists_mul_inv {a : BF64} (h : a ≠ 0) : ∃ b : BF64, a * b = 1

items.name: BF64.inv_def
items.doc: Inversion unfolds to the Itoh-Tsujii chain.
items.statement: theorem inv_def (a : BF64) : a⁻¹ = invItohTsujii a

items.name: BF64.div_def
items.doc: Division unfolds to multiplication by the Itoh-Tsujii inverse.
items.statement: theorem div_def (a b : BF64) : a / b = a * invItohTsujii b

items.name: BF64.inv_zero_bf64
items.statement: theorem inv_zero_bf64 : (0 : BF64)⁻¹ = 0

items.name: BF64.isField_bf64
items.doc: `BF64` satisfies `IsField`, the bundled-data-free form of the field axioms.
items.statement: theorem isField_bf64 : IsField BF64

modules.title: Reducing a carry-less product modulo the `GF(2^64)` modulus
modules.doc:
A product of two 64-bit values occupies 128 bits. Because `x^64 ≡ x^4 + x^3 + x + 1`
(`BF64.mul_pow_reduce`), the high half can be folded back down by a single carry-less
multiplication by `reductionConstant = 0x1B`. Each fold shrinks the excess, and two folds
land back inside 64 bits — no long division is needed.

This mirrors `CompPoly.Fields.Binary.BF128Ghash`'s reduction for the GHASH polynomial,
at the 64-bit width and with this modulus.

## Main definitions

* `highHalf`, `lowHalf` — the two 64-bit halves of a 128-bit value.
* `reductionConstant` — `0x1B`, the modulus below its leading term.
* `foldStep` — one reduction fold.
* `reduce` — two folds and a truncation.

## Main statements

* `toPoly_reductionConstant` — `0x1B` denotes `baseTail`.
* `foldStep_mod` — a fold preserves the residue modulo the modulus.
* `foldStep_lt` — a fold shrinks the value.
* `toPoly_reduce` — `reduce` computes the remainder modulo the modulus.

items.name: BF64.highHalf
items.doc: The high 64 bits of a 128-bit value.
items.statement: def highHalf (x : BitVec 128) : BitVec 64

items.name: BF64.lowHalf
items.doc: The low 64 bits of a 128-bit value.
items.statement: def lowHalf (x : BitVec 128) : BitVec 64

items.name: BF64.highHalf_testBit
items.doc: Bit `i` of the high half is bit `64 + i` of the whole.
items.statement:
theorem highHalf_testBit (x : BitVec 128) (i : ℕ) (h : i < 64) :
    (highHalf x).toNat.testBit i = x.toNat.testBit (64 + i)

items.name: BF64.lowHalf_testBit
items.doc: Bit `i` of the low half is bit `i` of the whole.
items.statement:
theorem lowHalf_testBit (x : BitVec 128) (i : ℕ) (h : i < 64) :
    (lowHalf x).toNat.testBit i = x.toNat.testBit i

items.name: BF64.toPoly_halves
items.doc: Splitting a 128-bit value into `high * x^64 + low`.
items.statement:
theorem toPoly_halves (x : BitVec 128) :
    toPoly x = toPoly (highHalf x) * X ^ 64 + toPoly (lowHalf x)

items.name: BF64.highHalf_lt
items.doc: If `x < 2 ^ (64 + d)` then its high half is below `2 ^ d`.
items.statement:
theorem highHalf_lt (x : BitVec 128) {d : ℕ} (hx : x.toNat < 2 ^ (64 + d)) :
    (highHalf x).toNat < 2 ^ d

items.name: BF64.lowHalf_lt
items.doc: The low half is always below `2 ^ 64`, being 64 bits wide.
items.statement: theorem lowHalf_lt (x : BitVec 128) : (lowHalf x).toNat < 2 ^ 64

items.name: BF64.carryLessMul_lt
items.doc: A carry-less product of values below `2 ^ p` and `2 ^ q` is below `2 ^ (p + q)`.

items.name: BF64.reductionConstant
items.doc:
The reduction constant `0x1B`: the modulus below its leading term,
`x^4 + x^3 + x + 1`.
items.statement: def reductionConstant : BitVec 64

items.name: BF64.toPoly_reductionConstant
items.doc:
**The reduction constant is the right one**: `0x1B` denotes `x^4 + x^3 + x + 1`.

A wrong constant here would compile and silently give a different field, so this ties the
bit pattern to the polynomial rather than leaving it to the reader.
items.statement: theorem toPoly_reductionConstant : toPoly reductionConstant = baseTail

items.name: BF64.reductionConstant_lt
items.doc: The reduction constant fits in five bits, which bounds how much a fold can grow.
items.statement: theorem reductionConstant_lt : reductionConstant.toNat < 2 ^ 5

items.name: BF64.foldStep
items.doc: One reduction fold: replace the high half's factor of `x^64` by `baseTail`.
items.statement: def foldStep (x : BitVec 128) : BitVec 128

items.name: BF64.foldStep_mod
items.doc: A fold preserves the residue modulo the modulus.
items.statement:
theorem foldStep_mod (x : BitVec 128) :
    toPoly (foldStep x) % basePoly = toPoly x % basePoly

items.name: BF64.foldStep_lt
items.doc: A fold of a value below `2 ^ (64 + d)` lands below `2 ^ (max 64 (d + 5))`.
items.statement:
theorem foldStep_lt (x : BitVec 128) {d : ℕ} (hx : x.toNat < 2 ^ (64 + d)) :
    (foldStep x).toNat < 2 ^ (max 64 (d + 5))

items.name: BF64.reduce
items.doc: Reduce a 128-bit carry-less product into the base field: two folds, then truncate.
items.statement: def reduce (x : BitVec 128) : BitVec 64

items.name: BF64.foldStep_foldStep_lt
items.doc: Two folds bring any 128-bit value below `2 ^ 64`.
items.statement: theorem foldStep_foldStep_lt (x : BitVec 128) : (foldStep (foldStep x)).toNat < 2 ^ 64

items.name: BF64.toPoly_lowHalf_of_lt
items.doc: Truncation is faithful on values already below `2 ^ 64`.
items.statement:
theorem toPoly_lowHalf_of_lt (x : BitVec 128) (h : x.toNat < 2 ^ 64) :
    toPoly (lowHalf x) = toPoly x

items.name: BF64.toPoly_reduce
items.doc: `reduce` computes the remainder of the denoted polynomial modulo the modulus.
items.statement:
theorem toPoly_reduce (x : BitVec 128) :
    toPoly (reduce x) = toPoly x % basePoly

modules.authors: Chung Thai Nguyen, Quang Dao, Derek Sorensen, Dimitris Mitsios
modules.title: Common Utilities for Binary Fields
modules.doc:
This file provides shared utilities for binary field implementations (fields of characteristic 2).
It includes:

1. **ZMod2Poly lemmas** — Properties of polynomials over GF(2)
2. **BitVec operations** — Carry-less multiplication, squaring
3. **BitVec ↔ Polynomial isomorphism** — `toPoly` and related lemmas

These utilities are used by both the tower construction (`Tower/`) and the
direct GF(2^128) implementation (`BF128Ghash/`). Import
`CompPoly.Fields.Binary.Common.Arithmetic` for word operations without polynomial support.

## Main Definitions

- `ZMod2Poly.add_self_cancel`: In char 2, `a + a = 0`
- `toPoly`: Convert a BitVec to a polynomial over GF(2)
- `clMul`: Carry-less multiplication of bit vectors
- `toPoly_xor`: `toPoly (a ^^^ b) = toPoly a + toPoly b`
- `toPoly_clMul`: `toPoly (clMul a b) = toPoly a * toPoly b`
- `toPoly_one_shiftLeft`: `toPoly (1 <<< n) = X^n`

items.name: ZMod2Poly.add_self_cancel
items.statement: lemma ZMod2Poly.add_self_cancel (a : Polynomial (ZMod 2)) : a + a = 0

items.name: ZMod2Poly.sub_eq_add
items.statement: lemma ZMod2Poly.sub_eq_add (a b : Polynomial (ZMod 2)) : a - b = a + b

items.name: ZMod2Poly.neg_eq_self
items.statement: lemma ZMod2Poly.neg_eq_self (a : Polynomial (ZMod 2)) : -a = a

items.name: ZMod2Poly.add_eq_sub
items.statement: lemma ZMod2Poly.add_eq_sub (a b : Polynomial (ZMod 2)) : a + b = a - b

items.name: ZMod2Poly.two_mul
items.statement: lemma ZMod2Poly.two_mul (a : Polynomial (ZMod 2)) : 2 * a = 0

items.name: ZMod2Poly.mul_two
items.statement: lemma ZMod2Poly.mul_two (a : Polynomial (ZMod 2)) : a * 2 = 0

items.name: ZMod2Poly.two_eq_zero
items.statement: lemma ZMod2Poly.two_eq_zero : (2 : Polynomial (ZMod 2)) = 0

items.name: ZMod2Poly.three_eq_one
items.statement: lemma ZMod2Poly.three_eq_one : (3 : Polynomial (ZMod 2)) = 1

items.name: ZMod2Poly.mul_three
items.statement: lemma ZMod2Poly.mul_three (a : Polynomial (ZMod 2)) : a * 3 = a

items.name: ZMod2Poly.natCast_ZMod2
items.statement: lemma ZMod2Poly.natCast_ZMod2 (n : ℕ) : (n : Polynomial (ZMod 2)) = ((n % 2) : ℕ)

items.name: ZMod2_value_eq_zero_or_one
items.statement: lemma ZMod2_value_eq_zero_or_one (x : ZMod 2) : x = 0 ∨ x = 1

items.name: eq_of_associated_ZMod2
items.doc:
Helper: In Polynomial (ZMod 2), the only unit is 1.
Therefore, if two polynomials are Associated (differ by a unit), they must be Equal.
items.statement: lemma eq_of_associated_ZMod2 {a b : Polynomial (ZMod 2)} (h : Associated a b) : a = b

items.name: ZMod2Poly.fintypeCard_eq_two
items.statement: lemma ZMod2Poly.fintypeCard_eq_two : Fintype.card (ZMod 2) = 2

items.name: ZMod2Poly.frobenius
items.statement: lemma ZMod2Poly.frobenius (a b : Polynomial (ZMod 2)) : (a + b) ^ 2 = a ^ 2 + b ^ 2

items.name: ZMod2Poly.euclidean_gcd_comm
items.doc:
**EuclideanDomain.gcd_comm for Polynomials**
Commutativity: EuclideanDomain.gcd(a, b) = EuclideanDomain.gcd(b, a)
Uses the fact that EuclideanDomain provides a GCDMonoid instance, which has gcd_comm'.
items.statement:
lemma ZMod2Poly.euclidean_gcd_comm (a b : Polynomial (ZMod 2)) :
    EuclideanDomain.gcd a b = EuclideanDomain.gcd b a

items.name: Polynomial.exists_factor_le_64_of_reducible
items.doc:
Helper Lemma:
If P is a degree 128 polynomial and is REDUCIBLE,
then it must have an irreducible factor q with degree ≤ 64.
items.statement:
lemma Polynomial.exists_factor_le_64_of_reducible.{u} {R : Type u} [Field R] (P : Polynomial R)
    (h_deg : P.natDegree = 128) (h_red : ¬ Irreducible P) :
    ∃ q, Irreducible q ∧ q ∣ P ∧ q.natDegree ≤ 64

items.name: BinaryField.BitVec.toNat_of_cast
items.statement:
lemma BitVec.toNat_of_cast {w w2 : ℕ} (x : BitVec w) (h_width_eq : w = w2) :
    BitVec.toNat ((cast (h := by rw [h_width_eq]) x) : BitVec w2) = BitVec.toNat x

items.name: BinaryField.toPoly
items.statement: noncomputable def toPoly {w : Nat} (v : BitVec w) : (ZMod 2)[X]

items.name: BinaryField.carryLessMul_unfold
items.doc:
Unfold `clMul` into an always-XOR form so that `toPoly_fold_xor`
applies directly in the proof of `toPoly_clMul`.
items.statement:
lemma carryLessMul_unfold {v w : ℕ} (a b : BitVec v) :
    carryLessMul (w := w) a b = Fin.foldl v
      (fun acc i => acc ^^^ (if a.getLsbD i
        then (zeroExtendTo b : BitVec w) <<< (i : Nat) else 0)) (0 : BitVec w)

items.name: BinaryField.clMul_unfold
items.statement:
lemma clMul_unfold (a b : B128) :
    clMul a b = Fin.foldl 128
      (fun acc i => acc ^^^ (if a.getLsbD i
        then to256 b <<< (i : Nat) else 0)) (0 : B256)

items.name: BinaryField.toPoly_one_shiftLeft
items.doc: A single set bit at position `n` denotes the monomial `X^n`.
items.statement:
lemma toPoly_one_shiftLeft {w : Nat} (n : Nat) (h : n < w) :
    toPoly (1 <<< n : BitVec w) = X^n

items.name: BinaryField.toPoly_one_eq_one
items.statement: lemma toPoly_one_eq_one {w : Nat} (h_w_pos : w > 0) : toPoly (BitVec.ofNat w 1) = 1

items.name: BinaryField.toPoly_zero_eq_zero
items.statement: lemma toPoly_zero_eq_zero {w : Nat} : toPoly (BitVec.ofNat w 0) = 0

items.name: BinaryField.toPoly_ne_zero_iff_ne_zero
items.statement:
lemma toPoly_ne_zero_iff_ne_zero {w : Nat} (v : BitVec w) :
    toPoly v ≠ 0 ↔ v ≠ 0

items.name: BinaryField.toPoly_degree_lt_w
items.doc: ToPoly degree is less than width
items.statement:
lemma toPoly_degree_lt_w {w : ℕ} (h_w_pos : w > 0) (v : BitVec w) :
    (toPoly v).degree < w

items.name: BinaryField.toPoly_degree_of_lt_two_pow
items.statement:
lemma toPoly_degree_of_lt_two_pow {w d : ℕ} (v : BitVec w)
    (hv : v.toNat < 2 ^ d) : (toPoly v).degree < d

items.name: BinaryField.BitVec_lt_two_pow_of_toPoly_degree_lt
items.statement:
lemma BitVec_lt_two_pow_of_toPoly_degree_lt {w d : ℕ} (v : BitVec w)
    (h_toPoly_degree_lt : (toPoly v).degree < d) : v.toNat < 2 ^ d

items.name: BinaryField.toPoly_xor
items.statement: lemma toPoly_xor {w} (a b : BitVec w) : toPoly (a ^^^ b) = toPoly a + toPoly b

items.name: BinaryField.toPoly_fold_xor
items.doc:
The "Homomorphism" Lemma.
Since toPoly(a ^^^ b) = toPoly a + toPoly b,
toPoly preserves the structure from Fold-XOR to Sum-Add.

lemma toPoly_fold_xor {α} {w} (s : Finset α) (f : α → (BitVec w)) :
    toPoly (s.fold BitVec.xor 0 f) = ∑ i ∈ s, toPoly (f i) := by
  induction s using Finset.cons_induction with
  | empty =>
    simp only [BitVec.ofNat_eq_ofNat, Finset.fold_empty, Finset.sum_empty]
    rw [toPoly_zero_eq_zero]
  | cons x s h_not_mem ih =>
    rw [Finset.fold_cons, Finset.sum_cons]
    change toPoly (f x ^^^ s.fold BitVec.xor 0 f) = toPoly (f x) + ∑ i ∈ s, toPoly (f i)
    rw [toPoly_xor]
    rw [ih]
items.statement:
lemma toPoly_fold_xor {w : Nat} (n : Nat) (f : Nat → (BitVec w)) :
    toPoly (Fin.foldl n (fun acc i => acc ^^^ (f i)) 0) =
    ∑ i ∈ (Finset.range n), toPoly (f i)

items.name: BinaryField.toPoly_128_extend_256
items.statement:
lemma toPoly_128_extend_256 (a : B128) :
    toPoly (to256 a) = toPoly a

items.name: BinaryField.BitVec_getLsb_eq_false_of_toNat_lt_two_pow
items.statement:
theorem BitVec_getLsb_eq_false_of_toNat_lt_two_pow {w d : ℕ} (a : BitVec w) (ha : a.toNat < 2 ^ d)
    (i : Fin w) (hd : d ≤ (i : ℕ)) : a.getLsb i = false

items.name: BinaryField.BitVec_getElem_eq_false_of_toNat_lt_two_pow
items.statement:
theorem BitVec_getElem_eq_false_of_toNat_lt_two_pow {w d : ℕ} (a : BitVec w) (ha : a.toNat < 2 ^ d)
    (n : ℕ) (hn : n < w) (hd : d ≤ n) : a[n] = false

items.name: BinaryField.BitVec_getLsb_shiftLeft
items.statement:
theorem BitVec_getLsb_shiftLeft {w : ℕ} (a : BitVec w) (shift n : ℕ) (hn : n < w) :
    (a <<< shift).getLsb ⟨n, hn⟩ =
      (if _ : shift ≤ n then
          a.getLsb ⟨n - shift, lt_of_le_of_lt (Nat.sub_le n shift) hn⟩
        else false)

items.name: BinaryField.toPoly_coeff
items.statement:
theorem toPoly_coeff {w : ℕ} (v : BitVec w) (n : ℕ) :
    (toPoly v).coeff n =
      (if h : n < w then (if v.getLsb ⟨n, h⟩ = true then (1 : ZMod 2) else 0) else 0)

items.name: BinaryField.toPoly_shiftLeft_no_overflow
items.statement:
theorem toPoly_shiftLeft_no_overflow {w d : ℕ} (a : BitVec w) (ha : a.toNat < 2 ^ d) {shift : ℕ}
    (h_no_overflow : d + shift ≤ w) : toPoly (a <<< shift) = (toPoly a) * X^shift

items.name: BinaryField.toPoly_zeroExtendTo
items.doc: Widening does not change the polynomial denoted.
items.statement:
lemma toPoly_zeroExtendTo {v w : ℕ} (a : BitVec v) (h : v ≤ w) :
    toPoly (zeroExtendTo (w := w) a) = toPoly a

items.name: BinaryField.toPoly_carryLessMul
items.doc:
`carryLessMul` denotes the product of the denoted polynomials, provided the result
width admits the full product.
items.statement:
lemma toPoly_carryLessMul {v w : ℕ} (a b : BitVec v) (h : v + v ≤ w) :
    toPoly (carryLessMul (w := w) a b) = toPoly a * toPoly b

items.name: BinaryField.toPoly_clMul
items.statement:
lemma toPoly_clMul (a b : B128) :
    toPoly (clMul a b) = toPoly a * toPoly b

items.name: BinaryField.toPoly_eq_range
items.doc: `toPoly` as a sum over the set bits, indexed by `ℕ`.
items.statement:
lemma toPoly_eq_range {w : ℕ} (v : BitVec w) :
    toPoly v = ∑ i ∈ Finset.range w, if v.toNat.testBit i then (X : (ZMod 2)[X]) ^ i else 0

items.name: BinaryField.toPoly_split
items.doc:
Splitting the denoted polynomial at bit position `n` into a high part carrying `X ^ n`
and a low part.
items.statement:
lemma toPoly_split {w : ℕ} (v : BitVec w) (n : ℕ) (hn : n ≤ w) :
    toPoly v
      = (∑ i ∈ Finset.range (w - n),
          if v.toNat.testBit (n + i) then (X : (ZMod 2)[X]) ^ i else 0) * X ^ n
        + ∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, if v.toNat.testBit i then (X : (ZMod 2)[X]) ^ i else 0

modules.title: Binary polynomial word arithmetic
modules.doc:
A word's bit `i` represents the coefficient of `X^i`. Changing word width
zero-extends or truncates the coefficient vector. Carry-less multiplication
accumulates shifted words using XOR and truncates at the chosen result width.
A width at least twice the operand width preserves the full polynomial product.
The 128-bit specialization returns a 256-bit product.

Polynomial interpretation and its correspondence proofs are available through
`CompPoly.Fields.Binary.Common`.

items.name: BinaryTower.BTField.RingHom_comp_cast
items.doc:
Cast of composition of BTField ring homomorphism is composition of casted BTField ring homomorphism.
Note that this assumes the SAME underlying instances (e.g. NonAssocSemiring)
for both the input and output ring homs.
items.statement:
theorem BTField.RingHom_comp_cast {α β γ δ : ℕ} (f : BTField α →+* BTField β)
    (g : BTField β →+* BTField γ) (h : γ = δ) :
    ((cast (BTField.RingHom_eq_of_dest_eq (k:=β) (m:=γ) (n:=δ) h) g).comp f)
    = cast (BTField.RingHom_eq_of_dest_eq (k:=α) (m:=γ) (n:=δ) h) (g.comp f)

items.name: BinaryTower.multilinearBasis
items.doc:
The multilinear basis for `BTField τ` over `BTField k` is the set of multilinear monomials
in the tower generators `Z(k+1), ..., Z(τ)`.
This is done via scalar tower multiplication of power basis across adjacent levels.

items.name: BinaryTower.BTField.PowerBasis.dim_of_eq_rec
items.statement:
theorem BTField.PowerBasis.dim_of_eq_rec
    (r1 r : ℕ)
    (h_r : r = r1 + 1)
    (b : PowerBasis (BTField r1) (BTField (r1 + 1))) :
    letI instAlgebra : Algebra (BTField r1) (BTField r) :=
      binaryAlgebraTower (l:=r1) (r:=r) (h_le:=by omega)
    ((Eq.rec (motive:=fun (x : ℕ) (_ : r1 + 1 = x) => by
      letI instAlgebraCur : Algebra (BTField r1) (BTField x) :=
        binaryAlgebraTower (l:=r1) (r:=x) (h_le:=by omega)
      exact PowerBasis (BTField r1) (BTField x)) (refl:=b) (t:=h_r.symm)) :
        PowerBasis (BTField r1) (BTField r)).dim
    = b.dim

items.name: BinaryTower.PowerBasis.cast_basis_succ_of_eq_rec_apply
items.statement:
theorem PowerBasis.cast_basis_succ_of_eq_rec_apply
    (r1 r : ℕ) (h_r : r = r1 + 1)
    (k : Fin 2) :
    letI instAlgebra : Algebra (BTField r1) (BTField r) :=
      binaryAlgebraTower (l:=r1) (r:=r) (h_le:=by omega)
    letI instAlgebraSucc : Algebra (BTField (r1 + 1)) (BTField (r)) :=
      binaryAlgebraTower (l:=r1 + 1) (r:=r) (h_le:=by omega)
    let b : PowerBasis (BTField r1) (BTField (r1 + 1)) := powerBasisSucc (k:=r1)
    let bCast : PowerBasis (BTField r1) (BTField r) := Eq.rec (motive:=
      fun (x : ℕ) (_ : r1 + 1 = x) => by
        letI instAlgebraCur : Algebra (BTField r1) (BTField x) :=
          binaryAlgebraTower (l:=r1) (r:=x) (h_le:=by omega)
        exact PowerBasis (BTField r1) (BTField x)) (refl:=b) (t:=h_r.symm)
    have h_pb_dim : b.dim = 2 := by
      exact powerBasisSucc_dim r1

    have h_pb'_dim : bCast.dim = 2 := by
      dsimp [bCast]
      erw [BTField.PowerBasis.dim_of_eq_rec (r1:=r1) (r:=r) (h_r:=h_r) (b:=b)]
      exact h_pb_dim

    have h_pb_type_eq : Basis (Fin bCast.dim) (BTField r1) (BTField r) =
      Basis (Fin 2) (BTField r1) (BTField r) := by
      congr

   -- The `cast` needs a proof that `bCast.dim = 2`. We construct it here.
    let left : Basis (Fin 2) (BTField r1) (BTField r) := cast (by exact h_pb_type_eq) bCast.basis
    let right := (algebraMap (BTField (r1 + 1)) (BTField r))
      (b.basis (Fin.cast h_pb_dim.symm k))
    left k = right

items.name: BinaryTower.algebraMap_𝕏_eq_of_index_eq
items.doc: When two indices are equal, the tower algebra maps send the respective 𝕏 to the same element.
items.statement:
lemma algebraMap_𝕏_eq_of_index_eq (r k m : ℕ) (h_k_le : k + 1 ≤ r) (h_m_le : m + 1 ≤ r)
    (h_eq : k = m) :
    letI := binaryAlgebraTower (l := k + 1) (r := r) (h_le := h_k_le)
    letI := binaryAlgebraTower (l := m + 1) (r := r) (h_le := h_m_le)
    (algebraMap _ _ (𝕏 k) : BTField r) = (algebraMap _ _ (𝕏 m) : BTField r)

items.note:
The basis element at index `j` is the product of the tower generators at
the ON bits in binary representation of `j`.

items.name: BinaryTower.multilinearBasis_apply
items.statement:
theorem multilinearBasis_apply (r : ℕ) : ∀ l : ℕ, (h_le : l ≤ r) → ∀ (j : Fin (2  ^ (r - l))),
    multilinearBasis (l:=l) (r:=r) (h_le:=h_le) j =
    (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin (r - l))).prod (fun i =>
      (binaryAlgebraTower (l:=l + i + 1) (r:=r) (h_le:=by omega)).algebraMap (
        (𝕏 (l + i)) ^ (Nat.getBit i j)))

structure BinaryTowerInductiveStepResult (k : ℕ) (prevBTField : Type _)
  (prevBTResult : BinaryTowerResult prevBTField k) [instPrevBTFieldIsField : Field prevBTField]
  (prevPoly : Polynomial prevBTField) (F : Type _) where
  binaryTowerResult : BinaryTowerResult F (k+1)
  eq_adjoin : F = AdjoinRoot prevPoly
  u_is_root : Eq.mp (eq_adjoin) binaryTowerResult.specialElement = AdjoinRoot.root prevPoly
  eval_defining_poly_at_root : Eq.mp (eq_adjoin) binaryTowerResult.specialElement^2 +

    + 1 = 0

    (Basis (Fin (i)) (BTField k) (BTField n)) = (Basis (Fin (j)) (BTField k) (BTField n))

items.name: BinaryTower.BTField.Basis_cast_dest_eq
BinaryTower.BTField.PowerBasis_cast_dest_eq

items.note:
The following two theorems are used to cast the basis of `BTField α` to `BTField β`
via changing in index type : `Fin (i)` to `Fin (j)` when `α ≤ β`.

items.name: BinaryTower.BTField.Basis_cast_index_apply
items.statement:
theorem BTField.Basis_cast_index_apply {α β i j : ℕ} {k : Fin j} (h_le : α ≤ β) (h_eq : i = j)
    {b : @Basis (Fin (i)) (BTField α) (BTField β) _ _
    (@binaryAlgebraTower (l := α) (r := β) (h_le := h_le)).toModule} :
  let castBasis : @Basis (Fin j) (BTField α) (BTField β) _ _
    (@binaryAlgebraTower (l:=α) (r:=β) (h_le:=h_le)).toModule :=
    cast (by exact BTField.Basis_cast_index_eq i j α β h_le h_eq) b
  (castBasis k) = b (Fin.cast (h_eq.symm) k)

items.name: BinaryTower.BTField.Basis_cast_dest_apply
items.statement:
theorem BTField.Basis_cast_dest_apply {ι : Type*} (α β γ : ℕ) (h_le1 : α ≤ β) (h_le2 : α ≤ γ)
    (h_eq : β = γ) {k : ι} (b : @Basis ι (BTField α) (BTField β) _ _
    (@binaryAlgebraTower (l := α) (r := β) (h_le := h_le1)).toModule) :
    let castBasis : @Basis ι (BTField α) (BTField γ) _ _
      (@binaryAlgebraTower (l := α) (r := γ) (h_le := h_le2)).toModule :=
      cast (by
        exact Basis_cast_dest_eq α γ β h_le2 h_le1 h_eq
      ) b
    (castBasis k) = cast (by exact BTField.cast_BTField_eq β γ h_eq) (b k)

items.note: The power basis for `BTField (k+1)` over `BTField k` is {1, Z (k+1)}

items.name: BinaryTower.powerBasisSucc
items.statement:
def powerBasisSucc (k : ℕ) :
    PowerBasis (BTField k) (BTField (k+1))

items.name: BinaryTower.powerBasisSucc_gen
items.statement:
lemma powerBasisSucc_gen (k : ℕ) :
    (powerBasisSucc k).gen = (Z (k+1))

items.name: BinaryTower.powerBasisSucc_dim
items.statement:
lemma powerBasisSucc_dim (k : ℕ) :
    powerBasisSucc (k:=k).dim = 2

items.name: BinaryTower.join_via_add_smul
items.statement:
def join_via_add_smul {k : ℕ} (h_pos : k > 0) (hi_btf lo_btf : BTField (k - 1)) :
    BTField k

items.name: BinaryTower.join_via_add_smul_zero
items.statement:
lemma join_via_add_smul_zero {k : ℕ} (h_pos : k > 0) :
    (⋘ 0, 0 ⋙ : BTField k) = 0

items.name: BinaryTower.join_via_add_smul_one_zero_eq_Z
items.statement:
lemma join_via_add_smul_one_zero_eq_Z {k : ℕ} (h_pos : k > 0) :
    ⋘ 1, 0 ⋙ = Z k

items.name: BinaryTower.join_via_add_smul_one
items.statement:
lemma join_via_add_smul_one {k : ℕ} (h_pos : k > 0) :
    (⋘ 0, 1 ⋙ : BTField k) = 1

items.name: BinaryTower.sum_join_via_add_smul
items.statement:
theorem sum_join_via_add_smul (k : ℕ) (h_pos : k > 0) (a₁ a₀ b₁ b₀ : BTField (k - 1)) :
    ⋘ a₁, a₀ ⋙ + ⋘ b₁, b₀ ⋙ = ⋘ a₁ + b₁, a₀ + b₀ ⋙

items.name: BinaryTower.mul_join_via_add_smul
items.doc:
(a₁ • Z k + a₀) * (b₁ • Z k + b₀)
= a₁ * b₁ • (Z k)^2 + (a₁ * b₀ + a₀ * b₁) • Z k + a₀ * b₀
= a₁ * b₁ • (Z (k-1) * Z k + 1) + (a₁ * b₀ + a₀ * b₁) • Z k + a₀ * b₀
= [a₁ * b₁ * Z (k - 1) + a₁ * b₀ + a₀ * b₁] * (Z k) + (a₀ * b₀ + a₁ * b₁)
items.statement:
theorem mul_join_via_add_smul (k : ℕ) (h_pos : k > 0) (a₁ a₀ b₁ b₀ : BTField (k - 1)) :
    ⋘ a₁, a₀ ⋙ * ⋘ b₁, b₀ ⋙ = ⋘ a₁ * b₁ * Z (k - 1) + a₁ * b₀ + a₀ * b₁, a₀ * b₀ + a₁ * b₁ ⋙

items.name: BinaryTower.unique_linear_decomposition_succ
items.statement:
theorem unique_linear_decomposition_succ (k : ℕ) :
    ∀ (x : BTField (k+1)), ∃! (p : BTField k × BTField k),
    x = ⋘ p.1, p.2 ⋙

items.name: BinaryTower.split
items.statement: def split (k : ℕ) (h_k : k > 0) (x : BTField k) : BTField (k-1) × BTField (k-1)

items.note: Proofs that `split` is the inverse of `join_via_add_smul`

items.name: BinaryTower.eq_join_via_add_smul_eq_iff_split
items.statement:
theorem eq_join_via_add_smul_eq_iff_split (k : ℕ) (h_pos : k > 0)
    (x : BTField k) (hi_btf lo_btf : BTField (k - 1)) :
    x = ⋘ hi_btf, lo_btf ⋙ ↔
  split (k:=k) (h_k:=h_pos) x = (hi_btf, lo_btf)

items.name: BinaryTower.split_join_via_add_smul_eq_iff_split
items.statement:
lemma split_join_via_add_smul_eq_iff_split (k : ℕ) (h_pos : k > 0)
    (hi_btf lo_btf : BTField (k - 1)) :
    split (k:=k) (h_k:=h_pos) (⋘ hi_btf, lo_btf ⋙) = (hi_btf, lo_btf)

items.name: BinaryTower.join_eq_join_iff
items.statement:
lemma join_eq_join_iff (k : ℕ) (h_pos : k > 0) (hi₁ hi₀ lo₁ lo₀ : BTField (k - 1)) :
    ⋘ hi₁, lo₁ ⋙ = ⋘ hi₀, lo₀ ⋙ ↔
  hi₁ = hi₀ ∧ lo₁ = lo₀

items.name: BinaryTower.split_algebraMap_eq_zero_x
items.doc:
An element `x` lifted from the base field `BTField (k-1)` has `(0, x)` as its
split representation in `BTField k`.
items.statement:
lemma split_algebraMap_eq_zero_x {k : ℕ} (h_pos : k > 0) (x : BTField (k - 1)) :
    letI instAlgebra := binaryAlgebraTower (l:=k-1) (r:=k) (h_le:=by omega)
  split (k:=k) (h_k:=h_pos) (algebraMap (BTField (k - 1)) (BTField k) x) = (0, x)

items.name: BinaryTower.algebraMap_succ_eq_zero_x
items.statement:
lemma algebraMap_succ_eq_zero_x {k : ℕ} (h_pos : k > 0) (x : BTField (k - 1)) :
    letI instAlgebra := binaryAlgebraTower (l:=k-1) (r:=k) (h_le:=by omega)
  algebraMap (BTField (k - 1)) (BTField k) x = ⋘ 0, x ⋙

items.name: BinaryTower.algebraMap_eq_zero_x
items.statement:
lemma algebraMap_eq_zero_x {i j : ℕ} (h_le : i < j) (x : BTField i) :
    letI instAlgebra := binaryAlgebraTower (l:=i) (r:=j) (h_le:=by omega)
    letI instAlgebraPred := binaryAlgebraTower (l:=i) (r:=j-1) (h_le:=by omega)
    algebraMap (BTField i) (BTField j) x
      = ⋘ 0, algebraMap (BTField i) (BTField (j-1)) x ⋙

items.name: BinaryTower.minPoly_of_powerBasisSucc_generator
items.statement:
theorem minPoly_of_powerBasisSucc_generator (k : ℕ) :
    (minpoly (BTField k) (powerBasisSucc k).gen) = X^2 + (Z k) • X + 1

modules.title: Serialization of the binary tower
modules.doc:
A level-`k` tower element `ConcreteBTField k` is its `2 ^ k` low-first tower-basis coordinates.
Its canonical natural is that bit pattern read as an integer and its encoding the little-endian
bytes of the pattern, `bytesFor (2 ^ 2 ^ k)` of them: one byte at level three, sixteen at level
seven. `FastBT128`, the two-limb level-seven carrier, agrees with `ConcreteBTField 7` through
`toConcrete` (`toList_toBytes_toConcrete`, `toByteArray_toConcrete`).

These are tower-basis coordinates. `AesField` at eight bits and `ConcreteBF128Ghash` at 128 bits
use different bases, and their encodings are not interchangeable with these.

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.ConcreteBTField.canonicalNat_bound
items.statement:
theorem canonicalNat_bound (k : ℕ) :
    CanonicalNat.bound (ConcreteBTField k) = 2 ^ 2 ^ k

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.ConcreteBTField.canonicalNat_toNat
items.statement:
theorem canonicalNat_toNat {k : ℕ} (x : ConcreteBTField k) :
    CanonicalNat.toNat x = x.toNat

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.ConcreteBTField.byteCodec_width
items.statement:
theorem byteCodec_width (k : ℕ) :
    ByteCodec.width (ConcreteBTField k) = Bytes.bytesFor (2 ^ 2 ^ k)

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.ConcreteBTField.byteCodec_width_eq
items.doc:
A level-`k` element takes `⌈2 ^ k / 8⌉` bytes: one byte at level three, sixteen at
level seven.
items.statement:
theorem byteCodec_width_eq (k : ℕ) :
    ByteCodec.width (ConcreteBTField k) = (2 ^ k + 7) / 8

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.ConcreteBTField.byteCodec_width_three
items.statement: theorem byteCodec_width_three : ByteCodec.width (ConcreteBTField 3) = 1

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.ConcreteBTField.byteCodec_width_seven
items.statement: theorem byteCodec_width_seven : ByteCodec.width (ConcreteBTField 7) = 16

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Fast.FastBT128.toBitVec
items.doc:
The two limbs read as a `2 ^ 7`-bit word, `lo` first. The width is written `2 ^ 7` so that
the carrier's codec has the same width term as `ConcreteBTField 7`.
items.statement: def toBitVec (v : FastBT128) : BitVec (2 ^ 7)

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Fast.FastBT128.ofBitVec
items.doc: Split a `2 ^ 7`-bit word into two limbs.
items.statement: def ofBitVec (b : BitVec (2 ^ 7)) : FastBT128

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Fast.FastBT128.toNat_lt
items.statement: theorem toNat_lt (v : FastBT128) : v.toNat < 2 ^ 2 ^ 7

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Fast.FastBT128.toNat_ofNat
items.statement: theorem toNat_ofNat (n : ℕ) : (ofNat n).toNat = n % 2 ^ 2 ^ 7

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Fast.FastBT128.ofNat_toNat
items.statement: theorem ofNat_toNat (v : FastBT128) : ofNat v.toNat = v

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Fast.FastBT128.ofBitVec_toBitVec
items.statement: theorem ofBitVec_toBitVec (v : FastBT128) : ofBitVec (toBitVec v) = v

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Fast.FastBT128.toBitVec_ofBitVec
items.statement: theorem toBitVec_ofBitVec (b : BitVec (2 ^ 7)) : toBitVec (ofBitVec b) = b

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Fast.FastBT128.canonicalNat_bound
items.statement: theorem canonicalNat_bound : CanonicalNat.bound FastBT128 = 2 ^ 2 ^ 7

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Fast.FastBT128.canonicalNat_toNat
items.statement: theorem canonicalNat_toNat (v : FastBT128) : CanonicalNat.toNat v = v.toNat

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Fast.FastBT128.byteCodec_width
items.statement: theorem byteCodec_width : ByteCodec.width FastBT128 = 16

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Fast.FastBT128.toList_toBytes_toConcrete
items.doc:
The fast carrier and the level-seven tower field encode the same element identically.

Stated on the byte lists: the two codecs' widths are both `bytesFor (2 ^ 2 ^ 7)`, but through
different instance paths, and a `Vector`-typed statement would ask the kernel to identify them
by evaluation, which sends it into `Nat.log2`'s well-founded recursion. Rewriting each width to
`16` through its own width lemma avoids that.
items.statement:
theorem toList_toBytes_toConcrete (v : FastBT128) :
    (ByteCodec.toBytes (toConcrete v)).toList = (ByteCodec.toBytes v).toList

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Fast.FastBT128.toByteArray_toConcrete
items.doc: The same agreement as a `ByteArray` equality, the form a transcript sees.
items.statement:
theorem toByteArray_toConcrete (v : FastBT128) :
    ByteCodec.toByteArray (toConcrete v) = ByteCodec.toByteArray v

modules.title: Concrete Binary Tower Algebra
modules.doc: Algebra maps and embeddings for the concrete bitvector binary tower.

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.canonicalAlgMap
items.statement: def canonicalAlgMap (k : ℕ)

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.toNat_canonicalAlgMap
items.doc: The embedding into the next level preserves the stored natural word.
items.statement:
theorem toNat_canonicalAlgMap (k : ℕ) (x : ConcreteBTField k) :
    (canonicalAlgMap k x).toNat = x.toNat

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.generator_is_not_lifted_to_succ
items.doc:
`Z(k+1)` is the adjoined root of `poly k` to `ConcreteBTField (k+1)`, so it is not
lifted to `ConcreteBTField (k+1)` by `canonicalAlgMap`
items.statement:
theorem generator_is_not_lifted_to_succ (k : ℕ) :
    ∀ x : ConcreteBTField k, canonicalAlgMap (k:=k) x ≠ Z (k + 1)

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.ConcreteBTField_add_eq
items.statement:
lemma ConcreteBTField_add_eq (k n m) :
    ConcreteBTField (k + n + m) = ConcreteBTField (k + (n + m))

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.ConcreteBTField.RingHom_eq_of_dest_eq
items.statement:
theorem ConcreteBTField.RingHom_eq_of_dest_eq (k m n : ℕ) (h_eq : m = n) :
    (ConcreteBTField k →+* ConcreteBTField m)
    = (ConcreteBTField k →+* ConcreteBTField n)

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.ConcreteBTField.RingHom_eq_of_source_eq
items.statement:
theorem ConcreteBTField.RingHom_eq_of_source_eq (k n m : ℕ) (h_eq : k = n) :
    (ConcreteBTField k →+* ConcreteBTField m)
    = (ConcreteBTField n →+* ConcreteBTField m)

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.ConcreteBTField.RingHom_cast_dest_apply
items.statement:
theorem ConcreteBTField.RingHom_cast_dest_apply (k m n : ℕ) (h_eq : m = n)
    (f : ConcreteBTField k →+* ConcreteBTField m) (x : ConcreteBTField k) :
    (cast (ConcreteBTField.RingHom_eq_of_dest_eq (k:=k) (m:=m) (n:=n) h_eq) f) x
    = cast (by apply cast_ConcreteBTField_eq (h_eq:=h_eq)) (f x)

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.ConcreteBTField.RingHom_cast_source_apply
items.statement:
theorem ConcreteBTField.RingHom_cast_source_apply (k n m : ℕ) (h_eq : k = n)
    (f : ConcreteBTField k →+* ConcreteBTField m) (x : ConcreteBTField n) :
    (cast (ConcreteBTField.RingHom_eq_of_source_eq (k:=k) (n:=n) (m:=m) h_eq) f) x
    = f (cast (by apply cast_ConcreteBTField_eq (h_eq:=h_eq.symm)) x)

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.concreteTowerAlgebraMap
items.doc:
Auxiliary definition for `concreteTowerAlgebraMap` using structural recursion.
This is easier to reason about in proofs than the `Nat.rec` version.
items.statement:
def concreteTowerAlgebraMap (l r : ℕ) (h_le : l ≤ r) :
    ConcreteBTField l →+* ConcreteBTField r

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.concreteTowerAlgebraMap_id
items.statement:
lemma concreteTowerAlgebraMap_id (k : ℕ) :
    concreteTowerAlgebraMap (h_le:=by omega) = RingHom.id (ConcreteBTField k)

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.concreteTowerAlgebraMap_succ_1
items.statement:
lemma concreteTowerAlgebraMap_succ_1 (k : ℕ) :
    concreteTowerAlgebraMap (l:=k) (r:=k + 1) (h_le:=by omega) = canonicalAlgMap k

items.note: Right associativity of the Tower Map

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.concreteTowerAlgebraMap_succ
items.statement:
lemma concreteTowerAlgebraMap_succ (l r : ℕ) (h_le : l ≤ r) :
    concreteTowerAlgebraMap (l:=l) (r:=r + 1) (h_le:=by omega) =
  (concreteTowerAlgebraMap (l:=r) (r:=r + 1) (h_le:=by omega)).comp
  (concreteTowerAlgebraMap (l:=l) (r:=r) (h_le:=by omega))

items.note: Left associativity of the Tower Map

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.concreteTowerAlgebraMap_succ_last
items.statement:
theorem concreteTowerAlgebraMap_succ_last (r : ℕ) : ∀ l : ℕ, (h_le : l ≤ r) →
    concreteTowerAlgebraMap (l:=l) (r:=r + 1) (h_le:=by
    exact Nat.le_trans (n:=l) (m:=r) (k:=r + 1) (h_le) (by omega)) =
  (concreteTowerAlgebraMap (l:=l + 1) (r:=r + 1) (by omega)).comp (concreteTowerAlgebraMap
    (l:=l) (r:=l + 1) (by omega))

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.ConcreteBTField.RingHom_comp_cast
items.doc:
Cast of composition of ConcreteBTField ring homomorphism is composition of
casted ConcreteBTField ring homomorphism.
Note that this assumes the SAME underlying instances (e.g. NonAssocSemiring)
for both the input and output ring homs.
items.statement:
theorem ConcreteBTField.RingHom_comp_cast {α β γ δ : ℕ}
    (f : ConcreteBTField α →+* ConcreteBTField β)
    (g : ConcreteBTField β →+* ConcreteBTField γ) (h : γ = δ) :
    ((cast (ConcreteBTField.RingHom_eq_of_dest_eq (k:=β) (m:=γ) (n:=δ) h) g).comp f)
    = cast (ConcreteBTField.RingHom_eq_of_dest_eq (k:=α) (m:=γ) (n:=δ) h) (g.comp f)

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.concreteTowerAlgebraMap_assoc
items.statement:
theorem concreteTowerAlgebraMap_assoc :
    ∀ r mid l : ℕ, (h_l_le_mid : l ≤ mid) → (h_mid_le_r : mid ≤ r) →
    concreteTowerAlgebraMap (l:=l) (r:=r) (h_le:=by exact Nat.le_trans h_l_le_mid h_mid_le_r) =
    (concreteTowerAlgebraMap (l:=mid) (r:=r) (h_le:=h_mid_le_r)).comp
    (concreteTowerAlgebraMap (l:=l) (r:=mid) (h_le:=h_l_le_mid))

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.toNat_concreteTowerAlgebraMap
items.doc: An embedding between any ordered levels preserves the stored natural word.
items.statement:
theorem toNat_concreteTowerAlgebraMap {i j : ℕ} (h : i ≤ j) (x : ConcreteBTField i) :
    (concreteTowerAlgebraMap i j h x).toNat = x.toNat

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.concreteTowerAlgebraMap_eq_setWidth
items.doc: An embedding between ordered levels zero-extends the original bitvector.
items.statement:
theorem concreteTowerAlgebraMap_eq_setWidth {i j : ℕ} (h : i ≤ j)
    (x : ConcreteBTField i) :
    (concreteTowerAlgebraMap i j h x).toBitVec = x.toBitVec.setWidth (2 ^ j)

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.concreteTowerAlgebraMap_Z_succ
items.doc: The image of the level-`k + 1` generator keeps its set bit at position `2 ^ k`.
items.statement:
theorem concreteTowerAlgebraMap_Z_succ {k j : ℕ} (h : k + 1 ≤ j) :
    (concreteTowerAlgebraMap (k + 1) j h (Z (k + 1))).toBitVec =
      BitVec.ofNat (2 ^ j) (2 ^ (2 ^ k))

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.instAlgebraTowerConcreteBTF
items.doc:
**Formalization of Cross - Level Algebra** : For any `k ≤ τ`, `ConcreteBTField τ` is an
algebra over `ConcreteBTField k`.
items.statement: instance instAlgebraTowerConcreteBTF : AlgebraTower (ConcreteBTField)

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.ConcreteBTFieldAlgebra
items.statement:
abbrev ConcreteBTFieldAlgebra {l r : ℕ} (h_le : l ≤ r) :
    Algebra (ConcreteBTField l) (ConcreteBTField r)

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.join_via_add_smul
items.statement:
def join_via_add_smul (k : ℕ) (h_pos : k > 0) (hi_btf lo_btf : ConcreteBTField (k - 1)) :
    ConcreteBTField k

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.split_algebraMap_eq_zero_x
items.doc:
An element `x` lifted from the base field `ConcreteBTField (k-1)` has `(0, x)` as its
split representation in `ConcreteBTField k`.
items.statement:
lemma split_algebraMap_eq_zero_x {k : ℕ} (h_pos : k > 0) (x : ConcreteBTField (k - 1)) :
    letI instAlgebra := ConcreteBTFieldAlgebra (l:=k-1) (r:=k) (h_le:=by omega)
  split h_pos (algebraMap (ConcreteBTField (k - 1)) (ConcreteBTField k) x) = (0, x)

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.algebraMap_succ_eq_zero_x
items.statement:
lemma algebraMap_succ_eq_zero_x {k : ℕ} (h_pos : k > 0) (x : ConcreteBTField (k - 1)) :
    letI instAlgebra := ConcreteBTFieldAlgebra (l:=k-1) (r:=k) (h_le:=by omega)
  algebraMap (ConcreteBTField (k - 1)) (ConcreteBTField k) x = 《 0, x 》

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.algebraMap_eq_zero_x
items.statement:
lemma algebraMap_eq_zero_x {i j : ℕ} (h_le : i < j) (x : ConcreteBTField i) :
    letI instAlgebra := ConcreteBTFieldAlgebra (l:=i) (r:=j) (h_le:=by omega)
    letI instAlgebraPred := ConcreteBTFieldAlgebra (l:=i) (r:=j-1) (h_le:=by omega)
    algebraMap (ConcreteBTField i) (ConcreteBTField j) x
      = 《 0, algebraMap (ConcreteBTField i) (ConcreteBTField (j-1)) x 》

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.split_smul_Z_eq_zero_x
items.statement:
lemma split_smul_Z_eq_zero_x {k : ℕ} (h_pos : k > 0) (x : ConcreteBTField (k - 1)) :
    letI instAlgebra := ConcreteBTFieldAlgebra (l:=k-1) (r:=k) (h_le:=by omega)
  split h_pos (x • Z k) = (x, 0)

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.smul_Z_eq_zero_x
items.statement:
lemma smul_Z_eq_zero_x {k : ℕ} (h_pos : k > 0) (x : ConcreteBTField (k - 1)) :
    letI instAlgebra := ConcreteBTFieldAlgebra (l:=k-1) (r:=k) (h_le:=by omega)
  x • Z k = 《 x, 0 》

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.join_eq_join_via_add_smul
items.statement:
theorem join_eq_join_via_add_smul {k : ℕ} (h_pos : k > 0)
    (hi_btf lo_btf : ConcreteBTField (k - 1)) :
    《 hi_btf, lo_btf 》 = join_via_add_smul k h_pos hi_btf lo_btf

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.split_join_via_add_smul_eq_iff_split
items.statement:
lemma split_join_via_add_smul_eq_iff_split {k : ℕ} (h_pos : k > 0)
    (hi_btf lo_btf : ConcreteBTField (k - 1)) :
    split (k:=k) (h:=by omega) (x:=join_via_add_smul (k:=k) (h_pos:=h_pos) hi_btf lo_btf) =
      (hi_btf, lo_btf)

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.ConcreteBTFieldAlgebra_def
ConcreteBinaryTower.algebraMap_ConcreteBTFieldAlgebra_def
items.statement:
lemma algebraMap_ConcreteBTFieldAlgebra_def (l r : ℕ) (h_le : l ≤ r) :
    (@ConcreteBTFieldAlgebra (l:=l) (r:=r) (h_le:=h_le)).algebraMap
    = concreteTowerAlgebraMap l r h_le

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.coe_one_succ
items.statement:
lemma coe_one_succ (l : ℕ) :
    (@ConcreteBTFieldAlgebra (l:=l) (r:=l + 1) (h_le:=by omega)).algebraMap

modules.title: Concrete binary tower arithmetic
modules.doc:
A nominal carrier with low-first bitvector coordinates, explicit word encoding, and executable
recursive multiplication, inversion, and powers. Elementary laws and the additive group are
available without the recursive field certificates.
`CompPoly.Fields.Binary.Tower.Concrete.Core` re-exports this interface and supplies law records
and instance assembly; `CompPoly.Fields.Binary.Tower.Concrete.Field` constructs the field.

At positive level `k`, the arithmetic adjoins a generator `z` satisfying
`z² = Z (k - 1) * z + 1` over the previous level, with `Z 0 = 1`.
An element `lo + hi * z` stores `lo` in the low half and `hi` in the high half of its word;
`split` returns `(hi, lo)`. This is the quadratic tower of [DP23], §2.3, where the paper's
`X (k - 1)` corresponds to `Z k`.

## References

* [Diamond, B. E. and Posen, J., *Succinct arguments over towers of binary fields*][DP23]

      = BitVec.extractLsb (hi:=hi2) (lo:=lo2) (x)

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.BitVec.extractLsb_concat_hi
items.statement:
theorem BitVec.extractLsb_concat_hi {hi_size lo_size : ℕ} (hi : BitVec hi_size)
    (lo : BitVec lo_size) (h_hi : hi_size > 0) :
  BitVec.extractLsb (hi:=hi_size + lo_size - 1) (lo:=lo_size)
  (BitVec.append (msbs:=hi) (lsbs:=lo)) = dcast (by
    rw [←Nat.sub_add_comm (by omega), Nat.sub_add_cancel (by omega), Nat.add_sub_cancel]
  ) hi

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.BitVec.extractLsb_concat_lo

  (BitVec.append (msbs:=hi) (lsbs:=lo)) = dcast (by
    rw [←Nat.sub_add_comm (h:=by omega), Nat.sub_add_cancel (h:=by omega), Nat.sub_zero]
  ) lo

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.BitVec.eq_append_iff_extract
items.statement:
theorem BitVec.eq_append_iff_extract {lo_size hi_size : ℕ} (lo : BitVec lo_size)
    (hi : BitVec hi_size) (h_hi_gt_0 : hi_size > 0) (h_lo_gt_0 : lo_size > 0)
  (x : BitVec (hi_size + lo_size)) : x = dcast (by rfl) (BitVec.append (msbs:=hi) (lsbs:=lo)) ↔
  hi = dcast (by omega) (BitVec.extractLsb (hi:=hi_size + lo_size - 1) (lo:=lo_size) x) ∧
  lo = dcast (by omega) (BitVec.extractLsb (hi:=lo_size - 1) (lo:=0) x)

    (hi_btf lo_btf : ConcreteBTField (k - 1)) :
  split h_pos x = (hi_btf, lo_btf) ↔
  (hi_btf = fromNat (k:=k - 1) (x.toNat >>> 2 ^ (k - 1)) ∧
  lo_btf = fromNat (k:=k - 1) (x.toNat &&& (2 ^ (2 ^ (k - 1)) - 1)))

    (hi lo : ConcreteBTField (k - 1)) :
    x = join (k := k) h_pos hi lo ↔
      dcast (h_sum_two_same_pow2 (k := k) h_pos).symm x.toBitVec =
        hi.toBitVec ++ lo.toBitVec

items.statement:
theorem join_eq_iff_dcast_extractLsb {k : ℕ} (h_pos : k > 0) (x : ConcreteBTField k)
    (hi_btf lo_btf : ConcreteBTField (k - 1)) :
    x = 《 hi_btf, lo_btf 》 ↔
      (hi_btf.toBitVec = dcast (h_sub_middle h_pos)
        (BitVec.extractLsb (hi := 2 ^ k - 1) (lo := 2 ^ (k - 1)) x.toBitVec) ∧
      lo_btf.toBitVec = dcast h_middle_sub
        (BitVec.extractLsb (hi := 2 ^ (k - 1) - 1) (lo := 0) x.toBitVec))

modules.doc: Basis constructions for the concrete bitvector binary tower.

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Basis_cast_index_eq
items.statement:
theorem Basis_cast_index_eq (i j k n : ℕ) (h_le : k ≤ n) (h_eq : i = j) :
    letI instAlgebra : Algebra (ConcreteBTField k) (ConcreteBTField n) :=
      ConcreteBTFieldAlgebra (l:=k) (r:=n) (h_le:=h_le)
    letI : Module (ConcreteBTField k) (ConcreteBTField n) := instAlgebra.toModule
    (Basis (Fin (i)) (ConcreteBTField k) (ConcreteBTField n)) =
    (Basis (Fin (j)) (ConcreteBTField k) (ConcreteBTField n))

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Basis_cast_dest_eq
ConcreteBinaryTower.PowerBasis_cast_dest_eq

items.note:
The following two theorems are used to cast the basis of `ConcreteBTField α`
to `ConcreteBTField β` via changing in index type : `Fin (i)` to `Fin (j)` when `α ≤ β`.

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Basis_cast_index_apply
items.statement:
theorem Basis_cast_index_apply {α β i j : ℕ} {k : Fin j}
    (h_le : α ≤ β) (h_eq : i = j)
    {b : @Basis (Fin (i)) (ConcreteBTField α) (ConcreteBTField β) _ _
      (@ConcreteBTFieldAlgebra (l := α) (r := β) (h_le := h_le)).toModule} :
  let castBasis : @Basis (Fin j) (ConcreteBTField α) (ConcreteBTField β) _ _
    (@ConcreteBTFieldAlgebra (l:=α) (r:=β) (h_le:=h_le)).toModule :=
    cast (by exact Basis_cast_index_eq i j α β h_le h_eq) b
  (castBasis k) = b (Fin.cast (h_eq.symm) k)

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Basis_cast_dest_apply
items.statement:
theorem Basis_cast_dest_apply {ι : Type*} (α β γ : ℕ)
    (h_le1 : α ≤ β) (h_le2 : α ≤ γ)
    (h_eq : β = γ) {k : ι} (b : @Basis ι (ConcreteBTField α) (ConcreteBTField β) _ _
    (@ConcreteBTFieldAlgebra (l := α) (r := β) (h_le := h_le1)).toModule) :
    let castBasis : @Basis ι (ConcreteBTField α) (ConcreteBTField γ) _ _
      (@ConcreteBTFieldAlgebra (l := α) (r := γ) (h_le := h_le2)).toModule :=
      cast (by
        exact Basis_cast_dest_eq α γ β h_le2 h_le1 h_eq
      ) b
    (castBasis k) = cast (by
      exact cast_ConcreteBTField_eq β γ h_eq) (b k)

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.multilinearBasis
items.doc:
The multilinear basis for `ConcreteBTField τ` over `ConcreteBTField k`
is the set of multilinear monomials in the tower generators `Z(k + 1), ..., Z(τ)`.
This is done via scalar tower multiplication of power basis across adjacent levels.

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.PowerBasis.dim_of_eq_rec
items.statement:
theorem PowerBasis.dim_of_eq_rec
    (r1 r : ℕ)
    (h_r : r = r1 + 1)
    (b : PowerBasis (ConcreteBTField r1) (ConcreteBTField (r1 + 1))) :
    letI instAlgebra : Algebra (ConcreteBTField r1) (ConcreteBTField r) :=
      ConcreteBTFieldAlgebra (l:=r1) (r:=r) (h_le:=by omega)
    ((Eq.rec (motive:=fun (x : ℕ) (_ : r1 + 1 = x) => by
      letI instAlgebraCur : Algebra (ConcreteBTField r1) (ConcreteBTField x) :=
        ConcreteBTFieldAlgebra (l:=r1) (r:=x) (h_le:=by omega)
      exact PowerBasis (ConcreteBTField r1) (ConcreteBTField x)) (refl:=b) (t:=h_r.symm)) :
        PowerBasis (ConcreteBTField r1) (ConcreteBTField r)).dim
    = b.dim

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.PowerBasis.cast_basis_succ_of_eq_rec_apply
items.statement:
theorem PowerBasis.cast_basis_succ_of_eq_rec_apply
    (r1 r : ℕ) (h_r : r = r1 + 1)
    (k : Fin 2) :
    letI instAlgebra : Algebra (ConcreteBTField r1) (ConcreteBTField r) :=
      ConcreteBTFieldAlgebra (l:=r1) (r:=r) (h_le:=by omega)
    letI instAlgebraSucc : Algebra (ConcreteBTField (r1 + 1)) (ConcreteBTField (r)) :=
      ConcreteBTFieldAlgebra (l:=r1 + 1) (r:=r) (h_le:=by omega)
    let b : PowerBasis (ConcreteBTField r1) (ConcreteBTField (r1 + 1)) :=
      powerBasisSucc (k:=r1)
    let bCast : PowerBasis (ConcreteBTField r1) (ConcreteBTField r) := Eq.rec (motive:=
      fun (x : ℕ) (_ : r1 + 1 = x) => by
        letI instAlgebraCur : Algebra (ConcreteBTField r1) (ConcreteBTField x) :=
          ConcreteBTFieldAlgebra (l:=r1) (r:=x) (h_le:=by omega)
        exact PowerBasis (ConcreteBTField r1) (ConcreteBTField x)) (refl:=b) (t:=h_r.symm)
    have h_pb_dim : b.dim = 2 := by
      exact powerBasisSucc_dim r1

    have h_pb'_dim : bCast.dim = 2 := by
      dsimp [bCast]
      rw [PowerBasis.dim_of_eq_rec (r1:=r1) (r:=r) (h_r:=h_r) (b:=b)]
      exact h_pb_dim

    have h_pb_type_eq : Basis (Fin bCast.dim) (ConcreteBTField r1) (ConcreteBTField r) =
      Basis (Fin 2) (ConcreteBTField r1) (ConcreteBTField r) := by
      congr

   -- The `cast` needs a proof that `bCast.dim = 2`. We construct it here.
    let left : Basis (Fin 2) (ConcreteBTField r1) (ConcreteBTField r) :=
      cast (by exact h_pb_type_eq) bCast.basis
    let right := (algebraMap (ConcreteBTField (r1 + 1)) (ConcreteBTField r))
      (b.basis (Fin.cast h_pb_dim.symm k))
    left k = right

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.algebraMap_𝕏_eq_of_index_eq
items.doc: When two indices are equal, the tower algebra maps send the respective 𝕏 to the same element.
items.statement:
lemma algebraMap_𝕏_eq_of_index_eq (r k m : ℕ) (h_k_le : k + 1 ≤ r) (h_m_le : m + 1 ≤ r)
    (h_eq : k = m) :
    letI := ConcreteBTFieldAlgebra (l := k + 1) (r := r) (h_le := h_k_le)
    letI := ConcreteBTFieldAlgebra (l := m + 1) (r := r) (h_le := h_m_le)
    (algebraMap _ _ (𝕏 k) : ConcreteBTField r) =
      (algebraMap _ _ (𝕏 m) : ConcreteBTField r)

items.note:
The basis element at index `j` is the product of the tower generators at
the ON bits in binary representation of `j`.

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.multilinearBasis_apply
items.statement:
theorem multilinearBasis_apply (r : ℕ) : ∀ l : ℕ, (h_le : l ≤ r) → ∀ (j : Fin (2 ^ (r - l))),
    multilinearBasis (l:=l) (r:=r) (h_le:=h_le) j =
    (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin (r - l))).prod (fun i =>
      (ConcreteBTFieldAlgebra (l:=l + i + 1) (r:=r) (h_le:=by omega)).algebraMap (
        (𝕏 (l + i)) ^ (Nat.getBit i j)))

modules.title: Existing multilinear basis and concrete coordinates
modules.doc:
The representation of `ConcreteBinaryTower.multilinearBasis` agrees at each numeric index
with `ConcreteBinaryTower.Coordinates.coordinates`. Consequently, packing a unit coefficient
vector computes the existing basis vector, and packing arbitrary coefficients is their linear
combination under the concrete tower embedding.

The proof compares the existing basis's generator-product formula with the successor-vector
law in `AlgebraTower.natBasisVector_succ`. Both use low-first coordinate order: earlier tower
generators correspond to lower index bits. An auxiliary basis constructed with
`Module.Basis.ofEquivFun` is private to the identification proof.

The generator-product basis and its ordering are those of [DP23], §2.3, with the
paper's generator `X_k` represented by `Z (k + 1)`.

## References

* [Diamond, B. E. and Posen, J., *Succinct arguments over towers of binary fields*][DP23]

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Coordinates.multilinearBasis_repr
items.doc:
The coefficient at numeric index `q` in the multilinear basis is the executable coordinate
at the same index, for the scalar action induced by the concrete tower embedding.
items.statement:
theorem multilinearBasis_repr {i j : ℕ} (h : i ≤ j) (x : ConcreteBTField j)
    (q : Fin (2 ^ (j - i))) :
    let := ConcreteBTFieldAlgebra h
    (multilinearBasis i j h).repr x q = coordinates h x q

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Coordinates.coordinates_multilinearBasis
items.doc:
The multilinear basis vector at numeric index `q` has coordinate one at `q`
and coordinate zero at every other index.
items.statement:
theorem coordinates_multilinearBasis {i j : ℕ} (h : i ≤ j)
    (q : Fin (2 ^ (j - i))) :
    coordinates h (multilinearBasis i j h q) = Pi.single q 1

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Coordinates.pack_single_eq_multilinearBasis
items.doc:
Packing a unit coefficient vector computes the multilinear basis vector at the same
numeric index.
items.statement:
theorem pack_single_eq_multilinearBasis {i j : ℕ} (h : i ≤ j)
    (q : Fin (2 ^ (j - i))) :
    pack h (Pi.single q 1) = multilinearBasis i j h q

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Coordinates.pack_eq_sum_multilinearBasis
items.doc:
Packing is the sum of the multilinear basis vectors multiplied by their
coefficients embedded from level `i` into level `j` through the concrete tower map.
items.statement:
theorem pack_eq_sum_multilinearBasis {i j : ℕ} (h : i ≤ j)
    (c : Fin (2 ^ (j - i)) → ConcreteBTField i) :
    pack h c = ∑ q, concreteTowerAlgebraMap i j h (c q) * multilinearBasis i j h q

modules.title: Quadratic arithmetic in concrete successor coordinates
modules.doc:
At level `k + 1`, write an element as `lo + hi * Z (k + 1)` using the chosen embedding
from level `k`. The relation
`Z (k + 1) ^ 2 = 1 + canonicalAlgMap k (Z k) * Z (k + 1)` gives multiplication,
conjugation and norm formulas over the predecessor field. The inverse formula is total,
including zero, and describes the canonical concrete inverse with its existing fast paths.

These are concrete coordinate contracts for the tower described in [DP23], §2.3.
They use the existing predecessor-field proofs without importing the abstract tower bridge.

## References

* [Diamond, B. E. and Posen, J., *Succinct arguments over towers of binary fields*][DP23]

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Coordinates.joinSucc_mul_joinSucc
items.doc:
Multiplication in constant-first successor coordinates follows the quadratic relation
with linear coefficient `Z k` and constant coefficient one.
items.statement:
theorem joinSucc_mul_joinSucc (k : ℕ) (a₀ a₁ b₀ b₁ : ConcreteBTField k) :
    joinSucc k a₀ a₁ * joinSucc k b₀ b₁ =
      joinSucc k (a₀ * b₀ + a₁ * b₁)
        (a₀ * b₁ + b₀ * a₁ + (a₁ * b₁) * Z k)

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Coordinates.low_mul
items.doc: The constant coefficient of a product is the sum of the two diagonal products.
items.statement:
theorem low_mul (k : ℕ) (x y : ConcreteBTField (k + 1)) :
    low k (x * y) = low k x * low k y + high k x * high k y

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Coordinates.high_mul
items.doc: The generator coefficient of a product includes the quadratic linear-coefficient term.
items.statement:
theorem high_mul (k : ℕ) (x y : ConcreteBTField (k + 1)) :
    high k (x * y) = low k x * high k y + low k y * high k x +
      (high k x * high k y) * Z k

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Coordinates.conjugate
items.doc: Quadratic conjugation replaces the generator by itself plus the embedded `Z k`.
items.statement: def conjugate (k : ℕ) (x : ConcreteBTField (k + 1)) : ConcreteBTField (k + 1)

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Coordinates.norm
items.doc: The predecessor-field norm in low/high coordinates.
items.statement: def norm (k : ℕ) (x : ConcreteBTField (k + 1)) : ConcreteBTField k

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Coordinates.conjugate_eq_joinSucc
items.doc: The conjugate keeps the high coefficient and adds `high * Z k` to the low coefficient.
items.statement:
theorem conjugate_eq_joinSucc (k : ℕ) (x : ConcreteBTField (k + 1)) :
    conjugate k x = joinSucc k (low k x + high k x * Z k) (high k x)

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Coordinates.norm_eq
items.doc: The norm is `lo * (lo + hi * Z k) + hi * hi` in the predecessor field.
items.statement:
theorem norm_eq (k : ℕ) (x : ConcreteBTField (k + 1)) :
    norm k x = low k x * (low k x + high k x * Z k) + high k x * high k x

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Coordinates.mul_conjugate
items.doc: Multiplication by the quadratic conjugate is the embedded predecessor-field norm.
items.statement:
theorem mul_conjugate (k : ℕ) (x : ConcreteBTField (k + 1)) :
    x * conjugate k x = canonicalAlgMap k (norm k x)

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Coordinates.conjugate_conjugate
items.doc: Conjugating twice recovers the original successor-field element.
items.statement:
theorem conjugate_conjugate (k : ℕ) (x : ConcreteBTField (k + 1)) :
    conjugate k (conjugate k x) = x

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Coordinates.norm_ne_zero
items.doc: A nonzero successor-field element has nonzero predecessor-field norm.
items.statement:
theorem norm_ne_zero (k : ℕ) (x : ConcreteBTField (k + 1)) (hx : x ≠ 0) :
    norm k x ≠ 0

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Coordinates.inv_eq_joinSucc
items.doc: The canonical inverse has conjugate coordinates divided by the norm, including at zero.
items.statement:
theorem inv_eq_joinSucc (k : ℕ) (x : ConcreteBTField (k + 1)) :
    x⁻¹ = joinSucc k ((norm k x)⁻¹ * (low k x + high k x * Z k))
      ((norm k x)⁻¹ * high k x)

modules.title: Successor coordinates for concrete binary tower fields
modules.doc:
`ConcreteBinaryTower.Coordinates.succCoordinates k` identifies level `k + 1` with two
coefficients in level `k`, ordered as the constant coefficient followed by the coefficient
of the new generator `Z (k + 1)`. Its scalar action is induced by the existing tower map
from level `k` to level `k + 1`.

The underlying `split` and `join` functions use high/low order. The executable `low`, `high`,
and `joinSucc` adapters expose low/high order and their bodies for direct word reduction.
The linear equivalence is characterized by its application and inverse-application lemmas.
The decomposition and linearity proofs use the existing algebraic expansion lemmas in
`CompPoly.Fields.Binary.Tower.Concrete.Algebra`.

These successor equivalences can be passed to `AlgebraTower.natCoordinatesOfLE` from
`CompPoly.Data.RingTheory.AlgebraTower.Coordinates` to obtain coordinates between any ordered
pair of levels.

The tower and constant-first successor expansion are described in [DP23], §2.3.
The paper's generator `X_k` corresponds to `Z (k + 1)` here.

## References

* [Diamond, B. E. and Posen, J., *Succinct arguments over towers of binary fields*][DP23]

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Coordinates.low
items.doc: The constant coefficient of a level-`k + 1` word, stored in its low `2 ^ k` bits.
items.statement: def low (k : ℕ) (x : ConcreteBTField (k + 1)) : ConcreteBTField k

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Coordinates.high
items.doc: The coefficient of `Z (k + 1)`, stored in the high `2 ^ k` bits of the word.
items.statement: def high (k : ℕ) (x : ConcreteBTField (k + 1)) : ConcreteBTField k

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Coordinates.joinSucc
items.doc: Construct a level-`k + 1` word with constant coefficient `lo` and generator coefficient `hi`.
items.statement: def joinSucc (k : ℕ) (lo hi : ConcreteBTField k) : ConcreteBTField (k + 1)

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Coordinates.low_joinSucc
items.doc: Reading the low coefficient after joining recovers it.
items.statement:
theorem low_joinSucc (k : ℕ) (lo hi : ConcreteBTField k) :
    low k (joinSucc k lo hi) = lo

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Coordinates.high_joinSucc
items.doc: Reading the high coefficient after joining recovers it.
items.statement:
theorem high_joinSucc (k : ℕ) (lo hi : ConcreteBTField k) :
    high k (joinSucc k lo hi) = hi

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Coordinates.joinSucc_low_high
items.doc: Joining the two coefficients recovers the original word.
items.statement:
theorem joinSucc_low_high (k : ℕ) (x : ConcreteBTField (k + 1)) :
    joinSucc k (low k x) (high k x) = x

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Coordinates.low_add
items.doc: The low coefficient preserves the canonical field addition.
items.statement:
theorem low_add (k : ℕ) (x y : ConcreteBTField (k + 1)) :
    low k (x + y) = low k x + low k y

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Coordinates.high_add
items.doc: The high coefficient preserves the canonical field addition.
items.statement:
theorem high_add (k : ℕ) (x y : ConcreteBTField (k + 1)) :
    high k (x + y) = high k x + high k y

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Coordinates.joinSucc_eq_map_mul_add
items.doc: A joined word is the sum of its embedded constant and generator terms.
items.statement:
theorem joinSucc_eq_map_mul_add (k : ℕ) (lo hi : ConcreteBTField k) :
    joinSucc k lo hi =
      concreteTowerAlgebraMap k (k + 1) (Nat.le_succ k) hi * Z (k + 1) +
        concreteTowerAlgebraMap k (k + 1) (Nat.le_succ k) lo

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Coordinates.smul_joinSucc
items.doc: The action induced by the tower embedding multiplies both coefficients by the scalar.
items.statement:
theorem smul_joinSucc (k : ℕ) (a lo hi : ConcreteBTField k) :
    letI := ConcreteBTFieldAlgebra (Nat.le_succ k)
    a • joinSucc k lo hi = joinSucc k (a * lo) (a * hi)

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Coordinates.low_smul
items.doc: The constant coefficient commutes with the scalar action induced by the tower embedding.
items.statement:
theorem low_smul (k : ℕ) (a : ConcreteBTField k) (x : ConcreteBTField (k + 1)) :
    letI := ConcreteBTFieldAlgebra (Nat.le_succ k)
    low k (a • x) = a * low k x

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Coordinates.high_smul
items.doc: The generator coefficient commutes with the scalar action induced by the tower embedding.
items.statement:
theorem high_smul (k : ℕ) (a : ConcreteBTField k) (x : ConcreteBTField (k + 1)) :
    letI := ConcreteBTFieldAlgebra (Nat.le_succ k)
    high k (a • x) = a * high k x

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Coordinates.succCoordinates
items.doc:
Coordinates `(constant coefficient, generator coefficient)` for the scalar action
induced by the tower embedding from level `k` to level `k + 1`.

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Coordinates.succCoordinates_apply
items.doc: The forward function is exactly low/high readback, in that order.
items.statement:
theorem succCoordinates_apply (k : ℕ) (x : ConcreteBTField (k + 1)) :
    succCoordinates k x = ![low k x, high k x]

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Coordinates.succCoordinates_symm_apply
items.doc:
The inverse constructs a word with constant coefficient `c 0` and generator coefficient
`c 1`.
items.statement:
theorem succCoordinates_symm_apply (k : ℕ) (c : Fin 2 → ConcreteBTField k) :
    (succCoordinates k).symm c = joinSucc k (c 0) (c 1)

modules.title: Concrete binary tower field construction interface
modules.doc:
Compatibility entry point for the executable arithmetic, together with the law records,
finite-field utilities, and field-instance assembly used by the recursive construction.
Arithmetic-only clients can import `CompPoly.Fields.Binary.Tower.Concrete.Arithmetic`;
canonical field clients use `CompPoly.Fields.Binary.Tower.Concrete.Field`.
