items.statement: noncomputable def toConcreteBTF0 : GF(2) → ConcreteBTField 0

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.fromConcreteBTF0
items.statement: noncomputable def fromConcreteBTF0 : ConcreteBTField 0 → (GF(2))

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.coeffsToBitVec
items.statement: def coeffsToBitVec {n : ℕ} (coeffs : List (ZMod 2)) : BitVec n

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.ConcreteBTFAddCommGroupProps
items.statement:
structure ConcreteBTFAddCommGroupProps (k : ℕ) where
  add_assoc : ∀ a b c : ConcreteBTField k, (a + b) + c = a + (b + c) := add_assoc
  add_comm : ∀ a b : ConcreteBTField k, a + b = b + a := add_comm
  add_zero : ∀ a : ConcreteBTField k, a + zero = a := add_zero
  zero_add : ∀ a : ConcreteBTField k, zero + a = a := zero_add
  add_neg : ∀ a : ConcreteBTField k, a + (neg a) = zero := neg_add_cancel

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.ConcreteBTFRingProps
items.statement:
structure ConcreteBTFRingProps (k : ℕ) extends (ConcreteBTFAddCommGroupProps k) where
  -- Multiplication equations and basic properties
  mul_eq : ∀ (a b : ConcreteBTField k) (h_k : k > 0)
    {a₁ a₀ b₁ b₀ : ConcreteBTField (k - 1)}
    (_h_a : (a₁, a₀) = split h_k a) (_h_b : (b₁, b₀) = split h_k b),
    concrete_mul a b =
      《 concrete_mul a₀ b₁ + concrete_mul b₀ a₁ + concrete_mul (concrete_mul a₁ b₁) (Z (k - 1)),
      concrete_mul a₀ b₀ + concrete_mul a₁ b₁ 》

  -- Zero and one laws
  zero_mul : ∀ a : ConcreteBTField k, concrete_mul zero a = zero
  zero_mul' : ∀ a : ConcreteBTField k, concrete_mul 0 a = 0
  mul_zero : ∀ a : ConcreteBTField k, concrete_mul a zero = zero
  mul_zero' : ∀ a : ConcreteBTField k, concrete_mul a 0 = 0
  one_mul : ∀ a : ConcreteBTField k, concrete_mul one a = a
  mul_one : ∀ a : ConcreteBTField k, concrete_mul a one = a

  -- Associativity and distributivity (Ring axioms)
  mul_assoc : ∀ a b c : ConcreteBTField k, concrete_mul (concrete_mul a b) c
    = concrete_mul a (concrete_mul b c)
  mul_left_distrib : ∀ a b c : ConcreteBTField k, concrete_mul a (b + c)
    = concrete_mul a b + concrete_mul a c
  mul_right_distrib : ∀ a b c : ConcreteBTField k, concrete_mul (a + b) c
    = concrete_mul a c + concrete_mul b c

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.ConcreteBTFDivisionRingProps
items.statement:
structure ConcreteBTFDivisionRingProps (k : ℕ) extends (ConcreteBTFRingProps k) where
  -- Multiplicative inverse property
  mul_inv_cancel : ∀ a : ConcreteBTField k, a ≠ zero → concrete_mul a (concrete_inv a) = one

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.ConcreteBTFieldProps
items.statement:
structure ConcreteBTFieldProps (k : ℕ) extends (ConcreteBTFDivisionRingProps k) where
  -- Commutativity (what makes it a Field vs just a DivisionRing)
  mul_comm : ∀ a b : ConcreteBTField k, concrete_mul a b = concrete_mul b a

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.mkRingInstance
items.statement:
def mkRingInstance {k : ℕ} (props : ConcreteBTFieldProps k) :
    Ring (ConcreteBTField k)

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.mkDivisionRingInstance
items.statement:
def mkDivisionRingInstance {k : ℕ} (props : ConcreteBTFieldProps k) :
    DivisionRing (ConcreteBTField k)

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.mkFieldInstance
items.statement:
def mkFieldInstance {k : ℕ} (props : ConcreteBTFieldProps k) :
    Field (ConcreteBTField k)

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.ConcreteBTFStepResult
items.statement:
structure ConcreteBTFStepResult (k : ℕ) extends (ConcreteBTFieldProps k) where
  instFintype : Fintype (ConcreteBTField k)
  fieldFintypeCard : Fintype.card (ConcreteBTField k) = 2^(2^k)
  -- Additional field theory properties for irreducibility proof
  sumZeroIffEq : ∀ (x y : ConcreteBTField k), x + y = 0 ↔ x = y
  traceMapEvalAtRootsIs1 :
    letI := mkFieldInstance (k:=k) (props:=toConcreteBTFieldProps)
    TraceMapProperty (ConcreteBTField k) (u:=Z k) k
  instIrreduciblePoly :
    letI := mkFieldInstance (k:=k) (props:=toConcreteBTFieldProps)
    (Irreducible (p := (definingPoly (s:=(Z k)))))

modules.title: Concrete Binary Tower Field
modules.doc:
Field-structure lemmas for successive levels of the concrete binary tower. The field
dictionary uses binary natural powers and integer powers that invert the natural-power
result for negative exponents. The named raw binary-power routine agrees with field powers.

Norm nonvanishing is certified using `QuadraticAlgebra.norm_eq_zero_iff_eq_zero` over the
predecessor field. This argument does not assume a field structure on the successor level.

items.note: Lemmas of field properties at level k that depends on field properties at level (k-1)

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.concrete_mul_eq
items.statement:
theorem concrete_mul_eq
    (prevBTFieldProps : ConcreteBTFieldProps (k := k - 1))
  (a b : ConcreteBTField k) {a₁ a₀ b₁ b₀ : ConcreteBTField (k - 1)}
  (h_a : (a₁, a₀) = split h_k a) (h_b : (b₁, b₀) = split h_k b) :
  concrete_mul a b =
    《 concrete_mul a₀ b₁ + concrete_mul b₀ a₁ + concrete_mul (concrete_mul a₁ b₁) (Z (k - 1)),
      concrete_mul a₀ b₀ + concrete_mul a₁ b₁ 》

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.concrete_zero_mul
items.statement:
lemma concrete_zero_mul
    (prevBTFieldProps : ConcreteBTFieldProps (k := k - 1))
  (a : ConcreteBTField k) : concrete_mul (zero (k:=k)) a = zero (k:=k)

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.concrete_mul_zero
items.statement:
lemma concrete_mul_zero
    (prevBTFieldProps : ConcreteBTFieldProps (k := k - 1))
  (a : ConcreteBTField k) : concrete_mul a (zero (k:=k)) = zero (k:=k)

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.concrete_one_mul
items.statement:
lemma concrete_one_mul
    (prevBTFieldProps : ConcreteBTFieldProps (k := k - 1))
  (a : ConcreteBTField k) : concrete_mul (one (k:=k)) a = a

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.concrete_mul_one
items.statement:
lemma concrete_mul_one
    (prevBTFieldProps : ConcreteBTFieldProps (k := k - 1))
  (a : ConcreteBTField k) : concrete_mul a (one (k:=k)) = a

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.concrete_pow_base_one
items.statement:
lemma concrete_pow_base_one
    (prevBTFieldProps : ConcreteBTFieldProps (k := k - 1)) (n : ℕ) :
  concrete_pow_nat (k:=k) (x:=1) n = 1

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.concrete_mul_comm
items.statement:
lemma concrete_mul_comm
    {h_k : k > 0} (prevBTFieldProps : ConcreteBTFieldProps (k := k - 1))
  (a b : ConcreteBTField k) :
  concrete_mul a b = concrete_mul b a

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.concrete_mul_assoc
items.doc:
The recursive multiplication is associative at a positive level whenever the predecessor
level satisfies its field laws.
items.statement:
lemma concrete_mul_assoc
    {h_k : k > 0} (prevBTFieldProps : ConcreteBTFieldProps (k := k - 1))
  (a b c : ConcreteBTField k) :
  concrete_mul (concrete_mul a b) c = concrete_mul a (concrete_mul b c)

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.concrete_mul_left_distrib
items.doc:
At a positive level, recursive multiplication distributes over addition in its second
argument whenever the predecessor level satisfies its field laws.
items.statement:
lemma concrete_mul_left_distrib
    {h_k : k > 0} (prevBTFieldProps : ConcreteBTFieldProps (k := k - 1))
  (a b c : ConcreteBTField k) :
    concrete_mul a (b + c) = concrete_mul a b + concrete_mul a c

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.concrete_mul_right_distrib
items.statement:
lemma concrete_mul_right_distrib
    {h_k : k > 0} (prevBTFieldProps : ConcreteBTFieldProps (k := k - 1))
  (a b c : ConcreteBTField k) :
    concrete_mul (a + b) c = concrete_mul a c + concrete_mul b c

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.norm_of_ne_zero_is_ne_zero
items.doc:
For a nonzero element at a positive level, `lo * (lo + hi * z) + hi * hi` is nonzero
in the predecessor field, where `lo` and `hi` are its low and high halves and `z = Z (k - 1)`.
This is the denominator in the quadratic inverse formula.
items.statement:
lemma norm_of_ne_zero_is_ne_zero {k : ℕ}
    {h_k_gt_0 : k > 0} (prevBTFieldResult : ConcreteBTFStepResult (k := k - 1))
  (a : ConcreteBTField k) (h_a_ne_zero : a ≠ 0) :
  let a₁ := (split h_k_gt_0 a).1
  let a₀ := (split h_k_gt_0 a).2
  concrete_mul a₀ (a₀ + concrete_mul a₁ (Z (k - 1))) + concrete_mul a₁ a₁ ≠ 0

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.concrete_mul_inv_cancel
items.statement:
lemma concrete_mul_inv_cancel
    (prevBTFieldResult : ConcreteBTFStepResult (k := k - 1))
  (a : ConcreteBTField k) (h : a ≠ 0) :
  concrete_mul a (concrete_inv a) = one

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.concrete_inv_one
items.statement:
lemma concrete_inv_one :
    concrete_inv (k:=k) 1 = 1

items.note: Inductive tower construction, using lemmas from `BTFieldPropsOneLevelLiftingLemmas`

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Z_square_eq
items.statement:
lemma Z_square_eq (k : ℕ) (prevBTFieldProps : ConcreteBTFieldProps (k := k))
    (curBTFieldProps : ConcreteBTFieldProps (k := (k + 1))) :
  letI : Field (ConcreteBTField (k + 1)) := mkFieldInstance curBTFieldProps
  (Z (k + 1)) ^ 2 = 《 Z (k), 1 》

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.liftBTFieldProps
items.statement:
theorem liftBTFieldProps (k : ℕ) (prevBTFResult : ConcreteBTFStepResult (k := k)) :
  ConcreteBTFieldProps (k + 1)

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.liftConcreteBTField
items.statement:
def liftConcreteBTField (k : ℕ) (prevBTFResult : ConcreteBTFStepResult (k := k)) :
  Field (ConcreteBTField (k + 1))

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.concreteCanonicalEmbedding
items.doc:
The canonical ring homomorphism embedding `ConcreteBTField k` into
`ConcreteBTField (k + 1)`.
This is the `AdjoinRoot.of` map.
items.statement:
def concreteCanonicalEmbedding (k : ℕ)
    (prevBTFieldProps : ConcreteBTFieldProps (k := (k)))
    (curBTFieldProps : ConcreteBTFieldProps (k := (k + 1))) :
  letI := mkFieldInstance prevBTFieldProps
  letI := mkFieldInstance curBTFieldProps
  ConcreteBTField k →+* ConcreteBTField (k + 1)

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.instAlgebraLiftConcreteBTField
items.statement:
instance instAlgebraLiftConcreteBTField (k : ℕ)
  (prevBTFResult : ConcreteBTFStepResult (k := k)) :
  letI := mkFieldInstance (prevBTFResult.toConcreteBTFieldProps)
  letI := liftConcreteBTField (k:=k) prevBTFResult
  Algebra (ConcreteBTField k) (ConcreteBTField (k + 1))

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Z_square_mul_form
items.statement:
lemma Z_square_mul_form
    (k : ℕ)
  (prev : ConcreteBTFStepResult (k := k)) :
  letI : Field (ConcreteBTField k) := mkFieldInstance (prev.toConcreteBTFieldProps)
  letI : Field (ConcreteBTField (k + 1)) := mkFieldInstance (k:=k+1)
    (props:=liftBTFieldProps (k:=k) (prevBTFResult:=prev))
  letI : Algebra (ConcreteBTField k) (ConcreteBTField (k + 1)) :=
    instAlgebraLiftConcreteBTField k prev
  Z (k + 1) ^ 2
    = Z (k + 1)
      * (algebraMap (ConcreteBTField k) (ConcreteBTField (k + 1))) (Z k)
      + 1

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.sum_inv_Z_next_eq
items.statement:
lemma sum_inv_Z_next_eq
    (k : ℕ)
  (prev : ConcreteBTFStepResult (k := k)) :
  letI : Field (ConcreteBTField k) := mkFieldInstance (prev.toConcreteBTFieldProps)
  letI : Field (ConcreteBTField (k + 1)) := mkFieldInstance (k:=k+1)
    (props:=liftBTFieldProps (k:=k) (prevBTFResult:=prev))
  letI : Algebra (ConcreteBTField k) (ConcreteBTField (k + 1)) :=
    instAlgebraLiftConcreteBTField k prev
  Z (k + 1) + (Z (k + 1))⁻¹ = (algebraMap (ConcreteBTField k) (ConcreteBTField (k + 1))) (Z k)

modules.title: Relative coordinates for concrete binary tower fields
modules.doc:
`ConcreteBinaryTower.Coordinates.coordinates h` identifies level `j` with
`2 ^ (j - i)` coefficients in level `i`, for `h : i ≤ j`. The scalar action is induced by
the existing concrete tower embedding. Coordinate `q` is the block of `2 ^ i` bits starting
at bit `2 ^ i * q`; blocks and bits within each block retain their numeric order.

The equivalence composes `succCoordinates` through `AlgebraTower.natCoordinatesConstOfLE`.
Its inverse `pack` reconstructs the original word. The readback theorems relate the algebraic
coordinates to bitvector slicing and natural-number bit blocks. They refer to raw stored words,
which differ from field numerals in characteristic two.

The coefficient ordering follows the relative multilinear basis of [DP23], §2.3:
earlier tower generators correspond to lower index bits.

## References

* [Diamond, B. E. and Posen, J., *Succinct arguments over towers of binary fields*][DP23]

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Coordinates.coordinates
items.doc:
Coordinates of level `j` over level `i`, ordered by increasing bit-block offset, for the
scalar action induced by the concrete tower embedding associated with `h`.

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Coordinates.coordinates_eq_natCoordinatesConstOfLE
items.doc:
The relative equivalence is the constant-two composition of the low-first successor
coordinate equivalences, with the scalar action induced by the concrete tower embedding.
items.statement:
theorem coordinates_eq_natCoordinatesConstOfLE {i j : ℕ} (h : i ≤ j) :
    coordinates h = natCoordinatesConstOfLE succCoordinates h

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Coordinates.pack
items.doc:
Construct a level-`j` word from level-`i` coefficients, with coefficient `q` occupying
the block of `2 ^ i` bits starting at bit `2 ^ i * q`.
items.statement:
def pack {i j : ℕ} (h : i ≤ j) (c : Fin (2 ^ (j - i)) → ConcreteBTField i) :
    ConcreteBTField j

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Coordinates.coordinates_pack
items.doc: Reading the coordinates of a packed word recovers every input coefficient.
items.statement:
theorem coordinates_pack {i j : ℕ} (h : i ≤ j)
    (c : Fin (2 ^ (j - i)) → ConcreteBTField i) : coordinates h (pack h c) = c

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Coordinates.pack_coordinates
items.doc: Packing all coordinates recovers the original word.
items.statement:
theorem pack_coordinates {i j : ℕ} (h : i ≤ j) (x : ConcreteBTField j) :
    pack h (coordinates h x) = x

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Coordinates.coordinates_self
items.doc: At equal endpoints the single coordinate is the original word.
items.statement:
theorem coordinates_self (i : ℕ) (h : i ≤ i) (x : ConcreteBTField i)
    (q : Fin (2 ^ (i - i))) : coordinates h x q = x

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Coordinates.pack_self
items.doc: Packing at equal endpoints returns the single coefficient.
items.statement:
theorem pack_self (i : ℕ) (h : i ≤ i) (c : Fin (2 ^ (i - i)) → ConcreteBTField i) :
    pack h c = c 0

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Coordinates.coordinates_add
items.doc: Coordinates preserve the canonical field addition, coefficient by coefficient.
items.statement:
theorem coordinates_add {i j : ℕ} (h : i ≤ j) (x y : ConcreteBTField j) :
    coordinates h (x + y) = coordinates h x + coordinates h y

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Coordinates.pack_add
items.doc: Packing preserves coefficientwise canonical field addition.
items.statement:
theorem pack_add {i j : ℕ} (h : i ≤ j)
    (c d : Fin (2 ^ (j - i)) → ConcreteBTField i) :
    pack h (c + d) = pack h c + pack h d

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Coordinates.coordinates_smul
items.doc: The tower embedding's scalar action multiplies each coordinate by the lower-level scalar.
items.statement:
theorem coordinates_smul {i j : ℕ} (h : i ≤ j) (a : ConcreteBTField i)
    (x : ConcreteBTField j) (q : Fin (2 ^ (j - i))) :
    letI := ConcreteBTFieldAlgebra h
    coordinates h (a • x) q = a * coordinates h x q

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Coordinates.pack_smul
items.doc: Scaling all coefficients commutes with packing under the tower embedding's scalar action.
items.statement:
theorem pack_smul {i j : ℕ} (h : i ≤ j) (a : ConcreteBTField i)
    (c : Fin (2 ^ (j - i)) → ConcreteBTField i) :
    letI := ConcreteBTFieldAlgebra h
    pack h (fun q => a * c q) = a • pack h c

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Coordinates.coordinates_eq_setWidth_ushiftRight
items.doc: Coordinate `q` is the raw bit block of width `2 ^ i` starting at bit `2 ^ i * q`.
items.statement:
theorem coordinates_eq_setWidth_ushiftRight {i j : ℕ} (h : i ≤ j) (x : ConcreteBTField j)
    (q : Fin (2 ^ (j - i))) :
    coordinates h x q =
      ConcreteBTField.ofBitVec
        ((BitVec.ushiftRight x.toBitVec (2 ^ i * q.val)).setWidth (2 ^ i))

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Coordinates.toBitVec_coordinates
items.doc: Encoding coordinate `q` returns the corresponding low-first bit block of the input word.
items.statement:
theorem toBitVec_coordinates {i j : ℕ} (h : i ≤ j) (x : ConcreteBTField j)
    (q : Fin (2 ^ (j - i))) :
    (coordinates h x q).toBitVec =
      (BitVec.ushiftRight x.toBitVec (2 ^ i * q.val)).setWidth (2 ^ i)

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Coordinates.getLsbD_coordinates
items.doc:
Reading bit `b` within coordinate `q` reads the bit at offset `2 ^ i * q + b`
in the original word. The bound keeps `b` inside the coefficient's bit width.
items.statement:
theorem getLsbD_coordinates {i j : ℕ} (h : i ≤ j) (x : ConcreteBTField j)
    (q : Fin (2 ^ (j - i))) (b : ℕ) (hb : b < 2 ^ i) :
    (coordinates h x q).toBitVec.getLsbD b = x.toBitVec.getLsbD (2 ^ i * q.val + b)

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Coordinates.toNat_coordinates
items.doc:
The stored natural word of coordinate `q` is the block of `2 ^ i` bits starting at
bit `2 ^ i * q` in the original word.
items.statement:
theorem toNat_coordinates {i j : ℕ} (h : i ≤ j) (x : ConcreteBTField j)
    (q : Fin (2 ^ (j - i))) :
    (coordinates h x q).toNat =
      Nat.getMiddleBits (2 ^ i * q.val) (2 ^ i) x.toNat

modules.title: Binary Tower Equivalence
modules.doc:
Equivalences between the abstract and concrete binary tower constructions.

The concrete-to-abstract equivalence commutes with the chosen tower embeddings and preserves
the multilinear basis at each numeric index. `multilinearBasis_map_towerEquiv` identifies
the bases after changing coefficients at the base level and transporting the ambient space.
The coefficient actions are selected locally from the tower maps.

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.towerEquiv_zero
items.statement: noncomputable def towerEquiv_zero : RingEquiv (R:=GF(2)) (S:=ConcreteBTField 0)

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.towerRingEquiv0
items.statement: noncomputable def towerRingEquiv0 : BTField 0 ≃+* ConcreteBTField 0

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.towerRingEquivFromConcrete0
items.statement: noncomputable def towerRingEquivFromConcrete0 : ConcreteBTField 0 ≃+* BTField 0

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.towerRingHomForwardMap
items.statement: noncomputable def towerRingHomForwardMap (k : ℕ) : ConcreteBTField k → BTField k

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.towerRingHomBackwardMap
items.statement: noncomputable def towerRingHomBackwardMap (k : ℕ) : BTField k → ConcreteBTField k

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.towerRingHomForwardMap0_eq
items.statement:
lemma towerRingHomForwardMap0_eq :
    towerRingEquivFromConcrete0.toFun = towerRingHomForwardMap 0

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.towerRingHomForwardMap_zero
items.statement:
lemma towerRingHomForwardMap_zero {k : ℕ} :
    (towerRingHomForwardMap k) 0 = 0

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.towerRingHomForwardMap_one
items.statement:
lemma towerRingHomForwardMap_one {k : ℕ} :
    (towerRingHomForwardMap k) 1 = 1

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.towerRingHomForwardMap_Z
items.statement:
lemma towerRingHomForwardMap_Z (k : ℕ) :
    towerRingHomForwardMap k (Z k) = BinaryTower.Z k

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.towerRingHomBackwardMap_forwardMap_eq
items.statement:
lemma towerRingHomBackwardMap_forwardMap_eq (k : ℕ) (x : ConcreteBTField k) :
    towerRingHomBackwardMap (k:=k) (towerRingHomForwardMap (k:=k) x) = x

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.towerRingHomForwardMap_backwardMap_eq
items.statement:
lemma towerRingHomForwardMap_backwardMap_eq (k : ℕ) (x : BTField k) :
    towerRingHomForwardMap (k:=k) (towerRingHomBackwardMap (k:=k) x) = x

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.towerRingHomForwardMap_add_eq
items.statement:
lemma towerRingHomForwardMap_add_eq (k : ℕ) (x y : ConcreteBTField k) :
    towerRingHomForwardMap (k:=k) (x + y)
    = towerRingHomForwardMap (k:=k) x + towerRingHomForwardMap (k:=k) y

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.split_mul_eq_mul_split
items.statement:
theorem split_mul_eq_mul_split {k : ℕ} (h_pos : k > 0) (x₀ x₁ : ConcreteBTField k)
    (hi₀ lo₀ hi₁ lo₁ : ConcreteBTField (k - 1))
  (h_split_x₀ : split h_pos x₀ = (hi₀, lo₀))
  (h_split_x₁ : split h_pos x₁ = (hi₁, lo₁)) :
  split h_pos (x₀ * x₁) =
    (lo₀ * hi₁ + lo₁ * hi₀ + hi₀ * hi₁ * Z (k - 1), lo₀ * lo₁ + hi₀ * hi₁)

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.towerRingHomForwardMap_mul_eq
items.statement:
lemma towerRingHomForwardMap_mul_eq (k : ℕ) (x y : ConcreteBTField k) :
    towerRingHomForwardMap (k:=k) (x * y)
    = towerRingHomForwardMap (k:=k) x * towerRingHomForwardMap (k:=k) y

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.towerRingHomForwardMap_split_eq
items.statement:
lemma towerRingHomForwardMap_split_eq (k : ℕ) (h_pos : k > 0) (x : ConcreteBTField k) :
    let p := split (k:=k) (h:=h_pos) x
  towerRingHomForwardMap (k:=k) (x) =
    BinaryTower.join_via_add_smul (k:=k) (h_pos:=h_pos)
      (hi_btf := towerRingHomForwardMap (k:=k-1) (p.1))
      (lo_btf := towerRingHomForwardMap (k:=k-1) (p.2))

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.towerRingHomForwardMap_join
items.statement:
lemma towerRingHomForwardMap_join {k : ℕ} (h_pos : k > 0) (hi lo : ConcreteBTField (k - 1)) :
    towerRingHomForwardMap (k:=k) (《 hi, lo 》) =
    BinaryTower.join_via_add_smul (k:=k) (h_pos:=by omega)
      (hi_btf := towerRingHomForwardMap (k:=k-1) hi)
      (lo_btf := towerRingHomForwardMap (k:=k-1) lo)

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.TowerEquivResult
items.statement:
structure TowerEquivResult (k : ℕ) where
  ringEquiv : ConcreteBTField k ≃+* BTField k
  ringEquivForwardMapEq : ringEquiv = towerRingHomForwardMap k

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.towerEquiv
items.statement: noncomputable def towerEquiv (n : ℕ) : TowerEquivResult n

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.BTField_algebraMap_succ_eq_join
items.statement:
theorem BTField_algebraMap_succ_eq_join (k : ℕ) (x : BTField k) :
    algebraMap (BTField k) (BTField (k+1)) x =
      BinaryTower.join_via_add_smul (k:=k+1) (h_pos:=by omega) 0 x

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.ConcreteBTField_algebraMap_succ_eq_join
items.statement:
theorem ConcreteBTField_algebraMap_succ_eq_join (k : ℕ) (r : ConcreteBTField k) :
    algebraMap (ConcreteBTField k) (ConcreteBTField (k+1)) r =
      join (k:=k+1) (h_pos:=by omega) 0 r

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.towerEquiv_ringEquiv_apply
items.statement:
theorem towerEquiv_ringEquiv_apply (k : ℕ) (r : ConcreteBTField k) :
    (towerEquiv k).ringEquiv r = towerRingHomForwardMap k r

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.towerEquiv_commutes_left_succ
items.statement:
theorem towerEquiv_commutes_left_succ (k : ℕ) : ∀ r : ConcreteBTField k,
    (AlgebraTower.algebraMap k (k+1) (by omega)) ((towerEquiv k).ringEquiv r) =
  (towerEquiv (k+1)).ringEquiv ((AlgebraTower.algebraMap k (k+1) (by omega)) r)

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.towerEquiv_commutes_left_diff
items.statement:
theorem towerEquiv_commutes_left_diff (i d : ℕ) : ∀ r : ConcreteBTField i,
    (AlgebraTower.algebraMap i (i+d) (by omega)) ((towerEquiv i).ringEquiv r) =
  (towerEquiv (i+d)).ringEquiv ((AlgebraTower.algebraMap i (i+d) (by omega)) r)

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.towerEquiv_commutes_left
items.statement:
theorem towerEquiv_commutes_left (i j : ℕ) (h : i ≤ j) : ∀ r : ConcreteBTField i,
    (AlgebraTower.algebraMap i j h) ((towerEquiv i).ringEquiv r) =
  (towerEquiv j).ringEquiv ((AlgebraTower.algebraMap i j h) r)

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.instAlgebraTowerEquiv
items.statement:
noncomputable def instAlgebraTowerEquiv : AlgebraTowerEquiv
  (ConcreteBTField) (BTField)

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.towerEquiv_multilinearBasis
items.doc:
The tower equivalence sends each concrete multilinear basis vector to the abstract
basis vector at the same numeric index.
items.statement:
theorem towerEquiv_multilinearBasis {i j : ℕ} (h : i ≤ j) (q : Fin (2 ^ (j - i))) :
    (towerEquiv j).ringEquiv (multilinearBasis i j h q) =
      BinaryTower.multilinearBasis i j h q

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.multilinearBasis_map_towerEquiv
items.doc:
Transporting the concrete multilinear basis along the tower equivalence gives the
abstract basis with coefficients changed by the inverse equivalence at the base level.
Both coefficient actions are the chosen tower actions.
items.statement:
theorem multilinearBasis_map_towerEquiv {i j : ℕ} (h : i ≤ j) :
    let := ConcreteBTFieldAlgebra h
    let := binaryAlgebraTower h
    let := instAlgebraTowerEquiv.toAlgebraOverLeft i j h
    (multilinearBasis i j h).map
        (instAlgebraTowerEquiv.toAlgEquivOverLeft i j h).toLinearEquiv =
      (BinaryTower.multilinearBasis i j h).mapCoeffs (towerEquiv i).ringEquiv.symm
        (by
          intro a x
          change towerAlgebraMap i j h
              ((towerEquiv i).ringEquiv ((towerEquiv i).ringEquiv.symm a)) * x =
            towerAlgebraMap i j h a * x
          rw [RingEquiv.apply_symm_apply])

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.multilinearBasis_repr_towerEquiv
items.doc:
The abstract basis coordinates of a mapped element are its concrete basis coordinates
mapped by the equivalence at the base level, at the same numeric indices.
Both representations use their chosen tower coefficient actions.
items.statement:
theorem multilinearBasis_repr_towerEquiv {i j : ℕ} (h : i ≤ j) (x : ConcreteBTField j)
    (q : Fin (2 ^ (j - i))) :
    let := ConcreteBTFieldAlgebra h
    let := binaryAlgebraTower h
    (BinaryTower.multilinearBasis i j h).repr ((towerEquiv j).ringEquiv x) q =
      (towerEquiv i).ringEquiv ((ConcreteBinaryTower.multilinearBasis i j h).repr x q)

modules.title: Fast Binary Tower Arithmetic
modules.doc:
Packed machine-word implementation of `ConcreteBTField` arithmetic, same bit layout:
one `UInt64` for levels `k ≤ 6`, two limbs at level 7. The runtime definitions live in
the zero-import `FastDefs`; this module proves them correct against the concrete tower
by induction over recursive twins, giving `Field` instances and ring isomorphisms at
every width.

items.note:
## Range bounds

Every operation maps values below `2 ^ s` to values below `2 ^ s`; the shift/mask
helpers cross into `ℕ` once and the per-width lemmas chain them.

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Fast.and_mask_lt
items.statement:
theorem and_mask_lt (s : ℕ) {a m : UInt64} (hm : m.toNat = 2 ^ s - 1) :
    (a &&& m).toNat < 2 ^ s

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Fast.xor_lt
items.statement:
theorem xor_lt {x y : UInt64} {s : ℕ} (hx : x.toNat < 2 ^ s) (hy : y.toNat < 2 ^ s) :
    (x ^^^ y).toNat < 2 ^ s

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Fast.shiftRight_lt
items.statement:
theorem shiftRight_lt (s : ℕ) {a sh : UInt64} {t : ℕ} (hsh : sh.toNat = s)
    (hs : s < 64) (ha : a.toNat < 2 ^ (s + t)) : (a >>> sh).toNat < 2 ^ t

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Fast.join_lt
items.statement:
theorem join_lt (s : ℕ) {hi lo sh : UInt64} (hsh : sh.toNat = s) (hs : 2 * s ≤ 64)
    (hhi : hi.toNat < 2 ^ s) (hlo : lo.toNat < 2 ^ s) :
    ((hi <<< sh) ||| lo).toNat < 2 ^ (2 * s)

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Fast.half_lit_lt
items.doc: Both half bounds for a literal shift/mask split.
items.statement:
theorem half_lit_lt (s : ℕ) (m sh : UInt64) {v : UInt64} (hm : m.toNat = 2 ^ s - 1)
    (hsh : sh.toNat = s) (hs : s < 64) (hv : v.toNat < 2 ^ (s + s)) :
    (v >>> sh).toNat < 2 ^ s ∧ (v &&& m).toNat < 2 ^ s

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Fast.half16_lt
items.doc: Half bounds of a 16-bit word.
items.statement:
theorem half16_lt {v : UInt64} (hv : v.toNat < 2 ^ 16) :
    (v >>> 8).toNat < 2 ^ 8 ∧ (v &&& 0xFF).toNat < 2 ^ 8

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Fast.half32_lt
items.doc: Half bounds of a 32-bit word.
items.statement:
theorem half32_lt {v : UInt64} (hv : v.toNat < 2 ^ 32) :
    (v >>> 16).toNat < 2 ^ 16 ∧ (v &&& 0xFFFF).toNat < 2 ^ 16

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Fast.half64_lt
items.doc: Half bounds of a full word.
items.statement:
theorem half64_lt (v : UInt64) :
    (v >>> 32).toNat < 2 ^ 32 ∧ (v &&& 0xFFFFFFFF).toNat < 2 ^ 32

items.note:
### Proof-side recursive twins

The runtime ladder is unrolled for code generation; proofs run over structurally
recursive twins, connected to each rung by `rfl` bridges (`mul8_eq_rec`, ...) and
meaningful for `k ≤ 6` (one word).

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Fast.mulByZRec
items.doc: Recursive twin of the `mulByZk` ladder.
items.statement: def mulByZRec : ℕ → UInt64 → UInt64

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Fast.mulRec
items.doc: Recursive twin of the multiplication ladder.
items.statement: def mulRec : ℕ → UInt64 → UInt64 → UInt64

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Fast.sqRec
items.doc: Recursive twin of the squaring ladder; level 0 is the identity (`v² = v` in GF(2)).
items.statement: def sqRec : ℕ → UInt64 → UInt64

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Fast.invRec
items.doc: Recursive twin of the inversion ladder; level 0 is the identity.
items.statement: def invRec : ℕ → UInt64 → UInt64

items.note:
One-step unfoldings as `rfl` theorems, so proofs rewrite with these instead of
realizing each twin's equation lemmas over and over.

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Fast.mulByZRec_succ
items.statement:
theorem mulByZRec_succ (k : ℕ) (v : UInt64) :
    mulByZRec (k + 1) v =
      let sh := UInt64.ofNat (2 ^ k)
      let m := ((1 : UInt64) <<< sh) - 1
      let v0 := v &&& m
      let v1 := v >>> sh
      ((v0 ^^^ mulByZRec k v1) <<< sh) ||| v1

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Fast.mulRec_succ
items.statement:
theorem mulRec_succ (k : ℕ) (a b : UInt64) :
    mulRec (k + 1) a b =
      let sh := UInt64.ofNat (2 ^ k)
      let m := ((1 : UInt64) <<< sh) - 1
      let a0 := a &&& m
      let a1 := a >>> sh
      let b0 := b &&& m
      let b1 := b >>> sh
      let p0 := mulRec k a0 b0
      let p2 := mulRec k a1 b1
      let p1 := mulRec k (a0 ^^^ a1) (b0 ^^^ b1)
      let lo := p0 ^^^ p2
      ((p1 ^^^ lo ^^^ mulByZRec k p2) <<< sh) ||| lo

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Fast.sqRec_succ
ConcreteBinaryTower.Fast.invRec_succ
items.statement:
theorem invRec_succ (k : ℕ) (v : UInt64) :
    invRec (k + 1) v =
      let sh := UInt64.ofNat (2 ^ k)
      let m := ((1 : UInt64) <<< sh) - 1
      let v0 := v &&& m
      let v1 := v >>> sh
      let next := v0 ^^^ mulByZRec k v1
      let delta := mulRec k v0 next ^^^ sqRec k v1
      let d := invRec k delta
      ((mulRec k d v1) <<< sh) ||| (mulRec k d next)

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Fast.toNat_ofNat_two_pow
items.statement:
theorem toNat_ofNat_two_pow {k : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ 5) :
    (UInt64.ofNat (2 ^ k)).toNat = 2 ^ k

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Fast.toNat_mask_two_pow
items.statement:
theorem toNat_mask_two_pow {k : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ 5) :
    (((1 : UInt64) <<< UInt64.ofNat (2 ^ k)) - 1).toNat = 2 ^ 2 ^ k - 1

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Fast.rec_step_bounds
items.doc: The arithmetic facts every inductive step needs about the half-width `2 ^ k`.

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Fast.half_lt
items.doc: Both halves of an in-range word are in range at the half level.
items.statement:
theorem half_lt {k : ℕ} (hk : k + 1 ≤ 6) {v : UInt64}
    (hv : v.toNat < 2 ^ 2 ^ (k + 1)) :
    (v >>> UInt64.ofNat (2 ^ k)).toNat < 2 ^ 2 ^ k
      ∧ (v &&& ((1 : UInt64) <<< UInt64.ofNat (2 ^ k) - 1)).toNat < 2 ^ 2 ^ k

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Fast.mulByZRec_lt
items.doc: One-word `mulByZ` bound, by induction on the level.
items.statement:
theorem mulByZRec_lt : ∀ (k : ℕ), k ≤ 6 → ∀ (v : UInt64),
    v.toNat < 2 ^ 2 ^ k → (mulByZRec k v).toNat < 2 ^ 2 ^ k
  | 0, _, _, hv => hv
  | k + 1, hk, v, hv => by
    obtain ⟨hk5, h2s, _, hpow⟩

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Fast.mulRec_lt
items.doc: One-word multiplication bound, by induction on the level.
items.statement:
theorem mulRec_lt : ∀ (k : ℕ), k ≤ 6 → ∀ (a b : UInt64),
    a.toNat < 2 ^ 2 ^ k → b.toNat < 2 ^ 2 ^ k → (mulRec k a b).toNat < 2 ^ 2 ^ k
  | 0, _, a, b, ha, _ => by
    show (a &&& b).toNat < 2 ^ 2 ^ 0
    exact Nat.lt_of_le_of_lt (by rw [UInt64.toNat_and]; exact Nat.and_le_left) ha
  | k + 1, hk, a, b, ha, hb => by
    obtain ⟨hk5, h2s, _, hpow⟩

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Fast.sqRec_lt
items.doc: One-word squaring bound, by induction on the level.
items.statement:
theorem sqRec_lt : ∀ (k : ℕ), k ≤ 6 → ∀ (v : UInt64),
    v.toNat < 2 ^ 2 ^ k → (sqRec k v).toNat < 2 ^ 2 ^ k
  | 0, _, _, hv => hv
  | k + 1, hk, v, hv => by
    obtain ⟨hk5, h2s, _, hpow⟩

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Fast.invRec_lt
items.doc: One-word inversion bound, by induction on the level.
items.statement:
theorem invRec_lt : ∀ (k : ℕ), k ≤ 6 → ∀ (v : UInt64),
    v.toNat < 2 ^ 2 ^ k → (invRec k v).toNat < 2 ^ 2 ^ k
  | 0, _, _, hv => hv
  | k + 1, hk, v, hv => by
    obtain ⟨hk5, h2s, _, hpow⟩

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Fast.mulByZ1_eq_rec

### Table bridges

`getElem_ofFn` turns a table lookup back into the generating ladder call, so each `*T`
rung equals its ladder twin on in-range words and no table is kernel-evaluated.

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Fast.byteTable_get_eq
items.doc: Lookup in a 256-entry `Array.ofFn` table is the generating function.
items.statement:
theorem byteTable_get_eq {f : UInt64 → UInt64}
    (hf : ∀ v : UInt64, v.toNat < 2 ^ 8 → (f v).toNat < 2 ^ 8)
    {v : UInt64} (hv : v.toNat < 2 ^ 8) :
    ((⟨Array.ofFn (n := 256) fun i => (f (UInt64.ofNat i)).toUInt8⟩ : ByteArray).get!
      v.toNat).toUInt64 = f v

## Correctness against the spec

The twins agree with `concrete_mul` / `concrete_inv` on in-range words, by induction on
the level; statements go through `fromNat` so the spec side reasons inside
`ConcreteBTField`.

    fromNat (k := k + 1) ((hi <<< UInt64.ofNat (2 ^ k)) ||| lo).toNat

      = (fromNat (k := k) (a >>> UInt64.ofNat (2 ^ k)).toNat,

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Fast.concrete_mul_step
items.doc:
`concrete_mul`'s one-level structure theorem, restated with all indices at the
half level `k` (the original lives at `k + 1 - 1`, which blocks syntactic rewriting).
items.statement:
theorem concrete_mul_step {k : ℕ} (a b : ConcreteBTField (k + 1))
    {a₁ a₀ b₁ b₀ : ConcreteBTField k}
    (ha : (a₁, a₀) = split (Nat.succ_pos k) a) (hb : (b₁, b₀) = split (Nat.succ_pos k) b) :
    concrete_mul a b
      = (《 concrete_mul a₀ b₁ + concrete_mul b₀ a₁
            + concrete_mul (concrete_mul a₁ b₁) (Z k),
          concrete_mul a₀ b₀ + concrete_mul a₁ b₁ 》 : ConcreteBTField (k + 1))

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Fast.mulByZRec_correct
items.doc: `mulByZRec` computes multiplication by the level generator on the spec side.
items.statement:
theorem mulByZRec_correct : ∀ (k : ℕ), k ≤ 6 → ∀ (v : UInt64), v.toNat < 2 ^ 2 ^ k →
    fromNat (k := k) (mulByZRec k v).toNat = concrete_mul (fromNat v.toNat) (Z k)
  | 0, _, v, hv => by
    show fromNat (k := 0) v.toNat = concrete_mul (fromNat v.toNat) (Z 0)
    rw [show Z 0 = ConcreteBinaryTower.one from rfl, concrete_mul_one0]
  | k + 1, hk, v, hv => by
    obtain ⟨hv1, hv0⟩

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Fast.mulRec_correct
items.doc: `mulRec` agrees with `concrete_mul` on in-range words.
items.statement:
theorem mulRec_correct : ∀ (k : ℕ), k ≤ 6 → ∀ (a b : UInt64),
    a.toNat < 2 ^ 2 ^ k → b.toNat < 2 ^ 2 ^ k →
    fromNat (k := k) (mulRec k a b).toNat = concrete_mul (fromNat a.toNat) (fromNat b.toNat)
  | 0, _, a, b, ha, hb => by
    rcases eq_zero_or_one ha with rfl | rfl <;> rcases eq_zero_or_one hb with rfl | rfl
    · show ConcreteBinaryTower.zero = concrete_mul zero zero
      rw [concrete_zero_mul0]
    · show ConcreteBinaryTower.zero = concrete_mul zero one
      rw [concrete_zero_mul0]
    · show ConcreteBinaryTower.zero = concrete_mul one zero
      rw [concrete_mul_zero0]
    · show ConcreteBinaryTower.one = concrete_mul one one
      rw [concrete_mul_one0]
  | k + 1, hk, a, b, ha, hb => by
    have hk6 : k ≤ 6 := Nat.le_of_succ_le hk
    obtain ⟨ha1, ha0⟩

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Fast.sqRec_correct
items.doc: `sqRec` computes the spec square on in-range words.
items.statement:
theorem sqRec_correct : ∀ (k : ℕ), k ≤ 6 → ∀ (v : UInt64), v.toNat < 2 ^ 2 ^ k →
    fromNat (k := k) (sqRec k v).toNat = concrete_mul (fromNat v.toNat) (fromNat v.toNat)
  | 0, hk, v, hv => by
    have h := mulRec_correct 0 hk v v hv hv
    rwa [show mulRec 0 v v = v from UInt64.and_self] at h
  | k + 1, hk, v, hv => by
    have hk6 : k ≤ 6 := Nat.le_of_succ_le hk
    obtain ⟨hv1, hv0⟩

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Fast.split_zero'
items.statement:
theorem split_zero' {k : ℕ} : split (Nat.succ_pos k) (0 : ConcreteBTField (k + 1))
    = ((0 : ConcreteBTField k), (0 : ConcreteBTField k))

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Fast.split_one'
items.statement:
theorem split_one' {k : ℕ} : split (Nat.succ_pos k) (1 : ConcreteBTField (k + 1))

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Fast.concrete_inv_step
items.doc:
`concrete_inv`'s one-level descent, restated at the half level `k`; the `a = 0`
and `a = 1` branches satisfy the same formula.
items.statement:
theorem concrete_inv_step {k : ℕ} (a : ConcreteBTField (k + 1))
    {a₁ a₀ : ConcreteBTField k} (ha : (a₁, a₀) = split (Nat.succ_pos k) a) :
    concrete_inv a
      = (《 (concrete_mul
              (concrete_inv (concrete_mul a₀ (a₀ + concrete_mul a₁ (Z k))
                + concrete_mul a₁ a₁)) a₁ : ConcreteBTField k),
            (concrete_mul
              (concrete_inv (concrete_mul a₀ (a₀ + concrete_mul a₁ (Z k))
                + concrete_mul a₁ a₁)) (a₀ + concrete_mul a₁ (Z k)) : ConcreteBTField k) 》 :
          ConcreteBTField (k + 1))

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Fast.invRec_correct
items.doc: `invRec` agrees with `concrete_inv` on in-range words.
items.statement:
theorem invRec_correct : ∀ (k : ℕ), k ≤ 6 → ∀ (v : UInt64), v.toNat < 2 ^ 2 ^ k →
    fromNat (k := k) (invRec k v).toNat = concrete_inv (fromNat v.toNat)
  | 0, _, v, hv => by
    simp only [invRec]
    rcases eq_zero_or_one hv with rfl | rfl
    · rw [fromNat_zero, concrete_inv_zero]
    · rw [fromNat_one, concrete_inv_one]
  | k + 1, hk, v, hv => by
    have hk6 : k ≤ 6 := Nat.le_of_succ_le hk
    obtain ⟨hv1, hv0⟩

modules.title: Packed binary-tower product accumulation
modules.doc:
The eager `FastBT128` backend uses its ordinary field multiplication and addition, with
identity reduction. Its existing ring equivalence transports arbitrary product accumulations
and coefficient-form multilinear evaluations to the concrete tower. No unreduced product
representation or delayed-reduction algorithm is introduced.

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Fast.FastBT128.toConcrete_accumulateProducts
items.doc:
Converting an eager product accumulation to the concrete tower preserves its initial
accumulator and the dot product of its two vectors.
items.statement:
theorem toConcrete_accumulateProducts {n : ℕ} (init : FastBT128)
    (a b : Vector FastBT128 n) :
    toConcrete (Vector.accumulateProducts (· * ·) init a b) =
      toConcrete init + Vector.dotProduct (a.map toConcrete) (b.map toConcrete)

items.name: ConcreteBinaryTower.Fast.FastBT128.toConcrete_evalWithProducts
items.doc:
Eager packed coefficient evaluation, followed by conversion to the concrete tower,
agrees with evaluating the converted coefficients at the converted point.
items.statement:
theorem toConcrete_evalWithProducts {n : ℕ} (p : CMlPolynomial FastBT128 n)
    (x : Vector FastBT128 n) :
    toConcrete (CMlPolynomial.evalWithProducts (· * ·) (AddMonoidHom.id FastBT128) p x) =
      CMlPolynomial.eval (CMlPolynomial.map ringEquiv.toRingHom p) (x.map toConcrete)

modules.title: Fast binary tower: runtime definitions (zero-import)
modules.doc:
The runtime definitions of the packed binary tower arithmetic, split out of
`CompPoly.Fields.Binary.Tower.Fast` verbatim. All correctness statements about them
live in that sibling module, which imports this one.

This module deliberately has **zero imports**: downstream consumers put it into
`precompileModules` native-compilation lanes, and `precompileModules` compiles the
entire import closure, so the runtime definitions must not pull in mathlib.

items.note:
## Raw word operations

Names carry the operand bit width (`mul8` multiplies level-3 values in the low 8 bits);
`mulByZk` multiplies by the tower generator `Z k`. A multiplication rung recombines the
Karatsuba half-products `p0 = a₀b₀`, `p2 = a₁b₁`, `p1 = (a₀+a₁)(b₀+b₁)` as
`lo = p0 + p2`, `hi = p1 + lo + Z·p2`; squaring drops the cross term; inversion is the
quadratic descent of `concrete_inv`. Inputs are assumed in range.

modules.title: Binary Tower Fin Helpers
modules.doc: Finite-index helper lemmas for bit manipulations used in binary tower proofs.

items.name: bit_finProdFinEquiv_symm_2_pow_succ
items.statement:
theorem bit_finProdFinEquiv_symm_2_pow_succ {n : ℕ} (j : Fin (2 ^ (n + 1))) (i : Fin (n + 1)) :
    let e := (finProdFinEquiv (m := 2 ^ n) (n := 2)).symm
    let j' : Fin (2 ^ n * 2) := Fin.cast (Nat.pow_succ 2 n) j
    Nat.getBit (i) j = if i.val > 0 then Nat.getBit (i.val-1) (e j').1 else (e j').2

items.name: leftDivNat
items.doc:
Equivalence between `Fin m × Fin n` and `Fin (m * n)`
which splits quotient part into Fin (n) and the remainder into Fin (m).
If m and n are powers of 2, the Fin (n) holds MSBs and Fin (m) holds LSBs.
This is a reversed version of `finProdFinEquiv`.
We put `m` before `n` for integration with `Basis.smulTower` in `multilinearBasis`
though it's a bit counter-intuitive.
items.statement: def leftDivNat {m n : ℕ} (i : Fin (m * n)) : Fin n

items.name: leftModNat
items.statement: def leftModNat {m n : ℕ} (h_m : m > 0) (i : Fin (m * n)) : Fin m

items.name: revFinProdFinEquiv
items.statement: def revFinProdFinEquiv {m n : ℕ} (h_m : m > 0) : Fin m × Fin n ≃ Fin (m * n)

items.name: bit_revFinProdFinEquiv_symm_2_pow_succ
items.statement:
theorem bit_revFinProdFinEquiv_symm_2_pow_succ {n : ℕ} (j : Fin (2 ^ (n + 1))) (i : Fin (n + 1)) :
    let e : Fin (2 ^ n * 2) ≃ Fin (2 ^ n) × Fin 2 :=
      (revFinProdFinEquiv (m := 2 ^ n) (n := 2) (h_m := Nat.two_pow_pos n)).symm
    let j' : Fin (2 ^ n * 2) := Fin.cast (Nat.pow_succ 2 n) j
    let msb : Fin 2 := (e j').2
    let lsbs : Fin (2 ^ n) := (e j').1
    Nat.getBit (i) j = if i.val < n then Nat.getBit (i.val) lsbs else msb

items.name: GaloisAutomorphism
items.doc:
Galois automorphism properties for a special element in a binary tower field.
Encapsulates the key relationship : u^(2^(2^k)) = u⁻¹ and (u⁻¹)^(2^(2^k)) = u
items.statement:
structure GaloisAutomorphism (F : Type*) [Field F] (u : F) (k : ℕ) : Prop where
  forward : u ^ (2 ^ (2 ^ k)) = u⁻¹
  reverse : (u⁻¹) ^ (2 ^ (2 ^ k)) = u

items.name: TraceMapProperty
items.doc:
Trace map properties for elements in a binary tower field extension.
Asserts that the trace of both an element and its inverse equals 1.
items.statement:
structure TraceMapProperty (F : Type*) [Field F] (u : F) (k : ℕ) : Prop where
  element_trace : ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (2 ^ k), u ^ (2 ^ i) = 1
  inverse_trace : ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (2 ^ k), (u⁻¹) ^ (2 ^ i) = 1

items.name: SpecialElementRelation
items.doc:
Special element relationship in binary tower fields.
Captures the key equation : u + u⁻¹ = t₁ (lifted previous special element)
items.statement:
structure SpecialElementRelation {F_prev : Type*} [Field F_prev] (t1 : F_prev)
  {F_cur : Type*} [Field F_cur] (u : F_cur) [Algebra F_prev F_cur] : Prop where
    sum_inv_eq : u + u⁻¹ = algebraMap F_prev F_cur t1
    h_u_square : u^2 = u * (algebraMap F_prev F_cur t1) + 1

modules.title: Computable field extensions
modules.doc:
Facade for the field-extension stack. Extensions are `F[X] / f` for an arbitrary monic modulus
`f`; the binomial case `f = X^d - W` is the special case `BinomialParams.toExtensionParams`. See the
individual modules for details:

* `CompPoly/Fields/Extension/Binomial.lean` — irreducibility of `X^d - W` over a finite field,
  via Rabin's test collapsed to two base-field exponentiations.
* `CompPoly/Fields/Extension/Arithmetic.lean` — `ExtensionParams` (an arbitrary monic modulus), the
  binomial front-end `BinomialParams`, plus the coefficient-vector carrier `Ext P` with its ring
  operations (`shiftReduce`, `monomialMod`, `mul`) and the inverse candidate.
* `CompPoly/Fields/Extension/Defs.lean` — polynomial specifications and binomial correspondence.
* `CompPoly/Fields/Extension/Bridge.lean` — `toQuot : Ext P → AdjoinRoot P.poly`, the
  multiply-by-`X` law `toQuot_shiftReduce`, and the `CommRing` structure.
* `CompPoly/Fields/Extension/Cardinality.lean` — optional finiteness and cardinality certificates.
* `CompPoly/Fields/Extension/Field.lean` — bijectivity and the certified `Field` structure.

modules.title: Computable arithmetic for monic quotient presentations
modules.doc:
`ExtensionParams F` stores the degree, lower modulus coefficients and an explicit inverse-exponent
parameter `q`. `Ext P` is one nominal carrier with coefficient vectors in ascending degree order.
Its coordinate maps require no algebraic structure; arithmetic uses a ring of coefficients.
The presentation index separates parameter values for a fixed coefficient algebra. Operations
and their theorems are relative to the supplied ring or field structure on `F`; the raw carrier
does not separate alternative algebra structures on that same type. Distinct coefficient
presentations should use nominal coefficient types and explicit ring maps. The polynomial quotient
interpretation uses commutative coefficients; the raw formulas are defined for any ring.

Multiplication reduces monomials with `shiftReduce`. The executable reduction-table implementation
`mulTbl` is connected to `mul` by `mul_eq_mulTbl`. Power uses binary exponentiation, and the
canonical inverse candidate uses the literal exponent `q^d - 2`.

This module supplies no cardinality or irreducibility certificate. Polynomial specifications and
quotient correspondence belong to `Extension/Defs.lean` and `Extension/Bridge.lean`; certified field
laws belong to `Extension/Field.lean`. Raw parameters with an incorrect `q` still admit arithmetic
but do not thereby acquire field laws. The binomial conversion describes the modulus `X^d - W`.

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.ExtensionParams
items.doc:
The data defining an extension `F[X] / f` by a monic modulus `f` of degree `d`.

The modulus is stored by its `d` lower coefficients: `f = X^d + ∑_{i < d} lower[i] · X^i`. The
leading coefficient is an implicit `1`, so `f` is monic by construction.

Irreducibility is not part of these parameters: the quotient is a commutative ring for every
monic modulus over a commutative ring. Field laws additionally require finite-cardinality and
irreducibility certificates.
items.statement:
structure ExtensionParams (F : Type*) where
  /-- The degree of the extension. -/
  d : ℕ
  /-- Degree at least two; a degree-one "extension" is just `F`. -/
  two_le : 2 ≤ d
  /-- The lower coefficients of the monic modulus, little-endian: `lower[i]` is the coefficient
  of `X^i` in `poly`, for `i < d`. The coefficient of `X^d` is an implicit `1`. -/
  lower : Vector F d
  /-- The proposed base cardinality, stored explicitly for the inverse exponent.

  Raw arithmetic does not certify this value. Field laws require a separate proof that
  `Nat.card F = q`, together with finiteness and irreducibility. -/
  q : ℕ

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.ExtensionParams.lowerCoeff
items.doc: The coefficient of `X^i` in the lower part of the modulus.
items.statement: def lowerCoeff (i : Fin P.d) : F

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.ExtensionParams.lowerCoeffNat
items.doc: The lower modulus coefficient at index `k`, or zero when `P.d ≤ k`.
items.statement: def lowerCoeffNat (k : ℕ) : F

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.ExtensionParams.lowerCoeffNat_coe
items.statement: theorem lowerCoeffNat_coe (i : Fin P.d) : P.lowerCoeffNat (i : ℕ) = P.lowerCoeff i

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.ExtensionParams.lowerCoeffNat_of_ge
items.statement: theorem lowerCoeffNat_of_ge {k : ℕ} (h : P.d ≤ k) : P.lowerCoeffNat k = 0

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.ExtensionParams.d_pos
items.statement: theorem d_pos : 0 < P.d

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext
items.doc:
The carrier of the quotient by the monic modulus in `P`, with coefficients in ascending
order of powers. The parameter remains part of the type even when two moduli have equal degree.
items.statement:
structure Ext {F : Type*} (P : ExtensionParams F) : Type _ where
  /-- The coefficient of `X^i` is stored at index `i`. -/
  coeffs : Vector F P.d

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.ofVector
items.doc: Build an element from coefficients in ascending order of powers.
items.statement: def ofVector (v : Vector F P.d) : Ext P

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.coeffs_ofVector
items.doc: Extracting the coefficients of a constructed element returns the input vector.
items.statement: theorem coeffs_ofVector (v : Vector F P.d) : coeffs (ofVector (P := P) v) = v

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.ofVector_coeffs
items.doc: Reconstructing an element from its coefficient vector returns that element.
items.statement: theorem ofVector_coeffs (x : Ext P) : ofVector (coeffs x) = x

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.coeffs_injective
items.doc: The coefficient vector uniquely determines an element.
items.statement: theorem coeffs_injective : Function.Injective (coeffs (P := P))

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.ofFn
items.doc: Build an element from a coefficient function.
items.statement: def ofFn (g : Fin P.d → F) : Ext P

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.coeff
items.doc: The coefficient of `X^i`.
items.statement: def coeff (x : Ext P) (i : Fin P.d) : F

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.coeff_ofFn
items.statement: theorem coeff_ofFn (g : Fin P.d → F) (i : Fin P.d) : coeff (ofFn g) i = g i

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.ext
items.doc: Two elements with the same coefficients are equal.
items.statement: theorem ext {x y : Ext P} (h : ∀ i, coeff x i = coeff y i) : x = y

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.ofFn_coeff
items.statement: theorem ofFn_coeff (x : Ext P) : ofFn (coeff x) = x

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.equivFn
items.doc: Coefficient vectors are exactly functions out of `Fin d`.
items.statement: def equivFn (P : ExtensionParams F) : Ext P ≃ (Fin P.d → F)

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.coeffNat
items.doc: The coefficient at index `i`, or zero when `P.d ≤ i`.
items.statement: def coeffNat (x : Ext P) (i : ℕ) : F

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.coeffNat_coe
items.statement: theorem coeffNat_coe (x : Ext P) (i : Fin P.d) : coeffNat x (i : ℕ) = coeff x i

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.coeffNat_of_lt
items.statement: theorem coeffNat_of_lt (x : Ext P) {i : ℕ} (h : i < P.d) : coeffNat x i = coeff x ⟨i, h⟩

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.coeffNat_of_ge
items.statement: theorem coeffNat_of_ge (x : Ext P) {i : ℕ} (h : P.d ≤ i) : coeffNat x i = 0

items.note:
### Distinguished elements

`ofBase` places a coefficient-ring element in the constant coordinate, and `gen` has the
coordinates of `X`. The quotient bridge over a field promotes the constant embedding to an
`Algebra` structure and identifies the reduced power `gen ^ d` with `monomialMod d`.

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.ofBase
items.doc: Place a coefficient-ring element in the constant coordinate.
items.statement: def ofBase (c : F) : Ext P

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.gen
items.doc: The coordinate vector with coefficient one at `X` and zero elsewhere.
items.statement: def gen : Ext P

items.note:
### Operations

Multiplication is defined in terms of `shiftReduce` — the "multiply by `X`, reduce mod `f`"
map — whose iterates `monomialMod k = shiftReduce^[k] 1` are the reduced monomials `X^k mod f`.
Everything downstream is proved from the single homomorphism law
`toQuot (shiftReduce e) = rt * toQuot e`.

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.shiftReduce
items.doc:
Multiply by `X` and reduce modulo `f`.

`X · (∑ eᵢ Xⁱ) = ∑ eᵢ X^(i+1)`, whose top term `e_{d-1} X^d` wraps via `X^d = -∑ lowerₘ Xᵐ`.
So coefficient `m` of the reduced result is `e_{m-1} - e_{d-1} · lowerₘ`, with `e_{-1} = 0`.
This is the single linear map whose iterates build the reduction table `red`.
items.statement: def shiftReduce (e : Ext P) : Ext P

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.monomialMod
items.doc:
The reduced form of `X^k` modulo `f`, obtained by iterating `shiftReduce` (multiply by `X`,
reduce) `k` times from `1 = X^0`. Its image under `toQuot` is `rt ^ k`.
items.statement: def monomialMod (k : ℕ) : Ext P

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.mul
items.doc:
The monic-reduction product formula, representing multiplication in `F[X] / f`
when the coefficient ring is commutative.

Each product monomial `Xⁱ⁺ʲ` is reduced modulo `f` by `monomialMod (i + j)`, so coefficient `m`
of the product collects `xᵢ · yⱼ · [X^(i+j) mod f]ₘ` over all pairs `(i, j)`.
items.statement: def mul (x y : Ext P) : Ext P

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.redScan
items.doc:
Append `cur, shiftReduce cur, …`, `n` entries in all, to `acc`; the scan that builds `red`.
This is the table the `shiftReduce` docstring above refers to.
items.statement: def redScan : ℕ → Ext P → Array (Ext P) → Array (Ext P)

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.redScan_size
items.statement:
theorem redScan_size (n : ℕ) (cur : Ext P) (acc : Array (Ext P)) :
    (redScan n cur acc).size = acc.size + n

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.redScan_getElem
items.doc: Entry `k` of the scan is `shiftReduce^[k - acc.size] cur` past the prefix it was given.
items.statement:
theorem redScan_getElem (n : ℕ) (cur : Ext P) (acc : Array (Ext P)) (k : ℕ)
    (h : k < (redScan n cur acc).size) :
    (redScan n cur acc)[k] =
      if hlt : k < acc.size then acc[k] else shiftReduce^[k - acc.size] cur

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.red
items.doc:
The reduction table: `red P` holds `X^k mod f` for every `k ≤ 2d - 2`, i.e. every exponent a
product of two reduced elements can reach.

Built by one `redScan` from `1`, so the whole table costs `O(d^2)`; `Vector.ofFn (monomialMod ·)`
would iterate `shiftReduce` from scratch for every entry, `O(d^3)` in all. It exists purely for
speed: `mul` is the specification, and `mulTbl` below is the compiled implementation that
consults this table.
items.statement: def red (P : ExtensionParams F) : Vector (Ext P) (2 * P.d - 1)

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.red_getElem
items.statement:
theorem red_getElem {k : ℕ} (hk : k < 2 * P.d - 1) :
    (red P)[k] = monomialMod k

items.name: Fin.foldl_add_eq_add_sum
items.doc:
A left fold that adds `f i` at each step is `a` plus the sum; the bridge from the loops the
compiler runs to the `Finset.sum`s the specification is stated with.
items.statement:
theorem _root_.Fin.foldl_add_eq_add_sum {M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M] {n : ℕ} (f : Fin n → M)
    (a : M) : Fin.foldl n (fun acc i => acc + f i) a = a + ∑ i, f i

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.convCoeff
items.doc:
Coefficient `k` of the unreduced product `x · y` in `F[X]`, the convolution `∑_{i + j = k} xᵢ yⱼ`,
as one loop over `i` with `j = k - i`; a pair outside `[0, d)` contributes zero. `k` ranges over
`[0, 2d - 1)`, the degrees a product of two reduced elements can reach.

Deliberately a separate function over its own `Mul` and `Add` instances, `@[noinline]` and
`@[nospecialize]`, and likewise `contractCoeff` below. Written inside `mulTbl`, or inlined or
specialised on the `Ring F` instance, `*` and `+` on `F` are re-derived from the ring dictionary
on every step of the innermost loop, through projections that allocate an intermediate structure
each time; the emitted C of the first loop run had `instDistribOfSemiring` in the loop body.
Here the two operations arrive as arguments, derived once per call of `mulTbl`, and the loop
only applies them. (`nospecialize` matters: instance arguments are specialised even without
`@[specialize]` on the callee.)
items.statement: def convCoeff [Mul F] [Add F] [Zero F] (x y : Ext P) (k : ℕ) (init : F) : F

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.contractCoeff
items.doc:
Coefficient `m` of the reduction of the unreduced product `prod` against the table `tbl`:
`∑_k prodₖ · [X^k mod f]ₘ`. See `convCoeff` for why this is a separate function.
items.statement:
def contractCoeff [Mul F] [Add F] (tbl : Vector (Ext P) (2 * P.d - 1))
    (prod : Vector F (2 * P.d - 1)) (m : Fin P.d) (init : F) : F

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.mulTbl
items.doc:
Table-driven multiplication: the compiled implementation of `mul`.

Mathematically identical to `mul`, in two stages: the unreduced product `x · y` in `F[X]`,
`2d - 1` coefficients by `convCoeff`, then one contraction of those against the reduction table
`red` by `contractCoeff`. That is `d^2 + (2d - 1) d` coefficient multiplications where `mul`
performs `d^3`, and the reduced monomials come from the table instead of being re-derived by
`monomialMod` for every output coefficient. The sums are `Fin.foldl` loops rather than
`Finset.sum`, which compiles to list-building `Multiset` machinery.

`mul` remains the definition everything is proved about; `mul_eq_mulTbl` below swaps this in for
compilation via `@[csimp]`. The loops live in `convCoeff` and `contractCoeff`, for the reason
given there.

Specialised on `P` as well as on the instances: at a call site whose modulus is a constant, which
is every concrete extension field, the table `red P` is then a closed term the compiler
evaluates once, rather than being rebuilt on every multiplication.
items.statement: def mulTbl (x y : Ext P) : Ext P

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.convCoeff_zero
items.doc: `convCoeff` from zero is the convolution sum, with the second index as a `coeffNat`.
items.statement:
theorem convCoeff_zero (x y : Ext P) (k : ℕ) :
    convCoeff x y k 0 = ∑ i : Fin P.d,
      if (i : ℕ) ≤ k ∧ k - (i : ℕ) < P.d then coeff x i * coeffNat y (k - (i : ℕ)) else 0

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.sum_fin_add_eq_sum_fin_ite
items.doc:
The reindexing behind `mul_eq_mulTbl`: summing `g (i + j)` over `j < d` is summing `g k` over
the `k < 2d - 1` that `i + j` reaches, for a fixed `i < d`.
items.statement:
theorem sum_fin_add_eq_sum_fin_ite {M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M] {d : ℕ} (i : Fin d)
    (g : ℕ → M) :
    ∑ j : Fin d, g ((i : ℕ) + (j : ℕ)) =
      ∑ k : Fin (2 * d - 1), if (i : ℕ) ≤ (k : ℕ) ∧ (k : ℕ) - (i : ℕ) < d then g k else 0

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.mul_eq_mulTbl
items.statement: theorem mul_eq_mulTbl : @mul = @mulTbl

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.coeff_zero
items.statement: theorem coeff_zero (i : Fin P.d) : coeff (0 : Ext P) i = 0

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.coeff_one
items.statement:
theorem coeff_one (i : Fin P.d) :
    coeff (1 : Ext P) i = if (i : ℕ) = 0 then 1 else 0

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.coeff_add
items.statement:
theorem coeff_add (x y : Ext P) (i : Fin P.d) :
    coeff (x + y) i = coeff x i + coeff y i

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.coeff_neg
items.statement: theorem coeff_neg (x : Ext P) (i : Fin P.d) : coeff (-x) i = -coeff x i

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.coeff_sub
items.statement:
theorem coeff_sub (x y : Ext P) (i : Fin P.d) :
    coeff (x - y) i = coeff x i - coeff y i

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.coeff_smul
items.statement:
theorem coeff_smul (c : F) (x : Ext P) (i : Fin P.d) :
    coeff (c • x) i = c * coeff x i

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.coeff_shiftReduce
items.statement:
theorem coeff_shiftReduce (e : Ext P) (m : Fin P.d) :
    coeff (shiftReduce e) m =
      (if (m : ℕ) = 0 then 0 else coeffNat e ((m : ℕ) - 1))
        - coeffNat e (P.d - 1) * P.lowerCoeff m

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.coeff_mul
items.statement:
theorem coeff_mul (x y : Ext P) (m : Fin P.d) :
    coeff (x * y) m =
      ∑ i : Fin P.d, ∑ j : Fin P.d,
        coeff x i * coeff y j * coeff (monomialMod ((i : ℕ) + (j : ℕ))) m

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.coeff_ofBase
items.statement:
theorem coeff_ofBase (c : F) (i : Fin P.d) :
    coeff (ofBase (P := P) c) i = if (i : ℕ) = 0 then c else 0

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.coeff_gen
items.statement:
theorem coeff_gen (i : Fin P.d) :
    coeff (gen : Ext P) i = if (i : ℕ) = 1 then 1 else 0

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.ofBase_one
items.doc: `ofBase` agrees with `1` on the multiplicative unit.
items.statement: theorem ofBase_one : ofBase (P := P) (1 : F) = 1

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.ofBase_zero
items.doc: `ofBase` agrees with `0`.
items.statement: theorem ofBase_zero : ofBase (P := P) (0 : F) = 0

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.ofBase_natCast
items.doc: `ofBase` agrees with the `ℕ`-cast, so scalars and numerals do not diverge.
items.statement: theorem ofBase_natCast (n : ℕ) : ofBase (P := P) (n : F) = (n : Ext P)

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.ofBase_intCast
items.doc: `ofBase` agrees with the `ℤ`-cast.
items.statement: theorem ofBase_intCast (n : ℤ) : ofBase (P := P) (n : F) = (n : Ext P)

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.coeff_natCast
items.statement:
theorem coeff_natCast (n : ℕ) (i : Fin P.d) :
    coeff (n : Ext P) i = if (i : ℕ) = 0 then (n : F) else 0

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.coeff_intCast
items.statement:
theorem coeff_intCast (n : ℤ) (i : Fin P.d) :
    coeff (n : Ext P) i = if (i : ℕ) = 0 then (n : F) else 0

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.pow_def
items.statement: theorem pow_def (x : Ext P) (n : ℕ) : x ^ n = npowBinRec n x

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.inv
items.doc:
The canonical inverse candidate `x ^ (q^d - 2)`.

Inverse laws require finite-cardinality and irreducibility certificates. For arbitrary `q`,
this operation need not send zero to zero.
items.statement: def inv (x : Ext P) : Ext P

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.instInv
items.statement: instance instInv : Inv (Ext P)

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.instDiv
items.statement: instance instDiv : Div (Ext P)

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.inv_def
items.statement: theorem inv_def (x : Ext P) : x⁻¹ = x ^ (P.q ^ P.d - 2)

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.div_def
items.statement: theorem div_def (x y : Ext P) : x / y = x * y⁻¹

items.note:
### Binomial extensions as a special case

A binomial extension `F[X] / (X^d - W)` is the case `lower = (-W, 0, …, 0)`. `BinomialParams`
keeps the `W`-only interface; `toExtensionParams` maps it into the general framework. The
polynomial correspondence and binomial irreducibility criterion are proved separately.

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.BinomialParams
items.doc:
Parameters for the quotient `F[X] / (X^d - W)`: the degree, constant `W`, and a proposed
base cardinality. The modulus has lower coefficients `(-W, 0, …, 0)`.
items.statement:
structure BinomialParams (F : Type*) where
  /-- The degree of the extension. -/
  d : ℕ
  /-- The extension adjoins a `d`-th root of `W`. -/
  W : F
  /-- Degree at least two; a degree-one "extension" is just `F`. -/
  two_le : 2 ≤ d
  /-- The proposed base cardinality used by the inverse exponent. -/
  q : ℕ

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.BinomialParams.d_pos
items.statement: theorem d_pos : 0 < P.d

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.BinomialParams.toExtensionParams
items.doc:
The general-framework parameters for the binomial modulus `X^d - W`: the lower coefficient
vector is `(-W, 0, …, 0)`.
items.statement: def toExtensionParams : ExtensionParams F

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.BinomialParams.toExtensionParams_d
items.statement: theorem toExtensionParams_d : P.toExtensionParams.d = P.d

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.BinomialParams.toExtensionParams_q
items.statement: theorem toExtensionParams_q : P.toExtensionParams.q = P.q

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.BinomialParams.toExtensionParams_lowerCoeff
items.statement:
theorem toExtensionParams_lowerCoeff (i : Fin P.toExtensionParams.d) :
    P.toExtensionParams.lowerCoeff i = if (i : ℕ) = 0 then -P.W else 0

modules.title: Irreducibility of binomials `X^d - W` over a finite field
modules.doc:
Applying Rabin's test (`CompPoly/Data/Polynomial/Rabin.lean`) to a *binomial* defining
polynomial collapses both conditions into single exponentiations **in the base field**.

The reason is that `X^d ≡ W`, so whenever `d ∣ N - 1`, writing `k = (N-1)/d`,

`X^N - X = X * (X^(d*k) - 1)`  and  `X^(d*k) ≡ W^k  (mod X^d - W)`.

Hence `X^d - W` divides `X^N - X` exactly when `W^k = 1`, and is coprime to it exactly when
`W^k ≠ 1`: the residue is then `X * C (W^k - 1)`, a unit multiple of `X`, and `X` does not
divide `X^d - W` because `W ≠ 0`.

Instantiating at `N = q^d` and `N = q^(d/ℓ)` turns Rabin's test into
`irreducible_X_pow_sub_C_iff`, whose conditions are two base-field exponentiations. Contrast
the ~2100 lines of hand-generated `BitVec` step certificates in
`CompPoly/Fields/Binary/BF128Ghash/XPowTwoPow{Mod,Gcd}Certificate.lean`, which is what the
same test costs when the defining polynomial is not a binomial.

## Main statements

* `Polynomial.X_pow_sub_C_dvd_X_pow_sub_X` / `Polynomial.isCoprime_X_pow_sub_C_X_pow_sub_X`:
  the two collapsed Rabin conditions, and their converses.
* `Polynomial.irreducible_X_pow_sub_C_iff`: the criterion for general `d`.
* `Polynomial.irreducible_X_pow_four_sub_C`: the `d = 4` corollary, which discharges
  `Nat.primeFactors` internally. This is the degree used by BabyBear, KoalaBear and Hachi
  extension fields.

Both take the field size as a numeral `q` together with `Fintype.card F = q`, as everything in
the Rabin layer does; pass `rfl` if you have no numeral.

## References

* [Rabin80] Michael O. Rabin, *Probabilistic Algorithms in Finite Fields*,
  SIAM Journal on Computing 9(2), 1980.
* [LN97] Rudolf Lidl and Harald Niederreiter, *Finite Fields*, 2nd ed., Theorem 3.75.

items.note: ### Reducing powers of `X` modulo a binomial

items.name: Polynomial.X_pow_sub_C_dvd_X_pow_mul_sub_C_pow
items.doc:
`X^d - C W` divides `X^(d * k) - C (W ^ k)`.

This is the algebraic content of "substituting `X^d = W`": apply `a - b ∣ a^k - b^k` with
`a = X^d` and `b = C W`.
items.statement:
theorem X_pow_sub_C_dvd_X_pow_mul_sub_C_pow (W : F) (d k : ℕ) :
    (X ^ d - C W) ∣ X ^ (d * k) - C (W ^ k)

items.name: Polynomial.not_X_dvd_X_pow_sub_C
items.doc: `X` does not divide `X^d - C W` when `W ≠ 0`: the constant coefficient is `-W`.
items.statement:
theorem not_X_dvd_X_pow_sub_C {W : F} {d : ℕ} (hd : 0 < d) (hW : W ≠ 0) :
    ¬ (X : F[X]) ∣ X ^ d - C W

items.name: Polynomial.X_pow_sub_C_dvd_X_pow_sub_X
items.doc:
**Rabin condition 1, collapsed.** If `d ∣ N - 1` and `W ^ ((N-1)/d) = 1`, then
`X^d - C W` divides `X^N - X`.
items.statement:
theorem X_pow_sub_C_dvd_X_pow_sub_X {W : F} {d N : ℕ} (hd : 0 < d) (hN : 1 ≤ N)
    (hdvd : d ∣ N - 1) (hW : W ^ ((N - 1) / d) = 1) :
    (X ^ d - C W) ∣ X ^ N - X

items.name: Polynomial.isCoprime_X_pow_sub_C_X_pow_sub_X
items.doc:
**Rabin condition 2, collapsed.** If `d ∣ N - 1`, `W ≠ 0` and `W ^ ((N-1)/d) ≠ 1`, then
`X^d - C W` is coprime to `X^N - X`.

Modulo `X^d - C W` the polynomial `X^N - X` reduces to `X * C (W^k - 1)`, a unit multiple of
`X`, and `X` is coprime to `X^d - C W` by `not_X_dvd_X_pow_sub_C`.
items.statement:
theorem isCoprime_X_pow_sub_C_X_pow_sub_X {W : F} {d N : ℕ} (hd : 0 < d) (hW0 : W ≠ 0)
    (hN : 1 ≤ N) (hdvd : d ∣ N - 1) (hW : W ^ ((N - 1) / d) ≠ 1) :
    IsCoprime (X ^ d - C W) (X ^ N - X)

items.name: Polynomial.eq_one_of_X_pow_sub_C_dvd_X_pow_sub_X
items.doc: Converse of `X_pow_sub_C_dvd_X_pow_sub_X`: divisibility forces `W ^ ((N-1)/d) = 1`.
items.statement:
theorem eq_one_of_X_pow_sub_C_dvd_X_pow_sub_X {W : F} {d N : ℕ} (hd : 0 < d) (hW0 : W ≠ 0)
    (hN : 1 ≤ N) (hdvd : d ∣ N - 1) (h : (X ^ d - C W) ∣ X ^ N - X) :
    W ^ ((N - 1) / d) = 1

items.name: Polynomial.ne_one_of_isCoprime_X_pow_sub_C_X_pow_sub_X
items.doc: Converse of `isCoprime_X_pow_sub_C_X_pow_sub_X`: coprimality forces `W ^ ((N-1)/d) ≠ 1`.
items.statement:
theorem ne_one_of_isCoprime_X_pow_sub_C_X_pow_sub_X {W : F} {d N : ℕ} (hd : 0 < d) (hN : 1 ≤ N)
    (hdvd : d ∣ N - 1) (h : IsCoprime ((X : F[X]) ^ d - C W) (X ^ N - X)) :
    W ^ ((N - 1) / d) ≠ 1

items.note:
### The irreducibility criterion

Each statement takes the field size as a numeral `q` with `hcard : Fintype.card F = q`, matching
`Polynomial.irreducible_of_rabin`; a concrete field supplies `ZMod.card _` and a caller with no
numeral passes `rfl`. The section comment in `CompPoly/Data/Polynomial/Rabin.lean` says why.

items.name: Polynomial.irreducible_X_pow_sub_C_iff
items.doc:
**Irreducibility criterion for binomials.**

Over a finite field with `q` elements, `X^d - W` is irreducible if and only if
`W^((q^d - 1)/d) = 1` and `W^((q^(d/ℓ) - 1)/d) ≠ 1` for every prime `ℓ ∣ d`.

The divisibility side conditions `h_top` and `h_mid` hold in every case of interest — for
`d = 4` and `q ≡ 1 mod 4`, for instance — and are decidable arithmetic facts about `q` and `d`.
items.statement:
theorem irreducible_X_pow_sub_C_iff {d q : ℕ} {W : F} (hcard : Fintype.card F = q)
    (hd : 0 < d) (hW0 : W ≠ 0)
    (h_top : d ∣ q ^ d - 1)
    (h_mid : ∀ ℓ ∈ d.primeFactors, d ∣ q ^ (d / ℓ) - 1) :
    Irreducible ((X : F[X]) ^ d - C W) ↔
      (W ^ ((q ^ d - 1) / d) = 1 ∧
        ∀ ℓ ∈ d.primeFactors, W ^ ((q ^ (d / ℓ) - 1) / d) ≠ 1)

items.name: Polynomial.irreducible_X_pow_sub_C
items.doc: The `mpr` direction of `irreducible_X_pow_sub_C_iff`, as a standalone lemma.
items.statement:
theorem irreducible_X_pow_sub_C {d q : ℕ} {W : F} (hcard : Fintype.card F = q)
    (hd : 0 < d) (hW0 : W ≠ 0)
    (h_top : d ∣ q ^ d - 1)
    (h_mid : ∀ ℓ ∈ d.primeFactors, d ∣ q ^ (d / ℓ) - 1)
    (rabin_top : W ^ ((q ^ d - 1) / d) = 1)
    (rabin_mid : ∀ ℓ ∈ d.primeFactors, W ^ ((q ^ (d / ℓ) - 1) / d) ≠ 1) :
    Irreducible ((X : F[X]) ^ d - C W)

items.name: Polynomial.irreducible_X_pow_four_sub_C_iff
items.doc:
**Irreducibility criterion for quartic binomials.**

`X^4 - W` is irreducible over a finite field with `q` elements exactly when
`W^((q^4 - 1)/4) = 1` and `W^((q^2 - 1)/4) ≠ 1`.

This is the shape used by the BabyBear, KoalaBear and Hachi degree-4 extensions. It differs
from `irreducible_X_pow_sub_C_iff` only in discharging `Nat.primeFactors 4 = {2}` internally,
so callers never touch `Nat.primeFactors`.

Being an `iff`, a *failed* check proves reducibility rather than merely failing to prove
irreducibility.

Concrete fields are defined as `ZMod fieldSize` where `fieldSize` is an *expression* such as
`2 ^ 31 - 2 ^ 24 + 1`, and the hypotheses are stated at the numeral `q`, which is what lets a
caller discharge them with `norm_num` and `reduce_mod_char`. `reduce_mod_char` still needs to see
the *type* as `ZMod <numeral>`, so the two exponentiation goals are usually preceded by a `show`;
see `CompPoly/Fields/KoalaBear/Ext4.lean` for the idiom.
items.statement:
theorem irreducible_X_pow_four_sub_C_iff {q : ℕ} {W : F} (hcard : Fintype.card F = q)
    (hW0 : W ≠ 0) (h_top : 4 ∣ q ^ 4 - 1) (h_mid : 4 ∣ q ^ 2 - 1) :
    Irreducible ((X : F[X]) ^ 4 - C W) ↔
      (W ^ ((q ^ 4 - 1) / 4) = 1 ∧ W ^ ((q ^ 2 - 1) / 4) ≠ 1)

items.name: Polynomial.irreducible_X_pow_four_sub_C_iff_of_card
items.statement: alias irreducible_X_pow_four_sub_C_iff_of_card

items.name: Polynomial.irreducible_X_pow_four_sub_C
items.doc: The `mpr` direction of `irreducible_X_pow_four_sub_C_iff`, as a standalone lemma.
items.statement:
theorem irreducible_X_pow_four_sub_C {q : ℕ} {W : F} (hcard : Fintype.card F = q)
    (hW0 : W ≠ 0) (h_top : 4 ∣ q ^ 4 - 1) (h_mid : 4 ∣ q ^ 2 - 1)
    (rabin_top : W ^ ((q ^ 4 - 1) / 4) = 1)
    (rabin_mid : W ^ ((q ^ 2 - 1) / 4) ≠ 1) :
    Irreducible ((X : F[X]) ^ 4 - C W)

items.name: Polynomial.irreducible_X_pow_four_sub_C_of_card
items.statement: alias irreducible_X_pow_four_sub_C_of_card

modules.title: Bridging `Ext P` to `AdjoinRoot P.poly`
modules.doc:
The computable coefficient-vector arithmetic of `CompPoly/Fields/Extension/Defs.lean` is related
to its specification `AdjoinRoot f` by

`toQuot x = ∑ i, algebraMap F _ (x.coeff i) * root ^ i`,

which is shown to be an injective ring homomorphism. The ring axioms on `Ext P` are then
discharged by pushing through `toQuot` rather than proved on coordinates.

The load-bearing lemma is `toQuot_shiftReduce`: `shiftReduce` is "multiply by `X`, reduce mod
`f`", and correspondingly `toQuot (shiftReduce e) = rt * toQuot e`. Everything about
multiplication follows from it: `monomialMod k = X^k mod f` satisfies `toQuot (monomialMod k) =
rt ^ k` by a one-line induction, and `toQuot_mul` is then a direct double sum with no case
analysis on wrap-around.

## Main definitions and statements

* `Ext.toQuot`: the map to `AdjoinRoot P.poly`.
* `Ext.rt_relation`: the defining relation `rt ^ d = -∑ lowerᵢ rt ^ i`, from `AdjoinRoot.mk_self`.
* `Ext.toQuot_shiftReduce`: the multiply-by-`X` homomorphism law.
* `Ext.toQuot_mul`, `Ext.toQuot_add`, ...: `toQuot` is a ring homomorphism.
* `Ext.toQuot_injective`: injective for any monic modulus; irreducibility is not needed.
* `Ext.instCommRing`: the `CommRing` structure.
* `Ext.toQuotRingHom`: `toQuot` packaged as a `RingHom`.

Bijectivity, cardinality and the `Field` structure are in
`CompPoly/Fields/Extension/Field.lean`.

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.rt
items.doc: The image of `X` in the quotient, i.e. the adjoined root of `f`.
items.statement: noncomputable def rt (P : ExtensionParams F) : Quot[P]

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.degree_poly
items.doc: The degree of the defining polynomial, as a `WithBot ℕ`.
items.statement: theorem degree_poly : P.poly.degree = (P.d : WithBot ℕ)

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.toQuot
items.doc: The map from coefficient vectors to the quotient ring.
items.statement: noncomputable def toQuot (x : Ext P) : Quot[P]

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.toQuot_zero
items.statement: theorem toQuot_zero : toQuot (0 : Ext P) = 0

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.toQuot_add
items.statement: theorem toQuot_add (x y : Ext P) : toQuot (x + y) = toQuot x + toQuot y

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.toQuot_neg
items.statement: theorem toQuot_neg (x : Ext P) : toQuot (-x) = -toQuot x

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.toQuot_sub
items.statement: theorem toQuot_sub (x y : Ext P) : toQuot (x - y) = toQuot x - toQuot y

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.toQuot_smul
items.statement:
theorem toQuot_smul (c : F) (x : Ext P) :
    toQuot (c • x) = algebraMap F Quot[P] c * toQuot x

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.toQuot_one
items.doc: Only the constant coefficient of `1` is nonzero, so `toQuot 1` collapses to `1`.
items.statement: theorem toQuot_one : toQuot (1 : Ext P) = 1

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.toQuot_natCast
items.statement: theorem toQuot_natCast (n : ℕ) : toQuot (n : Ext P) = n

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.toQuot_intCast
items.statement: theorem toQuot_intCast (n : ℤ) : toQuot (n : Ext P) = n

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.toQuot_eq_mk
items.doc: `toQuot` as the class of an explicit degree-`< d` polynomial representative.
items.statement:
theorem toQuot_eq_mk (x : Ext P) :
    toQuot x = AdjoinRoot.mk P.poly (∑ i : Fin P.d, C (coeff x i) * X ^ (i : ℕ))

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.toQuot_injective
items.statement: theorem toQuot_injective : Function.Injective (toQuot (P := P))

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.toQuot_inj
items.statement: theorem toQuot_inj {x y : Ext P} : toQuot x = toQuot y ↔ x = y

items.note: ### The defining relation and the multiply-by-`X` homomorphism law

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.toQuot_rangeForm
items.doc:
`toQuot` as a sum over `Finset.range`, using the total `coeffNat`. Convenient for the shift
reindexing in `toQuot_shiftReduce`.
items.statement:
theorem toQuot_rangeForm (x : Ext P) :
    toQuot x = ∑ k ∈ Finset.range P.d, algebraMap F Quot[P] (coeffNat x k) * (rt P) ^ k

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.rt_relation
items.doc:
**The defining relation**, from `AdjoinRoot.mk_self`: the adjoined root `rt` satisfies
`rt ^ d + ∑ lowerᵢ · rt ^ i = 0`.
items.statement:
theorem rt_relation :
    (rt P) ^ P.d + ∑ i : Fin P.d, algebraMap F Quot[P] (P.lowerCoeff i) * (rt P) ^ (i : ℕ)
      = 0

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.sum_lower_rangeForm
items.doc: In `range` form: `∑_{m < d} lowerₘ · rt ^ m = -rt ^ d`.
items.statement:
theorem sum_lower_rangeForm :
    (∑ m ∈ Finset.range P.d, algebraMap F Quot[P] (P.lowerCoeffNat m) * (rt P) ^ m)
      = -(rt P) ^ P.d

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.coeffNat_shiftReduce
items.doc: The coefficient formula for `shiftReduce`, in `coeffNat` form.
items.statement:
theorem coeffNat_shiftReduce (e : Ext P) {m : ℕ} (h : m < P.d) :
    coeffNat (shiftReduce e) m
      = (if m = 0 then 0 else coeffNat e (m - 1)) - coeffNat e (P.d - 1) * P.lowerCoeffNat m

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.toQuot_shiftReduce
items.doc:
**The multiply-by-`X` homomorphism law.** `shiftReduce` is multiplication by `X` in the quotient,
so `toQuot (shiftReduce e) = rt * toQuot e`. This is the one place `rt_relation` is consumed, and
everything about multiplication reduces to it.
items.statement: theorem toQuot_shiftReduce (e : Ext P) : toQuot (shiftReduce e) = rt P * toQuot e

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.monomialMod_zero
items.statement: theorem monomialMod_zero : (monomialMod 0 : Ext P) = 1

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.monomialMod_succ
items.statement:
theorem monomialMod_succ (k : ℕ) :
    (monomialMod (k + 1) : Ext P) = shiftReduce (monomialMod k)

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.toQuot_monomialMod
items.doc: `monomialMod k` really is `X^k` reduced: its image under `toQuot` is `rt ^ k`.
items.statement: theorem toQuot_monomialMod (k : ℕ) : toQuot (monomialMod k : Ext P) = (rt P) ^ k

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.toQuot_mul
items.statement: theorem toQuot_mul (x y : Ext P) : toQuot (x * y) = toQuot x * toQuot y

items.note:
### Exponentiation

`x ^ n` on `Ext P` is `npowBinRec`, i.e. repeated squaring, so it costs `O(log n)`
multiplications. `npowBinRec_succ` needs only `Semigroup`, and associativity is already
available from `toQuot_mul` plus injectivity — so exponentiation can be handled before the full
ring structure is transported.

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.mul_assoc'
items.doc:
Associativity. Kept out of the instance graph as a plain theorem to avoid a `Semigroup`
diamond with the `CommRing` instance below.
items.statement: theorem mul_assoc' (x y z : Ext P) : x * y * z = x * (y * z)

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.toQuot_pow
items.statement: theorem toQuot_pow (x : Ext P) (n : ℕ) : toQuot (x ^ n) = toQuot x ^ n

items.note:
### Algebraic structure

The axioms are all discharged by pushing through the injective `toQuot`, but the instances are
built field-by-field with `where` rather than via `Function.Injective.commRing`. That transport
takes `toQuot` as *data*, which would make the resulting instance `noncomputable` and — because
`Monoid.toNatPow` then outranks `Ext.instPow` — would silently break compiled `x ^ n`. Building
by hand keeps every operation computable, matching how `CPolynomial` assembles its instances in
`CompPoly/Univariate/Basic.lean`.
