items.statement: instance instAddCommGroup : AddCommGroup (Ext P)

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.instCommRing
items.statement: instance instCommRing : CommRing (Ext P)

items.note: ### The base field and the adjoined root

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.toQuot_ofBase
items.doc: `ofBase` lands on the constant coefficient, so it agrees with `algebraMap` into the quotient.
items.statement:
theorem toQuot_ofBase (c : F) :
    toQuot (ofBase (P := P) c) = algebraMap F Quot[P] c

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.toQuot_gen
items.doc: `gen` is the class of `X`, i.e. the adjoined root.
items.statement: theorem toQuot_gen : toQuot (gen : Ext P) = rt P

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.ofBaseRingHom
items.doc: The base-field embedding, as a ring homomorphism.
items.statement: def ofBaseRingHom (P : ExtensionParams F) : F →+* Ext P

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.ofBaseRingHom_apply
items.statement: theorem ofBaseRingHom_apply (c : F) : ofBaseRingHom P c = ofBase c

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.instAlgebra
items.doc: The extension is an `F`-algebra.
items.statement: instance instAlgebra : Algebra F (Ext P)

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.algebraMap_eq_ofBase
items.statement: theorem algebraMap_eq_ofBase (c : F) : algebraMap F (Ext P) c = ofBase c

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.toQuot_sum
items.statement:
theorem toQuot_sum {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (f : ι → Ext P) :
    toQuot (∑ i ∈ s, f i) = ∑ i ∈ s, toQuot (f i)

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.gen_pow_d
items.doc:
**The defining relation** at the level of `Ext`: `gen ^ d` equals the reduced monomial
`monomialMod d`.
items.statement: theorem gen_pow_d : (gen : Ext P) ^ P.d = monomialMod P.d

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.aeval_gen_poly
items.doc: `gen` is a root of the defining polynomial, in the form Mathlib's `aeval` expects.
items.statement: theorem aeval_gen_poly : aeval (gen : Ext P) P.poly = 0

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.toQuotRingHom
items.doc: `toQuot` packaged as a ring homomorphism.
items.statement: noncomputable def toQuotRingHom (P : ExtensionParams F) : Ext P →+* Quot[P]

items.note:
### Binomial compatibility

For a binomial modulus `X^d - W`, the general defining relation `rt ^ d = -∑ lowerᵢ rt ^ i`
collapses (the only nonzero lower coefficient is `lower₀ = -W`) to `rt ^ d = W`, recovering the
`gen ^ d = ofBase W` law the degree-4 extensions rely on.

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.rt_pow_d_binomial
items.doc: The collapsed defining relation for a binomial modulus: `rt ^ d = W`.
items.statement:
theorem rt_pow_d_binomial (P : BinomialParams F) :
    (rt P.toExtensionParams) ^ P.d = algebraMap F Quot[P.toExtensionParams] P.W

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.gen_pow_d_binomial
items.doc: **The binomial defining relation** at the level of `Ext`: `gen ^ d = ofBase W`.
items.statement:
theorem gen_pow_d_binomial (P : BinomialParams F) :
    (gen : Ext P.toExtensionParams) ^ P.d = ofBase P.W

modules.title: Serialization of field extensions
modules.doc:
An element of `Ext P` is its coefficient vector, ascending powers of the adjoined root, and it
encodes as the concatenation of the coefficient encodings: `P.d * width F` bytes. This is how
arkworks and plonky3 serialize extension fields, and it is *not* the little-endian expansion of
the element's base-`q` canonical natural, which is why `Ext` carries a `ByteCodec` but no
`CanonicalNat`.

A challenge in `Ext P` is likewise read coefficient by coefficient from `P.d * k` bytes
(`Deserialize (Ext P) (Vector UInt8 (P.d * k))`), matching how a sponge over the base field
samples extension elements.

`CompPoly.Data.Bytes.CanonicalNat` is imported so that an extension of a `ZMod` base field
serializes with no further imports.

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.byteCodec_width
items.statement:
theorem byteCodec_width [ByteCodec F] :
    ByteCodec.width (Ext P) = P.d * ByteCodec.width F

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.toBytes_eq
items.statement: theorem toBytes_eq [ByteCodec F] (x : Ext P) : ByteCodec.toBytes x = ByteCodec.toBytes x.coeffs

modules.title: Finiteness and cardinality of monic quotient presentations
modules.doc:
The coordinate equivalence gives `Finite (Ext P)` from `Finite F`, and gives an optional
`Fintype (Ext P)` when an enumeration of the base is available. A separate certificate
`Fact (Nat.card F = P.q)` identifies the stored exponent parameter with the base cardinality.
The resulting extension cardinality is `P.q ^ P.d`.

These facts require neither a polynomial quotient bridge nor irreducibility. All finiteness
and cardinality assumptions used by field laws are propositions, so executable arithmetic
never receives an enumeration dictionary merely to use those laws.

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.ExtensionParams.card_eq
items.doc: The certified cardinality agrees with any enumeration of the base type.
items.statement:
theorem ExtensionParams.card_eq {F : Type*} [Fintype F] (P : ExtensionParams F)
    [Fact (Nat.card F = P.q)] : Fintype.card F = P.q

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.BinomialParams.card_eq
items.doc: The certified binomial base cardinality agrees with any enumeration.
items.statement:
theorem BinomialParams.card_eq {F : Type*} [Fintype F] (P : BinomialParams F)
    [Fact (Nat.card F = P.q)] : Fintype.card F = P.q

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.instFinite
items.statement: instance instFinite [Finite F] : Finite (Ext P)

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.instFintype
items.statement: instance instFintype [Fintype F] : Fintype (Ext P)

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.card_ext
items.doc: The enumerated extension cardinality is the certified base cardinality to the degree.
items.statement: theorem card_ext [Fintype F] [Fact (Nat.card F = P.q)] : Fintype.card (Ext P) = P.q ^ P.d

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.nat_card_ext
items.doc: The extension has `q^d` elements, independently of any chosen enumeration.
items.statement:
theorem nat_card_ext [Finite F] [Fact (Nat.card F = P.q)] :
    Nat.card (Ext P) = P.q ^ P.d

modules.title: Polynomial specifications for monic quotient presentations
modules.doc:
`ExtensionParams.poly` interprets the lower coefficient vector as the monic polynomial
`X^d + ∑ i, C lower[i] * X^i`. The binomial specification is `X^d - W`; its conversion to
an arbitrary monic presentation preserves that polynomial.

The carrier and executable operations are defined in `Extension/Arithmetic.lean`. These
specifications do not certify the cardinality parameter or irreducibility. The quotient bridge
and field laws are supplied separately in `Extension/Bridge.lean` and `Extension/Field.lean`.

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.ExtensionParams.poly
items.doc:
The monic defining polynomial `X^d + ∑_{i < d} lower[i] · X^i`. Part of the specification
only; the computable arithmetic on `Ext P` never evaluates it.
items.statement: noncomputable def poly : F[X]

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.ExtensionParams.degree_lower_lt
items.doc: The lower part of the modulus has degree strictly less than `d`.
items.statement:
theorem degree_lower_lt :
    (∑ i : Fin P.d, C (P.lowerCoeff i) * X ^ (i : ℕ)).degree < (P.d : WithBot ℕ)

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.ExtensionParams.degree_poly
items.statement: theorem degree_poly : P.poly.degree = (P.d : WithBot ℕ)

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.ExtensionParams.monic_poly
items.statement: theorem monic_poly : P.poly.Monic

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.ExtensionParams.natDegree_poly
items.statement: theorem natDegree_poly : P.poly.natDegree = P.d

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.BinomialParams.poly
items.doc: The defining polynomial `X^d - W`. Part of the specification only.
items.statement: noncomputable def poly : F[X]

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.BinomialParams.natDegree_poly
items.statement: theorem natDegree_poly : P.poly.natDegree = P.d

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.BinomialParams.monic_poly
items.statement: theorem monic_poly : P.poly.Monic

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.BinomialParams.toExtensionParams_poly
items.doc: The general-framework polynomial of a binomial agrees with `X^d - W`.
items.statement: theorem toExtensionParams_poly : P.toExtensionParams.poly = P.poly

modules.title: The field structure on an extension
modules.doc:
`toQuot` is not just injective but bijective: every class in `F[X] / f` has a unique
representative of degree `< d`. That gives `Ext.ringEquivQuot : Ext P ≃+* AdjoinRoot P.poly`,
and the separately certified base cardinality gives `Nat.card (Ext P) = q ^ d`. A `Field`
structure requires `[Finite F]`, `[Fact (Nat.card F = P.q)]`, and irreducibility of the defining
polynomial.

Inversion is by Fermat's little theorem, `x⁻¹ = x ^ (q^d - 2)`, matching how
`CompPoly/Fields/Montgomery/Native32Field.lean` inverts in the base field. Exponentiation is
binary, so this costs `O(d · log q)` extension multiplications.

The instance is assembled by hand rather than via `Function.Injective.field`, for the same
reason as `Ext.instCommRing`: that transport takes `toQuot` as data and would make the whole
structure `noncomputable`, which then shadows the computable `Mul` and `Pow`. The `qsmul` /
`nnqsmul` fields use the `castRec` defaults, following `mkDivisionRingInstance` in
`CompPoly/Fields/Binary/Tower/Concrete/Core.lean`.

## Main definitions and statements

* `Ext.toQuot_surjective`, `Ext.ringEquivQuot`: `Ext P ≃+* AdjoinRoot P.poly`.
* `Ext.inv`: Fermat inversion.
* `Ext.instField`: the `Field` structure, given finite base field, certified `Nat.card F = P.q`,
  and irreducibility of `P.poly`.

## Implementation notes

The inverse candidate is defined in `Extension/Arithmetic.lean`; its correctness depends on
the certificates above. `Extension/Cardinality.lean` supplies the finite-coordinate facts
without importing the polynomial quotient bridge.

items.statement: instance instNontrivial : Nontrivial (Ext P)

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.four_le_card_pow
items.doc: `4 ≤ q ^ d`, since `2 ≤ q` and `2 ≤ d`. Used to justify the Fermat exponent `q ^ d - 2`.
items.statement: theorem four_le_card_pow [Finite F] [Fact (Nat.card F = P.q)] : 4 ≤ P.q ^ P.d

items.statement: theorem toQuot_surjective : Function.Surjective (toQuot (P := P))

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.toQuot_bijective
items.statement: theorem toQuot_bijective : Function.Bijective (toQuot (P := P))

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.ringEquivQuot
items.doc: The extension is isomorphic to its specification `F[X] / f`.
items.statement: noncomputable def ringEquivQuot (P : ExtensionParams F) : Ext P ≃+* Quot[P]

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.ringEquivQuot_apply
items.statement: theorem ringEquivQuot_apply (x : Ext P) : ringEquivQuot P x = toQuot x

items.name: CompPoly.Extension.Ext.instFintypeQuot
items.doc: The quotient is finite, transported along the ring equivalence.
items.statement: noncomputable instance instFintypeQuot [Fintype F] : Fintype Quot[P]

modules.title: Fast Goldilocks Field
modules.doc:
Verified `UInt64`-backed implementation of Goldilocks arithmetic, `p = 2^64 - 2^32 + 1`.
The carrier is a subtype of `UInt64` holding canonical representatives, wrapping the raw
kernels from `FastDefs` with the bounds proved in `FastReduction`. Every operation is
identified with its counterpart in the canonical `ZMod` model, and the field instances
are transferred across `toField`.

Reduction rests on `2^64 ≡ 2^32 - 1 (mod p)`, which folds a 128-bit product back into one
word with shifts, additions and carry corrections.

modules.title: Fast Goldilocks: runtime definitions (zero-import)
modules.doc:
Runtime word kernels of the native Goldilocks field, proved correct in
`CompPoly.Fields.Goldilocks.FastReduction`. This module has zero imports so that
`precompileModules` lanes, which compile the whole import closure, can take it without Mathlib.

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.modulus
items.doc: Goldilocks modulus `2^64 - 2^32 + 1` as a native word.
items.statement: def modulus : UInt64

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.negModulus
items.doc: Two's complement of the modulus: `2^64 - modulus = 2^32 - 1 = 0xFFFFFFFF`.
items.statement: def negModulus : UInt64

items.note:
## Raw word kernels

Kernels take and return canonical words below the modulus; the `Lazy` ones take and
return any congruent word, so a chain canonicalizes once at the end.

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.wideMul
items.doc:
Full 64-by-64 product as `(lo, hi)` words from 32-bit limbs, in the shape clang fuses
into one widening multiply.
items.statement: def wideMul (x y : UInt64) : UInt64 × UInt64

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.reduceUInt64Raw
items.doc: Canonicalize a word by one conditional subtraction, since every `UInt64` is below `2 * p`.
items.statement: def reduceUInt64Raw (x : UInt64) : UInt64

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.foldUInt128Borrow
items.doc: Borrow arm of the 128-bit fold, out of line so the common path takes a predicted branch.
items.statement: def foldUInt128Borrow (lo hiHi hiLo : UInt64) : UInt64

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.foldUInt128Lazy
items.doc:
Fold `lo + hi * 2^64` into one congruent, not necessarily canonical, word using
`2^64 ≡ 2^32 - 1`; the middle term is `(hi <<< 32) - hiLo` rather than a multiply.
items.statement: def foldUInt128Lazy (lo hi : UInt64) : UInt64

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.reduceUInt128Raw
items.doc: Raw reduction of a 128-bit integer represented by low and high words modulo Goldilocks.
items.statement: def reduceUInt128Raw (lo hi : UInt64) : UInt64

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.mulLazy
items.doc: Product of two arbitrary words as one congruent, not necessarily canonical, word.
items.statement: def mulLazy (x y : UInt64) : UInt64

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.reduceMulRaw
items.doc: Raw reduction of a 64-by-64 product modulo Goldilocks.
items.statement: def reduceMulRaw (x y : UInt64) : UInt64

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.addRaw
items.doc: Canonical sum as `x - (p - y)`, which borrows exactly when `x + y < p`.
items.statement: def addRaw (x y : UInt64) : UInt64

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.negRaw
items.doc: Raw modular negation in canonical form.
items.statement: def negRaw (x : UInt64) : UInt64

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.subRaw
items.doc: Raw modular subtraction in canonical form.
items.statement: def subRaw (x y : UInt64) : UInt64

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.powLazy
items.doc: Square-and-multiply on unreduced words: `powLazy acc x n` computes `acc * x^n`.
items.statement: def powLazy (acc x : UInt64) (n : Nat) : UInt64

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.squareNLazy
items.doc: `x^(2^n)` on unreduced words.
items.statement: def squareNLazy (x : UInt64) : Nat → UInt64

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.invLazy
items.doc:
Fermat chain for `x^(p - 2)` on unreduced words, with
`p - 2 = (2^32 - 2) * 2^32 + (2^32 - 1)`.
items.statement: def invLazy (x : UInt64) : UInt64

modules.title: Fast Goldilocks: word-level correctness
modules.doc:
Correctness of the raw `UInt64` kernels in `CompPoly.Fields.Goldilocks.FastDefs`:
low-level word lemmas (limb splitting, borrow and overflow correction, the 64-by-64
product decomposition), then for each kernel a bound showing the result is below the
modulus and a cast lemma identifying it with the corresponding operation in
`Goldilocks.Field`.

The field carrier and its API are built on these in
`CompPoly.Fields.Goldilocks.Fast`.

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.modulus_toNat
items.doc: The native `UInt64` modulus agrees with the mathematical Goldilocks modulus.
items.statement: theorem modulus_toNat : modulus.toNat = Goldilocks.fieldSize

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.negModulus_toNat
items.doc: The native negated-modulus constant agrees with `2^32 - 1`.
items.statement: theorem negModulus_toNat : negModulus.toNat = 2 ^ 32 - 1

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.fieldSize_pos
items.doc: The Goldilocks modulus is positive.
items.statement: theorem fieldSize_pos : 0 < Goldilocks.fieldSize

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.fieldSize_lt_uint64Size
items.doc: The Goldilocks modulus fits in a `UInt64`.
items.statement: theorem fieldSize_lt_uint64Size : Goldilocks.fieldSize < UInt64.size

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.uint64_toNat_lt_two_fieldSize
items.doc: Every `UInt64` value is below twice the Goldilocks modulus.
items.statement:
theorem uint64_toNat_lt_two_fieldSize (x : UInt64) :
    x.toNat < 2 * Goldilocks.fieldSize

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.uint64_cast_eq_negModulus
items.doc:
The folding congruence used by the Goldilocks reducer.

`2^64 ≡ 2^32 - 1 (mod p)`.
items.statement:
theorem uint64_cast_eq_negModulus :
    (UInt64.size : Goldilocks.Field) = (negModulus.toNat : Goldilocks.Field)

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.pow32_mul_negModulus_cast
items.doc: Multiplying by `2^32 - 1` after shifting by `2^32` is negation modulo Goldilocks.
items.statement:
theorem pow32_mul_negModulus_cast :
    ((2 ^ 32 : Nat) : Goldilocks.Field) *
        (negModulus.toNat : Goldilocks.Field) =
      -1

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.shiftRight32_toNat
items.doc: Right shifting a `UInt64` by 32 gives division by `2^32` on naturals.
items.statement:
theorem shiftRight32_toNat (x : UInt64) :
    (x >>> 32).toNat = x.toNat / 2 ^ 32

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.and_negModulus_toNat
items.doc: Masking with `2^32 - 1` gives the low 32 bits on naturals.
items.statement:
theorem and_negModulus_toNat (x : UInt64) :
    (x &&& negModulus).toNat = x.toNat % 2 ^ 32

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.subBorrow_cast
items.doc:
A `UInt64` subtraction with the Goldilocks borrow correction represents subtraction modulo `p`.

The assumption says the subtrahend is a 32-bit limb, which is the case for
`hi >>> 32` in the 128-bit reducer.
items.statement:
theorem subBorrow_cast (a b : UInt64) (hb : b.toNat < 2 ^ 32) :
    (((if a < b then a - b - negModulus else a - b).toNat) : Goldilocks.Field) =
      (a.toNat : Goldilocks.Field) - (b.toNat : Goldilocks.Field)

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.addOverflowBounded_cast
items.doc:
A bounded `UInt64` addition with the Goldilocks overflow correction represents
addition modulo `p`.
items.statement:
theorem addOverflowBounded_cast (a b : UInt64)
    (hbound : a.toNat + b.toNat < 2 * UInt64.size - negModulus.toNat) :
    (((if a + b < a then a + b + negModulus else a + b).toNat) :
      Goldilocks.Field) =
      (a.toNat : Goldilocks.Field) + (b.toNat : Goldilocks.Field)

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.mul_negModulus_toNat_of_lt
items.doc: Multiplication by `2^32 - 1` does not overflow for a 32-bit limb.
items.statement:
theorem mul_negModulus_toNat_of_lt (x : UInt64) (hx : x.toNat < 2 ^ 32) :
    (x * negModulus).toNat = x.toNat * negModulus.toNat

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.mul_negModulus_toNat_le
items.doc: The product of a 32-bit limb by `2^32 - 1` leaves enough headroom for correction.
items.statement:
theorem mul_negModulus_toNat_le (x : UInt64) (hx : x.toNat < 2 ^ 32) :
    (x * negModulus).toNat ≤ UInt64.size - 2 * negModulus.toNat

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.hi_split_cast
items.doc: Splitting a high word into 32-bit limbs matches the Goldilocks folding congruence.
items.statement:
theorem hi_split_cast (hi : UInt64) :
    (hi.toNat : Goldilocks.Field) * (UInt64.size : Goldilocks.Field) =
      ((hi &&& negModulus).toNat : Goldilocks.Field) *
          (negModulus.toNat : Goldilocks.Field) -
        ((hi >>> 32).toNat : Goldilocks.Field)

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.uint64_split32
items.doc: A `UInt64` value decomposes into its low and high 32-bit limbs.
items.statement:
theorem uint64_split32 (x : UInt64) :
    x.toNat = (x &&& negModulus).toNat + 2 ^ 32 * (x >>> 32).toNat

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.uint64_low32_lt
items.doc: The low 32-bit limb of a `UInt64` is below `2^32`.
items.statement:
theorem uint64_low32_lt (x : UInt64) :
    (x &&& negModulus).toNat < 2 ^ 32

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.uint64_high32_lt
items.doc: The high 32-bit limb of a `UInt64` is below `2^32`.
items.statement:
theorem uint64_high32_lt (x : UInt64) :
    (x >>> 32).toNat < 2 ^ 32

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.mul32_toNat
items.doc: Multiplying two 32-bit limbs does not overflow `UInt64`.
items.statement:
theorem mul32_toNat (a b : UInt64) (ha : a.toNat < 2 ^ 32) (hb : b.toNat < 2 ^ 32) :
    (a * b).toNat = a.toNat * b.toNat

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.product_split32
items.doc: Algebraic decomposition of a product after splitting both factors into 32-bit limbs.
items.statement:
theorem product_split32 (x y : UInt64) :
    x.toNat * y.toNat =
      (x &&& negModulus).toNat * (y &&& negModulus).toNat +
        2 ^ 32 *
          ((x &&& negModulus).toNat * (y >>> 32).toNat +
            (x >>> 32).toNat * (y &&& negModulus).toNat) +
          2 ^ 64 * ((x >>> 32).toNat * (y >>> 32).toNat)

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.wideMul_low_toNat
items.doc: Low word returned by a 64-by-64 product implementation.
items.statement:
theorem wideMul_low_toNat (lo : UInt64) (x y : UInt64) (hlo : lo = x * y) :
    lo.toNat = x.toNat * y.toNat % UInt64.size

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.wideMul_snd_toNat
items.doc: The high word of `wideMul` is the high half of the product.
items.statement:
theorem wideMul_snd_toNat (x y : UInt64) :
    (wideMul x y).2.toNat = x.toNat * y.toNat / 2 ^ 64

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.wideMul_cast
items.doc: Combined semantic correctness of a 64-by-64 product represented by low and high words.
items.statement:
theorem wideMul_cast
    (x y lo hi : UInt64)
    (hlo : lo = x * y)
    (hhi : hi.toNat = x.toNat * y.toNat / UInt64.size) :
    (lo.toNat : Goldilocks.Field) +
        (hi.toNat : Goldilocks.Field) * (UInt64.size : Goldilocks.Field) =
      (x.toNat : Goldilocks.Field) * (y.toNat : Goldilocks.Field)

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.reduceUInt64Raw_lt
items.doc: The raw one-word reducer returns a canonical representative.
items.statement:
theorem reduceUInt64Raw_lt (x : UInt64) :
    (reduceUInt64Raw x).toNat < Goldilocks.fieldSize

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.reduceUInt64Raw_cast
items.doc: One-word reduction preserves the represented canonical field element.
items.statement:
theorem reduceUInt64Raw_cast (x : UInt64) :
    ((reduceUInt64Raw x).toNat : Goldilocks.Field) =
      (x.toNat : Goldilocks.Field)

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.shiftLeft32_sub_low
items.doc: The middle limb times `2^32 - 1`, formed as a shift and a subtraction.
items.statement:
theorem shiftLeft32_sub_low (hi : UInt64) :
    (hi <<< 32) - (hi &&& negModulus) = (hi &&& negModulus) * negModulus

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.foldUInt128Lazy_cast
items.doc: The lazy fold represents `lo + hi * 2^64`.
items.statement:
theorem foldUInt128Lazy_cast (lo hi : UInt64) :
    ((foldUInt128Lazy lo hi).toNat : Goldilocks.Field) =
      (lo.toNat : Goldilocks.Field) +
        (hi.toNat : Goldilocks.Field) * (UInt64.size : Goldilocks.Field)

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.reduceUInt128Raw_lt
items.doc: The raw 128-bit reducer returns a canonical representative below the modulus.
items.statement:
theorem reduceUInt128Raw_lt (lo hi : UInt64) :
    (reduceUInt128Raw lo hi).toNat < Goldilocks.fieldSize

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.reduceUInt128Raw_cast
items.doc: Semantic correctness of raw 128-bit Goldilocks reduction.
items.statement:
theorem reduceUInt128Raw_cast (lo hi : UInt64) :
    ((reduceUInt128Raw lo hi).toNat : Goldilocks.Field) =
      (lo.toNat : Goldilocks.Field) +
        (hi.toNat : Goldilocks.Field) * (UInt64.size : Goldilocks.Field)

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.mulLazy_cast
items.doc: The lazy product of any two words represents their product.
items.statement:
theorem mulLazy_cast (x y : UInt64) :
    ((mulLazy x y).toNat : Goldilocks.Field) =
      (x.toNat : Goldilocks.Field) * (y.toNat : Goldilocks.Field)

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.reduceMulRaw_lt
items.doc: Product reduction returns a canonical representative below the modulus.
items.statement:
theorem reduceMulRaw_lt (x y : UInt64) :
    (reduceMulRaw x y).toNat < Goldilocks.fieldSize

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.reduceMulRaw_cast
items.doc: Semantic correctness of native 64-by-64 product reduction.
items.statement:
theorem reduceMulRaw_cast (x y : UInt64) :
    ((reduceMulRaw x y).toNat : Goldilocks.Field) =
      (x.toNat : Goldilocks.Field) * (y.toNat : Goldilocks.Field)

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.addRaw_toNat
items.doc: Raw addition of canonical words computes the reduced sum.
items.statement:
theorem addRaw_toNat {x y : UInt64} (hx : x.toNat < Goldilocks.fieldSize)
    (hy : y.toNat < Goldilocks.fieldSize) :
    (addRaw x y).toNat = (x.toNat + y.toNat) % Goldilocks.fieldSize

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.addRaw_lt
items.doc: Raw addition of canonical words returns a canonical representative.
items.statement:
theorem addRaw_lt {x y : UInt64} (hx : x.toNat < Goldilocks.fieldSize)
    (hy : y.toNat < Goldilocks.fieldSize) :
    (addRaw x y).toNat < Goldilocks.fieldSize

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.addRaw_cast
items.doc: Raw addition agrees with canonical-field addition on canonical words.
items.statement:
theorem addRaw_cast {x y : UInt64} (hx : x.toNat < Goldilocks.fieldSize)
    (hy : y.toNat < Goldilocks.fieldSize) :
    ((addRaw x y).toNat : Goldilocks.Field) =
      (x.toNat : Goldilocks.Field) + (y.toNat : Goldilocks.Field)

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.negRaw_lt
items.doc: Raw negation returns a canonical representative when given one.
items.statement:
theorem negRaw_lt (x : UInt64) (hx : x.toNat < Goldilocks.fieldSize) :
    (negRaw x).toNat < Goldilocks.fieldSize

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.negRaw_cast
items.doc: Raw negation agrees with canonical-field negation.
items.statement:
theorem negRaw_cast (x : UInt64) (hx : x.toNat < Goldilocks.fieldSize) :
    ((negRaw x).toNat : Goldilocks.Field) =
      -((x.toNat : Goldilocks.Field))

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.subRaw_lt
items.doc: Raw subtraction returns a canonical representative when given canonical operands.
items.statement:
theorem subRaw_lt (x y : UInt64)
    (hx : x.toNat < Goldilocks.fieldSize)
    (hy : y.toNat < Goldilocks.fieldSize) :
    (subRaw x y).toNat < Goldilocks.fieldSize

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.subRaw_cast
items.doc: Raw subtraction agrees with canonical-field subtraction for canonical operands.
items.statement:
theorem subRaw_cast (x y : UInt64)
    (_hx : x.toNat < Goldilocks.fieldSize)
    (hy : y.toNat < Goldilocks.fieldSize) :
    ((subRaw x y).toNat : Goldilocks.Field) =
      (x.toNat : Goldilocks.Field) - (y.toNat : Goldilocks.Field)

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.powLazy_cast
items.doc: The lazy ladder computes `acc * x^n`.
items.statement:
theorem powLazy_cast (acc x : UInt64) (n : Nat) :
    ((powLazy acc x n).toNat : Goldilocks.Field) =
      (acc.toNat : Goldilocks.Field) * (x.toNat : Goldilocks.Field) ^ n

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.squareNLazy_cast
items.doc: Lazy repeated squaring computes `x^(2^n)`.
items.statement:
theorem squareNLazy_cast (x : UInt64) (n : Nat) :
    ((squareNLazy x n).toNat : Goldilocks.Field) = (x.toNat : Goldilocks.Field) ^ (2 ^ n)

items.name: Goldilocks.Fast.invLazy_cast
items.doc: The lazy chain computes the Fermat exponent `p - 2`.
items.statement:
theorem invLazy_cast (x : UInt64) :
    ((invLazy x).toNat : Goldilocks.Field) =
      (x.toNat : Goldilocks.Field) ^ (Goldilocks.fieldSize - 2)

modules.title: Hachi prime field `2^32 - 99`
modules.doc:
A 32-bit prime field. The name is provisional.

`p - 1 = 2^2 · 3 · 13 · 67 · 163 · 2521`, so:

* `p ≡ 1 mod 4`, which is what makes `X^4 - W` irreducible for any non-square `W`
  (see `CompPoly/Fields/Hachi/Ext4.lean`);
* the two-adicity is only **2**, so unlike BabyBear and KoalaBear this field admits no large
  smooth multiplicative subgroup and therefore **no radix-2 NTT domain**. That is irrelevant for
  degree-4 extension arithmetic, which is schoolbook, but it does rule out the
  `CompPoly/Univariate/NTT*` fast-multiplication paths for polynomials over this field.

## Implementation notes

There is deliberately no `FastField` (Montgomery) implementation for this modulus.
`Montgomery/Native32Field.lean` requires `modulus < 2 ^ 31`, because radix-`2^32` Montgomery
reduction needs `x + m * p < 2 ^ 64`; at `p ≈ 2 ^ 32` that overflows `UInt64`. A 64-bit-radix
(or two-limb) Montgomery layer would be needed, and is orthogonal to the extension framework —
`CompPoly/Fields/Extension/` is generic over the base-field carrier and would pick it up
unchanged.

items.name: Hachi.fieldSize
items.doc: The Hachi field modulus, `2^32 - 99`.
items.statement: def fieldSize : Nat

items.name: Hachi.Field
items.doc: The Hachi prime field as a `ZMod`.
items.statement: abbrev Field

items.name: Hachi.is_prime
items.doc: The Hachi modulus is prime.
items.statement: theorem is_prime : Nat.Prime fieldSize

items.name: Hachi.pBits
items.doc: Bit width of the Hachi modulus.
items.statement: def pBits : Nat

items.name: Hachi.twoAdicity
items.doc:
The two-adicity of `fieldSize - 1`, i.e. `2` — deliberately small; see the module
docstring.
items.statement: def twoAdicity : Nat

items.name: Hachi.fieldSize_sub_one_factorization
items.statement: theorem fieldSize_sub_one_factorization : fieldSize - 1 = 2 ^ twoAdicity * 1073741799

modules.title: The degree-4 extension of Hachi
modules.doc:
`Hachi[X] / (X^4 - 2)`, the degree-4 extension of the 32-bit prime field `2^32 - 99`.

`W = 2` is the smallest non-square modulo `p`, which also makes multiplication by `W` a
doubling. Because `p ≡ 1 mod 4`, `X^4 - W` is irreducible for any non-square `W`; concretely
this is discharged by `Polynomial.irreducible_X_pow_four_sub_C` from
`2^((p^4-1)/4) = 1` and `2^((p^2-1)/4) ≠ 1`.

## Main definitions

* `Hachi.ext4Params`: the `BinomialParams` for `X^4 - 2`.
* `Hachi.Ext4`: the extension field itself.

items.name: Hachi.ext4Params
items.doc: The parameters of the quartic extension `Hachi[X] / (X^4 - 2)`.
items.statement: def ext4Params : BinomialParams Field

items.name: Hachi.ext4Params_d
items.statement: theorem ext4Params_d : ext4Params.d = 4

items.name: Hachi.ext4Params_W
items.statement: theorem ext4Params_W : ext4Params.W = 2

items.name: Hachi.ext4Params_q
items.statement: theorem ext4Params_q : ext4Params.q = fieldSize

items.name: Hachi.ext4Params_poly_irreducible
items.doc: `X^4 - 2` is irreducible over Hachi, by the collapsed Rabin criterion.
items.statement: theorem ext4Params_poly_irreducible : Irreducible ext4Params.poly

items.name: Hachi.Ext4
items.doc: The degree-4 extension field of Hachi.
items.statement: abbrev Ext4 : Type

items.name: Hachi.ext4Gen
items.doc: The adjoined fourth root of `2`, as an element of `Ext4`.
items.statement: def ext4Gen : Ext4

items.name: Hachi.ext4Gen_eq_gen
items.doc:
`ext4Gen` is the framework's `Ext.gen`.

Deliberately **not** `@[simp]`: as a rewrite it fires before `ext4Gen_pow_four` can match, which
would knock that lemma out of the simp set. Use `simp [ext4Gen_eq_gen]` to reach the general
`Ext.gen` lemmas (`Ext.coeff_gen`, `Ext.gen_pow_d`) when the specialized ones below are not
enough.
items.statement: theorem ext4Gen_eq_gen : ext4Gen = Ext.gen

items.name: Hachi.toQuot_ext4Gen
items.doc: `ext4Gen` maps to the adjoined root of the specification.
items.statement: theorem toQuot_ext4Gen : Ext.toQuot ext4Gen = Ext.rt ext4Params.toExtensionParams

items.name: Hachi.ext4Gen_pow_four
items.doc: **The defining relation**, as a theorem rather than only an executable check.
items.statement: theorem ext4Gen_pow_four : ext4Gen ^ 4 = Ext.ofBase (2 : Field)

items.name: Hachi.aeval_ext4Gen
items.doc: `ext4Gen` is a root of `X^4 - 2`, in the form `aeval` expects.
items.statement: theorem aeval_ext4Gen : aeval ext4Gen ext4Params.poly = 0

items.name: Hachi.card_ext4
items.statement: theorem card_ext4 : Fintype.card Ext4 = fieldSize ^ 4

modules.title: KoalaBear Field
modules.doc:
Facade module for the KoalaBear field. It re-exports the canonical `ZMod` model
from `CompPoly.Fields.KoalaBear.Basic` and the native-word implementation from
`CompPoly.Fields.KoalaBear.Fast`.

modules.title: KoalaBear Field `2^{31} - 2^{24} + 1`
modules.doc: This is the field used for lean Ethereum spec.

items.name: KoalaBear.fieldSize
items.doc: The KoalaBear field modulus, `2^31 - 2^24 + 1`.
items.statement: def fieldSize : Nat

items.name: KoalaBear.Field
items.doc: The KoalaBear prime field as a `ZMod`.
items.statement: abbrev Field

items.name: KoalaBear.is_prime
items.doc: The KoalaBear modulus is prime.
items.statement: theorem is_prime : Nat.Prime fieldSize

items.note:
## Constants

These are convenience constants to match the Python module:
- `pBits = 31`
- `twoAdicity = 24` with `fieldSize - 1 = 2^24 * 127`

items.name: KoalaBear.pBits
items.doc: Bit width of the KoalaBear modulus.
items.statement: def pBits : Nat

items.name: KoalaBear.twoAdicity
items.doc: The largest supported power-of-two root-of-unity exponent for KoalaBear.
items.statement: def twoAdicity : Nat

items.note:
Provide instances so `KoalaBear.Field = ZMod fieldSize` is available as a `Field`
and as a `NonBinaryField` (char ≠ 2).

## Two-adicity and roots of unity table

We record the factorization of `fieldSize - 1` and provide a precomputed table
of `2^n`-th roots of unity for `0 ≤ n ≤ twoAdicity`.

items.name: KoalaBear.fieldSize_sub_one_factorization
items.doc: The factorization `fieldSize - 1 = 2^twoAdicity * 127`.
items.statement: lemma fieldSize_sub_one_factorization : fieldSize - 1 = 2 ^ twoAdicity * 127

items.note:
A table of `2^n`-th roots of unity. The element at index `n` generates the
multiplicative subgroup of order `2^n`.

The first entry n = 0 is 1.

items.name: KoalaBear.twoAdicGenerators
items.doc: Precomputed generators for the KoalaBear two-adic subgroups.
items.statement: def twoAdicGenerators : List Field

items.name: KoalaBear.twoAdicGenerators_length
items.statement: lemma twoAdicGenerators_length : twoAdicGenerators.length = twoAdicity + 1

items.name: KoalaBear.twoAdicGenerators_succ_square_eq'
items.statement:
lemma twoAdicGenerators_succ_square_eq' (idx : Fin twoAdicity) :
    twoAdicGenerators[idx.val + 1] ^ 2 = twoAdicGenerators[idx]

items.name: KoalaBear.twoAdicGenerators_succ_square_eq
items.statement:
lemma twoAdicGenerators_succ_square_eq (idx : Nat) (h : idx < twoAdicity) :
    haveI : idx + 1 < twoAdicGenerators.length := by simp [twoAdicGenerators_length, h]
    twoAdicGenerators[idx + 1] ^ 2 = twoAdicGenerators[idx]

items.note: Statements requested by the Python spec translation.

items.name: KoalaBear.inv_eq_pow
items.doc: Fermat-style inversion in `ZMod fieldSize`.
items.statement: lemma inv_eq_pow (a : Field) (ha : a ≠ 0) : a⁻¹ = a ^ (fieldSize - 2)

items.name: KoalaBear.cube_map_bijective
items.doc: Bijectivity of the cube map on the unit group, using `gcd(3, fieldSize-1)=1`.
items.statement:
lemma cube_map_bijective :
    Function.Bijective (fun x : Fieldˣ ↦ x ^ 3)

items.note:
The cube map x ↦ x^3 is an automorphism on the multiplicative group because
`Nat.coprime 3 (fieldSize - 1)` holds. We record the coprimality here.

items.name: KoalaBear.coprime_three_fieldSize_sub_one
items.statement: lemma coprime_three_fieldSize_sub_one : Nat.Coprime 3 (fieldSize - 1)

items.note: Additional statements matching the Python spec API.

items.name: KoalaBear.twoAdicity_maximal
items.doc: `twoAdicity` is maximal: `2^(twoAdicity+1)` does not divide `fieldSize - 1`.
items.statement: lemma twoAdicity_maximal : ¬ (2 ^ (twoAdicity + 1)) ∣ (fieldSize - 1)

items.name: KoalaBear.twoAdicGenerators_pow_twoPow_eq_one
items.doc: The power `(twoAdicGenerators[bits])^(2^bits) = 1`.
items.statement:
lemma twoAdicGenerators_pow_twoPow_eq_one (bits : Fin (twoAdicity + 1)) :
    twoAdicGenerators[bits] ^ (2 ^ (bits : Nat)) = 1

items.name: KoalaBear.twoAdicGenerators_pow_twoPow_ne_one_of_lt
items.doc: If `m < bits`, then `(twoAdicGenerators[bits])^(2^m) ≠ 1`.
items.statement:
lemma twoAdicGenerators_pow_twoPow_ne_one_of_lt
    {bits : Fin (twoAdicity + 1)} {m : Nat} (hm : m < bits) :
    (twoAdicGenerators[bits]) ^ (2 ^ m) ≠ (1 : Field)

items.name: KoalaBear.isPrimitiveRoot_twoAdicGenerator
items.doc: The precomputed element at index `bits` is a primitive `2^bits`-th root of unity.
items.statement:
lemma isPrimitiveRoot_twoAdicGenerator (n : Fin (twoAdicity + 1)) :
    IsPrimitiveRoot (twoAdicGenerators[n]) (2 ^ (n : Nat))

items.name: KoalaBear.twoAdicGenerator_unit_mem_rootsOfUnity
items.doc: As a unit, the precomputed element is a member of `rootsOfUnity (2^bits)`.
items.statement:
lemma twoAdicGenerator_unit_mem_rootsOfUnity
    (bits : Fin (twoAdicity + 1)) (h : twoAdicGenerators[bits] ≠ 0) :
    Units.mk0 (twoAdicGenerators[bits]) h ∈ rootsOfUnity (2 ^ (bits : Nat)) Field

items.name: KoalaBear.twoAdicGenerators_order
items.doc: The order of `twoAdicGenerators[bits]` equals `2^bits`.
items.statement:
lemma twoAdicGenerators_order (bits : Fin (twoAdicity + 1)) :
    orderOf (twoAdicGenerators[bits]) = 2 ^ (bits : Nat)

items.name: KoalaBear.primitiveRoot
items.doc: Primitive generator used by the smooth field-root splitter.
items.statement: def primitiveRoot : Field

items.name: KoalaBear.primitiveRoot_order
items.doc: The smooth field-root splitter generator has full multiplicative order.
items.statement: lemma primitiveRoot_order : orderOf primitiveRoot = fieldSize - 1

items.name: KoalaBear.smoothRootSchedule
items.doc: Smooth subgroup refinement schedule for `fieldSize - 1 = 2^24 * 127`.
items.statement: def smoothRootSchedule : Array Nat

items.name: KoalaBear.smoothRootSchedule_fold_eq_one
items.doc: The KoalaBear smooth schedule refines the multiplicative group down to singleton cosets.
items.statement:
lemma smoothRootSchedule_fold_eq_one :
    smoothRootSchedule.toList.foldl (fun order ell ↦ order / ell) (fieldSize - 1) = 1

modules.title: The degree-4 extension of KoalaBear
modules.doc:
`KoalaBear[X] / (X^4 - 3)`, the challenge field used alongside the KoalaBear base field in
Plonky3-style STARKs.

Irreducibility of `X^4 - 3` is discharged by `Polynomial.irreducible_X_pow_four_sub_C`,
whose two hypotheses are single exponentiations in the base field:
`3^((p^4-1)/4) = 1` and `3^((p^2-1)/4) ≠ 1`. Both are closed by `reduce_mod_char`, which does
modular repeated squaring at elaboration time — no `native_decide`, and no generated
certificate file.

## Main definitions

* `KoalaBear.ext4Params`: the `BinomialParams` for `X^4 - 3`.
* `KoalaBear.Ext4`: the extension field itself.

items.name: KoalaBear.ext4Params
items.doc: The parameters of the quartic extension `KoalaBear[X] / (X^4 - 3)`.
items.statement: def ext4Params : BinomialParams Field

items.name: KoalaBear.ext4Params_d
items.statement: theorem ext4Params_d : ext4Params.d = 4

items.name: KoalaBear.ext4Params_W
items.statement: theorem ext4Params_W : ext4Params.W = 3

items.name: KoalaBear.ext4Params_q
items.statement: theorem ext4Params_q : ext4Params.q = fieldSize

items.name: KoalaBear.ext4Params_poly_irreducible
items.doc: `X^4 - 3` is irreducible over KoalaBear, by the collapsed Rabin criterion.
items.statement: theorem ext4Params_poly_irreducible : Irreducible ext4Params.poly

items.name: KoalaBear.Ext4
items.doc: The degree-4 extension field of KoalaBear.
items.statement: abbrev Ext4 : Type

items.name: KoalaBear.ext4Gen
items.doc: The adjoined fourth root of `3`, as an element of `Ext4`.
items.statement: def ext4Gen : Ext4

items.name: KoalaBear.ext4Gen_eq_gen
items.doc:
`ext4Gen` is the framework's `Ext.gen`.

modules.title: Irreducibility of `X^5 + X^2 - 1` over KoalaBear
modules.doc:
The quintic `X^5 + X^2 - 1` is irreducible over `KoalaBear.Field`, proved by Rabin's test at
prime degree (`CompPoly.RabinCert.irreducible_of_rabin_prime_degree`). No degree-5
*binomial* does the job: `gcd(5, p - 1) = 1`, so `x ↦ x^5` is a bijection on KoalaBear and every
`X^5 - W` has a root. This non-binomial quintic is the defining polynomial of the degree-5
extension in `CompPoly/Fields/KoalaBear/Ext5.lean`.

The two Rabin conditions — `f ∣ X^(p^5) - X` and `IsCoprime f (X^p - X)` — are discharged by
kernel-checked certificates from `CompPoly/Fields/KoalaBear/Ext5/QuinticCertData.lean`
(generated by `scripts/gen_rabin_certificate.py`): a 211-step square-and-multiply chain for the
trace condition, a 37-step chain plus a Bézout identity for coprimality. Each chain is verified
by a single kernel reduction of `CompPoly.RabinCert.runChain` — `Nat` arithmetic only, no
`native_decide`.

## Main statements

* `KoalaBear.quinticPoly`: the polynomial `X^5 + X^2 - 1` over `KoalaBear.Field`.
* `KoalaBear.quinticPoly_irreducible`, and the `Fact` instance consumed by
  `CompPoly.Extension.Ext.instField`.

modules.title: The degree-6 extension of KoalaBear
modules.doc:
`KoalaBear[X] / (X^6 + X^3 + 1)`, a field of `p^6 ≈ 2^186` elements. The modulus is `Φ₉`, the
ninth cyclotomic polynomial, so the adjoined root `θ` is a primitive 9th root of unity.

As at degree 5, the modulus is necessarily *not* a binomial, and for a stronger reason: since
`p - 1 = 2^24 · 127` we have `3 ∤ p - 1`, so `x ↦ x^3` is a bijection on KoalaBear and every `W`
is a cube `V^3`, whence `X^6 - W = (X^2 - V)(X^4 + V X^2 + V^2)` factors for *every* `W`. So no
degree-6 binomial extension of KoalaBear exists at all.

`Φ₉` is chosen among the irreducible sextics because every entry of its reduction table
`X^6 … X^10 mod f` is `±1` — reduction costs no base-field multiplications — and the same holds
for its Frobenius matrix, since `p ≡ 2 mod 9` makes Frobenius `θ ↦ θ^2`. It also carries the
`2`-then-`3` tower implicitly: `θ^3` is a primitive cube root of unity generating the `F_p²`
subfield, because `Y^2 + Y + 1` is irreducible over KoalaBear.

Irreducibility of `X^6 + X^3 + 1` is `KoalaBear.sexticPoly_irreducible`
(`CompPoly/Fields/KoalaBear/Ext6/SexticIrreducible.lean`), proved by Rabin's test at a degree with
two prime factors, with kernel-checked certificates for all three conditions. Supporting files
live under `KoalaBear/Ext6/`.

This sits alongside `KoalaBear.Ext5` rather than replacing it; the two are independent instances
of the same framework.

modules.title: `Ext6` as a computable model of `GaloisField KoalaBear.fieldSize 6`
modules.doc:
Mathlib's `GaloisField p n` is the abstract field of order `p^n`, defined as a splitting field and
therefore noncomputable. Downstream developments that only need "the field of order `p^6`" state
things in those terms — ArkLib's `KoalaSextic := GaloisField KoalaBear.fieldSize 6` is exactly
this, used for the KoalaBear-sextic parameter point of the Proximity Prize open problems
([ABF26], ePrint 2026/680).

`ext6AlgEquivGaloisField` identifies `KoalaBear.Ext6` with that field, so the computable
arithmetic here is usable as a model for statements phrased over `GaloisField`.

Two things worth noting about *why* this is unconditional:

* `GaloisField p n` commits to no defining polynomial, so this is not a coincidence of
  presentation. Any two finite fields of the same cardinality are isomorphic, and the isomorphism
  follows from `card_ext6` alone — the choice of `X^6 + X^3 + 1` is irrelevant to it.
* The isomorphism is *noncanonical*, as Mathlib's own docstring says. There is no distinguished
  map, so nothing here pins down where `ext6Gen` lands. Consumers that need a specific element
  (a domain generator, a high-order element) should construct it on whichever side they compute.

This lives in its own module so that the `Mathlib.FieldTheory.Finite.GaloisField` import is
opt-in: users of `Ext6` who do not need the bridge do not pay for it.

The same one-liner works for any `Ext P` with a cardinality lemma in hand; `card_ext` in
`CompPoly/Fields/Extension/Field.lean` supplies it generically.

Noncomputable because the isomorphism is obtained by a splitting-field argument, not because
either side's arithmetic is: `Ext6` itself computes.

    Ext6 ≃ₐ[Field] GaloisField fieldSize 6

modules.title: Irreducibility of `X^6 + X^3 + 1` over KoalaBear
modules.doc:
The sextic `X^6 + X^3 + 1` is the ninth cyclotomic polynomial `Φ₉`, so it is irreducible over
`KoalaBear.Field` exactly because `p` has multiplicative order 6 modulo 9 (`p ≡ 2 mod 9`); its
root is a primitive 9th root of unity. It is the defining polynomial of the degree-6 extension in
`CompPoly/Fields/KoalaBear/Ext6.lean`.

No degree-6 *binomial* does the job, for the same reason as at degree 5 but one step stronger:
`p - 1 = 2^24 · 127`, so `3 ∤ p - 1`, `x ↦ x^3` is a bijection on KoalaBear, and every `W` is a
cube `V^3` — whence `X^6 - W = (X^2 - V)(X^4 + V X^2 + V^2)` factors for *every* `W`.

`Φ₉` is chosen among the irreducible sextics for arithmetic reasons. Every entry of the reduction
table `X^6 … X^10 mod f` is `±1`, so reduction costs no base-field multiplications, and the same
holds for the Frobenius matrix (`θ ↦ θ^2`, since `p ≡ 2 mod 9`). It also exposes the `2`-then-`3`
tower for free: `θ^3` is a primitive cube root of unity, and `F_p(θ^3) = F_p²` because
`Y^2 + Y + 1` is irreducible over KoalaBear.

## Certificates

Degree 6 is *composite*, so Rabin's test needs the trace condition plus one coprimality check per
prime factor of 6 — at `p^3` (for `ℓ = 2`) and `p^2` (for `ℓ = 3`). The collapsed prime-degree
form is not just weaker but unsound here: `(X^3 + X + 4)(X^3 + X - 4)` divides `X^(p^6) - X` and
is coprime to `X^p - X`, so it would pass. The three conditions are discharged by kernel-checked
certificates from `CompPoly/Fields/KoalaBear/Ext6/SexticCertData.lean` (generated by
`scripts/gen_rabin_certificate.py`): a 258-step chain for the trace, 121 and 75 steps plus a
Bézout identity for the two coprimality checks. Each chain is verified by a single kernel
reduction of `CompPoly.RabinCert.runChain` — `Nat` arithmetic only, no `native_decide`.

## Main statements

* `KoalaBear.sexticPoly`: the polynomial `X^6 + X^3 + 1` over `KoalaBear.Field`.
* `KoalaBear.sexticPoly_irreducible`, and the `Fact` instance consumed by
  `CompPoly.Extension.Ext.instField`.

theorem sextic_cop3_w_check :
    eqModP fieldSize SexticCert.cop3Rp (addNat SexticCert.cop3W [0, 1]) = true

items.name: KoalaBear.sextic_cop3_bezout_check
items.doc: The Bézout identity `cop3U·f + cop3V·cop3W = 1` verifies.
items.statement:
theorem sextic_cop3_bezout_check :
    eqModP fieldSize
      (addNat (mulNat SexticCert.cop3U sexticL) (mulNat SexticCert.cop3V SexticCert.cop3W)) [1]
      = true

items.note: #### Coprimality with `X^(p^2) - X`, the check for the prime factor `3` of `6`

items.name: KoalaBear.sextic_cop2_chain
items.doc: The 75-step chain for `X^(p^2) mod f` verifies and ends at the recorded residue.
items.statement:
theorem sextic_cop2_chain :
    runChain fieldSize sexticL [0, 1] SexticCert.cop2Steps = some SexticCert.cop2Rp

items.name: KoalaBear.sextic_cop2_exp
items.doc: The chain computes the exponent `p^2`.
items.statement: theorem sextic_cop2_exp : chainExp 1 SexticCert.cop2Steps = fieldSize ^ 2

items.name: KoalaBear.sextic_cop2_w_check
items.doc: The recorded residue satisfies `cop2Rp = cop2W + X`.
items.statement:
theorem sextic_cop2_w_check :
    eqModP fieldSize SexticCert.cop2Rp (addNat SexticCert.cop2W [0, 1]) = true

items.name: KoalaBear.sextic_cop2_bezout_check
items.doc: The Bézout identity `cop2U·f + cop2V·cop2W = 1` verifies.
items.statement:
theorem sextic_cop2_bezout_check :
    eqModP fieldSize
      (addNat (mulNat SexticCert.cop2U sexticL) (mulNat SexticCert.cop2V SexticCert.cop2W)) [1]
      = true

items.name: KoalaBear.sexticPoly_irreducible
items.doc:
**`X^6 + X^3 + 1` is irreducible over KoalaBear**, by Rabin's test at a degree with two prime
factors, with kernel-checked certificates for all three conditions.

The application uses the same carrier and instances as the certificate lemmas.
With Lean and Mathlib 4.34, replaying the earlier proof and its dependencies in an empty kernel
environment hit the kernel's recursion limit. With Lean and Mathlib 4.36, both proof forms
passed that check. See `docs/wiki/field-extensions.md` for the KoalaBear replay history.
items.statement: theorem sexticPoly_irreducible : Irreducible sexticPoly

modules.title: Fast KoalaBear Field
modules.doc:
A native-word Montgomery implementation of KoalaBear arithmetic. The shared algorithms and
proofs live in `CompPoly.Fields.Montgomery.Native32Field`; this module supplies the KoalaBear
constants and its concrete API.

items.name: KoalaBear.Fast.instMont32Field
items.doc: The per-field data realizing KoalaBear as a fast 32-bit-word Montgomery field.
items.statement: instance instMont32Field : Mont32Field KoalaBear.fieldSize

items.name: KoalaBear.Fast.Field
items.doc: The fast native-word KoalaBear field carrier, stored as a Montgomery residue.
items.statement: abbrev Field : Type

items.name: KoalaBear.Fast.ofUInt32
items.doc: Convert a 32-bit word into fast Montgomery representation.
items.statement: def ofUInt32 (x : UInt32) : Field

items.name: KoalaBear.Fast.ofField
items.doc: Convert from the canonical `ZMod` KoalaBear field into fast Montgomery form.
items.statement: def ofField (x : KoalaBear.Field) : Field

items.name: KoalaBear.Fast.ringEquiv
items.doc: Ring equivalence between the fast Montgomery representation and canonical `KoalaBear.Field`.
items.statement: def ringEquiv : Field ≃+* KoalaBear.Field
