modules.title: Mersenne31 prime field `2^{31} - 1`
modules.doc:
Facade module for the Mersenne31 field. It re-exports the canonical `ZMod` model
from `CompPoly.Fields.Mersenne31.Basic` and the native-word implementation from
`CompPoly.Fields.Mersenne31.Fast`, plus the circle group and domain-indexing API from
`CompPoly.Fields.Mersenne31.Circle`.

modules.title: Mersenne prime field `2^{31} - 1`
modules.doc: This is the field used in Circle STARKs.

items.name: Mersenne31.fieldSize
items.doc: The Mersenne31 prime modulus `2^31 - 1`.
items.statement: def fieldSize : Nat

items.name: Mersenne31.Field
items.doc:
The canonical mathematical Mersenne31 field, implemented as integers modulo
`fieldSize`.
items.statement: abbrev Field

items.name: Mersenne31.is_prime
items.doc: The Mersenne31 modulus is prime, verified by a Pratt certificate.
items.statement: theorem is_prime : Nat.Prime fieldSize

modules.title: Serialization of the fast Mersenne31 carrier
modules.doc:
`Mersenne31.Fast.Field` stores the canonical residue in a `UInt32`, so its canonical natural is
the stored word and the four-byte little-endian encoding agrees with `Mersenne31.Field`
(`toBytes_ofField`).

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.toNat_lt
items.statement: theorem toNat_lt (x : Field) : toNat x < Mersenne31.fieldSize

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.ofField_cast_toNat
items.statement: theorem ofField_cast_toNat (x : Field) : ofField (toNat x : Mersenne31.Field) = x

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.canonicalNat_bound
items.statement: theorem canonicalNat_bound : CanonicalNat.bound Field = Mersenne31.fieldSize

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.canonicalNat_toNat
items.statement: theorem canonicalNat_toNat (x : Field) : CanonicalNat.toNat x = toNat x

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.byteCodec_width
items.statement: theorem byteCodec_width : ByteCodec.width Field = 4

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.toBytes_ofField
items.doc: The fast carrier and `Mersenne31.Field` encode the same element identically.
items.statement:
theorem toBytes_ofField (n : Mersenne31.Field) :
    ByteCodec.toBytes (ofField n) = ByteCodec.toBytes n

modules.title: Mersenne31 Circle Domains
modules.doc:
This module mirrors the structural circle-domain layer used by STWO over the
Mersenne31 field. It records the circle equation, the STWO M31 circle generator,
index arithmetic modulo the circle order, and the coset/domain shapes used by
canonical circle domains.

Circle points form an additive commutative group, with binary scalar multiplication.
The STWO generator has order `2^31`, and `CirclePointIndex.toPoint` is injective and
respects addition. Each subgroup step has the requested exact order.

`Coset.Valid` requires the step order to equal the declared size. Standard constructors
satisfy it; valid cosets enumerate distinct indices and points and have the declared
range cardinality. Circle domains still need a validity condition requiring disjoint
halves before their declared size can be identified with set cardinality.

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.OnCircle
items.doc: Predicate for points on the circle `x^2 + y^2 = 1`.
items.statement: def OnCircle (x y : Field) : Prop

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.Point
items.doc: A point on the Mersenne31 circle.
items.statement:
structure Point where
  x : Field
  y : Field
  onCircle : OnCircle x y

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.Point.ext
items.doc: Two circle points are equal when both coordinates are equal.
items.statement: theorem ext {p q : Point} (hx : p.x = q.x) (hy : p.y = q.y) : p = q

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.Point.zero
items.doc: The identity point of the circle group.
items.statement: def zero : Point

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.Point.conjugate
items.doc: The circle-group inverse, equal to complex conjugation.
items.statement: def conjugate (p : Point) : Point

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.Point.antipode
items.doc: The antipodal point, obtained by negating both coordinates.
items.statement: def antipode (p : Point) : Point

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.Point.add
items.doc: Circle-group addition, written as multiplication of complex coordinates.
items.statement: def add (p q : Point) : Point

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.Point.zero_x
items.doc: The identity point has x-coordinate one.
items.statement: theorem zero_x : (0 : Point).x = 1

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.Point.zero_y
items.doc: The identity point has y-coordinate zero.
items.statement: theorem zero_y : (0 : Point).y = 0

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.Point.conjugate_x
items.doc: Conjugation preserves the x-coordinate.
items.statement: theorem conjugate_x (p : Point) : (-p).x = p.x

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.Point.conjugate_y
items.doc: Conjugation negates the y-coordinate.
items.statement: theorem conjugate_y (p : Point) : (-p).y = -p.y

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.Point.antipode_x
items.doc: The antipode negates the x-coordinate.
items.statement: theorem antipode_x (p : Point) : p.antipode.x = -p.x

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.Point.antipode_y
items.doc: The antipode negates the y-coordinate.
items.statement: theorem antipode_y (p : Point) : p.antipode.y = -p.y

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.Point.add_x
items.doc: The x-coordinate of circle addition.
items.statement: theorem add_x (p q : Point) : (p + q).x = p.x * q.x - p.y * q.y

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.Point.add_y
items.doc: The y-coordinate of circle addition.
items.statement: theorem add_y (p q : Point) : (p + q).y = p.x * q.y + p.y * q.x

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.generatorX
items.doc: STWO's Mersenne31 circle generator x-coordinate.
items.statement: def generatorX : Field

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.generatorY
items.doc: STWO's Mersenne31 circle generator y-coordinate.
items.statement: def generatorY : Field

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.generatorX_eq
items.doc: The STWO generator's x-coordinate constant is two.
items.statement: theorem generatorX_eq : generatorX = 2

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.generatorY_eq
items.doc: The value of the STWO generator's y-coordinate constant.
items.statement: theorem generatorY_eq : generatorY = 1268011823

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.generator_onCircle
items.doc: STWO's Mersenne31 circle generator lies on `x^2 + y^2 = 1`.
items.statement: theorem generator_onCircle : OnCircle generatorX generatorY

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.generator
items.doc: STWO's generator for the Mersenne31 circle group.
items.statement: def generator : Point

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.generator_x
items.doc: The STWO generator has x-coordinate two.
items.statement: theorem generator_x : generator.x = 2

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.generator_y
items.doc: The STWO generator's y-coordinate.
items.statement: theorem generator_y : generator.y = 1268011823

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.generator_half_order
items.doc: The half-order multiple of the STWO generator is the antipode of the identity.
items.statement: theorem generator_half_order : (2 ^ 30 : Nat) • generator = Point.antipode 0

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.logOrder
items.doc: The log order of STWO's Mersenne31 circle group.
items.statement: def logOrder : Nat

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.order
items.doc: The order of the Mersenne31 circle-index group, `2^31`.
items.statement: def order : Nat

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.order_nsmul_generator
items.doc: The circle-index modulus annihilates the STWO generator.
items.statement: theorem order_nsmul_generator : order • generator = 0

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.addOrderOf_generator
items.doc: The STWO Mersenne31 circle generator has exact additive order `2^31`.
items.statement: theorem addOrderOf_generator : addOrderOf generator = 2 ^ 31

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.CirclePointIndex
items.doc: Integer index for multiples of the Mersenne31 circle generator.
items.statement: abbrev CirclePointIndex

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.CirclePointIndex.generator
items.doc: The distinguished generator index.
items.statement: def generator : CirclePointIndex

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.CirclePointIndex.generator_eq
items.doc: The distinguished generator index is one.
items.statement: theorem generator_eq : generator = 1

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.CirclePointIndex.subgroupGen
items.doc:
Subgroup generator index for the subgroup of order `2^logSize`.
The explicit bound rules out truncated subtraction for out-of-range inputs.
items.statement: def subgroupGen (logSize : Nat) (_hlogSize : logSize ≤ logOrder) : CirclePointIndex

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.CirclePointIndex.subgroupGen_eq
items.doc: The subgroup step is the corresponding power of two modulo the circle order.
items.statement:
theorem subgroupGen_eq (logSize : Nat) (h : logSize ≤ logOrder) :
    subgroupGen logSize h = ((2 ^ (logOrder - logSize) : Nat) : CirclePointIndex)

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.CirclePointIndex.toPoint
items.doc: Interpret the canonical representative of an index as a multiple of the STWO generator.
items.statement: def toPoint (i : CirclePointIndex) : Point

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.CirclePointIndex.toPoint_def
items.doc: Index interpretation uses the canonical natural representative.
items.statement:
theorem toPoint_def (i : CirclePointIndex) :
    toPoint i = i.val • Circle.generator

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.CirclePointIndex.toPoint_zero
items.doc: Index zero maps to the circle identity.
items.statement: theorem toPoint_zero : toPoint 0 = 0

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.CirclePointIndex.toPoint_generator
items.doc: The distinguished index maps to the STWO circle generator.
items.statement: theorem toPoint_generator : toPoint CirclePointIndex.generator = Circle.generator

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.CirclePointIndex.toPoint_one
items.doc: Index one maps to the STWO circle generator.
items.statement: theorem toPoint_one : toPoint 1 = Circle.generator

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.CirclePointIndex.toPoint_add
items.doc: Index addition agrees with circle addition, including wraparound at the circle order.
items.statement: theorem toPoint_add (i j : CirclePointIndex) : toPoint (i + j) = toPoint i + toPoint j

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.CirclePointIndex.toPointHom
items.doc: The additive homomorphism interpreting circle indices as points.
items.statement: def toPointHom : CirclePointIndex →+ Point

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.CirclePointIndex.toPointHom_apply
items.doc: The homomorphism uses the executable index interpretation.
items.statement: theorem toPointHom_apply (i : CirclePointIndex) : toPointHom i = toPoint i

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.CirclePointIndex.toPoint_injective
items.doc: Different circle indices represent different points.
items.statement: theorem toPoint_injective : Function.Injective toPoint

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.CirclePointIndex.toPoint_inj
items.doc: Equality of interpreted points is exactly equality of their indices.
items.statement: theorem toPoint_inj {i j : CirclePointIndex} : toPoint i = toPoint j ↔ i = j

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.CirclePointIndex.addOrderOf_toPoint
items.doc: Interpreting an index preserves its additive order.
items.statement:
theorem addOrderOf_toPoint (i : CirclePointIndex) :
    addOrderOf (toPoint i) = addOrderOf i

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.CirclePointIndex.addOrderOf_subgroupGen
items.doc: The subgroup step has the requested exact order, including log sizes zero and 31.
items.statement:
theorem addOrderOf_subgroupGen (n : Nat) (h : n ≤ logOrder) :
    addOrderOf (subgroupGen n h) = 2 ^ n

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.CirclePointIndex.toPoint_neg
items.doc: Negating an index conjugates its circle point.
items.statement: theorem toPoint_neg (i : CirclePointIndex) : toPoint (-i) = -toPoint i

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.CirclePointIndex.toPoint_sub
items.doc: Subtracting indices agrees with subtracting their circle points.
items.statement: theorem toPoint_sub (i j : CirclePointIndex) : toPoint (i - j) = toPoint i - toPoint j

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.CirclePointIndex.subgroupGen_zero
items.doc: The subgroup generator for the trivial subgroup is zero modulo the circle order.
items.statement: theorem subgroupGen_zero (h : 0 ≤ logOrder) : subgroupGen 0 h = 0

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.CirclePointIndex.subgroupGen_logOrder
items.doc: The full-order subgroup generator is the distinguished generator index.
items.statement:
theorem subgroupGen_logOrder (h : logOrder ≤ logOrder) :
    subgroupGen logOrder h = generator

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.Coset
items.doc:
An indexing shape with a fixed additive step.
No relation between `stepSize` and `logSize` is required; a zero step is allowed.
`Coset.Valid` supplies the exact-order condition for distinctness and cardinality.
items.statement:
structure Coset where
  initialIndex : CirclePointIndex
  stepSize : CirclePointIndex
  logSize : Nat
  logSize_le_logOrder : logSize ≤ logOrder

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.Coset.new
items.doc: Create a coset with STWO's subgroup step for `logSize`.
items.statement:
def new (initialIndex : CirclePointIndex) (logSize : Nat) (hlogSize : logSize ≤ logOrder) :
    Coset

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.Coset.new_initialIndex
items.doc: The coset constructor preserves the initial index.
items.statement:
theorem new_initialIndex (i : CirclePointIndex) (n : Nat) (h : n ≤ logOrder) :
    (new i n h).initialIndex = i

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.Coset.new_stepSize
items.doc: The coset constructor uses the subgroup generator as its step.
items.statement:
theorem new_stepSize (i : CirclePointIndex) (n : Nat) (h : n ≤ logOrder) :
    (new i n h).stepSize = CirclePointIndex.subgroupGen n h

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.Coset.new_logSize
items.doc: The coset constructor preserves the log size.
items.statement:
theorem new_logSize (i : CirclePointIndex) (n : Nat) (h : n ≤ logOrder) :
    (new i n h).logSize = n

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.Coset.subgroup
items.doc: The additive subgroup of size `2^logSize`.
items.statement: def subgroup (logSize : Nat) (hlogSize : logSize ≤ logOrder) : Coset

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.Coset.subgroup_eq
items.doc: A subgroup is the coset starting at zero.
items.statement: theorem subgroup_eq (n : Nat) (h : n ≤ logOrder) : subgroup n h = new 0 n h

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.Coset.odds
items.doc: The STWO coset `G_{2n} + <G_n>`.
items.statement: def odds (logSize : Nat) (hlogSize : logSize + 1 ≤ logOrder) : Coset

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.Coset.odds_eq
items.doc: The odds coset starts at the next larger subgroup's generator.
items.statement:
theorem odds_eq (n : Nat) (h : n + 1 ≤ logOrder) :
    odds n h = new (CirclePointIndex.subgroupGen (n + 1) h) n
      (Nat.le_trans (Nat.le_succ n) h)

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.Coset.halfOdds
items.doc: The STWO coset `G_{4n} + <G_n>`, whose conjugate completes `odds (logSize + 1)`.
items.statement: def halfOdds (logSize : Nat) (hlogSize : logSize + 2 ≤ logOrder) : Coset

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.Coset.halfOdds_eq
items.doc: The half-odds coset starts two subgroup levels above its step.
items.statement:
theorem halfOdds_eq (n : Nat) (h : n + 2 ≤ logOrder) :
    halfOdds n h = new (CirclePointIndex.subgroupGen (n + 2) h) n
      (Nat.le_trans (Nat.le_add_right n 2) h)

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.Coset.size
items.doc: Declared number of index positions, not necessarily the number of distinct points.
items.statement: def size (c : Coset) : Nat

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.Coset.size_eq
items.doc: A coset's size is two to its log size.
items.statement: theorem size_eq (c : Coset) : c.size = 2 ^ c.logSize

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.Coset.indexAt
items.doc: The `i`th index in the coset order.
items.statement: def indexAt (c : Coset) (i : Nat) : CirclePointIndex

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.Coset.indexAt_eq
items.doc:
Closed-form coset indexing, without recursive expansion of literal indices.
Lower priority lets the zero and conjugation lemmas simplify first.
items.statement:
theorem indexAt_eq (c : Coset) (i : Nat) :
    c.indexAt i = c.initialIndex + c.stepSize * (i : CirclePointIndex)

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.Coset.pointAt
items.doc: The circle point at the `i`th coset index.
items.statement: def pointAt (c : Coset) (i : Nat) : Point

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.Coset.pointAt_def
items.doc: A coset point is the interpretation of its index.
items.statement:
theorem pointAt_def (c : Coset) (i : Nat) :
    c.pointAt i = CirclePointIndex.toPoint (c.indexAt i)

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.Coset.Valid
items.doc: The step has exactly as many distinct multiples as the declared coset size.
items.statement: def Valid (c : Coset) : Prop

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.Coset.valid_iff
items.doc: Validity is an exact-order condition on the step, independent of the initial index.
items.statement: theorem valid_iff (c : Coset) : c.Valid ↔ addOrderOf c.stepSize = c.size

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.Coset.new_valid
items.doc: The standard constructor uses a step of the requested order.
items.statement:
theorem new_valid (i : CirclePointIndex) (n : Nat) (h : n ≤ logOrder) :
    (new i n h).Valid

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.Coset.subgroup_valid
items.doc: The subgroup constructor has a step of the declared order.
items.statement: theorem subgroup_valid (n : Nat) (h : n ≤ logOrder) : (subgroup n h).Valid

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.Coset.odds_valid
items.doc: The odds constructor has a step of the declared order.
items.statement: theorem odds_valid (n : Nat) (h : n + 1 ≤ logOrder) : (odds n h).Valid

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.Coset.halfOdds_valid
items.doc: The half-odds constructor has a step of the declared order.
items.statement: theorem halfOdds_valid (n : Nat) (h : n + 2 ≤ logOrder) : (halfOdds n h).Valid

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.Coset.indexAt_injective
items.doc: Valid cosets enumerate distinct indices within their declared size.
items.statement:
theorem indexAt_injective (c : Coset) (hc : c.Valid) :
    Function.Injective (fun i : Fin c.size => c.indexAt i.val)

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.Coset.pointAt_injective
items.doc: Valid cosets enumerate distinct circle points within their declared size.
items.statement:
theorem pointAt_injective (c : Coset) (hc : c.Valid) :
    Function.Injective (fun i : Fin c.size => c.pointAt i.val)

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.Coset.card_range_indexAt
items.doc: The bounded index range of a valid coset has its declared cardinality.
items.statement:
theorem card_range_indexAt (c : Coset) (hc : c.Valid) :
    Nat.card (Set.range (fun i : Fin c.size => c.indexAt i.val)) = c.size

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.Coset.card_range_pointAt
items.doc: The bounded point range of a valid coset has its declared cardinality.
items.statement:
theorem card_range_pointAt (c : Coset) (hc : c.Valid) :
    Nat.card (Set.range (fun i : Fin c.size => c.pointAt i.val)) = c.size

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.Coset.conjugate
items.doc: The conjugate coset `-initial - <step>`.
items.statement: def conjugate (c : Coset) : Coset

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.Coset.indexAt_zero
items.doc: The first coset index is its initial index.
items.statement: theorem indexAt_zero (c : Coset) : c.indexAt 0 = c.initialIndex

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.Coset.indexAt_succ
items.doc: Successive coset indices differ by the fixed step size.
items.statement:
theorem indexAt_succ (c : Coset) (i : Nat) :
    c.indexAt (i + 1) = c.indexAt i + c.stepSize

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.Coset.conjugate_logSize
items.doc: Conjugation preserves the coset log size.
items.statement: theorem conjugate_logSize (c : Coset) : c.conjugate.logSize = c.logSize

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.Coset.conjugate_initialIndex
items.doc: The conjugate coset starts at the negated initial index.
items.statement:
theorem conjugate_initialIndex (c : Coset) :
    c.conjugate.initialIndex = -c.initialIndex

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.Coset.conjugate_stepSize
items.doc: The conjugate coset uses the negated step size.
items.statement: theorem conjugate_stepSize (c : Coset) : c.conjugate.stepSize = -c.stepSize

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.Coset.conjugate_valid_iff
items.doc: Conjugation preserves the exact-order condition.
items.statement: theorem conjugate_valid_iff (c : Coset) : c.conjugate.Valid ↔ c.Valid

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.Coset.conjugate_indexAt
items.doc: Each conjugate-coset index is the negation of the corresponding original index.
items.statement:
theorem conjugate_indexAt (c : Coset) (i : Nat) :
    c.conjugate.indexAt i = -c.indexAt i

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.CircleDomain
items.doc:
A domain indexing shape: a half coset followed by its conjugate.
The halves need not be disjoint, and either half may contain repeated points.
A follow-up must impose validity conditions before identifying `size` with cardinality.
items.statement:
structure CircleDomain where
  halfCoset : Coset

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.CircleDomain.new
items.doc: Construct a circle domain from the half coset.
items.statement: def new (halfCoset : Coset) : CircleDomain

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.CircleDomain.new_halfCoset
items.doc: The domain constructor preserves its half coset.
items.statement: theorem new_halfCoset (c : Coset) : (new c).halfCoset = c

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.CircleDomain.logSize
items.doc: Domain log size. A domain contains a half coset and its conjugate.
items.statement: def logSize (D : CircleDomain) : Nat

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.CircleDomain.logSize_eq
items.doc: A domain's log size is one more than its half coset's log size.
items.statement: theorem logSize_eq (D : CircleDomain) : D.logSize = D.halfCoset.logSize + 1

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.CircleDomain.size
items.doc: Declared number of index positions, not necessarily the number of distinct points.
items.statement: def size (D : CircleDomain) : Nat

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.CircleDomain.size_eq
items.doc: A domain's size is two to its log size.
items.statement: theorem size_eq (D : CircleDomain) : D.size = 2 ^ D.logSize

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.CircleDomain.indexAt
items.doc: The `i`th domain index: first the half coset, then the conjugate coset.
items.statement: def indexAt (D : CircleDomain) (i : Nat) : CirclePointIndex

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.CircleDomain.indexAt_def
items.doc: Domain indexing splits at the half-coset size.

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.CircleDomain.pointAt
items.doc: The circle point at the `i`th domain index.
items.statement: def pointAt (D : CircleDomain) (i : Nat) : Point

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.CircleDomain.pointAt_def
items.doc: A domain point is the interpretation of its index.
items.statement:
theorem pointAt_def (D : CircleDomain) (i : Nat) :
    D.pointAt i = CirclePointIndex.toPoint (D.indexAt i)

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.CircleDomain.size_eq_two_mul_halfSize
items.doc: A circle domain has twice as many indices as its half coset.
items.statement:
theorem size_eq_two_mul_halfSize (D : CircleDomain) :
    D.size = 2 * D.halfCoset.size

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.CircleDomain.indexAt_left
items.doc: Indices in the first half of a circle domain come from its half coset.
items.statement:
theorem indexAt_left (D : CircleDomain) (i : Nat) (hi : i < D.halfCoset.size) :
    D.indexAt i = D.halfCoset.indexAt i

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.CircleDomain.indexAt_of_le
items.doc: Indices at or beyond the half-coset size come from the conjugate half.
items.statement:
theorem indexAt_of_le (D : CircleDomain) (i : Nat) (hi : D.halfCoset.size ≤ i) :
    D.indexAt i = -D.halfCoset.indexAt (i - D.halfCoset.size)

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.CircleDomain.indexAt_right
items.doc: Indices in the second half come from the negated half coset.
items.statement:
theorem indexAt_right (D : CircleDomain) (i : Nat) :
    D.indexAt (D.halfCoset.size + i) = -D.halfCoset.indexAt i

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.CanonicCoset
items.doc: A canonical STWO coset `G_{2n} + <G_n>` for `1 ≤ logSize < logOrder`.
items.statement:
structure CanonicCoset where
  logSize : Nat
  one_le_logSize : 1 ≤ logSize
  logSize_succ_le_logOrder : logSize + 1 ≤ logOrder

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.CanonicCoset.coset
items.doc: The full canonical coset `G_{2n} + <G_n>`.
items.statement: def coset (c : CanonicCoset) : Coset

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.CanonicCoset.coset_eq
items.doc: A canonical coset is the odds coset at its log size.
items.statement:
theorem coset_eq (c : CanonicCoset) :
    c.coset = Coset.odds c.logSize c.logSize_succ_le_logOrder

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.CanonicCoset.halfCoset
items.doc: The half coset used to form the canonical circle domain.
items.statement: def halfCoset (c : CanonicCoset) : Coset

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.CanonicCoset.halfCoset_eq
items.doc: The canonical half coset is the half-odds coset one log size below.
items.statement:
theorem halfCoset_eq (c : CanonicCoset) :
    c.halfCoset = Coset.halfOdds (c.logSize - 1) (by
      have hOne := c.one_le_logSize
      have hBound := c.logSize_succ_le_logOrder
      omega)

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.CanonicCoset.coset_valid
items.doc: The full canonical coset has a step of the declared order.
items.statement: theorem coset_valid (c : CanonicCoset) : c.coset.Valid

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.CanonicCoset.halfCoset_valid
items.doc: The canonical half coset has a step of the declared order.
items.statement: theorem halfCoset_valid (c : CanonicCoset) : c.halfCoset.Valid

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.CanonicCoset.circleDomain
items.doc: The canonical circle domain with the same log size.
items.statement: def circleDomain (c : CanonicCoset) : CircleDomain

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.CanonicCoset.circleDomain_eq
items.doc: The canonical domain is built from the canonical half coset.
items.statement:
theorem circleDomain_eq (c : CanonicCoset) :
    c.circleDomain = CircleDomain.new c.halfCoset

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.CanonicCoset.circleDomain_logSize
items.doc: The canonical circle domain preserves the canonical coset log size.
items.statement: theorem circleDomain_logSize (c : CanonicCoset) : c.circleDomain.logSize = c.logSize

items.name: Mersenne31.Circle.CanonicCoset.circleDomain_size
items.doc: The canonical circle domain has `2^logSize` indices.
items.statement: theorem circleDomain_size (c : CanonicCoset) : c.circleDomain.size = 2 ^ c.logSize

modules.title: FastMersenne31 — UInt32-backed Mersenne-31 field arithmetic
modules.doc:
This module provides a native-word implementation of Mersenne31 arithmetic as a
sidecar to the canonical `Mersenne31.Field := ZMod Mersenne31.fieldSize`
model.

Fast field values are stored as canonical `UInt32` representatives below
`2^31 - 1`. Multiplication reduces a bounded `UInt64` product using the Mersenne
identity `2^31 ≡ 1 (mod 2^31 - 1)`: split at bit 31, add the halves, then perform
one final subtraction if needed.

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.Field
items.doc:
The fast native-word Mersenne31 field carrier, stored as a canonical `UInt32`
representative below the prime modulus.
items.statement: abbrev Field : Type

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.modulus
items.doc: The Mersenne31 prime `2^31 - 1` as a native `UInt32`.
items.statement: def modulus : UInt32

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.modulus_toNat
items.doc: The native `UInt32` modulus agrees with the mathematical Mersenne31 modulus.
items.statement: theorem modulus_toNat : modulus.toNat = Mersenne31.fieldSize

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.raw
items.doc: The raw native word backing a fast Mersenne31 element.
items.statement: def raw (x : Field) : UInt32

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.raw_mk
items.doc: Reading the raw word from a subtype literal returns its stored word.
items.statement:
theorem raw_mk (x : UInt32) (h : x.toNat < Mersenne31.fieldSize) :
    raw ⟨x, h⟩ = x

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.raw_eq_val
items.doc: `raw` is the underlying `UInt32` value.
items.statement: theorem raw_eq_val (x : Field) : raw x = x.val

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.instZeroField
items.doc: Use the canonical zero representative for standard `0` notation.
items.statement: instance instZeroField : Zero Field

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.instOneField
items.doc: Use the canonical one representative for standard `1` notation.
items.statement: instance instOneField : One Field

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.ofNat
items.doc: Convert a natural number into fast representation by reducing modulo Mersenne31.
items.statement: def ofNat (n : Nat) : Field

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.toNat
items.doc: Convert a fast Mersenne31 element to its canonical natural representative.
items.statement: def toNat (x : Field) : Nat

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.toNat_mk
items.doc:
Reading the natural representative from a subtype literal returns the stored word's
natural value.
items.statement:
theorem toNat_mk (x : UInt32) (h : x.toNat < Mersenne31.fieldSize) :
    toNat ⟨x, h⟩ = x.toNat

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.toNat_eq_val_toNat
items.doc: `toNat` is the natural value of the underlying `UInt32` word.
items.statement: theorem toNat_eq_val_toNat (x : Field) : toNat x = x.val.toNat

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.ofField
items.doc: Convert from the canonical `ZMod` Mersenne31 field into fast representation.
items.statement: def ofField (x : Mersenne31.Field) : Field

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.toField
items.doc: Convert a fast Mersenne31 element to the canonical `ZMod` field.
items.statement: def toField (x : Field) : Mersenne31.Field

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.ofUInt32
items.doc: Convert a 32-bit word into fast representation.
items.statement: def ofUInt32 (x : UInt32) : Field

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.ofInt
items.doc: Convert an integer into fast representation.
items.statement: def ofInt (z : Int) : Field

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.instNatCastField
items.doc: Use `ofNat` for natural-number casts into fast Mersenne31.
items.statement: instance instNatCastField : NatCast Field

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.instIntCastField
items.doc: Interpret integer casts through the canonical Mersenne31 field.
items.statement: instance instIntCastField : IntCast Field

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.instNNRatCastField
items.doc: Interpret nonnegative rational casts through the canonical Mersenne31 field.
items.statement: instance instNNRatCastField : NNRatCast Field

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.instRatCastField
items.doc: Interpret rational casts through the canonical Mersenne31 field.
items.statement: instance instRatCastField : RatCast Field

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.raw_zero
items.doc: The raw word backing fast zero is zero.
items.statement: theorem raw_zero : raw (0 : Field) = 0

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.raw_one
items.doc: The raw word backing fast one is one.
items.statement: theorem raw_one : raw (1 : Field) = 1

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.toNat_zero
items.doc: The natural representative of fast zero is zero.
items.statement: theorem toNat_zero : toNat (0 : Field) = 0

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.toNat_one
items.doc: The natural representative of fast one is one.
items.statement: theorem toNat_one : toNat (1 : Field) = 1

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.toNat_ofNat
items.doc:
Converting a natural number to fast form and reading it back gives its canonical
representative modulo Mersenne31.
items.statement:
theorem toNat_ofNat (n : Nat) :
    toNat (ofNat n) = n % Mersenne31.fieldSize

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.toField_ofNat
items.doc:
Converting a natural number to fast form agrees with the same natural cast in the
canonical field.
items.statement:
theorem toField_ofNat (n : Nat) :
    toField (ofNat n) = (n : Mersenne31.Field)

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.toField_ofUInt32
items.doc:
Converting a `UInt32` to fast form agrees with casting its natural value into the
canonical field.
items.statement:
theorem toField_ofUInt32 (x : UInt32) :
    toField (ofUInt32 x) = (x.toNat : Mersenne31.Field)

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.toNat_ofUInt32
items.doc:
Converting a `UInt32` to fast form and reading it back gives its value modulo
Mersenne31.
items.statement:
theorem toNat_ofUInt32 (x : UInt32) :
    toNat (ofUInt32 x) = x.toNat % Mersenne31.fieldSize

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.toNat_ofField
items.doc:
Converting from the canonical field to fast form and reading the natural
representative returns the canonical `ZMod` representative.
items.statement: theorem toNat_ofField (x : Mersenne31.Field) : toNat (ofField x) = x.val

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.toField_ofField
items.doc: Converting from the canonical `ZMod` field to fast form and back is the identity.
items.statement:
theorem toField_ofField (x : Mersenne31.Field) :
    toField (ofField x) = x

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.toField_ofInt
items.doc: Converting an integer to fast form agrees with casting it into the canonical field.
items.statement:
theorem toField_ofInt (z : Int) :
    toField (ofInt z) = (z : Mersenne31.Field)

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.ofField_toField
items.doc: Converting from fast form to the canonical `ZMod` field and back is the identity.
items.statement:
theorem ofField_toField (x : Field) :
    ofField (toField x) = x

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.toField_zero
items.doc: The fast zero maps to zero in the canonical field.
items.statement: theorem toField_zero : toField (0 : Field) = 0

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.toField_one
items.doc: The fast one maps to one in the canonical field.
items.statement: theorem toField_one : toField (1 : Field) = 1

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.toField_natCast
items.doc: Natural casts in the fast field agree with natural casts in the canonical field.
items.statement:
theorem toField_natCast (n : Nat) :
    toField (n : Field) = (n : Mersenne31.Field)

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.toField_intCast
items.doc: Integer casts in the fast field agree with integer casts in the canonical field.
items.statement:
theorem toField_intCast (n : Int) :
    toField (n : Field) = (n : Mersenne31.Field)

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.toField_nnratCast
items.doc: Nonnegative rational casts in the fast field agree with canonical-field casts.
items.statement:
theorem toField_nnratCast (q : ℚ≥0) :
    toField (q : Field) = (q : Mersenne31.Field)

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.toField_ratCast
items.doc: Rational casts in the fast field agree with canonical-field casts.
items.statement:
theorem toField_ratCast (q : ℚ) :
    toField (q : Field) = (q : Mersenne31.Field)

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.add
items.doc: Fast modular addition.
items.statement: def add (x y : Field) : Field

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.instAddField
items.doc: Use fast modular addition for the standard `+` notation on Mersenne31 fast elements.
items.statement: instance instAddField : Add Field

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.toField_add
items.doc: Fast addition agrees with addition in the canonical `ZMod` Mersenne31 field.
items.statement:
theorem toField_add (x y : Field) :
    toField (x + y) = toField x + toField y

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.sub
items.doc:
Fast modular subtraction, using `x - y` when no underflow occurs and
`x + p - y` otherwise.
items.statement: def sub (x y : Field) : Field

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.instSubField
items.doc: Use fast modular subtraction for the standard `-` notation on Mersenne31 fast elements.
items.statement: instance instSubField : Sub Field

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.toField_sub
items.doc: Fast subtraction agrees with subtraction in the canonical `ZMod` Mersenne31 field.
items.statement: theorem toField_sub (x y : Field) : toField (x - y) = toField x - toField y

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.neg
items.doc: Fast modular negation. Zero remains zero; nonzero `x` maps to `p - x`.
items.statement: def neg (x : Field) : Field

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.instNegField
items.doc: Use fast modular negation for the standard unary `-` notation on Mersenne31 fast elements.
items.statement: instance instNegField : Neg Field

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.toField_neg
items.doc: Fast negation agrees with negation in the canonical `ZMod` Mersenne31 field.
items.statement: theorem toField_neg (x : Field) : toField (-x) = -toField x

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.mul
items.doc: Fast modular multiplication.
items.statement: def mul (x y : Field) : Field

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.instMulField
items.doc:
Use fast modular multiplication for the standard `*` notation on Mersenne31 fast
elements.
items.statement: instance instMulField : Mul Field

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.instNatSMulField
items.doc: Natural scalar multiplication is multiplication by the corresponding fast natural cast.
items.statement: instance instNatSMulField : SMul Nat Field

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.instIntSMulField
items.doc: Integer scalar multiplication is multiplication by the corresponding fast integer cast.
items.statement: instance instIntSMulField : SMul Int Field

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.instNNRatSMulField
items.doc: Nonnegative rational scalar multiplication is transported through the canonical field.
items.statement: instance instNNRatSMulField : SMul ℚ≥0 Field

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.instRatSMulField
items.doc: Rational scalar multiplication is transported through the canonical field.
items.statement: instance instRatSMulField : SMul ℚ Field

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.toField_mul
items.doc:
Fast multiplication agrees with multiplication in the canonical `ZMod` Mersenne31
field.
items.statement: theorem toField_mul (x y : Field) : toField (x * y) = toField x * toField y

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.square
items.doc: Fast squaring.
items.statement: def square (x : Field) : Field

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.toField_square
items.doc: Fast squaring agrees with multiplying the canonical field value by itself.
items.statement: theorem toField_square (x : Field) : toField (square x) = toField x * toField x

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.pow
items.doc: Exponentiation over the fast representation using binary exponentiation.
items.statement: def pow (x : Field) (n : Nat) : Field

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.instPowFieldNat
items.doc: Use fast binary exponentiation for natural powers.
items.statement: instance instPowFieldNat : Pow Field Nat

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.toField_pow
items.doc: Fast natural-power computation agrees with powers in the canonical field.
items.statement: theorem toField_pow (x : Field) (n : Nat) : toField (pow x n) = toField x ^ n

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.inv
items.doc:
Fast modular inversion using a fixed Fermat addition chain for `x^(p - 2)`.

The exponent is `p - 2 = 2147483645 = 0x7FFFFFFD`. The chain builds the
hex digits `7 F F F F F F D` by repeatedly applying `shift4Mul`, which raises
the accumulator to the 16th power and multiplies by the next 4-bit digit.

This sends zero to zero, matching Lean's field inverse convention.
items.statement: def inv (x : Field) : Field

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.instInvField
items.doc: Use Fermat-based fast inversion for the standard inverse notation.
items.statement: instance instInvField : Inv Field

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.toField_inv
items.doc: Fast inversion agrees with inversion in the canonical field.
items.statement: theorem toField_inv (x : Field) : toField x⁻¹ = (toField x)⁻¹

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.div
items.doc: Division through inversion and fast multiplication.
items.statement: def div (x y : Field) : Field

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.instDivField
items.doc: Use fast inversion and multiplication for the standard `/` notation.
items.statement: instance instDivField : Div Field

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.toField_div
items.doc: Fast division agrees with division in the canonical field.
items.statement: theorem toField_div (x y : Field) : toField (x / y) = toField x / toField y

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.instPowFieldInt
items.doc: Use fast natural powers and inversion for integer powers.
items.statement: instance instPowFieldInt : Pow Field Int

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.toField_nsmul
items.doc: Fast natural scalar multiplication agrees with canonical-field scalar multiplication.
items.statement: theorem toField_nsmul (n : Nat) (x : Field) : toField (n • x) = n • toField x

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.toField_zsmul
items.doc: Fast integer scalar multiplication agrees with canonical-field scalar multiplication.
items.statement: theorem toField_zsmul (n : Int) (x : Field) : toField (n • x) = n • toField x

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.toField_npow
items.doc: Standard fast natural powers agree with powers in the canonical field.
items.statement: theorem toField_npow (x : Field) (n : Nat) : toField (x ^ n) = toField x ^ n

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.toField_zpow
items.doc: Standard fast integer powers agree with integer powers in the canonical field.
items.statement: theorem toField_zpow (x : Field) (n : Int) : toField (x ^ n) = toField x ^ n

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.toField_nnqsmul
items.doc:
Fast nonnegative rational scalar multiplication agrees with canonical-field scalar
multiplication.
items.statement: theorem toField_nnqsmul (q : ℚ≥0) (x : Field) : toField (q • x) = q • toField x

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.toField_qsmul
items.doc: Fast rational scalar multiplication agrees with canonical-field scalar multiplication.
items.statement: theorem toField_qsmul (q : ℚ) (x : Field) : toField (q • x) = q • toField x

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.ringEquiv
items.doc: Ring equivalence between the fast representation and canonical `Mersenne31.Field`.
items.statement: def ringEquiv : Field ≃+* Mersenne31.Field

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.ringEquiv_apply
items.doc: Applying `ringEquiv` is the same as interpreting a fast value canonically.
items.statement: theorem ringEquiv_apply (x : Field) : ringEquiv x = toField x

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.ringEquiv_symm_apply
items.doc: Applying the inverse `ringEquiv` converts a canonical value into fast form.
items.statement: theorem ringEquiv_symm_apply (x : Mersenne31.Field) : ringEquiv.symm x = ofField x

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.instField
items.doc: Field instance transferred from canonical Mersenne31 through `toField`.
items.statement: instance (priority := low) instField : _root_.Field Field

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.instCommRing
items.doc: Commutative-ring instance inherited from the transferred field structure.
items.statement: instance (priority := low) instCommRing : CommRing Field

items.name: Mersenne31.Fast.instNonBinaryField
items.doc: Fast Mersenne31 is a non-binary field.
items.statement: instance (priority := low) instNonBinaryField : NonBinaryField Field

modules.title: Montgomery Reduction
modules.doc:
Radix-generic specification and correctness lemmas for single-word Montgomery reduction.
Word-specific implementations refine these results in sibling modules.

items.name: Montgomery.reduceNat
items.doc: Natural-number Montgomery reduction used to specify the native-word reducer.
items.statement: def reduceNat (R p negInv x : ℕ) : ℕ

items.name: Montgomery.reduceNatQuotient
items.doc: The quotient before the final conditional subtraction in Montgomery reduction.
items.statement: def reduceNatQuotient (R p negInv x : ℕ) : ℕ

items.name: Montgomery.reduceNatQuotient_lt_two_mul
items.doc: The pre-subtraction quotient is below twice the modulus.
items.statement:
theorem reduceNatQuotient_lt_two_mul (R p negInv x : ℕ)
    (hR : 0 < R) (hp : 0 < p) (hx : x < p * R) :
    reduceNatQuotient R p negInv x < 2 * p

items.name: Montgomery.reduceNat_lt
items.doc: Montgomery reduction returns a canonical representative.
items.statement:
theorem reduceNat_lt (R p negInv x : ℕ)
    (hR : 0 < R) (hp : 0 < p) (hx : x < p * R) :
    reduceNat R p negInv x < p

items.name: Montgomery.dvd_add
items.doc:
The Montgomery divisibility identity: if `(negInv * p) % R = R - 1` (i.e.
`negInv = -p⁻¹ mod R`), then `R ∣ x + ((x mod R)·negInv mod R)·p` for every `x`.
items.statement:
theorem dvd_add (R p negInv : ℕ) (hR : 0 < R)
    (hnegInv : negInv * p % R = R - 1) (x : ℕ) :
    R ∣ x + ((x % R * negInv) % R) * p

items.name: Montgomery.reduceNatQuotient_cast
items.doc: The pre-subtraction quotient represents multiplication by `R⁻¹` in `ZMod p`.
items.statement:
theorem reduceNatQuotient_cast (R p negInv : ℕ) [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (hR : 0 < R)
    (hnegInv : negInv * p % R = R - 1) (hRne : (R : ZMod p) ≠ 0) (x : ℕ) :
    (reduceNatQuotient R p negInv x : ZMod p) = (x : ZMod p) * (R : ZMod p)⁻¹

items.name: Montgomery.reduceNat_cast
items.doc: Montgomery reduction represents multiplication by `R⁻¹` in `ZMod p`.
items.statement:
theorem reduceNat_cast (R p negInv : ℕ) [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (hR : 0 < R)
    (hnegInv : negInv * p % R = R - 1) (hRne : (R : ZMod p) ≠ 0) (x : ℕ) :
    (reduceNat R p negInv x : ZMod p) = (x : ZMod p) * (R : ZMod p)⁻¹

items.name: Montgomery.natCast_inj_of_lt
items.doc: Two naturals below `p` are equal once their `ZMod p` casts agree.
items.statement:
theorem natCast_inj_of_lt {p a b : ℕ} (h : (a : ZMod p) = (b : ZMod p))
    (ha : a < p) (hb : b < p) : a = b

modules.title: Word-sized divsteps: coefficient bounds
modules.doc:
Unfolding lemmas for `gcdInner` of `Montgomery/DivstepDefs`, and the bound on the entries of
its transition matrix. A chunk of at most 31 divsteps keeps `|f| + |g| ≤ 2^31` in each row.
The linear combinations of the multi-limb inversion runtimes require that bound.

items.name: Montgomery.gcdInner_zero
items.doc: Unfolding of the empty divstep run.
items.statement:
theorem gcdInner_zero (a b : UInt64) (f0 g0 f1 g1 : Int) :
    gcdInner 0 a b f0 g0 f1 g1 = (a, b, f0, g0, f1, g1)

items.name: Montgomery.gcdInner_succ
items.doc: Unfolding of one divstep.
items.statement:
theorem gcdInner_succ (rounds : Nat) (a b : UInt64) (f0 g0 f1 g1 : Int) :
    gcdInner (rounds + 1) a b f0 g0 f1 g1 =
      if a &&& 1 == 0 then
        gcdInner rounds (a >>> 1) b f0 g0 (f1 * 2) (g1 * 2)
      else if a < b then
        gcdInner rounds ((b - a) >>> 1) a (f1 - f0) (g1 - g0) (f0 * 2) (g0 * 2)
      else
        gcdInner rounds ((a - b) >>> 1) b (f0 - f1) (g0 - g1) (f1 * 2) (g1 * 2)

items.doc: Transition entries at most double per divstep.

items.name: Montgomery.gcdInner_natAbs_le_31
items.doc: Chunks of at most 31 divsteps satisfy the linear-combination bound.

    (hnegInv : negInv.toNat * modulus % 2 ^ 32 = 2 ^ 32 - 1)

items.name: Montgomery.Native32.Mont32Field
items.doc: Per-field data for a fast 32-bit Montgomery field.
items.statement:
class Mont32Field (modulus : ℕ) where
  /-- `modulus` is prime. -/
  prime : modulus.Prime
  /-- `modulus` as a 32-bit word. -/
  modulus32 : UInt32
  /-- `modulus` as a 64-bit word. -/
  modulus64 : UInt64
  /-- `2^32 mod modulus`, the Montgomery representation of one. -/
  rModModulus : UInt32
  /-- `(2^32)^2 mod modulus`, used to enter Montgomery form. -/
  r2ModModulus : UInt64
  /-- `-modulus⁻¹ mod 2^32`, used by Montgomery reduction. -/
  montgomeryNegInv : UInt32
  modulus32_toNat : modulus32.toNat = modulus := by decide
  modulus64_toNat : modulus64.toNat = modulus := by decide
  two_lt_modulus : 2 < modulus := by decide
  modulus_lt_two_pow_31 : modulus < 2 ^ 31 := by decide
  rModModulus_toNat : rModModulus.toNat = 2 ^ 32 % modulus := by decide
  r2ModModulus_toNat : r2ModModulus.toNat = (2 ^ 32) ^ 2 % modulus := by decide
  montgomeryNegInv_mul_modulus_mod_two_pow_32 :
    (montgomeryNegInv.toNat * modulus) % 2 ^ 32 = 2 ^ 32 - 1 := by decide

modules.title: Native Montgomery arithmetic over four 64-bit limbs
modules.doc:
Raw word operations for prime moduli below `2 ^ 256`, represented as four 64-bit limbs
(`Limbs4`); the definitions live in the zero-import module `Montgomery/Native64x4Defs`.  Each
word helper's specification exhibits the pair it returns, so a chain of `let (s, c) := ...`
bindings unfolds to a linear system over naturals that `omega` closes.

## Main results

* `condSub_toNat`, `condSubWide_toNat`, `add_toNat`, `sub_toNat`, `neg_toNat` — correctness
  of the raw operations
* `addLimbs_spec`, `subLimbs_spec` — the underlying carry/borrow chains
* `mac_spec`, `mulHi_spec` — the widening multiply-accumulate

items.name: Montgomery.Native64x4.adc_spec
items.doc: Add-with-carry, existential form: the exact sum identity with a one-bit carry.
items.statement:
theorem adc_spec (x y c : UInt64) (hc : c.toNat ≤ 1) :
    ∃ s co : UInt64, adc x y c = (s, co) ∧
      s.toNat + 2 ^ 64 * co.toNat = x.toNat + y.toNat + c.toNat ∧ co.toNat ≤ 1

items.name: Montgomery.Native64x4.sbb_spec
items.doc:
Subtract-with-borrow, existential form: the exact difference identity with a one-bit
borrow.
items.statement:
theorem sbb_spec (x y b : UInt64) (hb : b.toNat ≤ 1) :
    ∃ d bo : UInt64, sbb x y b = (d, bo) ∧
      d.toNat + y.toNat + b.toNat = x.toNat + 2 ^ 64 * bo.toNat ∧ bo.toNat ≤ 1

items.name: Montgomery.Native64x4.mulHi_spec
items.doc: The low and high words recompose the exact `64 × 64` product.
items.statement:
theorem mulHi_spec (a b : UInt64) :
    (a * b).toNat + 2 ^ 64 * (mulHi a b).toNat = a.toNat * b.toNat

items.name: Montgomery.Native64x4.mac_spec
items.doc: Multiply-accumulate, existential form: `t + a * b + c` never overflows two words.
items.statement:
theorem mac_spec (t a b c : UInt64) :
    ∃ lo hi : UInt64, mac t a b c = (lo, hi) ∧
      lo.toNat + 2 ^ 64 * hi.toNat = t.toNat + a.toNat * b.toNat + c.toNat

items.name: Montgomery.Native64x4.montM_toNat
items.doc: The Montgomery multiplier agrees with its natural-number specification.
items.statement:
theorem montM_toNat (s negInv : UInt64) :
    (montM s negInv).toNat = s.toNat * negInv.toNat % 2 ^ 64

items.name: Montgomery.Native64x4.carry_chain_sum
items.doc: Weighted telescoping of a four-step carry chain.

items.name: Montgomery.Native64x4.borrow_chain_sum
items.doc: Weighted telescoping of a four-step borrow chain.

items.name: Montgomery.Native64x4.addLimbs_spec
items.doc: The limbwise sum and the top carry recompose the sum of the inputs.
items.statement:
theorem addLimbs_spec (a b : Limbs4) :
    ∃ s0 s1 s2 s3 c : UInt64, addLimbs a b = (s0, s1, s2, s3, c) ∧ c.toNat ≤ 1 ∧
      (⟨s0, s1, s2, s3⟩ : Limbs4).toNat + 2 ^ 256 * c.toNat = a.toNat + b.toNat

items.name: Montgomery.Native64x4.subLimbs_spec
items.doc: The limbwise difference and the final borrow recompose the difference of the inputs.
items.statement:
theorem subLimbs_spec (a b : Limbs4) :
    ∃ d0 d1 d2 d3 bo : UInt64, subLimbs a b = (d0, d1, d2, d3, bo) ∧ bo.toNat ≤ 1 ∧
      (⟨d0, d1, d2, d3⟩ : Limbs4).toNat + b.toNat = a.toNat + 2 ^ 256 * bo.toNat

items.name: Montgomery.Native64x4.condSub_toNat
items.doc: `condSub` subtracts the modulus exactly when the input is at least the modulus.
items.statement:
theorem condSub_toNat (q t : Limbs4) :
    (condSub q t).toNat = if t.toNat < q.toNat then t.toNat else t.toNat - q.toNat

items.name: Montgomery.Native64x4.condSub_lt
items.doc: `condSub` returns a canonical representative for inputs below `2 * q`.
items.statement:
theorem condSub_lt (q t : Limbs4) (h : t.toNat < 2 * q.toNat) :
    (condSub q t).toNat < q.toNat

items.name: Montgomery.Native64x4.condSubWide_toNat
items.doc:
`condSubWide` subtracts the modulus exactly when an accumulator below `2 * q` is at least
the modulus.
items.statement:
theorem condSubWide_toNat (q : Limbs4) (t : State5) (h : t.toNat < 2 * q.toNat) :
    (condSubWide q t).toNat = if t.toNat < q.toNat then t.toNat else t.toNat - q.toNat

items.name: Montgomery.Native64x4.condSubWide_lt
items.doc: `condSubWide` returns a canonical representative for accumulators below `2 * q`.
items.statement:
theorem condSubWide_lt (q : Limbs4) (t : State5) (h : t.toNat < 2 * q.toNat) :
    (condSubWide q t).toNat < q.toNat

items.name: Montgomery.Native64x4.add_toNat
items.doc: Modular addition is correct for canonical inputs of any modulus.
items.statement:
theorem add_toNat (q a b : Limbs4) (haq : a.toNat < q.toNat) (hbq : b.toNat < q.toNat) :
    (add q a b).toNat = (a.toNat + b.toNat) % q.toNat

items.name: Montgomery.Native64x4.add_lt
items.statement:
theorem add_lt (q a b : Limbs4) (haq : a.toNat < q.toNat) (hbq : b.toNat < q.toNat) :
    (add q a b).toNat < q.toNat

items.name: Montgomery.Native64x4.sub_toNat
items.doc: Modular subtraction is correct for canonical inputs of any modulus.
items.statement:
theorem sub_toNat (q a b : Limbs4) (haq : a.toNat < q.toNat) (hbq : b.toNat < q.toNat) :
    (sub q a b).toNat = (a.toNat + (q.toNat - b.toNat)) % q.toNat

items.name: Montgomery.Native64x4.sub_lt
items.statement:
theorem sub_lt (q a b : Limbs4) (haq : a.toNat < q.toNat) (hbq : b.toNat < q.toNat) :
    (sub q a b).toNat < q.toNat

items.name: Montgomery.Native64x4.neg_toNat
items.doc: Modular negation is correct for canonical inputs of any modulus.
items.statement:
theorem neg_toNat (q a : Limbs4) (haq : a.toNat < q.toNat) :
    (neg q a).toNat = (q.toNat - a.toNat) % q.toNat

items.name: Montgomery.Native64x4.neg_lt
items.statement: theorem neg_lt (q a : Limbs4) (haq : a.toNat < q.toNat) : (neg q a).toNat < q.toNat

modules.title: Serialization of the four-limb Montgomery carrier
modules.doc:
`Native64x4.FastField modulus` stores a Montgomery residue in four 64-bit limbs.  Its canonical
natural is the value after one Montgomery reduction, `FastField.toNat`, so the bytes agree with
the `ZMod modulus` codec (`toBytes_ofField`, `toNat_ofField`).  Decoding converts through
`ofField`.

items.doc: The canonical natural of a fast element is the residue of its canonical field value.
items.statement: theorem toNat_eq_val_toField (x : FastField modulus) : toNat x = (toField x).val

items.name: Montgomery.Native64x4.FastField.toNat_ofField
items.doc: Carrier agreement: the canonical natural of `ofField n` is the residue `n.val`.
items.statement: theorem toNat_ofField (n : ZMod modulus) : toNat (ofField n) = n.val

items.name: Montgomery.Native64x4.FastField.ofField_cast_toNat
items.statement: theorem ofField_cast_toNat (x : FastField modulus) : ofField (toNat x : ZMod modulus) = x

items.name: Montgomery.Native64x4.FastField.canonicalNat_bound
items.statement: theorem canonicalNat_bound : CanonicalNat.bound (FastField modulus) = modulus

items.name: Montgomery.Native64x4.FastField.canonicalNat_toNat
items.statement: theorem canonicalNat_toNat (x : FastField modulus) : CanonicalNat.toNat x = toNat x

items.name: Montgomery.Native64x4.FastField.canonicalNat_ofNat
items.statement:
theorem canonicalNat_ofNat (n : ℕ) :
    CanonicalNat.ofNat (F := FastField modulus) n = ofField (n : ZMod modulus)

items.name: Montgomery.Native64x4.FastField.byteCodec_width
items.statement: theorem byteCodec_width : ByteCodec.width (FastField modulus) = Bytes.bytesFor modulus

items.name: Montgomery.Native64x4.FastField.toBytes_ofField
items.doc: The fast carrier and `ZMod modulus` encode the same element identically.
items.statement:
theorem toBytes_ofField (n : ZMod modulus) :
    ByteCodec.toBytes (ofField n) = ByteCodec.toBytes n

items.name: Montgomery.Native64x4.FastField.toBytes_eq_toBytes_toField
items.doc: Encoding then converting to the spec field is encoding in the spec field.
items.statement:
theorem toBytes_eq_toBytes_toField (x : FastField modulus) :
    ByteCodec.toBytes x = ByteCodec.toBytes (toField x)

modules.title: Four-limb Montgomery arithmetic: runtime definitions (zero-import)
modules.doc:
The runtime definitions of the four-limb Montgomery arithmetic over 64-bit limbs; all
correctness statements live in `CompPoly.Fields.Montgomery.Native64x4`, which imports this
one.  Products widen through `mulHi` (four 32-bit partial products) and every word helper
returns a pair the caller destructures, so nothing is boxed.

This module deliberately has **zero imports**, for `precompileModules` consumers.

items.doc: A 256-bit value as four little-endian 64-bit limbs.
items.statement:
structure Limbs4 where
  /-- Limb of weight `2 ^ 0`. -/

  /-- Limb of weight `2 ^ 64`. -/
  l1 : UInt64
  /-- Limb of weight `2 ^ 128`. -/
  l2 : UInt64
  /-- Limb of weight `2 ^ 192`. -/

deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited

items.note:
## Limbwise addition and subtraction

Chains return flat words and a `Limbs4` is built only inside a branch: one bound before the
branch is allocated whether or not that side runs.

modules.title: Fast four-limb Montgomery fields
modules.doc:
The carrier `{ x : Limbs4 // x.toNat < modulus }` stores the Montgomery residue
`x * 2 ^ 256 mod modulus` for any prime modulus below `2 ^ 256`; `toField` divides by `2 ^ 256`
and lands in `ZMod modulus`, and all arithmetic is transported along that ring isomorphism.

## Main results

* `FastField` — the carrier, `{ x : Limbs4 // x.toNat < modulus }`
* `toField_add`, `toField_mul`, … — `@[simp]` equivalences with the canonical field
* `Mont64x4Field` — the per-field constants class
* `ringEquiv`, `instField` — the ring isomorphism and the transferred `Field` instance

items.name: Montgomery.Native64x4.Mont64x4Field
items.doc:
Per-field data for a fast four-limb Montgomery field with radix `R = 2 ^ 256`.  All side
conditions are concrete numeral facts, discharged by `decide` at instantiation.
items.statement:
class Mont64x4Field (modulus : ℕ) where
  /-- `modulus` is prime. -/
  prime : modulus.Prime
  /-- The modulus in four 64-bit limbs. -/
  modulusLimbs : Limbs4
  /-- `2 ^ 256 mod modulus`, the Montgomery representation of one. -/
  rModModulus : Limbs4
  /-- `(2 ^ 256) ^ 2 mod modulus`, used to enter Montgomery form. -/
  r2ModModulus : Limbs4
  /-- `-modulus⁻¹ mod 2 ^ 64`, used by Montgomery reduction. -/
  montgomeryNegInv : UInt64
  modulusLimbs_toNat : modulusLimbs.toNat = modulus := by decide
  two_lt_modulus : 2 < modulus := by decide
  rModModulus_toNat : rModModulus.toNat = 2 ^ 256 % modulus := by decide
  r2ModModulus_toNat : r2ModModulus.toNat = (2 ^ 256) ^ 2 % modulus := by decide
  montgomeryNegInv_mul_modulus_mod_two_pow_64 :
    montgomeryNegInv.toNat * modulus % 2 ^ 64 = 2 ^ 64 - 1 := by decide

items.statement: theorem negInv_mul_q : P.montgomeryNegInv.toNat * P.modulusLimbs.toNat % 2 ^ 64 = 2 ^ 64 - 1

modules.doc:
Correctness of the checked inversion of `Montgomery/Native64x4InvDefs`: `invGcdRaw`
computes the field inverse and `FastField.invGcd` is its proof-carrying wrapper.  The
divstep coefficient bound comes from `Montgomery/Divstep`.  This module proves the mac-width
safety of the candidate for the five-word linear combinations.

items.name: Montgomery.Native64x4.subLimbs_borrow_eq_one_iff
items.doc: The final borrow decides the numeric order.
items.statement:
theorem subLimbs_borrow_eq_one_iff {a b : Limbs4} {d0 d1 d2 d3 bo : UInt64}
    (e : subLimbs a b = (d0, d1, d2, d3, bo)) : bo = 1 ↔ a.toNat < b.toNat

items.name: Montgomery.Native64x4.mulWord_spec
items.doc: `mulWord` is the exact five-word product.
items.statement:
theorem mulWord_spec (x : Limbs4) (k : UInt64) :
    ∃ w0 w1 w2 w3 w4 : UInt64, mulWord x k = (w0, w1, w2, w3, w4) ∧
      w0.toNat + 2 ^ 64 * w1.toNat + 2 ^ 128 * w2.toNat + 2 ^ 192 * w3.toNat +
        2 ^ 256 * w4.toNat = x.toNat * k.toNat

items.name: Montgomery.Native64x4.add5_spec
items.doc: `add5` is the exact five-word sum with a one-bit carry.
items.statement:
theorem add5_spec (a0 a1 a2 a3 a4 b0 b1 b2 b3 b4 : UInt64) :
    ∃ s0 s1 s2 s3 s4 c : UInt64,
      add5 a0 a1 a2 a3 a4 b0 b1 b2 b3 b4 = (s0, s1, s2, s3, s4, c) ∧ c.toNat ≤ 1 ∧
      s0.toNat + 2 ^ 64 * s1.toNat + 2 ^ 128 * s2.toNat + 2 ^ 192 * s3.toNat +
          2 ^ 256 * s4.toNat + 2 ^ 320 * c.toNat =
        (a0.toNat + 2 ^ 64 * a1.toNat + 2 ^ 128 * a2.toNat + 2 ^ 192 * a3.toNat +
          2 ^ 256 * a4.toNat) +
        (b0.toNat + 2 ^ 64 * b1.toNat + 2 ^ 128 * b2.toNat + 2 ^ 192 * b3.toNat +
          2 ^ 256 * b4.toNat)

    (hnq : negInv.toNat * q.toNat % 2 ^ 64 = 2 ^ 64 - 1)
    (huS : uS.toNat ≤ q.toNat) (hvS : vS.toNat ≤ q.toNat)
    (hFG : F.toNat + G.toNat ≤ 2 ^ 31) :

modules.title: Four-limb inversion: runtime definitions (Mathlib-free)
modules.doc:
The Pornin binary-GCD inverse candidate over `Limbs4` and its checked wrapper
(`invGcdRaw`), Mathlib-free for `precompileModules` consumers.  The word-sized divstep loop
and bit-length helper come from `Montgomery/DivstepDefs`.  The proof side is

items.name: Montgomery.Native64x4.GcdData
items.doc:
Per-field schedule of the binary-GCD inverse candidate; every obligation defaults to
`decide`.
items.statement:
class GcdData (modulus : Nat) where
  /-- Divsteps in the final word-sized phase: `2·bits(p) - 2 - 15·31`. -/
  finalRounds : Nat
  /-- Initial `u`: the power of two that keeps the candidate in Montgomery form. -/
  initU : Limbs4
  initU_toNat : initU.toNat = 2 ^ (1135 - finalRounds) % modulus := by decide
  /-- Final-phase chunks stay at mac width. -/
  finalRounds_le : finalRounds ≤ 62 := by decide

modules.title: Correctness of four-limb CIOS Montgomery multiplication
modules.doc:
A round accumulates `a * bi` exactly (`mulAccum_spec`) and cancels the low limb against a
multiple of the modulus (`mulReduce_spec`); folding four rounds gives
`2 ^ 256 * ⟦t₄⟧ = ⟦a⟧ * ⟦b⟧ + M * q`, the Montgomery product up to the final conditional
subtraction.

## Main results

* `mulRound_spec` — the round invariant with the `2 * q` bound
* `mul_spec` — `mul` is canonical and satisfies `2 ^ 256 * ⟦mul a b⟧ ≡ ⟦a⟧ * ⟦b⟧ [MOD q]`

items.name: Montgomery.Native64x4.State5.toNat_eq
items.doc: The value of an accumulator in terms of its limbs.
items.statement:
theorem State5.toNat_eq (t : State5) :
    t.toNat = t.t0.toNat + 2 ^ 64 * t.t1.toNat + 2 ^ 128 * t.t2.toNat + 2 ^ 192 * t.t3.toNat +
      2 ^ 256 * t.t4.toNat

items.name: Montgomery.Native64x4.mulAccum_spec
items.doc: `mulAccum` adds `a * bi` to the accumulator exactly, with a one-bit carry limb.
items.statement:
theorem mulAccum_spec (a : Limbs4) (bi : UInt64) (t : State5) :
    (mulAccum a bi t).t5.toNat ≤ 1 ∧
      (mulAccum a bi t).toNat = t.toNat + a.toNat * bi.toNat

items.name: Montgomery.Native64x4.mulReduce_spec
items.doc:
`mulReduce` adds the multiple of the modulus that cancels the low limb, so dropping that
limb divides by `2 ^ 64` exactly.
items.statement:
theorem mulReduce_spec (q : Limbs4) (negInv : UInt64) (s : State6) (hs5 : s.t5.toNat ≤ 1)
    (hnq : negInv.toNat * q.toNat % 2 ^ 64 = 2 ^ 64 - 1) :
    2 ^ 64 * (mulReduce q negInv s).toNat =
      s.toNat + (montM s.t0 negInv).toNat * q.toNat

items.name: Montgomery.Native64x4.mulRound_spec
items.doc:
The CIOS round invariant: one round accumulates `a * bi` and cancels the low limb against
a multiple `m` of the modulus; the accumulator stays below `2 * q`.
items.statement:
theorem mulRound_spec (q a : Limbs4) (negInv bi : UInt64) (t : State5)
    (hnq : negInv.toNat * q.toNat % 2 ^ 64 = 2 ^ 64 - 1)
    (haq : a.toNat < q.toNat) (htq : t.toNat < 2 * q.toNat) :
    (mulRound q negInv a bi t).toNat < 2 * q.toNat ∧
      ∃ m : ℕ, m < 2 ^ 64 ∧
        2 ^ 64 * (mulRound q negInv a bi t).toNat =
          t.toNat + a.toNat * bi.toNat + m * q.toNat

items.name: Montgomery.Native64x4.mul_spec
items.doc: Montgomery multiplication is canonical and computes `a * b * (2 ^ 256)⁻¹ mod q`.
items.statement:
theorem mul_spec (q : Limbs4) (negInv : UInt64) (a b : Limbs4)
    (hnq : negInv.toNat * q.toNat % 2 ^ 64 = 2 ^ 64 - 1) (haq : a.toNat < q.toNat) :
    (mul q negInv a b).toNat < q.toNat ∧
      2 ^ 256 * (mul q negInv a b).toNat ≡ a.toNat * b.toNat [MOD q.toNat]

modules.title: Pasta (Pallas / Vesta) fields

Facade module for the Pasta base fields.  It re-exports the canonical `ZMod` models with

modules.title: The Pasta (Pallas / Vesta) base prime fields
modules.doc:
The Pallas and Vesta curves form a 2-cycle: the base field of one is the scalar field of the
other.  This module defines the two underlying 255-bit primes together with their Lucas/Pratt
primality certificates, following the pattern of `CompPoly.Fields.Secp256k1`.

* `Pallas.baseFieldSize` is the Pallas base field size, equal to the Vesta scalar field size;
* `Vesta.baseFieldSize` is the Vesta base field size, equal to the Pallas scalar field size.

Both primes are `1 mod 2 ^ 32` and have 2-adicity 32.  The certificates were generated from
the factorizations of `p - 1` and `q - 1`; see <https://github.com/zcash/pasta>.

modules.title: The Lucas test for primes.
modules.doc:
This file implements the Lucas test for primes (not to be confused with the Lucas-Lehmer test for
Mersenne primes). A number `a` witnesses that `n` is prime if `a` has order `n-1` in the
multiplicative group of integers mod `n`. This is checked by verifying that `a^(n-1) = 1 (mod n)`
and `a^d ≠ 1 (mod n)` for any divisor `d | n - 1`. This test is the basis of the Pratt primality
certificate.

## TODO

- Bonus: Show the reverse implication i.e. if a number is prime then it has a Lucas witness.
  Use `Units.IsCyclic` from `RingTheory/IntegralDomain` to show the group is cyclic.
- Write a tactic that uses this theorem to generate Pratt primality certificates
- Integrate Pratt primality certificates into the norm_num primality verifier

## Implementation notes

Note that the proof for `lucas_primality` relies on analyzing the multiplicative group
modulo `p`. Despite this, the theorem still holds vacuously for `p = 0` and `p = 1`: In these
cases, we can take `q` to be any prime and see that `hd` does not hold, since `a^((p-1)/q)` reduces
to `1`.

items.name: Nat.Prime.dvd_mul_list
items.statement:
lemma Nat.Prime.dvd_mul_list {p : ℕ} {l : List ℕ} (h : p.Prime) :
    p ∣ l.prod ↔ ∃ r ∈ l, p ∣ r

items.name: PrattPartList
items.doc:
Recursive form of a Pratt certificate for `p`, which may take in Pratt certificates
for a list of prime powers `r` less than `p` whose product is equal to `p - 1`.
items.statement:
inductive PrattPartList : (p : ℕ) → (a : ZMod p) → ℕ → Prop
  | prime : {p : ℕ} → {a : ZMod p} → (n k nk : ℕ) → n.Prime →
      a ^ ((p - 1) / n) ≠ 1 → n ^ k = nk → PrattPartList p a nk
  | split : {p : ℕ} → {a : ZMod p} → {n : ℕ} → (list : List ℕ) →
      (∀ r ∈ list, PrattPartList p a r) → list.prod = n → PrattPartList p a n

items.name: PrattCertificate'
items.doc:
Alternative form of a Pratt certificate for `p`, which may take in Pratt certificates
for a list of prime powers `r` less than `p` whose product is equal to `p - 1`.
items.statement:
structure PrattCertificate' (p : ℕ) : Type where
  a : ZMod p
  pow_eq_one : a ^ (p - 1) = 1
  part : PrattPartList p a (p - 1)

items.name: PrattPartList.out
items.statement:
theorem PrattPartList.out {p : ℕ} {a : ZMod p} {n : ℕ} (h : PrattPartList p a n) :
    ∀ q : ℕ, q.Prime → q ∣ n → a ^ ((p - 1) / q) ≠ 1

items.name: PrattCertificate'.out
items.statement: theorem PrattCertificate'.out {p : ℕ} (c : PrattCertificate' p) : p.Prime

items.name: PrattPart
items.doc: The binary version of `PrattPartList`. This is the one in the original file.
items.statement:
inductive PrattPart : (p : ℕ) → (a : ZMod p) → ℕ → Prop
  | prime : {p : ℕ} → {a : ZMod p} → (n k nk : ℕ) → n.Prime →
      a ^ ((p - 1) / n) ≠ 1 → n ^ k = nk → PrattPart p a nk
  | split : {p : ℕ} → {a : ZMod p} → {n : ℕ} → (l r : ℕ) →
      PrattPart p a l → PrattPart p a r → l * r = n → PrattPart p a n

items.name: Tactic.ZMod.powEqOfPowMod

theorem ZMod.powEqOfPowMod :
    ∀ {n a' c : ℕ} (a : ZMod n), (a' : ZMod n) = a →
      Nat.mod (Nat.pow a' (n - 1)) n = c → c = 1 → a ^ (n - 1) = 1

    MetaM Q($a ^ ($n - 1) = 1)

items.name: Tactic.ZMod.powNeOfPowMod
items.statement:
theorem ZMod.powNeOfPowMod :
    ∀ {n a' q c : ℕ} (a : ZMod n), (a' : ZMod n) = a → decide (n ≥ 2) = true →
      Nat.mod (Nat.pow a' ((n - 1) / q)) n = c → decide (c ≠ 1) = true → a ^ ((n - 1) / q) ≠ 1
  | n, a, q, _, _, rfl, hn, rfl, h => by
    rw [← Nat.cast_pow]
    conv_rhs => rw [← Nat.cast_one]
    intro h'
    rw [CharP.natCast_eq_natCast (ZMod n) n] at h'
    replace h

    ∀ {n q c : ℕ} (a : ZMod n), (decide (n ≥ 2) = true) → (decide (c < n) = true) →
      (decide (c ≠ 1) = true) → IsNat (a ^ ((n - 1) / q)) c → a ^ ((n - 1) / q) ≠ 1

items.name: Tactic.verifyCertificate
items.statement:
meta partial def verifyCertificate (n' : Q(ℕ)) (n : ℕ) :
    UnverifiedPrattCertificate n → MetaM Q(Nat.Prime $n')
  | .knownPrime n => verifySmallPrime n'
  | .of n a part => do
      let cert ← generateCertificate n' n a part
      return q(PrattCertificate.out $cert)

modules.title: The Secp256k1 base and scalar prime fields
modules.doc:
We define the two primes underlying the Secp256k1 elliptic curve.

The base prime is the prime on which the elliptic curve is defined.

The scalar prime is the prime that divides the order of the curve.

## References

`p` is the base prime, and `n` is the scalar prime in [Section 2.4.1](http://www.secg.org/sec2-v2.pdf).

modules.title: Dense Homogeneous-Kernel Basis Correctness
modules.doc:
`homogeneousKernelBasis M` coincides with the row-array kernel
`homogeneousKernelBasisRows (toRows M) M.cols` for every well-formed `M`: the
two Gauss-Jordan loops make the same pivot choices and produce the same reduced
entries. The row-array soundness and completeness theorems therefore transfer to
the dense kernel.

items.name: CompPoly.DenseMatrix.toRows_size
items.doc: The number of rows of `toRows M`.
items.statement: theorem toRows_size [Zero F] (M : DenseMatrix F) : M.toRows.size = M.rows

items.name: CompPoly.DenseMatrix.toRows_getD
items.doc: Entries of `toRows M` below the matrix dimensions are the entries of `M`.
items.statement:
theorem toRows_getD [Zero F] (M : DenseMatrix F) {i j : Nat} (hi : i < M.rows)
    (hj : j < M.cols) : (M.toRows.getD i #[]).getD j 0 = M.get i j

items.name: CompPoly.DenseMatrix.normalizeAndEliminate_get
items.doc:
Entries of `normalizeAndEliminate` below the matrix dimensions: the pivot row
is divided by the pivot, and every other row loses its pivot-column multiple of
the normalized pivot row.
items.statement:
theorem normalizeAndEliminate_get [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    {M : DenseMatrix F} (hM : WellFormed M) {pivotRow pivotCol row k : Nat}
    (hpr : pivotRow < M.rows) (hpc : pivotCol < M.cols)
    (hpivot : M.get pivotRow pivotCol ≠ 0) (hrow : row < M.rows) (hk : k < M.cols) :
    (normalizeAndEliminate M pivotRow pivotCol).get row k =
      if row = pivotRow then
        M.get pivotRow k / M.get pivotRow pivotCol
      else
        M.get row k -
          M.get row pivotCol * (M.get pivotRow k / M.get pivotRow pivotCol)

items.name: CompPoly.DenseMatrix.rref_pivots_eq_scalarRrefRows
items.doc:
For a well-formed matrix, `rref` records the same pivot columns as the
row-array reduction of its rows.
items.statement:
theorem rref_pivots_eq_scalarRrefRows [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    {M : DenseMatrix F} (hM : WellFormed M) :
    (rref M).pivots = (scalarRrefRows M.toRows M.cols).pivots

items.name: CompPoly.DenseMatrix.homogeneousKernelBasis_eq_homogeneousKernelBasisRows
items.doc:
The dense homogeneous-kernel basis equals the row-array kernel basis of the
matrix rows.
items.statement:
theorem homogeneousKernelBasis_eq_homogeneousKernelBasisRows [Field F] [BEq F]
    [LawfulBEq F] {M : DenseMatrix F} (hM : WellFormed M) :
    homogeneousKernelBasis M = homogeneousKernelBasisRows M.toRows M.cols

items.name: CompPoly.DenseMatrix.dotRow_eq_sum
items.doc: `dotRow` is the finite sum of products over the columns.
items.statement:
theorem dotRow_eq_sum [Semiring F] (M : DenseMatrix F) (row : Nat) (v : Array F) :
    dotRow M row v = ∑ k ∈ Finset.range M.cols, M.get row k * v.getD k 0

items.name: CompPoly.DenseMatrix.homogeneousKernelBasis_width
items.doc: Every vector of the dense homogeneous-kernel basis has the matrix column width.

items.name: CompPoly.DenseMatrix.homogeneousKernelBasis_isHomogeneousSolution
items.doc:
**Soundness of the dense kernel basis.** Every emitted vector solves the
homogeneous system.

items.name: CompPoly.DenseMatrix.homogeneousKernelBasis_complete
items.doc:
**Completeness of the dense kernel basis.** Every homogeneous solution is,
below the column count, the linear combination of the basis vectors whose
coefficients are its entries at the free columns of `rref M`.
items.statement:
theorem homogeneousKernelBasis_complete [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    {M : DenseMatrix F} (hM : WellFormed M) {v : Array F}
    (hv : IsHomogeneousSolution M v) :
    ∀ k, k < M.cols →
      v.getD k 0 =
        ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (homogeneousKernelBasis M).size,
          v.getD ((freeColumns M.cols (rref M).pivots).getD i 0) 0 *
            ((homogeneousKernelBasis M).getD i #[]).getD k 0

items.name: CompPoly.DenseMatrix.homogeneousKernelBasis_size
items.doc: The number of dense kernel basis vectors is the number of free columns.
items.statement:
theorem homogeneousKernelBasis_size [Field F] [BEq F] (M : DenseMatrix F) :
    (homogeneousKernelBasis M).size = (freeColumns M.cols (rref M).pivots).size

items.name: CompPoly.DenseMatrix.freeColumns_size_add_pivots_size
items.doc:
Strictly increasing pivot columns below `cols` and the free columns partition
the columns `0, …, cols - 1`.
items.statement:
theorem freeColumns_size_add_pivots_size {cols : Nat} {pivots : Array Nat}
    (hstrict : PivotColumnsStrict pivots)
    (hlt : ∀ i, i < pivots.size → pivots.getD i 0 < cols) :
    (freeColumns cols pivots).size + pivots.size = cols

items.name: CompPoly.DenseMatrix.homogeneousKernelBasis_size_add_rank
items.doc:
**Rank-nullity for the dense kernel basis.** The basis has one vector per
non-pivot column of `rref M`.
items.statement:
theorem homogeneousKernelBasis_size_add_rank [Field F] [BEq F] (M : DenseMatrix F) :
    (homogeneousKernelBasis M).size + (rref M).pivots.size = M.cols

items.name: CompPoly.DenseMatrix.homogeneousKernelBasis_getD_freeColumn
items.doc:
The `i`-th dense kernel basis vector is one at the `i`-th free column and zero
at every other free column.
items.statement:
theorem homogeneousKernelBasis_getD_freeColumn [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    {M : DenseMatrix F} (hM : WellFormed M) {i j : Nat}
    (hi : i < (freeColumns M.cols (rref M).pivots).size)
    (hj : j < (freeColumns M.cols (rref M).pivots).size) :
    ((homogeneousKernelBasis M).getD i #[]).getD
        ((freeColumns M.cols (rref M).pivots).getD j 0) 0 =
      if j = i then 1 else 0

items.name: CompPoly.DenseMatrix.homogeneousKernelBasis_linearIndependent
items.doc:
**Linear independence of the dense kernel basis.** A linear combination of
the basis vectors that vanishes below the column count has all coefficients
zero.
items.statement:
theorem homogeneousKernelBasis_linearIndependent [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    {M : DenseMatrix F} (hM : WellFormed M) (c : Nat → F)
    (hc : ∀ k, k < M.cols →
      ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (homogeneousKernelBasis M).size,
        c i * ((homogeneousKernelBasis M).getD i #[]).getD k 0 = 0) :
    ∀ i, i < (homogeneousKernelBasis M).size → c i = 0

items.statement:
theorem homogeneousWitness_sound [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    {M : DenseMatrix F} (hM : WellFormed M) {v : Array F}

items.name: CompPoly.DenseMatrix.homogeneousWitness_none_complete

modules.title: In-Place Dense Homogeneous Kernels
modules.doc:
A memory-efficient executable variant of the dense Gauss-Jordan homogeneous-kernel
backend.

The functions in `RowOps.lean` and `Kernel.lean` thread a whole `DenseMatrix`
structure through every row operation. Because `scaleRow`/`addScaledRow`/`swapRows`
read the matrix through `M.get` while the structure `M` is still live, the backing
`Array` is multiply-referenced at the first `setD`, so `Array.setIfInBounds` copies
the entire array on every row-operation call. Gauss-Jordan elimination performs
`Θ(rows)` row operations per pivot and `Θ(min rows cols)` pivots, so the copies turn
an `O(n³)` algorithm into `O(n⁴)` work plus `Θ(n⁴)` words of short-lived allocation.

This module performs the same arithmetic, in the same order, threading a bare
`Array F` (with the dimensions carried as separate `Nat` arguments) through the
reduction. The array is uniquely referenced as it flows from one operation to the
next, so `setIfInBounds` mutates in place after at most one fork from a shared input.
The reduced matrix and pivot data are bit-for-bit identical to `rref`, so the
extracted witnesses agree with `homogeneousWitness`.

The free-column witness extraction (`freeColumns`, `basisVectorForFreeColumn`) is
cheap and shared verbatim with `Kernel.lean`.

items.name: CompPoly.DenseMatrix.swapRowsData
items.doc: Swap rows `rowA` and `rowB` of a width-`cols` row-major array, in place.
items.statement: def swapRowsData [Zero F] (cols rowA rowB : Nat) (data : Array F) : Array F

items.name: CompPoly.DenseMatrix.scaleRowData
items.doc: Scale row `row` of a width-`cols` row-major array by `factor`, in place.
items.statement:
def scaleRowData [Field F] (cols row : Nat) (factor : F) (data : Array F) :
    Array F
