items.name: CompPoly.PolynomialMatrix.mulBoundedWith_eq_mulWith
items.doc: The degree-capped matrix product equals the naive matrix product.
items.statement:
theorem mulBoundedWith_eq_mulWith [Semiring F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (lowCtx : MulLowContext F) (A B : PolynomialMatrix F) :
    mulBoundedWith lowCtx A B = mulWith lowCtx.mulContext A B

items.name: CompPoly.PolynomialMatrix.rowGet_rowTruncateColumns
items.doc: Entry access for column truncation of a row.
items.statement:
theorem rowGet_rowTruncateColumns [Semiring F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (orders : Array Nat) (row : PolynomialRow F) (j : Nat) :
    rowGet (rowTruncateColumns orders row) j =
      truncateX (orders.getD j 0) (rowGet row j)

items.name: CompPoly.PolynomialMatrix.truncateColumns_size
items.doc: Row count of a column-truncated matrix.
items.statement:
theorem truncateColumns_size [Semiring F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (orders : Array Nat) (M : PolynomialMatrix F) :
    (truncateColumns orders M).size = M.size

items.name: CompPoly.PolynomialMatrix.truncateColumns_getD
items.doc: Rows of a column-truncated matrix.
items.statement:
theorem truncateColumns_getD [Semiring F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (orders : Array Nat) (M : PolynomialMatrix F) {i : Nat} (hi : i < M.size) :
    (truncateColumns orders M).getD i #[] =
      rowTruncateColumns orders (M.getD i #[])

items.name: CompPoly.PolynomialMatrix.rowMulMatrixTruncColumnWith_eq
items.doc: The truncated row product is the truncation of the naive row product.
items.statement:
theorem rowMulMatrixTruncColumnWith_eq [Semiring F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (lowCtx : MulLowContext F) (orders : Array Nat) (row : PolynomialRow F)
    (M : PolynomialMatrix F) :
    rowMulMatrixTruncColumnWith lowCtx orders row M =
      rowTruncateColumns orders (rowMulMatrixWith lowCtx.mulContext row M)

items.name: CompPoly.PolynomialMatrix.mulTruncColumnWith_eq
items.doc: The column-truncated product is the truncation of the naive product.
items.statement:
theorem mulTruncColumnWith_eq [Semiring F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (lowCtx : MulLowContext F) (orders : Array Nat) (A B : PolynomialMatrix F) :
    mulTruncColumnWith lowCtx orders A B =
      truncateColumns orders (mulWith lowCtx.mulContext A B)

items.note: ## Structural `ofFn` rewrites for the block combinators

items.name: CompPoly.PolynomialMatrix.add_ofFn
items.doc: Pointwise addition of equally shaped `ofFn` matrices.
items.statement:
theorem add_ofFn [Semiring F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F] (rows width : Nat)
    (f g : Nat → Nat → CPolynomial F) :
    add (ofFn rows width f) (ofFn rows width g) =
      ofFn rows width (fun i j ↦ f i j + g i j)

items.name: CompPoly.PolynomialMatrix.sub_ofFn
items.doc: Pointwise subtraction of equally shaped `ofFn` matrices.
items.statement:
theorem sub_ofFn [Ring F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F] (rows width : Nat)
    (f g : Nat → Nat → CPolynomial F) :
    sub (ofFn rows width f) (ofFn rows width g) =
      ofFn rows width (fun i j ↦ f i j - g i j)

items.name: CompPoly.PolynomialMatrix.mulWith_ofFn_ofFn
items.doc: The naive product of square `ofFn` matrices.
items.statement:
theorem mulWith_ofFn_ofFn [Semiring F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (mulCtx : CPolynomial.MulContext F) (n : Nat)
    (f g : Nat → Nat → CPolynomial F) :
    mulWith mulCtx (ofFn n n f) (ofFn n n g) =
      ofFn n n (fun i j ↦ ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, f i k * g k j)

items.name: CompPoly.PolynomialMatrix.truncateColumns_ofFn
items.doc: Column truncation of an `ofFn` matrix.
items.statement:
theorem truncateColumns_ofFn [Semiring F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F] (orders : Array Nat)
    (rows width : Nat) (entry : Nat → Nat → CPolynomial F) :
    truncateColumns orders (ofFn rows width entry) =
      ofFn rows width (fun i j ↦ truncateX (orders.getD j 0) (entry i j))

items.name: CompPoly.PolynomialMatrix.mulStrassenWithFuel_eq_mulWith
items.doc: The fuel-bounded Strassen product equals the naive matrix product.
items.statement:
theorem mulStrassenWithFuel_eq_mulWith [Ring F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (lowCtx : MulLowContext F) (leafCutoff fuel : Nat) (A B : PolynomialMatrix F) :
    mulStrassenWithFuel lowCtx leafCutoff fuel A B = mulWith lowCtx.mulContext A B

items.name: CompPoly.PolynomialMatrix.mulStrassenWith_eq_mulWith
items.doc: The Strassen product equals the naive matrix product.
items.statement:
theorem mulStrassenWith_eq_mulWith [Ring F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (lowCtx : MulLowContext F) (leafCutoff : Nat) (A B : PolynomialMatrix F) :
    mulStrassenWith lowCtx leafCutoff A B = mulWith lowCtx.mulContext A B

items.name: CompPoly.PolynomialMatrix.mulStrassenWith_size
items.doc: Row count of the Strassen product.
items.statement:
theorem mulStrassenWith_size [Ring F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (lowCtx : MulLowContext F) (leafCutoff : Nat) (A B : PolynomialMatrix F) :
    (mulStrassenWith lowCtx leafCutoff A B).size = A.size

items.name: CompPoly.PolynomialMatrix.mulStrassenWith_getD
items.doc: Rows of the Strassen product are the naive row-by-matrix products.
items.statement:
theorem mulStrassenWith_getD [Ring F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (lowCtx : MulLowContext F) (leafCutoff : Nat) (A B : PolynomialMatrix F)
    {i : Nat} (hi : i < A.size) :
    (mulStrassenWith lowCtx leafCutoff A B).getD i #[] =
      rowMulMatrixWith lowCtx.mulContext (A.getD i #[]) B

items.name: CompPoly.PolynomialMatrix.matrixRows_mulStrassenWith
items.doc: Row list of the Strassen product.
items.statement:
theorem matrixRows_mulStrassenWith [Ring F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (lowCtx : MulLowContext F) (leafCutoff : Nat) (A B : PolynomialMatrix F) :
    MatrixRows (mulStrassenWith lowCtx leafCutoff A B) =
      (MatrixRows A).map fun row ↦ rowMulMatrixWith lowCtx.mulContext row B

items.name: CompPoly.PolynomialMatrix.mulTruncColumnStrassenWithFuel_eq_truncateColumns
items.doc:
The fuel-bounded column-truncated Strassen product equals the
column-truncated naive matrix product.
items.statement:
theorem mulTruncColumnStrassenWithFuel_eq_truncateColumns [Ring F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (lowCtx : MulLowContext F) (leafCutoff fuel : Nat) (orders : Array Nat)
    (A B : PolynomialMatrix F) :
    mulTruncColumnStrassenWithFuel lowCtx leafCutoff fuel orders A B =
      truncateColumns orders (mulWith lowCtx.mulContext A B)

items.name: CompPoly.PolynomialMatrix.mulTruncColumnStrassenWith_eq_truncateColumns
items.doc:
The column-truncated Strassen product equals the column-truncated naive
matrix product.
items.statement:
theorem mulTruncColumnStrassenWith_eq_truncateColumns [Ring F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (lowCtx : MulLowContext F) (leafCutoff : Nat) (orders : Array Nat)
    (A B : PolynomialMatrix F) :
    mulTruncColumnStrassenWith lowCtx leafCutoff orders A B =
      truncateColumns orders (mulWith lowCtx.mulContext A B)

items.name: CompPoly.PolynomialMatrix.mulTruncColumnStrassenWith_size
items.doc: Row count of the column-truncated Strassen product.
items.statement:
theorem mulTruncColumnStrassenWith_size [Ring F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (lowCtx : MulLowContext F) (leafCutoff : Nat) (orders : Array Nat)
    (A B : PolynomialMatrix F) :
    (mulTruncColumnStrassenWith lowCtx leafCutoff orders A B).size = A.size

items.name: CompPoly.PolynomialMatrix.mulTruncColumnStrassenWith_entry
items.doc:
Entries of the column-truncated Strassen product are the order-truncated
naive product entries.
items.statement:
theorem mulTruncColumnStrassenWith_entry [Ring F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (lowCtx : MulLowContext F) (leafCutoff : Nat) (orders : Array Nat)
    (A B : PolynomialMatrix F) {i : Nat} (hi : i < A.size) (j : Nat) :
    rowGet ((mulTruncColumnStrassenWith lowCtx leafCutoff orders A B).getD i #[]) j =
      truncateX (orders.getD j 0)
        (rowGet (rowMulMatrixWith lowCtx.mulContext (A.getD i #[]) B) j)

modules.title: Bases for the right scalar action on tensor products
modules.doc:
`Module.Basis.baseChangeRight` lifts a basis of `Left` over `K` to a basis of
`Left ⊗[K] Right` over `Right`, with scalars acting on the right tensor factor.
The action is explicit in each declaration; importing this module preserves Mathlib's
default action on the left factor, including when `Left = Right`.

For equal factors, select the right `Algebra`, `Module`, `DistribMulAction` and `SMul`
locally when combining this basis with scalar notation and module laws. Tensor products
provide independent default instances at each of these levels.

For background on tensor-product bases, see [Lan02]. For equal field factors, this
right-action basis is the basis used for the row representation in [DP24], §2.5.

## References

* [Lang, S., *Algebra*][Lan02]
* [Diamond, B. E. and Posen, J., *Polylogarithmic proofs for multilinears over binary towers*][DP24]

items.name: Module.Basis.baseChangeRight
items.doc:
Lift a `K`-basis of `Left` to a `Right`-basis of `Left ⊗[K] Right`, using the
right-factor scalar action. This is the right-sided counterpart to `Basis.baseChange`.
items.statement:
noncomputable def baseChangeRight (b : Basis ι K Left) :
    letI rightAlgebra := Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra (R := K) (A := Left) (B := Right)
    letI := rightAlgebra.toModule
    Basis ι Right (Left ⊗[K] Right)

items.name: Module.Basis.baseChangeRight_repr_tmul
items.doc: Coordinates of a pure tensor in the basis for the right-factor scalar action.
items.statement:
lemma baseChangeRight_repr_tmul (b : Basis ι K Left) (x : Left) (y : Right) (i : ι) :
    letI rightAlgebra := Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra (R := K) (A := Left) (B := Right)
    letI := rightAlgebra.toModule
    (b.baseChangeRight (Right := Right)).repr (x ⊗ₜ[K] y) i = b.repr x i • y

items.name: Module.Basis.baseChangeRight_apply
items.doc: The right-action basis vectors are the original basis vectors tensored with one.
items.statement:
lemma baseChangeRight_apply (b : Basis ι K Left) (i : ι) :
    letI rightAlgebra := Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra (R := K) (A := Left) (B := Right)
    letI := rightAlgebra.toModule
    b.baseChangeRight (Right := Right) i = b i ⊗ₜ[K] 1

modules.authors: Quang Dao, Chung Thai Nguyen, Aristotle (Harmonic), Elias Judin
modules.title: Multilinear Polynomials
modules.doc:
This file defines computable representations of **multilinear polynomials**.

The first representation is by their coefficients, and the second representation is by their
evaluations over the Boolean hypercube `{0,1}^n`. Both representations are defined as `Vector`s of
length `2^n`, where `n` is the number of variables. We will define operations on these
representations, and prove equivalence between them, and with the standard Mathlib definition of
multilinear polynomials, which is the type `R⦃≤ 1⦄[X Fin n]` (notation for
`MvPolynomial.restrictDegree (Fin n) R 1`).

## TODOs
- The abstract zeta formula for `monoToLagrange`
- A naive `O(4^n)` zeta spec `monoToLagrangeSpec` mirroring `lagrangeToMonoSpec`,
  plus equivalence `monoToLagrange = monoToLagrangeSpec`

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial
items.doc:
`CMlPolynomial n R` is the type of multilinear polynomials in `n` variables over a ring `R`.
It is represented by its monomial coefficients as a `Vector` of length `2^n`.
The indexing is **little-endian** (i.e. the least significant bit is the first bit).
items.statement: def CMlPolynomial (R : Type*) (n : ℕ)

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.mk
items.statement: def CMlPolynomial.mk {R : Type*} (n : ℕ) (v : Vector R (2 ^ n)) : CMlPolynomial R n

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomialEval
items.doc:
`CMlPolynomialEval n R` is the type of multilinear polynomials in `n` variables over a ring `R`.
It is represented by its evaluations over the Boolean hypercube `{0,1}^n`,
i.e. Lagrange basis coefficients.
The indexing is **little-endian** (i.e. the least significant bit is the first bit).
items.statement: def CMlPolynomialEval (R : Type*) (n : ℕ)

items.statement: def monomialBasis (w : Vector R n) : Vector R (2 ^ n)

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.map_monomialBasis
items.doc:
Mapping each monomial-basis value by a ring homomorphism equals evaluating the
monomial basis at the mapped point.
items.statement:
theorem map_monomialBasis (f : R →+* S) (x : Vector R n) :
    (monomialBasis x).map f = monomialBasis (x.map f)

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.monomialBasis_zero
items.statement: theorem monomialBasis_zero {w : Vector R 0} : monomialBasis w = #v[1]

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.monomialBasis_getElem
items.doc:
The `i`-th element of `monomialBasis w` is the product of `w[j]` if the `j`-th bit of `i` is 1,
and `1` if the `j`-th bit of `i` is 0.
items.statement:
theorem monomialBasis_getElem {w : Vector R n} (i : Fin (2 ^ n)) :
    (monomialBasis w)[i] = ∏ j : Fin n, if (BitVec.ofFin i).getLsb j then w[j] else 1

items.doc: Evaluate a `CMlPolynomial` at a point
items.statement: def eval (p : CMlPolynomial R n) (x : Vector R n) : R

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.map_eval
items.doc:
Mapping a coefficient-form evaluation by a ring homomorphism equals evaluating the
mapped coefficients at the mapped point.
items.statement:
theorem map_eval (f : R →+* S) (p : CMlPolynomial R n) (x : Vector R n) :
    f (eval p x) = eval (map f p) (x.map f)

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.evalWithProducts
items.doc:
Evaluate monomial coefficients by accumulating their products with the monomial-basis
values in `W`, starting at zero, then reducing once to a value in `R`.
items.statement:
def evalWithProducts {W : Type*} [AddZero W] (product : R → R → W) (reduce : W →+ R)
    (p : CMlPolynomial R n) (x : Vector R n) : R

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.evalWithProducts_eq_eval
items.doc:
Product accumulation followed by additive reduction agrees with coefficient evaluation
when reducing each product gives the ordinary product of its two factors.
items.statement:
theorem evalWithProducts_eq_eval {W : Type*} [AddZero W]
    (product : R → R → W) (reduce : W →+ R)
    (hproduct : ∀ a b, reduce (product a b) = a * b)
    (p : CMlPolynomial R n) (x : Vector R n) :
    evalWithProducts product reduce p x = eval p x

items.statement: def eval₂ (p : CMlPolynomial R n) (f : R →+* S) (x : Vector S n) : S

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.eval_horner_eq_eval
items.doc: Horner evaluation agrees with the dot-product evaluator.
items.statement:
theorem eval_horner_eq_eval (p : CMlPolynomial R n) (x : Vector R n) :
    evalHorner p x = eval p x

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.eval₂_horner_eq_eval₂
items.doc: Horner evaluation through a ring homomorphism agrees with the dot-product evaluator.
items.statement:
theorem eval₂_horner_eq_eval₂ (p : CMlPolynomial R n) (f : R →+* S) (x : Vector S n) :
    eval₂Horner p f x = eval₂ p f x

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.eval_add
items.doc: Evaluation is additive in the coefficient vector.
items.statement:
theorem eval_add (p q : CMlPolynomial R n) (x : Vector R n) :
    eval (p + q) x = eval p x + eval q x

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.eval_zero
items.doc: The zero coefficient vector evaluates to zero.
items.statement: theorem eval_zero (x : Vector R n) : eval (0 : CMlPolynomial R n) x = 0

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.eval_smul
items.doc: Evaluation commutes with scalar multiplication of the coefficient vector.
items.statement:
theorem eval_smul (a : R) (p : CMlPolynomial R n) (x : Vector R n) :
    eval (a • p) x = a * eval p x

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomialEval.lagrangeBasis
items.doc:
Lagrange (hypercube) basis at point `w`.

Returns the length-`2^n` vector `v` such that for any `x ∈ {0,1}^n`, letting
`i = ∑_{j=0}^{n-1} x_j · 2^j` (little‑endian indexing), we have
`v[i] = ∏_{j < n} (x_j · w[j] + (1 - x_j) · (1 - w[j]))`.
Equivalently, for `i : Fin (2^n)`,
`v[i] = ∏_{j < n}, (if the j-th bit of i is 1 then w[j] else 1 - w[j])`.
items.statement: def lagrangeBasis (w : Vector R n) : Vector R (2 ^ n)

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomialEval.lagrangeBasis_zero
items.statement: theorem lagrangeBasis_zero {w : Vector R 0} : lagrangeBasis w = #v[1]

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomialEval.lagrangeBasis_getElem
items.doc:
The `i`-th element of `lagrangeBasis w` is the product of `w[j]` if the `j`-th bit of `i` is 1,
and `1 - w[j]` if the `j`-th bit of `i` is 0.
items.statement:
theorem lagrangeBasis_getElem {w : Vector R n} (i : Fin (2 ^ n)) :
    (lagrangeBasis w)[i] = ∏ j : Fin n, if (BitVec.ofFin i).getLsb j then w[j] else 1 - w[j]

items.doc: One multilinear-extension interpolation step, eliminating the next little-endian variable.
items.statement:
def evalMleStep {n : ℕ}
    (values : Vector R (2 ^ (n + 1))) (x0 : R) : Vector R (2 ^ n)

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomialEval.evalMleLayer
items.doc: Public multilinear-extension interpolation layer.
items.statement:
def evalMleLayer {n : ℕ}
    (values : CMlPolynomialEval R (n + 1)) (x0 : R) : CMlPolynomialEval R n

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomialEval.evalMleLayer_get
items.doc: The `j`-th entry after one MLE layer is the affine interpolation of its input pair.
items.statement:
theorem evalMleLayer_get [CommRing R] {n : ℕ}
    (values : CMlPolynomialEval R (n + 1)) (x0 : R) (j : Fin (2 ^ n)) :
    (evalMleLayer values x0).get j =
      (1 - x0) * values.get ⟨2 * j.val, by omega⟩ +
        x0 * values.get ⟨2 * j.val + 1, by omega⟩

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomialEval.evalMle_zero
items.doc: Evaluating a zero-variable hypercube table returns its only value.
items.statement:
theorem evalMle_zero [CommRing R] (p : CMlPolynomialEval R 0) (x : Vector R 0) :
    evalMle p x = p.get ⟨0, by norm_num⟩

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomialEval.evalMle_succ
items.doc: Recursive MLE evaluation first folds the head variable, then evaluates the tail.

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomialEval.eval₂Mle
items.doc:
Evaluate a `CMlPolynomialEval` through a ring homomorphism using multilinear-extension
interpolation.
items.statement: def eval₂Mle (p : CMlPolynomialEval R n) (f : R →+* S) (x : Vector S n) : S

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomialEval.eval
items.doc: Evaluate a `CMlPolynomialEval` at a point
items.statement: def eval (p : CMlPolynomialEval R n) (x : Vector R n) : R

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomialEval.eval_smul
items.doc: Evaluation commutes with scalar multiplication of a hypercube table.
items.statement:
theorem eval_smul (a : R) (p : CMlPolynomialEval R n) (x : Vector R n) :
    eval (a • p) x = a * eval p x

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomialEval.eval₂
items.doc: Evaluate a `CMlPolynomialEval` at a point using a ring homomorphism
items.statement: def eval₂ (p : CMlPolynomialEval R n) (f : R →+* S) (x : Vector S n) : S

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomialEval.eqTilde
items.doc: Evaluate the multilinear equality kernel `eq̃(w, x)`.
items.statement: def eqTilde (w x : Vector R n) : R

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomialEval.eval_mle_eq_eval
items.doc: Multilinear-extension interpolation agrees with the dot-product evaluator.
items.statement:
theorem eval_mle_eq_eval (p : CMlPolynomialEval R n) (x : Vector R n) :
    evalMle p x = eval p x

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomialEval.eqTilde_eq_prod
items.doc: The multilinear equality kernel is the product of its coordinatewise affine factors.
items.statement:
theorem eqTilde_eq_prod (w x : Vector R n) :
    eqTilde w x = ∏ i : Fin n, (w[i] * x[i] + (1 - w[i]) * (1 - x[i]))

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomialEval.eqTilde_append
items.doc: The equality kernel factors across appended coordinate blocks.
items.statement:
theorem eqTilde_append {m : ℕ} (w₁ x₁ : Vector R n) (w₂ x₂ : Vector R m) :
    eqTilde (w₁ ++ w₂) (x₁ ++ x₂) = eqTilde w₁ x₁ * eqTilde w₂ x₂

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomialEval.eval₂_mle_eq_eval₂
items.doc:
Multilinear-extension interpolation through a ring homomorphism agrees with the
dot-product evaluator.
items.statement:
theorem eval₂_mle_eq_eval₂ (p : CMlPolynomialEval R n) (f : R →+* S) (x : Vector S n) :
    eval₂Mle p f x = eval₂ p f x

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomialEval.eval_add
items.doc: Evaluation is additive in the coefficient vector.
items.statement:
theorem eval_add (p q : CMlPolynomialEval R n) (x : Vector R n) :
    eval (p + q) x = eval p x + eval q x

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomialEval.eval_zero
items.doc: The zero coefficient vector evaluates to zero.
items.statement: theorem eval_zero (x : Vector R n) : eval (0 : CMlPolynomialEval R n) x = 0

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.monoToLagrangeLevel
items.doc:
**One level** of the zeta‑transform (coefficient to evaluation).

Processes the `j`-th variable by folding the "partner" index (with bit `j` cleared) into
every index that has bit `j` set. At output index `i`:
$$ (\text{monoToLagrangeLevel}\ j\ v)[i] \ =\ \begin{cases}
  v[i] + v[i - 2^j] & \text{if bit } j \text{ of } i \text{ is } 1 \\
  v[i] & \text{otherwise}
\end{cases} $$

After applying every level `0, 1, …, n-1` the resulting entry at `i` is
$\sum_{j \subseteq i} p[j]$ (bitwise subset), which is the hypercube evaluation at the
Boolean point encoded by `i`. Cost per level: $O(2^n)$ additions, so the full transform
is $O(n \cdot 2^n)$.

The `stride` is $2^j$, the distance between indices that differ only in bit `j`.
items.statement: def monoToLagrangeLevel {n : ℕ} (j : Fin n) : Vector R (2 ^ n) → Vector R (2 ^ n)

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.monoToLagrange
items.doc:
**Full zeta transform**: coefficients → evaluations.

Applies `monoToLagrangeLevel 0, 1, …, n-1` in that order via `foldl`. The resulting entry
at each index `i : Fin (2 ^ n)` is $\sum_{j \subseteq i} p[j]$ (the classical zeta
transform on the Boolean lattice).

**Complexity:** $O(n \cdot 2^n)$ additions — this is the butterfly form. Contrast with
the naive `monoToLagrangeSpec` which is $O(4^n)$.
items.statement: def monoToLagrange (n : ℕ) : CMlPolynomial R n → CMlPolynomialEval R n

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.lagrangeToMonoLevel
items.doc:
**One level** of the inverse zeta‑transform / Möbius transform (evaluation to
coefficient).

Processes the `j`-th variable by subtracting the partner entry (bit `j` cleared) from
every index that has bit `j` set. At output index `i`:
$$ (\text{lagrangeToMonoLevel}\ j\ v)[i] \ =\ \begin{cases}
  v[i] - v[i - 2^j] & \text{if bit } j \text{ of } i \text{ is } 1 \\
  v[i] & \text{otherwise}
\end{cases} $$

Each level is the exact inverse of `monoToLagrangeLevel j` (see
`lagrangeToMonoLevel_monoToLagrangeLevel_id`).

The `stride` is $2^j$.
items.statement: def lagrangeToMonoLevel {n : ℕ} (j : Fin n) : Vector R (2 ^ n) → Vector R (2 ^ n)

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.lagrangeToMono
items.doc:
**Full inverse / Möbius transform**: evaluations → coefficients.

Applies `lagrangeToMonoLevel (n-1), (n-2), …, 0` via `foldr`. The resulting entry at
each index `i : Fin (2 ^ n)` is the inclusion-exclusion sum
$\sum_{j \subseteq i} (-1)^{\mathrm{popCount}(i) - \mathrm{popCount}(j)} \cdot p[j]$ —
see `lagrangeToMono_eq_lagrangeToMonoSpec`.

**Complexity:** $O(n \cdot 2^n)$ additions/subtractions. Contrast with the naive
`lagrangeToMonoSpec` which is $O(4^n)$.
items.statement:
def lagrangeToMono (n : ℕ) :
    Vector R (2 ^ n) → Vector R (2 ^ n)

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.lagrangeToMonoSpec
items.doc:
The $O(4^n)$ inclusion-exclusion specification for the Möbius transform.

For each output index `i`, this sums over all indices `j` that are bitwise subsets of `i`
(`i &&& j = j`), with sign
$(-1)^{\mathrm{popCount}(i) - \mathrm{popCount}(j)}$:
$$ (\text{lagrangeToMonoSpec}\ p)[i]
  = \sum_{j \subseteq i} (-1)^{\mathrm{popCount}(i) - \mathrm{popCount}(j)} \cdot p[j]. $$

Provable equivalent to the fast `lagrangeToMono` — see `lagrangeToMono_eq_lagrangeToMonoSpec`.
items.statement: def lagrangeToMonoSpec (p : CMlPolynomialEval R n) : CMlPolynomialEval R n

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.monoToLagrangeSpec
items.doc:
The $O(4^n)$ specification for the zeta transform (the mirror of
`lagrangeToMonoSpec`).

For each output index `i`, this sums `p[j]` over every index `j` that is a bitwise subset
of `i` (`i &&& j = j`):
$$ (\text{monoToLagrangeSpec}\ p)[i]\ =\ \sum_{j \subseteq i} p[j]. $$

Provable equivalent to the fast `monoToLagrange` — see `monoToLagrange_eq_monoToLagrangeSpec`.
items.statement: def monoToLagrangeSpec (p : CMlPolynomial R n) : CMlPolynomialEval R n

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.forwardRange
items.doc:
Generates a list of indices representing a range of bit positions [l, r] in increasing order.
Used for optimized recursive transforms that operate on segments of variables.
Returns a list containing `l, l+1, ..., r`.
The result is used to fold over dimensions in `monoToLagrangeSegment` and `lagrangeToMonoSegment`.
items.statement: def forwardRange (n : ℕ) (r : Fin (n)) (l : Fin (r.val + 1)) : List (Fin n)

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.forwardRange_length
items.statement:
lemma forwardRange_length (n : ℕ) (r : Fin n) (l : Fin (r.val + 1)) :
    (forwardRange n r l).length = r.val - l.val + 1

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.forwardRange_eq_of_r_eq
items.statement:
lemma forwardRange_eq_of_r_eq (n : ℕ) (r1 r2 : Fin n) (h_r_eq : r1 = r2) (l : Fin (r1.val + 1)) :
    forwardRange n r1 l = forwardRange n r2 ⟨l, by omega⟩

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.forwardRange_getElem
items.statement:
lemma forwardRange_getElem (n : ℕ) (r : Fin n) (l : Fin (r.val + 1)) (k : Fin (r.val - l.val + 1)) :
    (forwardRange n r l).get ⟨k, by
    rw [forwardRange]; simp only [List.length_ofFn]; omega⟩ = ⟨l.val + k, by omega⟩

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.forwardRange_succ_right_ne_empty
items.statement:
lemma forwardRange_succ_right_ne_empty (n : ℕ) (r : Fin (n - 1)) (l : Fin (r.val + 1)) :
    forwardRange n ⟨r + 1, by omega⟩ ⟨l, by simp only; omega⟩ ≠ []

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.forwardRange_pred_le_ne_empty
items.statement:
lemma forwardRange_pred_le_ne_empty (n : ℕ) (r : Fin n) (l : Fin (r.val + 1))
    (h_l_gt_0 : l.val > 0) : forwardRange n r ⟨l.val - 1, by omega⟩ ≠ []

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.forwardRange_dropLast
items.statement:
lemma forwardRange_dropLast (n : ℕ) (r : Fin (n - 1)) (l : Fin (r.val + 1)) :
    (forwardRange n ⟨r + 1, by omega⟩ ⟨l, by simp only; omega⟩).dropLast
  = forwardRange n ⟨r, by omega⟩ ⟨l, by simp only [Fin.is_lt]⟩

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.forwardRange_tail
items.statement:
lemma forwardRange_tail (n : ℕ) (r : Fin n) (l : Fin (r.val + 1)) (h_l_gt_0 : l.val > 0) :
    (forwardRange n r ⟨l.val - 1, by omega⟩).tail = forwardRange n r l

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.forwardRange_0_eq_finRange
items.statement:
lemma forwardRange_0_eq_finRange (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] : forwardRange n ⟨n - 1, by
    have h_ne_zero : n ≠ 0 := NeZero.ne n
    omega
  ⟩ 0 = List.finRange n

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.monoToLagrangeSegment
items.doc:
Performs the zeta-transform (coefficient to evaluation) on a segment of dimensions from `l` to `r`.
Iteratively applies `monoToLagrangeLevel` for each dimension in the range.
`0 ≤ l ≤ r < n`.
items.statement:
def monoToLagrangeSegment (n : ℕ) (r : Fin n) (l : Fin (r.val + 1)) :
    Vector R (2 ^ n) → Vector R (2 ^ n)

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.lagrangeToMonoSegment
items.doc:
Performs the inverse zeta-transform (evaluation to coefficient) on a segment of dimensions

from `l` to `r`.

Iteratively applies `lagrangeToMonoLevel` for each dimension in the range (in reverse order).

`0 ≤ l ≤ r < n`.
items.statement:
def lagrangeToMonoSegment (n : ℕ) (r : Fin n) (l : Fin (r.val + 1)) :

    Vector R (2 ^ n) → Vector R (2 ^ n)

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.monoToLagrange_eq_monoToLagrangeSegment
items.statement:
lemma monoToLagrange_eq_monoToLagrangeSegment (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] (v : Vector R (2 ^ n)) :
    have h_n_ne_zero: n ≠ 0 := by exact NeZero.ne n
  monoToLagrange n v = monoToLagrangeSegment n (r:=⟨n - 1, by omega⟩) (l:=⟨0, by omega⟩) v

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.lagrangeToMono_eq_lagrangeToMonoSegment
items.statement:
lemma lagrangeToMono_eq_lagrangeToMonoSegment (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] (v : Vector R (2 ^ n)) :
    have h_n_ne_zero: n ≠ 0 := by exact NeZero.ne n
  lagrangeToMono n v = lagrangeToMonoSegment n (r:=⟨n - 1, by omega⟩) (l:=⟨0, by omega⟩) v

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.testBit_of_sub_two_pow_of_bit_1
items.statement:
lemma testBit_of_sub_two_pow_of_bit_1 {n i : ℕ} (h_testBit_eq_1 : (n).testBit i = true) :
    (n - 2^i).testBit i = false

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.lagrangeToMonoLevel_monoToLagrangeLevel_id
items.statement:
theorem lagrangeToMonoLevel_monoToLagrangeLevel_id (v : Vector R (2 ^ n)) (i : Fin n) :
    lagrangeToMonoLevel i (monoToLagrangeLevel i v) = v

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.monoToLagrangeLevel_lagrangeToMonoLevel_id
items.statement:
theorem monoToLagrangeLevel_lagrangeToMonoLevel_id (v : Vector R (2 ^ n)) (i : Fin n) :
    monoToLagrangeLevel i (lagrangeToMonoLevel i v) = v

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.mobius_apply_zeta_apply_eq_id
items.statement:
theorem mobius_apply_zeta_apply_eq_id (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] (r : Fin n) (l : Fin (r.val + 1))
    (v : Vector R (2 ^ n)) : lagrangeToMonoSegment n r l (monoToLagrangeSegment n r l v) = v

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.zeta_apply_mobius_apply_eq_id
items.statement:
lemma zeta_apply_mobius_apply_eq_id (n : ℕ) (r : Fin n) (l : Fin (r.val + 1))
    (v : Vector R (2 ^ n)) :
    monoToLagrangeSegment n r l (lagrangeToMonoSegment n r l v) = v

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.equivMonomialLagrangeRepr

The equivalence between the monomial basis representation (`CMlPolynomial`)
and the Lagrange basis representation (`CMlPolynomialEval`) of a multilinear polynomial.

modules.title: Serialization of multilinear polynomials
modules.doc:
`CMlPolynomial R n` and `CMlPolynomialEval R n` are `Vector R (2 ^ n)`, so they serialize
through the vector codec with no further definitions: `2 ^ n` coefficients, or `2 ^ n`
hypercube evaluations, in little-endian index order, `2 ^ n * width R` bytes. The two
representations have the same bytes for different meanings; the type says which.

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.width
items.statement:
theorem CMlPolynomial.width [ByteCodec R] :
    ByteCodec.width (CMlPolynomial R n) = 2 ^ n * ByteCodec.width R

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomialEval.width
items.statement:
theorem CMlPolynomialEval.width [ByteCodec R] :
    ByteCodec.width (CMlPolynomialEval R n) = 2 ^ n * ByteCodec.width R

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.toBytes_eq
items.statement:
theorem CMlPolynomial.toBytes_eq [ByteCodec R] (p : CMlPolynomial R n) :
    ByteCodec.toBytes p = ByteCodec.toBytes (p : Vector R (2 ^ n))

modules.title: Equivalence between `CMlPolynomial` and multilinear polynomials in `MvPolynomial`
modules.doc:
This file establishes the mathematical foundations for `CMlPolynomial` by proving:
1. Basis properties for the coefficient representation
2. Change-of-basis matrices between different representations
3. Equivalences with mathlib's `MvPolynomial.restrictDegree`: `equivMvPolynomialDeg1`
4. Arithmetic operation compatibilities

items.note:
### Equivalence with Mathlib MvPolynomial
- Note: maybe we have to add more restrictions on `CMlPolynomial R n` and `CMlPolynomialEval R n`
  so we can differentiate them?

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.monomialOfNat
items.doc:
Converts a natural number to a monomial with 0/1 exponents.
Uses little‑endian bit encoding: bit 0 is the least significant bit.
The exponent at variable j is `Nat.getBit j i ∈ {0,1}`.
items.statement: noncomputable def monomialOfNat (i : ℕ) : (Fin n) →₀ ℕ

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.eq_monomialOfNat_iff_eq_bitRepr
items.statement:
theorem eq_monomialOfNat_iff_eq_bitRepr (m : Fin n →₀ ℕ)
    (h_binary : ∀ j : Fin n, m j ≤ 1) (i: Fin (2^n)) :
  monomialOfNat i = m ↔ i = Nat.binaryFinMapToNat m h_binary

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.toMvPolynomial
items.doc:
Converts an `CMlPolynomial` to a mathlib multivariate polynomial.
Sums over all indices `i : Fin (2^n)` with monomial exponents from `monomialOfNat i`
and coefficients `p[i]`.
items.statement: def toMvPolynomial (p : CMlPolynomial R n) : MvPolynomial (Fin n) R

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.toMvPolynomial_is_multilinear
items.statement:
theorem toMvPolynomial_is_multilinear (p : CMlPolynomial R n) :
    (toMvPolynomial p) ∈ MvPolynomial.restrictDegree (Fin n) R 1

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.coeff_of_toMvPolynomial_eq_coeff_of_CMlPolynomial
items.statement:
theorem coeff_of_toMvPolynomial_eq_coeff_of_CMlPolynomial (p : CMlPolynomial R n) (m : Fin n →₀ ℕ) :
    (toMvPolynomial p).coeff m =
    if h_binary : (∀ j : Fin n, m j ≤ 1) then
        let i_of_m : ℕ := Nat.binaryFinMapToNat (m := m) (h_binary := h_binary)
        p[i_of_m]
      else
        0

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.toMvPolynomialDeg1
items.doc:
Converts an `CMlPolynomial` to a mathlib restricted-degree multivariate polynomial.
Wraps `toMvPolynomial` with a proof that the result is multilinear (i.e. individual degrees ≤ 1).

modules.authors: Quang Dao, Chung Thai Nguyen, Natalie Klaus
modules.title: Fast ↔ Spec equivalence for the multilinear zeta / Möbius transforms
modules.doc:
This file proves that the $O(n \cdot 2^n)$ butterfly transforms
`monoToLagrange` and `lagrangeToMono` (defined in `CompPoly.Multilinear.Basic`) coincide
pointwise with their $O(4^n)$ inclusion-exclusion specifications
`monoToLagrangeSpec` and `lagrangeToMonoSpec` respectively.

The proofs use a common pattern: an indexed family of partial subset sums that
interpolates between the identity and the full spec, with each transform level
corresponding to exactly one step of the interpolation.

* `section MobiusEquivalence` proves `lagrangeToMono = lagrangeToMonoSpec`.
* `section ZetaEquivalence` proves `monoToLagrange = monoToLagrangeSpec`.

All helper lemmas are `private`; only the two top-level theorems
`lagrangeToMono_eq_lagrangeToMonoSpec` and `monoToLagrange_eq_monoToLagrangeSpec`
are exported.

items.note:
### Fast ↔ Spec equivalence for the Möbius transform

We prove `lagrangeToMono = lagrangeToMonoSpec` by introducing an indexed family of
"partial Möbius sums" `mobiusPartial k` that interpolates between the identity (at `k = n`)
and the full spec (at `k = 0`). Each step of the fast transform
`lagrangeToMonoLevel (k - 1)` decrements the parameter by exactly one. Combined with the
base case we obtain the result by descending induction on `k`.

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.lagrangeToMono_eq_lagrangeToMonoSpec
items.doc:
The fast Möbius transform `lagrangeToMono` is pointwise equal to the inclusion-exclusion
specification `lagrangeToMonoSpec`. Combines the fold lemma with the `k = 0` base case.
items.statement:
theorem lagrangeToMono_eq_lagrangeToMonoSpec
    (p : Vector R (2 ^ n)) :
    lagrangeToMono n p = lagrangeToMonoSpec p

items.note:
### Fast ↔ Spec equivalence for the zeta transform

Mirror of `MobiusEquivalence`: we prove `monoToLagrange = monoToLagrangeSpec` with an
indexed family `zetaPartial k` of partial subset sums. Instead of the low-bits constraint
used in the Möbius proof, here `k` counts how many leading levels have already been
applied — the constraint is that `j` must agree with `i` on bits **at or above**
position `k` (`i / 2 ^ k = j / 2 ^ k`).

* At `k = 0` only `j = i` matches, so `zetaPartial 0 p i = p[i]`.
* At `k = n` the constraint is vacuous, recovering `monoToLagrangeSpec`.

Each application of `monoToLagrangeLevel k` to `Vector.ofFn (zetaPartial k p)` increments
`k` by one. `monoToLagrange n` is a `foldl`, so applying the levels `0, 1, …, n-1`
transports us from `zetaPartial 0 = id` to `zetaPartial n = spec`.

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.monoToLagrange_eq_monoToLagrangeSpec
items.doc:
The fast zeta transform `monoToLagrange` is pointwise equal to the naive
`monoToLagrangeSpec`. Mirror of `lagrangeToMono_eq_lagrangeToMonoSpec`.
items.statement:
theorem monoToLagrange_eq_monoToLagrangeSpec
    (p : Vector R (2 ^ n)) :
    monoToLagrange n p = monoToLagrangeSpec p

modules.title: Multilinear extensions on the Boolean hypercube
modules.doc:
- evaluation: a hypercube table evaluates to its entries at the Boolean vertices.
- bridge: a coefficient form and its `MvPolynomial` image evaluate alike at every point.
- uniqueness: no other polynomial of degree at most one per variable has those vertex values.

So the multilinear extension computed by CompPoly is the multilinear extension.

The reference is Thaler, "Proofs, Arguments, and Zero-Knowledge", Lemma 3.6.

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomialEval.vertex
items.doc: The Boolean vertex with index `i`, in little-endian order: coordinate `j` is bit `j` of `i`.
items.statement: def vertex [Zero R] [One R] (i : Fin (2 ^ n)) : Vector R n

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomialEval.exists_vertex_get_eq
items.doc: Every point with coordinates in `{0, 1}` is a Boolean vertex.
items.statement:
theorem exists_vertex_get_eq [Zero R] [One R] {x : Fin n → R}
    (hx : ∀ j, x j = 0 ∨ x j = 1) : ∃ i : Fin (2 ^ n), (vertex i).get = x

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomialEval.lagrangeBasis_vertex
items.doc: At a Boolean vertex the Lagrange basis is the indicator of that vertex.
items.statement:
theorem lagrangeBasis_vertex (i k : Fin (2 ^ n)) :
    (lagrangeBasis (vertex (R := R) i))[(k : ℕ)] = if i = k then 1 else 0

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomialEval.eval_vertex
items.doc: A hypercube table evaluates to its entry `i` at the vertex `i`.
items.statement:
theorem eval_vertex (p : CMlPolynomialEval R n) (i : Fin (2 ^ n)) :
    eval p (vertex i) = p[i]

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomialEval.ext_of_eval_vertex
items.doc: Hypercube tables with the same values at every vertex are equal.
items.statement:
theorem ext_of_eval_vertex {p q : CMlPolynomialEval R n}
    (h : ∀ i : Fin (2 ^ n), eval p (vertex i) = eval q (vertex i)) : p = q

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.monomialBasis_vertex
items.doc: At a Boolean vertex the monomial basis indicates the bitwise subsets of that vertex.
items.statement:
theorem monomialBasis_vertex [CommSemiring R] (i k : Fin (2 ^ n)) :
    (monomialBasis (vertex (R := R) i))[(k : ℕ)] = if (i : ℕ) &&& k = k then 1 else 0

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.eval_vertex
items.doc: A coefficient form evaluates at the vertex `i` to entry `i` of its hypercube table.
items.statement:
theorem eval_vertex [CommRing R] (p : CMlPolynomial R n) (i : Fin (2 ^ n)) :
    eval p (vertex i) = (monoToLagrange n p)[i]

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.eval_lagrangeToMono_vertex
items.doc: The coefficient form of a hypercube table evaluates to the table entries at the vertices.
items.statement:
theorem eval_lagrangeToMono_vertex [CommRing R] (f : CMlPolynomialEval R n) (i : Fin (2 ^ n)) :
    eval (lagrangeToMono n f) (vertex i) = f[i]

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.ext_of_eval_vertex
items.doc: Coefficient forms with the same values at every vertex are equal.
items.statement:
theorem ext_of_eval_vertex [CommRing R] {p q : CMlPolynomial R n}
    (h : ∀ i : Fin (2 ^ n), eval p (vertex i) = eval q (vertex i)) : p = q

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.eval_toMvPolynomial
items.doc: The `MvPolynomial` image of a coefficient form evaluates like it at every point.
items.statement:
theorem eval_toMvPolynomial [CommSemiring R] (p : CMlPolynomial R n) (x : Vector R n) :
    MvPolynomial.eval x.get (toMvPolynomial p) = eval p x

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.degreeOf_toMvPolynomial_le_one
items.doc: The `MvPolynomial` image of a coefficient form has degree at most one in each variable.
items.statement:
theorem degreeOf_toMvPolynomial_le_one [CommSemiring R] (p : CMlPolynomial R n) (j : Fin n) :
    (toMvPolynomial p).degreeOf j ≤ 1

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomial.toMvPolynomial_eq_of_eval_vertex
items.doc:
The `MvPolynomial` image of a coefficient form is fixed by its vertex values.

Any polynomial of degree at most one per variable that matches the form on the vertices equals it.
items.statement:
theorem toMvPolynomial_eq_of_eval_vertex [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] {p : CMlPolynomial R n}
    {q : MvPolynomial (Fin n) R} (hq : ∀ j, q.degreeOf j ≤ 1)
    (h : ∀ i : Fin (2 ^ n), MvPolynomial.eval (vertex i).get q = eval p (vertex i)) :
    toMvPolynomial p = q

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomialEval.eval_toMvPolynomial_vertex
items.doc: The `MvPolynomial` image of a hypercube table evaluates to entry `i` at the vertex `i`.
items.statement:
theorem eval_toMvPolynomial_vertex (f : CMlPolynomialEval R n) (i : Fin (2 ^ n)) :
    MvPolynomial.eval (vertex i).get (toMvPolynomial f) = f[i]

items.name: CompPoly.CMlPolynomialEval.toMvPolynomial_eq_of_eval_vertex
items.doc:
The `MvPolynomial` image of a hypercube table is its unique multilinear extension.

Any polynomial of degree at most one per variable taking the table values on the vertices equals it.
items.statement:
theorem toMvPolynomial_eq_of_eval_vertex [IsDomain R] {f : CMlPolynomialEval R n}
    {q : MvPolynomial (Fin n) R} (hq : ∀ j, q.degreeOf j ≤ 1)
    (h : ∀ i : Fin (2 ^ n), MvPolynomial.eval (vertex i).get q = f[i]) :
    toMvPolynomial f = q

modules.authors: Frantisek Silvasi, Julian Sutherland, Andrei Burdușa, Derek Sorensen, Dimitris Mitsios
modules.title: Computable multivariate polynomials
modules.doc:
Polynomials of the form `α₁ * m₁ + α₂ * m₂ + ... + αₖ * mₖ` where `αᵢ` is any semiring
and `mᵢ` is a `CMvMonomial`.

This is implemented as a wrapper around `CPoly.Lawful`, which ensures that all stored
coefficients are non-zero.

This file contains the core type definition and basic operations. Higher-level definitions
that depend on ring instances (monomial orders, `rename`, `aeval`, etc.) are in
`CMvPolynomial.lean`. The `CommSemiring` and `CommRing` instances are in `MvPolyEquiv.lean`.

## Main definitions

* `CPoly.CMvPolynomial n R`: The type of multivariate polynomials in `n` variables
  with coefficients in `R`.
* `CPoly.CMvPolynomial.C`: Constant polynomial constructor.
* `CPoly.CMvPolynomial.X`: Variable polynomial constructor.
* `CPoly.CMvPolynomial.monomial`: Monomial constructor.
* `CPoly.CMvPolynomial.coeff`: Extract the coefficient of a monomial.
* `CPoly.CMvPolynomial.eval₂`, `CPoly.CMvPolynomial.eval`: Polynomial evaluation.
* `CPoly.CMvPolynomial.eval₂Horner`, `CPoly.CMvPolynomial.evalHorner`:
  Polynomial evaluation using Horner's method.
* `CPoly.CMvPolynomial.support`, `CPoly.CMvPolynomial.totalDegree`,
  `CPoly.CMvPolynomial.degreeOf`, `CPoly.CMvPolynomial.degrees`,
  `CPoly.CMvPolynomial.vars`: Degree and support queries.

items.doc: A computable multivariate polynomial in `n` variables with coefficients in `R`.
items.statement: abbrev CMvPolynomial (n : ℕ) (R : Type*) [Zero R] : Type _

items.doc: Construct a constant polynomial.
items.statement: def C {n : ℕ} {R : Type*} [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Zero R] (c : R) : CMvPolynomial n R

items.doc: Construct the polynomial $X_i$.

    (i : Fin n) : CMvPolynomial n R

items.statement: def coeff {R : Type*} {n : ℕ} [Zero R] (m : CMvMonomial n) (p : CMvPolynomial n R) : R

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.ext
items.doc: Extensionality: two polynomials are equal if all their coefficients are equal.
items.statement:
theorem ext {n : ℕ} [Zero R] (p q : CMvPolynomial n R)
    (h : ∀ m, coeff m p = coeff m q) : p = q

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.fromUnlawful_zero
items.statement: lemma fromUnlawful_zero {n : ℕ} [Zero R] : Lawful.fromUnlawful 0 = (0 : Lawful n R)

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.add_getD?
items.statement: lemma add_getD? : (p + q).val[m]?.getD 0 = p.val[m]?.getD 0 + q.val[m]?.getD 0

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.coeff_zero
items.statement: lemma coeff_zero : ∀ σ, coeff σ (0 : CMvPolynomial n R) = 0

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.coeff_add
items.statement: lemma coeff_add : coeff m (p + q) = coeff m p + coeff m q

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.fromUnlawful_fold_eq_fold_fromUnlawful₀
items.doc: Auxiliary lemma showing that conversion from unlawful polynomials respects the sum fold.
items.statement:
lemma fromUnlawful_fold_eq_fold_fromUnlawful₀
    {t : List (CMvMonomial n × R)} {f : CMvMonomial n → R → Unlawful n R} :
    ∀ init : Unlawful n R,
    Lawful.fromUnlawful (List.foldl (fun u term => (f term.1 term.2) + u) init t) =
    List.foldl (fun l term => (Lawful.fromUnlawful (f term.1 term.2)) + l)
               (Lawful.fromUnlawful init) t

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.fromUnlawful_fold_eq_fold_fromUnlawful
items.doc:
Auxiliary lemma showing that conversion from unlawful polynomials respects
the fold over terms.
items.statement:
lemma fromUnlawful_fold_eq_fold_fromUnlawful {t : Unlawful n R}
    {f : CMvMonomial n → R → Unlawful n R} :
  Lawful.fromUnlawful (ExtTreeMap.foldl (fun u m c => (f m c) + u) 0 t) =
  ExtTreeMap.foldl (fun l m c => (Lawful.fromUnlawful (f m c)) + l) 0 t

The support of a polynomial (set of monomials with non-zero coefficients),

lemma degreeOf_eq_count_degrees {n : ℕ} {R : Type*} [Zero R]

    p.degreeOf i = Multiset.count i p.degrees

modules.title: Serialization of multivariate polynomials
modules.doc:
A `CMvPolynomial n R` is a sorted map from exponent vectors to nonzero coefficients, so its
`toList` is already a canonical sequence of terms. It encodes as a `u64` term count followed
by the terms in key order, each term its `n` exponents as `u64` words and then its coefficient.
Decoding rebuilds the map and drops zero coefficients, so it lands on the polynomial. There is
no fixed-width multivariate codec: genuinely multivariate protocol messages are multilinear,
and those have the dense codec of `CompPoly.Multilinear.Bytes`.

A polynomial is `Valid` when its term count and every exponent fit in a `u64` and its
coefficients are valid.

items.name: CPoly.CMvMonomial.instDelimitedCodec
items.statement: instance CMvMonomial.instDelimitedCodec (n : ℕ) : DelimitedCodec (CMvMonomial n)

items.name: CPoly.CMvMonomial.instDelimitedCodecVector
items.doc:
The same codec at `Vector ℕ n`, the underlying type of `CMvMonomial n`, for goals that
instance search sees only after unfolding (the `#m[…]` notation elaborates to a `Vector`).
items.statement: instance CMvMonomial.instDelimitedCodecVector (n : ℕ) : DelimitedCodec (Vector ℕ n)

items.name: CPoly.CMvMonomial.valid_iff
items.statement:
theorem CMvMonomial.valid_iff {n : ℕ} (m : CMvMonomial n) :
    Valid m ↔ ∀ e ∈ (m : Vector ℕ n).toList, e < 2 ^ 64

items.name: CPoly.CMvMonomial.encode_eq
items.statement:
theorem CMvMonomial.encode_eq {n : ℕ} (m : CMvMonomial n) :
    encode m = encodeList (m : Vector ℕ n).toList

items.note: ## Rebuilding a map from its own term list

items.name: CPoly.CMvMonomial.instLawfulBEqCmp
items.doc:
`compare` and `==` agree on monomials: both decide equality. Built from `LawfulEqCmp` and
`LawfulBEq` rather than transported from `Vector.compareLex`, whose instance body is not
available to the kernel here.
items.statement:
instance CMvMonomial.instLawfulBEqCmp (n : ℕ) :
    LawfulBEqCmp (Ord.compare (α := CMvMonomial n))

items.name: CPoly.Unlawful.ofList_toList
items.doc: A tree map is the map of its own term list.
items.statement: theorem Unlawful.ofList_toList (p : Unlawful n R) : Unlawful.ofList p.toList = p

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.instDelimitedCodec
items.doc: A `u64` term count, then each term as `n` exponents and a coefficient.
items.statement:
instance CMvPolynomial.instDelimitedCodec [DelimitedCodec R] :
    DelimitedCodec (CMvPolynomial n R)

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.valid_iff
items.statement:
theorem CMvPolynomial.valid_iff [DelimitedCodec R] (p : CMvPolynomial n R) :
    Valid p ↔ p.1.toList.length < 2 ^ 64 ∧
      ∀ t ∈ p.1.toList, (∀ e ∈ (t.1 : Vector ℕ n).toList, e < 2 ^ 64) ∧ Valid t.2

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.encode_eq
items.statement:
theorem CMvPolynomial.encode_eq [DelimitedCodec R] (p : CMvPolynomial n R) :
    encode p = encodeU64 p.1.toList.length ++ encodeList p.1.toList

modules.authors: Frantisek Silvasi, Julian Sutherland, Andrei Burdușa
modules.title: Computable monomials
modules.doc:
Monomials of the form `X₀ᵃ * X₁ᵇ * ... * Xₖᶻ`. These are represented as vectors of natural numbers,
where each element corresponds to the exponent of a variable.

## Main definitions

* `CPoly.CMvMonomial n`: The type of monomials in `n` variables, implemented as `Vector ℕ n`.

items.name: CPoly.CMvMonomial
items.doc:
Monomial in `n` variables.
- `#v[e₀, e₁, e₂]` denotes X₀^e₀ * X₁^e₁ * X₂^e₂
items.statement: def CMvMonomial (n : ℕ) : Type

items.name: CPoly.CMvMonomial.ext
items.statement: protected theorem ext (h : (i : Nat) → (_ : i < n) → m₁[i] = m₂[i]) : m₁ = m₂

items.name: CPoly.CMvMonomial.extend
items.doc: Extend a monomial to a larger number of variables by padding with zeros.
items.statement: def extend (n' : ℕ) (m : CMvMonomial n) : CMvMonomial (max n n')

items.name: CPoly.CMvMonomial.totalDegree
items.doc: The total degree of a monomial (sum of all exponents).
items.statement: def totalDegree (m : CMvMonomial n) : ℕ

items.name: CPoly.CMvMonomial.degreeOf
items.doc: The degree of the $i$-th variable in the monomial.
items.statement: def degreeOf (m : CMvMonomial n) (i : Fin n) : ℕ

items.name: CPoly.CMvMonomial.zero
items.doc: The zero monomial (all exponents are zero).
items.statement: def zero : CMvMonomial n

items.name: CPoly.CMvMonomial.add
items.doc: Monomial multiplication (adds exponents element-wise).
items.statement: def add : CMvMonomial n → CMvMonomial n → CMvMonomial n

items.name: CPoly.CMvMonomial.getElem_add

items.name: CPoly.CMvMonomial.add_zero

`m₁ ∣ m₂` holds exactly when every exponent of `m₁` is at most the matching exponent of

items.statement: theorem dvd_iff : m₁ ∣ m₂ ↔ ∀ (i : ℕ) (h : i < n), m₁[i] ≤ m₂[i]

The monomial division $m_1 / m_2$ (subtracts exponents element-wise).

The result makes sense assuming  `m₂ | m₁`.

modules.title: Evaluation of computable multivariate polynomials, bundled and over `Finset`s
modules.doc:
CompPoly records that `CMvPolynomial.eval vals` respects each ring operation separately
(`eval_zero`, `eval_one`, `eval_add`, `eval_mul`, `eval_C`, …), which is what `simp`/`grind`
need to normalize a *fixed* expression. Two things are missing for reasoning about a **family**
of polynomials: the value of a bare variable, and commutation with `Finset.sum` / `Finset.prod`.

Both follow at once from bundling: `CMvPolynomial.eval vals` is `eval₂Hom (RingHom.id R) vals`,
so `map_sum` and `map_prod` apply verbatim. `evalHom` records that bundling; the two `Finset`
lemmas are its immediate corollaries, stated in unbundled form so that call sites can rewrite
without unfolding.

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.evalHom
items.doc:
Evaluation at a fixed point, bundled as a ring homomorphism — the identity-coefficient case
of `eval₂Hom`. This is what gives evaluation the `map_*` API of a `RingHom`.
items.statement: def evalHom : CMvPolynomial n R →+* R

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.evalHom_apply
items.statement: theorem evalHom_apply (p : CMvPolynomial n R) : evalHom vals p = p.eval vals

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.eval_zero
items.statement: lemma eval_zero : (0 : CMvPolynomial n R).eval vals = 0

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.eval_one
items.statement: lemma eval_one : (1 : CMvPolynomial n R).eval vals = 1

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.eval_C
items.statement: lemma eval_C (c : R) : (CMvPolynomial.C c : CMvPolynomial n R).eval vals = c

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.eval_X
items.statement: theorem eval_X (i : Fin n) : (X (R := R) i).eval vals = vals i

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.eval_add
items.statement:
lemma eval_add (p q : CMvPolynomial n R) :
    (p + q).eval vals = p.eval vals + q.eval vals

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.eval_mul
items.statement:
lemma eval_mul (p q : CMvPolynomial n R) :
    (p * q).eval vals = p.eval vals * q.eval vals

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.eval_pow
items.statement:
lemma eval_pow (p : CMvPolynomial n R) (k : ℕ) :
    (p ^ k).eval vals = (p.eval vals) ^ k

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.eval_neg
items.statement:
lemma eval_neg (p : CMvPolynomial n R) :
    (-p).eval vals = -(p.eval vals)

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.eval_sub
items.statement:
lemma eval_sub (p q : CMvPolynomial n R) :
    (p - q).eval vals = p.eval vals - q.eval vals

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.eval_sum
items.doc: Evaluation commutes with a finite sum of polynomials.
items.statement:
theorem eval_sum {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (f : ι → CMvPolynomial n R) :
    (∑ i ∈ s, f i).eval vals = ∑ i ∈ s, (f i).eval vals

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.eval_prod
items.doc: Evaluation commutes with a finite product of polynomials.
items.statement:
theorem eval_prod {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (f : ι → CMvPolynomial n R) :
    (∏ i ∈ s, f i).eval vals = ∏ i ∈ s, (f i).eval vals

items.note:
## Transporting a whole polynomial

The lemmas above are enough for statements about *values*. A statement about *degrees* is not
determined by values (two distinct polynomials agree everywhere over a finite field), so it has to
cross the representation boundary at the level of the polynomial itself, through
`fromCMvPolynomial`. That map is the forward direction of `polyRingEquiv`, hence a ring
homomorphism, so it too commutes with `Finset.sum` and `Finset.prod`.

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.eval_ext_univariate
items.doc:
**Bridge from univariate eval-extensionality.** Two single-variable
`CMvPolynomial`s over an integral domain that agree on more than $d$ points
of a `Finset S` are equal, when $d$ bounds the `degreeOf 0` of their
difference through the `CPolynomial.cmvEquiv` bridge.

The hypothesis form matches Schwartz–Zippel usage at call sites: callers
typically have a degree bound on the difference polynomial, not on `p` and
`q` individually.
items.statement:
theorem eval_ext_univariate
    [CommRing R] [DecidableEq R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [IsDomain R]
    {p q : CMvPolynomial 1 R} {d : ℕ} {S : Finset R}
    (hdeg : (fromCMvPolynomial p - fromCMvPolynomial q).degreeOf 0 ≤ d)
    (hagree :
      d < (S.filter
              (fun r ↦ p.eval (fun _ ↦ r) = q.eval (fun _ ↦ r))).card) :
    p = q

modules.authors: Elias Judin, Aristotle (Harmonic), Dimitris Mitsios, Julian Sutherland
modules.title: `finSuccEquiv` for `CMvPolynomial`
modules.doc:
This file defines the computable multivariate polynomial equivalence for
splitting off one variable, mirroring `MvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv` from Mathlib.

In Mathlib, `MvPolynomial` accepts a general type `σ` for the index set of the
variables. Then, `optionEquivLeft` provides the algebra isomorphism
`MvPolynomial (Option σ) R ≃ₐ[R] Polynomial (MvPolynomial σ R)`. Finally,
`finSuccEquiv` is defined as the composition of the rename step
(`Fin (n+1) ≃ Option (Fin n)`) with `optionEquivLeft`. There is no such
distinction in `CMvPolynomial` because the variables are of type `Fin n` by
definition. Therefore, only `CMvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv` applies.

## Main definitions

* `CMvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv` — `noncomputable` ring equivalence
    `CMvPolynomial (n+1) R ≃+* Polynomial (CMvPolynomial n R)`,
    viewing a polynomial in `n+1` variables as a univariate polynomial over `n` variables.
* `CMvPolynomial.finSuccEquivNth p` — **computable** ring equivalence
    `CMvPolynomial (n+1) R ≃+* CompPoly.CPolynomial (CMvPolynomial n R)` for an *arbitrary* pivot
    `p`, splitting off variable `p`. Both directions are `eval₂` folds, so they compute; the
    ring-equivalence laws are proved by extensionality on the `C`/`X` generators.
* `CMvPolynomial.finSuccEquivNthHom p` / `finSuccEquivNthInvHom p` — its two directions as
    `RingHom`s.

## Implementation notes

`finSuccEquiv` is `noncomputable` because it goes through the `polyRingEquiv` bridge between
`CMvPolynomial` and `MvPolynomial`; its forward/inverse correctness is obtained structurally from
the underlying Mathlib `AlgEquiv` via `RingEquiv.trans`.

`finSuccEquivNth` avoids that bridge in its *definition* (staying inside the computable
`CMvPolynomial` / `CPolynomial` world), and only crosses to Mathlib in the *proof* of
`map_polyRingEquiv_toPoly_finSuccEquivNth`, which identifies it with
`MvPolynomial.finSuccEquivNth` after transport.

items.name: CPoly.polynomialCMvPolyEquiv
items.doc: `Polynomial.mapEquiv` through the CMvPolynomial ↔ MvPolynomial bridge.
items.statement:
noncomputable def polynomialCMvPolyEquiv :
    Polynomial (CMvPolynomial n R) ≃+* Polynomial (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R)

items.name: CMvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv
items.doc:
Ring equivalence splitting off the first variable:
`CMvPolynomial (n+1) R ≃+* Polynomial (CMvPolynomial n R)`.

This mirrors `MvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv R n`. The 0-th variable becomes
the univariate indeterminate `Polynomial.X`, and variables `1, …, n` become
the multivariate variables of the coefficient ring `CMvPolynomial n R`.
items.statement:
noncomputable def finSuccEquiv :
    CMvPolynomial (n + 1) R ≃+* Polynomial (CMvPolynomial n R)

items.name: CMvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv_symm_apply_apply
items.doc: The equivalence is a left inverse: applying the inverse then forward is the identity.
items.statement:
theorem finSuccEquiv_symm_apply_apply (p : CMvPolynomial (n + 1) R) :
    finSuccEquiv.symm (finSuccEquiv p) = p

items.name: CMvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv_apply_symm_apply
items.doc: The equivalence is a right inverse: applying forward then the inverse is the identity.
items.statement:
theorem finSuccEquiv_apply_symm_apply
    (q : Polynomial (CMvPolynomial n R)) :
    finSuccEquiv (finSuccEquiv.symm q) = q

items.name: CMvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv_add
items.doc: `finSuccEquiv` preserves addition.
items.statement:
theorem finSuccEquiv_add (p q : CMvPolynomial (n + 1) R) :
    finSuccEquiv (p + q) =
      finSuccEquiv p + finSuccEquiv q

items.name: CMvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv_mul
items.doc: `finSuccEquiv` preserves multiplication.
items.statement:
theorem finSuccEquiv_mul (p q : CMvPolynomial (n + 1) R) :
    finSuccEquiv (p * q) =
      finSuccEquiv p * finSuccEquiv q

items.name: CMvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv_zero
items.doc: `finSuccEquiv` maps zero to zero.
items.statement:
theorem finSuccEquiv_zero :
    finSuccEquiv (0 : CMvPolynomial (n + 1) R) = 0

items.name: CMvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv_one
items.doc: `finSuccEquiv` maps one to one.
items.statement:
theorem finSuccEquiv_one :
    finSuccEquiv (1 : CMvPolynomial (n + 1) R) = 1

items.note:
### The computable `finSuccEquivNth` (arbitrary pivot)

Unlike `finSuccEquiv` above, this stays inside the computable `CMvPolynomial` / `CPolynomial`
world and works for an arbitrary pivot `p`.

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.fseVars
items.doc:
Assignment used by the forward direction: variable `p` goes to the univariate `X`, every
other variable `p.succAbove j` goes to the constant `C (X j)`.
items.statement: def fseVars (p : Fin (n + 1)) : Fin (n + 1) → CPolynomial (CMvPolynomial n R)

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.fseVars_same
items.statement:
theorem fseVars_same (p : Fin (n + 1)) :
    fseVars (R := R) p p = CPolynomial.X

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.fseVars_succAbove
items.statement:
theorem fseVars_succAbove (p : Fin (n + 1)) (j : Fin n) :
    fseVars (R := R) p (p.succAbove j) = CPolynomial.C (CMvPolynomial.X j)

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.finSuccEquivNthHom
items.doc:
Forward direction of `finSuccEquivNth`, as a `RingHom`.  Splits variable `p` off as the
univariate indeterminate over the other `n` variables.  Computable.
items.statement:
def finSuccEquivNthHom (p : Fin (n + 1)) :
    CMvPolynomial (n + 1) R →+* CPolynomial (CMvPolynomial n R)

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.insertVarHom
items.doc:
"Insert a dummy variable at position `p`": the embedding `CMvPolynomial n R →+* CMvPolynomial
(n+1) R` sending `X j` to `X (p.succAbove j)`.  Computable.
items.statement: def insertVarHom (p : Fin (n + 1)) : CMvPolynomial n R →+* CMvPolynomial (n + 1) R

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.finSuccEquivNthInvHom
items.doc: Inverse direction of `finSuccEquivNth`, as a `RingHom`.  Computable.
items.statement:
def finSuccEquivNthInvHom (p : Fin (n + 1)) :
    CPolynomial (CMvPolynomial n R) →+* CMvPolynomial (n + 1) R

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.finSuccEquivNthHom_C
items.statement:
theorem finSuccEquivNthHom_C (p : Fin (n + 1)) (c : R) :
    finSuccEquivNthHom (R := R) p (CMvPolynomial.C c) = CPolynomial.C (CMvPolynomial.C c)

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.finSuccEquivNthHom_X_same
items.statement:
theorem finSuccEquivNthHom_X_same (p : Fin (n + 1)) :
    finSuccEquivNthHom (R := R) p (CMvPolynomial.X p) = CPolynomial.X

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.finSuccEquivNthHom_X_succAbove
items.statement:
theorem finSuccEquivNthHom_X_succAbove (p : Fin (n + 1)) (j : Fin n) :
    finSuccEquivNthHom (R := R) p (CMvPolynomial.X (p.succAbove j))
      = CPolynomial.C (CMvPolynomial.X j)

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.insertVarHom_C
items.statement:
theorem insertVarHom_C (p : Fin (n + 1)) (c : R) :
    insertVarHom (R := R) p (CMvPolynomial.C c) = CMvPolynomial.C c

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.insertVarHom_X
items.statement:
theorem insertVarHom_X (p : Fin (n + 1)) (j : Fin n) :
    insertVarHom (R := R) p (CMvPolynomial.X j) = CMvPolynomial.X (p.succAbove j)

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.finSuccEquivNthInvHom_C
items.statement:
theorem finSuccEquivNthInvHom_C (p : Fin (n + 1)) (q : CMvPolynomial n R) :
    finSuccEquivNthInvHom (R := R) p (CPolynomial.C q) = insertVarHom p q

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.finSuccEquivNthInvHom_X
items.statement:
theorem finSuccEquivNthInvHom_X (p : Fin (n + 1)) :
    finSuccEquivNthInvHom (R := R) p (CPolynomial.X) = CMvPolynomial.X p

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.finSuccEquivNthHom_comp_insertVarHom
items.doc:
`finSuccEquivNthHom` composed with `insertVarHom` is the constant embedding
`CMvPolynomial n R →+* CPolynomial (CMvPolynomial n R)`.
items.statement:
theorem finSuccEquivNthHom_comp_insertVarHom (p : Fin (n + 1)) :
    (finSuccEquivNthHom (R := R) p).comp (insertVarHom p) = CPolynomial.CHom

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.finSuccEquivNthHom_comp_inv
items.statement:
theorem finSuccEquivNthHom_comp_inv (p : Fin (n + 1)) :
    (finSuccEquivNthHom (R := R) p).comp (finSuccEquivNthInvHom p)
      = RingHom.id (CPolynomial (CMvPolynomial n R))

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.finSuccEquivNthInvHom_comp_fwd
items.statement:
theorem finSuccEquivNthInvHom_comp_fwd (p : Fin (n + 1)) :
    (finSuccEquivNthInvHom (R := R) p).comp (finSuccEquivNthHom p)
      = RingHom.id (CMvPolynomial (n + 1) R)

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.finSuccEquivNth
items.doc:
**The computable `finSuccEquivNth`**: a ring equivalence
`CMvPolynomial (n+1) R ≃+* CompPoly.CPolynomial (CMvPolynomial n R)` for an arbitrary pivot `p`.
Both directions compute.
items.statement:
def finSuccEquivNth (p : Fin (n + 1)) :
    CMvPolynomial (n + 1) R ≃+* CPolynomial (CMvPolynomial n R)

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.finSuccEquivNth_apply
items.statement:
theorem finSuccEquivNth_apply (p : Fin (n + 1)) (P : CMvPolynomial (n + 1) R) :
    finSuccEquivNth p P = finSuccEquivNthHom p P

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.finSuccEquivNth_symm_apply
items.statement:
theorem finSuccEquivNth_symm_apply (p : Fin (n + 1))
    (Q : CPolynomial (CMvPolynomial n R)) :
    (finSuccEquivNth p).symm Q = finSuccEquivNthInvHom p Q

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.map_polyRingEquiv_toPoly_finSuccEquivNth
items.doc:
The computable `finSuccEquivNth`, transported to Mathlib's `MvPolynomial`/`Polynomial` world
along `polyRingEquiv` and `CPolynomial.toPoly`, is Mathlib's `MvPolynomial.finSuccEquivNth`.
items.statement:
theorem map_polyRingEquiv_toPoly_finSuccEquivNth (p : Fin (n + 1)) (P : CMvPolynomial (n + 1) R) :
    Polynomial.map (CPoly.polyRingEquiv (n := n) (R := R)).toRingHom
        (CPolynomial.toPoly (finSuccEquivNthHom p P))
      = MvPolynomial.finSuccEquivNth R p (CPoly.fromCMvPolynomial P)

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.natDegree_finSuccEquivNthHom
items.doc: The univariate degree of `finSuccEquivNth p P` is the degree of variable `p` in `P`.
items.statement:
theorem natDegree_finSuccEquivNthHom (p : Fin (n + 1)) (P : CMvPolynomial (n + 1) R) :
    (finSuccEquivNthHom p P).natDegree = P.degreeOf p

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.natDegree_finSuccEquivNthHom_le
items.doc:
`finSuccEquivNth p P` has univariate degree at most `d` whenever `P` has per-variable
degree at most `d`.
items.statement:
theorem natDegree_finSuccEquivNthHom_le {d : ℕ} (p : Fin (n + 1)) (P : CMvPolynomial (n + 1) R)
    (hP : ∀ k, P.degreeOf k ≤ d) : (finSuccEquivNthHom p P).natDegree ≤ d

modules.authors: Frantisek Silvasi, Julian Sutherland, Andrei Burdușa, Derek Sorensen, Dimitris Mitsios
modules.title: Correctness lemmas for multivariate Horner evaluation
modules.doc:
This file proves that the fixed-order multivariate Horner evaluator in
`CompPoly.Multivariate.Basic` agrees with ordinary multivariate
evaluation.

items.note: ### Mathematical specifications for Horner helper functions

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.eval₂Horner_eq_eval₂
items.doc: Fixed-order multivariate Horner evaluation agrees with ordinary evaluation.
items.statement:
theorem eval₂Horner_eq_eval₂ {R S : Type*} {n : ℕ} [Semiring R] [CommSemiring S]
    (f : R →+* S) (vs : Fin n → S) (p : CMvPolynomial n R) :
    eval₂Horner f vs p = eval₂ f vs p

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.evalHorner_eq_eval
items.doc: Fixed-order multivariate Horner evaluation agrees with ordinary evaluation.
items.statement:
theorem evalHorner_eq_eval {R : Type*} {n : ℕ} [CommSemiring R]
    (vs : Fin n → R) (p : CMvPolynomial n R) :
    evalHorner vs p = eval vs p

modules.title: 'Lawful' finite supports
modules.doc:
This file defines the `Lawful` subtype, which consists of `Unlawful` polynomials
where all stored coefficients are guaranteed to be non-zero. This provides a canonical
representation (similar to `Finsupp`) and is the primary representation used for
computable multivariate polynomials.

## Main definitions

* `CPoly.Lawful n R`: The subtype of `Unlawful n R` with no zero coefficients.

items.name: CPoly.Lawful
items.doc: The subtype of polynomials with no zero coefficients.
items.statement: def Lawful (n : ℕ) (R : Type*) [Zero R] : Type _

items.name: CPoly.instEmptyCol
items.statement: instance instEmptyCol : EmptyCollection (Lawful n R)

items.name: CPoly.Lawful.getElem?_eq_val_getElem?
items.statement: lemma getElem?_eq_val_getElem? : p[m]? = p.1[m]?

items.name: CPoly.Lawful.mem_iff_cast
items.statement: lemma mem_iff_cast : x ∈ p.1 ↔ x ∈ p

items.name: CPoly.Lawful.mem_iff
items.statement: lemma mem_iff : x ∈ p ↔ ∃ v, v ≠ 0 ∧ p[x]? = .some v

items.name: CPoly.Lawful.getElem?_ne_some_zero
items.statement: theorem getElem?_ne_some_zero : p[m]? ≠ some 0

items.name: CPoly.Lawful.getD_getElem?_ne_zero_of_mem
items.statement: theorem getD_getElem?_ne_zero_of_mem (h : m ∈ p) : p[m]?.getD 0 ≠ 0

items.name: CPoly.Lawful.getElem_eq_getElem
items.statement: lemma getElem_eq_getElem (h : m ∈ p) : p[m] = p.1[m]

items.name: CPoly.Lawful.grind_add_skip_aggressive
items.doc: Note to self: This goes too far.
items.statement:
protected lemma grind_add_skip_aggressive [Add R] {p₁ p₂ : Lawful n R} :
    p₁ + p₂ = fromUnlawful (ExtTreeMap.mergeWith (fun _ c₁ c₂ => c₁ + c₂) p₁.1 p₂.1)

items.name: CPoly.Lawful.npow
items.doc:
Polynomial exponentiation via repeated multiplication. `O(k)` multiplications.

This is the specification; `npowBySq` is the efficient `O(log k)` implementation
used by the `NatPow` instance once the equivalence with this naive form has been
proven.
items.statement: def npow [NatCast R] [Add R] [Mul R] : ℕ → Lawful n R → Lawful n R

items.name: CPoly.Lawful.npowBySq
items.doc:
Polynomial exponentiation via repeated squaring. `O(log k)` multiplications
instead of `O(k)`.

For `k > 0`, computes `p ^ k` by recursing on `k / 2`:
* If `k` is even: `(p ^ (k / 2))²`
* If `k` is odd:  `p · (p ^ (k / 2))²`

Equivalent to `npow` (see `npowBySq_eq_npow`).
items.statement: def npowBySq [NatCast R] [Add R] [Mul R] (p : Lawful n R) : ℕ → Lawful n R

modules.doc: Compatibility lemmas used to transport algebraic structure across the conversion.

items.name: CPoly.map_add
items.statement:
lemma map_add (a b : CMvPolynomial n R) :
    fromCMvPolynomial (a + b) = fromCMvPolynomial a + fromCMvPolynomial b

items.name: CPoly.map_zero
items.statement: lemma map_zero : fromCMvPolynomial (0 : CMvPolynomial n R) = 0

items.name: CPoly.map_one
items.statement: lemma map_one : fromCMvPolynomial (1 : CMvPolynomial n R) = 1

items.name: CPoly.toList_pairs_monomial_coeff
items.statement:
lemma toList_pairs_monomial_coeff {β : Type*} [AddCommMonoid β]
    {t : Unlawful n R}
  {f : CMvMonomial n → R → β} :
  t.toList.map (fun term => f term.1 term.2) =
    t.monomials.map (fun m => f m (t.coeff m))

items.name: CPoly.foldl_eq_sum
items.statement:
lemma foldl_eq_sum {β : Type*} [AddCommMonoid β]
    {t : CMvPolynomial n R}
    {f : CMvMonomial n → R → β} :
    ExtTreeMap.foldl (fun x m c => (f m c) + x) 0 t.1 =
      Finsupp.sum (AddMonoidAlgebra.coeff (fromCMvPolynomial t))
        (f ∘ CMvMonomial.ofFinsupp)

items.name: CPoly.coeff_sum
items.statement:
lemma coeff_sum [AddCommMonoid α]
    (s : Finset α)
    (f : α → CMvPolynomial n R)
    (m : CMvMonomial n) :
    coeff m (∑ x ∈ s, f x) = ∑ x ∈ s, coeff m (f x)

items.name: CPoly.fromCMvPolynomial_sum_eq_sum_fromCMvPolynomial
items.statement:
lemma fromCMvPolynomial_sum_eq_sum_fromCMvPolynomial
    {f : (Fin n →₀ ℕ) → R → Lawful n R }
    {a : CMvPolynomial n R} :
    fromCMvPolynomial (Finsupp.sum (AddMonoidAlgebra.coeff (fromCMvPolynomial a)) f) =
      Finsupp.sum (AddMonoidAlgebra.coeff (fromCMvPolynomial a))
        (fun m c ↦ fromCMvPolynomial (f m c))

items.name: CPoly.map_mul
items.statement:
lemma map_mul (a b : CMvPolynomial n R) :
    fromCMvPolynomial (a * b) = fromCMvPolynomial a * fromCMvPolynomial b

items.name: CPoly.map_neg
items.statement:
lemma map_neg (a : CMvPolynomial n R) :
    fromCMvPolynomial (-a) = -fromCMvPolynomial a

items.name: CPoly.map_sub
items.statement:
lemma map_sub (a b : CMvPolynomial n R) :
    fromCMvPolynomial (Sub.sub a b) = fromCMvPolynomial a - fromCMvPolynomial b

modules.authors: Frantisek Silvasi, Julian Sutherland, Andrei Burdușa, Derek Sorensen, Dimitris Mitsios
modules.title: Computable multivariate polynomials (extended operations)
modules.doc:
Operations on `CMvPolynomial` that depend on ring instances from `MvPolyEquiv.lean`,
such as monomial orders, leading terms, restriction, variable renaming, and substitution.

The core type and basic operations (`CMvPolynomial`, `C`, `X`, `coeff`, `eval`, etc.)
are in `CMvPolynomial.lean`. The `CommSemiring` and `CommRing` instances are in
`MvPolyEquiv.lean`.

## Main definitions

* `MonomialOrder`: Typeclass for comparing monomials.
* `leadingMonomial`, `leadingCoeff`, `leadingTerm`: Leading term operations
  according to a monomial order.
* `rename`: Rename variables using a function `Fin n → Fin m`.
* `aeval`: Algebra evaluation.
* `bind₁`: Substitution of polynomials for variables.

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.MonomialOrder
items.doc:
Monomial ordering typeclass for `n` variables.

Provides a way to compare monomials for determining leading terms.
items.statement:
class MonomialOrder (n : ℕ) where
  compare : CMvMonomial n → CMvMonomial n → Ordering

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.MonomialOrder.degree
items.doc:
Baseline degree of a monomial.

Currently this is the ordinary total degree and is independent of
`MonomialOrder.compare`.
items.statement: def MonomialOrder.degree {n : ℕ} (m : CMvMonomial n) : ℕ

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.leadingMonomial
items.doc:
Leading monomial of a polynomial according to a monomial order.

Returns `none` for the zero polynomial.
items.statement:
def leadingMonomial {n : ℕ} {R : Type*} [Zero R] [MonomialOrder n]
    (p : CMvPolynomial n R) : Option (CMvMonomial n)

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.leadingTerm
items.doc:
Leading term of a polynomial according to a monomial order.

Returns `0` for the zero polynomial, and otherwise returns the monomial with
leading monomial and leading coefficient.
items.statement:
def leadingTerm {n : ℕ} {R : Type*} [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [MonomialOrder n]
    (p : CMvPolynomial n R) : CMvPolynomial n R

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.leadingCoeff
items.doc:
Leading coefficient of a polynomial according to a monomial order.

Returns `0` for the zero polynomial.
items.statement:
def leadingCoeff {n : ℕ} {R : Type*} [Zero R] [MonomialOrder n]
    (p : CMvPolynomial n R) : R

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.leadingCoeff_eq_zero_of_leadingMonomial_eq_none
CPoly.CMvPolynomial.leadingCoeff_eq_coeff_of_leadingMonomial_eq_some
CPoly.CMvPolynomial.leadingCoeff_eq_coeff_leadingMonomial
items.doc:
Packaged form of `leadingCoeff`: it is the coefficient at the optional leading monomial,
defaulting to `0` when no leading monomial exists.
items.statement:
lemma leadingCoeff_eq_coeff_leadingMonomial
    {n : ℕ} {R : Type*} [Zero R] [MonomialOrder n] (p : CMvPolynomial n R) :
    leadingCoeff p = (leadingMonomial p).elim 0 (fun m => coeff m p)

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.leadingTerm_eq_zero_of_leadingMonomial_eq_none
items.statement:
lemma leadingTerm_eq_zero_of_leadingMonomial_eq_none
    {n : ℕ} {R : Type*} [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [MonomialOrder n]
    {p : CMvPolynomial n R} (h : leadingMonomial p = none) :
    leadingTerm p = 0

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.leadingTerm_eq_monomial_of_leadingMonomial_eq_some
items.statement:
lemma leadingTerm_eq_monomial_of_leadingMonomial_eq_some
    {n : ℕ} {R : Type*} [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [MonomialOrder n]
    {p : CMvPolynomial n R} {m : CMvMonomial n} (h : leadingMonomial p = some m) :
    leadingTerm p = monomial m (coeff m p)

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.aeval
items.doc:
Algebra evaluation: evaluates polynomial in an algebra.

Given an algebra `σ` over `R` and a function `f : Fin n → σ`, evaluates the polynomial.
items.statement:
def aeval {n : ℕ} {R σ : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [CommSemiring σ] [Algebra R σ]
    (f : Fin n → σ) (p : CMvPolynomial n R) : σ

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.aeval_eq_eval₂
items.statement:
lemma aeval_eq_eval₂ {n : ℕ} {R σ : Type*}
    [CommSemiring R] [CommSemiring σ] [Algebra R σ]
    (f : Fin n → σ) (p : CMvPolynomial n R) :
    aeval f p = eval₂ (algebraMap R σ) f p

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.aeval_C
items.statement:
lemma aeval_C {n : ℕ} {R σ : Type*}
    [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    [CommSemiring σ] [Algebra R σ]
    (f : Fin n → σ) (c : R) :
    aeval f (CMvPolynomial.C (n := n) c) = algebraMap R σ c

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.aeval_add
items.statement:
lemma aeval_add {n : ℕ} {R σ : Type*}
    [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    [CommSemiring σ] [Algebra R σ]
    (f : Fin n → σ) (p q : CMvPolynomial n R) :
    aeval f (p + q) = aeval f p + aeval f q

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.aeval_mul
items.statement:
lemma aeval_mul {n : ℕ} {R σ : Type*}
    [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    [CommSemiring σ] [Algebra R σ]
    (f : Fin n → σ) (p q : CMvPolynomial n R) :
    aeval f (p * q) = aeval f p * aeval f q

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.aeval_zero
items.statement:
lemma aeval_zero {n : ℕ} {R σ : Type*}
    [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    [CommSemiring σ] [Algebra R σ]
    (f : Fin n → σ) :
    aeval f (0 : CMvPolynomial n R) = 0

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.aeval_one
items.statement:
lemma aeval_one {n : ℕ} {R σ : Type*}
    [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    [CommSemiring σ] [Algebra R σ]
    (f : Fin n → σ) :
    aeval f (1 : CMvPolynomial n R) = 1

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.aeval_pow
items.statement:
lemma aeval_pow {n : ℕ} {R σ : Type*}
    [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    [CommSemiring σ] [Algebra R σ]
    (f : Fin n → σ) (p : CMvPolynomial n R) (k : ℕ) :
    aeval f (p ^ k) = (aeval f p) ^ k

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.aeval_neg
items.statement:
lemma aeval_neg {n : ℕ} {R σ : Type*}
    [CommRing R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    [CommRing σ] [Algebra R σ]
    (f : Fin n → σ) (p : CMvPolynomial n R) :
    aeval f (-p) = -(aeval f p)

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.aeval_sub
items.statement:
lemma aeval_sub {n : ℕ} {R σ : Type*}
    [CommRing R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    [CommRing σ] [Algebra R σ]
    (f : Fin n → σ) (p q : CMvPolynomial n R) :
    aeval f (p - q) = aeval f p - aeval f q

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.bind₁
items.doc:
Substitution: substitutes polynomials for variables.

Given `f : Fin n → CMvPolynomial m R`, substitutes `f i` for variable `X i`.
items.statement:
def bind₁ {n m : ℕ} {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (f : Fin n → CMvPolynomial m R) (p : CMvPolynomial n R) : CMvPolynomial m R

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.bind₁_eq_aeval
items.doc: The computable substitution `bind₁` agrees with algebraic evaluation.
items.statement:
lemma bind₁_eq_aeval {n m : ℕ} {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (f : Fin n → CMvPolynomial m R) (p : CMvPolynomial n R) :
    bind₁ f p = aeval (σ := CMvPolynomial m R) f p

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.bind₁_C
items.statement:
lemma bind₁_C {n m : ℕ} {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (f : Fin n → CMvPolynomial m R) (c : R) :
    bind₁ f (CMvPolynomial.C (n := n) c) = CMvPolynomial.C (n := m) c

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.bind₁_add
items.statement:
lemma bind₁_add {n m : ℕ} {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (f : Fin n → CMvPolynomial m R) (p q : CMvPolynomial n R) :
    bind₁ f (p + q) = bind₁ f p + bind₁ f q

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.bind₁_mul
items.statement:
lemma bind₁_mul {n m : ℕ} {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (f : Fin n → CMvPolynomial m R) (p q : CMvPolynomial n R) :
    bind₁ f (p * q) = bind₁ f p * bind₁ f q

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.rename
items.doc:
Rename variables using a function.

Given `f : Fin n → Fin m`, renames variable `X i` to `X (f i)`.
items.statement:
def rename {n m : ℕ} {R : Type*} [Zero R] [Add R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (f : Fin n → Fin m) (p : CMvPolynomial n R) : CMvPolynomial m R

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.sumToIter
items.doc: Iterative reconstruction of a polynomial by folding over terms.
items.statement:
def sumToIter {n : ℕ} {R : Type*} [Zero R] [Add R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (p : CMvPolynomial n R) : CMvPolynomial n R

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.X_eq_monomial
items.statement:
lemma X_eq_monomial {k : ℕ} {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (i : Fin k) :
    CMvPolynomial.X (R := R) i = CMvPolynomial.monomial
      (Vector.ofFn (fun j => if j = i then 1 else 0))
      (1 : R)

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.toFinsupp_unitMono
CPoly.CMvPolynomial.fromCMvPolynomial_monomial
items.statement:

    fromCMvPolynomial (CMvPolynomial.monomial mono c) =
