    (i : Fin k) :
    fromCMvPolynomial (CMvPolynomial.X (R := R) i) =
    MvPolynomial.X i

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.eval₂_C
items.statement:
theorem eval₂_C {n : ℕ} {R S : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    [CommSemiring S] (f : R →+* S) (vs : Fin n → S) (c : R) :
    CMvPolynomial.eval₂ f vs (CMvPolynomial.C c) = f c

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.eval₂_X
items.statement:
theorem eval₂_X {n : ℕ} {R S : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    [CommSemiring S] (f : R →+* S) (vs : Fin n → S) (i : Fin n) :
    CMvPolynomial.eval₂ f vs (CMvPolynomial.X i) = vs i

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.eval₂Hom_C
items.statement:
theorem eval₂Hom_C {n : ℕ} {R S : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    [CommSemiring S] (f : R →+* S) (vs : Fin n → S) (c : R) :
    CMvPolynomial.eval₂Hom f vs (CMvPolynomial.C c) = f c

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.eval₂Hom_X
items.statement:
theorem eval₂Hom_X {n : ℕ} {R S : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    [CommSemiring S] (f : R →+* S) (vs : Fin n → S) (i : Fin n) :
    CMvPolynomial.eval₂Hom f vs (CMvPolynomial.X i) = vs i

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.ringHom_ext
items.doc:
Two ring homomorphisms out of `CMvPolynomial n R` are equal once they agree on the constants
and on every variable.
items.statement:
theorem ringHom_ext {n : ℕ} {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    {T : Type*} [Semiring T] {f g : CMvPolynomial n R →+* T}
    (hC : ∀ c, f (CMvPolynomial.C c) = g (CMvPolynomial.C c))
    (hX : ∀ i, f (CMvPolynomial.X i) = g (CMvPolynomial.X i)) : f = g

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.aeval_X
items.statement:
lemma aeval_X {n : ℕ} {R σ : Type*}
    [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    [CommSemiring σ] [Algebra R σ]
    (f : Fin n → σ) (i : Fin n) :
    aeval f (CMvPolynomial.X (R := R) i) = f i

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.bind₁_X
items.statement:
lemma bind₁_X {n m : ℕ} {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (f : Fin n → CMvPolynomial m R) (i : Fin n) :
    bind₁ f (CMvPolynomial.X (R := R) i) = f i

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.bind₁_id
items.statement:
lemma bind₁_id {n : ℕ} {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (p : CMvPolynomial n R) :
    bind₁ (fun i => CMvPolynomial.X (R := R) i) p = p

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.list_foldl_add_comm
items.statement:
lemma list_foldl_add_comm {β K V : Type*} [AddCommMonoid β]
    (g : K → V → β) (l : List (K × V)) (init : β) :
    List.foldl (fun acc pair => acc + g pair.1 pair.2) init l =
    List.foldl (fun acc pair => g pair.1 pair.2 + acc) init l

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.foldl_add_comm
items.statement:
lemma foldl_add_comm {β : Type*} [AddCommMonoid β] {k : ℕ}
    {R' : Type*} (g : CMvMonomial k → R' → β)
    (t : Std.ExtTreeMap (CMvMonomial k) R') :
    Std.ExtTreeMap.foldl (fun acc m c => acc + g m c) (0 : β) t =
    Std.ExtTreeMap.foldl (fun acc m c => g m c + acc) (0 : β) t

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.fromCMvPolynomial_finsupp_sum
items.statement:
lemma fromCMvPolynomial_finsupp_sum {n k : ℕ} [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (g : (Fin n →₀ ℕ) → R → CMvPolynomial k R)
    (a : CMvPolynomial n R) :
    fromCMvPolynomial (Finsupp.sum (AddMonoidAlgebra.coeff (fromCMvPolynomial a)) g) =
    Finsupp.sum (AddMonoidAlgebra.coeff (fromCMvPolynomial a))
      (fun μ c => fromCMvPolynomial (g μ c))

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.sumToIter_eq
items.statement:
lemma sumToIter_eq {n : ℕ} {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (p : CMvPolynomial n R) : sumToIter p = p

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.coeff_sumToIter
items.statement:
lemma coeff_sumToIter {n : ℕ} {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (m : CMvMonomial n) (p : CMvPolynomial n R) :
    coeff m (sumToIter p) = coeff m p

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.sumToIter_zero
items.statement:
lemma sumToIter_zero {n : ℕ} {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] :
    sumToIter (0 : CMvPolynomial n R) = 0

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.sumToIter_add
items.statement:
lemma sumToIter_add {n : ℕ} {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (p q : CMvPolynomial n R) :
    sumToIter (p + q) = sumToIter p + sumToIter q

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.sumToIter_idempotent
items.statement:
lemma sumToIter_idempotent {n : ℕ} {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (p : CMvPolynomial n R) :
    sumToIter (sumToIter p) = sumToIter p

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.fromCMvPolynomial_bind₁
items.doc:
The computable substitution `bind₁` agrees with Mathlib substitution after
transporting through `fromCMvPolynomial`.
items.statement:
theorem fromCMvPolynomial_bind₁ {n m : ℕ} {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [BEq R]
    [LawfulBEq R] (f : Fin n → CMvPolynomial m R) (p : CMvPolynomial n R) :
    fromCMvPolynomial (bind₁ f p) =
      MvPolynomial.eval₂ MvPolynomial.C (fun i => fromCMvPolynomial (f i))
        (fromCMvPolynomial p)

items.note:
### Equivalence between `npow` and `npowBySq`

`Lawful.npow` (defined in `Multivariate/Lawful.lean`) is the naive `O(k)`
specification; `Lawful.npowBySq` is the `O(log k)` repeated-squaring
implementation. We prove pointwise equality here so that the `NatPow` instance
can be safely routed through the fast version.

The proofs need `mul_assoc` / `mul_one` / `mul_comm`, which are only available
once the `CommSemiring (CMvPolynomial n R)` instance has been built — that is
why these lemmas live in `Operations.lean` rather than in `Lawful.lean`.

items.name: CPoly.Lawful.npow_add
items.doc: Additive law for the naive `npow`: $p^{a+b} = p^a \cdot p^b$.
items.statement:
lemma npow_add (p : Lawful n R) (a b : ℕ) :
    npow (a + b) p = npow a p * npow b p

items.name: CPoly.Lawful.npowBySq_eq_npow
items.doc:
The fast repeated-squaring `npowBySq` agrees pointwise with the naive
`npow`. This is the equivalence that lets the `NatPow (Lawful n R)` instance
be routed through `npowBySq` without changing observable behavior.
items.statement: theorem npowBySq_eq_npow (p : Lawful n R) : ∀ k : ℕ, npowBySq p k = npow k p

modules.title: Partial evaluation of the first variable of a `CMvPolynomial`
modules.doc:
`partialEvalFirst a p` fixes variable `0` of a multivariate computable
polynomial to a scalar value, together with its evaluation lemma and the
per-variable degree-bound lemma.

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.partialEvalFirst
items.doc: Fix variable 0 of a multivariate polynomial to a scalar value `a`.
items.statement: def partialEvalFirst (a : R) (p : CMvPolynomial (n + 1) R) : CMvPolynomial n R

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.partialEvalFirst_eval
items.doc: `partialEvalFirst a p` correctly implements partial evaluation.
items.statement:
theorem partialEvalFirst_eval (a : R) (p : CMvPolynomial (n + 1) R) (v : Fin n → R) :
    (partialEvalFirst a p).eval v = p.eval (Fin.cons a v)

items.name: CPoly.CMvPolynomial.partialEvalFirst_degreeOf_le
items.doc: `partialEvalFirst` preserves degree bounds for each remaining variable.
items.statement:
theorem partialEvalFirst_degreeOf_le [Nontrivial R] {deg : ℕ} (a : R)
    (i : Fin n) (p : CMvPolynomial (n + 1) R)
    (hDeg : ∀ mono ∈ Lawful.monomials p, mono.degreeOf i.succ ≤ deg) :
    ∀ mono ∈ Lawful.monomials (partialEvalFirst a p), mono.degreeOf i ≤ deg

modules.title: Properties of variable renaming for `CMvPolynomial`
modules.doc:
This file proves properties of the `rename` function defined in `CMvPolynomial.lean`,
by transferring results from Mathlib's `MvPolynomial.rename` through the
`polyRingEquiv : CMvPolynomial n R ≃+* MvPolynomial (Fin n) R` equivalence.

## Main results

* `fromCMvPolynomial_rename` — correspondence between `CMvPolynomial.rename` and
  `MvPolynomial.rename`
* `rename_C`, `rename_X`, `rename_add`, `rename_mul`, `rename_id`, `rename_rename`
  — algebraic properties
* `CMvPolynomial.renameEquiv` — ring isomorphism for bijective variable renaming

items.name: CPoly.list_foldl_add_comm
items.doc:
In a commutative additive monoid, the order of addition in a list fold
does not matter.
items.statement:
lemma list_foldl_add_comm {β K V : Type*} [AddCommMonoid β]
    (g : K → V → β) (l : List (K × V)) (init : β) :
    List.foldl (fun acc pair => acc + g pair.1 pair.2) init l =
    List.foldl (fun acc pair => g pair.1 pair.2 + acc) init l

items.name: CPoly.foldl_add_comm'
items.doc: Swapping addition order in `ExtTreeMap.foldl` does not change the result.
items.statement:
lemma foldl_add_comm' {β : Type*} [AddCommMonoid β] {k : ℕ}
    {R' : Type*} (g : CMvMonomial k → R' → β)
    (t : Std.ExtTreeMap (CMvMonomial k) R') :
    Std.ExtTreeMap.foldl (fun acc m c => acc + g m c) (0 : β) t =
    Std.ExtTreeMap.foldl (fun acc m c => g m c + acc) (0 : β) t

items.name: CPoly.toFinsupp_apply
items.doc: Applying `CMvMonomial.toFinsupp` at index `i` equals `Vector.get`.
items.statement:
lemma toFinsupp_apply (mono : CMvMonomial n) (i : Fin n) :
    (CMvMonomial.toFinsupp mono) i = mono.get i

items.name: CPoly.renameMonomial_eq
items.doc:
Monomial renaming via `Vector.ofFn` corresponds to `Finsupp.mapDomain`
on the `Finsupp` side.
items.statement:
lemma renameMonomial_eq (f : Fin n → Fin m) (mono : CMvMonomial n) :
    (Vector.ofFn (fun j => (Finset.univ.filter (fun i => f i = j)).sum
      (fun i => mono.get i)) : CMvMonomial m) =
    CMvMonomial.ofFinsupp
      (Finsupp.mapDomain f (CMvMonomial.toFinsupp mono))

items.name: CPoly.fromCMvPolynomial_monomial
items.doc:
`fromCMvPolynomial` maps `CMvPolynomial.monomial` to
`MvPolynomial.monomial`.
items.statement:
lemma fromCMvPolynomial_monomial {k : ℕ} (mono : CMvMonomial k) (c : R) :
    fromCMvPolynomial (CMvPolynomial.monomial mono c) =
    MvPolynomial.monomial (CMvMonomial.toFinsupp mono) c

items.name: CPoly.fromCMvPolynomial_finsupp_sum
items.doc: `fromCMvPolynomial` distributes over `Finsupp.sum`.
items.statement:
lemma fromCMvPolynomial_finsupp_sum {k : ℕ}
    (g : (Fin n →₀ ℕ) → R → CMvPolynomial k R)
    (a : CMvPolynomial n R) :
    fromCMvPolynomial (Finsupp.sum (AddMonoidAlgebra.coeff (fromCMvPolynomial a)) g) =
    Finsupp.sum (AddMonoidAlgebra.coeff (fromCMvPolynomial a))
      (fun μ c => fromCMvPolynomial (g μ c))

items.name: CPoly.fromCMvPolynomial_rename
items.doc:
`CMvPolynomial.rename` agrees with `MvPolynomial.rename` under the
`fromCMvPolynomial` equivalence.
items.statement:
lemma fromCMvPolynomial_rename (f : Fin n → Fin m)
    (p : CMvPolynomial n R) :
    fromCMvPolynomial (CMvPolynomial.rename f p) =
    MvPolynomial.rename f (fromCMvPolynomial p)

items.name: CPoly.C_eq_monomial
items.doc: `CMvPolynomial.C c` equals `CMvPolynomial.monomial 0 c`.
items.statement:
lemma C_eq_monomial {k : ℕ} (c : R) :
    CMvPolynomial.C (n := k) c = CMvPolynomial.monomial 0 c

items.name: CPoly.toFinsupp_zero
items.doc: The `Finsupp` of the zero monomial is zero.
items.statement:
lemma toFinsupp_zero {k : ℕ} :
    CMvMonomial.toFinsupp (0 : CMvMonomial k) = 0

items.name: CPoly.fromCMvPolynomial_C
items.doc: `fromCMvPolynomial` maps `CMvPolynomial.C` to `MvPolynomial.C`.
items.statement:
lemma fromCMvPolynomial_C {k : ℕ} (c : R) :
    fromCMvPolynomial (CMvPolynomial.C (n := k) c) =
    MvPolynomial.C c

items.name: CPoly.rename_C
items.doc: Constants are unchanged under renaming.
items.statement:
lemma rename_C (f : Fin n → Fin m) (c : R) :
    CMvPolynomial.rename f (CMvPolynomial.C c) =
    CMvPolynomial.C (n := m) c

items.name: CPoly.X_eq_monomial
items.doc:
`CMvPolynomial.X i` equals `CMvPolynomial.monomial eᵢ 1`
where `eᵢ` is the `i`-th standard basis vector.
items.statement:
lemma X_eq_monomial {k : ℕ} (i : Fin k) :
    CMvPolynomial.X (R := R) i = CMvPolynomial.monomial
      (Vector.ofFn (fun j => if j = i then 1 else 0))
      (1 : R)

items.name: CPoly.toFinsupp_unitMono
items.doc:
The `Finsupp` of the `i`-th standard basis monomial is
`Finsupp.single i 1`.
items.statement:
lemma toFinsupp_unitMono {k : ℕ} (i : Fin k) :
    CMvMonomial.toFinsupp
      (Vector.ofFn (fun j : Fin k =>
        if j = i then 1 else 0)) =
    Finsupp.single i 1

items.name: CPoly.fromCMvPolynomial_X
items.doc:
`fromCMvPolynomial` maps `CMvPolynomial.X i` to
`MvPolynomial.X i`.
items.statement:
lemma fromCMvPolynomial_X {k : ℕ} (i : Fin k) :
    fromCMvPolynomial (CMvPolynomial.X (R := R) i) =
    MvPolynomial.X i

items.name: CPoly.rename_X
items.doc: Renaming maps variable `X i` to `X (f i)`.
items.statement:
lemma rename_X (f : Fin n → Fin m) (i : Fin n) :
    CMvPolynomial.rename f (CMvPolynomial.X (R := R) i) =
    CMvPolynomial.X (f i)

items.name: CPoly.rename_add
items.doc: Renaming preserves addition.
items.statement:
lemma rename_add (f : Fin n → Fin m)
    (p q : CMvPolynomial n R) :
    CMvPolynomial.rename f (p + q) =
    CMvPolynomial.rename f p +
    CMvPolynomial.rename f q

items.name: CPoly.rename_mul
items.doc: Renaming preserves multiplication.
items.statement:
lemma rename_mul (f : Fin n → Fin m)
    (p q : CMvPolynomial n R) :
    CMvPolynomial.rename f (p * q) =
    CMvPolynomial.rename f p *
    CMvPolynomial.rename f q

items.name: CPoly.rename_id
items.doc: Renaming by the identity function is the identity.
items.statement:
lemma rename_id (p : CMvPolynomial n R) :
    CMvPolynomial.rename id p = p

items.name: CPoly.rename_rename
items.doc: Composing two renamings equals renaming by the composition.
items.statement:
lemma rename_rename {k : ℕ} (f : Fin n → Fin m)
    (g : Fin m → Fin k) (p : CMvPolynomial n R) :
    CMvPolynomial.rename g (CMvPolynomial.rename f p) =
    CMvPolynomial.rename (g ∘ f) p

items.name: CMvPolynomial.renameEquiv
items.doc:
Ring equivalence for variable renaming when the function is
a bijection.
items.statement:
noncomputable def renameEquiv
    (f : Fin n ≃ Fin m) :
    CMvPolynomial n R ≃+* CMvPolynomial m R

modules.title: Lemmas for `CMvPolynomial.restrictBy`, `restrictTotalDegreeOf`, and `restrictDegreeOf`
modules.doc:
Degree-bounded restriction of multivariate polynomials: filtering monomials by total degree
or per-variable degree bounds.

Also proves correctness against Mathlib: transporting these restrictions across
`fromCMvPolynomial` lands in Mathlib's degree-bounded submodules.

items.name: CPoly.coeff_restrictBy
items.doc: Coefficient of `restrictBy keep p` at `m`: `p.coeff m` if `keep m`, else `0`.
items.statement:
lemma coeff_restrictBy (keep : CMvMonomial n → Prop) [DecidablePred keep]
    (m : CMvMonomial n) (p : CMvPolynomial n R) :
    (CMvPolynomial.restrictBy keep p).coeff m = if keep m then p.coeff m else 0

items.name: CPoly.coeff_restrictTotalDegreeOf
items.doc: Coeff at `m`: `p.coeff m` if `m.totalDegree ≤ d`, else `0`.
items.statement:
lemma coeff_restrictTotalDegreeOf (d : ℕ) (m : CMvMonomial n) (p : CMvPolynomial n R) :
    (restrictTotalDegreeOf d p).coeff m =
      if m.totalDegree ≤ d then p.coeff m else 0

items.name: CPoly.coeff_restrictDegreeOf
items.doc:
Coefficient of `restrictDegreeOf d p` at `m`: `p.coeff m` if `∀ i, m.degreeOf i ≤ d`,
else `0`.
items.statement:
lemma coeff_restrictDegreeOf (d : ℕ) (m : CMvMonomial n) (p : CMvPolynomial n R) :
    (restrictDegreeOf d p).coeff m =
      if ∀ i : Fin n, m.degreeOf i ≤ d then p.coeff m else 0

items.name: CPoly.coeff_restrictTotalDegreeOf_eq_self_of_le
items.doc: When `m.totalDegree ≤ d`, coeff at `m` is unchanged by `restrictTotalDegreeOf d`.

items.name: CPoly.coeff_restrictTotalDegreeOf_eq_zero_of_lt
items.doc: When `d < m.totalDegree`, coeff at `m` is `0` in `restrictTotalDegreeOf d p`.

items.name: CPoly.coeff_restrictDegreeOf_eq_self_of_le
items.doc: When `∀ i, m.degreeOf i ≤ d`, coeff at `m` is unchanged by `restrictDegreeOf d`.

items.name: CPoly.coeff_restrictDegreeOf_eq_zero_of_not_le
items.doc: When `¬(∀ i, m.degreeOf i ≤ d)`, coeff at `m` is `0` in `restrictDegreeOf d p`.

items.name: CPoly.totalDegree_le_of_mem_monomials_restrictTotalDegreeOf
items.doc: Monomials in `restrictTotalDegreeOf d p` have `totalDegree ≤ d`.

items.name: CPoly.degreeOf_le_of_mem_monomials_restrictDegreeOf
items.doc: Monomials in `restrictDegreeOf d p` have `degreeOf i ≤ d` for each variable `i`.

items.name: CPoly.totalDegree_restrictTotalDegreeOf_le
items.doc: `restrictTotalDegreeOf d p` has `totalDegree ≤ d`.
items.statement:
lemma totalDegree_restrictTotalDegreeOf_le
    {R' : Type*} [CommSemiring R'] [BEq R'] [LawfulBEq R']
    (d : ℕ) (p : CMvPolynomial n R') :
    (restrictTotalDegreeOf d p).totalDegree ≤ d

items.name: CPoly.degreeOf_restrictDegreeOf_le
items.doc: `restrictDegreeOf d p` has `degreeOf i ≤ d` for each variable `i`.
items.statement:
lemma degreeOf_restrictDegreeOf_le (d : ℕ) (p : CMvPolynomial n R) (i : Fin n) :
    (restrictDegreeOf d p).degreeOf i ≤ d

items.name: CPoly.restrictTotalDegreeOf_zero
items.doc: `restrictTotalDegreeOf d 0 = 0`.
items.statement:
lemma restrictTotalDegreeOf_zero (d : ℕ) :
    restrictTotalDegreeOf d (0 : CMvPolynomial n R) = 0

items.name: CPoly.restrictDegreeOf_zero
items.doc: `restrictDegreeOf d 0 = 0`.
items.statement:
lemma restrictDegreeOf_zero (d : ℕ) :
    restrictDegreeOf d (0 : CMvPolynomial n R) = 0

items.name: CPoly.restrictTotalDegreeOf_restrictTotalDegreeOf
items.doc: Double `restrictTotalDegreeOf` equals `restrictTotalDegreeOf (min d d')`.
items.statement:
lemma restrictTotalDegreeOf_restrictTotalDegreeOf (d d' : ℕ) (p : CMvPolynomial n R) :
    restrictTotalDegreeOf d (restrictTotalDegreeOf d' p) =
      restrictTotalDegreeOf (min d d') p

items.name: CPoly.restrictDegreeOf_restrictDegreeOf
items.doc: Double `restrictDegreeOf` equals `restrictDegreeOf (min d d')`.
items.statement:
lemma restrictDegreeOf_restrictDegreeOf (d d' : ℕ) (p : CMvPolynomial n R) :
    restrictDegreeOf d (restrictDegreeOf d' p) =
      restrictDegreeOf (min d d') p

items.name: CPoly.restrictTotalDegreeOf_restrictDegreeOf_comm
items.doc: `restrictTotalDegreeOf d` and `restrictDegreeOf d'` commute.
items.statement:
lemma restrictTotalDegreeOf_restrictDegreeOf_comm (d d' : ℕ) (p : CMvPolynomial n R) :
    restrictTotalDegreeOf d (CMvPolynomial.restrictDegreeOf d' p) =
      restrictDegreeOf d' (restrictTotalDegreeOf d p)

items.name: CPoly.fromCMvPolynomial_restrictTotalDegreeOf_mem
items.doc:
`fromCMvPolynomial (restrictTotalDegreeOf d p) ∈
MvPolynomial.restrictTotalDegree (Fin n) R d`.
items.statement:
theorem fromCMvPolynomial_restrictTotalDegreeOf_mem {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [BEq R]
    [LawfulBEq R] (d : ℕ) (p : CMvPolynomial n R) :
    fromCMvPolynomial (restrictTotalDegreeOf d p) ∈
      MvPolynomial.restrictTotalDegree (Fin n) R d

items.name: CPoly.fromCMvPolynomial_restrictDegreeOf_mem
items.doc: `fromCMvPolynomial (restrictDegreeOf d p) ∈ MvPolynomial.restrictDegree (Fin n) R d`.
items.statement:
theorem fromCMvPolynomial_restrictDegreeOf_mem {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [BEq R]
    [LawfulBEq R] (d : ℕ) (p : CMvPolynomial n R) :
    fromCMvPolynomial (restrictDegreeOf d p) ∈
      MvPolynomial.restrictDegree (Fin n) R d

items.name: CPoly.restrictDegree
items.doc:
The `Submodule` of polynomials all of whose support monomials have every variable's
exponent at most `degree`.
items.statement:
def restrictDegree (R : Type v) [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (n degree : ℕ) :
    Submodule R (CMvPolynomial n R)

items.name: CPoly.restrictDegree_elem
items.doc:
`p ∈ restrictDegree R n degree` iff every variable's exponent in every support
monomial of `p` is at most `degree`.
items.statement:
lemma restrictDegree_elem {R : Type v} [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] {n degree : ℕ} :
    ∀ p, p ∈ restrictDegree R n degree ↔ ∀ σ ∈ p.support, ∀ i, σ i ≤ degree

modules.authors: Frantisek Silvasi, Julian Sutherland, Andrei Burdusa
modules.title: Unlawful multivariate polynomials
modules.doc:
This file defines the `Unlawful` type, which represents multivariate polynomials
as a map from monomials to coefficients. Unlike `Lawful`, it does not enforce
the absence of zero coefficients.

## Main definitions

* `CPoly.Unlawful n R`: A map from `CMvMonomial n` to `R`, implemented using `Std.ExtTreeMap`.

items.name: CPoly.Unlawful
items.doc:
Polynomial in `n` variables with coefficients in `R`.
Internally represented as a tree map from monomials to coefficients.
items.statement: abbrev Unlawful (n : ℕ) (R : Type*) : Type _

items.name: CPoly.Unlawful.ext_getElem?
items.statement:
lemma ext_getElem? {n R} {t₁ t₂ : Unlawful n R}
    (h : ∀ (k : CMvMonomial n), t₁[k]? = t₂[k]?) : t₁ = t₂

items.name: CPoly.Unlawful.ofList
items.doc: Construct an `Unlawful` polynomial from a list of monomial-coefficient pairs.
items.statement: def ofList (l : List (CMvMonomial n × R)) : Unlawful n R

items.name: CPoly.Unlawful.extend
items.doc: Extend the number of variables by padding monomials with zeros.
items.statement: def extend (n' : ℕ) (p : Unlawful n R) : Unlawful (n ⊔ n') R

items.name: CPoly.Unlawful.isNoZeroCoef
items.doc: Check if the polynomial has no zero coefficients.
items.statement: abbrev isNoZeroCoef [Zero R] (p : Unlawful n R) : Prop

items.name: CPoly.Unlawful.toFinset
items.statement: def toFinset [DecidableEq R] (p : Unlawful n R) : Finset (CMvMonomial n × R)

items.name: CPoly.Unlawful.monomials
items.doc: The list of monomials present in the polynomial.
items.statement: abbrev monomials (p : Unlawful n R) : List (CMvMonomial n)

items.name: CPoly.Unlawful.mem_monomials
items.statement:
lemma mem_monomials {m : CMvMonomial n} {up : Unlawful n R} :
    m ∈ up.monomials ↔ m ∈ up

items.name: CPoly.Unlawful.C
items.doc: Constant polynomial.
items.statement: def C [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Zero R] (c : R) : Unlawful n R

items.name: CPoly.Unlawful.C_zero
items.statement: lemma C_zero : C (n := n) (0 : R) = 0

items.name: CPoly.Unlawful.C_zero'
items.statement: lemma C_zero' : C (n := n) (0 : ℕ) = 0

items.name: CPoly.Unlawful.zero_eq_zero
items.statement: lemma zero_eq_zero : (Zero.zero : R) = 0

items.name: CPoly.Unlawful.zero_eq_empty
items.statement: lemma zero_eq_empty [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] : (0 : Unlawful n R) = ∅

items.name: CPoly.Unlawful.not_mem_C_zero
items.statement: lemma not_mem_C_zero : x ∉ C 0

items.name: CPoly.Unlawful.not_mem_zero
items.statement: lemma not_mem_zero : x ∉ (0 : Unlawful n R)

items.name: CPoly.Unlawful.isNoZeroCoef_zero
items.statement: lemma isNoZeroCoef_zero : isNoZeroCoef (n := n) (R := R) 0

items.name: CPoly.Unlawful.add
items.doc: Pointwise addition of coefficients.
items.statement: def add [Add R] (p₁ p₂ : Unlawful n R) : Unlawful n R

items.name: CPoly.Unlawful.grind_add_skip
items.statement:
protected lemma grind_add_skip [Add R] {p₁ p₂ : Unlawful n R} :
    p₁ + p₂ = p₁.mergeWith (fun _ c₁ c₂ ↦ c₁ + c₂) p₂

items.name: CPoly.Unlawful.addMonoR
items.doc: Add a single monomial-coefficient term to a polynomial.
items.statement: def addMonoR [Add R] (p : Unlawful n R) (term : MonoR n R) : Unlawful n R

items.name: CPoly.Unlawful.mul₀
items.doc: Multiply a polynomial by a single monomial term.
items.statement: def mul₀ [Mul R] (t : MonoR n R) (p : Unlawful n R) : Unlawful n R

items.name: CPoly.Unlawful.mul₀_zero
items.statement: lemma mul₀_zero [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Mul R] {t : MonoR n R} : mul₀ t 0 = 0

items.name: CPoly.Unlawful.mul
items.doc: Polynomial multiplication using a nested fold (distributive law).
items.statement: def mul [Mul R] [Add R] [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (p₁ p₂ : Unlawful n R) : Unlawful n R

items.name: CPoly.Unlawful.neg
items.doc: Negation (negates all coefficients).
items.statement: def neg (p : Unlawful n R) : Unlawful n R

items.name: CPoly.Unlawful.sub
items.doc: Subtraction.
items.statement: def sub [Add R] (p₁ p₂ : Unlawful n R) : Unlawful n R

items.name: CPoly.Unlawful.leadingTerm?
items.doc: Return the term with the lexicographically largest monomial.
items.statement: def leadingTerm? : Unlawful n R → Option (MonoR n R)

items.name: CPoly.Unlawful.leadingMonomial?
items.doc: Return the lexicographically largest monomial.
items.statement: def leadingMonomial? : Unlawful n R → Option (CMvMonomial n)

items.name: CPoly.Unlawful.instDecidableEq
items.statement: instance instDecidableEq [DecidableEq R] : DecidableEq (Unlawful n R)

items.name: CPoly.Unlawful.coeff
items.statement: def coeff {R : Type*} {n : ℕ} [Zero R] (m : CMvMonomial n) (p : Unlawful n R) : R

items.name: CPoly.Unlawful.filter_get
items.statement:
lemma filter_get {R : Type*} [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] {v : R} {m : CMvMonomial n} (a : Unlawful n R) :
    (ExtTreeMap.filter (fun _ c => c != v) a)[m]?.getD v = a[m]?.getD v

items.name: CPoly.Unlawful.add_getD?
items.statement:
lemma add_getD? [AddZeroClass R] {m : CMvMonomial n} {p q : Unlawful n R} :
    (p.add q)[m]?.getD 0 = p[m]?.getD 0 + q[m]?.getD 0

items.doc: `removeNth` for maps `Fin n →₀ M`. See `Fin.removeNth` for more details.

items.name: Finsupp.snoc_init_self

items.statement:
theorem snoc_support :
    (s.snoc y).support ⊆ insert (Fin.last n) (s.support.map Fin.castSuccEmb)

items.name: Finsupp.snoc_left_injective
items.statement: theorem snoc_left_injective : Injective (Finsupp.snoc · y : (Fin n →₀ M) → Fin (n + 1) →₀ M)

items.statement:
theorem insertNth_support :
    (insertNth p y s).support ⊆ insert p (s.support.map (Fin.succAboveEmb p))

items.name: Finsupp.insertNth_right_injective
items.statement:
theorem insertNth_right_injective :
    Injective (Finsupp.insertNth p y : (Fin n →₀ M) → Fin (n + 1) →₀ M)

items.name: Finsupp.sum_insertNth
items.statement:
lemma sum_insertNth [AddCommMonoid M] {n : ℕ} (σ : Fin n →₀ M) (i : M) (p : Fin (n + 1)) :
    (insertNth p i σ).sum (fun _ e ↦ e) = i + σ.sum (fun _ e ↦ e)

items.name: Finsupp.sum_insertNth'
items.statement:
lemma sum_insertNth' [AddCommMonoid M] [AddCommMonoid N] {n : ℕ} (σ : Fin n →₀ M) (i : M)
    (p : Fin (n + 1)) (f : Fin (n+1) → M → N) (h : ∀ x, f x 0 = 0) :
    sum (insertNth p i σ) f = f p i + sum σ (Fin.removeNth p f)

modules.title: MvPolynomial Equiv
modules.doc: Equivalences for multivariable polynomials, including `finSuccEquivNth`.

items.name: MvPolynomial.finSuccEquivNth
items.doc:
The algebra isomorphism between multivariable polynomials in `Fin (n + 1)` and polynomials over
multivariable polynomials in `Fin n`, where the `p`-th (pivot) variable is the indeterminate `X`.

`finSuccEquiv` is the special case when `p = 0`.
items.statement: def finSuccEquivNth : MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) R ≃ₐ[R] Polynomial (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R)

items.name: MvPolynomial.finSuccEquivNth_eq
items.statement:
theorem finSuccEquivNth_eq :
    (finSuccEquivNth R p : MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) R →+* Polynomial (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R)) =
      eval₂Hom (Polynomial.C.comp (C : R →+* MvPolynomial (Fin n) R))
        (Fin.insertNth p Polynomial.X (Polynomial.C ∘ X))

items.name: MvPolynomial.finSuccEquivNth_apply
items.statement:
theorem finSuccEquivNth_apply (f : MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) R) :
    finSuccEquivNth R p f =
      eval₂Hom (Polynomial.C.comp (C : R →+* MvPolynomial (Fin n) R))
        (Fin.insertNth p Polynomial.X (Polynomial.C ∘ X)) f

items.name: MvPolynomial.finSuccEquivNth_comp_C_eq_C
items.statement:
theorem finSuccEquivNth_comp_C_eq_C :
    (↑(finSuccEquivNth R p).symm : Polynomial (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R) →+* _).comp
        (Polynomial.C.comp C) = (C : R →+* MvPolynomial (Fin n.succ) R)

items.name: MvPolynomial.finSuccEquivNth_X_same
items.statement: theorem finSuccEquivNth_X_same : finSuccEquivNth R p (X p) = Polynomial.X

items.name: MvPolynomial.finSuccEquivNth_X_above
items.statement:
theorem finSuccEquivNth_X_above {i : Fin n} (h : p < i.succ) :
    finSuccEquivNth R p (X i.succ) = Polynomial.C (X i)

items.name: MvPolynomial.finSuccEquivNth_X_below
items.statement:
theorem finSuccEquivNth_X_below {i : Fin n} (h : i.castSucc < p) :
    finSuccEquivNth R p (X i.castSucc) = Polynomial.C (X i)

items.name: MvPolynomial.finSuccEquivNth_coeff_coeff
items.doc:
The coefficient of `m` in the `i`-th coefficient of `finSuccEquivNth R p f` equals the
coefficient of `m.insertNth p i` in `f`.
items.statement:
theorem finSuccEquivNth_coeff_coeff (m : Fin n →₀ ℕ) (f : MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) R) (i : ℕ) :
    ((finSuccEquivNth R p f).coeff i).coeff m = f.coeff (m.insertNth p i)

items.name: MvPolynomial.eval_eq_eval_mv_eval_finSuccEquivNth
items.doc:
The evaluation of `f` at `Fin.insertNth p y s` equals the evaluation at `y` of the polynomial
obtained by partially evaluating `finSuccEquivNth R p f` at `s`.
items.statement:
theorem eval_eq_eval_mv_eval_finSuccEquivNth (s : Fin n → R) (y : R)
    (f : MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) R) :
      eval (Fin.insertNth p y s : Fin (n + 1) → R) f =
        Polynomial.eval y (Polynomial.map (eval s) (finSuccEquivNth R p f))

items.name: MvPolynomial.support_coeff_finSuccEquivNth
items.doc:
A monomial index `m` is in the support of the `i`-th coefficient of `finSuccEquivNth R p f` if
and only if `m.insertNth p i` is in the support of `f`.
items.statement:
theorem support_coeff_finSuccEquivNth {f : MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) R} {i : ℕ} {m : Fin n →₀ ℕ} :
    m ∈ ((finSuccEquivNth R p f).coeff i).support ↔ m.insertNth p i ∈ f.support

items.name: MvPolynomial.totalDegree_coeff_finSuccEquivNth_add_le
items.doc:
The `totalDegree` of a multivariable polynomial `f` is at least `i` more than the `totalDegree` of
the `i`th coefficient of `finSuccEquivNth R p` applied to `f`, if this is nonzero.
items.statement:
theorem totalDegree_coeff_finSuccEquivNth_add_le (f : MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) R) (i : ℕ)
    (hi : (finSuccEquivNth R p f).coeff i ≠ 0) :
      totalDegree ((finSuccEquivNth R p f).coeff i) + i ≤ totalDegree f

items.name: MvPolynomial.support_finSuccEquivNth
items.doc:
The support of `finSuccEquivNth R p f` equals the support of `f` projected onto the `p`-th
variable.
items.statement:
theorem support_finSuccEquivNth (f : MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) R) :
    (finSuccEquivNth R p f).support = Finset.image (fun m : Fin (n + 1) →₀ ℕ => m p) f.support

items.name: MvPolynomial.mem_support_finSuccEquivNth
items.statement:
theorem mem_support_finSuccEquivNth {f : MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) R} {x} :
    x ∈ (finSuccEquivNth R p f).support ↔ x ∈ (fun m : Fin (n + 1) →₀ _ ↦ m p) '' f.support

items.name: MvPolynomial.image_support_finSuccEquivNth
items.statement:
theorem image_support_finSuccEquivNth {f : MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) R} {i : ℕ} :
    Finset.image (Finsupp.insertNth p i) ((finSuccEquivNth R p f).coeff i).support =
      f.support.filter fun m => m p = i

items.name: MvPolynomial.mem_image_support_coeff_finSuccEquivNth
items.statement:
lemma mem_image_support_coeff_finSuccEquivNth {f : MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) R} {i : ℕ} {x} :
    x ∈ Finsupp.insertNth p i '' ((finSuccEquivNth R p f).coeff i).support ↔
      x ∈ f.support ∧ x p = i

items.name: MvPolynomial.mem_support_coeff_finSuccEquivNth
items.statement:
lemma mem_support_coeff_finSuccEquivNth {f : MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) R} {i : ℕ} {x} :
    x ∈ ((finSuccEquivNth R p f).coeff i).support ↔ x.insertNth p i ∈ f.support

items.name: MvPolynomial.support_finSuccEquivNth_nonempty
items.statement:
theorem support_finSuccEquivNth_nonempty {f : MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) R} (h : f ≠ 0) :
    (finSuccEquivNth R p f).support.Nonempty

items.name: MvPolynomial.degree_finSuccEquivNth
items.doc: The degree of `finSuccEquivNth R p f` equals the `p`-th degree of `f`.
items.statement:
theorem degree_finSuccEquivNth {f : MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) R} (h : f ≠ 0) :
    (finSuccEquivNth R p f).degree = degreeOf p f

items.name: MvPolynomial.natDegree_finSuccEquivNth
items.doc: The `natDegree` of `finSuccEquivNth R p f` equals the `p`-th `natDegree` of `f`.
items.statement:
theorem natDegree_finSuccEquivNth (f : MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) R) :
    (finSuccEquivNth R p f).natDegree = degreeOf p f

items.name: MvPolynomial.degreeOf_coeff_finSuccEquivNth
items.doc:
The degree of `j` in the `i`th coefficient of `finSuccEquivNth R p f` is at most the degree of
`j.succ` in `f`.
items.statement:
theorem degreeOf_coeff_finSuccEquivNth (f : MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) R) (j : Fin n) (i : ℕ) :
    degreeOf j ((finSuccEquivNth R p f).coeff i) ≤ degreeOf (p.succAbove j) f

items.name: MvPolynomial.finSuccEquivNth_rename_finSuccEquivNth
items.doc:
Consider a multivariate polynomial `φ` whose variables are indexed by `Option σ`,
and suppose that `σ ≃ Fin n`.
Then one may view `φ` as a polynomial over `MvPolynomial (Fin n) R`, by

1. renaming the variables via `Option σ ≃ Fin (n+1)`, and then singling out the `p`-th variable
    via `MvPolynomial.finSuccEquivNth R p`;
2. first viewing it as polynomial over `MvPolynomial σ R` via `MvPolynomial.optionEquivLeft`,
    and then renaming the variables.

This theorem shows that both constructions are the same.
items.statement:
theorem finSuccEquivNth_rename_finSuccEquivNth (e : σ ≃ Fin n) (φ : MvPolynomial (Option σ) R) :
    ((finSuccEquivNth R p) ((rename ((Equiv.optionCongr e).trans (_root_.finSuccEquiv' p).symm)) φ))
      = Polynomial.map (rename e).toRingHom (optionEquivLeft R σ φ)

modules.title: Polynomials of degree at most one per variable
modules.doc:
Such a polynomial is fixed by its values on the Boolean hypercube $\{0, 1\}^\sigma$.

This is a corollary of the combinatorial Nullstellensatz.

items.name: MvPolynomial.eq_of_degreeOf_le_one_of_eval_zeroOne
items.doc:
Two polynomials of degree at most one per variable that agree on the hypercube are equal.

This is Lemma 3.6 of Thaler, "Proofs, Arguments, and Zero-Knowledge".

modules.title: Strict additive monotonicity on `WithBot ℕ`
modules.doc:
Mathlib's `WithBot.add_lt_add_of_le_of_lt` / `WithBot.add_lt_add_of_lt_of_le` carry `≠ ⊥`
side conditions; the fully strict version below needs none of them over `ℕ`.
Upstreaming candidate.

items.name: WithBot.add_lt_add
items.doc: Strict monotonicity of `+` on `WithBot ℕ`: `a < b → c < d → a + c < b + d`.
items.statement: lemma add_lt_add {a b c d : WithBot ℕ} (h1 : a < b) (h2 : c < d) : a + c < b + d

modules.title: Mathlib-Facing Bivariate Degree Helpers
modules.doc:
This file collects degree- and evaluation-oriented helpers for Mathlib's bivariate
polynomial surface `R[X][Y]` that are useful as a bridge layer between CompPoly and
downstream developments such as ArkLib.

The intended split is:

- `CompPoly/Bivariate/*` for the native computable `CBivariate` representation;
- `CompPoly/ToMathlib/*` for Mathlib-facing transport and helper lemmas.

items.name: Polynomial.Bivariate.coeff
items.doc: `(i, j)`-coefficient of a polynomial, i.e. the coefficient of `X^i Y^j`.
items.statement: def coeff (f : F[X][Y]) (i j : ℕ) : F

items.name: Polynomial.Bivariate.leadingCoeffY
items.doc:
The polynomial coefficient of the highest power of `Y`. This is the leading coefficient in the
classical sense if the bivariate polynomial is interpreted as a univariate polynomial over `F[X]`.
items.statement: def leadingCoeffY (f : F[X][Y]) : F[X]

items.name: Polynomial.Bivariate.natDegreeY
items.doc: The `Y`-degree of a bivariate polynomial, as a natural number.
items.statement: def natDegreeY (f : F[X][Y]) : ℕ

items.name: Polynomial.Bivariate.degreeX
items.doc: The `X`-degree of a bivariate polynomial.
items.statement: def degreeX (f : F[X][Y]) : ℕ

items.name: Polynomial.Bivariate.totalDegree
items.doc: The total degree of a bivariate polynomial.
items.statement: def totalDegree (f : F[X][Y]) : ℕ

items.name: Polynomial.Bivariate.weightedDegree
items.doc:
`(u, v)`-weighted degree of a polynomial.
The maximal `u * i + v * j` such that the polynomial `p`
contains a monomial `x^i * y^j`.
items.statement: def weightedDegree (p : F[X][Y]) (u v : ℕ) : Option ℕ

items.name: Polynomial.Bivariate.natWeightedDegree
items.doc: The natural-number-valued `(u, v)`-weighted degree.
items.statement: def natWeightedDegree (f : F[X][Y]) (u v : ℕ) : ℕ

items.name: Polynomial.Bivariate.weightedDegree_ne_none
items.doc: The weighted degree is always defined (never `none`).
items.statement:
lemma weightedDegree_ne_none (f : F[X][Y]) (u v : ℕ) :
    weightedDegree f u v ≠ none

items.name: Polynomial.Bivariate.natWeightedDegree_mem_weight_list
items.statement:
theorem natWeightedDegree_mem_weight_list {u v : ℕ} :
    natWeightedDegree f u v ∈
      List.map (fun n => u * (f.coeff n).natDegree + v * n)
        (List.range f.natDegree.succ)

items.name: Polynomial.Bivariate.weight_le_natWeightedDegree_of_lt_natDegree_succ
Polynomial.Bivariate.weightedDegree_eq_natWeightedDegree
items.statement:
lemma weightedDegree_eq_natWeightedDegree {u v : ℕ} :
    weightedDegree f u v = natWeightedDegree f u v

items.name: Polynomial.Bivariate.total_deg_as_weighted_deg
items.doc: The total degree of a bivariate polynomial is equal to the `(1, 1)`-weighted degree.
items.statement:
lemma total_deg_as_weighted_deg :
    totalDegree f = natWeightedDegree f 1 1

items.name: Polynomial.Bivariate.degreeX_as_weighted_deg
items.doc: The `X`-degree of a bivariate polynomial is equal to the `(1, 0)`-weighted degree.
items.statement:
lemma degreeX_as_weighted_deg :
    degreeX f = natWeightedDegree f 1 0

items.name: Polynomial.Bivariate.degreeY_as_weighted_deg
items.doc: The `Y`-degree of a bivariate polynomial is equal to the `(0, 1)`-weighted degree.
items.statement:
lemma degreeY_as_weighted_deg :
    natDegreeY f = natWeightedDegree f 0 1

items.name: Polynomial.Bivariate.coeff_natDegree_le_degreeX
items.statement: theorem coeff_natDegree_le_degreeX (f : F[X][Y]) (n : ℕ) : (f.coeff n).natDegree ≤ degreeX f

items.name: Polynomial.Bivariate.degreeX_mul_le
items.statement: theorem degreeX_mul_le (f g : F[X][Y]) : degreeX (f * g) ≤ degreeX f + degreeX g

items.name: Polynomial.Bivariate.exists_max_index_degreeX
items.statement:
theorem exists_max_index_degreeX (f : F[X][Y]) (hf : f ≠ 0) :
    ∃ mm ∈ f.support,
      (f.coeff mm).natDegree = degreeX f ∧
      ∀ n, mm < n → (f.coeff n).natDegree < degreeX f ∨ f.coeff n = 0

items.name: Polynomial.Bivariate.natDegree_sum_eq_of_unique
items.statement:
theorem natDegree_sum_eq_of_unique {α : Type*} {s : Finset α} {f : α → F[X]} {deg : ℕ}
    (mx : α) (hmx : mx ∈ s) :
    (f mx).natDegree = deg →
    (∀ y ∈ s, y ≠ mx → (f y).natDegree < deg ∨ f y = 0) →
    (∑ x ∈ s, f x).natDegree = deg

items.name: Polynomial.Bivariate.degreeX_mul_ge
items.statement:
theorem degreeX_mul_ge [IsDomain F] (f g : F[X][Y]) (hf : f ≠ 0) (hg : g ≠ 0) :
    degreeX f + degreeX g ≤ degreeX (f * g)

items.name: Polynomial.Bivariate.degreeX_mul
items.statement:
theorem degreeX_mul [IsDomain F] (f g : F[X][Y]) (hf : f ≠ 0) (hg : g ≠ 0) :
    degreeX (f * g) = degreeX f + degreeX g

items.name: Polynomial.Bivariate.evalX
items.doc: The evaluation at a point of a bivariate polynomial in the first variable `X`.
items.statement: def evalX (a : F) (f : F[X][Y]) : Polynomial F

items.name: Polynomial.Bivariate.evalY
items.doc: The evaluation at a point of a bivariate polynomial in the second variable `Y`.
items.statement: def evalY (a : F) (f : F[X][Y]) : Polynomial F

items.name: Polynomial.Bivariate.evalX_eq_map
items.statement:
lemma evalX_eq_map (x : F) (f : F[X][Y]) :
    Polynomial.Bivariate.evalX x f = f.map (Polynomial.evalRingHom x)

items.name: Polynomial.Bivariate.degreeX_swap
items.statement:
lemma degreeX_swap (f : F[X][Y]) :
    Polynomial.Bivariate.degreeX (Polynomial.Bivariate.swap f) =
      Polynomial.Bivariate.natDegreeY f

items.name: Polynomial.Bivariate.evalY_eq_evalX_swap
items.statement:
lemma evalY_eq_evalX_swap (y : F) (f : F[X][Y]) :
    Polynomial.Bivariate.evalY y f =
      Polynomial.Bivariate.evalX y (Polynomial.Bivariate.swap f)

items.name: Polynomial.Bivariate.natDegreeY_swap
items.statement:
lemma natDegreeY_swap (f : F[X][Y]) :
    Polynomial.Bivariate.natDegreeY (Polynomial.Bivariate.swap f) =
      Polynomial.Bivariate.degreeX f

items.name: Polynomial.Bivariate.card_evalX_eq_zero_le_degreeX
items.statement:
lemma card_evalX_eq_zero_le_degreeX (A : F[X][Y]) (hA : A ≠ 0) (P : Finset F) :
    (P.filter (fun x => evalX x A = 0)).card ≤ degreeX A

items.name: Polynomial.Bivariate.descend_evalX
items.statement:
lemma descend_evalX {A B G A1 B1 : F[X][Y]} (hA : A = G * A1) (hB : B = G * B1)
    (x : F) (hx : evalX x G ≠ 0) (q : F[X]) (h : evalX x B = q * evalX x A) :
    evalX x B1 = q * evalX x A1

items.name: Polynomial.Bivariate.exists_x_preserve_natDegreeY
items.statement:
lemma exists_x_preserve_natDegreeY (B : F[X][Y]) (hB : B ≠ 0) (P : Finset F)
    (hcard : degreeX B < P.card) :
    ∃ x ∈ P, (evalX x B).natDegree = natDegreeY B

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.degreeX_toPoly
items.doc: The computable X-degree agrees with the Mathlib-facing `degreeX` after `toPoly`.
items.statement:
theorem degreeX_toPoly {R : Type*} [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [Ring R]
    (f : CBivariate R) :
    Polynomial.Bivariate.degreeX (toPoly f) =
      CBivariate.natDegreeX (R := R) f

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.totalDegree_toPoly_spec
items.doc: The computable total degree agrees with the Mathlib-facing total degree after `toPoly`.
items.statement:
theorem totalDegree_toPoly_spec {R : Type*} [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [Ring R]
    (f : CBivariate R) :
    Polynomial.Bivariate.totalDegree (toPoly f) =
      CBivariate.totalDegree (R := R) f

items.name: CompPoly.CBivariate.natWeightedDegree_toPoly
items.statement:
theorem natWeightedDegree_toPoly {R : Type*} [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [Ring R]
    (f : CBivariate R) (u v : ℕ) :
    Polynomial.Bivariate.natWeightedDegree (toPoly f) u v =
      CBivariate.natWeightedDegree (R := R) f u v

modules.title: Mathlib-Facing Bivariate Multiplicity Helpers
modules.doc:
This file collects multiplicity- and discriminant-oriented helpers for Mathlib's
bivariate polynomial surface `R[X][Y]`.

items.name: Polynomial.Bivariate.rootMultiplicity₀
items.doc: Root multiplicity of a bivariate polynomial at the origin.
items.statement: def rootMultiplicity₀ [DecidableEq F] (f : F[X][Y]) : Option ℕ

items.name: Polynomial.Bivariate.shift
items.doc: Shift a bivariate polynomial by `(x, y)`.
items.statement: def shift (f : F[X][Y]) (x y : F) : F[X][Y]

items.name: Polynomial.Bivariate.rootMultiplicity
items.doc: Root multiplicity (order of vanishing) of a bivariate polynomial at `(x, y)`.
items.statement: def rootMultiplicity (f : F[X][Y]) (x y : F) : Option ℕ

items.name: Polynomial.Bivariate.rootMultiplicity₀_ge_iff
items.doc:
`rootMultiplicity₀ g` is at least `r` (vacuously so when `g = 0`, where it is `none`)
iff every coefficient of total degree `< r` vanishes.
items.statement:
theorem rootMultiplicity₀_ge_iff (g : F[X][Y]) (r : ℕ) :
    (∀ i j, i + j < r → coeff g i j = 0) ↔ ∀ m ∈ rootMultiplicity₀ g, r ≤ m

items.name: Polynomial.Bivariate.discr_y
items.doc:
A discriminant-like helper in the outer `Y` variable.

Unlike Mathlib's univariate `discr`, this returns `0` for constant bivariate polynomials.
items.statement: def discr_y (f : F[X][Y]) : F[X]

modules.title: Mathlib-Facing Bivariate Weighted-Degree Helpers
modules.doc:
This file extends `Polynomial.Bivariate` with weighted-degree algebra that is generic
and reusable across downstream protocol developments.

items.name: Polynomial.Bivariate.monomial
items.doc: The monomial `X^i Y^j` as a bivariate polynomial.
items.statement: def monomial (i j : ℕ) : F[X][Y]

items.name: Polynomial.Bivariate.natWeightedDegree_add_le
items.doc: The weighted degree of a sum is at most the maximum of the weighted degrees.
items.statement:
lemma natWeightedDegree_add_le (p q : F[X][Y]) (u v : ℕ) :
    natWeightedDegree (p + q) u v ≤ max (natWeightedDegree p u v) (natWeightedDegree q u v)

items.name: Polynomial.Bivariate.natWeightedDegree_sum_le
items.doc: The weighted degree of a sum is bounded by the supremum of the weighted degrees.
items.statement:
lemma natWeightedDegree_sum_le {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (f : ι → F[X][Y]) (u v : ℕ) :
    natWeightedDegree (∑ i ∈ s, f i) u v ≤ s.sup (fun i ↦ natWeightedDegree (f i) u v)

items.name: Polynomial.Bivariate.natWeightedDegree_smul_le
items.doc: The weighted degree of a scalar multiple is at most the weighted degree of the polynomial.
items.statement:
lemma natWeightedDegree_smul_le (a : F) (p : F[X][Y]) (u v : ℕ) :
    natWeightedDegree (a • p) u v ≤ natWeightedDegree p u v

items.name: Polynomial.Bivariate.degree_eval_le_weightedDegree
items.doc:
The degree of `Q(X, P(X))` is bounded by the weighted degree of `Q`,
provided `deg(P) ≤ k - 1`.
items.statement:
lemma degree_eval_le_weightedDegree (Q : F[X][Y]) (P : F[X]) (k : ℕ) (hP : P.natDegree ≤ k - 1) :
    (Q.eval P).natDegree ≤ natWeightedDegree Q 1 (k - 1)

items.name: Polynomial.Bivariate.natWeightedDegree_monomial
items.doc: The weighted degree of `X^i Y^j` is `u * i + v * j`.
items.statement:
lemma natWeightedDegree_monomial (i j u v : ℕ) :
    natWeightedDegree (monomial (F := F) i j) u v = u * i + v * j

modules.title: Lagrange interpolation on a coset of the `n`-th roots of unity
modules.doc:
Let `omega` be a primitive `n`-th root of unity, and let `s != 0`.

The points `x_i = s omega^i`, for `i < n`, form the coset `s mu_n`.

- nodal polynomial: it is `X^n - s^n`.
- barycentric weights: the weight of `x_i` is `x_i / (n s^n)`.
- Lagrange basis: off the coset, `L_i(x) = (x^n - s^n) x_i / (n s^n (x - x_i))`.
- periodic functions: with `n = p m`, a function of period `p` interpolates to `Q(X^m)`.

In the last result, `Q` is the interpolant of the same values over the coset `s^m mu_p`.

```text
    n = 8, p = 2, m = 4:   f = (a, b, a, b, a, b, a, b) on s mu_8
                           Q interpolates (a, b) on s^4 mu_2
                           interpolate(f) = Q(X^4)
```

A STARK verifier uses this to evaluate a periodic column out of the domain.

The cost drops from `O(n)` to `O(p)`.

The weights follow Berrut and Trefethen, *Barycentric Lagrange Interpolation*.

That paper appeared in SIAM Review 46(3), 2004.

The folding follows the Plonky3 periodic-column evaluator.

items.name: Polynomial.rootsOfUnityCoset
items.doc: The points `s omega^i` of the coset `s mu_n`.
items.statement: def rootsOfUnityCoset (s ω : F) (n : ℕ) : Fin n → F

items.name: Polynomial.rootsOfUnityCoset_injective
items.statement:
theorem rootsOfUnityCoset_injective {s ω : F} {n : ℕ} (hω : IsPrimitiveRoot ω n) (hs : s ≠ 0) :
    Function.Injective (rootsOfUnityCoset s ω n)

items.name: Polynomial.nodal_rootsOfUnityCoset
items.doc: The nodal polynomial of `s mu_n` is `X^n - s^n`.
items.statement:
theorem nodal_rootsOfUnityCoset {s ω : F} {n : ℕ} (hω : IsPrimitiveRoot ω n) (hn : 0 < n) :
    nodal univ (rootsOfUnityCoset s ω n) = X ^ n - C (s ^ n)

items.name: Polynomial.nodalWeight_rootsOfUnityCoset
items.doc: The barycentric weight of `x_i = s omega^i` is `x_i / (n s^n)`.
items.statement:
theorem nodalWeight_rootsOfUnityCoset {s ω : F} {n : ℕ} (hω : IsPrimitiveRoot ω n)
    (hn : (n : F) ≠ 0) (hs : s ≠ 0) (i : Fin n) :
    nodalWeight univ (rootsOfUnityCoset s ω n) i = rootsOfUnityCoset s ω n i / (n * s ^ n)

items.name: Polynomial.eval_basis_rootsOfUnityCoset
items.doc: Off the coset, `L_i(x) = (x^n - s^n) x_i / (n s^n (x - x_i))`.
items.statement:
theorem eval_basis_rootsOfUnityCoset {s ω x : F} {n : ℕ} (hω : IsPrimitiveRoot ω n)
    (hn : (n : F) ≠ 0) (hs : s ≠ 0) (i : Fin n) (hx : x ≠ rootsOfUnityCoset s ω n i) :
    (Lagrange.basis univ (rootsOfUnityCoset s ω n) i).eval x =
      (x ^ n - s ^ n) *
        (rootsOfUnityCoset s ω n i / (n * s ^ n) * (x - rootsOfUnityCoset s ω n i)⁻¹)

items.name: Polynomial.interpolate_rootsOfUnityCoset_periodic
items.doc:
A function of period `p` on `s mu_n`, with `n = p m`, interpolates to `Q(X^m)`.

Here `Q` interpolates the same values over the coset `s^m mu_p`.
items.statement:
theorem interpolate_rootsOfUnityCoset_periodic {s ω : F} {p m : ℕ} [NeZero p]
    (hω : IsPrimitiveRoot ω (p * m)) (hs : s ≠ 0) (hm : 0 < m) (g : Fin p → F) :
    interpolate univ (rootsOfUnityCoset s ω (p * m)) (fun i => g (Fin.ofNat p i)) =
      (interpolate univ (rootsOfUnityCoset (s ^ m) (ω ^ m) p) g).comp (X ^ m)

modules.title: Small-factor extraction for reducible polynomials
modules.doc:
A reducible polynomial of degree `n` always has an irreducible factor of degree at most
`n / 2`: it splits as a product of two non-units whose degrees sum to `n`, and the smaller
of the two dominates an irreducible factor.

This is the pigeonhole step of Rabin's irreducibility test (see
`CompPoly/Data/Polynomial/Rabin.lean`), which needs to bound the degree of a hypothetical
small factor in order to derive a contradiction.

## Main statements

* `Polynomial.exists_factor_natDegree_le_of_reducible`: a reducible polynomial of degree `n`
  has an irreducible factor of degree at most `n / 2`.

items.name: Polynomial.exists_factor_natDegree_le_of_reducible
items.doc:
A reducible polynomial of positive degree `n` has an irreducible factor of degree at most
`n / 2`.

Writing `P = a * b` with both factors non-units, their degrees sum to `n`, so the smaller one
has degree at most `n / 2`; any irreducible factor of it works.

modules.title: Root sets of products of distinct linear factors
modules.doc:
- `∏ i ∈ s, (X - C (a i))` over injectively indexed points: it divides every polynomial
vanishing on the points (`prod_X_sub_C_dvd`)
- A nonzero polynomial vanishes at boundedly many of the points (`card_eval_zero_le_natDegree`)
- The product divides `(∏ i ∈ E, (X - C (a i))) * (f - b)` whenever `f` and `b` agree off `E`
(`prod_X_sub_C_dvd_prod_mul_sub`).

items.name: Polynomial.prod_X_sub_C_dvd
items.doc: `∏ i ∈ s, (X - aᵢ)` divides `p` when the distinct `aᵢ` are all roots of `p`.
items.statement:
lemma prod_X_sub_C_dvd [Field R]
    {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (a : ι → R) (hinj : Set.InjOn a s)
    (p : R[X]) (hr : ∀ i ∈ s, p.eval (a i) = 0) :
    (∏ i ∈ s, (X - C (a i))) ∣ p

items.name: Polynomial.card_eval_zero_le_natDegree
items.doc: A nonzero `v` vanishes at at most `v.natDegree` of the distinct points.
items.statement:
lemma card_eval_zero_le_natDegree [CommRing R] [IsDomain R]
    {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq R] (s : Finset ι) (a : ι → R)
    (hinj : Set.InjOn a s) (v : R[X]) (hv : v ≠ 0) :
    {i ∈ s | v.eval (a i) = 0}.card ≤ v.natDegree

items.name: Polynomial.prod_X_sub_C_dvd_prod_mul_sub
items.doc:
When `f, b` agree off `E ⊆ s`, the product `∏_{i∈s}(X−aᵢ)` divides
`(∏_{i∈E}(X−aᵢ))·(f − b)`.
items.statement:
lemma prod_X_sub_C_dvd_prod_mul_sub [Field R] {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι]
    (s E : Finset ι) (hE : E ⊆ s) (a : ι → R) (hinj : Set.InjOn a s)
    (f b : R[X]) (hagree : ∀ i ∈ s \ E, f.eval (a i) = b.eval (a i)) :
    (∏ i ∈ s, (X - C (a i))) ∣ (∏ i ∈ E, (X - C (a i))) * (f - b)

modules.title: Barycentric Interpolation
modules.doc:
This file provides a **fixed-domain barycentric interpolation** structure and evaluator
for univariate computable polynomials.

## Main definitions

* `CLagrange.BarycentricDomain` – a structure bundling `n` distinct nodes in `R` together with
  precomputed barycentric weights `w_i = ∏_{j ≠ i} (x_i − x_j)⁻¹`.

* `CLagrange.BarycentricDomain.eval` – the standard second-form barycentric evaluator:
  - if `z` equals a node `x_i`, returns `y_i` (the explicit node-hit fast path);
  - otherwise returns
    `(∑ w_i y_i / (z − x_i)) / (∑ w_i / (z − x_i))`.

## Main results

* `weights_eq_nodalWeight` – stored weights agree with `Lagrange.nodalWeight`.
* `eval_at_node` – the evaluator returns `y i` at node `x_i`.
* `eval_eq_cinterpolate_eval` – the evaluator equals
  `(CLagrange.interpolate Finset.univ nodes y).eval z`.
* `eval_eq_interpolate_eval` – variant in terms of `Lagrange.interpolate`.
* `ofPow_eval_eq_interpolatePow_eval` – specialization to `CLagrange.interpolatePow`.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.CLagrange.BarycentricDomain
items.doc:
A fixed-domain barycentric interpolation structure.

Bundles `n` distinct evaluation nodes together with precomputed barycentric weights.
The evaluator `BarycentricDomain.eval` can then be called repeatedly for different
value vectors and query points with no redundant per-query work on the nodes.
items.statement:
structure BarycentricDomain (R : Type*) [Field R] [DecidableEq R] (n : ℕ) where
  /-- The evaluation nodes. -/
  nodes : Fin n → R
  /-- The nodes are pairwise distinct. -/
  nodes_injective : Function.Injective nodes
  /-- Precomputed barycentric weights. -/
  weights : Fin n → R
  /-- The stored weights satisfy the standard product-inverse formula:
  `w_i = ∏_{j ≠ i} (x_i − x_j)⁻¹`. -/
  weights_spec : ∀ i, weights i =
    ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n)).erase i).prod (fun j => (nodes i - nodes j)⁻¹)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.CLagrange.BarycentricDomain.mk'
items.doc:
Construct a `BarycentricDomain` from nodes and an injectivity proof,
computing the weights automatically.
items.statement:
def BarycentricDomain.mk' (nodes : Fin n → R) (hinj : Function.Injective nodes) :
    BarycentricDomain R n

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.CLagrange.BarycentricDomain.weights_eq_nodalWeight
items.doc: The stored weights are exactly `Lagrange.nodalWeight Finset.univ nodes`.
items.statement:
theorem BarycentricDomain.weights_eq_nodalWeight (dom : BarycentricDomain R n) (i : Fin n) :
    dom.weights i = Lagrange.nodalWeight Finset.univ dom.nodes i

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.CLagrange.BarycentricDomain.eval
items.doc:
The standard second-form barycentric evaluator.

* If `z` equals a node `x_i`, returns `y i` (the explicit node-hit fast path).
  The node-hit is found by a computable finite search over `Fin n` via `Fin.find`.
* Otherwise returns
  `(∑ i, w_i * y_i * (z − x_i)⁻¹) / (∑ i, w_i * (z − x_i)⁻¹)`,
  the classical barycentric ratio.
items.statement: def BarycentricDomain.eval (dom : BarycentricDomain R n) (y : Fin n → R) (z : R) : R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.CLagrange.BarycentricDomain.evalStep
items.doc:
One step of the single-inversion barycentric fold.

The state `(a, b, p)` carries both barycentric sums over a common denominator: after the
nodes `l` it is `(p·∑ wᵢyᵢ/dᵢ, p·∑ wᵢ/dᵢ, p)` with `p = ∏ dᵢ` and `dᵢ = z - xᵢ`.
items.statement:
def BarycentricDomain.evalStep (dom : BarycentricDomain R n) (y : Fin n → R) (z : R)
    (acc : R × R × R) (i : Fin n) : R × R × R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.CLagrange.BarycentricDomain.evalFast
items.doc:
The barycentric evaluator with a single field division off the nodes.

It agrees with `eval` everywhere (`eval_eq_evalFast`), and the compiler uses it in place of
`eval`.
items.statement: def BarycentricDomain.evalFast (dom : BarycentricDomain R n) (y : Fin n → R) (z : R) : R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.CLagrange.BarycentricDomain.eval_eq_evalFast
items.doc: The single-division evaluator agrees with the two-sum evaluator.
items.statement:
theorem BarycentricDomain.eval_eq_evalFast :
    @BarycentricDomain.eval = @BarycentricDomain.evalFast

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.CLagrange.BarycentricDomain.eval_at_node
items.doc: At a node, the barycentric evaluator returns the corresponding value.
items.statement:
theorem BarycentricDomain.eval_at_node (dom : BarycentricDomain R n) (y : Fin n → R)
    (i : Fin n) : dom.eval y (dom.nodes i) = y i

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.CLagrange.BarycentricDomain.eval_eq_interpolate_eval
items.statement:
theorem BarycentricDomain.eval_eq_interpolate_eval (dom : BarycentricDomain R n)
    (y : Fin n → R) (z : R) :
    dom.eval y z = (Lagrange.interpolate Finset.univ dom.nodes y).eval z

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.CLagrange.BarycentricDomain.eval_eq_cinterpolate_eval
items.doc:
The barycentric evaluator equals
`(CLagrange.interpolate Finset.univ dom.nodes y).eval z`.
items.statement:
theorem BarycentricDomain.eval_eq_cinterpolate_eval [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (dom : BarycentricDomain R n) (y : Fin n → R) (z : R) :
    dom.eval y z = (CLagrange.interpolate Finset.univ dom.nodes y).eval z

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.CLagrange.BarycentricDomain.ofPow
items.doc:
Build a barycentric domain from a primitive root of unity `ω` with
`n ≤ orderOf ω`, so nodes are `ω^0, ω^1, …, ω^{n-1}`.
items.statement:
def BarycentricDomain.ofPow (ω : Rˣ) (hord : n ≤ orderOf ω) :
    BarycentricDomain R n

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.CLagrange.BarycentricDomain.ofPow_eval_eq_interpolatePow_eval
items.doc:
The barycentric evaluator on power-of-ω nodes agrees with
`(CLagrange.interpolatePow ω r).eval z`.
items.statement:
theorem BarycentricDomain.ofPow_eval_eq_interpolatePow_eval [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (ω : Rˣ) (hord : n ≤ orderOf ω) (r : Vector R n) (z : R) :
    (BarycentricDomain.ofPow ω hord).eval r.get z =
    (CLagrange.interpolatePow ω.1 r).eval z

modules.authors: Quang Dao, Gregor Mitscha-Baude, Derek Sorensen, Desmond Coles, Valerii Huhnin, Julian Sutherland
modules.title: Computable Univariate Polynomials
modules.doc:
This file defines `CPolynomial R`, the type of canonical univariate polynomials.
Canonicality is tracked semantically by requiring the last stored coefficient, when present,
to be nonzero.

This provides a unique representation for each polynomial, enabling stronger extensionality
properties compared to the raw `CPolynomial.Raw` type.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial
items.doc:
Computable univariate polynomials are represented canonically with no trailing zeros.

A polynomial `p : CPolynomial.Raw R` is canonical if its last stored coefficient is nonzero
whenever the underlying array is nonempty. This gives an instance-stable carrier while keeping
the raw normalization algorithms available separately.

`Raw.mul` defers trimming to the end of its convolution fold (it accumulates with the
untrimmed `Raw.mulRaw` and trims once). `Raw.powBySq` likewise routes through an
untrimmed `powBySqUntrimmed` and trims once at the top of the repeated-squaring
recursion. `CPolynomial.divX` skips trimming entirely: the input is canonical and
`extract 1 size` only strips from the front, so the leading coefficient (when present)
is preserved and the result is already canonical. The division wrappers (`divByMonic`,
`modByMonic`, `modByMonicRemainderOnly`, `modByMonicByReversal`, `div`, `mod`) likewise
skip the redundant post-trim: each underlying `Raw` algorithm bottoms out in operations
(`Raw.add`, `Raw.sub`, `subScaledShift`) that already trim. `CLagrange.basis` folds the
`s.erase i` factors with the untrimmed `Raw.mulRaw` via `Quotient.liftOn` on the
underlying multiset and trims once at the end, and `CLagrange.interpolate` does the
analogous deferred-trim sum via `Raw.addRaw`/`Raw.mulRaw`.
Remaining opportunities to trim only at the end of an iterative computation:
the `Array.foldl` accumulator in `Bivariate/ToPoly.lean` (`toPoly_foldl_zipIdx_eq_sum`),
and the two `ExtTreeMap.foldl` monomial accumulators in `Multivariate/Operations.lean`.
The NTT `butterflyStage` in `Univariate/NTT/Transform.lean` is not on this list: it
operates on a scalar coefficient `Array R` and never calls `trim`.
items.statement: def CPolynomial (R : Type*) [Zero R]

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.ext
items.doc: Extensionality for canonical polynomials.
items.statement: theorem ext [Zero R] {p q : CPolynomial R} (h : p.val = q.val) : p = q

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.trim_eq
items.doc: Canonical computable polynomials are trim-stable.
items.statement: theorem trim_eq [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (p : CPolynomial R) : p.val.trim = p.val

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.add_comm
items.statement:
protected theorem add_comm [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (p q : CPolynomial R) : p + q = q + p

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.add_assoc
items.statement:
protected theorem add_assoc [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (p q r : CPolynomial R) : p + q + r = p + (q + r)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.zero_add
items.statement: protected theorem zero_add [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (p : CPolynomial R) : 0 + p = p

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.add_zero
items.statement: protected theorem add_zero [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (p : CPolynomial R) : p + 0 = p

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.nsmul
items.doc: Scalar multiplication by a natural number (result is canonical).
items.statement: def nsmul [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (n : ℕ) (p : CPolynomial R) : CPolynomial R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.nsmul_zero
items.statement:
protected theorem nsmul_zero [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (p : CPolynomial R) : nsmul 0 p = 0

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.nsmul_succ
items.statement:
theorem nsmul_succ [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (n : ℕ) (p : CPolynomial R) : nsmul (n + 1) p = nsmul n p + p

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.one_is_trimmed
items.statement:
lemma one_is_trimmed [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] :
    (1 : CPolynomial.Raw R).trim = 1

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.coeff
items.doc: The coefficient of `X^i` in the polynomial. Returns `0` if `i` is out of bounds.
items.statement: def coeff [Zero R] (p : CPolynomial R) (i : ℕ) : R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.ofArray
items.doc: Build a canonical polynomial from a dense coefficient array.
items.statement:
def ofArray [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (coeffs : Array R) : CPolynomial R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.coeff_ofArray
items.doc: Coefficients of `ofArray` are exactly the source array entries, with zero default.
items.statement:
theorem coeff_ofArray [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (coeffs : Array R) (i : Nat) :
    (CPolynomial.ofArray coeffs).coeff i = coeffs.getD i 0

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.ofFn
items.doc:
Construct a canonical polynomial from a coefficient function `Fin n → R`.

Index `i` gives the coefficient of `X^i`; the resulting array is trimmed to remove
trailing zeros.
items.statement: def ofFn [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] {n : ℕ} (f : Fin n → R) : CPolynomial R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.coeff_ofFn
items.doc: Coefficients of `ofFn` are the source function entries below `n`, and zero at or above `n`.
items.statement:
theorem coeff_ofFn [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] {n : ℕ} (f : Fin n → R) (i : ℕ) :
    (CPolynomial.ofFn f).coeff i = if h : i < n then f ⟨i, h⟩ else 0

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.C
items.doc: The constant polynomial `C r`.
items.statement: def C [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (r : R) : CPolynomial R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.X
items.doc: The variable `X`.
items.statement: def X [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] : CPolynomial R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.linearFactor
items.doc: The monic linear factor `X - C x`.
items.statement: def linearFactor [Field R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (x : R) : CPolynomial R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.monomial
items.doc:
Construct a canonical monomial `c * X^n` as a `CPolynomial R`.

The result is canonical (no trailing zeros) when `c ≠ 0`.
For example, `monomial 2 3` represents `3 * X^2`.

Note: If `c = 0`, this returns `0` (the zero polynomial).
items.statement:
def monomial [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [DecidableEq R]
    (n : ℕ) (c : R) : CPolynomial R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.degree
items.doc: Return the degree of a `CPolynomial`.
items.statement: def degree [Zero R] (p : CPolynomial R) : WithBot ℕ

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.natDegree
items.doc:
Natural number degree of a canonical polynomial.

Returns the degree as a natural number. For the zero polynomial, returns `0`.
This matches Mathlib's `Polynomial.natDegree` API.
items.statement: def natDegree [Zero R] (p : CPolynomial R) : ℕ

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.leadingCoeff
items.doc:
Return the leading coefficient of a `CPolynomial` as the last coefficient
of the trimmed array, or `0` if the trimmed array is empty.
items.statement: def leadingCoeff [Zero R] (p : CPolynomial R) : R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.eval
items.doc: Evaluate a polynomial at a point.
items.statement: def eval [Semiring R] (x : R) (p : CPolynomial R) : R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.eval₂
items.doc:
Evaluate at `x : S` via a ring hom
`f : R →+* S`; `eval₂ f x p = f(a₀) + f(a₁)*x + f(a₂)*x² + ...`.
items.statement:
def eval₂ {S : Type*} [Semiring R] [Semiring S]
    (f : R →+* S) (x : S) (p : CPolynomial R) : S

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.eval₂Horner
items.doc: Evaluate at `x : S` via a ring hom using Horner's method.
items.statement:
def eval₂Horner {S : Type*} [Semiring R] [Semiring S]
    (f : R →+* S) (x : S) (p : CPolynomial R) : S

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.evalHorner
items.doc: Evaluate a polynomial at a point using Horner's method.
items.statement: def evalHorner [Semiring R] (x : R) (p : CPolynomial R) : R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.eval₂_horner_eq_eval₂
items.doc: Horner evaluation agrees with the sum-of-powers evaluation.
items.statement:
theorem eval₂_horner_eq_eval₂ {S : Type*} [Semiring R] [Semiring S]
    (f : R →+* S) (x : S) (p : CPolynomial R) :
    eval₂Horner f x p = eval₂ f x p

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.eval_horner_eq_eval
items.doc: Horner evaluation agrees with the sum-of-powers evaluation.
items.statement:
theorem eval_horner_eq_eval [Semiring R] (x : R) (p : CPolynomial R) :
    evalHorner x p = eval x p

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.eval₂_eq_eval₂Horner
items.doc: Compiled code evaluates by Horner's method; `eval₂` remains the specification.
items.statement: theorem eval₂_eq_eval₂Horner : @eval₂ = @eval₂Horner

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.eval_eq_evalHorner
items.doc: Compiled code evaluates by Horner's method; `eval` remains the specification.
items.statement: theorem eval_eq_evalHorner : @eval = @evalHorner

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.support
items.doc: The support of a polynomial: indices with nonzero coefficients.
items.statement: def support [Zero R] [BEq R] (p : CPolynomial R) : Finset ℕ

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.size
items.doc: Number of coefficients (length of the underlying array).
items.statement: def size [Zero R] (p : CPolynomial R) : ℕ

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.degreeBound
items.doc: Upper bound on degree: `size - 1` if non-empty, `⊥` if empty.
items.statement: def degreeBound [Zero R] (p : CPolynomial R) : WithBot Nat

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.natDegreeBound
items.doc: Convert `degreeBound` to a natural number by sending `⊥` to `0`.
items.statement: def natDegreeBound [Zero R] (p : CPolynomial R) : Nat

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.monic
items.doc: Check if a `CPolynomial` is monic, i.e. its leading coefficient is 1.
items.statement: def monic [Zero R] [One R] [BEq R] (p : CPolynomial R) : Bool

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.divX
items.doc:
The polynomial with the constant term removed; `coeff (divX p) i = coeff p (i + 1)`.

No post-extract trim is needed: since `p` is canonical, its last entry is nonzero, and
`extract 1 p.val.size` strips only from the front, so the result is already canonical
(vacuously when `p.val.size ≤ 1`).
items.statement: def divX [Zero R] (p : CPolynomial R) : CPolynomial R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.coeff_C
items.doc: Coefficient of the constant polynomial `C r`.
items.statement:
lemma coeff_C [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (r : R) (i : ℕ) :
    coeff (C r) i = if i = 0 then r else 0

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.coeff_X
items.doc: Coefficient of the variable `X`.
items.statement:
lemma coeff_X [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] (i : ℕ) :
    coeff X i = if i = 1 then 1 else 0

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.coeff_zero
items.doc: Coefficient of the zero polynomial.
items.statement: lemma coeff_zero [Zero R] (i : ℕ) : coeff (0 : CPolynomial R) i = 0

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.coeff_one
items.doc: Coefficient of the constant polynomial `1`.
items.statement:
lemma coeff_one [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] (i : ℕ) :
    coeff (1 : CPolynomial R) i = if i = 0 then 1 else 0

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.coeff_add
items.doc: Coefficient of a sum.
items.statement:
lemma coeff_add [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (p q : CPolynomial R) (i : ℕ) : coeff (p + q) i = coeff p i + coeff q i

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.coeff_monomial
items.doc: Coefficient of a monomial.
items.statement:
lemma coeff_monomial [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [DecidableEq R]
    (n i : ℕ) (c : R) :
    coeff (monomial n c) i = if i = n then c else 0

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.coeff_mul
items.doc: Coefficient of a product (convolution sum).
items.statement:
lemma coeff_mul [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (p q : CPolynomial R) (k : ℕ) :
    coeff (p * q) k = (Finset.range (k + 1)).sum (fun i => coeff p i * coeff q (k - i))

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.eq_iff_coeff
items.doc: Two polynomials are equal iff they have the same coefficients.
items.statement:
theorem eq_iff_coeff [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] {p q : CPolynomial R} :
    p = q ↔ ∀ i, coeff p i = coeff q i

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.monomial_add
items.doc: Monomials are additive in their coefficient.
items.statement:
theorem monomial_add [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [DecidableEq R]
    (n : ℕ) (a b : R) :
    monomial n (a + b) = monomial n a + monomial n b

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.eq_zero_iff_coeff_zero
items.doc: Zero characterization: `p = 0` iff all coefficients are zero.
items.statement:
theorem eq_zero_iff_coeff_zero [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] {p : CPolynomial R} :
    p = 0 ↔ ∀ i, coeff p i = 0

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.coeff_eq_zero_of_size_le
items.doc: Coefficients past the stored canonical array are zero.
items.statement:
theorem coeff_eq_zero_of_size_le [Zero R] (p : CPolynomial R) {i : ℕ}
    (hi : p.val.size ≤ i) : coeff p i = 0

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.coeff_monomial_mul
items.doc: Coefficient of a monomial multiple: shift by `n` and scale by `c`.
items.statement:
lemma coeff_monomial_mul [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [DecidableEq R]
    (n : ℕ) (c : R) (p : CPolynomial R) (i : ℕ) :
    coeff (monomial n c * p) i = if n ≤ i then c * coeff p (i - n) else 0

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.mem_support_iff
items.doc: An index is in the support iff the coefficient there is nonzero.
items.statement:
lemma mem_support_iff [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (p : CPolynomial R) (i : ℕ) :
    i ∈ p.support ↔ coeff p i ≠ 0

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.support_empty_iff
items.doc: The support is empty iff the polynomial is zero.
items.statement:
theorem support_empty_iff [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (p : CPolynomial R) :
    p.support = ∅ ↔ p = 0

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.C_zero
items.doc: The constant polynomial `C 0` is zero.
items.statement:
lemma C_zero [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] :
    (C (0 : R) : CPolynomial R) = 0

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.natDegree_C
items.doc: The natDegree of a constant polynomial `C r` is zero.
items.statement:
theorem natDegree_C [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (r : R) :
    (C r).natDegree = 0

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.natDegree_zero
items.statement:
theorem natDegree_zero [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] :
    (0 : CPolynomial R).natDegree = 0

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.support_C
items.doc: The support of a constant polynomial `C r` is `{0}`.
items.statement:
theorem support_C [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] {r : R} (hr : r ≠ 0) :
    (C r).support = {0}

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.support_monomial
items.doc: The support of a nonzero monomial `c * X^n` is `{n}`.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.natDegree_monomial
items.doc: The natDegree of a nonzero monomial `c * X^n` is `n`.
items.statement:
theorem natDegree_monomial [Semiring R] [DecidableEq R]
    [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] {n : ℕ} {c : R} (hc : c ≠ 0) :
    (monomial n c).natDegree = n

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.support_add_subset
items.doc: The support of the sum of two polynomials is a subset of the union of their supports.
items.statement:
theorem support_add_subset [Semiring R] [DecidableEq R]
    [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (p q : CPolynomial R) : (p + q).support ⊆ p.support ∪ q.support

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.eval_eq_sum_support
items.doc: Evaluation equals the sum over support of coefficients times powers.
items.statement:
theorem eval_eq_sum_support [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (p : CPolynomial R) (x : R) :
    p.eval x = p.support.sum (fun i => p.coeff i * x ^ i)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.eval₂_eq_sum_support
items.doc: Evaluation via a ring hom equals the sum over support of mapped coefficients times powers.
items.statement:
theorem eval₂_eq_sum_support {S : Type*} [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Semiring S]
    (f : R →+* S) (p : CPolynomial R) (x : S) :
    p.eval₂ f x = p.support.sum (fun i => f (p.coeff i) * x ^ i)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.coeff_C_mul
items.statement:
lemma coeff_C_mul [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R]
    (p : CPolynomial R) (c : R) :
    ∀ i, coeff ((C c) * p) i = c * (coeff p i)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.coeff_X_mul_succ
items.doc: Lemmas on coefficients and multiplication by `X`.
items.statement:
lemma coeff_X_mul_succ [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R]
    (p : CPolynomial R) (n : ℕ) :
    coeff (X * p) (n + 1) = coeff p n

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.coeff_X_mul_zero
items.statement:
lemma coeff_X_mul_zero [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R]
    (p : CPolynomial R) : coeff (X * p) 0 = 0

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.coeff_mul_X_succ
items.statement:
theorem coeff_mul_X_succ [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R]
    (p : CPolynomial R) (n : ℕ) :
    coeff (p * X) (n + 1) = coeff p n

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.coeff_mul_X_zero
items.statement:
theorem coeff_mul_X_zero [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R]
    (p : CPolynomial R) : coeff (p * X) 0 = 0

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.coeff_extract_succ
items.statement:

CompPoly.CPolynomial.degree_eq_support_max
items.doc:
Degree equals the maximum of the support when the polynomial is non-zero.
Here `p.degree = some n` where `n` is the maximum index in `p.support`.
items.statement:
theorem degree_eq_support_max [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (p : CPolynomial R) (hp : p ≠ 0) :
    ∃ n, n ∈ p.support ∧ p.degree = n

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.erase
items.doc:
Erase the coefficient at index `n` (same as `p` except `coeff n = 0`, then trimmed).

Uses an in-place `Array.setIfInBounds` and avoids allocating a length-`n` monomial
array plus the padding/zip passes of `sub`.
items.statement: def erase [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (n : ℕ) (p : CPolynomial R) : CPolynomial R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.coeff_erase

lemma coeff_erase [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (n i : ℕ) (p : CPolynomial R) :
    coeff (erase n p) i = if i = n then 0 else coeff p i

    p.leadingCoeff = p.coeff p.natDegree

items.doc: A polynomial equals its leading monomial plus the rest (`erase` at `natDegree`).
items.statement:
lemma monomial_add_erase [Ring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [DecidableEq R]
    (p : CPolynomial R) :
    p = monomial p.natDegree p.leadingCoeff + erase p.natDegree p

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.subMulMonomial
items.doc:
Fused `a - c * X^d * b` on canonical coefficient arrays.

Each output coefficient is computed directly, so one call costs
`O(max (deg a) (d + deg b))` field operations instead of the `O(d * deg b)`
convolution behind `monomial d c * b` followed by a subtraction pass.
The guards skip the array construction entirely when either factor is zero.
items.statement:
def subMulMonomial [Ring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (a : CPolynomial R) (c : R) (d : Nat) (b : CPolynomial R) : CPolynomial R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.subMulMonomial_eq
items.doc: `subMulMonomial` agrees with the generic `a - monomial d c * b`.
items.statement:
theorem subMulMonomial_eq [Ring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [DecidableEq R]
    (a : CPolynomial R) (c : R) (d : Nat) (b : CPolynomial R) :
    subMulMonomial a c d b = a - monomial d c * b

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.erase_correct
items.doc:
The in-place `erase` agrees with the subtraction-based characterization:
`erase n p` equals `p - monomial n (p.coeff n)`.
items.statement:
lemma erase_correct [Ring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [DecidableEq R]
    (n : ℕ) (p : CPolynomial R) :
    erase n p = p - monomial n (p.coeff n)

modules.title: Subproduct-Tree Interpolation
modules.doc:
Fast interpolation on arbitrary distinct nodes, reusing the subproduct tree of
`BatchEval/SubproductTree.lean`. With `G = ∏ (X - xᵢ)` at the root, the interpolant of the
values `yᵢ` is

  `∑ᵢ cᵢ · G / (X - xᵢ)`, where `cᵢ = yᵢ / G'(xᵢ)`,

and both halves run over the tree. The weights come from descending with `G'` by
remainders, as batch evaluation descends with `p`. The sum is then assembled bottom-up as
`L · M_right + R · M_left` at each node. With an NTT-backed `MulContext` this is the
classical `O(M(n) log n)` algorithm; it needs no root of unity and no power-of-two size.

## Main definitions

* `SubproductTree.interpolateAux`: the fused descent and recombination over one tree.
* `interpolateSubproduct`: interpolation of values on an array of nodes.

## Main results

* `interpolateSubproduct_eq_interpolateArrays`: for pairwise distinct nodes, the result is
  the Lagrange interpolant `CLagrange.interpolateArrays`.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.SubproductTree.leafCount
items.doc: The number of leaves of a subproduct tree.
items.statement: def leafCount [Zero R] : SubproductTree R → Nat

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.SubproductTree.interpolateAux
items.doc:
Descend with remainders of `r` and recombine the weighted leaves bottom-up.

At a leaf `x` holding the value `y` the contribution is the constant `y / r(x)`; at a node
the two children's contributions are cross-multiplied by the sibling's product polynomial.
Called with `r = G'` on the whole tree this is the Lagrange interpolant.
items.statement:
def interpolateAux [Field R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (M : MulContext R) (D : ModContext R) :
    SubproductTree R → CPolynomial R → List R → CPolynomial R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.interpolateSubproduct
items.doc:
Interpolate the values `ys` on the nodes `xs` through a subproduct tree.

Missing values default to `0`, as in `CLagrange.interpolateArrays`.
items.statement:
def interpolateSubproduct [Field R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (M : MulContext R) (D : ModContext R) (xs ys : Array R) : CPolynomial R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.interpolateSubproduct_eq_interpolateArrays
items.doc: On pairwise distinct nodes, subproduct-tree interpolation is Lagrange interpolation.
items.statement:
theorem interpolateSubproduct_eq_interpolateArrays [Field R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (M : MulContext R) (D : ModContext R) (xs ys : Array R) (hxs : xs.toList.Nodup) :
    interpolateSubproduct M D xs ys = CLagrange.interpolateArrays xs ys
