modules.title: Serialization of univariate polynomials
modules.doc:
Two encodings of a `CPolynomial R`, and they agree.

* **Fixed width, for protocol messages.** A polynomial of degree below `n`, an element of
  `↥(degreeLT n)`, is its first `n` coefficients, zero-padded: `n * width R` bytes through the
  vector codec. Decoding trims. This is `ByteCodec ↥(degreeLT n)`, unconditionally injective,
  the message shape of a sumcheck round polynomial or a FRI fold.
* **Self-delimiting, for fixtures and hashing.** A `u64` little-endian coefficient count, then
  the coefficients. This is `DelimitedCodec (CPolynomial R)` over any delimited coefficient
  codec, so it nests (`CompPoly.Bivariate.Bytes`). Injective because the representation is
  canonical: no trailing zeros, so equal coefficient lists are equal polynomials. A polynomial
  is `Valid` when its size fits in a `u64` and its coefficients are valid.

`encode_eq_encodeU64_append_toBytes` ties the two: the self-delimiting encoding is the count
followed by the fixed-width encoding at `n = size`.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.ofArray_val
items.doc: Rebuilding a canonical polynomial from its own coefficient array gives it back.
items.statement: theorem ofArray_val (p : CPolynomial R) : ofArray p.val = p

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.coeffVector
items.doc: The coefficient vector of a polynomial of degree below `n`, zero-padded.
items.statement: def coeffVector (n : ℕ) (p : ↥(degreeLT (R := R) n)) : Vector R n

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.ofCoeffVector
items.doc: The polynomial with the given `n` coefficients, as an element of `degreeLT n`.
items.statement: def ofCoeffVector (n : ℕ) (v : Vector R n) : ↥(degreeLT (R := R) n)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.ofCoeffVector_eq_ofFnEquiv
items.doc: Rebuilding from a vector agrees with applying `ofFnEquiv` to its entries.
items.statement:
theorem ofCoeffVector_eq_ofFnEquiv (n : ℕ) (v : Vector R n) :
    ofCoeffVector n v = ofFnEquiv n (fun i => v[i])

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.ofCoeffVector_coeffVector
items.doc: Reading the coefficients into a vector and rebuilding the polynomial recovers `p`.
items.statement:
theorem ofCoeffVector_coeffVector (n : ℕ) (p : ↥(degreeLT (R := R) n)) :
    ofCoeffVector n (coeffVector n p) = p

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.instByteCodecDegreeLT
items.doc: Degree below `n`: the `n` coefficients, `n * width R` bytes.
items.statement: instance instByteCodecDegreeLT [ByteCodec R] (n : ℕ) : ByteCodec ↥(degreeLT (R := R) n)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.width_degreeLT
items.statement:
theorem width_degreeLT [ByteCodec R] (n : ℕ) :
    ByteCodec.width ↥(degreeLT (R := R) n) = n * ByteCodec.width R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.toBytes_degreeLT
items.statement:
theorem toBytes_degreeLT [ByteCodec R] {n : ℕ} (p : ↥(degreeLT (R := R) n)) :
    ByteCodec.toBytes p = ByteCodec.toBytes (coeffVector n p)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.instDelimitedCodec
items.doc: A `u64` coefficient count, then the coefficients.
items.statement: instance instDelimitedCodec [DelimitedCodec R] : DelimitedCodec (CPolynomial R)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.valid_iff
items.statement:
theorem valid_iff [DelimitedCodec R] (p : CPolynomial R) :
    DelimitedCodec.Valid p ↔ p.val.size < 2 ^ 64 ∧ ∀ c ∈ p.val.toList, DelimitedCodec.Valid c

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.valid_iff_size_lt
items.doc: Over a fixed-width coefficient type, a polynomial is valid exactly when its size fits.
items.statement:
theorem valid_iff_size_lt [ByteCodec R] (p : CPolynomial R) :
    DelimitedCodec.Valid p ↔ p.val.size < 2 ^ 64

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.encode_eq
items.statement:
theorem encode_eq [DelimitedCodec R] (p : CPolynomial R) :
    DelimitedCodec.encode p
      = DelimitedCodec.encodeU64 p.val.size ++ DelimitedCodec.encodeList p.val.toList

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.toList_val_eq_ofFn
items.doc: The coefficient list of a polynomial is its coefficient function on `Fin p.val.size`.
items.statement:
theorem toList_val_eq_ofFn (p : CPolynomial R) :
    p.val.toList = List.ofFn fun i : Fin p.val.size => coeff p i

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.encode_eq_encodeU64_append_toBytes
items.doc:
The self-delimiting encoding is the count followed by the fixed-width encoding at
`n = size`: the two formats agree on their common part.
items.statement:
theorem encode_eq_encodeU64_append_toBytes [ByteCodec R] (p : CPolynomial R) :
    DelimitedCodec.encode p
      = DelimitedCodec.encodeU64 p.val.size
        ++ (ByteCodec.toBytes (⟨p, mem_degreeLT_iff_size_le.mpr le_rfl⟩ :
            ↥(degreeLT (R := R) p.val.size))).toList

modules.title: Equivalence between `CPolynomial` and `CMvPolynomial 1`
modules.doc:
This file establishes the ring equivalence
`CPolynomial.cmvEquiv : CPolynomial R ≃+* CMvPolynomial 1 R`.

The equivalence chain is:
  `CPolynomial R ≃ R[X] ≃ (CMvPolynomial 0 R)[X] ≃ CMvPolynomial 1 R`

The bridge lemmas expose how the inverse equivalence interacts with evaluation
and degree, so one-variable results proved for `CPolynomial` can be transported
to callers that still use `CMvPolynomial 1`.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.cmvEquiv
items.doc:
Ring equivalence between computable univariate polynomials and
single-variable computable multivariate polynomials.
items.statement:
noncomputable def cmvEquiv
    [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] :
    CPolynomial R ≃+* CMvPolynomial 1 R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.eval_cmvEquiv_symm
items.doc:
Evaluation after converting a single-variable `CMvPolynomial` back to
`CPolynomial` agrees with multivariate evaluation at the constant assignment.
items.statement:
theorem eval_cmvEquiv_symm
    [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R]
    (p : CMvPolynomial 1 R) (x : R) :
    ((cmvEquiv (R := R)).symm p).eval x = p.eval (fun _ ↦ x)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.natDegree_cmvEquiv_symm_sub
items.doc: Degree transport for differences through the inverse of `cmvEquiv`.
items.statement:
theorem natDegree_cmvEquiv_symm_sub
    [CommRing R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R]
    (p q : CMvPolynomial 1 R) :
    (((cmvEquiv (R := R)).symm p - (cmvEquiv (R := R)).symm q).natDegree) =
      (fromCMvPolynomial p - fromCMvPolynomial q).degreeOf 0

modules.doc:
Build the coefficient polynomial interpolating packed points from the node
vanishing polynomial `G = ∏ᵢ (X - xᵢ)` using the formula
`R = ∑ᵢ yᵢ / G'(xᵢ) * G / (X - xᵢ)`.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.divByLinearFactor
items.doc:
Synthetic quotient by the monic linear factor `X - x`.

This is the quotient part of division by `X - x`, computed in one high-to-low
coefficient pass. When `x` is a root of `p`, it is exactly `p / (X - x)`.
items.statement: def divByLinearFactor (p : CPolynomial F) (x : F) : CPolynomial F

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.divByLinearFactor_eq_divByMonic
items.doc: Synthetic division by `X - x` agrees with generic monic division.
items.statement:
theorem divByLinearFactor_eq_divByMonic (p : CPolynomial F) (x : F) :
    divByLinearFactor p x = p.divByMonic (linearFactor x)

items.doc:
Coefficient-form interpolation from packed points using a vanishing-polynomial
context and a batch-evaluation context.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.interpolateCoefficientForm_eval_point
items.doc: Coefficient-form interpolation evaluates to the packed values at distinct nodes.
items.statement:
theorem interpolateCoefficientForm_eval_point [DecidableEq F]
    (V : CPolynomial.VanishingPolynomialContext F)
    (E : CPolynomial.BatchEvalContext F)
    {points : Array (F × F)}
    (hdistinct : (points.toList.map fun point ↦ point.1).Nodup)
    {point : F × F} (hpoint : point ∈ points.toList) :
    CPolynomial.eval point.1 (CPolynomial.interpolateCoefficientForm V E points) =
      point.2

modules.title: Univariate Algorithm Contexts
modules.doc:
Algorithm dictionaries for reusable univariate polynomial operations, including
canonical, NTT, and NTTFast-backed implementations.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.MulContext
items.doc: Explicit multiplication backend for univariate polynomial algorithms.
items.statement:
structure MulContext (R : Type*) [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] where
  /-- Multiply two canonical polynomials. -/
  mul : CPolynomial R → CPolynomial R → CPolynomial R
  /-- The backend agrees with canonical polynomial multiplication. -/
  mul_eq_mul : ∀ p q, mul p q = p * q

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.ModContext
items.doc: Explicit remainder backend for algorithms that only need reduction modulo monic divisors.
items.statement:
structure ModContext (R : Type*) [Field R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] where
  /-- Reduce the first polynomial modulo the second, assuming the divisor is monic. -/
  modByMonic : CPolynomial R → CPolynomial R → CPolynomial R
  /-- The backend agrees with the canonical monic-remainder operation. -/
  modByMonic_eq_modByMonic : ∀ p q, modByMonic p q = CPolynomial.modByMonic p q

modules.title: Formal Derivative and Taylor Shift of Computable Univariate Polynomials
modules.doc:
Defines the formal derivative `CPolynomial.derivative` and the Taylor shift
`CPolynomial.taylor`, with proofs of their core properties.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.derivative
items.doc:
The formal derivative of a computable polynomial.
Coefficient `n` of the result is `coeff p (n+1) * (n+1)`.
items.statement:
def derivative [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (p : CPolynomial R) : CPolynomial R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.coeff_derivative
items.doc: Coefficient formula for the derivative.
items.statement:
theorem coeff_derivative [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (p : CPolynomial R) (n : ℕ) :
    coeff (derivative p) n = coeff p (n + 1) * (↑(n + 1) : R)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.derivative_zero
items.doc: The derivative of the zero polynomial is zero.
items.statement:
theorem derivative_zero [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] :
    derivative (0 : CPolynomial R) = 0

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.derivative_C
items.doc: The derivative of a constant is zero.
items.statement:
theorem derivative_C [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (r : R) :
    derivative (C r) = 0

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.derivative_monomial
items.doc: The derivative of a monomial.
items.statement:
theorem derivative_monomial [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    [DecidableEq R] (n : ℕ) (r : R) :
    derivative (monomial n r) =
      monomial (n - 1) (r * (↑n : R))

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.derivative_add
items.doc: The derivative distributes over addition.
items.statement:
theorem derivative_add [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [DecidableEq R]
    (p q : CPolynomial R) :
    derivative (p + q) = derivative p + derivative q

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.derivative_toPoly
items.doc: The computable derivative matches Mathlib's `Polynomial.derivative` under `toPoly`.
items.statement:
theorem derivative_toPoly [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (p : CPolynomial R) :
    (derivative p).toPoly = Polynomial.derivative (R := R) p.toPoly

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.derivative_mul
items.doc: The derivative satisfies the Leibniz product rule.
items.statement:
theorem derivative_mul [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] (p q : CPolynomial R) :
    derivative (p * q) = derivative p * q + p * derivative q

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.taylor
items.doc: The Taylor shift `taylor a p = p(X + a)`.
items.statement:
def taylor [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (a : R) (p : CPolynomial R) : CPolynomial R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.taylor_toPoly
items.doc: The computable Taylor shift matches `Polynomial.taylor` under `toPoly`.
items.statement:
theorem taylor_toPoly [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (a : R) (p : CPolynomial R) :
    (taylor a p).toPoly = Polynomial.taylor a p.toPoly

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.taylor_zero
items.doc: The Taylor shift of zero is zero.
items.statement:
theorem taylor_zero [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (a : R) : taylor a (0 : CPolynomial R) = 0

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.taylor_coeff_zero
items.doc: The constant coefficient of the Taylor shift is evaluation at the shift point.
items.statement:
theorem taylor_coeff_zero [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] [DecidableEq R]
    (a : R) (p : CPolynomial R) : coeff (taylor a p) 0 = eval a p

modules.title: Univariate Division Correctness
modules.doc: Correctness theorems for division-style univariate polynomial algorithms.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.divByMonic_toPoly_eq_divByMonic
items.doc: CompPoly's `divByMonic` is correct w.r.t. Mathlib's `divByMonic`
items.statement:
theorem divByMonic_toPoly_eq_divByMonic (p q : CPolynomial R)
    (hmonic : q.monic) :
    (p.divByMonic q).toPoly = p.toPoly /ₘ q.toPoly

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.modByMonic_toPoly_eq_modByMonic
items.doc: CompPoly's `modByMonic` is correct w.r.t. Mathlib's `modByMonic`
items.statement:
theorem modByMonic_toPoly_eq_modByMonic (p q : CPolynomial R)
    (hmonic : q.monic) :
    (p.modByMonic q).toPoly = p.toPoly %ₘ q.toPoly

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.modByMonic_add_mul_divByMonic
items.doc:
Euclidean division identity for a monic divisor, stated directly on
`CPolynomial`: `p.modByMonic q + q * p.divByMonic q = p` whenever `q` is monic.

This holds over an arbitrary commutative ring, so it
instantiates at nested coefficient rings, e.g. `CBivariate R =
CPolynomial (CPolynomial R)`, giving Euclidean division by any monic divisor in
the outer variable.
items.statement:
theorem modByMonic_add_mul_divByMonic (p q : CPolynomial R) (hmonic : q.monic) :
    p.modByMonic q + q * p.divByMonic q = p

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.leadingCoeff_inv_smul_monic
items.doc:
Any nonzero polynomial scaled by the inverse of its leading
coefficient is monic.
items.statement:
theorem leadingCoeff_inv_smul_monic (p : CPolynomial R) (hp : p ≠ 0) :
    (p.leadingCoeff⁻¹ • p).monic

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.div_toPoly_eq_divByMonic
items.doc: Equality between CompPoly's `div` and Mathlib's `divByMonic`
items.statement:
theorem div_toPoly_eq_divByMonic (p q : CPolynomial R) (hq : q ≠ 0) :
    (p.div q).toPoly =
      q.leadingCoeff⁻¹ • p.toPoly /ₘ (q.leadingCoeff⁻¹ • q.toPoly)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.mod_toPoly_eq_modByMonic
items.doc: Equality between CompPoly's `mod` and Mathlib's `modByMonic`
items.statement:
theorem mod_toPoly_eq_modByMonic (p q : CPolynomial R) (hq : q ≠ 0) :
    (p.mod q).toPoly =
      q.leadingCoeff⁻¹ • p.toPoly %ₘ (q.leadingCoeff⁻¹ • q.toPoly)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.div_toPoly_eq_div
items.doc: CompPoly's `div` is correct w.r.t. Mathlib's `div`.
items.statement:
theorem div_toPoly_eq_div (p q : CPolynomial R) :
    (p.div q).toPoly = p.toPoly / q.toPoly

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.mod_toPoly_eq_smul_mod
items.doc: CompPoly's `mod` is Mathlib's `%` scaled by `q.leadingCoeff⁻¹`.
items.statement:
theorem mod_toPoly_eq_smul_mod (p q : CPolynomial R) :
    (p.mod q).toPoly = q.leadingCoeff⁻¹ • (p.toPoly % q.toPoly)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.exactDiv_toPoly_iff
items.doc:
Exact-division bridge: `G.toPoly` factors as `f.toPoly * V.toPoly` iff the computable
`mod` vanishes and the computable division recovers `f`.
items.statement:
theorem exactDiv_toPoly_iff (G V f : CPolynomial R) (hV : V.toPoly ≠ 0) :
    G.toPoly = f.toPoly * V.toPoly ↔ G.mod V = 0 ∧ (G / V).toPoly = f.toPoly

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.modByMonicByReversal_eq_modByMonic
items.doc: The reversal monic remainder agrees with the canonical monic remainder.
items.statement:
theorem modByMonicByReversal_eq_modByMonic
    (M : Raw.MulLowContext R) (p q : CPolynomial R) :
    modByMonicByReversal M p q = modByMonic p q

modules.title: Extended Euclidean Algorithm for `CPolynomial`
modules.doc:
`xgcd p q` returns a triple `(r, s, t)` with `r = s * p + t * q`.
Early stop when `r.natDegree < threshold`.
The default `threshold = 0` makes `r` the Greatest Common Divisor of `p` and `q`.

For positive thresholds, `xgcd_stopSpec` characterizes the output: `BezoutStopSpec` packages
the Bézout identity together with the residue/cofactor degree bounds at the stopping point,
via the loop invariant `BezoutDegreeInvariant`.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.xgcdAux
items.doc:
Extended euclidean algorithm on `p, q`.

Stops when `r.natDegree < threshold`, `r = 0`, or fuel `n` exhausted.

If `threshold > 0` then `xgcdAux` need not compute the greatest common divisor.

Potential optimization: the raw long division behind `r' / r` already computes
`r' - (r' / r) * r` but it's not exposed through `CPolynomial R`.
items.statement:
def xgcdAux [Field R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (threshold n : ℕ) (r s t r' s' t' : CPolynomial R) :
    CPolynomial R × CPolynomial R × CPolynomial R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.xgcd
items.doc:
Extended euclidean algorithm for `(p, q)`.

Returns `(r, s, t)` with `r = s * p + t * q`.

With the default `threshold = 0` returns the gcd of `p` and `q`.
With `threshold > 0` stops when `r.natDegree < threshold`.

If `threshold > 0` then `xgcdAux` need not compute the greatest common divisor.
items.statement:
def xgcd [Field R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (p q : CPolynomial R) (threshold : ℕ := 0) :
    CPolynomial R × CPolynomial R × CPolynomial R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Bezout
items.doc: Bezout predicate on a triple `(r, s, t)`: `r = s * p + t * q`.
items.statement:
def Bezout [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (p q : CPolynomial R) :
    CPolynomial R × CPolynomial R × CPolynomial R → Prop

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.xgcdAux_bezout
items.doc: `xgcdAux` preserves the Bezout identity.
items.statement:
theorem xgcdAux_bezout [Field R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (p q : CPolynomial R) (threshold n : ℕ)
    {r r' : CPolynomial R} {s t s' t'}
    (h : Bezout p q (r, s, t)) (h' : Bezout p q (r', s', t')) :
    Bezout p q (xgcdAux threshold n r s t r' s' t')

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.xgcd_bezout
items.doc: The output of `xgcd` is a Bezout triple for `(p, q)`.
items.statement:
theorem xgcd_bezout [Field R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (p q : CPolynomial R) (threshold : ℕ) :
    Bezout p q (xgcd p q threshold)

items.note:
# `xgcd` correctness (threshold 0)

Correctness theorems for `xgcd` with the default threshold 0.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.xgcdAux_toPoly_eq_gcd
items.doc:
The gcd component of CompPoly's `xgcdAux` at threshold `0` coincides with
Mathlib's `EuclideanDomain.gcd`.
items.statement:
lemma xgcdAux_toPoly_eq_gcd
    [Field R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [DecidableEq R]
    (n : ℕ) (r r' s t s' t' : CPolynomial R)
    (hn : r.toPoly.degree < n) :
    (xgcdAux 0 n r s t r' s' t').1.toPoly =
      EuclideanDomain.gcd r.toPoly r'.toPoly

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.xgcd_toPoly_eq_gcd
items.doc:
The gcd component of CompPoly's `xgcd` at threshold `0`
coincides with Mathlib's `EuclideanDomain.gcd`.
items.statement:
theorem xgcd_toPoly_eq_gcd [Field R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [DecidableEq R] (p q : CPolynomial R) :
    (xgcd p q).1.toPoly = EuclideanDomain.gcd p.toPoly q.toPoly

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.xgcdAux_toPoly_eq_xgcdAux
items.doc:
CompPoly's `xgcdAux` at threshold `0` coincides with
Mathlib's `EuclideanDomain.xgcdAux`.
items.statement:
lemma xgcdAux_toPoly_eq_xgcdAux
    [Field R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [DecidableEq R]
    (n : ℕ) (r s t r' s' t' : CPolynomial R)
    (hn : r.toPoly.degree < n) :
    Prod.map (·.toPoly) (·.map (·.toPoly) (·.toPoly))
      (xgcdAux 0 n r s t r' s' t') =
      EuclideanDomain.xgcdAux r.toPoly s.toPoly t.toPoly r'.toPoly s'.toPoly t'.toPoly

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.xgcd_toPoly_eq_xgcd
items.doc:
The Bezout component of CompPoly's `xgcd` coincides with
Mathlib's `EuclideanDomain.xgcd`.
items.statement:
theorem xgcd_toPoly_eq_xgcd
    [Field R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [DecidableEq R]
    (p q : CPolynomial R) :
    (xgcd p q).2.map (·.toPoly) (·.toPoly) =
      EuclideanDomain.xgcd p.toPoly q.toPoly

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.normXgcd
items.doc:
CompPoly's `xgcd p q` scaled by the inverse leading coefficient
of the gcd component, normalizing it to monic.
items.statement:
def normXgcd [Field R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (p q : CPolynomial R) (threshold : ℕ := 0) :
    CPolynomial R × CPolynomial R × CPolynomial R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.normXgcd_bezout
items.doc: The normalized extended-gcd output satisfies the Bezout identity.
items.statement:
theorem normXgcd_bezout [Field R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (p q : CPolynomial R) (threshold : ℕ) :
    Bezout p q (normXgcd p q threshold)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.normXgcd_fst_toPoly
items.doc:
The gcd component of CompPoly's `normXgcd` is the normalization
of Mathlib's `EuclideanDomain.gcd`
items.statement:
theorem normXgcd_fst_toPoly
    [Field R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [DecidableEq R]
    (p q : CPolynomial R) :
    (normXgcd p q).1.toPoly = normalize (EuclideanDomain.gcd p.toPoly q.toPoly)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.monicNormalize_toPoly_eq_normalize
items.doc: Monic normalization of computable polynomials agrees with Mathlib normalization.
items.statement:
theorem monicNormalize_toPoly_eq_normalize
    [Field R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [DecidableEq R]
    (p : CPolynomial R) :
    (CPolynomial.monicNormalize p).toPoly = normalize p.toPoly

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.gcdMonic_toPoly_eq_normalize_gcd
items.doc:
The specialized monic gcd has the normalized Mathlib gcd as its `toPoly`
image.
items.statement:
theorem gcdMonic_toPoly_eq_normalize_gcd
    [Field R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [DecidableEq R]
    (p q : CPolynomial R) :
    (CPolynomial.gcdMonic p q).toPoly =
      normalize (EuclideanDomain.gcd p.toPoly q.toPoly)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.gcdMonic_eq_normXgcd_fst
items.doc:
The specialized monic gcd agrees with the gcd component of normalized
extended gcd.
items.statement:
theorem gcdMonic_eq_normXgcd_fst
    [Field R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [DecidableEq R]
    (p q : CPolynomial R) :
    CPolynomial.gcdMonic p q = (CPolynomial.normXgcd p q).1

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.normXgcd_snd_toPoly
items.doc:
The Bezout component of `normXgcd` under `toPoly` is Mathlib's
`EuclideanDomain.xgcd` scaled by the inverse leading coefficient
of the gcd
items.statement:
theorem normXgcd_snd_toPoly
    [Field R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [DecidableEq R]
    (p q : CPolynomial R) :
    (normXgcd p q).2.map (·.toPoly) (·.toPoly) =
      (EuclideanDomain.gcd p.toPoly q.toPoly).leadingCoeff⁻¹ •
        EuclideanDomain.xgcd p.toPoly q.toPoly

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.normXgcd_fst_comm
items.doc: `normXgcd` is commutative for the gcd component
items.statement:
theorem normXgcd_fst_comm
    [Field R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [DecidableEq R]
    (p q : CPolynomial R) :
    (normXgcd p q).1 = (normXgcd q p).1

items.note:
## Stop specification for positive thresholds

`BezoutDegreeInvariant` is the invariant of the partial-EEA (`xgcd`) loop: each non-stop
step preserves it (`BezoutDegreeInvariant.step`), and at the stopping threshold it yields
the output specification `BezoutStopSpec` (`xgcd_stopSpec`).

This is the classical degree theory of the extended Euclidean algorithm — the row identity
`deg t + deg r' = deg g₀` and the complementary cofactor bound at the stop — i.e. the
contract behind rational-function reconstruction and Reed-Solomon decoding.

items.name: CompPoly.BezoutDegreeInvariant
items.doc: Loop invariant of one partial-EEA (`xgcd`) step.
items.statement:
structure BezoutDegreeInvariant [Ring F] (g₀ g₁ : F[X]) (threshold : ℕ)
    (r s t r' s' t' : F[X]) : Prop where
  bez : r = s * g₀ + t * g₁
  bez' : r' = s' * g₀ + t' * g₁
  det : IsUnit (s' * t - s * t')
  degt : t'.degree < t.degree
  degr : r.degree < r'.degree
  thr : threshold ≤ r'.degree

items.name: CompPoly.BezoutDegreeInvariantOf
items.doc:
`BezoutDegreeInvariant` on the `toPoly` images of a `CPolynomial` reference pair `g₀, g₁` and
the two state triples `(r, s, t)`, `(r', s', t')`.
items.statement:
abbrev BezoutDegreeInvariantOf [Ring F] (g₀ g₁ : CPolynomial F) (threshold : ℕ)
    (r s t r' s' t' : CPolynomial F) : Prop

items.name: CompPoly.BezoutDegreeInvariant.degree_complement
items.doc: `BezoutDegreeInvariant` implies `deg t + deg r' = deg g₀`.
items.statement:
lemma BezoutDegreeInvariant.degree_complement [CommRing F] [NoZeroDivisors F] [Nontrivial F]
    {g₀ g₁ : F[X]} {threshold : ℕ} {r s t r' s' t' : F[X]}
    (h : BezoutDegreeInvariant g₀ g₁ threshold r s t r' s' t') :
    t.degree + r'.degree = g₀.degree

items.name: CompPoly.BezoutDegreeInvariant.step
items.doc: A non-stop Euclidean step preserves the invariant.
items.statement:
lemma BezoutDegreeInvariant.step [Field F]
    {g₀ g₁ : F[X]} {threshold : ℕ} {r s t r' s' t' : F[X]}
    (h : BezoutDegreeInvariant g₀ g₁ threshold r s t r' s' t') (hr : r ≠ 0)
    (hstop : ¬ r.natDegree < threshold) :
    BezoutDegreeInvariant
      g₀ g₁ threshold (r' - r' / r * r) (s' - r' / r * s) (t' - r' / r * t) r s t

items.name: CompPoly.BezoutStopSpec
items.doc:
Stop spec of the partial EEA: `R = S g₀ + T g₁`, residue degree below `threshold`,
and the cofactor `T` nonzero with complementary degree `deg T + threshold ≤ deg g₀`.
items.statement:
structure BezoutStopSpec [Semiring F] (g₀ g₁ : F[X]) (threshold : ℕ) (R S T : F[X]) : Prop where
  bez : R = S * g₀ + T * g₁
  resDeg : R.natDegree < threshold
  cofDeg : T.degree + threshold ≤ g₀.degree
  cofNe : T ≠ 0

items.name: CompPoly.BezoutStopSpecOf
items.doc:
`BezoutStopSpec` on the `toPoly` images of a `CPolynomial` reference pair `g₀, g₁` and
result triple.
items.statement:
abbrev BezoutStopSpecOf [Semiring F] (g₀ g₁ : CPolynomial F) (threshold : ℕ)
    (result : CPolynomial F × CPolynomial F × CPolynomial F) : Prop

items.name: CompPoly.xgcdAux_stopSpec_of_invariant
items.doc: `BezoutDegreeInvariant` implies `xgcdAux`'s output satisfies the stop spec.
items.statement:
lemma xgcdAux_stopSpec_of_invariant
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F] (g₀ g₁ : CPolynomial F) (threshold : ℕ) (hthr : 1 ≤ threshold)
    (hg₀ : g₀.toPoly ≠ 0) :
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (r s t r' s' t' : CPolynomial F),
      BezoutDegreeInvariantOf g₀ g₁ threshold r s t r' s' t' →
      r.natDegree < n →
      BezoutStopSpecOf g₀ g₁ threshold (xgcdAux threshold n r s t r' s' t')

items.name: CompPoly.xgcd_stopSpec
items.doc: `xgcd`'s output satisfies the stop spec.
items.statement:
lemma xgcd_stopSpec
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F] (g₀ g₁ : CPolynomial F) (threshold : ℕ)
    (hdeg : g₁.degree < g₀.degree)
    (hthr : 1 ≤ threshold) (hthr' : threshold ≤ g₀.degree) :
    BezoutStopSpecOf g₀ g₁ threshold (xgcd g₀ g₁ threshold)

modules.authors: Quang Dao, Gregor Mitscha-Baude, Derek Sorensen, Katerina Hristova, Julian Sutherland
modules.title: Lagrange Interpolation
modules.doc:
This file defines computable Lagrange interpolation
for univariate polynomials, i.e. `CPolynomial`s.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.CLagrange.basisDivisor
items.doc:
`basisDivisor xᵢ xⱼ` is the unique linear or constant computable polynomial such that
when evaluated at `xᵢ` it gives `1` and `xⱼ` it gives `0` (where when `xᵢ = xⱼ` it is
identically `0`). Such polynomials are the building blocks for the Lagrange interpolants.
items.statement: def basisDivisor (xᵢ xⱼ : R) : CPolynomial R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.CLagrange.cbasisDivisor_eq_basisDivisor
items.statement:
lemma cbasisDivisor_eq_basisDivisor {xᵢ xⱼ : R} :
    (basisDivisor xᵢ xⱼ).toPoly = Lagrange.basisDivisor xᵢ xⱼ

items.note:
### Helpers for deferred-trim folds

The `basis` product and `interpolate` sum below combine raw arrays with the untrimmed
`Raw.mulRaw`/`Raw.addRaw` and trim once at the end, rather than paying a trim per factor
(as `Finset.prod`/`Finset.sum` over the canonical `CPolynomial.Mul`/`.Add` instances
would). Computability requires bypassing the noncomputable `Finset.toList`, so the folds
go through `Quotient.liftOn` on the underlying multiset with a permutation-invariance
proof routed through `toPoly`.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.CLagrange.basisListRaw
items.doc:
`basisDivisor`-product fold over a list, combining factors with the untrimmed
`Raw.mulRaw`. The wrapping `basis` definition trims this once.
items.statement:
def basisListRaw {ι : Type*} (x : ι → R) (i : ι) (l : List ι) :
    CPolynomial.Raw R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.CLagrange.basisListRaw_trim_perm
items.statement:
lemma basisListRaw_trim_perm {ι : Type*} (x : ι → R) (i : ι)
    {l₁ l₂ : List ι} (h : l₁.Perm l₂) :
    (basisListRaw x i l₁).trim = (basisListRaw x i l₂).trim

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.CLagrange.basis
items.doc:
Computable Lagrange basis polynomials indexed by `s : Finset ι`, defined at nodes `x i` for a
map `x : ι → F`. For `i, j ∈ s`, `basis s x i` evaluates to `0` at `x j` for `i ≠ j`. When
`x` is injective on `s`, `basis s x i` evaluates to 1 at `x i`.

The product folds `(s.erase i).val` with the untrimmed `Raw.mulRaw` via `Quotient.liftOn`
and trims once at the end, rather than paying one `Raw.mul` trim per factor (as the
`Finset.prod` formulation would).
items.statement:
def basis {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] (s : Finset ι) (x : ι → R) (i : ι) :
    CPolynomial R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.CLagrange.cbasis_eq_basis
items.statement:
lemma cbasis_eq_basis {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] (s : Finset ι) (x : ι → R) (i : ι) :
    (basis s x i).toPoly = Lagrange.basis s x i

items.note:
### Interpolation sum

The `interpolate` sum is folded with the untrimmed `Raw.addRaw`, with each addend itself
formed by `Raw.mulRaw (Raw.C (y i)) (basis s x i).val` (also untrimmed). One `trim` runs
at the end of the entire fold.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.CLagrange.interpolateListRaw
items.statement:
def interpolateListRaw {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι]
    (s : Finset ι) (x : ι → R) (y : ι → R) (l : List ι) : CPolynomial.Raw R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.CLagrange.interpolateListRaw_trim_perm
items.statement:
lemma interpolateListRaw_trim_perm {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι]
    (s : Finset ι) (x : ι → R) (y : ι → R) {l₁ l₂ : List ι} (h : l₁.Perm l₂) :
    (interpolateListRaw s x y l₁).trim = (interpolateListRaw s x y l₂).trim

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.CLagrange.interpolateRaw
items.doc:
Computable raw-fold form of the interpolation polynomial: defer trimming to the
end of the `Finset.sum`.
items.statement:
def interpolateRaw {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι]
    (s : Finset ι) (x : ι → R) (y : ι → R) : CPolynomial R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.CLagrange.interpolate
items.doc:
Computable Lagrange interpolation: given a finset `s : Finset ι`, a nodal map `x : ι → F`
injective on `s` and a value function `y : ι → F`, `interpolate s x y` is the unique computable
polynomial of degree `< #s` that takes value `y i` on `x i` for all `i` in `s`.
items.statement:
def interpolate {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] (s : Finset ι) (x : ι → R) :
    (ι → R) →ₗ[R] CPolynomial R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.CLagrange.cinterpolate_eq_interpolate
items.statement:
lemma cinterpolate_eq_interpolate
    {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {s : Finset ι} {x : ι → R} {y : ι → R} :
      (interpolate s x y).toPoly = Lagrange.interpolate s x y

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.CLagrange.interpolatePow
items.doc:
Produces the unique polynomial of degree at most n-1 that equals r[i] at ω^i
for i = 0, 1, ..., n-1.

Uses Lagrange interpolation: p(X) = Σᵢ rᵢ · Lᵢ(X)
where Lᵢ(X) = ∏_{j≠i} (X - ωʲ) / (ωⁱ - ωʲ).
items.statement:
def interpolatePow {n : ℕ} (ω : R) (r : Vector R n) :
    CPolynomial R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.CLagrange.eq_of_pow_eq_pow_of_lt_orderOf
items.statement:
theorem eq_of_pow_eq_pow_of_lt_orderOf {G : Type*} [Group G] {ω : G} {n : ℕ}
    (h_order : n ≤ orderOf ω) (a b : Fin n) (h_pow : ω ^ (a : ℕ) = ω ^ (b : ℕ)) : a = b

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.CLagrange.eval_interpolatePow_at_node
items.doc: Key correctness theorem for `interpolatePow`.
items.statement:
lemma eval_interpolatePow_at_node {n : ℕ} {ω : Rˣ} {r : Vector R n} : n ≤ orderOf ω →
    ∀ i : Fin n, (interpolatePow ω.1 r).eval (ω.1 ^ i.1) = r.get i

modules.title: Array Wrappers for Computable Lagrange Interpolation
modules.doc: Finite-index adapters for `CPolynomial.CLagrange.interpolate`.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.CLagrange.arrayNode
items.doc: The `i`th node in an array, exposed through a `Fin` index.
items.statement: def arrayNode (xs : Array F) (i : Fin xs.size) : F

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.CLagrange.arrayValue
items.doc: The `i`th value in an array, defaulting only when the value array is shorter.
items.statement: def arrayValue (ys : Array F) {n : Nat} (i : Fin n) : F

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.CLagrange.interpolateArrays
items.doc: Lagrange interpolation from separate node and value arrays.
items.statement: def interpolateArrays (xs ys : Array F) : CPolynomial F

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.CLagrange.pointNode
items.doc: The `x` coordinate of the `i`th packed point.
items.statement: def pointNode (points : Array (F × F)) (i : Fin points.size) : F

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.CLagrange.pointValue
items.doc: The `y` coordinate of the `i`th packed point.
items.statement: def pointValue (points : Array (F × F)) (i : Fin points.size) : F

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.CLagrange.interpolateArray
items.doc: Lagrange interpolation from packed `(x, y)` points.
items.statement: def interpolateArray (points : Array (F × F)) : CPolynomial F

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.CLagrange.DistinctPointNodes
items.doc: Packed points have pairwise distinct Lagrange nodes.
items.statement: def DistinctPointNodes (points : Array (F × F)) : Prop

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.CLagrange.eval_interpolateArray_at_index
items.doc: Evaluating the packed-array interpolant at one indexed node returns the indexed value.
items.statement:
theorem eval_interpolateArray_at_index
    (points : Array (F × F)) (hdistinct : DistinctPointNodes points)
    (i : Fin points.size) :
    CPolynomial.eval (pointNode points i) (interpolateArray points) =
      pointValue points i

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.CLagrange.eval_interpolateArray_at_mem
items.doc: Evaluating the packed-array interpolant at a listed point returns that point's value.
items.statement:
theorem eval_interpolateArray_at_mem
    (points : Array (F × F)) (hdistinct : DistinctPointNodes points)
    {point : F × F} (hpoint : point ∈ points.toList) :
    CPolynomial.eval point.1 (interpolateArray points) = point.2

modules.authors: Desmond Coles, Derek Sorensen, Alexander Hicks
modules.title: Linear Algebra API for Computable Univariate Polynomials
modules.doc:
This file defines coefficient linear maps and bounded-degree subtypes for `CPolynomial`.
The subtypes depend only on `Zero R`.

`ofFnEquiv n` identifies the coefficient vectors `Fin n → R` with the polynomials of degree below
`n`. Over a finite coefficient type, it gives the executable enumeration `instFintypeDegreeLT`.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.lcoeff
items.doc: This is an R-linear function that returns the coefficient of X^n.
items.statement: def lcoeff (n : ℕ) : (CPolynomial R) →ₗ[R] R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.lcoeff_apply
items.doc: Applying `lcoeff n` returns the coefficient of degree `n`.
items.statement: theorem lcoeff_apply (n : ℕ) (p : CPolynomial R) : lcoeff n p = coeff p n

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.degreeLE
items.doc: The set of `CPolynomial R` consisting of polynomials of degree ≤ `n`.
items.statement: def degreeLE (n : WithBot ℕ) : Set (CPolynomial R)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.degreeLT
items.doc: The set of `CPolynomial R` consisting of polynomials of degree < `n`.
items.statement: def degreeLT (n : ℕ) : Set (CPolynomial R)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.mem_degreeLE
items.doc: Membership in `degreeLE` is the corresponding degree bound.
items.statement:
theorem mem_degreeLE {n : WithBot ℕ} {p : CPolynomial R} :
    p ∈ degreeLE (R := R) n ↔ p.degree ≤ n

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.mem_degreeLT
items.doc: Membership in `degreeLT` is the corresponding strict degree bound.
items.statement:
theorem mem_degreeLT {n : ℕ} {p : CPolynomial R} :
    p ∈ degreeLT (R := R) n ↔ p.degree < n

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.mem_degreeLT_iff_size_le
items.doc: `degreeLT n` is exactly the bounded-size carrier storing at most `n` coefficients.
items.statement:
theorem mem_degreeLT_iff_size_le {n : ℕ} {p : CPolynomial R} :
    p ∈ degreeLT (R := R) n ↔ p.val.size ≤ n

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.zero_mem_degreeLT
items.doc: The zero polynomial has bounded degree for every cutoff.
items.statement: theorem zero_mem_degreeLT (n : ℕ) : (0 : CPolynomial R) ∈ degreeLT (R := R) n

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.ofFn_mem_degreeLT
items.doc: `ofFn` on `n` coefficients has degree below `n`.
items.statement: theorem ofFn_mem_degreeLT {n : ℕ} (f : Fin n → R) : ofFn f ∈ degreeLT (R := R) n

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.ofFn_coeff_of_mem_degreeLT
items.doc: A polynomial of degree below `n` is `ofFn` of its first `n` coefficients.
items.statement:
theorem ofFn_coeff_of_mem_degreeLT {n : ℕ} {p : CPolynomial R} (hp : p ∈ degreeLT (R := R) n) :
    ofFn (fun i : Fin n => coeff p i) = p

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.ofFnEquiv
items.doc:
`ofFnEquiv n` is the equivalence, through `ofFn`, from the coefficient vectors `Fin n → R` to
the polynomials of degree below `n`. Its inverse reads the first `n` coefficients. Both directions
are executable.
items.statement: def ofFnEquiv (n : ℕ) : (Fin n → R) ≃ ↥(degreeLT (R := R) n)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.ofFnEquiv_apply_val
items.doc: The polynomial that `ofFnEquiv n` assigns to `f` is `ofFn f`.
items.statement: theorem ofFnEquiv_apply_val (n : ℕ) (f : Fin n → R) : (ofFnEquiv n f).val = ofFn f

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.ofFnEquiv_symm_apply
items.doc: The inverse of `ofFnEquiv n` reads the first `n` coefficients.
items.statement:
theorem ofFnEquiv_symm_apply (n : ℕ) (p : ↥(degreeLT (R := R) n)) (i : Fin n) :
    (ofFnEquiv n).symm p i = p.val.coeff i

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.instFintypeDegreeLT
items.doc:
Over a finite coefficient type, the polynomials of degree below `n` form a finite type.

The enumeration converts each coefficient function `Fin n → R` to a polynomial with `ofFn`.
At `n = 0` it lists only the zero polynomial.

Downstream `by decide` can count small concrete enumerations. Use compiled evaluation such as
`#guard` to test predicates that inspect the polynomials. For proofs about such searches, use the
quantifier lemmas in `CompPoly.Univariate.ToPoly.Degree`.

The enumeration uses `BEq R` to trim trailing zeros. When the `BEq R` instance changes,
the subtype stays definitionally equal, but its enumerations may require a proof of equality.
`card_degreeLT` applies to any enumeration.
items.statement: instance instFintypeDegreeLT [Fintype R] (n : ℕ) : Fintype ↥(degreeLT (R := R) n)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.card_degreeLT
items.doc:
Over a finite coefficient type, there are `card R ^ n` polynomials of degree below `n`.
The statement holds for every `Fintype` instance on `↥(degreeLT n)`.
items.statement:
theorem card_degreeLT [Zero R] [Fintype R] (n : ℕ) [Fintype ↥(degreeLT (R := R) n)] :
    Fintype.card ↥(degreeLT (R := R) n) = Fintype.card R ^ n

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.add_mem_degreeLT
items.doc: `degreeLT n` is closed under addition.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.nsmul_mem_degreeLT
items.doc: `degreeLT n` is closed under additive scalar multiplication.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.smul_mem_degreeLT
items.doc: `degreeLT n` is closed under semiring scalar multiplication.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.degreeLTCoeffs
items.doc: The first `n` coefficients on `degreeLT n` form a computable linear map to `Fin n → R`.
items.statement: def degreeLTCoeffs (n : ℕ) : ↥(degreeLT (R := R) n) →ₗ[R] (Fin n → R)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.degreeLTCoeffs_apply
items.doc: Applying `degreeLTCoeffs` returns the corresponding bounded coefficient.
items.statement:
theorem degreeLTCoeffs_apply (n : ℕ) (p : ↥(degreeLT (R := R) n)) (i : Fin n) :
    degreeLTCoeffs n p i = coeff p.1 i

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.ofFnEquiv_symm_eq_degreeLTCoeffs
items.doc: The inverse of `ofFnEquiv` is the coefficient linear map.
items.statement:
theorem ofFnEquiv_symm_eq_degreeLTCoeffs (n : ℕ) :
    ((ofFnEquiv (R := R) n).symm : ↥(degreeLT (R := R) n) → (Fin n → R)) =
      degreeLTCoeffs n

modules.title: Barycentric Interpolation on an NTT Domain
modules.doc:
On the full group of `n`-th roots of unity the nodal polynomial is `Xⁿ - 1`, so the
barycentric weight of the node `ωⁱ` has the closed form `ωⁱ / n`. This file builds the
`BarycentricDomain` of an NTT domain from that formula, in `O(n)` field operations and one
inversion, rather than through the generic `O(n²)` product of `BarycentricDomain.mk'`.

## Main definitions

* `NTT.Domain.barycentric`: the barycentric domain of `D`, with weights `ωⁱ · n⁻¹`.

## Main results

* `NTT.Domain.nodal_eq_X_pow_sub_one`: the nodal polynomial of the domain is `Xⁿ - 1`.
* `NTT.Domain.nodalWeight_eq`: the barycentric weight of `ωⁱ` is `ωⁱ · n⁻¹`.
* `NTT.Domain.barycentric_eval_eq_interpolatePow_eval`: evaluating through the domain is
  evaluating `CLagrange.interpolatePow D.omega`.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Domain.node_injective
items.doc: The nodes of an NTT domain are pairwise distinct.
items.statement: theorem node_injective (D : Domain R) : Function.Injective D.node

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Domain.node_pow_n
items.doc: Every node of an NTT domain is an `n`-th root of unity.
items.statement: theorem node_pow_n (D : Domain R) (i : D.Idx) : D.node i ^ D.n = 1

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Domain.nodal_eq_X_pow_sub_one
items.doc: The nodal polynomial of an NTT domain is `Xⁿ - 1`.
items.statement:
theorem nodal_eq_X_pow_sub_one (D : Domain R) :
    Lagrange.nodal Finset.univ D.node = Polynomial.X ^ D.n - 1

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Domain.nodalWeight_eq
items.doc: The barycentric weight of the node `ωⁱ` of an NTT domain is `ωⁱ / n`.
items.statement:
theorem nodalWeight_eq (D : Domain R) (i : D.Idx) :
    Lagrange.nodalWeight Finset.univ D.node i = D.node i * D.nInv

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Domain.barycentric
items.doc: The barycentric domain of an NTT domain, with the closed-form weights `ωⁱ · n⁻¹`.
items.statement: def barycentric [DecidableEq R] (D : Domain R) : CLagrange.BarycentricDomain R D.n

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Domain.barycentric_nodes
items.statement:
theorem barycentric_nodes [DecidableEq R] (D : Domain R) (i : D.Idx) :
    D.barycentric.nodes i = D.node i

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Domain.barycentric_eval_eq_interpolatePow_eval
items.doc: Barycentric evaluation on an NTT domain is evaluation of `CLagrange.interpolatePow`.
items.statement:
theorem barycentric_eval_eq_interpolatePow_eval [DecidableEq R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (D : Domain R) (values : Vector R D.n) (z : R) :
    D.barycentric.eval values.get z =
      (CLagrange.interpolatePow D.omega values).eval z

modules.title: Coset NTT
modules.doc:
Evaluation and interpolation on a multiplicative coset `g·⟨ω⟩ = {g·ωᵏ}` of an NTT domain,
the shape of a STARK/FRI low-degree extension. Both reduce to the plain transform by
scaling coefficients: `p(g·x) = (∑ gʲ pⱼ xʲ)`, so evaluating `p` on the coset is the
forward NTT of `(gʲ pⱼ)ⱼ`, and interpolating on the coset is the inverse NTT followed by
scaling with `g⁻¹`.

## Main definitions

* `NTT.Coset.scale g m a`: the coefficient array `(gʲ · aⱼ)ⱼ<m`.
* `NTT.evalOnCoset D g p`: `p` evaluated at every coset node `g·ωᵏ`, in natural order.
* `NTT.Coset.forwardImpl`, `NTT.Coset.inverseImpl`: the coset transforms.
* `NTT.Coset.interpolate`: interpolation of natural-order values on the coset.

## Main results

* `NTT.Coset.eval_scale`: `(scale g m p).eval x = p.eval (g * x)` below the size bound.
* `NTT.Coset.forwardImpl_eq_evalOnCoset`: the coset forward transform evaluates on the coset.
* `NTT.Coset.inverseImpl_evalOnCoset_eq`: the coset inverse transform interpolates.
* `NTT.Coset.interpolate_eq_interpolate`: coset interpolation is Lagrange interpolation on
  the nodes `g·ωᵏ`.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.evalOnCoset
items.doc: Evaluate a raw polynomial at every coset node `g·ωᵏ`, in natural order.
items.statement: def evalOnCoset (D : Domain R) (g : R) (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) : Array R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.size_evalOnCoset
items.statement:
theorem size_evalOnCoset (D : Domain R) (g : R) (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) :
    (evalOnCoset D g p).size = D.n

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Coset.scale
items.doc: Scale the first `m` coefficients by powers of `g`: `(gʲ · aⱼ)ⱼ<m`.
items.statement: def scale (g : R) (m : Nat) (a : Array R) : CPolynomial.Raw R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Coset.size_scale
items.statement: theorem size_scale (g : R) (m : Nat) (a : Array R) : (scale g m a).size = m

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Coset.getD_scale
items.statement:
theorem getD_scale (g : R) (m : Nat) (a : Array R) (j : Nat) (hj : j < m) :
    (scale g m a).getD j 0 = g ^ j * a.getD j 0

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Coset.eval_eq_sum_fin
items.doc: A raw polynomial below degree `m` is the sum of its first `m` monomials.
items.statement:
theorem eval_eq_sum_fin (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) (m : Nat)
    (hdeg : p.toPoly.natDegree < m) (x : R) :
    p.eval x = ∑ j : Fin m, p.getD j 0 * x ^ (j : Nat)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Coset.natDegree_lt_of_size_le
items.doc: A raw polynomial of size at most `m > 0` has degree below `m`.
items.statement:
theorem natDegree_lt_of_size_le (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) {m : Nat} (hm : 0 < m)
    (hsize : p.size ≤ m) : p.toPoly.natDegree < m

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Coset.eval_scale
items.doc: Scaling coefficients by powers of `g` composes the polynomial with `x ↦ g·x`.
items.statement:
theorem eval_scale (g : R) (m : Nat) (p : CPolynomial.Raw R)
    (hdeg : p.toPoly.natDegree < m) (x : R) :
    CPolynomial.Raw.eval x (scale g m p) = p.eval (g * x)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Coset.eval_scale_inv
items.doc: Scaling by `g` and then by `g⁻¹` restores the first `m` coefficients.
items.statement:
theorem eval_scale_inv (g : R) (hg : g ≠ 0) (m : Nat) (p : CPolynomial.Raw R)
    (hdeg : p.toPoly.natDegree < m) (x : R) :
    CPolynomial.Raw.eval (g * x) (scale g⁻¹ m p) = p.eval x

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Coset.forwardImpl
items.doc: Forward transform on the coset `g·⟨ω⟩`: values `p(g·ωᵏ)` in natural order.
items.statement: def forwardImpl (D : Domain R) (g : R) (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) : Array R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Coset.inverseImpl
items.doc: Inverse transform on the coset `g·⟨ω⟩`, from natural-order values.
items.statement: def inverseImpl (D : Domain R) (g : R) (v : Array R) : CPolynomial.Raw R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Coset.forwardImpl_eq_evalOnCoset
items.doc: The coset forward transform evaluates the polynomial on the coset.
items.statement:
theorem forwardImpl_eq_evalOnCoset (D : Domain R) (g : R) (p : CPolynomial.Raw R)
    (hdeg : p.toPoly.natDegree < D.n) :
    forwardImpl D g p = evalOnCoset D g p

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Coset.natDegree_inverseImpl_lt
items.doc: The coset inverse transform has degree below the domain size.
items.statement:
theorem natDegree_inverseImpl_lt (D : Domain R) (g : R) (v : Array R) :
    (inverseImpl D g v).toPoly.natDegree < D.n

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Coset.inverseImpl_eval_node_eq
items.doc: The coset inverse transform takes each value at its coset node.
items.statement:
theorem inverseImpl_eval_node_eq (D : Domain R) (g : R) (hg : g ≠ 0) (v : Array R)
    (k : D.Idx) :
    CPolynomial.Raw.eval (g * D.node k) (inverseImpl D g v) = v.getD k.1 0

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Coset.inverseImpl_evalOnCoset_eq
items.doc: The coset inverse transform evaluates back to its input on the coset.
items.statement:
theorem inverseImpl_evalOnCoset_eq (D : Domain R) (g : R) (hg : g ≠ 0) (v : Array R) :
    evalOnCoset D g (inverseImpl D g v) = loadNaturalArray D v

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Coset.forwardImpl_inverseImpl
items.doc: The coset forward transform inverts the coset inverse transform.
items.statement:
theorem forwardImpl_inverseImpl (D : Domain R) (g : R) (hg : g ≠ 0) (v : Array R) :
    forwardImpl D g (inverseImpl D g v) = loadNaturalArray D v

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Coset.interpolate
items.doc: Interpolate natural-order values on the coset `g·⟨ω⟩`, in `O(n log n)`.
items.statement:
def interpolate [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (D : Domain R) (g : R) (values : Vector R D.n) :
    CPolynomial R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Coset.eval_interpolate_node
items.doc: Coset interpolation takes each value at its coset node.
items.statement:
theorem eval_interpolate_node [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (D : Domain R) (g : R) (hg : g ≠ 0)
    (values : Vector R D.n) (k : D.Idx) :
    (interpolate D g values).eval (g * D.node k) = values.get k

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Coset.interpolate_eq_interpolate
items.doc: Coset interpolation is Lagrange interpolation on the nodes `g·ωᵏ`.
items.statement:
theorem interpolate_eq_interpolate [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (D : Domain R) (g : R) (hg : g ≠ 0)
    (values : Vector R D.n) :
    interpolate D g values =
      CLagrange.interpolate Finset.univ (fun k : D.Idx => g * D.node k) values.get

modules.authors: Salih Erdem Koçak, Doran Pamukçu, Valerii Huhnin
modules.title: NTT Domain
modules.doc:
This file defines the radix-2 NTT domain parameters and basic raw-polynomial
shape helpers used by forward/inverse NTT.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Domain
items.doc: Parameters for a radix-2 NTT domain of size `2 ^ logN`.
items.statement:
structure Domain (R : Type*) [Field R] where
  logN : Nat
  omega : R
  primitive : IsPrimitiveRoot omega (2 ^ logN)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Domain.n
items.doc: Domain size.
items.statement: def n (D : Domain R) : Nat

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Domain.Idx
items.doc: Index type for vectors over the domain.
items.statement: abbrev Idx (D : Domain R)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Domain.node
items.doc: The `i`-th evaluation node `omega^i`.
items.statement: def node (D : Domain R) (i : D.Idx) : R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Domain.omegaInv
items.doc: Inverse root of unity.
items.statement: def omegaInv (D : Domain R) : R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Domain.inverse
items.doc: The domain with the inverse root, used by inverse NTT butterflies.
items.statement: def inverse (D : Domain R) : Domain R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Domain.nInv
items.doc: Multiplicative inverse of the domain size in `R`.
items.statement: def nInv (D : Domain R) : R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Domain.n_pos
items.statement: lemma n_pos (D : Domain R) : 0 < D.n

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Domain.n_ne_zero
items.statement: lemma n_ne_zero (D : Domain R) : D.n ≠ 0

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Domain.natCast_ne_zero
items.doc: The size of an NTT domain is nonzero in its coefficient field.
items.statement: theorem natCast_ne_zero (D : Domain R) : ((D.n : Nat) : R) ≠ 0

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Domain.requiredLength
items.doc: Required convolution length for multiplying `p` and `q`.
items.statement: def requiredLength (p q : CPolynomial.Raw R) : Nat

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Domain.requiredLength_eq_zero_of_left_trim_size_zero
items.statement:
theorem requiredLength_eq_zero_of_left_trim_size_zero
    (p q : CPolynomial.Raw R) (hp : p.trim.size = 0) :

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Domain.requiredLength_eq_zero_of_right_trim_size_zero
items.statement:
theorem requiredLength_eq_zero_of_right_trim_size_zero
    (p q : CPolynomial.Raw R) (hq : q.trim.size = 0) :
    requiredLength p q = 0

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Domain.requiredLength_eq_of_trim_size_pos
items.statement:
theorem requiredLength_eq_of_trim_size_pos
    (p q : CPolynomial.Raw R) (hp : 0 < p.trim.size) (hq : 0 < q.trim.size) :
    requiredLength p q = p.trim.size + q.trim.size - 1

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Domain.fits
items.doc: Whether domain `D` is large enough for multiplying `p` and `q`.
items.statement: def fits (D : Domain R) (p q : CPolynomial.Raw R) : Prop

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Domain.truncate
items.doc: Truncate a polynomial to at most `m` coefficients.
items.statement: def truncate (m : Nat) (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) : CPolynomial.Raw R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.bestLogN
items.doc: The smallest radix-2 exponent that can cover a requested convolution length.
items.statement: def bestLogN (requiredLen : Nat) : Nat

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.loadNaturalArray
items.doc: Load an array in natural order and pad it to a domain-sized array.
items.statement: def loadNaturalArray (D : Domain R) (a : Array R) : Array R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.size_loadNaturalArray
items.statement:
theorem size_loadNaturalArray (D : Domain R) (a : Array R) :
    (loadNaturalArray D a).size = D.n

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.getElem_loadNaturalArray
items.statement:
theorem getElem_loadNaturalArray (D : Domain R) (a : Array R) (i : Nat)
    (hi : i < (loadNaturalArray D a).size) :
    (loadNaturalArray D a)[i] = a.getD i 0

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.loadNaturalVector
items.doc: Load an array in natural order and pad it to a domain-sized vector.
items.statement: def loadNaturalVector (D : Domain R) (a : Array R) : Vector R D.n

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.FittingDomain
items.doc: An NTT domain bundled with proof that it covers the requested convolution length.
items.statement: abbrev FittingDomain (R : Type*) [Field R] (requiredLen : Nat)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.bestDomainForLength?
items.doc:
Generic adapter from field-specific radix-2 domain tables to a best-fitting domain lookup.

The adapter chooses `logN = Nat.clog 2 requiredLen`, then returns `none` if that exponent
is outside the supported table.
items.statement:
def bestDomainForLength?
    (maxLogN : Nat) (domainOfLogN : (logN : Nat) → logN ≤ maxLogN → Domain R)
    (domainOfLogN_logN : ∀ logN hlogN, (domainOfLogN logN hlogN).logN = logN)
    (requiredLen : Nat) : Option (FittingDomain R requiredLen)

modules.title: NTT and Evaluation
modules.doc:
Bridge definitions and theorems connecting the NTT specification layer to
evaluation on the root-of-unity domain.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.evalOnDomain
items.doc: Evaluate a raw polynomial on all nodes of an NTT domain in natural order.
items.statement: def evalOnDomain (D : Domain R) (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) : Array R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.evalOnDomain_eq_evalBatch
items.doc: `evalOnDomain` is `evalBatch` specialized to the NTT domain nodes.
items.statement:
theorem evalOnDomain_eq_evalBatch (D : Domain R) (p : CPolynomial R) :
    evalOnDomain D p.val =
      evalBatch p (Array.ofFn (fun k : D.Idx => D.node k))

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Forward.forwardSpec_eval_node_eq
items.doc: Pointwise form: the forward NTT specification evaluates a raw polynomial at a domain node.
items.statement:
theorem forwardSpec_eval_node_eq (D : Domain R) (p : CPolynomial.Raw R)
    (hdeg : p.toPoly.natDegree < D.n) (k : D.Idx) :
    (forwardSpec D p)[k.1] = p.eval (D.node k)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Forward.forwardSpec_eq_evalOnDomain
items.doc: The forward NTT specification evaluates a raw polynomial on all domain nodes.
items.statement:
theorem forwardSpec_eq_evalOnDomain (D : Domain R) (p : CPolynomial.Raw R)
    (hdeg : p.toPoly.natDegree < D.n) :
    forwardSpec D p = evalOnDomain D p

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Forward.forwardImpl_eval_node_eq
items.doc: Pointwise form: the forward NTT implementation evaluates a raw polynomial at a domain node.
items.statement:
theorem forwardImpl_eval_node_eq (D : Domain R) (p : CPolynomial.Raw R)
    (hdeg : p.toPoly.natDegree < D.n) (k : D.Idx) :
    (forwardImpl D p).getD k.1 0 = p.eval (D.node k)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Forward.forwardImpl_eq_evalOnDomain
items.doc: The forward NTT implementation evaluates a raw polynomial on all domain nodes.
items.statement:
theorem forwardImpl_eq_evalOnDomain (D : Domain R) (p : CPolynomial.Raw R)
    (hdeg : p.toPoly.natDegree < D.n) :
    forwardImpl D p = evalOnDomain D p

modules.title: Fast Multiplication via NTT
modules.doc:
This file wires forward NTT, pointwise multiplication, and inverse NTT into a
spec/implementation pipeline.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.FastMul.pointwiseMul
items.doc: Pointwise multiplication in evaluation form.
items.statement: def pointwiseMul (D : Domain R) (a b : Array R) : Array R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.FastMul.size_pointwiseMul
items.statement:
theorem size_pointwiseMul (D : Domain R) (a b : Array R) :
    (pointwiseMul D a b).size = D.n

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.FastMul.Raw.fastMulSpec
items.doc:
Raw spec pipeline for NTT-based multiplication.

This is the low-level array computation and deliberately does not trim the
output.
items.statement: def fastMulSpec (D : Domain R) (p q : CPolynomial.Raw R) : CPolynomial.Raw R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.FastMul.Raw.fastMulImpl
items.doc:
Raw implementation pipeline for NTT-based multiplication.

Correctness as ordinary polynomial multiplication requires
`Domain.fits D p q`; see `fastMulImpl_trim_eq_mul`. Without this precondition,
this function only exposes the raw NTT pipeline result, which may include cyclic
wraparound and has no product-correctness guarantee. The output is not trimmed;
use `FastMul.fastMulImpl` for the canonical public API.
items.statement: def fastMulImpl (D : Domain R) (p q : CPolynomial.Raw R) : CPolynomial.Raw R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.FastMul.Raw.fastMulImpl_correct
items.statement:
theorem fastMulImpl_correct (D : Domain R) (p q : CPolynomial.Raw R) :
    fastMulImpl D p q = fastMulSpec D p q

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.FastMul.Raw.fastMulSpec_coeff
items.statement:
theorem fastMulSpec_coeff (D : Domain R) (p q : CPolynomial.Raw R)
    (hfit : Domain.fits D p q) (i : Nat) :
    (fastMulSpec D p q).coeff i = (p * q).coeff i

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.FastMul.Raw.fastMulSpec_trim_eq_mul
items.statement:
theorem fastMulSpec_trim_eq_mul (D : Domain R) (p q : CPolynomial.Raw R)
    (hfit : Domain.fits D p q) : (fastMulSpec D p q).trim = p * q

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.FastMul.Raw.fastMulImpl_trim_eq_mul
items.statement:
theorem fastMulImpl_trim_eq_mul (D : Domain R) (p q : CPolynomial.Raw R)
    (hfit : Domain.fits D p q) : (fastMulImpl D p q).trim = p * q

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.FastMul.fastMulSpec
items.doc: Spec pipeline for NTT-based multiplication as a canonical polynomial.
items.statement: def fastMulSpec (D : Domain R) (p q : CPolynomial R) : CPolynomial R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.FastMul.fastMulImpl
items.doc:
Implementation pipeline for NTT-based multiplication as a canonical polynomial.

Correctness as ordinary polynomial multiplication requires
`Domain.fits D p.val q.val`; see `fastMulImpl_eq_mul`. Without this precondition,
the raw NTT computation may include cyclic wraparound before canonicalization.
items.statement: def fastMulImpl (D : Domain R) (p q : CPolynomial R) : CPolynomial R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.FastMul.safeFastMul
items.doc:
Safe NTT-based multiplication wrapper.

This computes with `fastMulImpl`, but requires the caller to provide the
`Domain.fits D p.val q.val` proof at the call site.
items.statement:
def safeFastMul
    (D : Domain R) (p q : CPolynomial R) (_hfit : Domain.fits D p.val q.val) :
    CPolynomial R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.FastMul.fastMulImpl_correct
items.statement:
theorem fastMulImpl_correct (D : Domain R) (p q : CPolynomial R) :
    fastMulImpl D p q = fastMulSpec D p q

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.FastMul.fastMulSpec_eq_mul
items.statement:
theorem fastMulSpec_eq_mul (D : Domain R) (p q : CPolynomial R)
    (hfit : Domain.fits D p.val q.val) : fastMulSpec D p q = p * q

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.FastMul.fastMulImpl_eq_mul
items.statement:
theorem fastMulImpl_eq_mul (D : Domain R) (p q : CPolynomial R)
    (hfit : Domain.fits D p.val q.val) : fastMulImpl D p q = p * q

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.FastMul.safeFastMul_eq_mul
items.doc:
The safe wrapper is equivalent to ordinary canonical polynomial multiplication.

There are no extra assumptions because the required `Domain.fits D p.val q.val`
proof is already an argument of `safeFastMul`.
items.statement:
theorem safeFastMul_eq_mul (D : Domain R) (p q : CPolynomial R)
    (hfit : Domain.fits D p.val q.val) : safeFastMul D p q hfit = p * q

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.FastMul.withFallback
items.doc:
NTT-backed multiplication with canonical multiplication as a fallback.

The selector should return a domain fitting the required convolution length.
When it does, this uses `fastMulImpl`; otherwise it falls back to canonical
`CPolynomial` multiplication.
items.statement:
def withFallback
    (bestDomainForLength? : (requiredLen : Nat) →
      Option (FittingDomain R requiredLen))
    (p q : CPolynomial R) : CPolynomial R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.FastMul.withFallback_eq_mul
items.doc: `withFallback` agrees with canonical polynomial multiplication.
items.statement:
theorem withFallback_eq_mul
    (bestDomainForLength? : (requiredLen : Nat) →
      Option (FittingDomain R requiredLen))
    (p q : CPolynomial R) :
    withFallback bestDomainForLength? p q = p * q

modules.title: Low Product via NTT
modules.doc:
This file exposes an NTT-backed `Raw.MulLowContext` for computing the low
coefficients of a raw polynomial product.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.FastMulLow.run
items.statement:
def run
    (bestDomainForLength? : (requiredLen : Nat) →
      Option (FittingDomain R requiredLen))
    (k : Nat) (p q : CPolynomial.Raw R) : CPolynomial.Raw R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.FastMulLow.withFallback
items.doc:
NTT-backed low-product context with low-convolution as a fallback.

This truncates both inputs to the requested output precision, multiplies them
with the selected fitting NTT domain when one is available, and truncates the
result back to the requested precision. If the domain table cannot cover the
requested product length, it falls back to the low-convolution backend.
items.statement:
def withFallback
    (bestDomainForLength? : (requiredLen : Nat) →
      Option (FittingDomain R requiredLen)) :
    CPolynomial.Raw.MulLowContext R

modules.title: Forward NTT
modules.doc:
This file provides spec-level forward NTT definitions together with an
iterative radix-2 implementation.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Forward.nttAt
items.doc: DFT/NTT formula at one output index.
items.statement: def nttAt (D : Domain R) (a : Array R) (k : D.Idx) : R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Forward.forwardSpec
items.doc: Full forward transform specified directly from the NTT formula.
items.statement: def forwardSpec (D : Domain R) (a : Array R) : Array R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Forward.forwardStageSpec
items.doc:
Proof-oriented stagewise specification for the forward transform.

`forwardStageSpec D completed a` means: start from the bit-reversed input `a`,
then apply exactly the first `completed` radix-2 butterfly stages.
items.statement: def forwardStageSpec (D : Domain R) (completed : Nat) (a : Array R) : Array R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Forward.forwardStagePureSpec
items.doc:
Stagewise pure specification built from `butterflyStageSpec`.

This removes the mutable-array implementation details but still mirrors the
radix-2 control flow exactly.
items.statement: def forwardStagePureSpec (D : Domain R) (completed : Nat) (a : Array R) : Array R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Forward.forwardMathStageSpec
items.doc:
Mathematical partial-DFT state after `completed` radix-2 stages.

Each contiguous block of size `2^completed` has already been transformed, while
the remaining `D.logN - completed` bits are still encoded by bit-reversed block
selection.
items.statement: def forwardMathStageSpec (D : Domain R) (completed : Nat) (a : Array R) : Array R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Forward.forwardStageSpec_zero
items.statement:
theorem forwardStageSpec_zero (D : Domain R) (a : Array R) :
    forwardStageSpec D 0 a = bitRevPermute D a

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Forward.forwardStageSpec_succ
items.statement:
theorem forwardStageSpec_succ (D : Domain R) (stage : Nat) (a : Array R) :
    forwardStageSpec D (stage + 1) a =
      butterflyStage D stage (forwardStageSpec D stage a)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Forward.forwardStagePureSpec_zero
items.statement:
theorem forwardStagePureSpec_zero (D : Domain R) (a : Array R) :
    forwardStagePureSpec D 0 a = bitRevPermute D a

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Forward.forwardStagePureSpec_succ
items.statement:
theorem forwardStagePureSpec_succ (D : Domain R) (stage : Nat) (a : Array R) :
    forwardStagePureSpec D (stage + 1) a =
      butterflyStageSpec D stage (forwardStagePureSpec D stage a)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Forward.size_forwardStageSpec
items.statement:
theorem size_forwardStageSpec (D : Domain R) (completed : Nat) (a : Array R) :
    (forwardStageSpec D completed a).size = D.n

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Forward.size_forwardStagePureSpec
items.statement:
theorem size_forwardStagePureSpec (D : Domain R) (completed : Nat) (a : Array R) :
    (forwardStagePureSpec D completed a).size = D.n

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Forward.forwardStageSpec_eq_forwardStagePureSpec
items.doc:
The algorithmic stage recursion agrees with the pure stage recursion.

This is the global bookkeeping bridge from the recursive algorithmic stages to
their pointwise closed-form counterparts.
items.statement:
theorem forwardStageSpec_eq_forwardStagePureSpec (D : Domain R) (a : Array R) :
    ∀ completed : Nat, forwardStageSpec D completed a = forwardStagePureSpec D completed a

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Forward.forwardMathStageSpec_zero
items.doc:
Base case of the mathematical stage invariant: before any butterflies, the
state is exactly the bit-reversed input.
items.statement:
theorem forwardMathStageSpec_zero (D : Domain R) (a : Array R) :
    forwardMathStageSpec D 0 a = bitRevPermute D a

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Forward.butterflyStageSpec_forwardMathStageSpec_succ
items.statement:
theorem butterflyStageSpec_forwardMathStageSpec_succ
    (D : Domain R) (stage : Nat) (a : Array R) (hstage : stage < D.logN) :
    butterflyStageSpec D stage (forwardMathStageSpec D stage a) =
      forwardMathStageSpec D (stage + 1) a

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Forward.forwardStagePureSpec_eq_forwardMathStageSpec
items.doc:
The pure stage recursion matches the mathematical partial-DFT state at every
stage.
items.statement:
theorem forwardStagePureSpec_eq_forwardMathStageSpec (D : Domain R) (a : Array R) :
    ∀ completed : Nat, completed ≤ D.logN →
      forwardStagePureSpec D completed a = forwardMathStageSpec D completed a

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Forward.runStages_bitRevPermute_eq_forwardStageSpec
items.doc:
Algorithmic stages coincide with the proof-oriented stagewise specification.

This is the loop-invariant bridge: the imperative `for stage in [0:D.logN]`
implementation computes the same intermediate states as `forwardStageSpec`.
Basically, this is recursion vs. `for` loop bookkeeping.
items.statement:
theorem runStages_bitRevPermute_eq_forwardStageSpec (D : Domain R) (a : Array R) :
    Transform.runStages D (Transform.bitRevPermute D a) = forwardStageSpec D D.logN a

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Forward.forwardMathStageSpec_final_eq_forwardSpec
items.doc:
Once all `logN` stages are completed, the stagewise specification matches the
direct NTT formula.
items.statement:
theorem forwardMathStageSpec_final_eq_forwardSpec (D : Domain R) (a : Array R) :
    forwardMathStageSpec D D.logN a = forwardSpec D a

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Forward.forwardStageSpec_final_eq_forwardSpec
items.doc:
Once all `logN` stages are completed, the stagewise specification matches the
direct NTT formula.
items.statement:
theorem forwardStageSpec_final_eq_forwardSpec (D : Domain R) (a : Array R) :
    forwardStageSpec D D.logN a = forwardSpec D a

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Forward.forwardImpl
items.doc: Intended fast implementation entry point for NTT.
items.statement: def forwardImpl (D : Domain R) (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) : Array R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Forward.size_forwardSpec
items.statement:
theorem size_forwardSpec (D : Domain R) (a : Array R) :
    (forwardSpec D a).size = D.n

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Forward.forwardImpl_correct
items.statement:
theorem forwardImpl_correct (D : Domain R) (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) :
    forwardImpl D p = forwardSpec D p

modules.title: NTT and Interpolation
modules.doc:
Bridge theorem declarations connecting the NTT specification layer to power-domain
interpolation.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Inverse.inverseSpec_eval_node_eq
items.doc: Pointwise form of `inverseSpec_interpolatePow_eq`.
items.statement:
theorem inverseSpec_eval_node_eq (D : Domain R) (values : Array R) (k : D.Idx) :
    CPolynomial.Raw.eval (D.node k) (inverseSpec D values) = values.getD k.1 0

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Inverse.inverseSpec_evalOnDomain_eq
items.doc: The inverse NTT specification evaluates back to the input values on the NTT domain.
items.statement:
theorem inverseSpec_evalOnDomain_eq (D : Domain R) (values : Array R) :
    evalOnDomain D (inverseSpec D values) = loadNaturalArray D values

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Inverse.inverseSpec_interpolatePow_eq
items.doc: The inverse NTT specification interpolates the input values on the NTT domain.
items.statement:
theorem inverseSpec_interpolatePow_eq [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (D : Domain R) (values : Array R) :
    CPolynomial.Raw.trim (inverseSpec D values) =
      (CLagrange.interpolatePow D.omega (loadNaturalVector D values)).val

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Inverse.inverseImpl_interpolatePow_eq
items.doc: The inverse NTT implementation interpolates the input values on the NTT domain.
items.statement:
theorem inverseImpl_interpolatePow_eq [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (D : Domain R) (values : Array R) :
    CPolynomial.Raw.trim (inverseImpl D values) =
      (CLagrange.interpolatePow D.omega (loadNaturalVector D values)).val

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Inverse.inverseImpl_eval_node_eq
items.doc: Pointwise form of `inverseImpl_interpolatePow_eq`.
items.statement:
theorem inverseImpl_eval_node_eq (D : Domain R) (values : Array R) (k : D.Idx) :
    CPolynomial.Raw.eval (D.node k) (inverseImpl D values) = values.getD k.1 0

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Inverse.inverseImpl_evalOnDomain_eq
items.doc: The inverse NTT implementation evaluates back to the input values on the NTT domain.
items.statement:
theorem inverseImpl_evalOnDomain_eq (D : Domain R) (values : Array R) :
    evalOnDomain D (inverseImpl D values) = loadNaturalArray D values

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.loadNaturalVector_toArray
items.doc: Loading a domain-sized vector back from its array is the identity.
items.statement:
theorem loadNaturalVector_toArray [Field R] (D : Domain R) (values : Vector R D.n) :
    loadNaturalVector D values.toArray = values

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.interpolate
items.doc:
Interpolate natural-order values on the NTT domain through the inverse transform.

This is `CLagrange.interpolatePow D.omega` (`interpolate_eq_interpolatePow`) computed with
`O(n log n)` field operations rather than the Lagrange formula's `O(n²)` per basis
polynomial.
items.statement:
def interpolate [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (D : Domain R) (values : Vector R D.n) :
    CPolynomial R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.interpolate_eq_interpolatePow
items.doc: NTT interpolation is Lagrange interpolation on the powers of the domain root.
items.statement:
theorem interpolate_eq_interpolatePow [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (D : Domain R) (values : Vector R D.n) :
    interpolate D values = CLagrange.interpolatePow D.omega values

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.eval_interpolate_node
items.doc: NTT interpolation takes each value at its domain node.
items.statement:
theorem eval_interpolate_node [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (D : Domain R) (values : Vector R D.n) (k : D.Idx) :
    (interpolate D values).eval (D.node k) = values.get k

modules.title: Inverse NTT
modules.doc: This file provides inverse NTT APIs and correctness statement.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Inverse.inttAt
items.doc: Inverse NTT formula at one output index.
items.statement: def inttAt (D : Domain R) (v : Array R) (k : D.Idx) : R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Inverse.inverseSpec
items.doc: Full inverse transform on arrays, specified from `inttAt`.
items.statement: def inverseSpec (D : Domain R) (v : Array R) : Array R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Inverse.normalize
items.doc: Apply the final `n⁻¹` normalization for the inverse transform.
items.statement: def normalize (D : Domain R) (a : Array R) : Array R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Inverse.size_inverseSpec
items.statement:
theorem size_inverseSpec (D : Domain R) (v : Array R) :
    (inverseSpec D v).size = D.n

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Inverse.size_normalize
items.statement:
theorem size_normalize (D : Domain R) (a : Array R) :
    (normalize D a).size = D.n

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Inverse.normalize_forwardSpec_inverse_eq_inverseSpec
items.statement:
theorem normalize_forwardSpec_inverse_eq_inverseSpec (D : Domain R) (v : Array R) :
    normalize D (Forward.forwardSpec D.inverse v) = inverseSpec D v

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Inverse.inverseImpl
items.doc: Intended fast implementation entry point for inverse NTT.
items.statement: def inverseImpl (D : Domain R) (v : Array R) : CPolynomial.Raw R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Inverse.inverseImpl_correct
items.statement:

modules.authors: Salih Erdem Koçak, Doran Pamukçu, Valerii Huhnin
modules.title: NTT Kernel Identities
modules.doc:
Shared root-of-unity orthogonality lemmas used by NTT evaluation,
interpolation, and multiplication proofs.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.omegaInv_pow_mul_eq
items.doc: Rewrite powers of the inverse root as powers of the forward root.
items.statement:
theorem omegaInv_pow_mul_eq (D : Domain R) {i : Nat} (hi : i < D.n) (k : Nat) :
    D.omegaInv ^ (i * k) = D.omega ^ ((D.n - i) * k)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.kernel_term_eq
items.doc: Combine a forward-kernel term with an inverse-kernel term.
items.statement:
theorem kernel_term_eq (D : Domain R) {i : Nat} (hi : i < D.n) (j k : Nat) :
    D.omega ^ (k * j) * D.omegaInv ^ (i * k) =
      D.omega ^ ((j + (D.n - i)) * k)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.omega_sum_pow_mul_eq_if_dvd
items.doc: Sum of powers over the NTT domain, expressed by divisibility of the exponent.
items.statement:
theorem omega_sum_pow_mul_eq_if_dvd (D : Domain R) (m : Nat) :
    (∑ k : D.Idx, D.omega ^ (m * (k : Nat))) = if D.n ∣ m then (D.n : R) else 0

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.dvd_add_sub_iff_fin_eq
items.doc: The kernel divisibility condition is equivalent to equality of domain indices.
items.statement:
theorem dvd_add_sub_iff_fin_eq (D : Domain R) (i j : D.Idx) :
    D.n ∣ (j.1 + (D.n - i.1)) ↔ j = i

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.kernel_sum_eq_if
items.doc: Orthogonality of the forward/inverse NTT kernels over the domain.
items.statement:
theorem kernel_sum_eq_if (D : Domain R) (i j : D.Idx) :
    (∑ k : D.Idx, D.omega ^ ((k : Nat) * (j : Nat)) *
        D.omegaInv ^ ((i : Nat) * (k : Nat))) =
      if j = i then (D.n : R) else 0

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.kernel_sum_forward_inverse_eq_if
items.doc: Orthogonality of the inverse/forward NTT kernels over the domain.
items.statement:
theorem kernel_sum_forward_inverse_eq_if (D : Domain R) (i j : D.Idx) :
    (∑ k : D.Idx, D.omegaInv ^ ((k : Nat) * (j : Nat)) *
        D.omega ^ ((i : Nat) * (k : Nat))) =
      if j = i then (D.n : R) else 0

modules.title: Shared radix-2 NTT transform
modules.doc:
This file provides the root-parametric bit-reversal and butterfly machinery used
by forward and inverse radix-2 NTTs.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Transform.bitRevNat
items.doc: Reverse the lowest `bits` bits of `i`.
items.statement: def bitRevNat : Nat → Nat → Nat

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Transform.bitRevNat_lt
items.statement: theorem bitRevNat_lt (bits i : Nat) : bitRevNat bits i < 2 ^ bits

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Transform.bitRevNat_even
items.statement:
theorem bitRevNat_even (bits b : Nat) :
    bitRevNat (bits + 1) (2 * b) = bitRevNat bits b

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Transform.bitRevNat_odd_or
items.statement:
theorem bitRevNat_odd_or (bits b : Nat) :
    bitRevNat (bits + 1) (2 * b + 1) = (1 <<< bits) ||| bitRevNat bits b

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Transform.bitRevNat_odd
items.statement:
theorem bitRevNat_odd (bits b : Nat) :
    bitRevNat (bits + 1) (2 * b + 1) = 2 ^ bits + bitRevNat bits b

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Transform.bitRevAcc
items.doc:
Accumulator form of `bitRevNat`: shifts the low bits of `i` into `acc` one at a time.
It replaces `bitRevNat` in compiled code (`bitRevNat_eq_bitRevNatFast`).
items.statement: def bitRevAcc : Nat → Nat → Nat → Nat

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Transform.bitRevAcc_eq
items.statement:
theorem bitRevAcc_eq (bits : Nat) :
    ∀ i acc, bitRevAcc bits i acc = acc * 2 ^ bits + bitRevNat bits i

items.statement: def bitRevNatFast (bits i : Nat) : Nat

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Transform.bitRevNat_eq_bitRevNatFast
items.statement: theorem bitRevNat_eq_bitRevNatFast : @bitRevNat = @bitRevNatFast

items.doc: Run all radix-2 butterfly stages (complexity: `O(n log n)`).
items.statement: def runStages (D : Domain R) (a : Array R) : Array R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTT.Transform.runStages_eq_rec
items.doc: The imperative stage loop agrees with the corresponding `Nat.rec`.
items.statement:
