    runStages D a = Nat.rec a (fun stage acc => butterflyStage D stage acc) D.logN

modules.title: Correctness proofs for NTTFast multiplication
modules.doc:
This module re-exports the correctness proofs for the `NTTFast` transforms and
multiplication pipelines.

modules.title: Basic NTTFast correctness facts
modules.doc:
Cached-plan well-formedness, twiddle-table facts, and shared proof helpers for
`NTTFast` correctness.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTTFast.Plan.WellFormed
items.doc: Well-formedness condition for cached plan data.
items.statement: def WellFormed (P : Plan R) : Prop

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTTFast.Plan.twiddlePowers_size
items.doc: The cached twiddle powers for a stage have exactly one entry per butterfly offset.
items.statement:
theorem twiddlePowers_size (D : NTT.Domain R) (stage : Nat) :
    (twiddlePowers D stage).size = 2 ^ stage

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTTFast.Plan.twiddlePowers_getD_eq_pow
items.doc: Entries of the cached twiddle powers are the corresponding powers of the stage root.
items.statement:
theorem twiddlePowers_getD_eq_pow (D : NTT.Domain R) (stage j : Nat)
    (hj : j < 2 ^ stage) :
    (twiddlePowers D stage).getD j 0 =
      (D.omega ^ (D.n / 2 ^ (stage + 1))) ^ j

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTTFast.Plan.twiddleTable_getD_eq_twiddlePowers
items.doc: Looking up a valid stage in the twiddle table returns that stage's twiddle powers.
items.statement:
theorem twiddleTable_getD_eq_twiddlePowers
    (D : NTT.Domain R) (stage : Nat) (hstage : stage < D.logN) :
    (twiddleTable D).getD stage #[] = twiddlePowers D stage

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTTFast.Plan.ofDomain_wellFormed
items.doc: A plan built directly from a domain has well-formed cached data.
items.statement:
theorem ofDomain_wellFormed (D : NTT.Domain R) :
    WellFormed (ofDomain D)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTTFast.Plan.loadNaturalArray_eq
items.doc: Loading raw coefficients into a domain-sized array is `Array.ofFn` with zero padding.
items.statement:
theorem loadNaturalArray_eq (D : NTT.Domain R) (a : Array R) :
    NTT.loadNaturalArray D a = Array.ofFn (fun i : D.Idx ↦ a.getD i.1 0)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTTFast.Plan.foldl_range_eq_rec
items.doc: Folding over `List.range` is equivalent to the corresponding natural recursion.
items.statement:
theorem foldl_range_eq_rec {α : Type*} (f : Nat → α → α) (x : α) :
    ∀ n : Nat,
      List.foldl (fun acc i ↦ f i acc) x (List.range n) = Nat.rec x (fun i acc ↦ f i acc) n

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTTFast.Plan.foldl_range_eq_rec_fst
items.doc: First projections of pair-valued folds over `List.range` match natural recursion.
items.statement:
theorem foldl_range_eq_rec_fst {α β : Type*}
    (f : Nat → α × β → α × β) (x : α × β) (n : Nat) :
    (List.foldl (fun acc i ↦ f i acc) x (List.range n)).1 =
      (Nat.rec (motive := fun _ ↦ α × β) x (fun i acc ↦ f i acc) n).1

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTTFast.Plan.foldl_range_congr
items.doc: Two fold functions give the same range fold when they agree at every step.
items.statement:
theorem foldl_range_congr {α : Type*} (f g : α → Nat → α) :
    ∀ n : Nat,
      (∀ i, i < n → ∀ acc, f acc i = g acc i) →
      ∀ acc, List.foldl f acc (List.range n) = List.foldl g acc (List.range n)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTTFast.Plan.foldl_range_preserve
items.doc: A property preserved by every step is preserved by folding over `List.range`.
items.statement:
theorem foldl_range_preserve {α : Type*} (p : α → Prop) (f : α → Nat → α) :
    ∀ n : Nat,
      (∀ i, i < n → ∀ acc, p acc → p (f acc i)) →
      ∀ acc, p acc → p (List.foldl f acc (List.range n))

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTTFast.Plan.foldl_range_congr_inv
items.doc: Congruence for range folds under an invariant preserved by the left fold.
items.statement:
theorem foldl_range_congr_inv {α : Type*} (p : α → Prop) (f g : α → Nat → α) :
    ∀ n : Nat,
      (∀ i, i < n → ∀ acc, p acc → f acc i = g acc i) →
      (∀ i, i < n → ∀ acc, p acc → p (f acc i)) →
      ∀ acc, p acc → List.foldl f acc (List.range n) = List.foldl g acc (List.range n)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTTFast.Plan.foldl_range'_succ_shift
items.doc: Shift a `List.range'` fold by one when the folded function shifts its index.
items.statement:
theorem foldl_range'_succ_shift {α : Type*} (f : Nat → α → α) :
    ∀ n offset (acc : α),
      List.foldl (fun acc t ↦ f (t + 1) acc) acc (List.range' offset n) =
        List.foldl (fun acc t ↦ f t acc) acc (List.range' (offset + 1) n)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTTFast.Plan.foldl_range'_eq_range_add
items.doc: Reindex a `List.range'` fold as a fold over `List.range` with an offset.
items.statement:
theorem foldl_range'_eq_range_add {α : Type*} (f : Nat → α → α)
    (n offset : Nat) (acc : α) :
    List.foldl (fun acc t ↦ f t acc) acc (List.range' offset n) =
      List.foldl (fun acc t ↦ f (offset + t) acc) acc (List.range n)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTTFast.Plan.foldl_range'_append_split
items.doc: Split a `List.range'` fold over an appended interval into two folds.
items.statement:
theorem foldl_range'_append_split {α : Type*} (f : α → Nat → α)
    (acc : α) (s m n : Nat) :
    List.foldl f acc (List.range' s (m + n)) =
      List.foldl f (List.foldl f acc (List.range' s m)) (List.range' (s + m) n)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTTFast.Plan.three_mul_add_eq_add_two_mul_add
items.doc: Arithmetic normal form used when rearranging adjacent radix-4 block indices.
items.statement:
theorem three_mul_add_eq_add_two_mul_add (q b : Nat) :
    3 * q + b = q + (2 * q + b)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTTFast.Plan.foldl_commute
items.doc: Move an operation through a range fold when it commutes with every step.
items.statement:
theorem foldl_commute {α : Type*} (op : α → α) (f : Nat → α → α) :
    ∀ n : Nat,
      (∀ i, i < n → ∀ x, op (f i x) = f i (op x)) →
      ∀ x, op (List.foldl (fun x i ↦ f i x) x (List.range n)) =
        List.foldl (fun x i ↦ f i x) (op x) (List.range n)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTTFast.Plan.foldl_commute_foldl
items.doc: Swap two range folds when every step of one commutes with every step of the other.
items.statement:
theorem foldl_commute_foldl {α : Type*} (f g : Nat → α → α) (m n : Nat)
    (hcomm : ∀ i j, i < m → j < n → ∀ x, g j (f i x) = f i (g j x)) :
    ∀ x,
      List.foldl (fun x i ↦ f i x) (List.foldl (fun x j ↦ g j x) x (List.range n))
          (List.range m) =
        List.foldl (fun x j ↦ g j x) (List.foldl (fun x i ↦ f i x) x (List.range m))
          (List.range n)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTTFast.Plan.foldl_pair
items.doc: Split a fold of paired same-index operations into two separate range folds.
items.statement:
theorem foldl_pair {α : Type*} (f g : Nat → α → α) :
    ∀ n : Nat,
      (∀ i j, i < j → j < n → ∀ x, f j (g i x) = g i (f j x)) →
      ∀ x,
        List.foldl (fun x i ↦ g i (f i x)) x (List.range n) =
          List.foldl (fun x i ↦ g i x)
            (List.foldl (fun x i ↦ f i x) x (List.range n)) (List.range n)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTTFast.Plan.foldl_range_pair
items.doc: Fold a pair of consecutive indexed operations as one fold over twice the range.
items.statement:
theorem foldl_range_pair {α : Type*} (f : Nat → α → α) :
    ∀ n (acc : α),
      List.foldl (fun acc b ↦ f (2 * b + 1) (f (2 * b) acc)) acc (List.range n) =
        List.foldl (fun acc k ↦ f k acc) acc (List.range (2 * n))

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTTFast.Plan.foldl_quad
items.doc: Split a fold of four same-index operations into four separate range folds.
items.statement:
theorem foldl_quad {α : Type*} (l₁ l₂ h₁ h₂ : Nat → α → α) :
    ∀ n : Nat,
      (∀ i j, i < j → j < n → ∀ x, l₁ j (l₂ i x) = l₂ i (l₁ j x)) →
      (∀ i j, i < j → j < n → ∀ x, l₁ j (h₁ i x) = h₁ i (l₁ j x)) →
      (∀ i j, i < j → j < n → ∀ x, l₁ j (h₂ i x) = h₂ i (l₁ j x)) →
      (∀ i j, i < j → j < n → ∀ x, l₂ j (h₁ i x) = h₁ i (l₂ j x)) →
      (∀ i j, i < j → j < n → ∀ x, l₂ j (h₂ i x) = h₂ i (l₂ j x)) →
      (∀ i j, i < j → j < n → ∀ x, h₁ j (h₂ i x) = h₂ i (h₁ j x)) →
      ∀ x,
        List.foldl (fun x i ↦ h₂ i (h₁ i (l₂ i (l₁ i x)))) x (List.range n) =
          List.foldl (fun x i ↦ h₂ i x)
            (List.foldl (fun x i ↦ h₁ i x)
              (List.foldl (fun x i ↦ l₂ i x)
                (List.foldl (fun x i ↦ l₁ i x) x (List.range n)) (List.range n))
              (List.range n))
            (List.range n)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTTFast.Plan.butterflyDITBlocks_eq_foldl
items.doc: Express the recursive DIT block loop as a fold over baseline NTT block steps.
items.statement:
theorem butterflyDITBlocks_eq_foldl
    (twiddles : Array R) (blockSize half : Nat) (wm : R)
    (htwiddles : ∀ j, j < half → twiddles.getD j 0 = wm ^ j) :
    ∀ n blocks block (acc : Array R),
      blocks = block + n →
      butterflyDITBlocks twiddles blockSize half blocks block acc =
        List.foldl (fun acc block ↦ NTT.Transform.butterflyBlockStep blockSize half wm block acc)
          acc (List.range' block n)

modules.doc: Correctness proofs for the decimation-in-frequency stage loop used by `NTTFast`.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTTFast.Plan.difMathValueAt
items.statement:
def difMathValueAt (D : NTT.Domain R) (completed : Nat) (a : Array R)
    (idx : Nat) : R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTTFast.Plan.difMathStageSpec_zero
items.doc: The initial DIF mathematical state is the naturally ordered input.

theorem difMathStageSpec_zero (D : NTT.Domain R) (a : Array R) :
    difMathStageSpec D 0 a = NTT.loadNaturalArray D a

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTTFast.Plan.difMathStageSpec_final
items.doc: The final DIF mathematical state is the bit-reversed forward NTT output.
items.statement:
theorem difMathStageSpec_final (D : NTT.Domain R) (a : Array R) :
    difMathStageSpec D D.logN a =
      NTT.Transform.bitRevPermute D (NTT.Forward.forwardSpec D a)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTTFast.Plan.butterflyStageDIFWithTwiddles_difMathStageSpec_succ
items.doc: One executable DIF butterfly stage advances the mathematical DIF stage spec.
items.statement:
theorem butterflyStageDIFWithTwiddles_difMathStageSpec_succ
    (D : NTT.Domain R) (stage : Nat) (twiddles : Array R) (a : Array R)
    (hstage : stage < D.logN)
    (htw : ∀ j, j < 2 ^ stage →
      twiddles.getD j 0 = (D.omega ^ (D.n / 2 ^ (stage + 1))) ^ j) :
    butterflyStageDIFWithTwiddles D stage twiddles
        (difMathStageSpec D (D.logN - (stage + 1)) a) =
      difMathStageSpec D (D.logN - stage) a

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTTFast.Plan.pointwiseMul_bitRevPermute_forwardSpec_eq
items.doc: Pointwise multiplication commutes with applying the bit-reversal permutation.

    (D : NTT.Domain R) (p q : CPolynomial.Raw R) :
    NTT.FastMul.pointwiseMul D

        (NTT.Transform.bitRevPermute D (NTT.Forward.forwardSpec D q)) =
      NTT.Transform.bitRevPermute D
        (NTT.FastMul.pointwiseMul D
          (NTT.Forward.forwardSpec D p) (NTT.Forward.forwardSpec D q))

modules.title: Planned Coset NTT
modules.doc:
The coset transforms of `NTT/Coset.lean` over a reusable `NTTFast.Plan`, with the shift
powers `gⁱ` and `g⁻ⁱ` computed once per plan rather than once per coefficient. As with
`Plan.forwardImpl`, the forward transform returns values in bit-reversed order and the
inverse transform consumes them in that order.

## Main definitions

* `NTTFast.powers g m`: the array `#[1, g, …, g^(m-1)]` by a running product.
* `NTTFast.CosetPlan`: a plan together with a shift `g` and its cached powers.
* `CosetPlan.forwardImpl`, `CosetPlan.inverseImpl`, `CosetPlan.interpolate`.

## Main results

* `powers_eq_ofFn`: the running product computes the powers.
* `CosetPlan.forwardImpl_eq_bitRevPermute_evalOnCoset`: the planned forward transform
  evaluates on the coset, in bit-reversed order.
* `CosetPlan.inverseImpl_correct`: the planned inverse agrees with `NTT.Coset.inverseImpl`.
* `CosetPlan.interpolate_eq_interpolate`: planned coset interpolation is Lagrange
  interpolation on the nodes `g·ωᵏ`.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTTFast.powersAux
items.doc: Tail-recursive running product appending `w, w·g, …, w·g^(k-1)` to `acc`.
items.statement: def powersAux (g : R) : Nat → R → Array R → Array R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTTFast.powers
items.doc: The powers `#[1, g, …, g^(m-1)]`, by a running product.
items.statement: def powers (g : R) (m : Nat) : Array R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTTFast.powers_eq_ofFn
items.doc: The running product computes the powers of `g`.
items.statement:
theorem powers_eq_ofFn (g : R) (m : Nat) :
    powers g m = Array.ofFn (fun i : Fin m => g ^ (i : Nat))

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTTFast.scaleWith
items.doc: Scale the first `m` coefficients by a cached power table.
items.statement: def scaleWith (pows : Array R) (m : Nat) (a : Array R) : CPolynomial.Raw R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTTFast.scaleWith_powers
items.doc: Scaling with the cached powers of `g` is `NTT.Coset.scale g`.
items.statement:
theorem scaleWith_powers (g : R) (m : Nat) (a : Array R) :
    scaleWith (powers g m) m a = NTT.Coset.scale g m a

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTTFast.CosetPlan
items.doc: A reusable plan for transforms on the coset `g·⟨ω⟩` of the plan's domain.
items.statement:
structure CosetPlan (R : Type*) [Field R] where
  plan : Plan R
  shift : R
  shiftPowers : Array R
  shiftInvPowers : Array R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTTFast.CosetPlan.ofPlan
items.doc: Build a coset plan from a domain plan and a shift `g`.
items.statement: def ofPlan (P : Plan R) (g : R) : CosetPlan R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTTFast.CosetPlan.WellFormed
items.doc: A coset plan is well formed when its domain plan is and its power tables are exact.
items.statement: def WellFormed (C : CosetPlan R) : Prop

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTTFast.CosetPlan.ofPlan_wellFormed
items.statement:
theorem ofPlan_wellFormed (P : Plan R) (hP : Plan.WellFormed P) (g : R) :
    WellFormed (ofPlan P g)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTTFast.CosetPlan.forwardImpl
items.doc: Forward transform on the coset, returning values in bit-reversed order.
items.statement: def forwardImpl (C : CosetPlan R) (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) : Array R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTTFast.CosetPlan.inverseImpl
items.doc: Inverse transform on the coset, from values in bit-reversed order.
items.statement: def inverseImpl (C : CosetPlan R) (v : Array R) : CPolynomial.Raw R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTTFast.CosetPlan.forwardImpl_eq_bitRevPermute_evalOnCoset
items.doc: The planned coset forward transform evaluates on the coset, in bit-reversed order.
items.statement:
theorem forwardImpl_eq_bitRevPermute_evalOnCoset (C : CosetPlan R) (hC : WellFormed C)
    (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) (hdeg : p.toPoly.natDegree < C.plan.domain.n) :
    forwardImpl C p =
      NTT.Transform.bitRevPermute C.plan.domain
        (NTT.evalOnCoset C.plan.domain C.shift p)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTTFast.CosetPlan.inverseImpl_correct
items.doc: The planned coset inverse agrees with `NTT.Coset.inverseImpl` on bit-reversed input.
items.statement:
theorem inverseImpl_correct (C : CosetPlan R) (hC : WellFormed C) (v : Array R) :
    inverseImpl C (NTT.Transform.bitRevPermute C.plan.domain v) =
      NTT.Coset.inverseImpl C.plan.domain C.shift v

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTTFast.CosetPlan.interpolate
items.doc: Interpolate natural-order values on the coset through the cached plan.
items.statement:
def interpolate [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (C : CosetPlan R) (values : Vector R C.plan.domain.n) :
    CPolynomial R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTTFast.CosetPlan.interpolate_eq_coset_interpolate
items.doc: A well-formed coset plan interpolates as `NTT.Coset.interpolate`.
items.statement:
theorem interpolate_eq_coset_interpolate [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (C : CosetPlan R)
    (hC : WellFormed C) (values : Vector R C.plan.domain.n) :
    interpolate C values = NTT.Coset.interpolate C.plan.domain C.shift values

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTTFast.CosetPlan.interpolate_eq_interpolate
items.doc: Planned coset interpolation is Lagrange interpolation on the nodes `g·ωᵏ`.
items.statement:
theorem interpolate_eq_interpolate [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (C : CosetPlan R)
    (hC : WellFormed C) (hg : C.shift ≠ 0) (values : Vector R C.plan.domain.n) :
    interpolate C values =
      CLagrange.interpolate Finset.univ
        (fun k : C.plan.domain.Idx => C.shift * C.plan.domain.node k) values.get

modules.title: NTTFast and Interpolation
modules.doc:
Bridge theorem declarations deriving NTTFast interpolation facts from the shared
NTT specification layer.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTTFast.Plan.inverseImpl_interpolatePow_eq
items.doc:
A well-formed planned inverse interpolates the natural-order values when called on
the corresponding bit-reversed value array.
items.statement:
theorem inverseImpl_interpolatePow_eq [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (P : Plan R) (hP : WellFormed P) (values : Array R) :
    CPolynomial.Raw.trim (inverseImpl P (NTT.Transform.bitRevPermute P.domain values)) =
      (CLagrange.interpolatePow P.domain.omega
        (NTT.loadNaturalVector P.domain values)).val

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTTFast.Plan.inverseImpl_eval_node_eq
items.doc: Pointwise form of `inverseImpl_interpolatePow_eq` for a well-formed planned inverse.
items.statement:
theorem inverseImpl_eval_node_eq
    (P : Plan R) (hP : WellFormed P) (values : Array R) (k : P.domain.Idx) :
    CPolynomial.Raw.eval (P.domain.node k)
      (inverseImpl P (NTT.Transform.bitRevPermute P.domain values)) = values.getD k.1 0

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTTFast.Plan.inverseImpl_evalOnDomain_eq
items.doc: A well-formed planned inverse evaluates back to the natural-order input values.
items.statement:
theorem inverseImpl_evalOnDomain_eq
    (P : Plan R) (hP : WellFormed P) (values : Array R) :
    NTT.evalOnDomain P.domain (inverseImpl P (NTT.Transform.bitRevPermute P.domain values)) =
      NTT.loadNaturalArray P.domain values

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTTFast.Plan.interpolate
items.doc:
Interpolate natural-order values on the plan's domain with the cached inverse transform.

The planned counterpart of `NTT.interpolate`: for a well-formed plan it is
`CLagrange.interpolatePow` on the domain root (`interpolate_eq_interpolatePow`).
items.statement:
def interpolate [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (P : Plan R) (values : Vector R P.domain.n) :
    CPolynomial R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTTFast.Plan.interpolate_eq_ntt_interpolate
items.doc: A well-formed plan's interpolation agrees with the unplanned `NTT.interpolate`.
items.statement:
theorem interpolate_eq_ntt_interpolate [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (P : Plan R) (hP : WellFormed P) (values : Vector R P.domain.n) :
    interpolate P values = NTT.interpolate P.domain values

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.NTTFast.Plan.interpolate_eq_interpolatePow
items.doc: A well-formed plan interpolates by Lagrange's formula on the powers of the domain root.
items.statement:
theorem interpolate_eq_interpolatePow [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (P : Plan R) (hP : WellFormed P) (values : Vector R P.domain.n) :
    interpolate P values = CLagrange.interpolatePow P.domain.omega values

modules.authors: Quang Dao, Gregor Mitscha-Baude, Derek Sorensen
modules.title: Quotient of Univariate Polynomials
modules.doc:
This file defines `QuotientCPolynomial R`, the quotient of `CPolynomial.Raw R` by the equivalence
relation that identifies polynomials with the same coefficients (allowing zero-padding).
This quotient is intended to be equivalent to mathlib's `Polynomial R`.

Operations on `CPolynomial.Raw` (addition, multiplication, etc.) are shown to respect the
equivalence relation and thus descend to the quotient.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.equiv_refl
items.doc: Reflexivity of the equivalence relation.
items.statement: theorem equiv_refl [Zero Q] (p : CPolynomial.Raw Q) : equiv p p

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.equiv_symm
items.doc: Symmetry of the equivalence relation.
items.statement: theorem equiv_symm [Zero Q] {p q : CPolynomial.Raw Q} : equiv p q → equiv q p

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.equiv_trans
items.doc: Transitivity of the equivalence relation.
items.statement:
theorem equiv_trans [Zero Q] {p q r : CPolynomial.Raw Q} :
    Trim.equiv p q → equiv q r → equiv p r

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.instEquivalenceEquiv
items.doc: The `CPolynomial.Raw.equiv` is indeed an equivalence relation.
items.statement: theorem instEquivalenceEquiv [Zero R] : Equivalence (equiv (R := R))

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.instSetoidCPolynomial
items.doc: The `Setoid` instance for `CPolynomial.Raw R` induced by `CPolynomial.Raw.equiv`.
items.statement: instance Raw.instSetoidCPolynomial [Zero R] : Setoid (CPolynomial.Raw R)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.QuotientCPolynomial
items.doc:
The quotient of `CPolynomial.Raw R` by coefficient-wise equivalence.

This quotient identifies polynomials that differ only by trailing zeros, and is intended
to be equivalent to mathlib's `Polynomial R`.
items.statement: def QuotientCPolynomial (R : Type*) [Zero R]

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.QuotientCPolynomial.eq_to_equiv
items.doc: Convert propositional equality to equivalence.
items.statement: lemma eq_to_equiv [Zero R] (p q : CPolynomial.Raw R) : p = q → p ≈ q

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.QuotientCPolynomial.smul_zero_equiv
items.doc: Scalar multiplication by 0 is equivalent to the zero polynomial.
items.statement:
lemma smul_zero_equiv {R : Type*} [Semiring R] (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) :
    (smul 0 p) ≈ 0

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.QuotientCPolynomial.add_equiv
items.doc: Addition respects the equivalence relation.
items.statement:
lemma add_equiv {R : Type*} [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (p1 p2 q1 q2 : CPolynomial.Raw R)
  (hp : equiv p1 p2) (hq : equiv q1 q2) :
  equiv (p1.add q1) (p2.add q2)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.QuotientCPolynomial.mulPowX_equiv
items.doc: Multiplication by `X^i` respects the equivalence relation.
items.statement:
lemma mulPowX_equiv {R : Type*} [Zero R]
    (i : ℕ) (p q : CPolynomial.Raw R) (h : equiv p q) :
  equiv (mulPowX i p) (mulPowX i q)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.QuotientCPolynomial.add_zero_equiv
items.doc: Adding a polynomial equivalent to zero acts as the identity.
items.statement:
lemma add_zero_equiv {R : Type*} [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (p q : CPolynomial.Raw R) (hq : equiv q 0) :
  equiv (add p q) p

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.QuotientCPolynomial.mulPowX_zero_equiv
items.doc: Multiplying the zero polynomial by `X^i` results in a polynomial equivalent to zero.
items.statement:
lemma mulPowX_zero_equiv {R : Type*} [Zero R]
    (i : ℕ) : equiv (mulPowX i (0 : CPolynomial.Raw R)) 0

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.QuotientCPolynomial.mulStep
items.doc: A single step in polynomial multiplication: add `(coefficient * q) * X^power` to accumulator.
items.statement:
def mulStep {R : Type*} [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (q : CPolynomial.Raw R) (acc : CPolynomial.Raw R) (x : R × ℕ) : CPolynomial.Raw R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.QuotientCPolynomial.mulStep_equiv
items.doc: The multiplication step respects equivalence of the accumulator.
items.statement:
lemma mulStep_equiv {R : Type*} [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (q : CPolynomial.Raw R) (acc1 acc2 : CPolynomial.Raw R) (x : R × ℕ)
  (h : equiv acc1 acc2) :
  equiv (mulStep q acc1 x) (mulStep q acc2 x)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.QuotientCPolynomial.mulStep_zero
items.doc: The multiplication step with a zero coefficient acts as the identity modulo equivalence.
items.statement:
lemma mulStep_zero {R : Type*} [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (q : CPolynomial.Raw R) (acc : CPolynomial.Raw R) (i : ℕ) :
  equiv (mulStep q acc (0, i)) acc

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.QuotientCPolynomial.foldl_mulStep_zeros
items.doc: Folding `mulStep` over a list of zero coefficients preserves equivalence.
items.statement:
lemma foldl_mulStep_zeros {R : Type*} [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (q : CPolynomial.Raw R) (acc : CPolynomial.Raw R) (l : List (R × ℕ))
  (hl : ∀ x ∈ l, x.1 = 0) :
  equiv (l.foldl (mulStep q) acc) acc

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.QuotientCPolynomial.zipIdx_trim_append
items.doc: The `zipIdx` of a polynomial is the `zipIdx` of its trim followed by zero coefficients.
items.statement:
lemma zipIdx_trim_append {R : Type*} [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) :
    ∃ l, p.zipIdx.toList = p.trim.zipIdx.toList ++ l ∧ ∀ x ∈ l, x.1 = 0

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.QuotientCPolynomial.mul_trim_equiv
items.doc: Multiplication by a trimmed polynomial is equivalent to multiplication by the original.
items.statement:
lemma mul_trim_equiv [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (a b : CPolynomial.Raw R) :
    a.mul b ≈ a.trim.mul b

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.QuotientCPolynomial.mul_equiv
items.doc: Multiplication is well-defined on the left with respect to equivalence.
items.statement:
lemma mul_equiv [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (a₁ a₂ b : CPolynomial.Raw R) :
    a₁ ≈ a₂ → a₁.mul b ≈ a₂.mul b

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.QuotientCPolynomial.mul_equiv₂
items.doc: Multiplication is well-defined on the right with respect to equivalence.
items.statement:
lemma mul_equiv₂ [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (a b₁ b₂ : CPolynomial.Raw R) :
    b₁ ≈ b₂ → a.mul b₁ ≈ a.mul b₂

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.QuotientCPolynomial.addDescending
items.doc: Helper function showing addition descends to the quotient.
items.statement:
def addDescending [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (p q : CPolynomial.Raw R) : QuotientCPolynomial R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.QuotientCPolynomial.add_descends
items.statement:
lemma add_descends [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (a₁ b₁ a₂ b₂ : CPolynomial.Raw R) :
    equiv a₁ a₂ → equiv b₁ b₂ → addDescending a₁ b₁ = addDescending a₂ b₂

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.QuotientCPolynomial.add
items.doc: Addition on the quotient.
items.statement:
def add {R : Type*} [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (p q : QuotientCPolynomial R) :
    QuotientCPolynomial R

items.doc: Helper function showing scalar multiplication descends to the quotient.
items.statement: def smulDescending [Semiring R] (r : R) (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) : QuotientCPolynomial R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.QuotientCPolynomial.smul_descends
items.statement:
lemma smul_descends [Semiring R] (r : R) (p₁ p₂ : CPolynomial.Raw R) :
    equiv p₁ p₂ → smulDescending r p₁ = smulDescending r p₂

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.QuotientCPolynomial.smul
items.doc: Scalar multiplication on the quotient.
items.statement:
def smul {R : Type*} [Semiring R] (r : R) (p : QuotientCPolynomial R) :
    QuotientCPolynomial R

items.statement: def nsmulDescending [Semiring R] [BEq R] (n : ℕ) (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) : QuotientCPolynomial R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.QuotientCPolynomial.nsmul_descends
items.statement:
lemma nsmul_descends [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (n : ℕ)

    equiv p₁ p₂ → nsmulDescending n p₁ = nsmulDescending n p₂

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.QuotientCPolynomial.nsmul

items.statement:
lemma neg_descends [NegZeroClass R] (a b : CPolynomial.Raw R) :

items.statement:

modules.title: QuotientCPolynomial <-> Polynomial Isomorphism
modules.doc:
This file establishes the ring equivalence between `QuotientCPolynomial R`
(the quotient of `CPolynomial.Raw R` by coefficient-wise equivalence) and
mathlib's `Polynomial R`.

## Main declarations

* `QuotientCPolynomial.toPoly` - quotient -> Polynomial via `Quotient.lift` on `Raw.toPoly`
* `QuotientCPolynomial.ofPoly` - Polynomial -> quotient via `Quotient.mk` on `Polynomial.toImpl`
* `QuotientCPolynomial.toPoly_ofPoly` - round-trip identity `toPoly ∘ ofPoly = id`
* `QuotientCPolynomial.ofPoly_toPoly` - round-trip identity `ofPoly ∘ toPoly = id`
* `QuotientCPolynomial.ringEquiv` - the ring equivalence `QuotientCPolynomial R ≃+* Polynomial R`

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.QuotientCPolynomial.toPoly_resp
items.doc: Well-definedness: equivalent raw polynomials map to the same `Polynomial`.
items.statement:
theorem toPoly_resp (p q : CPolynomial.Raw R) (h : p ≈ q) :
    p.toPoly = q.toPoly

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.QuotientCPolynomial.toPoly
items.doc:
Convert a `QuotientCPolynomial` to a mathlib `Polynomial R`.

Defined by lifting `Raw.toPoly` through the quotient; well-definedness follows from
the fact that equivalent raw polynomials have equal coefficients.
items.statement: noncomputable def toPoly (p : QuotientCPolynomial R) : Polynomial R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.QuotientCPolynomial.ofPoly
items.doc:
Convert a mathlib `Polynomial R` to a `QuotientCPolynomial R`.

Defined by extracting coefficients via `Polynomial.toImpl` and taking the
equivalence class.
items.statement: def ofPoly (p : Polynomial R) : QuotientCPolynomial R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.QuotientCPolynomial.toPoly_ofPoly
items.doc: Round-trip identity: `toPoly ∘ ofPoly = id`.
items.statement: theorem toPoly_ofPoly (p : Polynomial R) : toPoly (ofPoly p) = p

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.QuotientCPolynomial.ofPoly_toPoly
items.doc: Round-trip identity: `ofPoly ∘ toPoly = id`.
items.statement:
theorem ofPoly_toPoly [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (q : QuotientCPolynomial R) :
    ofPoly (toPoly q) = q

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.QuotientCPolynomial.ringEquiv
items.doc:
The ring equivalence between `QuotientCPolynomial R` and `Polynomial R`.

The forward map is `toPoly` (quotient-lift of `Raw.toPoly`); the inverse is
`ofPoly` (coefficient extraction via `Polynomial.toImpl`).
Preserves both addition and multiplication.
items.statement: noncomputable def ringEquiv [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] : QuotientCPolynomial R ≃+* Polynomial R

modules.title: Raw Univariate Algorithm Contexts
modules.doc:
Array-level execution dictionaries for reusable raw univariate polynomial
kernels.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.MulContext
items.doc: Internal raw multiplication backend for array-level polynomial kernels.
items.statement:
structure MulContext (R : Type*) [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] where
  /-- Multiply two raw polynomials, returning the trimmed raw product. -/
  mul : CPolynomial.Raw R → CPolynomial.Raw R → CPolynomial.Raw R
  /-- The backend agrees with raw polynomial multiplication. -/
  mul_eq_mul : ∀ p q, mul p q = p * q

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.ModContext
items.doc: Internal raw monic-remainder backend for array-level polynomial kernels.
items.statement:
structure ModContext (R : Type*) [Field R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] where
  /-- Reduce the first raw polynomial modulo the second raw monic divisor. -/
  modByMonic : CPolynomial.Raw R → CPolynomial.Raw R → CPolynomial.Raw R
  /-- The backend agrees with raw monic remainders for canonical raw inputs. -/
  modByMonic_eq_modByMonic :
    ∀ p q, p.trim = p → q.trim = q → modByMonic p q = CPolynomial.Raw.modByMonic p q

modules.authors: Quang Dao, Gregor Mitscha-Baude, Derek Sorensen, Desmond Coles
modules.title: Raw Computable Univariate Polynomials
modules.doc: Core definitions for array-backed computable univariate polynomials.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw
items.doc:
A type analogous to `Polynomial` that supports computable operations. This is defined to be a
wrapper around `Array`.

For example, the Array `#[1,2,3]` represents the polynomial `1 + 2x + 3x^2`.
Two arrays may represent the same polynomial via zero-padding,
for example `#[1,2,3] = #[1,2,3,0,0,0,...]`.
items.statement: def CPolynomial.Raw (R : Type*)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.mk
items.doc: Construct a `CPolynomial.Raw` from an array of coefficients.
items.statement: def mk {R : Type*} (coeffs : Array R) : CPolynomial.Raw R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.coeffs
items.doc: Extract the underlying array of coefficients.
items.statement: def coeffs {R : Type*} (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) : Array R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.coeff
items.doc: The coefficient of `X^i` in the polynomial. Returns `0` if `i` is out of bounds.
items.statement: def coeff [Zero R] (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) (i : ℕ) : R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.C
items.doc: The constant polynomial `C r`.
items.statement: def C (r : R) : CPolynomial.Raw R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.X
items.doc: The variable `X`.
items.statement: def X [Zero R] [One R] : CPolynomial.Raw R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.monomial
items.doc:
Construct a monomial `c * X^n` as a `CPolynomial.Raw R`.

The result is an array with `n` zeros followed by `c`.
For example, `monomial 2 3` = `#[0, 0, 3]` represents `3 * X^2`.

Note: If `c = 0`, this returns `#[]` (the zero polynomial).
items.statement: def monomial [Zero R] [DecidableEq R] (n : ℕ) (c : R) : CPolynomial.Raw R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.lastNonzero
items.doc: Return the index of the last non-zero coefficient of a `CPolynomial.Raw`
items.statement: def lastNonzero [Zero R] [BEq R] (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) : Option (Fin p.size)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.trim
items.doc:
Remove trailing zeroes from a `CPolynomial.Raw`.
Requires `BEq` to check if the coefficients are zero.
items.statement: def trim [Zero R] [BEq R] (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) : CPolynomial.Raw R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.degree
items.doc: Return the degree of a `CPolynomial.Raw`.
items.statement: def degree [Zero R] [BEq R] (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) : WithBot ℕ

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.natDegree
items.doc:
Natural number degree of a `CPolynomial.Raw`.

Returns the degree as a natural number. For the zero polynomial, returns `0`.
This matches Mathlib's `Polynomial.natDegree` API.
items.statement: def natDegree [Zero R] [BEq R] (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) : ℕ

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.leadingCoeff
items.doc:
Return the leading coefficient of a `CPolynomial.Raw` as the last coefficient
of the trimmed array, or `0` if the trimmed array is empty.
items.statement: def leadingCoeff [Zero R] [BEq R] (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) : R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.IsCanonical
items.doc:
Semantic canonicality for raw coefficient arrays: a polynomial is canonical iff its
last stored coefficient, when present, is nonzero. This invariant is independent of any
particular `BEq` instance.
items.statement: def IsCanonical [Zero R] (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) : Prop

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.canonical
items.doc: A polynomial is canonical if it has no trailing zeros, i.e. `p.trim = p`.
items.statement: def canonical [Zero R] [BEq R] (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) : Prop

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.Trim.lastNonzero_none
items.doc: If all coefficients are zero, `lastNonzero` is `none`.
items.statement:
theorem lastNonzero_none [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] {p : CPolynomial.Raw R} :
    (∀ i, (hi : i < p.size) → p[i] = 0) → p.lastNonzero = none

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.Trim.lastNonzero_some
items.doc: If there is a non-zero coefficient, `lastNonzero` is `some`.
items.statement:
theorem lastNonzero_some [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    {p : CPolynomial.Raw R} {i} (hi : i < p.size)
    (h : p[i] ≠ 0) : ∃ k, p.lastNonzero = some k

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.Trim.lastNonzero_spec
items.doc: `lastNonzero` returns the largest index with a non-zero coefficient.
items.statement:
theorem lastNonzero_spec [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] {p : CPolynomial.Raw R} {k} :
    p.lastNonzero = some k
  → p[k] ≠ 0 ∧ (∀ j, (hj : j < p.size) → j > k → p[j] = 0)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.Trim.lastNonzeroProp
items.doc: The property that an index is the last non-zero coefficient.
items.statement: def lastNonzeroProp [Zero R] {p : CPolynomial.Raw R} (k : Fin p.size) : Prop

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.Trim.lastNonzero_unique
items.doc: The last non-zero index is unique.
items.statement:
lemma lastNonzero_unique [Zero Q] {p : CPolynomial.Raw Q} {k k' : Fin p.size} :
    lastNonzeroProp k → lastNonzeroProp k' → k = k'

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.Trim.lastNonzero_some_iff
items.doc: Characterization of `lastNonzero` via `lastNonzeroProp`.
items.statement:
theorem lastNonzero_some_iff [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] {p : CPolynomial.Raw R} {k} :
    p.lastNonzero = some k ↔ (p[k] ≠ 0 ∧ (∀ j, (hj : j < p.size) → j > k → p[j] = 0))

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.Trim.lastNonzero_induct
items.doc:
eliminator for `p.lastNonzero`, e.g. use with the induction tactic as follows:
```
induction p using lastNonzero_induct with
| case1 p h_none h_all_zero => ...
| case2 p k h_some h_nonzero h_max => ...
```
items.statement:
theorem lastNonzero_induct [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] {motive : CPolynomial.Raw R → Prop}
    (case1 : ∀ p, p.lastNonzero = none → (∀ i, (hi : i < p.size) → p[i] = 0) → motive p)
  (case2 : ∀ p : CPolynomial.Raw R, ∀ k : Fin p.size, p.lastNonzero = some k → p[k] ≠ 0 →
    (∀ j : ℕ, (hj : j < p.size) → j > k → p[j] = 0) → motive p)
  (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) : motive p

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.Trim.induct
items.doc:
eliminator for `p.trim`; use with the induction tactic as follows:
```
induction p using induct with
| case1 p h_empty h_all_zero => ...
| case2 p k h_extract h_nonzero h_max => ...
```
items.statement:
theorem induct [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] {motive : CPolynomial.Raw R → Prop}
    (case1 : ∀ p, p.trim = #[] → (∀ i, (hi : i < p.size) → p[i] = 0) → motive p)
  (case2 : ∀ p : CPolynomial.Raw R, ∀ k : Fin p.size, p.trim = p.extract 0 (k + 1)
    → p[k] ≠ 0 → (∀ j : ℕ, (hj : j < p.size) → j > k → p[j] = 0) → motive p)
  (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) : motive p

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.Trim.elim
items.doc:
eliminator for `p.trim`; e.g. use for case distinction as follows:
```
rcases (Trim.elim p) with ⟨ h_empty, h_all_zero ⟩ | ⟨ k, h_extract, h_nonzero, h_max ⟩
```
items.statement:
theorem elim [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) :
    (p.trim = #[] ∧  (∀ i, (hi : i < p.size) → p[i] = 0))
    ∨ (∃ k : Fin p.size,
        p.trim = p.extract 0 (k + 1)
      ∧ p[k] ≠ 0
      ∧ (∀ j : ℕ, (hj : j < p.size) → j > k → p[j] = 0))

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.Trim.size_eq_degree_plus_one
items.statement:
theorem size_eq_degree_plus_one [Zero R] [BEq R]
    (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) (h_trim : p.trim ≠ (mk #[])) :
    p.trim.size = p.degree + 1

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.Trim.size_eq_natDegree_plus_one
items.statement:
theorem size_eq_natDegree_plus_one [Zero R] [BEq R]
    (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) (h_trim : p.trim ≠ (mk #[])) :
    p.trim.size = p.natDegree + 1

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.Trim.size_eq_natDegree_of_zero
items.statement:
theorem size_eq_natDegree_of_zero [Zero R] [BEq R]
    (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) (h_trim : p.trim = (mk #[])) :
    p.trim.size = p.natDegree

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.Trim.size_le_size
items.statement: theorem size_le_size [Zero R] [BEq R] (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) : p.trim.size ≤ p.size

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.Trim.coeff_eq_getElem_of_lt
items.statement:
theorem coeff_eq_getElem_of_lt [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    {p : CPolynomial.Raw R} {i} (hi : i < p.size) :
    p.trim.coeff i = p[i]

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.Trim.coeff_eq_coeff
items.statement:
theorem coeff_eq_coeff [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) (i : ℕ) :
    p.trim.coeff i = p.coeff i

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.Trim.coeff_eq_getElem
items.statement:
lemma coeff_eq_getElem [Zero Q] {p : CPolynomial.Raw Q} {i} (hp : i < p.size) :
    p.coeff i = p[i]

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.Trim.equiv
items.doc: Equivalence relation: two polynomials are equivalent if all coefficients agree.
items.statement: def equiv [Zero R] (p q : CPolynomial.Raw R) : Prop

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.Trim.coeff_eq_zero
items.statement:
lemma coeff_eq_zero [Zero Q] {p : CPolynomial.Raw Q} :
    (∀ i, (hi : i < p.size) → p[i] = 0) ↔ ∀ i, p.coeff i = 0

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.Trim.eq_degree_of_equiv
items.statement:
lemma eq_degree_of_equiv [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] {p q : CPolynomial.Raw R} :
    equiv p q → p.degree = q.degree

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.Trim.eq_of_equiv
items.statement:
theorem eq_of_equiv [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] {p q : CPolynomial.Raw R} :
    equiv p q → p.trim = q.trim

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.Trim.trim_equiv
items.statement:
theorem trim_equiv [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) :
    equiv p.trim p

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.Trim.trim_twice
items.statement:
theorem trim_twice [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) :
    p.trim.trim = p.trim

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.Trim.canonical_empty
items.statement: theorem canonical_empty [Zero R] [BEq R] : (mk (R := R) #[]).trim = #[]

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.Trim.canonical_of_size_zero
items.statement:
theorem canonical_of_size_zero [Zero R] [BEq R] {p : CPolynomial.Raw R} :
    p.size = 0 → p.trim = p

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.Trim.canonical_nonempty_iff
items.statement:
theorem canonical_nonempty_iff [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    {p : CPolynomial.Raw R} (hp : p.size > 0) :
    p.trim = p ↔ p.lastNonzero = some ⟨ p.size - 1, Nat.pred_lt_self hp ⟩

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.Trim.lastNonzero_last_iff
items.statement:
theorem lastNonzero_last_iff [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    {p : CPolynomial.Raw R} (hp : p.size > 0) :
    p.lastNonzero = some ⟨ p.size - 1, Nat.pred_lt_self hp ⟩ ↔ p.getLast hp ≠ 0

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.Trim.canonical_iff
items.statement:
theorem canonical_iff [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] {p : CPolynomial.Raw R} :
    p.trim = p ↔ IsCanonical p

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.Trim.isCanonical_empty
items.statement: theorem isCanonical_empty [Zero R] : IsCanonical (mk (R := R) #[])

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.Trim.isCanonical_of_size_zero
items.statement:
theorem isCanonical_of_size_zero [Zero R] {p : CPolynomial.Raw R} (hp : p.size = 0) :
    IsCanonical p

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.Trim.isCanonical_iff_trim_eq
items.doc: Canonicality bridge (semantic view to computational view).
items.statement:
theorem isCanonical_iff_trim_eq [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    {p : CPolynomial.Raw R} :
    IsCanonical p ↔ p.trim = p

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.Trim.isCanonical_iff_size_eq_zero_or_getLastD_ne_zero
items.doc: Non-dependent canonicality criterion using `getLastD`.
items.statement:
theorem isCanonical_iff_size_eq_zero_or_getLastD_ne_zero [Zero R]
    {p : CPolynomial.Raw R} :
    IsCanonical p ↔ p.size = 0 ∨ p.getLastD 0 ≠ 0

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.Trim.trim_eq_iff_size_eq_zero_or_getLastD_ne_zero
items.doc: Computational canonicality criterion in non-dependent form.
items.statement:
theorem trim_eq_iff_size_eq_zero_or_getLastD_ne_zero [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    {p : CPolynomial.Raw R} :
    p.trim = p ↔ p.size = 0 ∨ p.getLastD 0 ≠ 0

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.Trim.trim_eq_of_isCanonical
items.statement:
theorem trim_eq_of_isCanonical [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    {p : CPolynomial.Raw R} (hp : IsCanonical p) :
    p.trim = p

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.Trim.isCanonical_of_trim_eq
items.statement:
theorem isCanonical_of_trim_eq [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    {p : CPolynomial.Raw R} (hp : p.trim = p) :
    IsCanonical p

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.Trim.isCanonical_trim
items.statement:
theorem isCanonical_trim [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) : IsCanonical p.trim

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.Trim.push_trim
items.statement:
lemma push_trim [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (arr : Array R) (c : R) :
    ¬c = 0 → trim (arr.push c) = arr.push c

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.Trim.non_zero_map
items.statement:
theorem non_zero_map [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (f : R → R) (hf : ∀ r, f r = 0 → r = 0) (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) :
    let fp := mk (p.map f);
  p.trim = p → fp.trim = fp

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.Trim.canonical_ext
items.doc:
Canonical polynomials enjoy a stronger extensionality theorem:
they just need to agree at all coefficients (without assuming equal sizes)
items.statement:
theorem canonical_ext [Zero R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    {p q : CPolynomial.Raw R} (hp : p.trim = p) (hq : q.trim = q) :
    equiv p q → p = q

modules.authors: Quang Dao, Gregor Mitscha-Baude, Derek Sorensen, Desmond Coles, Natalie Klaus, Dimitris Mitsios, Alexander Hicks
modules.title: Raw Univariate Polynomial Operations
modules.doc:
Operations and evaluation lemmas for raw computable univariate polynomials. The file also states
the sizes of `smul`, `mulPowX`, `addRaw` and `mulRaw`, and the coefficients of `addRaw`, of a
shifted `smul` and of `mulRaw`. It defines `mulRawFast`, a loop for `mulRaw` that computes each
entry of the result as one sum. The `@[csimp]` lemma `mulRaw_eq_mulRawFast` makes compiled code
compute `mulRaw` with `mulRawFast`.

`size_smul`, `size_mulPowX`, `size_addRaw` and `size_mulRaw` were ported from ArkLib's raw-size
adapter under Apache 2.0. The file header records their copyright.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.eval₂
items.doc:
Evaluates a `CPolynomial.Raw` at `x : S` using a ring homomorphism `f : R →+* S`.

Computes `f(a₀) + f(a₁) * x + f(a₂) * x² + ...` where `aᵢ` are the coefficients.
items.statement: def eval₂ [Semiring R] [Semiring S] (f : R →+* S) (x : S) (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) : S

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.eval₂Horner
items.doc:
Evaluates a `CPolynomial.Raw` at `x : S` using Horner's method.

Computes `f(aₙ) + x * (f(aₙ₋₁) + x * (... + x * f(a₀)))` via a right fold.
items.statement: def eval₂Horner [Semiring R] [Semiring S] (f : R →+* S) (x : S) (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) : S

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.eval
items.doc: Evaluates a `CPolynomial.Raw` at a given value
items.statement: def eval [Semiring R] (x : R) (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) : R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.evalHorner
items.doc: Evaluates a `CPolynomial.Raw` at a given value using Horner's method.
items.statement: def evalHorner [Semiring R] (x : R) (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) : R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.addRaw
items.doc:
Raw addition: pointwise sum of coefficient arrays (padded to equal length).

The result may have trailing zeros and should be trimmed for canonical form.
items.statement: def addRaw [Zero R] [Add R] (p q : CPolynomial.Raw R) : CPolynomial.Raw R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.add
items.doc: Addition of two `CPolynomial.Raw`s, with result trimmed.
items.statement: def add [Zero R] [Add R] [BEq R] (p q : CPolynomial.Raw R) : CPolynomial.Raw R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.smul
items.doc: Scalar multiplication: multiplies each coefficient by `r`.
items.statement: def smul [Mul R] (r : R) (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) : CPolynomial.Raw R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.smulRight
items.doc:
Right scalar multiplication: multiplies each coefficient by `r` on the right.

Corresponds to `p.toPoly * Polynomial.C r`, in contrast to `smul` which corresponds
to `Polynomial.C r * p.toPoly`. The distinction matters in non-commutative semirings.
items.statement: def smulRight [Mul R] (r : R) (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) : CPolynomial.Raw R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.nsmulRaw
items.doc: Raw scalar multiplication by a natural number (may have trailing zeros).
items.statement: def nsmulRaw [Semiring R] (n : ℕ) (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) : CPolynomial.Raw R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.nsmul
items.doc: Scalar multiplication of `CPolynomial.Raw` by a natural number, with result trimmed.
items.statement: def nsmul [Semiring R] [BEq R] (n : ℕ) (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) : CPolynomial.Raw R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.mulPowX
items.doc: Multiplication by `X^i`: shifts coefficients right by `i` positions (prepends `i` zeros).
items.statement: def mulPowX [Zero R] (i : Nat) (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) : CPolynomial.Raw R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.mulX
items.doc: Multiplication of a `CPolynomial.Raw` by `X`, reduces to `mulPowX 1`.
items.statement: def mulX [Zero R] (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) : CPolynomial.Raw R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.mulRaw
items.doc:
Multiplication accumulator using the naive `O(n²)` algorithm: `Σᵢ (aᵢ * q) * X^i`.

The partial sums are combined with the untrimmed `addRaw`, so the result may carry
trailing zeros and should be trimmed for canonical form. Deferring the trim to the
end (see `mul`) avoids an `O(size)` scan after every partial sum.

Compiled code computes `mulRaw` with `mulRawFast` (see `mulRaw_eq_mulRawFast`).
items.statement: def mulRaw [Semiring R] (p q : CPolynomial.Raw R) : CPolynomial.Raw R

items.note:
### Sizes and coefficients of the operations in `mulRaw`

The sizes count the stored coefficients, including trailing zeros.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.size_smul
items.doc: Scalar multiplication preserves the stored coefficient count.
items.statement:
theorem size_smul [Mul R] (x : R) (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) :
    (smul x p).size = p.size

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.size_mulPowX
items.doc: Multiplication by `X^i` retains all of the prepended zero coefficients.
items.statement:
theorem size_mulPowX [Zero R] (i : Nat) (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) :
    (mulPowX i p).size = i + p.size

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.size_addRaw
items.doc: Padded raw addition stores the larger input size.
items.statement:
theorem size_addRaw [Zero Q] [Add Q] {p q : CPolynomial.Raw Q} :
    (addRaw p q).size = max p.size q.size

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.add_coeff?
items.doc: Coefficient `i` of `addRaw p q` is the sum of coefficient `i` of `p` and of `q`.
items.statement:
theorem add_coeff? [AddZeroClass Q] (p q : CPolynomial.Raw Q) (i : ℕ) :
    (addRaw p q).coeff i = p.coeff i + q.coeff i

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.smul_mulPowX_coeff
items.doc:
Coefficient `k` of `smul a q` shifted by `i` places: `0` below `i`, and `a * q.coeff (k - i)`
from `i` on.
items.statement:
theorem smul_mulPowX_coeff [MulZeroClass R] (a : R) (q : CPolynomial.Raw R) (i k : ℕ) :
    ((smul a q).mulPowX i).coeff k = if k < i then 0 else a * q.coeff (k - i)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.size_mulRaw
items.doc: Raw multiplication retains every shifted row, including padding from an empty right array.
items.statement:
theorem size_mulRaw [Semiring R] (p q : CPolynomial.Raw R) :
    (mulRaw p q).size = if p.size = 0 then 0 else q.size + p.size - 1

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.coeff_mulRaw
items.doc: Coefficient `k` of `mulRaw p q` is the convolution sum of the coefficients of `p` and `q`.
items.statement:
theorem coeff_mulRaw [Semiring R] (p q : CPolynomial.Raw R) (k : ℕ) :
    (mulRaw p q).coeff k =
      ∑ i ∈ Finset.range p.size, if k < i then 0 else p.coeff i * q.coeff (k - i)

items.note:
### Compiled raw multiplication

`mulRawFast` computes the same array as `mulRaw`. The `@[csimp]` lemma `mulRaw_eq_mulRawFast`
makes compiled code use it. The lemma comes before `mul` and the other definitions in this file
that use `mulRaw`. When the compiler compiles such a definition, it inlines or specializes `mulRaw`
into the code. A `@[csimp]` lemma later in the file would not change that code.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.mulRawFast
items.doc:
Raw multiplication that computes each entry of the result as one sum.

The result is empty when `p` is empty. Otherwise it has `q.size + p.size - 1` entries, as in
`mulRaw`. Entry `k` is the sum of the products `p[i] * q[k - i]` over the indices `i` with
`k + 1 - q.size ≤ i < min (k + 1) p.size`, added to `0` in increasing order of `i`. Each pair
`(i, j)` with `i < p.size` and `j < q.size` occurs in exactly one entry, so the loop makes
`p.size * q.size` multiplications and the same number of additions.
items.statement: def mulRawFast [inst : Semiring R] (p q : CPolynomial.Raw R) : CPolynomial.Raw R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.size_mulRawFast
items.doc: `mulRawFast p q` is empty when `p` is empty. Otherwise it has `q.size + p.size - 1` entries.
items.statement:
theorem size_mulRawFast [Semiring R] (p q : CPolynomial.Raw R) :
    (mulRawFast p q).size = if p.size = 0 then 0 else q.size + p.size - 1

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.getElem_mulRawFast
items.doc: Entry `k` of `mulRawFast p q` is the convolution sum of the coefficients of `p` and `q`.
items.statement:
theorem getElem_mulRawFast [Semiring R] (p q : CPolynomial.Raw R) (k : ℕ)
    (hk : k < (mulRawFast p q).size) :
    (mulRawFast p q)[k] =
      ∑ i ∈ Finset.range p.size, if k < i then 0 else p.coeff i * q.coeff (k - i)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.mulRaw_eq_mulRawFast
items.doc:
`mulRaw` equals `mulRawFast`. As a `@[csimp]` lemma, it makes compiled code use
`mulRawFast`.
items.statement: theorem mulRaw_eq_mulRawFast : @mulRaw = @mulRawFast

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.mul
items.doc:
Multiplication using the naive `O(n²)` algorithm: `Σᵢ (aᵢ * q) * X^i`.

Trims only once, at the end of the convolution fold, rather than after every
partial sum (`mulRaw` does the untrimmed accumulation). Compiled code computes the product with
`mulRawFast` (see `mulRaw_eq_mulRawFast`).
items.statement: def mul [Semiring R] [BEq R] (p q : CPolynomial.Raw R) : CPolynomial.Raw R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.pow
items.doc:
Exponentiation of a `CPolynomial.Raw` by a natural number `n` via repeated multiplication.
This is the specification; `powBySq` is the efficient O(log n) implementation.
items.statement: def pow [Semiring R] [BEq R] (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) (n : Nat) : CPolynomial.Raw R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.powBySqUntrimmed
items.doc:
Repeated-squaring core that accumulates with the untrimmed `mulRaw`, deferring
the canonicalization trim to the outer `powBySq` wrapper. The output may carry
trailing zeros and is not in canonical form. Compiled code computes each product with
`mulRawFast`.

For $ n > 0 $, computes $ p ^ n $ by recursing on $ n / 2 $:
* If $ n $ is even: $ (p ^ {n/2})^2 $
* If $ n $ is odd:  $ p \cdot (p ^ {n/2})^2 $
items.statement: def powBySqUntrimmed [Semiring R] (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) : Nat → CPolynomial.Raw R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.powBySq
items.doc:
Exponentiation via repeated squaring: $ O(\log n) $ multiplications
instead of $ O(n) $. Delegates to `powBySqUntrimmed` and trims only once
at the end, rather than after every squaring step.
items.statement: def powBySq [Semiring R] [BEq R] (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) (n : Nat) : CPolynomial.Raw R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.truncate
items.doc: Keep only the stored coefficients with index `< k`.
items.statement: def truncate [Zero R] (k : Nat) (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) : CPolynomial.Raw R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.takeLow
items.doc: Return exactly the first `k` coefficients, padding missing coefficients with zero.
items.statement: def takeLow [Zero R] (k : Nat) (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) : CPolynomial.Raw R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.reverse
items.doc: Reverse the first `n` coefficients, padding missing coefficients with zero.
items.statement: def reverse [Zero R] (n : Nat) (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) : CPolynomial.Raw R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.mulLowConvolution
items.doc: Low product computed by the coefficient convolution formula.
items.statement: def mulLowConvolution [Semiring R] (k : Nat) (p q : CPolynomial.Raw R) : CPolynomial.Raw R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.MulLowContext
items.doc: Backend for computing the low `k` coefficients of a raw product.
items.statement:
structure MulLowContext (R : Type*) [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] where
  /-- Return the low `k` coefficients of `p * q`. -/
  mulLow : Nat → CPolynomial.Raw R → CPolynomial.Raw R → CPolynomial.Raw R
  /-- The backend does not return coefficients at degree `>= k`. -/
  size_le : ∀ k p q, (mulLow k p q).size ≤ k
  /-- Low coefficients agree with ordinary raw multiplication. -/
  coeff_of_lt : ∀ k p q i, i < k → (mulLow k p q).coeff i = (p * q).coeff i

items.doc: Upper bound on degree: `size - 1` if non-empty, `⊥` if empty.
items.statement: def degreeBound (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) : WithBot Nat

items.statement: def monic [Zero R] [One R] [BEq R] (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) : Bool

items.doc: Pseudo-division by `X`: removes the constant term and shifts remaining coefficients left.
items.statement: def divX (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) : CPolynomial.Raw R

items.statement: def neg [Neg R] (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) : CPolynomial.Raw R

modules.authors: Quang Dao, Gregor Mitscha-Baude, Derek Sorensen, Desmond Coles, Natalie Klaus, Dimitris Mitsios, Valerii Huhnin
modules.title: Raw Univariate Polynomial Proofs
modules.doc: Proofs about operations on raw computable univariate polynomials.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.pow_zero
items.statement:
lemma pow_zero (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) :
    p ^ 0 = C 1

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.pow_succ
items.statement:
lemma pow_succ (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) (n : ℕ) :
    p ^ (n + 1) = p * (p ^ n)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.matchSize_size_eq
items.statement:
lemma matchSize_size_eq {p q : CPolynomial.Raw Q} :
    let (p', q') := Array.matchSize p q 0
    p'.size = q'.size

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.matchSize_size
items.statement:
lemma matchSize_size {p q : CPolynomial.Raw Q} :
    let (p', _) := Array.matchSize p q 0
    p'.size = max p.size q.size

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.zipWith_size
items.statement:
lemma zipWith_size {R} {f : R → R → R} {a b : Array R} (h : a.size = b.size) :
    (Array.zipWith f a b).size = a.size

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.concat_coeff₁
items.statement:
lemma concat_coeff₁ (i : ℕ) : i < p.size →
    (p ++ q).coeff i = p.coeff i

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.foldl_preserves_canonical
items.statement:
lemma foldl_preserves_canonical {α : Type*}
    (f : CPolynomial.Raw R → α → CPolynomial.Raw R)
    (z : CPolynomial.Raw R) (as : Array α)
    (hz : z.trim = z)
    (hf : ∀ acc x, (f acc x).trim = f acc x) :
    (as.foldl f z).trim = as.foldl f z

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.coeff_foldl_add
items.statement:
lemma coeff_foldl_add {α : Type*} [LawfulBEq R]
    (l : List α)
    (f : α → CPolynomial.Raw R)
    (z : CPolynomial.Raw R) (k : ℕ) :
    (l.foldl (fun acc x => acc + f x) z).coeff k
      = z.coeff k + (l.map (fun x => (f x).coeff k)).sum

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.coeff_foldl_addRaw
items.doc:
Coefficient of an untrimmed `addRaw` accumulator fold: the same statement as
`coeff_foldl_add`, but the partial sums are combined with `addRaw` (no per-step
trim). This is what `mulRaw` folds with.
items.statement:
lemma coeff_foldl_addRaw {α : Type*} [LawfulBEq R]
    (l : List α)
    (f : α → CPolynomial.Raw R)
    (z : CPolynomial.Raw R) (k : ℕ) :
    (l.foldl (fun acc x => acc.addRaw (f x)) z).coeff k
      = z.coeff k + (l.map (fun x => (f x).coeff k)).sum

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.mul_eq_foldl
items.doc:
`mul` agrees with the trimmed-add convolution fold (the previous definition of
`mul`). `mul` now folds with the untrimmed `addRaw` and trims once at the end;
this lemma is the bridge that lets the existing coefficient and equivalence
proofs go through unchanged.
items.statement:
lemma mul_eq_foldl [LawfulBEq R] (p q : CPolynomial.Raw R) :
    p * q = p.zipIdx.foldl (fun acc ⟨a, i⟩ => acc + (smul a q).mulPowX i) (mk #[])

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.sum_zipIdx_eq_sum_range
items.statement:
lemma sum_zipIdx_eq_sum_range {α : Type*} [AddCommMonoid α] (p : CPolynomial.Raw R)
    (f : R → ℕ → α) : (p.zipIdx.toList.map (fun ⟨a, i⟩ => f a i)).sum =
    (Finset.range p.size).sum (fun i => f (p.coeff i) i)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.double_sum_eq
items.statement:
theorem double_sum_eq [LawfulBEq R] (p q r : CPolynomial.Raw R) (n : ℕ) :
    (Finset.range (n + 1)).sum (fun j =>
      (Finset.range (j + 1)).sum (fun i =>
        p.coeff i * q.coeff (j - i) * r.coeff (n - j)))
    =
    (Finset.range (n + 1)).sum (fun i =>
      (Finset.range (n - i + 1)).sum (fun k =>
        p.coeff i * q.coeff k * r.coeff (n - i - k)))

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.sum_range_extend
items.statement:
lemma sum_range_extend  (p q : CPolynomial.Raw R) (k : ℕ) :
    (Finset.range p.size).sum (fun i => if k < i then 0 else p.coeff i * q.coeff (k - i)) =
    (Finset.range (k + 1)).sum (fun i => p.coeff i * q.coeff (k - i))

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.sum_range_reverse
items.statement:
lemma sum_range_reverse [LawfulBEq R] (p q : CPolynomial.Raw R) (k : ℕ) :
    (Finset.range (k + 1)).sum (fun i => p.coeff i * q.coeff (k - i)) =
    (Finset.range (k + 1)).sum (fun j => p.coeff (k - j) * q.coeff j)

items.statement: theorem nsmul_zero [LawfulBEq R] (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) : nsmul 0 p = 0

items.statement:
theorem nsmul_succ [LawfulBEq R] (n : ℕ) {p : CPolynomial.Raw R} :

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.smul_coeff
items.statement:
lemma smul_coeff [LawfulBEq R] (a : R) (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) (k : ℕ) :

items.statement:

items.statement:

lemma coeff_smul_add_distrib [LawfulBEq R] (a : R) (q r : CPolynomial.Raw R) (i : ℕ) :

items.statement:
lemma coeff_add_smul [LawfulBEq R]  (a b : R) (q : CPolynomial.Raw R) (k : ℕ) :

items.statement:
lemma coeff_sum : ∀ (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) (k : ℕ),
    (p.zipIdx.map (fun ⟨a, i⟩ => ((smul a 1).mulPowX i).coeff k)).sum = p.coeff k

items.statement:
lemma coeff_mul [LawfulBEq R] (p q : CPolynomial.Raw R) (k : ℕ) :
    (p * q).coeff k = (p.zipIdx.toList.map (fun ⟨a, i⟩ =>

items.statement:
lemma coeff_mulPowX [LawfulBEq R] (i : ℕ) (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) (k : ℕ) :
    (p.mulPowX i).coeff k = if k < i then 0 else p.coeff (k - i)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.coeff_mulPowX'
items.statement:
lemma coeff_mulPowX' [LawfulBEq R] (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) (n i : ℕ) :

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.mulPowX_coeff'
items.statement:
lemma mulPowX_coeff' [LawfulBEq R] (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) (n k : ℕ) :
    (p.mulPowX n).coeff k = if k < n then 0 else p.coeff (k - n)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.coeff_mulPowX_smul_add
items.statement:
lemma coeff_mulPowX_smul_add [LawfulBEq R] (i : ℕ) (a b : R) (q : CPolynomial.Raw R) (k : ℕ) :
    ((smul (a + b) q).mulPowX i).coeff k =
        ((smul a q).mulPowX i).coeff k + ((smul b q).mulPowX i).coeff k

        (Finset.range (j + 1)).sum (fun i =>

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.mul_assoc_coeff

lemma mul_assoc_coeff [LawfulBEq R] (p q r : CPolynomial.Raw R) (n : ℕ) :
