items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.sub_is_trimmed
items.doc: `Raw.sub` reduces to `p + -q`, whose final `add` step trims, so the result is canonical.
items.statement: theorem sub_is_trimmed [LawfulBEq R] (p q : CPolynomial.Raw R) : (p - q).trim = p - q

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.coeff_mul_X_pow
items.statement:
lemma coeff_mul_X_pow [LawfulBEq R] (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) (n i : ℕ) :
    (p * X ^ n).coeff i =
      if n ≤ i ∧ i - n < p.size then p.coeff (i - n) else 0

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.coeff_C_mul_X_pow
items.statement:
lemma coeff_C_mul_X_pow [LawfulBEq R] (scale : R) (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) (n i : ℕ) :
    (C scale * (p * X ^ n)).coeff i =
      if n ≤ i ∧ i - n < p.size then scale * p.coeff (i - n) else 0

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.subScaledShift_eq_sub_C_mul_X_pow
items.statement:
lemma subScaledShift_eq_sub_C_mul_X_pow [LawfulBEq R]
    (p q : CPolynomial.Raw R) (scale : R) (shift : ℕ)
    (hsize : shift + q.size ≤ p.size) :
    subScaledShift p q scale shift = (p - C scale * (q * X ^ shift)).trim

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.modByMonicRemainderOnly_go_eq_divModByMonicAux_go_snd
items.statement:
lemma modByMonicRemainderOnly_go_eq_divModByMonicAux_go_snd [LawfulBEq R] :
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (p q : CPolynomial.Raw R),
      modByMonicRemainderOnly.go n p q = (divModByMonicAux.go n p q).2

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.modByMonicRemainderOnly_eq_modByMonic
items.doc: The remainder-only raw monic remainder agrees with the canonical raw monic remainder.
items.statement:
theorem modByMonicRemainderOnly_eq_modByMonic [LawfulBEq R]
    (p q : CPolynomial.Raw R) :
    modByMonicRemainderOnly p q = modByMonic p q

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.divModByMonicAux_go_fst_canonical
items.doc:
The quotient produced by the monic long-division recursion is canonical regardless of input:
each non-base step accumulates via `Raw.add` (which trims), and the base case returns `0`.
items.statement:
lemma divModByMonicAux_go_fst_canonical [LawfulBEq R] :
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (p q : CPolynomial.Raw R),
      (divModByMonicAux.go n p q).1.trim = (divModByMonicAux.go n p q).1

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.divModByMonicAux_go_snd_canonical
items.doc:
The remainder produced by the monic long-division recursion is canonical when the input is.
Each recursive step feeds the next call a trimmed `(p - q').trim`, and the base case returns the
input unchanged.
items.statement:
lemma divModByMonicAux_go_snd_canonical [LawfulBEq R] :
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (p q : CPolynomial.Raw R), p.trim = p →
      (divModByMonicAux.go n p q).2.trim = (divModByMonicAux.go n p q).2

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.divByMonic_canonical
items.doc: `Raw.divByMonic` returns a canonical polynomial regardless of whether `p` is canonical.
items.statement:
theorem divByMonic_canonical [LawfulBEq R] (p q : CPolynomial.Raw R) :
    (divByMonic p q).trim = divByMonic p q

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.modByMonic_canonical
items.doc: `Raw.modByMonic` returns a canonical polynomial when `p` is canonical.
items.statement:
theorem modByMonic_canonical [LawfulBEq R] {p : CPolynomial.Raw R} (hp : p.trim = p)
    (q : CPolynomial.Raw R) : (modByMonic p q).trim = modByMonic p q

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.subScaledShift_is_trimmed
items.doc: `subScaledShift` ends with `.trim`, so its result is canonical.
items.statement:
theorem subScaledShift_is_trimmed [LawfulBEq R]
    (p q : CPolynomial.Raw R) (scale : R) (shift : ℕ) :
    (subScaledShift p q scale shift).trim = subScaledShift p q scale shift

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.modByMonicRemainderOnly_go_canonical
items.doc: The remainder-only long-division recursion preserves canonicality of `p`.
items.statement:
lemma modByMonicRemainderOnly_go_canonical [LawfulBEq R] :
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (p q : CPolynomial.Raw R), p.trim = p →
      (modByMonicRemainderOnly.go n p q).trim = modByMonicRemainderOnly.go n p q

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.modByMonicRemainderOnly_canonical
items.doc: `Raw.modByMonicRemainderOnly` returns a canonical polynomial when `p` is canonical.
items.statement:
theorem modByMonicRemainderOnly_canonical [LawfulBEq R]
    {p : CPolynomial.Raw R} (hp : p.trim = p) (q : CPolynomial.Raw R) :
    (modByMonicRemainderOnly p q).trim = modByMonicRemainderOnly p q

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.modByMonicByReversal_canonical
items.doc:
`Raw.modByMonicByReversal` returns a canonical polynomial when `p` is canonical.
Either branch ends in a result whose trim is itself: the reversal branch ends with `Raw.sub`
(which trims), and the fallback uses `modByMonicRemainderOnly`.
items.statement:
theorem modByMonicByReversal_canonical [LawfulBEq R]
    (M : MulLowContext R) {p : CPolynomial.Raw R} (hp : p.trim = p) (q : CPolynomial.Raw R) :
    (modByMonicByReversal M p q).trim = modByMonicByReversal M p q

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.div_canonical
items.doc: `Raw.div` returns a canonical polynomial (no condition on inputs).
items.statement:
theorem div_canonical [LawfulBEq R] (p q : CPolynomial.Raw R) :
    (div p q).trim = div p q

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.mod_canonical
items.doc:
`Raw.mod` returns a canonical polynomial (no condition on inputs).
The intermediate `C (q.leadingCoeff)⁻¹ • p` is `C _ * p` via `Mul.toSMul`, which trims.
items.statement:
theorem mod_canonical [LawfulBEq R] (p q : CPolynomial.Raw R) :
    (mod p q).trim = mod p q

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.pow_is_trimmed
items.doc: `pow` preserves trimming (Raw-level version).
items.statement:
lemma pow_is_trimmed (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) (n : ℕ) :
    (p ^ n).trim = p ^ n

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.pow_add
items.doc: Additive law for exponentiation: $ p ^ {a + b} = p ^ a \cdot p ^ b $.
items.statement:
theorem pow_add (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) (a b : ℕ) :
    p ^ (a + b) = p ^ a * p ^ b

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.mul_trim_eq_mul
items.doc:
Multiplication depends only on the coefficient sequences of its inputs,
so trimming either side preserves the product.
items.statement: lemma mul_trim_eq_mul (a b : CPolynomial.Raw R) : a.trim * b.trim = a * b

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.powBySq_eq_pow
items.doc:
`powBySq` agrees with `pow` (repeated squaring = repeated multiplication).

`powBySq` accumulates intermediate squarings with the untrimmed `mulRaw` and trims
once at the end, so the proof bridges through `mul_trim_eq_mul` to relate each
`mulRaw` step back to the spec `pow`.
items.statement: theorem powBySq_eq_pow (p : CPolynomial.Raw R) : ∀ n : ℕ, powBySq p n = p ^ n

modules.title: Sizes of raw polynomial operations
modules.doc:
These bounds concern stored coefficient arrays, including trailing zero coefficients.
Raw multiplication retains the padding of its shifted rows even when the right input is empty.
`CompPoly.Univariate.Raw.Ops` states the size equations of `smul`, `mulPowX`, `addRaw` and
`mulRaw`, next to the operations. This module imports it publicly. The product bound
`size_mulRaw_le` was ported from ArkLib's raw-size adapter under Apache 2.0. The file header keeps
its original copyright attribution.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.size_C
items.doc: A raw constant stores one coefficient, including when that coefficient is zero.
items.statement: theorem size_C {R : Type*} (x : R) : (C x).size = 1

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.add_size
items.doc: Compatibility name for the public theorem previously provided by `Raw.Proofs`.
items.statement: alias add_size

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.size_mulRaw_le
items.doc: The raw product's stored size is at most the sum of the input sizes minus one.
items.statement:
theorem size_mulRaw_le {R : Type*} [Semiring R] (p q : Raw R) :
    (mulRaw p q).size ≤ p.size + q.size - 1

modules.title: Reed-Solomon Codes
modules.doc:
The Reed-Solomon code over a finite field: evaluation domain, message polynomial, and
encoder. Decoders live in their own files.

A Reed-Solomon code is fixed by an evaluation domain `(a₀, ..., aₙ₋₁) ∈ Fⁿ` of distinct
points and a message length `k`. The codeword for a message `(m₀, ..., mₖ₋₁) ∈ Fᵏ` is
`cᵢ = f(aᵢ)` with `f(x) = m₀ + m₁ x + ... + mₖ₋₁ xᵏ⁻¹`. For `1 ≤ k < n ≤ #F` this is an
`(n, k, d)` code of minimum distance `d = n − k + 1`.

## Main definitions

* `Domain`: evaluation domain, an array of distinct points of `F`.
* `messagePoly`, `encode`: the message polynomial of a coefficient vector and the encoder
  evaluating it on the domain.

items.name: CompPoly.ReedSolomon.Domain
items.doc: Evaluation domain: an array of distinct points in `F`.
items.statement: def Domain (F : Type*)

items.name: CompPoly.ReedSolomon.Domain.n
items.doc: Block length.
items.statement: abbrev n (D : Domain F) : ℕ

items.name: CompPoly.ReedSolomon.Domain.node_injective
items.doc: Indexing into the (nodup) domain array is injective on `Fin D.n`.
items.statement:
lemma node_injective (D : Domain F) :
    Function.Injective (fun i : Fin D.n => D.val[i])

items.name: CompPoly.ReedSolomon.messagePoly
items.doc:
Message polynomial `m₀ + m₁ x + ... + mₖ₋₁ xᵏ⁻¹` from a length-`k`
coefficient vector `msg`.
items.statement:
def messagePoly [Zero F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    {k : ℕ} (msg : Vector F k) : CPolynomial F

items.name: CompPoly.ReedSolomon.messagePoly_degree_lt
items.doc: `(messagePoly msg).degree < k`.
items.statement:
lemma messagePoly_degree_lt [Zero F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F] {k : ℕ} (msg : Vector F k) :
    (messagePoly msg).degree < k

items.name: CompPoly.ReedSolomon.messagePoly_ofFn_coeff
items.doc: `messagePoly` recovers a `CPolynomial` of degree `< k` from its bounded coefficient vector.
items.statement:
lemma messagePoly_ofFn_coeff [Semiring F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F] (k : ℕ) (f : CPolynomial F)
    (hf : f.degree < k) : messagePoly (Vector.ofFn fun i : Fin k => f.coeff i) = f

items.name: CompPoly.ReedSolomon.encode
items.doc: Encode: the message polynomial `messagePoly msg` evaluated at the domain `D`.
items.statement:
def encode [Semiring F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (D : Domain F) {k : ℕ} (msg : Vector F k) : Vector F D.n

items.name: CompPoly.ReedSolomon.encode_get
items.doc: The codeword entry at node `i` is `messagePoly msg` evaluated at `D.val[i]`.

modules.title: Gao Decoder Correctness
modules.doc:
Correctness of the computable `Gao.decode` decoder from `GaoDecoder.lean`, formalizing
[Gao02, Theorem 3.3]: `decode` succeeds exactly on received words within the decoding
radius `⌊(n − k) / 2⌋` (soundness, failure, completeness, and uniqueness).

## Main results

* `decode_sound`: every success of `Gao.decode` is the message polynomial of a codeword
  within the decoding radius of the received word.
* `decode_eq_none`: if no codeword lies within the decoding radius, `Gao.decode` fails.
* `decode_eq_some`: within the decoding radius, `Gao.decode` recovers the sent message.
* `decode_unique`: the decoded message polynomial is unique within the decoding radius.

## References

* [Gao, S., *A New Algorithm for Decoding Reed-Solomon Codes*][Gao02]

items.note:
## Uniqueness of degree-bounded Bézout solutions

Two degree-bounded solutions of the Bézout identity cross-multiply
(`bezout_solutions_cross_mul`), so the quotient `G / V` is unique.

items.name: CompPoly.ReedSolomon.Gao.bezout_solutions_cross_mul
items.doc:
Two degree-bounded Bézout solutions `(U,V,G)`, `(U',V',G')` of `U g₀ + V g₁ = ·`
(with `deg G, deg G' < d₀` and `deg V + d₀, deg V' + d₀ ≤ deg g₀`) cross-multiply:
`V * G' = V' * G`.
items.statement:
theorem bezout_solutions_cross_mul [CommRing F] [NoZeroDivisors F]
    (g₀ g₁ G U V G' U' V' : F[X]) (d₀ : ℕ) (hg₀ : g₀ ≠ 0)
    (hBez : U * g₀ + V * g₁ = G) (hBez' : U' * g₀ + V' * g₁ = G')
    (hG : G.degree < d₀) (hG' : G'.degree < d₀)
    (hV : V.degree + d₀ ≤ g₀.degree) (hV' : V'.degree + d₀ ≤ g₀.degree) :
    V * G' = V' * G

items.note:
## Error locators and Hamming distance

A nonzero error locator vanishes on every disagreement node, so its degree bounds the
Hamming distance between the received word and a candidate codeword.

items.name: CompPoly.ReedSolomon.Gao.disagreement_subset_error_locator_zeros
items.doc:
If `V * (f₁ - g₁) = U * g₀` and `g₀` vanishes on aᵢ, then `V` vanishes at every
aᵢ where `f₁` and `g₁` disagree.
items.statement:
lemma disagreement_subset_error_locator_zeros [CommRing F] [NoZeroDivisors F]
    {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq F] (s : Finset ι) (a : ι → F) (g₀ g₁ U V f₁ : F[X])
    (hroot : ∀ i ∈ s, g₀.eval (a i) = 0) (hlocator : V * (f₁ - g₁) = U * g₀) :
    {i ∈ s | f₁.eval (a i) ≠ g₁.eval (a i)} ⊆ {i ∈ s | V.eval (a i) = 0}

items.name: CompPoly.ReedSolomon.Gao.disagreement_card_le_error_locator_natDegree
items.doc:
From the Bézout identity `G = U g₀ + V g₁` and `G = f₁ V` (with `V ≠ 0`,
`g₀` rooted on the aᵢ), `f₁` disagrees with `g₁` at at most `V.natDegree` nodes.
items.statement:
lemma disagreement_card_le_error_locator_natDegree [CommRing F] [IsDomain F]
    {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq F] (s : Finset ι) (a : ι → F) (hinj : Set.InjOn a s)
    (g₀ g₁ G U V f₁ : F[X]) (hroot : ∀ i ∈ s, g₀.eval (a i) = 0)
    (hbez : G = U * g₀ + V * g₁) (hsucc : G = f₁ * V) (hV : V ≠ 0) :
    {i ∈ s | f₁.eval (a i) ≠ g₁.eval (a i)}.card ≤ V.natDegree

items.name: CompPoly.ReedSolomon.Gao.hammingDist_le_error_locator_natDegree
items.doc:
From the Bézout identity `G = U g₀ + V g₁` and `G = f₁ V`
(with `V ≠ 0`, `g₀` rooted on the aᵢ), a word `b` with `g₁(aᵢ) = b i` satisfies
`hammingDist b (f₁ ∘ a) ≤ V.natDegree`.
items.statement:
lemma hammingDist_le_error_locator_natDegree [CommRing F] [IsDomain F]
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq F] (a : ι → F)
    (hinj : Function.Injective a)
    (g₀ g₁ G U V f₁ : F[X]) (b : ι → F)
    (hroot : ∀ i, g₀.eval (a i) = 0) (hb : ∀ i, g₁.eval (a i) = b i)
    (hbez : G = U * g₀ + V * g₁) (hsucc : G = f₁ * V) (hV : V ≠ 0) :
    hammingDist b (fun i => f₁.eval (a i)) ≤ V.natDegree

items.note:
## Decoder components meet their specifications

Transports the abstract `Polynomial` results to the implementation along the decoder
pipeline:
the received interpolant interpolates `r`, `nodalPoly = ∏ (X - aᵢ)` is monic of degree
`D.n`, and `partialGcd` meets the Bézout stop spec.

items.name: CompPoly.ReedSolomon.Gao.receivedInterpolant_eval_node
items.doc: The received interpolant evaluates to `r i` at each domain node.
items.statement:
lemma receivedInterpolant_eval_node [Field F] (D : Domain F) (r : Vector F D.n) (i : Fin D.n) :
    (receivedInterpolant D r).toPoly.eval (D.val[i]) = r.get i

items.name: CompPoly.ReedSolomon.Gao.receivedInterpolant_degree_lt
items.doc: The received interpolant has degree `< D.n`.
items.statement:
lemma receivedInterpolant_degree_lt [Field F] (D : Domain F) (r : Vector F D.n) :
    (receivedInterpolant D r).toPoly.degree < D.n

items.name: CompPoly.ReedSolomon.Gao.toPoly_nodalPoly
items.doc: `(nodalPoly D).toPoly = ∏ i, (X - C D.val[i])`.
items.statement:
lemma toPoly_nodalPoly [CommRing F] [Nontrivial F] (D : Domain F) :
    (nodalPoly D).toPoly = ∏ i : Fin D.n, (X - C (D.val[i]))

items.name: CompPoly.ReedSolomon.Gao.natDegree_nodalPoly
items.doc: `(nodalPoly D).toPoly.natDegree = D.n`.
items.statement:
lemma natDegree_nodalPoly [CommRing F] [NoZeroDivisors F] [Nontrivial F] (D : Domain F) :
    (nodalPoly D).toPoly.natDegree = D.n

items.name: CompPoly.ReedSolomon.Gao.toPoly_nodalPoly_ne_zero
items.doc: `(nodalPoly D).toPoly ≠ 0` (it is monic, a product of distinct linear factors).
items.statement:
lemma toPoly_nodalPoly_ne_zero [CommRing F] [Nontrivial F] (D : Domain F) :
    (nodalPoly D).toPoly ≠ 0

items.name: CompPoly.ReedSolomon.Gao.degree_nodalPoly
items.doc: `(nodalPoly D).toPoly.degree = D.n`.
items.statement:
lemma degree_nodalPoly [CommRing F] [NoZeroDivisors F] [Nontrivial F] (D : Domain F) :
    (nodalPoly D).toPoly.degree = D.n

items.name: CompPoly.ReedSolomon.Gao.nodalPoly_eval_node_eq_zero
items.doc: `nodalPoly D` vanishes at every domain node.
items.statement:
lemma nodalPoly_eval_node_eq_zero [CommRing F] [Nontrivial F] (D : Domain F) (i : Fin D.n) :
    (nodalPoly D).toPoly.eval (D.val[i]) = 0

items.name: CompPoly.ReedSolomon.Gao.partialGcd_stopSpec
items.doc:
`partialGcd`'s output satisfies the stop spec for `(nodalPoly D, receivedInterpolant D r)` at
threshold `(D.n + k + 1) / 2`.
items.statement:
lemma partialGcd_stopSpec [Field F] (k : ℕ) (D : Domain F) (r : Vector F D.n) (hkn : k < D.n) :
    BezoutStopSpecOf (nodalPoly D) (receivedInterpolant D r) ((D.n + k + 1) / 2)
      (partialGcd k D r)

items.note:
## Soundness

A decoder success comes from a codeword within the decoding radius `⌊(D.n - k) / 2⌋` of the
received word; `decode_eq_none` is the contrapositive.

items.name: CompPoly.ReedSolomon.Gao.decode_sound
items.doc:
Soundness: any success of `Gao.decode` returns `messagePoly msg` for
some `msg` whose codeword is within the decoding radius `⌊(D.n-k)/2⌋ = (d-1)/2` of `r`.
items.statement:
theorem decode_sound [Field F]
    (k : ℕ) (D : Domain F) (r : Vector F D.n) (hkn : k < D.n)
    (f₁ : CPolynomial F) (h : Gao.decode k D r = some f₁) :
    ∃ msg : Vector F k, messagePoly msg = f₁ ∧
      hammingDist r.get (encode D msg).get ≤ (D.n - k) / 2

items.name: CompPoly.ReedSolomon.Gao.decode_eq_none
items.doc:
Failure: if `r` is beyond the decoding radius `⌊(D.n-k)/2⌋` of every message,
`Gao.decode` returns `none` (contrapositive of soundness).
items.statement:
theorem decode_eq_none [Field F]
    (k : ℕ) (D : Domain F) (r : Vector F D.n) (hkn : k < D.n)
    (h : ∀ msg : Vector F k,
      (D.n - k) / 2 < hammingDist r.get (encode D msg).get) :
    Gao.decode k D r = none

items.note:
## Completeness and uniqueness

Within the guaranteed-decoding radius `⌊(D.n-k)/2⌋` the decoder returns exactly
`messagePoly msg`, and that decoded word is unique (`decode_unique`).

items.name: CompPoly.ReedSolomon.Gao.decode_eq_some
items.doc:
Completeness: if `r` is within the guaranteed-decoding radius `⌊(D.n-k)/2⌋`
(`2 * (error count) ≤ D.n - k`) of `encode D msg`, then `Gao.decode` returns `messagePoly msg`.
items.statement:
theorem decode_eq_some [Field F]
    (k : ℕ) (D : Domain F) (r : Vector F D.n) (hkn : k < D.n)
    (msg : Vector F k)
    (herr : 2 * hammingDist r.get (encode D msg).get ≤ D.n - k) :
    Gao.decode k D r = some (messagePoly msg)

items.name: CompPoly.ReedSolomon.Gao.decode_none_farness
items.doc:
**Decoder refusal is a farness certificate**: if the decoder returns `none`, the
received word is beyond the guaranteed radius `⌊(n-k)/2⌋` of *every* codeword — positive,
polynomial-time-checkable evidence of farness from the code (the contrapositive of
`decode_eq_some`).
items.statement:
theorem decode_none_farness [Field F]
    (k : ℕ) (D : Domain F) (r : Vector F D.n) (hkn : k < D.n)
    (hnone : Gao.decode k D r = none) :
    ∀ msg : Vector F k, D.n - k < 2 * hammingDist r.get (encode D msg).get

items.name: CompPoly.ReedSolomon.Gao.decode_eq_none_iff
items.doc:
Outcome characterization: `Gao.decode` returns `none` iff the received word is beyond
the guaranteed radius `⌊(n-k)/2⌋` of every codeword (combines `decode_eq_none` and
`decode_none_farness`).
items.statement:
theorem decode_eq_none_iff [Field F]
    (k : ℕ) (D : Domain F) (r : Vector F D.n) (hkn : k < D.n) :
    Gao.decode k D r = none ↔
      ∀ msg : Vector F k, D.n - k < 2 * hammingDist r.get (encode D msg).get

items.name: CompPoly.ReedSolomon.Gao.decode_unique
items.doc:
Uniqueness: within the guaranteed-decoding radius `⌊(D.n-k)/2⌋`, two messages
whose codewords lie within that radius of `r` decode to the same polynomial.
items.statement:
theorem decode_unique [Field F] (k : ℕ) (D : Domain F) (r : Vector F D.n)
    (hkn : k < D.n) (msg₁ msg₂ : Vector F k)
    (h₁ : 2 * hammingDist r.get (encode D msg₁).get ≤ D.n - k)
    (h₂ : 2 * hammingDist r.get (encode D msg₂).get ≤ D.n - k) :
    messagePoly msg₁ = messagePoly msg₂

modules.title: Gao Decoder for Reed-Solomon Codes
modules.doc:
Gao's decoding algorithm [Gao02] for the Reed-Solomon code of `ReedSolomon.lean`;
correctness is proved in `GaoCorrectness.lean`.

## Main definitions

* `nodalPoly`, `receivedInterpolant`: the decoder's inputs to the partial EEA, the nodal
  polynomial `g₀ = ∏ (x − aᵢ)` and the interpolant `g₁` of the received word.
* `partialGcd`: the partial extended Euclidean algorithm on `(g₀, g₁)` with stopping
  threshold `⌈(n+k)/2⌉`.
* `decode`: the decoder; returns the recovered message polynomial, or `none`.

## References

* [Gao, S., *A New Algorithm for Decoding Reed-Solomon Codes*][Gao02]

items.name: CompPoly.ReedSolomon.Gao.nodalPoly
items.doc: Nodal polynomial of the evaluation domain: `g₀(x) = ∏ a ∈ D, (x − a)`.
items.statement: def nodalPoly [Ring F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F] [Nontrivial F] (D : Domain F) : CPolynomial F

items.name: CompPoly.ReedSolomon.Gao.receivedInterpolant
items.doc:
Unique polynomial `g₁ ∈ 𝔽[X]` of degree < `D.n` such that
`g₁(aᵢ) = r[i]` for `aᵢ ∈ D`.
items.statement:
def receivedInterpolant [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (D : Domain F) (r : Vector F D.n) : CPolynomial F

items.name: CompPoly.ReedSolomon.Gao.partialGcd
items.doc:
Partial extended Euclidean algorithm stopping when the remainder
has degree less than `(n + k + 1)/2 = ⌈(n+k)/2⌉`.
items.statement:
def partialGcd [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (k : ℕ) (D : Domain F) (r : Vector F D.n) :
    CPolynomial F × CPolynomial F × CPolynomial F

items.name: CompPoly.ReedSolomon.Gao.decode
items.doc:
Gao's algorithm.

Apply the partial EEA to the nodal polynomial `g₀` and the interpolant `g₁` of
the received word, stopping at threshold `(n + k + 1)/2`, where `n = D.n` is the
block length and `k` the message length. This yields a triple `(g, u, v)`
satisfying the Bézout identity `g = u * g₀ + v * g₁`, where:
- `g` is the first residue with degree below the threshold
- `v` is the error-locator polynomial (`u` is discarded)

Decoding succeeds when `v` divides `g` and `g / v` has degree below `k`, in
which case the recovered message polynomial is `g / v`.
items.statement:
def decode [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (k : ℕ) (D : Domain F) (r : Vector F D.n) :
    Option (CPolynomial F)

modules.title: Gao Decoding on an NTT Domain
modules.doc:
`Gao.decode` builds its two Euclidean inputs by definition: the nodal polynomial as a fold of
`n` linear factors, and the received interpolant by Lagrange's formula, `O(n²)` per basis
polynomial. On the evaluation domain of a radix-2 NTT domain both have fast forms. The nodal
polynomial is `Xⁿ - 1` (`NTT.Domain.nodal_eq_X_pow_sub_one`), and the interpolant is the
inverse NTT (`NTT.interpolate`). `decodeNTT` uses both, and `decodeNTT_eq_decode` proves it
equal to `decode`, so every correctness theorem of `GaoCorrectness.lean` transfers unchanged.

## Main definitions

* `Gao.decodeFrom`: the Euclidean stage of `decode` on given inputs `(g₀, g₁)`.
* `Gao.vanishingNTT`: the polynomial `Xⁿ - 1` of an NTT domain.
* `Gao.decodeNTT`, `Gao.decodePlan`: `decode` with the fast inputs, unplanned and planned.

## Main results

* `Gao.nodalPoly_nttDomainToRS`: the nodal polynomial of the induced domain is `Xⁿ - 1`.
* `Gao.receivedInterpolant_nttDomainToRS`: the received interpolant is the inverse NTT.
* `Gao.decodeNTT_eq_decode`, `Gao.decodePlan_eq_decode`: the fast decoders are `decode`.

items.name: CompPoly.ReedSolomon.Gao.decodeFrom
items.doc: The Euclidean stage of Gao's decoder on the inputs `(g₀, g₁)`, for block length `n`.
items.statement: def decodeFrom (k n : ℕ) (g₀ g₁ : CPolynomial F) : Option (CPolynomial F)

items.name: CompPoly.ReedSolomon.Gao.decode_eq_decodeFrom
items.doc: `decode` is its Euclidean stage applied to the nodal polynomial and the interpolant.
items.statement:
theorem decode_eq_decodeFrom (k : ℕ) (D : Domain F) (r : Vector F D.n) :
    decode k D r = decodeFrom k D.n (nodalPoly D) (receivedInterpolant D r)

items.statement: def vanishingRaw (n : ℕ) : CPolynomial.Raw F

items.name: CompPoly.ReedSolomon.Gao.vanishingNTT
items.doc:
The vanishing polynomial `Xⁿ - 1` of an NTT domain, written down coefficient by

items.statement: def vanishingNTT (D : NTT.Domain F) : CPolynomial F

items.statement:
theorem toPoly_vanishingNTT (D : NTT.Domain F) :
    (vanishingNTT D).toPoly = Polynomial.X ^ D.n - 1

items.name: CompPoly.ReedSolomon.Gao.castToRS
items.doc: Transport a received word over the NTT domain to the induced Reed-Solomon domain.
items.statement: def castToRS (D : NTT.Domain F) (r : Vector F D.n) : Vector F (nttDomainToRS D).n

items.name: CompPoly.ReedSolomon.Gao.nodalPoly_nttDomainToRS
items.doc: The nodal polynomial of the Reed-Solomon domain induced by an NTT domain is `Xⁿ - 1`.
items.statement:
theorem nodalPoly_nttDomainToRS (D : NTT.Domain F) :
    nodalPoly (nttDomainToRS D) = vanishingNTT D

items.name: CompPoly.ReedSolomon.Gao.receivedInterpolant_nttDomainToRS
items.doc: The received interpolant on the induced domain is the inverse NTT of the word.
items.statement:
theorem receivedInterpolant_nttDomainToRS (D : NTT.Domain F) (r : Vector F D.n) :
    receivedInterpolant (nttDomainToRS D) (castToRS D r) = NTT.interpolate D r

items.name: CompPoly.ReedSolomon.Gao.decodeNTT
items.doc:
Gao's decoder on an NTT domain, with `Xⁿ - 1` as the nodal polynomial and the inverse
NTT as the interpolant.
items.statement:
def decodeNTT (k : ℕ) (D : NTT.Domain F) (r : Vector F D.n) :
    Option (CPolynomial F)

items.name: CompPoly.ReedSolomon.Gao.decodeNTT_eq_decode
items.doc: The NTT decoder is Gao's decoder on the induced Reed-Solomon domain.
items.statement:
theorem decodeNTT_eq_decode (k : ℕ) (D : NTT.Domain F) (r : Vector F D.n) :
    decodeNTT k D r = decode k (nttDomainToRS D) (castToRS D r)

items.name: CompPoly.ReedSolomon.Gao.decodePlan
items.doc: Gao's decoder through a reusable NTT plan.
items.statement:
def decodePlan (k : ℕ) (P : NTTFast.Plan F) (r : Vector F P.domain.n) :
    Option (CPolynomial F)

items.name: CompPoly.ReedSolomon.Gao.decodePlan_eq_decode
items.doc: A well-formed plan decodes as Gao's decoder on the induced Reed-Solomon domain.
items.statement:
theorem decodePlan_eq_decode (k : ℕ) (P : NTTFast.Plan F)
    (hP : NTTFast.Plan.WellFormed P) (r : Vector F P.domain.n) :
    decodePlan k P r = decode k (nttDomainToRS P.domain) (castToRS P.domain r)

modules.title: NTT Encoding of Reed-Solomon Codewords
modules.doc:
Over the evaluation domain induced by a radix-2 NTT domain (the node array
`#[ω⁰, ω¹, …, ω^(n-1)]`, nodup because powers of a primitive `n`-th root below `n` are
pairwise distinct), the forward NTT of a message polynomial's coefficients **is** the
Reed-Solomon encoding: `forwardImpl_eq_encode` ties the `O(n log n)` evaluation path
(`NTT.Forward.forwardImpl`, in natural order) to the definitional encoder
(`ReedSolomon.encode`) exactly, for every message of length at most the domain size.
No padding is required: `messagePoly` trims, so the degree bound `k ≤ D.n` suffices.

`nttCodeword` packages the forward-NTT output as a length-indexed vector over the induced
domain, with `nttCodeword_eq_encode` the packaged form of the equality.

Note the natural-order caveat: `NTTFast.forwardImpl` returns evaluations in bit-reversed
order (`forwardImpl_eq_bitRevPermute_evalOnDomain`), so the fast variant relates to
`encode` only after composing with `bitRevPermute`; this file deliberately uses the
natural-order `NTT.Forward.forwardImpl`.

## Main definitions

* `ReedSolomon.nttDomainToRS`: the Reed-Solomon evaluation domain induced by an NTT domain.
* `ReedSolomon.nttCodeword`: the forward-NTT output as a `Vector F (nttDomainToRS D).n`.

## Main results

* `ReedSolomon.forwardImpl_eq_encode`: the forward NTT of `messagePoly msg` equals
  `encode (nttDomainToRS D) msg`, as arrays.
* `ReedSolomon.nttCodeword_eq_encode`: the packaged (vector-level) form.

items.name: CompPoly.ReedSolomon.nttDomainToRS
items.doc:
The Reed-Solomon evaluation domain induced by a radix-2 NTT domain: the node array
`#[ω⁰, ω¹, …, ω^(n-1)]`, nodup because powers of a primitive `n`-th root below `n` are
pairwise distinct.
items.statement: def nttDomainToRS (D : CPolynomial.NTT.Domain F) : ReedSolomon.Domain F

items.name: CompPoly.ReedSolomon.nttDomainToRS_n
items.statement:
lemma nttDomainToRS_n (D : CPolynomial.NTT.Domain F) :
    (nttDomainToRS D).n = D.n

items.name: CompPoly.ReedSolomon.forwardImpl_eq_encode
items.doc:
**The certified NTT encoder**: over the induced evaluation domain, the forward NTT of
the message polynomial's coefficients is exactly the Reed-Solomon encoding — the
`O(n log n)` evaluation path and the definitional encoder agree, with no padding needed.
items.statement:
theorem forwardImpl_eq_encode (D : CPolynomial.NTT.Domain F) {k : ℕ} (msg : Vector F k)
    (hk : k ≤ D.n) :
    Forward.forwardImpl D (messagePoly msg).val
      = (encode (nttDomainToRS D) msg).toArray

items.name: CompPoly.ReedSolomon.nttCodeword
items.doc: The forward-NTT output packaged as a length-indexed vector over the induced domain.
items.statement:
def nttCodeword (D : CPolynomial.NTT.Domain F) {k : ℕ} (msg : Vector F k) (hk : k ≤ D.n) :
    Vector F (nttDomainToRS D).n

items.name: CompPoly.ReedSolomon.nttCodeword_eq_encode
items.doc: Vector-level form of `forwardImpl_eq_encode`.
items.statement:
theorem nttCodeword_eq_encode (D : CPolynomial.NTT.Domain F) {k : ℕ} (msg : Vector F k)
    (hk : k ≤ D.n) : nttCodeword D msg hk = encode (nttDomainToRS D) msg

Executable field-root extraction over finite fields. The public operation

root product modulo the input polynomial, splits the product into linear

Explicit contexts for executable univariate root finding over finite fields.
The algorithms use the cardinality carried here; downstream proofs use the
finite-field and splitter contracts without unfolding concrete implementations.

structure FiniteFieldContext (F : Type*) [Field F] where
  q : Nat

  card_eq : Nat.card F = q

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Roots.FiniteField.LinearFactorProductSplitter
items.doc:
A deterministic splitter for squarefree products of linear factors.

The executable function consumes the field cardinality and the current factor.
Completeness of the public root backend depends on splitter completeness for
every linear-factor product reached by the recursion.
items.statement:
structure LinearFactorProductSplitter (F : Type*) [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F] where
  splitLinearFactors : Nat → CPolynomial F → Array (CPolynomial F)
  /--
  The precondition under which `complete` is claimed for the splitter input.

  Root backends should establish this predicate for the field-root product they
  pass to the splitter. Executable splitters may remain defensive outside this
  predicate, but completeness is only part of the contract under it.
  -/
  validInput : Nat → CPolynomial F → Prop := fun _ _ ↦ True
  sound :
    ∀ q p factor,
      factor ∈ (splitLinearFactors q p).toList →
        IsLinearFactor factor
  complete :
    ∀ q p a,
      validInput q p →
        p ≠ 0 →
        CPolynomial.eval a p = 0 →
          ∃ factor,
            factor ∈ (splitLinearFactors q p).toList ∧
              IsLinearRootFactorCandidate factor a

    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (M : CPolynomial.Raw.MulContext F) (D : CPolynomial.Raw.ModContext F)

    {p : CPolynomial F} {a : F}

    a ∈ (rootsInFiniteFieldWith M D ctx splitter p).toList

      ∀ {p : CPolynomial F}, p ≠ 0 →
        splitter.validInput ctx.q (finiteFieldRootProduct ctx p))
    {p : CPolynomial F} {a : F}

    a ∈ (rootsInFiniteField ctx splitter p).toList

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Roots.FiniteField.rootsInFiniteField_spec
items.doc:
The complete executable finite-field root pipeline is sound and complete
for nonzero inputs under the finite-field and splitter contracts.
items.statement:
theorem rootsInFiniteField_spec {F : Type*}
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (ctx : FiniteFieldContext F) (splitter : LinearFactorProductSplitter F)
    (splitterValid :
      ∀ {p : CPolynomial F}, p ≠ 0 →
        splitter.validInput ctx.q (finiteFieldRootProduct ctx p))
    {p : CPolynomial F} {a : F} (hp : p ≠ 0) :
    a ∈ (rootsInFiniteField ctx splitter p).toList ↔
      CPolynomial.eval a p = 0

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Roots.FiniteField.cantorZassenhausOddAttemptWith
items.doc:
One odd-field Cantor-Zassenhaus degree-one split attempt.

The probe is reduced modulo `g`, then the split candidates are
`gcd(g, h)`, `gcd(g / zeroPart, h^((q - 1) / 2) - 1)`, and the remaining
quotient. The attempt succeeds only when at least two nonconstant proper
distinct children are produced.
items.statement:
def cantorZassenhausOddAttemptWith {F : Type*}
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (M : CPolynomial.Raw.MulContext F) (D : CPolynomial.Raw.ModContext F)
    (q : Nat) (probes : ProbeFamily F) (g : CPolynomial F) (attempt : Nat) :
    Option (Array (CPolynomial F))

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Roots.FiniteField.cantorZassenhausEvenTraceAttemptWith
items.doc:
One characteristic-two trace split attempt.

The probe is reduced modulo `g`, then the trace power sum
`h + h^2 + ... + h^(2^(m-1))` is computed modulo `g` using the supplied Shoup
small-prime trace metadata. The attempt succeeds only when `gcd(g, Tr(h))` and
the remaining quotient are both nonconstant proper children.
items.statement:
def cantorZassenhausEvenTraceAttemptWith {F : Type*}
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (M : CPolynomial.Raw.MulContext F) (D : CPolynomial.Raw.ModContext F)
    (traceCtx : SmallPrimeTraceContext F)
    (q : Nat) (probes : ProbeFamily F) (g : CPolynomial F) (attempt : Nat) :
    Option (Array (CPolynomial F))

theorem stackWork_append {F : Type*}

theorem stackWork_push {F : Type*}

theorem stackWork_eraseDups_fold_le {F : Type*}

    ∀ (xs : List (CPolynomial F)) (out : Array (CPolynomial F)),
      stackWork (List.foldl
          (fun out x ↦ if x ∈ out then out else out.push x) out xs).toList ≤
        stackWork out.toList + stackWork xs

CompPoly.CPolynomial.Roots.FiniteField.cantorZassenhausEvenTraceAttemptWith_probe_congr
items.doc:
The trace split attempt depends on the probe family only through the probe
it actually draws.
items.statement:
theorem cantorZassenhausEvenTraceAttemptWith_probe_congr {F : Type*}
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (M : CPolynomial.Raw.MulContext F) (D : CPolynomial.Raw.ModContext F)
    (traceCtx : SmallPrimeTraceContext F)
    (q : Nat) {p1 p2 : ProbeFamily F} {g : CPolynomial F} {a1 a2 : Nat}
    (hprobe : p1.probe q (CPolynomial.monicNormalize g) a1 =
      p2.probe q (CPolynomial.monicNormalize g) a2) :
    cantorZassenhausEvenTraceAttemptWith M D traceCtx q p1 g a1 =
      cantorZassenhausEvenTraceAttemptWith M D traceCtx q p2 g a2

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Roots.FiniteField.tryEvenTraceSplitAttemptsWith_probe_congr
items.doc:
The trace retry loop depends on the probe family only through the probes it
actually draws.
items.statement:
theorem tryEvenTraceSplitAttemptsWith_probe_congr {F : Type*}
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (M : CPolynomial.Raw.MulContext F) (D : CPolynomial.Raw.ModContext F)
    (traceCtx : SmallPrimeTraceContext F)
    (q : Nat) {p1 p2 : ProbeFamily F} {g : CPolynomial F} :
    ∀ (attempts offset1 offset2 : Nat),
      (∀ i, i < attempts →
        p1.probe q (CPolynomial.monicNormalize g) (offset1 + i) =
          p2.probe q (CPolynomial.monicNormalize g) (offset2 + i)) →
      tryEvenTraceSplitAttemptsWith M D traceCtx q p1 g attempts offset1 =
        tryEvenTraceSplitAttemptsWith M D traceCtx q p2 g attempts offset2

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Roots.FiniteField.tryEvenTraceSplitAttemptsWith_eq_some_exists_attempt
items.doc: A successful trace retry loop result is produced by some single attempt.
items.statement:
theorem tryEvenTraceSplitAttemptsWith_eq_some_exists_attempt {F : Type*}
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (M : CPolynomial.Raw.MulContext F) (D : CPolynomial.Raw.ModContext F)
    (traceCtx : SmallPrimeTraceContext F)
    (q : Nat) (probes : ProbeFamily F) {g : CPolynomial F} :
    ∀ (attempts offset : Nat) {children : Array (CPolynomial F)},
      tryEvenTraceSplitAttemptsWith M D traceCtx q probes g attempts offset =
        some children →
      ∃ attempt,
        cantorZassenhausEvenTraceAttemptWith M D traceCtx q probes g attempt =
          some children

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Roots.FiniteField.tryEvenTraceSplitAttemptsWith_root
items.statement:
theorem tryEvenTraceSplitAttemptsWith_root {F : Type*}
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (M : CPolynomial.Raw.MulContext F) (D : CPolynomial.Raw.ModContext F)
    (traceCtx : SmallPrimeTraceContext F)
    (q : Nat) (probes : ProbeFamily F) {g : CPolynomial F} {a : F}
    (hg : g ≠ 0) (hroot : CPolynomial.eval a g = 0) :
    ∀ attempts offset {children : Array (CPolynomial F)},
      tryEvenTraceSplitAttemptsWith M D traceCtx q probes g attempts offset = some children →
        ∃ child, child ∈ children.toList ∧ CPolynomial.eval a child = 0

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Roots.FiniteField.tryEvenTraceSplitAttemptsWith_stackWork_le
items.statement:
theorem tryEvenTraceSplitAttemptsWith_stackWork_le {F : Type*}
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (M : CPolynomial.Raw.MulContext F) (D : CPolynomial.Raw.ModContext F)
    (traceCtx : SmallPrimeTraceContext F)
    (q : Nat) (probes : ProbeFamily F) {g : CPolynomial F}
    (hg : g ≠ 0) :
    ∀ attempts offset {children : Array (CPolynomial F)},
      tryEvenTraceSplitAttemptsWith M D traceCtx q probes g attempts offset = some children →
        stackWork children.toList ≤ splitWork (CPolynomial.monicNormalize g) - 1

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Roots.FiniteField.tryEvenTraceSplitAttemptsWith_child_normSplitWork_pos
items.statement:
theorem tryEvenTraceSplitAttemptsWith_child_normSplitWork_pos {F : Type*}
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (M : CPolynomial.Raw.MulContext F) (D : CPolynomial.Raw.ModContext F)
    (traceCtx : SmallPrimeTraceContext F)
    (q : Nat) (probes : ProbeFamily F) {g child : CPolynomial F}

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Roots.FiniteField.eval_tracePowerSumPolynomialWith_eq
items.doc:
Evaluating the modular trace power sum at a root of the modulus computes
the field-level trace power sum of the probe value.
items.statement:
theorem eval_tracePowerSumPolynomialWith_eq {F : Type*}
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (M : CPolynomial.Raw.MulContext F) (D : CPolynomial.Raw.ModContext F)
    {modulus : CPolynomial F} {z : F}
    (hroot : CPolynomial.eval z modulus = 0) (p k : Nat) (h : CPolynomial F) :
    CPolynomial.eval z (tracePowerSumPolynomialWith M D modulus p k h) =
      tracePowerSum p k (CPolynomial.eval z h)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Roots.FiniteField.cantorZassenhausEvenTraceAttemptWith_size_ge_two

CompPoly.CPolynomial.Roots.FiniteField.cantorZassenhausEvenTraceAttemptWith_success_of_trace_separated
items.doc:
A fixed probe whose trace power sums separate two roots of `g` forces the
characteristic-two trace split attempt to succeed: the root with trace zero
lands in `gcd(g, Tr(h))` and the root with nonzero trace survives into the
complement, so both candidates are nontrivial proper children.
items.statement:
theorem cantorZassenhausEvenTraceAttemptWith_success_of_trace_separated {F : Type*}
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (M : CPolynomial.Raw.MulContext F) (D : CPolynomial.Raw.ModContext F)
    (traceCtx : SmallPrimeTraceContext F)
    (q : Nat) {g h : CPolynomial F} {a b : F} (attempt : Nat)
    (hg : g ≠ 0)
    (hrootA : CPolynomial.eval a g = 0)
    (hrootB : CPolynomial.eval b g = 0)
    (hsepA : tracePowerSum traceCtx.p traceCtx.k (CPolynomial.eval a h) = 0)
    (hsepB : tracePowerSum traceCtx.p traceCtx.k (CPolynomial.eval b h) ≠ 0) :
    ∃ children,
      cantorZassenhausEvenTraceAttemptWith M D traceCtx q
        ({ probe := fun _q _factor _attempt ↦ h } : ProbeFamily F)
        g attempt = some children

        IsLinearRootFactorCandidate factor a
