modules.title: Shoup-Style Small-Characteristic Root Splitting
modules.doc: Public module for the Shoup-style trace splitter.

modules.title: Shoup-Style Small-Characteristic Linear-Factor Splitting
modules.doc:
Executable trace-coordinate splitter for finite-field root products over fields
presented as `GF(p^k)` with small base characteristic `p`. The splitter refines a
valid root product by `k` trace coordinates and the `p` embedded base constants;
it does not enumerate all `p^k` field elements, following the small-characteristic
Frobenius-map factoring method of von zur Gathen and Shoup [vzGS92].

## References

* [J. von zur Gathen and Victor Shoup, *Computing Frobenius maps and factoring
    polynomials*, Computational Complexity 2, 187-224, 1992][vzGS92]

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Roots.FiniteField.tracePowerSum
items.doc: Trace power sum `z + z^p + ... + z^(p^(k-1))`.
items.statement: def tracePowerSum {F : Type*} [Field F] (p k : Nat) (z : F) : F

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Roots.FiniteField.tracePowerSum_eq_sum_range
items.doc: The list-fold trace power sum is the corresponding finite range sum.
items.statement:
theorem tracePowerSum_eq_sum_range {F : Type*} [Field F] (p k : Nat) (z : F) :
    tracePowerSum p k z = ∑ i ∈ Finset.range k, z ^ (p ^ i)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Roots.FiniteField.SmallPrimeTraceContext
items.doc:
Executable and proof data for a Shoup-style small-characteristic trace splitter.

The field-theoretic facts are carried by the context so the generic executable
splitter can stay representation-independent. Concrete fields can discharge the
trace-image and separating-basis obligations using their own basis libraries.
items.statement:
structure SmallPrimeTraceContext (F : Type*) [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    extends FiniteFieldContext F where
  p : Nat
  k : Nat
  p_prime : Nat.Prime p
  q_eq : q = p ^ k
  baseConstants : Array F
  baseConstants_size : baseConstants.size = p
  basis : Array F
  basis_size : basis.size = k
  traceValue : F → F
  traceValue_eq_powerSum : ∀ z, traceValue z = tracePowerSum p k z
  traceValue_mem_base : ∀ z, traceValue z ∈ baseConstants.toList
  trace_separates :
    ∀ {a b : F}, a ≠ b →
      ∃ beta, beta ∈ basis.toList ∧ traceValue (beta * (a - b)) ≠ 0

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Roots.FiniteField.shoupSplitterInput
items.doc:
Input predicate for the Shoup splitter.

Completeness is only claimed for nonzero products of distinct field-linear
factors, represented here by divisibility into `X^q - X`. This is the contract
satisfied by the finite-field root product, not by arbitrary input polynomials.
items.statement:
def shoupSplitterInput {F : Type*} [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Roots.FiniteField.lookupTracePowers_eq
items.doc: A hit in a valid cache returns the Frobenius powers of the queried modulus.
items.statement:
theorem lookupTracePowers_eq {F : Type*} [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    {M : CPolynomial.Raw.MulContext F} {D : CPolynomial.Raw.ModContext F}
    {ctx : SmallPrimeTraceContext F} {u : CPolynomial F} {powers : Array (CPolynomial F)} :
    ∀ {cache : ShoupTracePowerCache F}, cache.Valid M D ctx →
      lookupTracePowers u cache = some powers →
        powers = modularXPowersWith M D u ctx.p ctx.k
  | [], _, h => by simp [lookupTracePowers] at h
  | (v, vs) :: rest, hvalid, h => by
      unfold lookupTracePowers at h
      by_cases huv : u = v
      · subst huv
        rw [ite_eq_left (beq_self_eq_true u)] at h
        obtain rfl

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Roots.FiniteField.tracePowersWithCache_spec
items.doc: Reading through a valid cache returns the Frobenius powers and keeps the cache valid.
items.statement:
theorem tracePowersWithCache_spec {F : Type*} [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (M : CPolynomial.Raw.MulContext F) (D : CPolynomial.Raw.ModContext F)
    (ctx : SmallPrimeTraceContext F) (u : CPolynomial F)
    {cache : ShoupTracePowerCache F} (hvalid : cache.Valid M D ctx) :
    (tracePowersWithCache M D ctx u cache).1 = modularXPowersWith M D u ctx.p ctx.k ∧
      (tracePowersWithCache M D ctx u cache).2.Valid M D ctx

items.doc: The cached single-factor refinement matches `shoupRefineFactorWith`.
items.statement:
theorem shoupRefineFactorCachedWith_spec {F : Type*}
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (M : CPolynomial.Raw.MulContext F) (D : CPolynomial.Raw.ModContext F)
    (ctx : SmallPrimeTraceContext F) (beta : F) (u : CPolynomial F)
    {cache : ShoupTracePowerCache F} (hvalid : cache.Valid M D ctx) :
    (shoupRefineFactorCachedWith M D ctx beta cache u).2 =
        shoupRefineFactorWith M D ctx beta u ∧
      (shoupRefineFactorCachedWith M D ctx beta cache u).1.Valid M D ctx

items.doc: The cached refinement of a factor array matches `shoupRefineFactorsWith`.
items.statement:
theorem shoupRefineFactorsCachedWith_spec {F : Type*}
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (M : CPolynomial.Raw.MulContext F) (D : CPolynomial.Raw.ModContext F)
    (ctx : SmallPrimeTraceContext F) (beta : F) (factors : Array (CPolynomial F))
    {cache : ShoupTracePowerCache F} (hvalid : cache.Valid M D ctx) :
    (shoupRefineFactorsCachedWith M D ctx beta cache factors).2 =
        shoupRefineFactorsWith M D ctx beta factors ∧
      (shoupRefineFactorsCachedWith M D ctx beta cache factors).1.Valid M D ctx

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Roots.FiniteField.shoupRefineBasisCachedWith_eq
items.doc: From a valid cache, the cached basis loop is the uncached fold over the basis.
items.statement:
theorem shoupRefineBasisCachedWith_eq {F : Type*}
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (M : CPolynomial.Raw.MulContext F) (D : CPolynomial.Raw.ModContext F)
    (ctx : SmallPrimeTraceContext F) :
    ∀ (basis : List F) {cache : ShoupTracePowerCache F} (factors : Array (CPolynomial F)),
      cache.Valid M D ctx →
      shoupRefineBasisCachedWith M D ctx basis cache factors =
        basis.foldl (fun factors beta ↦ shoupRefineFactorsWith M D ctx beta factors) factors
  | [], _, _, _ => rfl
  | beta :: basis, cache, factors, hvalid => by
      obtain ⟨hfactors, hvalid'⟩

modules.title: Correctness Surface for Shoup-Style Trace Splitting
modules.doc:
This file states the proof obligations for the executable Shoup trace splitter.
The main completeness contract is intentionally limited to valid root products:
nonzero divisors of `X^q - X`, as produced by the finite-field root-product
construction.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Roots.FiniteField.eval_shoupModularXPowerWith_eq_pow
items.doc: Evaluation of a Shoup modular power at a root of the modulus.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Roots.FiniteField.eval_traceCoordinatePolynomialWith
items.doc: Trace-coordinate polynomial evaluation at a root of the modulus.
items.statement:
theorem eval_traceCoordinatePolynomialWith {F : Type*}
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (M : CPolynomial.Raw.MulContext F) (D : CPolynomial.Raw.ModContext F)
    (ctx : SmallPrimeTraceContext F) {modulus : CPolynomial F} {a beta : F}
    (hroot : CPolynomial.eval a modulus = 0) :
    CPolynomial.eval a (traceCoordinatePolynomialWith M D ctx modulus beta) =
      ctx.traceValue (beta * a)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Roots.FiniteField.traceValue_sub
items.doc: The trace power-sum is additive for subtraction.
items.statement:
theorem traceValue_sub {F : Type*}
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (ctx : SmallPrimeTraceContext F) (x y : F) :
    ctx.traceValue (x - y) = ctx.traceValue x - ctx.traceValue y

items.doc: Trace coordinates convert equal bucket values into zero trace on differences.

items.doc: Matching every trace coordinate in the separating basis forces equality.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Roots.FiniteField.shoup_gcdBucket_root
items.doc: The trace-coordinate gcd bucket preserves roots whose trace coordinate matches the bucket.
items.statement:
theorem shoup_gcdBucket_root {F : Type*}
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (M : CPolynomial.Raw.MulContext F) (D : CPolynomial.Raw.ModContext F)
    (ctx : SmallPrimeTraceContext F) {u : CPolynomial F} {a beta c : F}
    (hroot : CPolynomial.eval a u = 0)
    (htrace : ctx.traceValue (beta * a) = c) :
    CPolynomial.eval a
        (CPolynomial.monicNormalize
          (CPolynomial.gcdMonic u
            (traceCoordinatePolynomialWith M D ctx u beta - CPolynomial.C c))) = 0

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Roots.FiniteField.shoup_gcdBucket_root_iff
items.doc: Roots of a trace-coordinate gcd bucket are roots of the parent in that bucket.
items.statement:
theorem shoup_gcdBucket_root_iff {F : Type*}
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (M : CPolynomial.Raw.MulContext F) (D : CPolynomial.Raw.ModContext F)
    (ctx : SmallPrimeTraceContext F) {u : CPolynomial F} {a beta c : F}
    (hu : u ≠ 0) :
    CPolynomial.eval a
        (CPolynomial.monicNormalize
          (CPolynomial.gcdMonic u
            (traceCoordinatePolynomialWith M D ctx u beta - CPolynomial.C c))) = 0 ↔
      CPolynomial.eval a u = 0 ∧ ctx.traceValue (beta * a) = c

items.statement:
theorem shoupSplitCandidatesWith_root {F : Type*}
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (M : CPolynomial.Raw.MulContext F) (D : CPolynomial.Raw.ModContext F)
    (ctx : SmallPrimeTraceContext F) {p : CPolynomial F} {a : F}

        factor ≠ 0 ∧
        CPolynomial.eval a factor = 0

modules.title: Frobenius Divisors with One Root are Linear
modules.doc:
This file contains the field-theoretic bridge used by the Shoup trace splitter:
a nonzero divisor of `X^q - X` over `GF(q)` with exactly one field root is a
represented nonconstant linear factor.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Roots.FiniteField.isRepresentedLinearFactor_of_dvd_frobenius_unique_root
items.doc:
A nonzero divisor of `X^q - X` with exactly one field root is represented as a
linear factor.
items.statement:
theorem isRepresentedLinearFactor_of_dvd_frobenius_unique_root {F : Type*}
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (ctx : SmallPrimeTraceContext F) {factor : CPolynomial F} {a : F}
    (hfactorNe : factor ≠ 0)
    (hdvd : factor.toPoly ∣ ((Polynomial.X : Polynomial F) ^ ctx.q - Polynomial.X))
    (hroot : CPolynomial.eval a factor = 0)
    (hunique : ∀ b, CPolynomial.eval b factor = 0 → b = a) :
    isRepresentedLinearFactor factor = true

modules.title: Smooth Multiplicative-Subgroup Root Splitting
modules.doc: Public module for the smooth cyclic subgroup splitter.

modules.title: Smooth Multiplicative-Subgroup Linear-Factor Splitting
modules.doc:
Executable splitter for field-root products over finite fields whose
multiplicative group admits a smooth cyclic refinement schedule, following the
subgroup-refinement root-finding method of [MOV92].

The generic root pipeline consumes a `LinearFactorProductSplitter`. This module
provides a contract-bearing smooth context plus an adapter from that context to
the shared splitter interface.

## References

* [Menezes, A. J., van Oorschot, P. C., and Vanstone, S. A., *Subgroup
    Refinement Algorithms for Root Finding in GF(q)*][MOV92]

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Roots.FiniteField.smoothSplitterInput
items.doc:
Splitter-input predicate for a smooth cyclic splitter.

This predicate records the mathematical input contract for the splitter. The
field-root pipeline proves it for `gcd(p, X^q - X)` values before using the
splitter completeness theorem.
items.statement:
def smoothSplitterInput {F : Type*} [Field F]
    (q : Nat) (_generator : F) (_schedule : Array Nat) (p : CPolynomial F) : Prop

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Roots.FiniteField.SmoothCyclicRootContext
items.doc: Package the executable smooth splitter with its field and schedule facts.
items.statement:
structure SmoothCyclicRootContext (F : Type*) [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F] where
  q : Nat
  generator : F
  schedule : Array Nat
  leafEvaluator : BatchEvalContext F
  validInput : CPolynomial F → Prop
  card_eq : Nat.card F = q
  generator_order : orderOf generator = q - 1
  schedule_complete :
    schedule.toList.foldl (fun order ell ↦ order / ell) (q - 1) = 1
  splitLinearFactorsWith :
    CPolynomial.Raw.MulContext F →
      CPolynomial.Raw.ModContext F →
        CPolynomial F → Array (CPolynomial F)
  sound :
    ∀ M D p factor,
      factor ∈ (splitLinearFactorsWith M D p).toList →
        IsLinearFactor factor
  complete :
    ∀ M D p a,
      validInput p →
        p ≠ 0 →
          CPolynomial.eval a p = 0 →
            ∃ factor,
              factor ∈ (splitLinearFactorsWith M D p).toList ∧
                IsLinearRootFactorCandidate factor a

items.doc: Build a smooth cyclic root context from executable constants and proof fields.

def smoothCyclicRootContextOf {F : Type*} [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (q : Nat) (generator : F) (schedule : Array Nat)
    (leafEvaluator : BatchEvalContext F)
    (validInput : CPolynomial F → Prop)
    (card_eq : Nat.card F = q)
    (generator_order : orderOf generator = q - 1)
    (schedule_complete :
      schedule.toList.foldl (fun order ell ↦ order / ell) (q - 1) = 1)
    (sound :
      ∀ M D p factor,
        factor ∈
            (smoothLinearFactorsAlgorithmWith M D leafEvaluator q generator schedule p).toList →
          IsLinearFactor factor)
    (complete :
      ∀ M D p a,
        validInput p →
              p ≠ 0 →
            CPolynomial.eval a p = 0 →
              ∃ factor,
                factor ∈
                    (smoothLinearFactorsAlgorithmWith M D leafEvaluator q generator schedule
                      p).toList ∧
                  IsLinearRootFactorCandidate factor a) :
    SmoothCyclicRootContext F

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Roots.FiniteField.smooth_coset_split_root_partition_mod
items.doc: A smooth coset split maps the residue class `k % ell` to the child-coset equation.
items.statement:
theorem smooth_coset_split_root_partition_mod {F : Type*}
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    {alpha gamma : F} {order ell k : Nat}
    (hgamma_pow : gamma ^ order = 1)
    (hell_dvd : ell ∣ order) :
    (alpha * gamma ^ k) ^ (order / ell) =
      alpha ^ (order / ell) * (gamma ^ (order / ell)) ^ (k % ell)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Roots.FiniteField.smooth_coset_split_root_partition
items.doc: A smooth coset split partitions roots according to the child-coset equation.
items.statement:
theorem smooth_coset_split_root_partition {F : Type*}
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    {alpha gamma x : F} {order ell : Nat}
    (hgamma_order : orderOf gamma = order)
    (hell_dvd : ell ∣ order) (hell_pos : 0 < ell)
    (hx : ∃ k : Nat, k < order ∧ x = alpha * gamma ^ k) :
    ∃ j : Nat, j < ell ∧
      x ^ (order / ell) = alpha ^ (order / ell) * (gamma ^ (order / ell)) ^ j

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Roots.FiniteField.SmoothCosetInvariant
items.doc: Roots of `p` are contained in the explicit coset `alpha * <gamma>` of order `order`.
items.statement:
def SmoothCosetInvariant {F : Type*} [Field F]
    (alpha gamma : F) (order : Nat) (p : CPolynomial F) : Prop

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Roots.FiniteField.smooth_schedule_recursion_preserves_coset_invariant
items.doc: Schedule recursion preserves the smooth coset invariant.
items.statement:
theorem smooth_schedule_recursion_preserves_coset_invariant {F : Type*}
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (M : CPolynomial.Raw.MulContext F) (D : CPolynomial.Raw.ModContext F)
    {order ell j : Nat} {alpha gamma : F} {p : CPolynomial F}
    (hchild_alpha_ne_zero : alpha * gamma ^ j ≠ 0)
    (hchild_order_pos : 0 < order / ell)
    (hchild_generator_order : orderOf (gamma ^ ell) = order / ell)
    (hchild_roots :
      ∀ x : F,
        CPolynomial.eval x
            (CPolynomial.monicNormalize
              (CPolynomial.gcdMonic p
                (xPowModWith M D p (order / ell) -
                  CPolynomial.C
                    (alpha ^ (order / ell) * (gamma ^ (order / ell)) ^ j)))) = 0 →
          ∃ k : Nat, k < order / ell ∧
            x = (alpha * gamma ^ j) * (gamma ^ ell) ^ k) :
    SmoothCosetInvariant
      (alpha * gamma ^ j)
      (gamma ^ ell)
      (order / ell)
      (CPolynomial.monicNormalize
        (CPolynomial.gcdMonic p
          (xPowModWith M D p (order / ell) -
            CPolynomial.C (alpha ^ (order / ell) * (gamma ^ (order / ell)) ^ j))))

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Roots.FiniteField.smoothCosetLinearFactorsWithSchedule_complete
items.doc: Path completeness for the schedule-driven smooth coset recursion.
items.statement:
theorem smoothCosetLinearFactorsWithSchedule_complete {F : Type*}
    [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (M : CPolynomial.Raw.MulContext F) (D : CPolynomial.Raw.ModContext F)
    (E : BatchEvalContext F) :
    ∀ (schedule : List Nat) (order : Nat) (alpha gamma : F) (p : CPolynomial F) (a : F),
      SmoothScheduleDivides schedule order →
        gamma ^ order = 1 →
          p ≠ 0 →
            CPolynomial.eval a p = 0 →
              (∃ k : Nat, k < order ∧ a = alpha * gamma ^ k) →
                ∃ factor,
                  factor ∈
                      (smoothCosetLinearFactorsWithSchedule M D E schedule order alpha gamma
                        p).toList ∧
                    IsLinearRootFactorCandidate factor a

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Roots.FiniteField.smoothLinearFactorsAlgorithmWith_complete
items.doc: Completeness of the top-level smooth linear-factor splitter.
items.statement:
theorem smoothLinearFactorsAlgorithmWith_complete {F : Type*}
    [Field F] [Finite F] [DecidableEq F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]
    (M : CPolynomial.Raw.MulContext F) (D : CPolynomial.Raw.ModContext F)
    (E : BatchEvalContext F) (q : Nat) (generator : F) (schedule : Array Nat)
    (hcard : Nat.card F = q)
    (hgenerator : orderOf generator = q - 1)
    (hschedule : SmoothScheduleDivides schedule.toList (q - 1))
    {p : CPolynomial F} {a : F}
    (hp : p ≠ 0) (hroot : CPolynomial.eval a p = 0) :
    ∃ factor,
      factor ∈ (smoothLinearFactorsAlgorithmWith M D E q generator schedule p).toList ∧
        IsLinearRootFactorCandidate factor a

modules.title: Degrees and degree bounds under `toPoly`
modules.doc:
Degree lemmas for the computable-univariate to `Polynomial` conversion.

`degreeLTEquiv` identifies computable polynomials of degree below `n` with their coefficient
functions `Fin n → R` by a linear equivalence.

The quantifier lemmas transport statements over `↥(degreeLT n)` to Mathlib polynomials.

* `exists_degreeLT_toPoly_iff` transports an existential quantifier with a degree bound.
* `forall_degreeLT_toPoly_iff` transports a universal quantifier with a degree bound.
* `forall₂_degreeLT_toPoly_iff` transports two universal quantifiers with separate bounds.
* `exists_degreeLT_toPoly_iff_of_degree_lt` drops the explicit bound when the predicate implies it.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.degreeLTEquiv_invFun_mem
items.statement:
lemma degreeLTEquiv_invFun_mem [DecidableEq R] (n : ℕ) (f : Fin n → R) :
    Finset.univ.sum (fun i : Fin n => monomial (R := R) (i : ℕ) (f i)) ∈ degreeLT (R := R) n

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.degreeLTEquiv_left_inv
items.statement:
lemma degreeLTEquiv_left_inv [DecidableEq R] (n : ℕ)
    (p : ↥(degreeLT (R := R) n)) :
    (⟨
      Finset.univ.sum (fun i : Fin n => monomial (R := R) (↑i) (coeff p.1 i)),
      degreeLTEquiv_invFun_mem (R := R) n (fun i => coeff p.1 i)
    ⟩ : ↥(degreeLT (R := R) n)) = p

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.degreeLTEquiv_right_inv
items.statement:
lemma degreeLTEquiv_right_inv [DecidableEq R] (n : ℕ)
    (f : Fin n → R) :
    (fun i : Fin n => coeff
      (Finset.univ.sum (fun j : Fin n => monomial (R := R) (↑j) (f j))) i) = f

def degreeLTEquiv [DecidableEq R] (n : ℕ) :

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.degreeLTLinearEquiv

abbrev degreeLTLinearEquiv [DecidableEq R] (n : ℕ) :
    ↥(degreeLT (R := R) n) ≃ₗ[R] (Fin n → R)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.degreeLTEquiv_toPoly
items.statement:
theorem degreeLTEquiv_toPoly [DecidableEq R] {n : ℕ} {p : CPolynomial R}
    (hp : p ∈ degreeLT (R := R) n) (i : Fin n) :
      degreeLTEquiv (R := R) n ⟨p, hp⟩ i =
          Polynomial.degreeLTEquiv R n ⟨p.toPoly, degreeLT_toPoly.mp hp⟩ i

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.degreeLTEquiv_eq_zero_iff_eq_zero
CompPoly.CPolynomial.eval_eq_sum_degreeLTEquiv
items.statement:
theorem eval_eq_sum_degreeLTEquiv [DecidableEq R] {n : ℕ} {p : CPolynomial R}
    (hp : p ∈ degreeLT (R := R) n) (x : R) :
    eval x p =
      Finset.univ.sum (fun i : Fin n => degreeLTEquiv (R := R) n ⟨p, hp⟩ i * x ^ (i : ℕ))

items.note:
### Quantifiers over bounded-degree polynomials

`toPoly` maps `degreeLT n` onto the Mathlib polynomials of degree below `n`. The lemmas in this
section use this fact to restate a quantifier over `↥(degreeLT n)` as a quantifier over Mathlib
polynomials. They serve only in proofs, because `toPoly` is noncomputable. A typical use decides
an executable predicate `P` by a search over the enumeration `instFintypeDegreeLT`. Suppose that
`P p` holds exactly when `Q p.toPoly` holds. The lemmas then relate the search to the corresponding
quantifier over Mathlib polynomials of degree below `n`.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.exists_degreeLT_toPoly_iff
items.doc:
Some polynomial of degree below `n` satisfies `Q` after `toPoly` exactly when some Mathlib
polynomial of degree below `n` satisfies `Q`.
items.statement:
theorem exists_degreeLT_toPoly_iff (n : ℕ) (Q : R[X] → Prop) :
    (∃ p : ↥(degreeLT (R := R) n), Q p.val.toPoly) ↔ ∃ p : R[X], p.degree < n ∧ Q p

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.forall_degreeLT_toPoly_iff
items.doc:
Every polynomial of degree below `n` satisfies `Q` after `toPoly` exactly when every Mathlib
polynomial of degree below `n` satisfies `Q`.
items.statement:
theorem forall_degreeLT_toPoly_iff (n : ℕ) (Q : R[X] → Prop) :
    (∀ p : ↥(degreeLT (R := R) n), Q p.val.toPoly) ↔ ∀ p : R[X], p.degree < n → Q p

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.forall₂_degreeLT_toPoly_iff
items.doc:
Transport two universal quantifiers through `toPoly`. The first polynomial has degree below
`m`, and the second has degree below `n`.
items.statement:
theorem forall₂_degreeLT_toPoly_iff (m n : ℕ) (Q : R[X] → R[X] → Prop) :
    (∀ f : ↥(degreeLT (R := R) m), ∀ g : ↥(degreeLT (R := R) n),
      Q f.val.toPoly g.val.toPoly) ↔
      ∀ f g : R[X], f.degree < m → g.degree < n → Q f g

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.exists_degreeLT_toPoly_iff_of_degree_lt
items.doc:
Suppose that every Mathlib polynomial that satisfies `Q` has degree below `n`. Then some
polynomial of degree below `n` satisfies `Q` after `toPoly` exactly when some Mathlib polynomial
satisfies `Q`.
items.statement:
theorem exists_degreeLT_toPoly_iff_of_degree_lt (n : ℕ) (Q : R[X] → Prop)
    (hQ : ∀ p, Q p → p.degree < n) :
    (∃ p : ↥(degreeLT (R := R) n), Q p.val.toPoly) ↔ ∃ p : R[X], Q p

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.degree_toPoly_ofFinCoeff_lt
items.doc: The polynomial built from `N` coefficients has `toPoly` of degree below `N`.
items.statement:
theorem degree_toPoly_ofFinCoeff_lt (N : ℕ) (c : ℕ → R) :
    (ofFinCoeff N c).toPoly.degree < (N : WithBot ℕ)

transferred through the `toPoly` coercion. The `@[simp]` attributes follow Mathlib's.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.eval_ext
items.doc:
**Univariate eval-extensionality (degree-bounded).** Two `CPolynomial`s
over an integral domain that agree on more than $d$ points of a `Finset S` are
equal, when $d$ bounds the natural degree of their difference.

The degree bound is needed over finite fields, where two distinct polynomials
may agree on every field element.
items.statement:
theorem eval_ext
    [CommRing R] [DecidableEq R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [IsDomain R]
    {p q : CPolynomial R} {d : ℕ} {S : Finset R}
    (hdeg : (p - q).natDegree ≤ d)
    (hagree :
      d < (S.filter
              (fun r ↦ p.eval r = q.eval r)).card) :
    p = q

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.eval_sub
items.doc: Evaluation preserves subtraction.
items.statement:
theorem eval_sub [Ring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    (a : R) (p q : CPolynomial R) :
    CPolynomial.eval a (p - q) = CPolynomial.eval a p - CPolynomial.eval a q

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.eval_one
items.doc: Evaluation of the constant one computable polynomial.
items.statement:
theorem eval_one [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R]
    (a : R) : CPolynomial.eval a (1 : CPolynomial R) = 1

items.note:
### Cast-oriented forms of the lift lemmas

The lift lemmas (`eval_toPoly`, `coeff_toPoly`, …) rewrite a `CPolynomial` query into a
Mathlib one. These are the same facts in the orientation `norm_cast` wants, with the coercion
on the left, so that `exact_mod_cast` pulls a Mathlib statement about `↑p` back to one about
`p`.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.toPoly_eval
items.statement:
theorem toPoly_eval [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (p : CPolynomial R) (x : R) :
    (p : Polynomial R).eval x = p.eval x

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.toPoly_coeff
items.statement:
theorem toPoly_coeff [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (p : CPolynomial R) (i : ℕ) :
    (p : Polynomial R).coeff i = p.coeff i

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.toPoly_degree
items.statement:
theorem toPoly_degree [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (p : CPolynomial R) :
    (p : Polynomial R).degree = p.degree

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.toPoly_natDegree
items.statement:
theorem toPoly_natDegree [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (p : CPolynomial R) :
    (p : Polynomial R).natDegree = p.natDegree

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.toPoly_leadingCoeff
items.statement:
theorem toPoly_leadingCoeff [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (p : CPolynomial R) :
    (p : Polynomial R).leadingCoeff = p.leadingCoeff

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.eval_zero
items.doc: Evaluation of the zero polynomial.
items.statement:
theorem eval_zero [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (a : R) :
    CPolynomial.eval a (0 : CPolynomial R) = 0

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.eval_add
items.doc: Evaluation preserves addition.
items.statement:
theorem eval_add [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (a : R) (p q : CPolynomial R) :
    CPolynomial.eval a (p + q) = CPolynomial.eval a p + CPolynomial.eval a q

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.eval_neg
items.doc: Evaluation preserves negation.
items.statement:
theorem eval_neg [Ring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (a : R) (p : CPolynomial R) :
    CPolynomial.eval a (-p) = -CPolynomial.eval a p

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.eval_X
items.doc: Evaluation of the variable.
items.statement:
theorem eval_X [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] (a : R) :
    CPolynomial.eval a (CPolynomial.X : CPolynomial R) = a

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.eval_pow
items.doc: Evaluation preserves powers.
items.statement:
theorem eval_pow [CommSemiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [Nontrivial R] (a : R)
    (p : CPolynomial R) (n : ℕ) :
    CPolynomial.eval a (p ^ n) = CPolynomial.eval a p ^ n

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.eval_monomial
items.doc: Evaluation of a monomial.
items.statement:
theorem eval_monomial [Semiring R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] [DecidableEq R] (a c : R) (n : ℕ) :
    CPolynomial.eval a (CPolynomial.monomial n c) = c * a ^ n

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.eval_divX_eq_zero_of_ne_zero_root
items.doc: Dividing by `X` preserves a nonzero root when the constant coefficient vanishes.
items.statement:
theorem eval_divX_eq_zero_of_ne_zero_root [Field R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    {p : CPolynomial R} {a : R} (ha : a ≠ 0)
    (hcoeff : p.coeff 0 = 0) (hroot : CPolynomial.eval a p = 0) :
    CPolynomial.eval a (CPolynomial.divX p) = 0

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.divX_ne_zero_of_ne_zero_coeff_zero
items.doc: If a nonzero polynomial has zero constant coefficient, its quotient by `X` is nonzero.
items.statement:
theorem divX_ne_zero_of_ne_zero_coeff_zero [Field R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R]
    {p : CPolynomial R} (hp : p ≠ 0) (hcoeff : p.coeff 0 = 0) :
    CPolynomial.divX p ≠ 0

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.eval_sub_C_mul_X_pow_trim_eq_self_of_eval_eq_zero
items.statement:
theorem eval_sub_C_mul_X_pow_trim_eq_self_of_eval_eq_zero
    [Field R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (p q : CPolynomial.Raw R) (scale : R)
    (shift : ℕ) {x : R} (hq : q.eval x = 0) :
    ((p - C scale * (q * X ^ shift)).trim).eval x = p.eval x

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.eval_divModByMonicAux_go_snd_eq_self_of_eval_eq_zero
items.statement:
theorem eval_divModByMonicAux_go_snd_eq_self_of_eval_eq_zero
    [Field R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] :
    ∀ (fuel : ℕ) (p q : CPolynomial.Raw R) {x : R}, q.eval x = 0 →
      (divModByMonicAux.go fuel p q).2.eval x = p.eval x

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.Raw.eval_modByMonic_eq_self_of_eval_eq_zero
items.doc: Reducing by a polynomial that vanishes at `x` preserves evaluation at `x`.
items.statement:
theorem eval_modByMonic_eq_self_of_eval_eq_zero
    [Field R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (p q : CPolynomial.Raw R) {x : R}
    (hq : q.eval x = 0) :
    (modByMonic p q).eval x = p.eval x

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.eval_modByMonic_eq_self_of_eval_eq_zero
items.doc: Reducing by a polynomial that vanishes at `x` preserves evaluation at `x`.
items.statement:
theorem eval_modByMonic_eq_self_of_eval_eq_zero
    [Field R] [BEq R] [LawfulBEq R] (p q : CPolynomial R) {x : R}
    (hq : q.eval x = 0) :
    (CPolynomial.modByMonic p q).eval x = p.eval x

modules.title: `C`, `eval₂`, and coefficient-mapping as ring homomorphisms
modules.doc:
`CPolynomial.C`, `CPolynomial.eval₂` and coefficient-mapping bundled as `RingHom`s, plus a
ring-hom extensionality principle transported from Mathlib's `Polynomial.ringHom_ext`.

`CHom` and `eval₂Hom` are computable; `toPolyRingHom` is the noncomputable bundling of
`toPoly` (it is `CPolynomial.ringEquiv`), used in proofs only.  These are the bundled-map
building blocks behind the computable `finSuccEquivNth` construction for `CMvPolynomial`.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.toPoly_injective
items.doc: `toPoly` is injective — it is the forward map of `CPolynomial.ringEquiv`.
items.statement: theorem toPoly_injective : Function.Injective (CPolynomial.toPoly (R := R))

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.eval_eq_eval₂
items.doc: `CPolynomial.eval` is the identity-coefficient case of `eval₂`.
items.statement:
theorem eval_eq_eval₂ (x : R) (p : CPolynomial R) :
    CPolynomial.eval x p = p.eval₂ (RingHom.id R) x

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.CHom
items.doc: `CPolynomial.C` bundled as a ring homomorphism.  Computable.
items.statement: def CHom : R →+* CPolynomial R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.CHom_apply
items.statement: theorem CHom_apply (r : R) : CHom r = CPolynomial.C r

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.toPolyRingHom
items.doc:
`toPoly` bundled as a ring homomorphism (it is `CPolynomial.ringEquiv`).  Noncomputable;
used in proofs only, e.g. to bring `MvPolynomial.eval₂_comp_left` to bear.
items.statement: noncomputable def toPolyRingHom : CPolynomial R →+* Polynomial R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.toPolyRingHom_apply
items.statement: theorem toPolyRingHom_apply (p : CPolynomial R) : toPolyRingHom p = p.toPoly

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.ringHom_ext
items.doc:
Two ring homomorphisms out of `CPolynomial R` are equal once they agree on the constants and
on `X`.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.eval₂Hom
items.doc:
`CPolynomial.eval₂` bundled as a ring homomorphism (the coefficient map `f` and the point `x`
are fixed).  Computable when `S`'s ring operations are.
items.statement: def eval₂Hom (f : R →+* S) (x : S) : CPolynomial R →+* S

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.eval₂Hom_apply
items.statement:
theorem eval₂Hom_apply (f : R →+* S) (x : S) (p : CPolynomial R) :
    eval₂Hom f x p = p.eval₂ f x

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.eval₂Hom_C
items.statement:
theorem eval₂Hom_C (f : R →+* S) (x : S) (r : R) :
    eval₂Hom f x (CPolynomial.C r) = f r

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.eval₂Hom_X
items.statement:
theorem eval₂Hom_X (f : R →+* S) (x : S) :
    eval₂Hom f x (CPolynomial.X) = x

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.evalHom
items.doc:
Evaluation at a point, bundled as a ring homomorphism. This is what gives evaluation the
`map_*` API of a `RingHom`, and in particular `map_sum` and `map_prod`.
items.statement: def evalHom (x : R) : CPolynomial R →+* R

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.evalHom_apply
items.statement: theorem evalHom_apply (x : R) (p : CPolynomial R) : evalHom x p = p.eval x

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.eval_sum
items.doc: Evaluation commutes with finite sums.
items.statement:
theorem eval_sum {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (f : ι → CPolynomial R) (x : R) :
    (∑ i ∈ s, f i).eval x = ∑ i ∈ s, (f i).eval x

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.eval_prod
items.doc: Evaluation commutes with finite products.
items.statement:
theorem eval_prod {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (f : ι → CPolynomial R) (x : R) :
    (∏ i ∈ s, f i).eval x = ∏ i ∈ s, (f i).eval x

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.mapRingHom
items.doc:
Map the coefficients of a computable univariate polynomial along a ring homomorphism.
Computable.
items.statement: def mapRingHom (f : R →+* S) : CPolynomial R →+* CPolynomial S

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.mapRingHom_C
items.statement:
theorem mapRingHom_C (f : R →+* S) (r : R) :
    mapRingHom f (CPolynomial.C r) = CPolynomial.C (f r)

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.mapRingHom_X
items.statement:
theorem mapRingHom_X (f : R →+* S) :
    mapRingHom f (CPolynomial.X) = CPolynomial.X

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.eval_mapRingHom
items.doc: Evaluating a coefficient-mapped polynomial: `eval x (mapRingHom f p) = eval₂ f x p`.
items.statement:
theorem eval_mapRingHom (f : R →+* S) (x : S) (p : CPolynomial R) :
    CPolynomial.eval x (mapRingHom f p) = p.eval₂ f x

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.toPoly_mapRingHom
items.doc: `toPoly` commutes with coefficient-mapping.
items.statement:
theorem toPoly_mapRingHom (f : R →+* S) (p : CPolynomial R) :
    (mapRingHom f p).toPoly = Polynomial.map f p.toPoly

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.natDegree_mapRingHom_le
items.doc: Coefficient-mapping does not increase the degree.
items.statement:
theorem natDegree_mapRingHom_le (f : R →+* S) (p : CPolynomial R) :
    (mapRingHom f p).natDegree ≤ p.natDegree

modules.title: Vanishing Polynomials for Array Nodes
modules.doc: Reusable executable construction of `∏ x in xs, (X - x)`.

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.vanishingPolynomialArray
items.doc: Direct folded vanishing polynomial `∏ x in xs, (X - x)`.
items.statement: def vanishingPolynomialArray (xs : Array F) : CPolynomial F

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.VanishingPolynomialContext
items.doc: Operation dictionary for array vanishing-polynomial construction.
items.statement:
structure VanishingPolynomialContext
    (F : Type*) [Field F] [BEq F] [LawfulBEq F] where
  vanishingPolynomial : Array F → CPolynomial F
  correct :
    ∀ xs, vanishingPolynomial xs = CPolynomial.vanishingPolynomialArray xs

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.VanishingPolynomialContext.direct
items.doc: Direct folded vanishing-polynomial context.
items.statement: def direct : VanishingPolynomialContext F

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.VanishingPolynomialContext.subproduct
items.doc: Subproduct-tree-backed vanishing-polynomial context.
items.statement: def subproduct (M : CPolynomial.MulContext F) : VanishingPolynomialContext F

items.name: CompPoly.CPolynomial.eval_vanishingPolynomialArray_eq_zero_of_mem
items.doc: Every listed node is a root of the direct vanishing polynomial.
items.statement:
theorem eval_vanishingPolynomialArray_eq_zero_of_mem
    (xs : Array F) {x : F} (hx : x ∈ xs.toList) :
    CPolynomial.eval x (CPolynomial.vanishingPolynomialArray xs) = 0
